Although this was already established by the preceding rule, the mention of "compound" (*samāsa*) is for the sake of restriction: if, in a word-formation (*saṃghāta*), the prior portion is a *pada*, then the designation applies only if it is a compound. Consequently, it does not apply to a sentence.
SK 180 *pratyayaḥ* (A 3.1.1):
This governing rule (*adhikāra*) extends until the completion of the fifth book [of Pāṇini’s grammar].
SK 181 *paraś ca* (A 3.1.2).
This [rule] is also like that.

(Pāṇini 4.1.1) "After a feminine suffix (*ḍī*) or a nominal stem (*prātipadika*)," is a governing rule (*adhikāra*) extending up to the end of the fifth book. Since the inclusion of a word qualified by gender is already established by the principle that "when a nominal stem is mentioned, that which is qualified by gender is also included," the explicit mention of *ḍī* and *āp* is for the purpose that the formation of secondary derivatives (*taddhita*) occurs after a stem ending in *ḍī* or *āp*, and not before them.
Pāṇini 4.1.2: *sv-au-ja-s-auṭ-cha-ṣṭā-bhyām-bhis-ṅe-bhyām-bhyas-ṅasi-bhyām-bhyas-ṅas-os-ām-ṅi-os-sup*.

The suffixes beginning with *su* and ending with *sup* occur after nominal stems (*prātipadika*) ending in a *ṅit* suffix or in the vowel *ā*. The letters *u* and *i* in *su* and *ṅsi* [respectively] indicate that the *jhal* and *aṭ* markers [of the preceding stem] are replaced by the *jaś* and *car* sounds.

SK 184 *vibhaktiś ca*: *su*, *tiṅ*, and *tiṅ* are designated as "case endings" (*vibhakti*). Among these, the seven groups of three beginning with *su*, *au*, *jas*, and so on, have the names "first" (*prathamā*) through "seventh" (*saptamī*) according to the Eastern grammarians; by means of these names, usage is also carried out here [in this work].
The three sets of three suffixes following *sup* shall each individually receive the technical designations of singular (*ekavacana*), dual (*dvivacana*), and plural (*bahuvacana*).
SK 186 *dvyekayor dvivacanaikavacane* (A 1.4.22): The dual and singular suffixes are used when two things and one thing are to be expressed, respectively.
These two [terms] apply to duality and unity.

SK 187 *bahuṣu bahuvacanam* (A 1.4.21): The plural suffix occurs when there is plurality. [The application of] *rutva* and *visarga* results in *rāmaḥ*. SK 188 *sarūpāṇām ekaśeṣa ekavibhaktau* (A 1.2.64): Among words that are identical in form, only one remains when they occur with the same case-ending.

Among those words which are seen to have identical forms when followed by the same case-ending, only one remains. In the first two cases (nominative and accusative), there is substitution of the homogeneous long vowel for the preceding [vowel]. When followed by *aci*, there is no *vṛddhi* substitution before *eci*. Thus: *rāmau*.
By the rule *cuṭū* (A 1.3.7),
"the *c*-series and the *ṭ*-series [are] *it* when they are at the beginning of an affix," the letter *j* receives the designation *it*.
SK 190: *na vibhaktau tusmāḥ* (A 1.3.4). In a case-ending (*vibhakti*), the retroflex *ṭu*-class sounds, *s*, and *m* do not become *it*. Thus, the *s* [of *sa*] does not become *it*.

SK 191: *ato guṇe* (Pāṇini 6.1.97). When it would follow that a single substitute of the form of the subsequent [vowel] (*pararūpa*) occurs when a *guṇa* follows an *a* that is not at the end of a word, the long vowel homogeneous with the preceding (*pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*) takes effect because it is subsequent. For, according to the maxim that "an exception (*apavāda*) subsequent to *ato guṇe* sublates only the immediately preceding rules, not those further ahead," this rule sublates only *akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ* (6.1.101) and not even *prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ* (6.1.102). Thus: *rāmāḥ*.
SK 192: *ekavacanaṃ saṃbuddhiḥ* (Pāṇini 2.3.49).
The singular number of the first case (*prathamā*) in the sense of addressing (*saṃbodhana*) shall be known as the vocative (*saṃbuddhi*).
Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.69: *eṅhrasvāt saṃbuddheḥ*.

A consonant (*hal*) following a stem (*aṅga*) ending in *eṅ* or a short vowel (*hrasva*) is elided when it follows the vocative suffix (*saṃbuddhi*). Since the stem is implied by the suffix *saṃbuddhi*, it is qualified by the terms *eṅ* and *hrasva*; therefore, this rule does not apply here: *he katarat kule* ("O which family!"). Examples: *he rāma*, *he rāmau*, *he rāmāḥ*. Why is *eṅ* mentioned? Consider *he hare* and *he viṣṇo*. For in these cases, because the *guṇa* substitution for the vocative suffix takes precedence due to its higher status and its obligatory nature, the [stem] no longer follows a short vowel.
SK 194: *ami pūrvaḥ* (Pāṇini A 6.1.107). When *ami* follows, there shall be a single substitution of the prior form (*pūrvarūpa*) for [the final vowel of] *aka*. Examples: *rāmam*, *rāmau*.
SK 195: *laśakvataddhite* (Pāṇini 1.3.8).

The letters *l*, *ś*, *k*, and the *varga*s [beginning with] *l*, *ś*, and *k* are designated as *it* when they occur at the beginning of an affix, excluding *taddhita* affixes. Thus, the *ś* of the suffix *śas* receives the designation *it*.

SK 196: *tasmāc chaso naḥ pumsi* (A 6.1.103). After a long vowel resulting from the substitution of a homogeneous preceding vowel (*pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*), the *sakāra* of the suffix *śas* shall be replaced by *na* when referring to a masculine.

SK 197: *aṭ-kupv-āṅ-num-vyavāye ’pi* (A 8.4.2). Even when there is an intervention (*vyavāya*) by *aṭ*, the *ku*-class, the *pu*-class, *āṅ*, or *num*—whether individually or combined as far as possible—the *na* following *ra* or *ṣ* becomes *ṇa* within the same word (*samānapada*). The inclusion of *āṅ* is intended to override the prohibition [contained in A 8.4.38] regarding intervention by a word boundary (*padavyavāye ’pi*). The inclusion of *num* is for the purpose of indicating the *anusvāra*; however, that could have been omitted, since it has already been stated that the *ayogavāha* sounds are taught under the *aṭ* category. Thus, the substitution of *ṇa* would [otherwise] apply.
SK 198 *padāntasya* (A 8.4.37): The substitution of *na* for a nasal (*ṇatva*) at the end of a word (*padānta*) shall not occur. Example: *rāmān*.

SK 199 *yasmāt pratyayavidhis tadādi pratyaye ’ṅgam* (A 1.4.13): That which is the basis for the prescription of an affix, along with what follows it, is called an *aṅga* (stem) when an affix follows.

That which constitutes the beginning of a word-form from which an affix (*pratyaya*) is derived shall be designated as a "stem" (*aṅga*) when that affix follows. The inclusion of the term "beginning" (*tadādi*) is for the purpose of granting the designation "stem" to the form qualified by the verbal suffix (*vikaraṇa*), as in *bhavāmi* and *bhaviṣyāmi*. Why [is it said] "an operation" (*vidhi*)? [Consider: *strī*, *iyatī*—[here the designation should not apply to the stem alone]. Why "when an affix follows"? [Consider: so that the designation does not apply to something more extensive than just the affix-qualified form.
With reference to the governing rule "of a member" (aṅgasya) [Pāṇini A 6.4.1].
SK 201 *tāṅsiṅsāminātsyāḥ* (A 7.1.12):

After a stem ending in the vowel *a*, the suffixes beginning with *ta* [i.e., *tas*, *thas*, *tha*, *sip*, *mip*, *vas*, *mas*, *tā*, *ātām*, *jha*, *thās*, *āthām*, *dhvam*, *iḍ*, *vahi*, *mahi*, SK 202 *supi ca* (A 7.3.102): When a case-ending (*sup*) beginning with *yañ* follows, there shall be lengthening of the vowel of the stem (*aṅga*) ending in *at*. [Example: *rāmābhyām*.

SK 203: *ato bhisa ais* (A 7.1.9). The substitute *ais* shall occur for *bhis* after an *aṅga* ending in short *a*. Because it consists of more than one phoneme (*anekāl*), it replaces the whole. Example: *rāmaiḥ*. SK 204: *ṅer yaḥ* (A 7.1.13). [The substitute *ya* occurs for *ṅi* after an *aṅga* ending in short *a*.]

In place of the *ṅe* of the word *para* (the fifth case ending), there shall be the substitution of *y*. Thus: *rāmāya*. Here, by virtue of the *sthānivadbhāva* rule, the substitute *y* is treated as having the nature of a *sup* (case-ending); consequently, the rule *supi ca* applies, resulting in the lengthening of the vowel. However, the paribhāṣā "a rule conditioned by a specific combination [of sounds] does not cause the destruction of that very combination" does not apply here. This is because the irregularity (*anityatva*) of that paribhāṣā is made known by the specific grammatical instruction *kaṣṭāya kramaṇe* and others. Thus: *rāmābhyām*.

SK 205 *bahuvacane jhalyet* (A 7.3.103): When a polysyllabic case-ending (*sup*) beginning with a *jhal* consonant follows, the final vowel of the stem (*aṅga*) is replaced by *e*. For example: *rāmebhyaḥ*. Why "polysyllabic"? [To exclude: *rāmaḥ*, *rāmasya*. Why "beginning with a *jhal*"? [To exclude: *rāmāṇām*. Why "case-ending (*sup*)"? [To exclude: *pacadhvam* [where the substitution is *jaśtva*]. SK 206 *vāvasāne* (A 8.4.56).

At the end [of a word], the *jhal* sounds may optionally become *car* sounds. Thus, from *rāma* we have *rāmāt* or *rāmād*. In the case of the dual, there are four forms: *rāmābhyām* and *rāmebhyaḥ*. Regarding *rāmasya*, even when the doubling of the *s* occurs under the rule *khari ca*, the substitute remains *s* itself due to internal similarity (*āntaratamya*), and not *t*, because of the difference in effort (*prayatna*)—namely, that *s* is a weak breath sound (*alpaprāṇa*). For this very reason, the substitution of *t* for *s* is prescribed by the rule *saḥ si*.
SK 207 *osi ca*:
When *osi* follows, the vowel *e* shall replace the final *a* of a stem; as in *rāmayoḥ*.

SK 208 *hrasvanadyāpo nuṭ* (A 7.1.54): The augment *nuṭ* shall be added after the case-ending *ām* when it follows a stem (*aṅga*) ending in a short vowel, or in *nadī*, or in *āp*. SK 209 *nāmi* (A 6.4.3).

Before an affix beginning with *n* that has *ām* as its marker, there shall be lengthening of the vowel of the final member of a word (*ajantāṅgasya*). As in *rāmāṇām*. Although the rule *supi ca* (Pāṇini 7.3.102) prescribes lengthening when a case-ending (*sup*) follows, it does not apply here because it would contradict the *saṃnipāta-paribhāṣā* (the metarule concerning the destruction of a cause by its own effect). However, the rule *nāmi* (Pāṇini 6.4.3) overrides the *paribhāṣā* due to the force of its specific formulation. [Examples: *rāme*, *rāmayoḥ*. When the substitution of *e* for the final vowel has been applied by the rule *supi* (Pāṇini 7.3.103):
SK 210: *apadāntasya mūrdhanyaḥ* (A 8.3.55). This is a governing rule (*adhikāra*) extending to the end of the book.
Having introduced the governing rule *iṇkoḥ* (Pāṇini A 8.3.57),
[the sūtra] *ādeśapratyayayoḥ* (A 8.3.59) follows.

From the rule *saheḥ sāḍaḥ saḥ*, the word *saḥ* (in the genitive case) is understood [as a governing term]. For a *s* that is not at the end of a word—whether it be a substitute (*ādeśa*) or part of an affix (*pratyaya*)—following a vowel (*iṇ*) or a guttural (*ku*), there shall be a cerebral (*mūrdhanya*) substitute. Since *s* is an unvoiced unaspirated sound, its substitute *ṣ* is likewise unvoiced unaspirated. Examples: *rāmeṣu*. Why "following a vowel or a guttural" (*iṇkoḥ*)? [Counter-example: *rāmasya*. Why "substitute or part of an affix" (*ādeśapratyayayoḥ*)? [Counter-examples: *supīḥ*, *supisau*, *supisaḥ* (from the root *supis*). Why "not at the end of a word" (*apadāntasya*)? [Counter-example: *haris tatra*. In the same way, *kṛṣṇa*, *mukunda*, and others [follow this rule].

SK 213: *sarvādīni sarvanāmāni* (A 1.1.27). Words beginning with *sarva* are designated as *sarvanāman*. This designation applies even to words ending in such [bases], because of the indicator (*jñāpaka*) in the rule *dvandve ca*. Consequently, forms such as *paramasarvatra* (with the suffix *tral*) and *paramabhavakān* (with the suffix *akac*) are established. SK 214: *jasaḥ śī* (7.1.17). [The substitute *śī* takes the place of *jas* after a stem ending in a vowel.]

After a pronominal stem (*sarvanāman*) that does not end in a dental consonant, *jasi* shall be replaced by *śī*. Because it consists of more than one phoneme (*anekāl*), it replaces the entire original form. It should not be argued that, as in the case of the rule *arvaṇas tṛ*, "being composed of more than one phoneme" is not determined by the indicatory letter (*anubandha*); for prior to the application of the replacement, the designation *it* simply does not exist. Thus: *sarve*.
By the rule *sarvanāmnaḥ smai* (A 7.1.14), for the dative singular suffix *ṅe* following a pronominal stem, *smai* shall be substituted. Thus: *sarvasmai*.

SK 216 *ṅasiṅyoḥ smātasminau* (A 7.1.15): For a pronoun ending in *a*, these two [suffixes] *smāt* and *asmin* take the place of *ṅasi* and *ṅi*. [Thus: *sarvasmāt*. SK 217 *āmi sarvanāmnaḥ suṭ* (A 7.1.52): After a pronoun, the augment *suṭ* is added before the suffix *ām*.

The augment *suṭ* is added to the case-ending *ām* prescribed after a pronoun that follows a vowel other than *a*. After the application of *etva* (the substitution of *e*) and *ṣatva* (the substitution of *ṣ*), the forms are *sarveṣām* and *sarvasmin*. The remainder is like that of *rāma*. Pronouns ending in *a*, such as *viśva* and others, are likewise treated; there are thirty-five such words beginning with *sarva*: *sarva*, *viśva*, *ubha*, *ubhaya*, *ḍatara*, *ḍatama*, *anya*, *anyatara*, *itara*, *tva-t*, *tva*, *nema*, *sama*, *sima*; and *pūrva*, *para*, *ava*, *dakṣiṇa*, *uttara*, *apara*, *adhara* when used in their restricted senses and not as proper names.

The term *sva* [is used] when not denoting one's own kinsmen or wealth; *antara* [is used] in the sense of "outside" (*bahiryoga*) or "inner garment" (*upasaṃvyāna*). *Tyad*, *tad*, *yad*, *etad*, *idam*, *adas*, *eka*, *dvi*, *yuṣmad*, *asmad*, *bhavatu*, and *kim*—these are the pronouns. The word *ubha* denotes that which is qualified by duality; for this very reason, it always ends in the dual number. Its inclusion here in the list, however, is for the sake of the suffix *akac* (as in *ubhaka*). Nor is the desired form established by the suffix *kap*; for if *kap* were applied, the suffix *āyac* would undesirably follow—as in *ubhayataḥ* and *ubhayatra*—due to the absence of a subsequent dual ending.

Thus it has been said: "ubhayo 'nyatra" (Pāṇini 1.1.28). Regarding the word "anyatra," Kaiyaṭa maintains that there is no dual form for the word *ubhaya* because it lacks a subsequent dual ending; Haradatta, however, holds that there is. Therefore, since the substitution of *ay* for *ja* (in *ubhaya*) would—by virtue of being a *sthānivadbhāva*—result in the suffix *tayap*, the option provided by the rule *prathamacarama-* (Pāṇini 1.1.33) would apply. However, because this [application of the current rule] is independent of case endings (*vibhakti*), it is more internal (*antaraṅga*) and thus the designation (*saṃjñā*) becomes obligatory. Hence: *ubhaye*. The suffixes are *ḍatara* and *ḍatama*.

When a suffix (*pratyaya*) is mentioned [in a rule], that which ends with it is to be understood. Although there is no inclusion of what ends with the suffix when a suffix is mentioned in a rule prescribing a technical name (*saṃjñā*), as evidenced by the rule *suptiṅantam* (P. 1.4.14), nevertheless, in this case, the inclusion of what ends with the suffix does apply because there is no purpose for the technical name itself to stand alone. The words *anyatara* and *anyatama* are underived (*avyutpanna*); by their very nature, they function to denote selection from among two or many respectively. Among these, the word *anyatama* does not form a technical name because it is not listed in the *gaṇa* [of indeclinables].

*tva* and *tva*—both are indeclinables (*adanta*) that serve as synonyms for "other. According to some, one is udātta and the other is anudātta; according to others, one ends in *-tā*. *Nema* means "half. *Sama* is a synonym for "all" (*sarva*); however, the synonym for "equal" (*tulya*) is not included here, because of the indicator (jñāpaka) in the rule "the subsequent designation of equals follows their respective order" (*yathāsaṃkhyam anudeśaḥ samānām*). Regarding the *gaṇasūtra* "antaraṃ bahiryogeti," it should be stated that this does not apply to a city (*apurī*); thus, [the form] *antarāyāṃ puri* is valid.

SK 218: *pūrvaparāvaradakṣiṇottarāparādharāṇi vyavasthāyām asaṃjñāyām* (A 1.1.34). When these [words]—*pūrva*, *para*, *avara*, *dakṣiṇa*, *uttara*, *apara*, and *adhara*—are used in the sense of "relative position" (*vyavasthā*) and not as a proper name (*asaṃjñā*), that designation of "pronominal" (*sarvanāman*) which applies everywhere due to their inclusion in the list [of pronominals] may optionally apply before the suffix *jas*. Thus: *pūrve* or *pūrvāḥ*. "Relative position" (*vyavasthā*) means a restriction regarding a limit relative to its own denoted object. Why "in the sense of relative position"? [Consider: *dakṣiṇā gāthakāḥ* ("the southern singers"). This means they are skillful. Why "not as a proper name"? [Consider: *uttarāḥ kuravaḥ* ("the Northern Kurus").

SK 219 *svam ajñātidhanākhyāyām* (A 1.1.35): For the word *sva*, when it does not denote kinsmen or wealth, the technical designation (*saṃjñā*) that would otherwise apply may optionally be applied in the *jas* case-ending. Thus, one says either *sve* or *svāḥ*, meaning "one's own" (*ātmīya*) or "oneself" (*ātman*). However, when denoting kinsmen or wealth, one says *svāḥ* in the sense of "kinsmen" or "riches. SK 220 *antaram bahiryogopasaṃvyānayoḥ* (A 1.1.36): [The term *antara* receives the technical designation of *saṃjñā*] when it signifies being outside (*bahiryoga*) or an undergarment (*upasaṃvyāna*).

The designation that applies to the word *antara* when it means "external" (*bāhya*) or "lower garment" (*paridhānīya*) may optionally occur in the *jas* case-ending. *Antare* or *antarā gṛhāḥ*: the meaning is "external houses. *Antare* or *antarā śāṭakāḥ*: the meaning is "lower garments. (SK 221) After the nine beginning with *pūrva*, the forms *smāt* and *smin* optionally replace the endings *ṅasi* and *ṅi*. *Pūrvasmāt* or *pūrvāt*; *pūrvasmin* or *pūrve*. The same applies to *para* and the others. The remainder is like *sarva*. The word *eka*, when used in the sense of number, is always in the singular.

SK 222: *na bahuvrīhau* (A 1.1.29). When a *bahuvrīhi* compound is intended to be formed, the designation of "pronoun" (*sarvanāman*) shall not apply. For example: *tvatkapitṛkaḥ* ("one whose father is you") and *matkapitṛkaḥ* ("one whose father is me"). Here, the designation of "pronoun" is prohibited even prior to the formation of the compound, specifically within the analytical sentence (*prakriyāvākya*). Otherwise, just as in the common analytical sentence (*vigrahavākya*), the suffix *akac* would apply there as well; and that [suffix] would be heard even in the compound, as in *atikrānto bhavakantam* → *atibhavakān*.

The author of the Bhāṣya, however, having accepted the forms *tvakatpitṛka* and *makapitṛka* as correct, rejected this sūtra; for among the sages, authority increases in descending order [of time]. Furthermore, those that have become technical names (*saṃjñā*) or subordinate members (*upasarjana*) are not included among the "sarvādi" group. This is because they were placed in the list only as items compatible with the definition of a "technical name" (*mahāsaṃjñā*). Consequently, neither the operations prescribed for technical names nor the internal operations of the group apply to them. For example: "Give to Sarva"—where *sarva* is a proper name; or "give to Atisarva," who has surpassed everything; or "the family has surpassed the other" (*atikataram kulam*); or "he has surpassed him" (*atitat*).

SK 223: In the case of a *tṛtīyā*-compound (A 1.1.30), the status of being a pronoun (*sarvanāmatā*) would not apply here: *māsapūrvāya*. Nor does it apply in a sentence expressing the meaning of a *tṛtīyā*-compound: *māsena pūrvāya*.
SK 224: *dvandve ca* (A 1.1.31).

In a *dvandva* compound, the technical designation (*saṃjñā*) previously mentioned [as "sarvanāman"] does not apply—as in *varṇāśrametarāṇām*. This prohibition applies to the aggregate (*samudāya*), but not to its individual components (*avayava*). Nor does this lead to the undesired application of *suṭ* by means of the rule of extension to what ends in that (*tadantavidhi*), because it has been explained that *suṭ* is applied to the case-ending *ām* prescribed after a pronominal (*sarvanāman*).

SK 225: *vibhāṣā jasi* (A 1.1.32). When an operation based on the suffix *jas*—namely, that which is called the substitution of *śī*—is to be applied, the previously mentioned designation (*saṃjñā*) for a *dvandva* compound may optionally apply. Thus: *varṇāśrametare* or *varṇāśrametarāḥ*. It has been stated that this optionality applies only with respect to the substitution of *śī*; therefore, the suffix *akac* does not occur. Rather, only the suffix *kap* occurs: *varṇāśrametarakāḥ*.

SK 226: *prathama-carama-taya-alpa-ardha-katipaya-nema-aś-ca* (A 1.1.33). These [words] ending in *taya*, as well as *alpa*, *ardha*, *katipaya*, and *nema*, may optionally receive the designation *ukta* (already mentioned) with respect to the operation of the suffix *jas*. *Prathame* / *prathamāḥ*. The rest is like *rāma*. *Taya* is a suffix; therefore, words ending in it are to be understood [as included]. *Dvitaye* / *dvitayāḥ*. The rest is like *rāma*. *Neme* / *nemāḥ*. The rest is like *sarva*. In the section on optionality (*vibhāṣā-prakaraṇa*), there is a supplementary rule (*upasaṃkhyāna*) for *tīya* when followed by a suffix marked with *ṅ*. *Dvitīyasmai* / *dvitīyāya*, etc. The same applies to *tṛtīyaḥ*. Because of the requirement that the word must be meaningful (*arthavad-grahaṇa*), it does not apply here: *paṭujātīyāya*. *Nirjaraḥ*.

Pāṇini 7.2.101: *jarāyā jaras anyatarasyām*. For the word *jarā*, the substitute *jaras* may optionally occur before a case-ending beginning with a vowel. Under the governing rules (*adhikāra*) concerning words and stems (*pada* and *aṅga*), when a substitute consists of more than one phoneme (*anekāl*), it would normally replace the entire original form; however, substitutes apply only to that which is explicitly mentioned. Since the word *jara-* is not different from *jarā-* when its final portion is modified, *jaras* replaces *jara-*. Thus: *nirjarasau*, *nirjarasaḥ*. Because it is subsequent in the order of rules, *jaras* overrides the suffixes *in* and others. *nirjarasā*, *nirjarase*, *nirjarasaḥ*. In the alternative case, and before endings beginning with consonants, it is like *rāma*.

The author of the Vṛtti, however, by means of a prior counter-exception (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*), having applied the suffixes *in* and *āt*, and relying on the non-eternality of the *saṃnipātaparibhāṣā*, states that when *jaras* is substituted, the forms are *nirjarasina* and *nirjarasāt*, but not *nirjarasā* and *nirjarasaḥ* as some claim; likewise, he mentions another form, *nirjarasaiḥ*, in the *bhis* case. Those who follow him accept the form *nirjarasya* alone for the singular genitive case; however, this contradicts the Bhāṣya.

SK 228: In the vocative singular (*saṃbuddhau*), the vowel *ā* is replaced by *e*. By the rule *eṅ hrasvāt*, the vocative ending *suP* is elided. Thus: *he rame* (O Ramā), *he ramāḥ* (O Ramās). [In the accusative: *ramām*, *rame*, *ramāḥ*. Because it is feminine (*strītvāt*), there is no substitution of *n* for *m*.

SK 229 *paddannomāṣṛnniśasanyūṣandoṣanyakañchakannudannāsañchasprabhṛtiṣu* (A 6.1.63): For the words *pāda*, *danta*, *nāsikā*, *māsa*, *hṛdaya*, *niśā*, *asṛj*, *yūṣ*, *doṣ*, *yakṛt*, *śakṛt*, *udaka*, and *āsya*, the substitutes *pada* and so forth shall optionally apply before suffixes beginning with *śas*. As for the statement in the *Kāśikā* that there is an optional substitute *āsanna* for the word *āsana*, that is an error. *pādaḥ*, *pādau*, *pādāḥ*; *pādam*, *pādau*, *padaḥ*; *pādān*; *padā*; *pādena*, and so forth. SK 230 *svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne* (A 1.4.17): [The term *bha* applies] after [a nominal stem ending in] *su* and the following [suffixes], except when followed by an *asarvanāmasthāna* case-ending.
SK 231: Before suffixes beginning with *su* and ending with *kap*, excluding those that are *asarvanāmasthāna*, the preceding element shall be designated as a *pada*.
(A 1.4.18) *yaci bham*:
Before suffixes beginning with *ya* or *ja* and ending with *kap*, excluding those that are *asarvanāmasthāna*, the preceding element shall be designated as *bha*.
SK 232: *ā kadārādekā saṃjñā* (A 1.4.1).

From this point forward, until the rule *kaḍārāḥ karmadhāraye* (A 2.2.38), it should be understood that for a single word there is only one technical designation (*saṃjñā*), whichever is subsequent and non-occasional (*anavakāśā*). Consequently, when [the suffixes] beginning with *śas* follow an *ac*, the designation *bha* alone applies, not the designation *pada*. Therefore, the substitution of *jaś* does not occur. Examples: *dataḥ*, *datā* (where *jaś*-substitution occurs); *dadbhyām*, etc. *māsaḥ*, *māsā*; after *bhyām*, following the application of *rutva* and *yatva*, there is elision of *ya*: *mābhyām*, *mābhiḥ*, etc.
SK 233 Bhāṣya (A 6.4.129): This is an introductory heading (adhikāra). SK 234 (A 6.4.134): There is elision (lopa) of the *an* [suffix] when followed by a *bha*-designated element.

When the letter *an* follows a consonant (*asvarṇam*) that is part of a word-base (*aṅgāvayava*) and is followed by a letter beginning with *sthā*, *ni*, *ha*, etc., or *sv*, etc., there is elision (*lopa*) of that *a*.

(Pāṇini 6.4.134). By the rule *raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade* (A 8.4.1), a nasal *na* following *repha* (*r*) or *ṣakāra* (*ṣ*) within the same word (*samānapada*) becomes *ṇa*. Thus: *yūṣṇaḥ*, *yūṣṇā*. Regarding the question of whether the status of being a "substitute" (*sthānivadbhāva*) applies even when a rule is conditioned by what precedes (*pūrvasmād api vidhau*), in this case, the change to *ṇa* occurs simply because of the intervention of the augment *aṭ* (*aḍvyavāya*). However, the principle that "what is not established in what precedes (*pūrvatrāsiddhe*) does not behave as a substitute" does not apply here. This is because that principle is restricted by the prohibition: "The fault [of applying *sthānivadbhāva*] exists in the cases of the elision of the first member of a conjunct (*saṃyogādilopa*), the substitution of *l* (*latva*), and the substitution of *ṇa* (*ṇatva*). (Pāṇini 1.1.58 Vārttika).

SK 236: *nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya* (A 8.2.7). The words *na* and *prātipadika* are here used with their sixth-case endings elided (*lupta-ṣaṣṭhīka*). The meaning is: there shall be elision of the letter *n* that stands at the end of a word (*pada*) which bears the technical designation *prātipadika*. Because the elision of *n* is treated as non-existent (*asiddha*), lengthening and the substitution of *ai* do not occur; thus we have *yūṣabhyām*, *yūṣabhiḥ*, *yūṣabhyaḥ*, and so forth.

SK 237: *vibhāṣā ṅiśyoḥ* (A 6.4.136). When *ṅi* or *śi* follow, there may optionally be elision (*lopa*) of the *a* that is part of a stem-final *an*, provided that this *an* is followed by a suffix beginning with *ya*, *ja*, or a vowel other than those [already mentioned]. Thus: *yuṣṇi* or *yūṣṇi*; in the alternative case, it is like *rāma*. In the rule *padanna...* (A 6.1.63), the inclusion of the term *prabhṛti* is intended to indicate "and others of its kind" (*prakāra*). Accordingly, even when *auṅ* is replaced by *śi*, the substitution of *doṣan* is mentioned in the Bhāṣya, as in the example *kakuddoṣaṇī*. By this, the following usage is justified: *padaṅghriś caraṇo 'striyām / svāntaṃ hṛnmānasaṃ manaḥ*, and also *āsanyaṃ prāṇam ūcire*.

*Āsanya* means "situated in the mouth. From this very *Bhāṣya*, it follows that the word *doṣ* can also be neuter; thus, the expression "the night-stalker [took] his right arm" (*dakṣiṇaṃ dor niśācaraḥ*) is consistent. Furthermore, because of its association with *bhuja*, *bāhu*, and *praveṣṭa* in the rule *dor bāhū praveṣṭaḥ*, it can also be masculine. The phrase "he partakes in the arm (*doṣam*) of such a one" is thus explained. That which occurs over two days is *dvyahnaḥ*.

SK 238: *saṃkhyā-visāya-pūrvasyāhnasyāhan anyatarasyāṃ ṅau* (A 6.3.110). For the word *ahna*, preceded by a numeral or the words *vi* and *sāya*, the substitute *ahan* may optionally take the place of *ahna* before the locative singular ending *ṅi*. Thus: *dvyahni*, *dvyahani*, or *dvyahne*; *vyahnaḥ* (from *vigatam ahar*), *vyahni*, *vyahani*, or *vyahne*; *sāyāhnaḥ* (from *sāyāhnaḥ*), *sāyāhni*, *sāyāhani*, or *sāyāhne*. These are the words ending in *-an*. [Next: *viśvapāḥ*. SK 239: *dīrghāj jasi ca* (A 6.1.105). [The substitution of *guṇa* occurs] after a long vowel before the suffix *jas* as well as [before *śas*].

Furthermore, by the rule *dīrghāj jasi*, the *pūrvasavarṇadīrgha* would not occur before the nominative-accusative dual endings (*prathamayoḥ*). [Thus,] *vṛddhi* applies: *viśvapau*. [Otherwise,] *savarṇadīrgha* would apply: *viśvapāḥ*. Although in this case [the form *viśvapau*] is already established by the rule *nādici* even when *auṅ* follows, and there is no defect even if *pūrvasavarṇadīrgha* were to apply before *jas*, nevertheless, for the sake of forms such as *gauryau* and *gauryaḥ*, this sūtra is introduced here as well because it is more logical. (SK 240) *āto dhātoḥ* (A 6.4.140).

There shall be elision (*lopa*) of the final *ā* of a verbal root (*dhātu*) when it occurs at the end of a *bha*-stem that is also a member of a complex base (*aṅga*). By the rule *alo ’ntyasya*, this applies to the final letter; thus, from *viśvapā-* we get *viśvapābhyām*, and so forth. Similarly for *śaṅkhadhmā-* and others. Why specify "of a verbal root"? Consider *hāhā-*: with the suffix *ṭā*, there is lengthening by *savarṇadīrgha*, resulting in *hāhā*. With *ṅe*, there is *vṛddhi*: *hāhai*. With *ṅasi* and *ṅas*, there is lengthening: *hāhāḥ*. With *osi*, there is *vṛddhi*: *hāhauḥ*. With *ṅi*, there is *guṇa* of the initial vowel: *hāhe*. The remainder follows the pattern of *viśvapā-*. Due to a grammatical split (*yogavibhāga*) of the rule *ātaḥ*, the elision of the final *ā* occurs occasionally even for non-verbal roots; e.g., *ktvaḥ śnaḥ*. Thus ends the section on stems ending in long *ā*.
SK 241 *jasi ca* (A 7.3.109): A short-final stem undergoes *guṇa* substitution when followed by the suffix *jas*. [Result: *harayaḥ*.
SK 242 *hrasvasya guṇaḥ* (A 7.3.108).

In the vocative singular, there should be *guṇa* for a short vowel. By the rule *eṅ hrasvāt*, the vocative suffix (*saṃbuddhi*) is elided. Thus: *he hare*. [The accusative forms are: *harim*, *harī*, *harīn*. SK 243: *śeṣo dhyasakhi* (A 1.4.7). Short *i* and *u* vowels that do not have the designation *nadī*, when not ending in the word *sakhi*, shall have the designation *ghi*. Why "the remainder" (*śeṣa*)? [Consider: *matyau*. Since this is established by the governing rule on the assignment of a single designation (*ekasaṃjñādhikāra*), the inclusion of the word "remainder" (*śeṣa*) is for the sake of clarity; this is the truth. Why "short" (*hrasva*)? [Consider: *vātapramye*. Why "short *i* and *u*" (*idutu*)? [Consider: *mātre*.

SK 244 *āṅo nāstriyām* (A 1.3.120): After a stem ending in *gh*, the substitute *nā* shall take the place of *āṅ*, provided it is not feminine. According to the Eastern grammarians, *āṅ* is a technical term (*saṃjñā*) for the suffix *ṭā*. Example: *hariṇā*. Why "not feminine"? Example: *matyā*.
SK 245 *gher ṅiti* (A 7.3.111): [The substitution of *ī* for the final vowel of a stem ending in *gh* occurs before a suffix marked with the *ṅ* indicatory letter.]

In the case of a stem ending in *gh*, there shall be *guṇa* substitution before a *sup* suffix beginning with a *ṅit* vowel. As in *haraye*. Why "of a stem ending in *gh*"? Consider *sakhye*. Why "before a *ṅit* vowel"? Consider *haribhyām*. Why "in the case of a *sup* suffix"? Consider *paṭvī*. When the *guṇa* has been applied by the rule "gher ṅiti" (Pāṇini 7.3.111), [the following applies]: **SK 246:** *ṅasiṅasoś ca* (A 6.1.110). When *ṅasi* or *ṅas* follows a stem ending in *eṅ* (*e* or *o*), the single substitute for both is the preceding form (*pūrvarūpa*). Thus: *hareḥ*, *haryoḥ*, *harīṇām*.

SK 247 *ac ca gheḥ* (A 7.3.119): After *i* and *u*, the ending *ṅi* becomes *aut*, and for a *ghi*-stem, the final letter is replaced by *a*. [Examples: *harau*, *haryoḥ*, *hariṣu*. Similarly, [the forms of] *śrīpati*, *agni*, *ravi*, *kavi*, etc., are formed. SK 248 *anaṅ sau* (A 7.1.93).

In place of the final phoneme of the word *sakhi*, there shall be the substitute *anaṅ* when followed by the nominative singular suffix *su*, provided it is not the vocative case. By the rule *ṅicca*, this is an initial substitute for the entire stem. Regarding the term *upadhā*: "The penultimate letter before the final consonant is called *upadhā*" (Pāṇini 1.1.65);
that is, the phoneme preceding the final consonant (*al*) shall bear the technical designation *upadhā*.

Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.8: In a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix, except for the vocative singular (*asaṃbuddhi*), there is lengthening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) of a stem ending in *n*, provided that a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix other than the vocative follows.
Pāṇini Sūtra 1.2.41: A suffix consisting of a single phoneme (*ekāl*) is termed *apṛkta*.
That which consists of a single phoneme shall be designated as *apṛkta*.

SK 252: *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal* (A 6.1.68). A single consonant (*hal*) that follows a long vowel (*dīrgha*) which itself follows a consonant (*hal*), or a single consonant that follows a long vowel ending in *ṅī* or *āp*, is elided. Why "after a consonant, a long *ṅī* or *āp*" (*halṅyābbhyaḥ*)? [Consider: *grāmaṇī*. Why "long" (*dīrghāt*)? [Consider: *niṣkauśāmbiḥ*; *atikhaṭvaḥ*. Why "the single consonants *su*, *ti*, and *si*" (*sutisi*)? [Consider: *abhaitsīt*. Because *si* is understood here as that which occurs in association with *tip*, there is no inclusion of the *sic* suffix. Why "single consonant" (*apṛktam*)? [Consider: *bibharti*. Why "consonant" (*hal*)? [Consider: *bibheda*. Why "the first consonant" (*prathamahal*)? [Consider: *rājā*.
There would be no elision of *n*, because the elision of the final consonant of a conjunct (*saṃyogāntalopa*) is considered non-existent (*asiddha*). [Thus we have] *sakhā* and *he sakhe*.
**SK 253**: *sakhyur asaṃbuddhau* (A 7.1.92).
A *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix, with the exception of the vocative singular (*asaṃbuddhau*), following the base *sakhi*, should effect the operations of a *ṇit* suffix.

SK 254 *aco ñṇiti* (A 7.2.115): When followed by a suffix marked with *ñ* or *ṇ*, there shall be *vṛddhi* substitution for a stem ending in a vowel. [Examples: *sakhāyau*, *sakhāyaḥ*, *sakhāyam*, *sakhāyau*. Because it lacks the designation *dhi*, its specific grammatical effects do not apply. [Examples: *sakhyā*, *sakhye*. SK 255 *khyatyāt parasya* (A 6.1.112): [The *u* of the dative singular ending *e*] is replaced by *ī* after a word ending in *kh* or *t* that is followed by a *taddhita* suffix marked with *ñ* or *ṇ*. [Example: *sakhye*.

After the words *khi* and *khī*, which have undergone the substitution of *yaṇ* [for the semivowels], the vowel *u* shall replace the *at* of the case endings *ṅasi* and *ṅas*. [Thus: *sakhyuḥ*. (Pāṇini 7.3.118:
*aut*)

The suffix *aut* shall be substituted for the case-ending *ṅi* (locative singular) following stems ending in *i* or *u*. The recurrence of the mention of *u* is for the sake of subsequent rules. *sakhyau*. The remainder is like *hari*. A good friend is *susakhā*. *susakhāyau*. *susakhāyaḥ*. Because the operations of *anaṅ* and the *ṇit*-like behavior apply to the stem (*aṅga*), they also apply when [the suffixes] follow a compound ending in that [stem]. Since the whole [compound] does not possess the form of *sakhi*, the prohibition *asakhi* does not apply, and thus the designation *dhi* is established. *susakhinā*. *susakhaye*. When the *guṇa* substitution has been made in the forms of *ṅasi* and *ṅas*, because the *yaṇ* replacement has not been effected, the substitution of *u* by the rule *khyatyāt* does not occur.

*Sasakheḥ* (genitive singular), *susakhau* (locative dual), and so forth. Similarly, one who has surpassed a friend is *atisakhā*. In the analysis (*vigraha*) "one for whom a friend is supreme," we have *paramasakhā*, *paramasakhāyau*, and so forth. Even when [the word] is secondary (*gauṇatva*), the forms *anaṅ* and *ṇit* proceed [as before]. One who has surpassed a female friend is *atisakhiḥ*; because the maxim regarding words qualified by gender (*liṅgaviśiṣṭaparibhāṣā*) is not universally valid, the suffix *ṭac* does not apply here. It is like *hari* (in the case of *harivat*). Here, the forms *anaṅ* and *ṇit* do not apply to a word with many vowels (*bahvacaḥ*), because the word *sakhi* is defined by a technical rule (*lākṣaṇika*) through the shortening [of the vowel] in the rule *go-striyoḥ*. This is because, between that which is defined by a general rule and that which is stated as a specific word (*pratipadokta*), only the specifically stated one is to be accepted.

SK 257 *patiḥ samāsa eva* (A 1.4.8): The word *pati* shall be designated as *ghi* only when it occurs in a compound. [Examples: *patyā*, *patye*, *patyuḥ* (dual), *patyau*. The remainder is like [the declension of] *hari*. But in a compound: *bhūpatinā*, *bhūpataye*. The word *kati* always ends in the plural. SK 258 *bahugaṇavatuḍati saṃkhyā* (A 1.1.23).
These shall be known as numerals.
According to A 1.1.25, *ḍati ca*, that which ends in the suffix *ḍati* is a numeral and shall be designated as *ṣaṭ*.

SK 260 *pratyayasya luk-ślulupaḥ* (A 1.1.61): The non-appearance of an affix (*pratyayādarśana*) effected by the terms *luk*, *ślu*, and *lup* shall, respectively, receive those specific designations. SK 261 *ṣaḍbhyo luk* (A 7.1.22): [The elision of the case-ending] occurs after the six [numerals].
There shall be elision (*luk*) of the nominative and accusative plural suffixes (*jaś* and *śas*) when they follow [a stem] ending in six [sounds].

According to the rule *pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam* (A 1.1.62), "when a suffix is elided, the grammatical operation conditioned by that suffix still takes place," the substitution of *guṇa* would apply here by the rule *jasi ca*. However—

SK 263 *na lumatāṅgasya* (A 1.1.63): *luk*, *ślu*, and *lup*—these are termed *lumat*. When [an affix] is elided by a word containing the marker *lum*, the grammatical operation (*aṅgakārya*) conditioned by that [affix] shall not take place. Examples: *kati*, *kati*, *katibhiḥ*, *katibhyaḥ*, *katibhyaḥ*, *katīnām*, *katiṣu*. The words *asmad*, *yuṣmad*, and those designated as *ṣaṭ* are identical in form across the three genders. The word *tri* is always used in the plural. Examples: *trayaḥ*, *trīn*, *tribhiḥ*, *tribhyaḥ*. SK 264 *tres trayaḥ* (A 7.1.53).

The word *tri* shall undergo the substitution of *traya* before the ending *ām*. Thus: *trayāṇām*, *paramatrayāṇām*. However, some maintain that this does not apply when [the word] is subordinate (*gauṇa*); thus: *priyatrīṇām*. In reality, however, it is *priyatrayāṇām*. [In the locative: *triṣu*. The word *dvi* always ends in the dual number. (SK 265) *tyadādīnāmaḥ* (A 7.2.102).

The substitution of *a* for the final sound of these [words] occurs before a case-ending (*vibhakti*). This rule is intended to apply only to those words ending in *dvi*. *dvau* (2), *dvābhyām* (3), *dvayoḥ* (2). Why "ending in *dvi*"? [Consider: *bhavān*, *bhavantau*, *bhavantaḥ*. There is no substitution of *ā* when the word is a technical name (*saṃjñā*) or when it is a subordinate member of a compound (*upasarjana*), because this is an operation belonging to the sub-group beginning with *sarva*. [Example: A certain person named *Dvi*. *dviḥ*, *dvī*. *Atidviḥ* ("one who has surpassed two") is treated like *hari*. However, when [the number] is primary (*prādhānya*), one says *paramadvau* and so forth. *Auḍulomiḥ*, *auḍulomī*.

In the plural, however, [the form is] *uḍulomāḥ*. Regarding the suffix *a* for descendants in the plural after the word *loman*, it should be stated that this is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *iñ* prescribed by the *bāhv-ādi* group. Thus: *auḍulomim*, *auḍulomī*, [and] *uḍulomān*. These are the words ending in *ī*. By the *uṇādi* sūtra, the suffix *ī* is added to the root *māṅ*, and it is marked with *k* (kit). One who measures the wind (*vātam pramimīte*) is a *vātapramīḥ*. By the rule *dīrghāj jasi ca*, [we have]: *vātapramyau*, *vātapramyaḥ*, and *he vātapramīḥ*. Before the accusative singular ending *am*, the preceding vowel is substituted [for both vowels]: *vātapramīm*. [The forms are: *vātapramyau*, *vātapramīn*, *vātapramyā*.

*vātapramībhyām* (3), *vātapramye*, *vātapramyaḥ* (2), *vātapramyoḥ* (2), *vātapramyām*. Because of the long vowel [in the stem], the augment *nuṭ* does not occur. However, in the locative singular (*ṅi*), there is a homogeneous long vowel (*savarṇadīrgha*): *vātapramī*. [In the plural locative: *vātapramīṣu*. In the same way are *yayī*, *papī*, and others. That by which they go is *yayī*, a path; he who protects the world is *papī*, the sun. The suffix *ī* is applied with the marker *k* and the doubling of the root, according to the rule *yāpoḥ kid dve ca*. But for the word *vātapramī* ending in the *kvip* suffix, there is a specific difference in the accusative singular (*ami*), the nominative plural (*śasi*), and the locative singular (*ṅau*): *vātapramyam*, *vātapramyaḥ*.

*vātapramī*: the *yaṇ* substitution is applied by the rule to be stated later, *eranekācaḥ*. *pradhīvāt*: like *pradhī*. *bahuśreyasī*: one for whom there are many (*bahvyaḥ*) excellent things (*śreyasyaḥ*) is *bahuśreyasī*. Because it ends in a long vowel (*dīrghaṅyantatvāt*), the *su* suffix is elided by the rule *halṅyābbhyaḥ*. SK 266: *yū stryākhyau nadī* (A 1.4.3).

Feminine bases ending in *ī* or *ū* that are always feminine in gender receive the technical designation *nadī*. And there is the inclusion of the "original gender" (*prathamaliṅgagrahaṇam*). The meaning is that the status of being a *nadī* must be stated even when a previously feminine base has become a subordinate member (*upasarjana*).

SK 267 *ambārthanadyor hrasvaḥ* (A 7.3.107): In the vocative case, the short vowel is substituted for words meaning "mother" (*ambā*) and for those ending in feminine suffixes marked with *ṅ* (the *nadī* class). [Examples: *he bahuśreyasi*; [in the nominative plural] *bahuśreyasīn*. SK 268 *āṇ nadyāḥ* (A 7.3.112): The suffix *āṅ* is added after a word ending in a feminine suffix marked with *ṅ* (the *nadī* class), provided it is not followed by a case-ending beginning with *i* or *u*. [Example: *bahuśreyasyām*.

The augment *āṬ* shall be applied to those *ṅit* endings that follow a stem ending in *nadī*. By A 6.1.90 (*āṬaś ca*), when *aci* follows *āṬ*, there shall be a single substitute *vṛddhi*. [Examples: *bahuśreyasyai*; *bahuśreyasyāḥ*. Because it follows a stem ending in *nadī*, the augment *nuṬ* is applied: *bahuśreyasīnām*.

SK 270: *ṅerām nadyāmnībhyaḥ* (A 7.3.116). After words ending in *nadī*, words ending in *ā*, and from the word *nī*, the suffix *ām* is substituted for the seventh case ending (*ṅi*). Here, because it is subsequent, *āṭ* supersedes *nuṭ*. Example: *bahuśreyasyām*. The remainder is like [the declension of] a feminine word ending in the suffix *ī*, such as *vātapramī*. Because it does not end in a *ṅit* suffix, there is no elision of the nominative singular *su*. Example: *atilakṣmīḥ*. The remainder is like *bahuśreyasī*. A Brāhmaṇa who desires a maiden, or who behaves like a maiden, is called *kumārī*. This is derived either from the desiderative *kyaj*-stem or from the denominative *ācārakviṣ*-stem, with the agentive suffix *kvip*. By the rule *halṅyābbhyaḥ*, there is elision of the nominative *su*. SK 271: *aciśnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau* (A 6.4.77). When a vowel follows, *iyaṅ* is substituted for the *yu* of roots ending in *śnu* and for the word *bhru*, and *uvaṅ* is substituted for the *vu* of the word *bhū*.

The *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ* substitutions occur for the final *i*-vowel or *u*-vowel of a verbal root ending in the *śnu* suffix, and for the stem *bhrū*, when followed by an affix beginning with a vowel. Since the rule "that which has the marker *ṅ* is a substitute for the final [phoneme]" applies, *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ* replace only the final phoneme. By the principle of closest proximity (*āntaratamya*), *iyaṅ* replaces the first *i* and *uvaṅ* replaces the first *u*. When *iyaṅ* would thus be expected to apply, A 6.4.82 states: "In place of *e*, *o*, and *ai*, there is substitution of *iy*, *uv*, and *ay* respectively, provided the stem consists of more than one syllable and the *e*, *o*, or *ai* is not preceded by a consonant cluster."

When a vowel *i* (ivarṇa) does not arise from the combination of two parts of a verbal root (*dhātu*), then for a stem (*aṅga*) ending in such a root that has more than one syllable, *yaṇ* shall be substituted [for the *i*] when followed by an affix beginning with a vowel. Thus, *yaṇ* is applied: *kumāryau*, *kumāryaḥ*; *he kumāri*; [in the accusative singular] *ami* and [in the plural] *śasi*: *kumāryam*, *kumāryaḥ*; [in the dative singular] *kumāryai*; [in the ablative and genitive singular] *kumāryāḥ* (twice); [in the genitive plural] *kumārīṇām*; [in the locative singular] *kumāryām*. *pradhīḥ*, *pradhyau*, *pradhyaḥ*; *pradhyam*, *pradhyaḥ*. [The word] *unnīḥ* means "one who leads up" (*unnayati*).

Because the suffix *dhātu* (verbal root) qualifies the compound (*saṃyoga*), the substitution *yaṇ* must indeed occur here: *unnyau*, *unnyaḥ*, *he unnīḥ*, *unnyam*. [In the locative singular] *ṅi* becomes *ām*: *unnyām*. Similarly for *grāmaṇīḥ*. Why "having more than one vowel" (*anekācaḥ*)? [Consider: *nīḥ*, *niyau*, *niyaḥ*. In the cases of *ami* and *śas*, *iyaṅ* applies because it is of higher priority: *niyam*, *niyaḥ*. [In the locative singular] *ṅi* becomes *ām*: *niyām*. Why "not preceded by a conjunct" (*asaṃyogapūrvasya*)? [Consider: *suśriyau*, *yavakriyau*. The substitution *yaṇ* is not desired when the preceding member is other than a *gati* or a *kāraka*: *śuddhadhiyau*, *paramadhiyau*.

How then is the phrase "those of evil intellect, out of fear of a scorpion," etc., to be explained? It is said: in the analysis *duḥsthitā dhīryeṣām* ("those whose intellect is ill-situated"), the word *dur* does not even possess the status of a prefix (*gati*) in relation to the word *dhī*. Furthermore, the status of the ablative (*apādāna*) attributed to the word *vṛścika* based on the intellect is not intended here. Alternatively, *vṛścikabhīḥ* means "fear connected with a scorpion," involving the elision of the middle member (*uttarapadalopa*).

SK 273: *na bhūsudhiyoḥ* (A 6.4.85). The *yaṇ* substitution shall not occur for these two (*bhū* and *sudhī*) before an *ac* vowel in a *sup* case-ending. Thus: *sudhiy-au*, *sudhiyaḥ*, and so forth. One who desires a friend is expressed as *sakhīyati*. From that [denominative stem], the elision of *a* (*allopa*) and the elision of *y* (*yalopa*) apply. Since the elision of *a* (*allopasya*) would be treated as if it were still present (*sthānivadbhāva*), the *yaṇ* substitution would be expected before the suffix *aṇ*. However, "that which is elided by *kvip* is not treated as *sthānivadbhūta*. Because a form modified in one part is not considered different from the original, the suffixes *anaṅ* and *ṇit* apply. Thus: *sakha-ā* → *sakhā*; *sakhāy-au* → *sakhāyau*; *sakhāya-as* → *sakhāyaḥ*. In the vocative singular, *he sakhi-i*, the *yaṇ* substitution would be expected because it applies after the *pūrvarūpa* rule. However, because it is further subsequent, the rule *sakhyur asaṃbuddhau* (A 7.1.92) takes effect. Therefore: *he sakhīḥ*.

*sakhāyam* (acc. sg.), *sakhāyau* (acc. du.). Before the suffix *śas*, *yaṇ* [substitution] occurs: *sakhyaḥ* (nom./acc. pl.). One who exists together with a friend (*sakha*) is a *sakha*; one who desires him is *sakhīḥ*. One who desires happiness is *sukhīḥ*; one who desires a son is *sutīḥ*. *sakhyau* (loc. sg.), *sukhyau*, *satyau*. Because of the rule *khyatyāt*, the vowel *u* is substituted even for a long vowel; thus: *sakhyuḥ* (abl./gen. sg.), *sukhyuḥ*, *sutyuḥ*. One who desires what is cut is *lūnīḥ*; one who desires what is emaciated is *kṣāmīḥ*; one who desires what is stiffened is *prastīmīḥ*.

In place of the *ṅasi* and *ṅas* [case endings] of these [words ending in *ī*], there is *yaṇ*. Because the rules for *natva* and *am-tva* are considered *asiddha*, the substitution of *u* by the rule *khyatyāt parasya* applies: *lūnyuḥ*, *kṣāmyuḥ*, *prastīmyuḥ*. From the verbal root *śuṣkīyati*, with the suffix *kvip*, we have *śuṣkīḥ*. By the rule *iyaṅ*, we have *śuṣkiyau*, *śuṣkiyaḥ*. In the forms of *ṅasi* and *ṅas*, we have *śuṣkiyaḥ*, and so forth. These are the words ending in *ī*. *Śambhuḥ* is like *hari*. Likewise are *viṣṇu*, *vāyu*, *bhānu*, and others. SK 274: *tṛjvat kroṣṭuḥ* (A 7.1.95). [The word *kroṣṭu* is treated like a word formed with the suffix *tṛc*.]

The word *kroṣṭu* functions like a form ending in *tṛc* when followed by a non-vocative *sarvanāmasthāna* [case-ending]. This means that in place of the word *kroṣṭu*, the word *kroṣṭṛ* should be employed.
Regarding this, the rule *ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ* (A 7.3.110) applies, which states:
"When a *sarvanāmasthāna* or a *ṅi* [ending] follows, there is *guṇa* substitution for a stem ending in *ṛ*. This being the case:
SK 276: In the case of words ending in *ṛ*, as well as *uśanas* and others, the substitution *anaṅ* occurs before the nominative singular suffix *su*, provided it is not the vocative. SK 277:
The substitution *anaṅ* occurs for the final vowel of *ap*, *tṛn*, *tṛc*, *svasṛ*, *naptṛ*, *neṣṭṛ*, *tvaṣṭṛ*, *kṣattṛ*, *hotṛ*, *potṛ*, and *praśāstṛ*.

In the case of words beginning with *naptr*, there shall be lengthening of the penultimate vowel when followed by a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix, excluding the vocative singular. The mention of *naptr* and so forth is for the purpose of restriction (*niyamārtha*) under the view that [these words] are derived through grammatical derivation (*vyutpattipakṣa*). If the lengthening occurs for words ending in *tṛn* or *tṛc* produced by the *uṇādi* suffixes, it occurs only for *naptr* and its kin. Therefore, it does not apply to words such as *pitṛ* (father) or *bhrātṛ* (brother). However, it certainly applies to the word *udgātṛ* (singer/priest), because of the usage *udgātāraḥ* found in the Bhāṣya on the *Samartha* Sūtra. *kroṣṭā* (nom. sg.), *kroṣṭārau* (nom. du.), *kroṣṭāraḥ* (nom. pl.); *kroṣṭāram* (acc. sg.), *kroṣṭārau* (acc. du.), *kroṣṭūn* (acc. pl.). SK 278: *vibhāṣā tṛtīyādiṣv aci* (A 7.1.97): [The substitution of *u* for the final vowel of *kroṣṭṛ*] is optional before vowel endings from the third case onwards.
In the case of *ajādi* stems and those beginning with the third case-ending (*tṛtīyādi*), the word *kroṣṭṛ* optionally takes the form of the suffix *tṛc*. Thus: *kroṣṭrā*, *kroṣṭre*.

By Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.1.111 (*ṛta ut*), when *ṅasi* or *ṅas* follows, there shall be a single substitute *u* for the final vowel of a stem ending in *ṛ*; this *u* is followed by *r* (i.e., it becomes *ur*).

SK 280 (*rāt sasya*, A 8.2.24): After the letter *r*, only the *s* of a final consonant cluster is elided, and no other [consonant]. The *r* becomes a *visarga*. *kroṣṭuḥ*. When the suffix *ām* follows, although the substitution of *tṛjvat* would apply by priority, the augment *nuṭ* applies by prior conflict (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*) over the operations of *num*, *aci raṅ*, and *tṛjvadbhāva*. Thus: *kroṣṭūnām*. In the forms *kroṣṭari* and *kroṣṭroḥ*, and in the alternative case where the suffix begins with a consonant, it is like *śambhu*. These are the words ending in *u*. SK 281 (*oḥ supi*, A 6.4.83): [The substitution of *guṇa* occurs] for the vowel *u* [of the stem] when followed by a case-ending (*sup*) beginning with a vowel.

When a verbal root ending in *u* is not preceded by a consonant cluster (*saṃyoga*), then for that root-final stem consisting of more than one syllable (*anekāc*), the *yaṇ* substitution shall take place before case-endings (*sup*) beginning with a vowel. However, the *yaṇ* substitution is not desired when the preceding member is other than a *gati* or a *kāraka*. Examples: *khalapv-au*, *khalapvaḥ*, and so forth. Similarly, *sulv-ā* and others. Why "consisting of more than one syllable"? [Counter-example: *luv-au*, *luvaḥ*. Why "not preceded by a part of the verbal root"? [Counter-example: *ullūḥ*, *ullv-au*, *ullvaḥ*. Why "not preceded by a consonant cluster"? [Counter-example: *kaṭapruv-au*, *kaṭapruvaḥ*. Why "a *gati* and so forth"? [Counter-example: ...
*paramaluvau*. Why [is it] *supi*? [Because in] *luluvatuḥ* [it does not apply]. [The rule] *na bhūsudhiyoḥ* [applies to] *svabhuvau*, *svabhuvaḥ*. SK 282: *varṣābhvaś ca* (A 6.4.84).

In place of the *u* of this [stem], *yaṇ* shall be substituted before a vowel ending in *suP*. [Examples: *varṣābhvau*, *varṣābhvaḥ*. [The word] *dṛmbhūḥ* is derived from the root *dṛbh* by the *uṇādi* sūtra: "andūdṛmbhūjambūkaphelūkarkandhūdidhiṣūḥ. [Examples: *dṛmbhvau*, *dṛmbhvaḥ*, *dṛmbhūm*, *dṛmbhvau*, *dṛmbhūn*. The remainder is like *hūhū*. [Alternatively,] when the indeclinable *dṛn*—meaning "injury"—ending in *n* is used as a prefix, the suffix *kvip* is added to the root *bhū*. [Thus: *dṛnbhūḥ*. It should be stated that *yaK* is substituted for *bhū* when preceded by *dṛn*, *kara*, or *punar*. [Examples: *dṛmbhvau*.

*dṛnbhū* and so forth are declined like *khalapū*. [The forms are: *karabhvau*, *karabhvaḥ*. However, in the long-vowel reading (*dīrghapāṭha*), *kāra* is simply *kara*; with the suffix *aṇ* in the sense of the base itself (*svārthika*) as in the *prajñādi* group, we have *kāra*. [The forms are: *kārabhvau*, *kārabhvaḥ*. *Punarbhū* is etymological (*yaugika*) and masculine; [the forms are] *punarbhvau* and so forth. The words *dṛgbhū* and *kārābhū* are declined like *svayambhū*. Thus end those ending in *ū*. *Dhātṛ*: *dhātā*, *he dhātaḥ*, *dhātārau*, *dhātāraḥ*. It should be stated that after a vowel ending in *ṛ*, there is optionally *ṇ*-substitution for *n*; thus *dhātṝṇām* and so forth. The same applies to *naptr* and others. *Udgātṛ*: *udgātārau*.

*Pitṛ-* [father]. In the view that this is a word derived through grammatical formation (*vyutpattipakṣa*), the long vowel does not occur because the inclusion of *naptr-* and others [in A 6.4.13] serves as a restrictive rule (*niyama*). Thus: *pitarau*, *pitaraḥ*, *pitaram*, *pitarau*. The remainder is like *dhātṛ-*. Similarly for *jāmātṛ-* [son-in-law], *bhrātṛ-* [brother], and so on. *Nṛ-* [man]: *nā*, *narau*, *naraḥ*, *he naḥ*. (SK 283) *nṛ ca* (A 6.4.6).

For this word *nṛ*, there may optionally be either the *nāmi* [strengthening] or the long vowel. Thus: *nṛṇām* or *nṝṇām*. These are the words ending in *ṛ*. Regarding the two roots *kṝ* and *tṛ*, because of the optional extended application (*atideśa*) based on the rule "an imitation is like its original" (*prakṛtivadanukaraṇam*), when the substitution of *it* occurs, *ra* replaces the *ṛ*. Thus: *kīḥ*, *kirau*, *kiraḥ*; *tīḥ*, *tirau*, *tiraḥ*, and so forth, like *gīḥ*. In the alternative where the substitution of *it* does not occur, however, due to the rule *ṛduśanas-puru-daṃsaḥ-an-ṅe* and the rule *ṛto ṅi*, the presence of the *tapara* marker prevents both *anaṅ* and *guṇa*. Thus: *kṝḥ*, *krau*, *kraḥ*; *kṝm*, *krau*, *kṝn*; *krā*, *kre*, and so forth.

Thus end the words ending in *ṛ*. In the case of the imitation (*anukaraṇa*) of the roots *gamḷ* and *śakḷ*, the augment *anaṅ* is applied: *gamā*, *śakā*. However, in the domain of *guṇa*, there is substitution by *la*. [Examples: *gamlau*, *gamaḷaḥ*, *gamaḷam*, *gamlau*, *gamṝn*, *gamlā*, *gamle*. But for the endings *ṅasi* and *ṅas*, after the substitution of *u* for *ṛ* (by *ṛta ut*) and the subsequent substitution of *la*, the final consonant of the cluster is elided (*saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ*): *gamul*, *śakul*, and so forth. Thus end the words ending in *ḷ*. *saiḥ*, *sayau*, *sayaḥ*; *smṛtaiḥ*, *smṛtayau*, *smṛtayaḥ*. Thus end the words ending in *e*. SK 284: *goto ṇit* (A 7.1.90). [This sūtra prescribes that the case endings following the word *go* are treated as having the marker *ṇ*.]
The *sarvanāmasthāna* suffixes following the word *go-* shall behave like a *ṇit*. [Thus: *gauḥ*, *gāvau*, *gāvaḥ*.
[This is governed by] A 6.1.93: *auto 'mśasoḥ*.

The word division is *ā-ota*. When an *ac* vowel follows the vowels *a* and *o*, there shall be a single substitute *ā* for both. Because of its association with the suffix *śas*, only the case-ending *am* (the accusative singular) is understood here. Thus, it does not apply in these cases: *acinavam*, *asunavam*, *gām*, *gāvau*, *gāḥ*, *gavā*, *gave*, *goḥ*, and so forth. It should be stated that [the rule] *āto ṇit* applies; furthermore, it is a qualifier of what is prescribed (*vihita-viśeṣaṇa*). Consequently, in *sudyauḥ*, *sudyāvau*, *sudyāvaḥ*, the designation *sarvanāmasthāna* does not apply here because of the interpretation that it must be prescribed after a stem ending in *o*. Therefore, it is not applied in *he bhāno* or *he bhānavaḥ*.

By whom Śambhu is remembered, he is *smṛta-uḥ* (in the nominative singular). [In the dual: *smṛt-au*, *smṛt-āvau*; [in the plural: *smṛt-āvaḥ*. [In the accusative singular: *smṛt-ām*; [in the dual: *smṛt-āvau*; [in the plural: *smṛt-āḥ*, and so forth. Thus end those ending in *-o*. [Now follows the rule: *rāyo hali* (Pāṇini 7.2.85).

In the case of the word *rāi*, the vowel *ā* is the substitute for the final [phoneme] before a consonant (*hal*) case-ending; before a vowel (*ac*), the substitute is *āy*. Thus: *rāḥ*, *rāyau*, *rāyaḥ*; *rāyam*, *rāyau*, *rāyaḥ*; *rāyā*, *rābhyām*, and so forth. These are the words ending in *ai* and *o*. *glau-*: *glauḥ*, *glāvau*, *glāvaḥ*; *glāvam*, *glāvau*, *glāvaḥ*, and so forth. Here, the rule *auto ’mśasoḥ* does not apply. This is because the rule *ais auj* indicates that there is no phonetic similarity (*sāvarṇya*) between *o* and *aut*. These are the words ending in *au*. Thus ends the section on masculine nouns ending in vowels.
Now begins the section on feminine stems ending in vowels.
*Ramā*. [SK 287] *auṅa āpaḥ* (A 7.1.18).

After a word ending in *āp*, the substitute *śī* shall take the place of the case-ending *auṅ*. *Auṅ* is a technical designation for the dual case-ending *au*. Thus: *rame*, *ramāḥ*. SK 288: *saṃbuddhau ca* (A 7.3.106).

In the vocative singular, the single substitute *e* shall take the place of *āp*. By A 6.1.69 (*eṅ hrasvāt*), the vocative suffix is elided. Thus: *he rame*, *he rame*, *he ramāḥ*. The accusative forms are: *ramām*, *rame*, *ramāḥ*. Because the word denotes femininity, there is no substitution of *n* [for the final consonant].

SK 289 *āṅi cāpaḥ* (A 7.3.105): When *āṅ* or *osi* follows, the vowel *e* shall replace the final *ā* of a stem ending in *āp*. [Examples: *ramayā*, *ramābhyām*, *ramābhiḥ*. SK 290 *yāḍāpaḥ* (A 7.3.113).

The augment *yāṭ* shall be applied to the word *āp* (feminine nominal stems ending in long *ā*) when followed by a suffix marked with *ṅ*. [Rule A 6.1.88: *vṛddhir eci*: *vṛddhi* is substituted for the final vowel of the first element and the initial vowel of the second element when both are *ec* vowels. *rāmayai*. [By A 6.1.101: *savarṇadīrghaḥ*: a long homogeneous vowel is substituted for two similar vowels. *rāmāyāḥ*. *ramayoḥ*. *ramāṇām*. *ramāyām*. *ramayoḥ*. *ramāsu*. In this same manner, *durgā* and others are declined. [Rule A 7.3.114: *sarvanāmnaḥ syāḍ ḍhrasvaś ca*: the augment *syāṭ* is added to a pronoun, and its final vowel is shortened.

After a pronominal stem ending in *ā*, the augment *syāṭ* is inserted before a case-ending marked with *ṅ*, and the *ā* of *āp* is shortened. This is an exception to the rule for *yāṭ*. Examples: *sarvasyai*, *sarvasyāḥ* (dual). Because the single substitute (*ekādeśa*) is treated as part of the preceding element, the augment *suṭ* is applied by the rule *āmi sarvanāmnaḥ*: *sarvāsām*. Examples: *sarvasyām*, *sarvayoḥ*, *sarvāsu*. In the same way, *viśva* and other stems ending in *ā* are declined. SK 292: *vibhāṣā diksamāse bahuvrīhau* (A 1.1.28).

In this case, there may optionally be the designation of a pronoun (*sarvanāmatā*): *uttarapūrvasyai* or *uttarapūrvāyai*. Because of the rule *diṅnāmāny antarāle* (Pāṇini 2.2.26), which prescribes the formation of a directional compound (*diksamāsa*) by its very wording, [the designation of a pronoun] does not apply here. For one who is confused such that what is north is east for her, [one says] *uttarapūrvāyai*. The mention of the *bahuvrīhi* is for the sake of clarity. As in *antarasyai śālāyai*, meaning "to the outer hall. Because of the statement *apurī* ("not a city"), it does not apply here: *antarāyai nagaryai*. (SK 293) *vibhāṣā dvitīyātṛtīyābhyām* (A 7.3.115).

From these two [suffixes], *syāṭ* may optionally be added after a stem ending in a *ṅit* suffix, and the vowel of *āp* becomes short. This rule can be dispensed with, because the addition of *ṅit*-markers is prescribed for ordinal numbers (*tīya*). [The forms are: *dvitīyasyai*, *dvitīyāyai*; *dvitīyasyāḥ*, *dvitīyāyāḥ*; *dvitīyasyām*, *dvitīyāyām*. The remainder is like *ramā*. The same applies to *tṛtīyā*. For stems meaning "mother" (*ambārtha*) and for *nadī* stems, the vowel becomes short: *he amba*, *he akka*, *he alla*. However, there is no shortening for those containing *ḍa*, *la*, or *ka* when they are not joined together: *he ambāḍe*, *he ambāle*, *he ambike*. [The word] *jarā*:

In the case of *jaras* (the feminine stem of *jara*), because the substitution of *jaras* is subsequent to the application of the *śī* augment, *jaras* replaces [the final vowel] before the nominative singular ending *am*. Because the insertion of *nuṭ* is subsequent to that, *jaras* replaces [the final vowel] even before *am*, resulting in forms such as *jarasām*, and so on. In other cases and before consonant endings, it follows the pattern of *ramā*. Regarding this, some say that by applying the *śī* augment through the principle of "priority of conflict" (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*) and by relying on the non-eternality of the *saṃnipāta-paribhāṣā*, the form *jarasī* is obtained; however, that is without foundation. Even if one were to rely on the status of the substitute *jaras* as being equivalent to the original (*sthānivadbhāva*) to establish its ending in *-ā*—thereby invoking the rules *auṅa āpaḥ*, *āṅi cāpaḥ*, *yāḍāpaḥ*, and *hrasvanadyāpaḥ*—[the aforementioned view remains untenable].

The five rules beginning with *ṅerām* (Pāṇini 7.3.112) would thus apply even to *nas*, *niṣ*, and *pṛt*. Nevertheless, they do not apply because of the statement "not when a rule concerning a letter (*analvidhi*) is being formulated. This is because, by reading *ā-āp* as a single compound (*praśliṣya*), the word *āp* is understood everywhere as referring specifically to that which has the form of the vowel *ā*. Similarly, in the rule *halaṅyābbhyo dīrghāt* (Pāṇini 6.1.68), since one can achieve forms such as *atikhaṭvaḥ* and *niṣkauśāmbiḥ* by reading *ā-āp-ṅī-ī* as a single compound, the explicit mention of the term "long" (*dīrgha*) may be rejected.

Even so, one should not argue that in *atikhaṭvāya*, the suffix *yāṭ* would occur by relying on *ākāratva* residing in its own base (*svāśraya*) and *āptva* [of the letter *ā*] through the application of *sthānivadbhāva*; for *yāṭ* is prescribed after an *aṅga* that ends in *ā*. Furthermore, when a feminine suffix is an *upasarjana*, there is the restriction that the word begins with that [suffix]. Thus, by the rule *paddanno...*, *nāsikā* becomes *nas*: *nasaḥ*, *nasā*, *nobhyām*, and so forth. In the alternative case where the suffix *su* is present, it is like *ramā*. [Similarly,] *niśā* becomes *niś*: *niśaḥ*, *niśā*. SK 294: *vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.36).

For the seven roots beginning with *vraśc* and for those ending in *ch* or *ś*, the letter *ṣ* is the substitute at the end of the word before a *jhal* consonant or at the end of a word. By the rule of *jaś*-ness, *ṣ* becomes *ḍ*. Thus: *niḍbhyām*, *niḍbhiḥ*. In the case of the locative plural (*sup*), by the rule "ḍaḥ si" (Pāṇini 8.2.34), the augment *dhuṭ* is optionally inserted. Then there is *carv*-ness (*ḍ* becomes *ṭ*). Because that [substitution] is considered asiddha, the rule "the second letter of the *caya* group" does not apply, so *ṭ* and *t* do not become *ṭh* and *th*. Furthermore, by the rule "na padāntāṭ ṭoḥ" (Pāṇini 8.4.41), the substitution of *ṣṭu* does not occur. Thus: *niṭtsu* or *niṭsu*. SK 295: *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si* (A 8.2.41). [The substitute *k* occurs in place of *ṣ* and *ḍh* before the suffix *si*.]

Regarding the rule "there shall be *k* for both *ṣ* and *ḍh* when followed by *s*," this does not apply here because [the substitution of *j*] is considered non-existent (*asiddha*) with respect to the *jaś*-rule. However, some maintain that the word "dhātuḥ" (of a root) is carried over from the rule *dāer dhātoḥ* into the *vraśca*-sūtra; according to their view, there is *jakāra* (substitution of *j*) by the *jaś*-rule. Thus: *nijbhyām*, *nijbhiḥ*. Then there is the *jaś*-rule, then the *ścu*-rule, then the *cartva*-rule, resulting in *nicaśu*. But the substitution of *k* (by *coḥ kuḥ*) does not occur, because the *jaś*-rule is considered non-existent (*asiddha*).

In place of *māṃsa*, *pṛtanā*, and *sānu*, the forms *māṃs*, *pṛt*, and *snau* may optionally be substituted before suffixes beginning with *śas* and so on. Thus: *pṛtaḥ*, *pṛtā*, *pṛdbhyām*; or, in the alternative case and before the nominative singular (*su*), they are like *ramā*. *Gopā* is like *viśvapā*. *Mati* is generally like *hari*; because it is feminine, there is no substitution of *n* [for *t*]. *Matīḥ*; there is no substitution of *ā* [for *i*]. *Matyā*.

SK 296 *ṅiti hrasvaś ca* (A 1.4.6): When followed by a suffix beginning with a *ṅ* (ṅ, ṇ, ṇ, n, m), the long vowels *ī* and *ū*—provided they are not the word *strī* and are always feminine—and the short vowels *i* and *u*, optionally receive the designation *nadī*. [In the case of *mati*: *āṇ nadyāḥ* (A 7.3.112). [The suffix *ṅe* becomes *āṅ* after a *nadī* stem. Thus: *matyai* or *mataye*; *matyāḥ* or *mateḥ*. When the *nadī* designation applies, the rule *aut* (A 7.3.118) would require *aut* for the suffix *ṅi*. However: SK 297 *idudbhyām* (A 7.3.117): [The suffix *ṅi* becomes *am*] after stems ending in *i* or *u*. [Thus: *matyām* or *mataḥ*.]

After [stems] ending in *i* or *u* that are designated as *nadī*, the replacement *ām* shall occur for the following *ṅi*; optionally, *at* shall also replace the *ghi* stem. Thus: *matyām* or *matau*. Similarly, *śruti*, *spṛti*, and so forth. SK 298: *tricaturor striyāṃ tisṛcatasṛ* (A 7.2.99).
When these two, *tri* and *catur*, are feminine, these two replacements—*tisṛ* and *catasṛ*—occur when a case-ending (*vibhakti*) follows.

SK 299 *aci ra ṛtaḥ* (A 7.2.100): In place of the *ṛ*-vowel of *tisṛ* and *catasṛ*, the substitute *ra* shall occur before a vowel (*ac*). This is an exception to [the application of] *guṇa*, *dīrgha*, and *utva*. Examples: *tisraḥ* (2). Before the suffix *ām*, by the rule *num aci ra ṛtaḥ*, the augment *nuṭ* is added.
SK 300 *na tisṛcatasṛ* (A 6.4.4).

The *nābh* (the substitution of *n* for *t*) shall not occur for these two [words] when they are long; nor shall it occur for three [words] among the three [cases]. Because the word *striyām* ("in the feminine") is a qualifier for the [numbers] three and four, it does not apply here: *priyāstrayastrīṇi vā yasyāḥ sā priyatriḥ*, like *mati*. However, in the case of the genitive plural (*āmi*), there is a distinction: *priyatrayāṇām*. But in the analysis (*vigraha*) "that which has three beloved women," it is *priyatisā*, *priyatisrau*, *priyatisraḥ*, *priyatisram*, and so forth. When [the compound] is "that family which has three beloved women," it is *priyatri*.

Because the case endings *su* and *am* are elided by *luk*, the condition for the application of suffixal markers (*pratyayalakṣaṇa*) does not exist, and thus the substitution of *tisṛ* does not occur. However, because the prohibition "na lumatā" (P. 1.1.63) is not universally valid (*anitya*), there is optionally the form *priyatisṛ*. By the rule of prior contradiction (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*), *num* is applied before the substitution of *r*. Thus: *priyatisṛṇī*; *priyatisṛṇe*. In the third case and onwards, due to the optional application of the masculine form (*puṃvadbhāva*) which will be explained later, there is an alternation between the presence and absence of *num*: *priyatisrā*; *priyatisṛṇā*, and so forth. When the feminine suffix *āp* is added after the substitution of *at* for *dvi*, we have: *dve* (2); *dvābhyām* (3); *dvayoḥ* (2). *Gaurī*.

*gaurī*, *gauryau*, *gauryaḥ*; the grammatical operations of a river-name (*nadī*) apply: *he gauri*, *gauryai*, and so forth. Likewise for *vāṇī*, *nadī*, and others. Since the mention of a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) includes its gender-distinct form (*liṅgaviśiṣṭa*), both the substitution of *anaṅ* and the treatment as a *ṇit* stem (causing *vṛddhi*) would apply; however, there is no inclusion of the gender-distinct form when a case-ending (*vibhakti*) follows. Thus: *sakhī*, *sakhyau*, *sakhyaḥ*, etc., like *gaurī*. Because it ends in the suffix *aṅ*, there is no elision of the nominative singular suffix (*su*). *lakṣmīḥ*; the rest is like *gaurī*. Likewise for *tarī*, *tantrī*, and others. *strī*, *he strī*. [The rule] *striyāḥ* (A 6.4.79).
The substitution *iyaṅ* occurs for the word *strī* when followed by a suffix beginning with a vowel. Thus: *striyau*, *striyaḥ*.
[Pāṇini 6.4.80] *vām śasoḥ*.

In the case of the word *strī* (woman), *iyaṅ* may optionally replace the final vowel before the suffixes *ami* and *śas*. Thus: *striyam* or *strīm*; *striyau*; *striyaḥ* or *strīḥ*. [The forms] *striyā*, *striyai*, and *striyāḥ* [are derived regularly]. Before the genitive plural suffix, *nuṭ* is inserted because it is of higher priority: *strīṇām*. [The forms] *striyām* and *striyoḥ* [are regular]. [The form] *strīṣu* [is regular]. One who has surpassed a woman is *atistriḥ*. [The forms] *atistriyau* [and *atistriyaḥ* follow]. It should be understood that for the word *strī*, *iyaṅ* is applied [in the masculine], as it is overridden by *guṇa*, the absence of *nābhāva*, *autva*, and *nuṭ* due to their higher priority; and in the neuter, it is overridden by *num*. [In the nominative plural] *jasi*, [the form is] *atistrayaḥ*.

*He atistre*, *he atistriyau*, *he atistrayaḥ*. [In the case of the suffix] *vāmśasi*: *atistriyam*, *atistrim*; *atistriyau*; *atistrīn*. *Atistriyaḥ*. *Atistriṇā*. By the rule *gher ṅiti*: *atistraye*; *atistreḥ* (two instances); *atistriyaḥ* (two instances); *atistrīṇām*. By the rule *acca gheḥ*: *atistrau*. In the case of *osi* and *aukāra*, the substitution of *iy* should always occur; however, it is optional in the case of *am* and *śas*. In the case of a feminine stem ending in *i*, the substitution of *iy* occurs before a vowel (*ac*) and not elsewhere. In the neuter, however, there is the augment *num*: *atistri*.

*atistriṇī*, *atistrīṇi*, *atistriṇā*, *atistriṇe*. From the *ṅe*-case onwards, in the beginning of vowel-initial suffixes, because of the upcoming rule for *puṃvadbhāva* (masculine-like behavior), the form is optionally as before; thus: *atistraye*, *atistriṇaḥ* (two), *atistreḥ* (two), *atistriṇoḥ*, *atistriyoḥ*, and so forth. In the feminine, however, it is generally like the masculine. In the *śas*-case: *atistrīḥ*. In the *ṅi*-case: *atistriyā*. Regarding the rule "and when a *ṅit* [suffix follows]," there is an option based on the fact that the stem ends in a short vowel. However, the prohibition "not *strī*" is an exclusion (*paryudāsa*) specifically of the rule concerning those stems that occupy the position of *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ*.

Since this [substitution] recurs only for that which is connected with it, this prohibition applies to the long vowel and not to the short one. Thus: *atistriyai*, *atistraye*; *atistriyāḥ* (genitive), *atistreḥ* (ablative); *atistrīṇām* (genitive plural); *atistriyām* (locative), *atistrau* (locative). *Śrīḥ*, *śriyau*, *śriyaḥ*. Pāṇini A 1.4.4 states:

*neyaṅuvaṅsthānāv astrī* ("Those [stems] ending in *ī* or *ū* which do not stand in the place of *iyaṅ* or *uvaṅ* are called *nadī*, except for the word *strī*"). Those two vowels *ī* and *ū* which remain as they are (*sthiti*) when *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ* substitutions would otherwise apply are designated as *nadī*, but not the word *strī*. Therefore: *he śrīḥ* (vocative); *śriye* (dative), *śriyai*; *śriyāḥ* (genitive), *śriyaḥ* (ablative).

SK 304 (*vāmi*): Feminine nouns ending in *ī* or *ū* that take the substitutes *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ* optionally receive the designation *nadī* before the genitive plural suffix *ām*, but not when they denote the feminine gender itself. Examples: *śrīṇām* or *śriyām*; *śriyi* or *śriyām*. However, according to the opinion of the Vṛttikāra and others, the word *pradhī* has forms like *lakṣmī*. This is because they accept that "constant femininity" (*nityastrītva*) consists in denoting the feminine even without another word [to qualify it]. According to Kaiyaṭa’s view, however, where there is no expression of another gender, it takes forms like the masculine. But in the analysis (*vigraha*) as *prakṛṣṭā dhīḥ* ("excellent intellect"), it follows the form of *lakṣmī*.

The distinction lies in the fact that *ami* and *śasi* are followed by *pradhyaṃ pradhya*. However, in the analysis (*vigraha*) as "one whose intellect (*dhī*) is excellent" (*suṣṭhu*) or "who meditates well" (*suṣṭhu dhyāyati*), according to the view of the *vṛtti*, *sudhīḥ* is like *śrī*; according to another opinion, it is like the masculine. But in the analysis as "excellent intellect" (*suṣṭhu dhīḥ*), it is like *śrī*. *Grāmaṇīḥ* is like the masculine; because leading a village is generally a male function, it does not apply to the feminine without another word [to qualify it]. In the same way, it should be understood that activities such as threshing grain (*khalapavana*) are also generally male functions. *Dhenuḥ* is like *mati*. (SK 305) And [the rule] *striyāṃ ca* (A 7.1.93).
The word *kroṣṭu*, when denoting a female, takes a form like that ending in the suffix *tṛ*;
[according to] Pāṇini 4.1.5: *ṛnnebhyo ṅīp*.

The suffix *ṅīp* shall be applied in the feminine after stems ending in *ṛ* and those ending in *n*. *kroṣṭrī*, *kroṣṭryau*, *kroṣṭryaḥ*. *Vadhū* is like *gaurī*. *Bhrūḥ* is like *śrī*: *he subhrūḥ*. How then is it that Bhaṭṭi says, "Alas, father! Where are you, O fair-browed one" (*hā pitaḥ kvāsi he subhru*)? Many say this is simply an error. *Khalapūḥ* is like the masculine. *Punarbhūḥ*. Because [the rule] *dṛnkara-* prescribes *yaṇ* and thereby blocks *uvaṅ*, the prohibition regarding *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ* does not apply: *he punarbhu*, *punarbhvam*, *punarbhvau*, *punarbhvaḥ*. SK 307: When the subsequent member of a compound consists of a single vowel, the substitution of *ṇ* [for the final consonant of the preceding member] is applied. (A 8.4.12)

In a compound consisting of one syllable more than one word, there shall be obligatory *ṇatva* (the substitution of *ṇ* for *n*) for the *n* situated at the end of a nominal stem (*prātipadika*), in the suffixes *num* or case-endings (*vibhakti*), following a cause (*nimitta*) located in the first member (*pūrvapada*). Although the obligatoriness is already established by the very fact of this rule's commencement, the explicit mention of *ṇa* again is for the sake of clarity. Because it is subsequent (*paratva*), the augment *nuṭ* supersedes the *yaṇ* [substitution]. Examples: *punarbhūṇām*; *varṣābhūḥ*. According to Kaiyaṭa’s view, in the case of the frog species (*bhekajāti*), because it lacks constant feminine gender (*nityastrītva*), the vocative is *he varṣābhūḥ*; however, according to other views, it is *he varṣābhu*.

Regarding *punarnavā*, there are two [forms]: *varṣābhū* and *bhekī*. Yādava states: "In the case of *punarnavā*, it is *varṣābhū* when feminine; in the case of a frog, it is *durdura* when masculine. [The forms are: *varṣābhvau*, *varṣābhvaḥ*. *Svayaṃbhū* is like the masculine.
(SK 308) Not [the addition of *ṅīp* occurs] after the six [beginning with *svasṛ*], nor after *svasṛ* and so on. (A 4.1.10)

The suffixes *ṅīp* and *ṭāp* do not occur after those [stems] designated as having six [vowels] (*ṣat-saṃjñaka*) nor after *svasṛ* and the others. *Svasṛ*, *tisṛ*, *catasṛ*, *nanāndṛ*, *duhitṛ*, *yātṛ*, and *mātṛ*—these seven are cited as beginning with *svasṛ*. [In *svasṛ*,] the vowel is long by the rule *aptṛn*. *Svasā*, *svasārau*, *svasāraḥ*. *Mātṛ* is like *pitṛ*. In the *śas* [case], *mātṝḥ*. *Div* is like *go*. *Rai* is like masculine [stems]. *Nau* is like *glau*. This concludes the section on feminine stems ending in vowels. Now begins the section on neuter stems ending in vowels.

SK 309 *ato 'm* (A 7.1.24): After this neuter stem, *am* shall be substituted for the nominative-accusative dual suffixes (*svamoḥ*). By the rule *ami pūrvaḥ*, [the preceding vowel and *am*] become a single substitute. Thus: *jñānam*. By the rule *eṅhrasvāt*, there is elision of the mere consonant (*hal-mātra*) [of the vocative suffix]. Thus: *he jñāna*. SK 310 *napuṃsakāc ca* (A 7.1.19): [The substitution of *śi* for the nominative-accusative plural occurs] after a neuter [stem].
After a neuter stem, *au* becomes *śī* [before a case-ending]. In the context of the designation *bha*:

by A 6.4.148 (*yasyeti ca*), there would be elision of the vowels *i* and *u* when a *taddhita* suffix beginning with *ī* follows. Since this would result in the elision of the vowel *a*, it must be stated that this elision is prohibited before the ending *auṅ* changed to *śī*. [Thus: *jñāne*.
SK 312 *jaśśasoḥ śiḥ* (A 7.1.20): After a neuter [stem], *śi* shall be substituted for these two (*jas* and *śas*). SK 313 *śi sarvanāmasthānam* (A 1.1.42): *Śi* is a *sarvanāmasthāna*.
The term *śi* shall have the designation [of *sarvanāmasthāna*] as previously stated.

(Pāṇini 7.1.72) *napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ*: the augment *num* is added to a neuter stem ending in a *jhal* consonant or in *ac*, when a *sarvanāmasthāna* follows. There is lengthening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhādīrghaḥ*). Thus: *jñānāni*. Before that, it is like that; the remainder is like *rāma*. In the same way are *dhanavat*, *naphala*, and so forth.
SK 315: *addḍḍatarādibhyaḥ pañcamyaḥ* (A 7.1.25). After these neuter words, there shall be the substitution of *adḍ* for the nominative and accusative singular endings (*su* and *am*).
SK 316: *ṭeḥ* (A 6.4.143). [The final phoneme] of the stem (*aṅga*) ending in *ṭi* is elided.

When a *ḍit* suffix follows, there is elision (*lopa*) of the final phoneme (*ṭi*) of a *bha*-stem. Examples: *vācasāne*, *katarat*, *katarad*, *katare*, *katarāṇi*. Why "of a *bha*-stem"?
