[Consider] *pañcamaḥ*; because the final phoneme has been elided, the substitution of the long vowel homogeneous with the preceding one (*pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*) does not occur, nor does the elision of the vocative suffix (*saṃbuddhilopa*) by the rule *eṅhrasvāt*. Thus: *he katarat*. Again, it is like that. The remainder is like the masculine (*puṃvat*). Examples: *katamat*, *anyat*, *anyatarat*, *itarat*. However, for the word *anyatama*, it remains simply *anyatamam*.

One or the other [alternative] must be rejected. [Consider: *ekatarām*. When the substitution of *am* for the nominative-accusative singular ending (*su*) has been applied, *jaras* does not occur due to the *saṃnipāta-paribhāṣā* (the rule that a grammatical operation caused by a specific configuration does not apply when that configuration is destroyed). Thus: *ajaram*, *ajarasī*, *ajare*. However, because the suffix *jaras* applies later [in the order of rules], and because the stem ends in a *jhal* consonant, the augment *num* is inserted [before the case-ending]. This is governed by A 6.4.10: *sāntamahataḥ saṃyogasya*.

In the presence of a *sarvanāmasthāna* case ending other than the vocative (*saṃbuddhi*), there shall be a long vowel for the penultimate (*upadhā*) of the syllable containing the letter *n*, provided that this *n* follows a conjunct consonant (*saṃyoga*) or the word *mahat*. [Examples: *ajarāṃsi* / *ajarāṇi*. In the case of the accusative singular ending *am*, the substitution of *jaras* occurs by virtue of its higher priority (*paratva*), overriding both the elision (*luk*) and the substitution of *ambhāva*. Consequently, due to the *saṃnipāta-paribhāṣā*, there is no elision. [Thus: *ajarasam* / *ajaram* / *ajarasī* / *ajare* / *ajarāṃsi* / *ajarāṇi*. The remainder is like the masculine. According to the rule *paddanno...* (Pāṇini 6.1.63), the words *hṛdaya*, *udaka*, and *āsya* become *hṛd*, *udan*, and *āsan* respectively. [Examples: *hṛndi* / *hṛdā*.

*hṛdbhyām* and so forth; *udāni*, *udgā*, *udabhyām* and so forth; *āsāni*, *āsnā*, *āsabhyām* and so forth; *māṃsi*, *māṃsā*, *mānbhyām* and so forth. In reality, however, it has been stated that the mention of "starting with" (*prabhṛti*) is for the sake of indicating the type [of forms]. For this very reason, the *Bhāṣya* cites *māṃspacanyā ukhāyāḥ* ("the pot for cooking meat") as an example. Because it is a *bha*-stem by virtue of belonging to the *ayasmaya*-class, there is no elision of the final consonant of the conjunction (*saṃyogāntalopa*).

Regarding the term *paddanna* here, one should understand that words such as *pada* and others may be employed even in common usage (*loke*), following the method stated by Kaiyaṭa: that by the force of the inclusion of the word "Vedic" (*chandasi*) in the Vārttika *māsaśchandasī*, they occur occasionally even in worldly usage.

SK 318: *hrasvo napuṃsake prātipadikasya* (A 1.2.47). In the neuter gender, there shall be a short vowel for a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) ending in a long vowel. Examples: *śrīpam*, *jñānavat*. [In the dative case: *śrīpāya*. Here, by the *saṃnipātaparibhāṣā* (the technical rule regarding the non-destruction of a cause), the elision of the final *ā* of the root prescribed by *āto dhātoḥ* does not take place.
SK 319 *svamor napuṃsakāt* (A 7.1.23): After a neuter base (*aṅga*), there is elision (*luk*) of the nominative-accusative singular suffixes (*su* and *am*). Example: *vāri*.
SK 320 *iko 'ci vibhaktau* (A 7.1.73): [The substitution of *yaṇ* for an *ik* vowel occurs] before a case-ending (*vibhakti*) beginning with a vowel (*ac*).

The augment *num* is applied to a neuter stem ending in a vowel before a case-ending beginning with a vowel. Thus: *vāriṇī*, *vāriṇi*. Because the prohibition "not when [an affix] marked by *lu*" (*na lumatā*) is not absolute, the guna substitution caused by the vocative occurs optionally: *he vāre*, *he vāri*. Before the suffix *āṅ* (the instrumental singular), *nā* is substituted: *vāriṇā*. When the rule "guṇa for a *ghi* stem before an affix marked by *ṅ*" (*gher ṅiti*) would apply, *num* takes precedence by prior contradiction (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*) over the rules for *vṛddhi*, the substitution of *aut*, the *tṛjvadbhāva*, and *guṇa*. Thus: *vāriṇe*, *vāriṇaḥ*, *vāriṇoḥ*. Before endings beginning with a consonant, the *nuṭ* augment is added by the rule "after a stem ending in *num* or *aciḥ*" (*numacira-*) etc. It is treated like *hari* (as in the consonant-initial forms). SK 321: In the third case and those following, a neuter stem that has a corresponding masculine form is optionally treated like the masculine according to Gālava’s view (*tṛtīyādiṣu bhāṣitapuṃskaṃ puṃvadgālavasya*).

When the cause of application (*pravṛttinimitta*) is identical, a neuter word ending in *i* or *u* that has been used in the masculine may optionally take the masculine form before endings beginning with *ṭa* followed by a vowel. For example: *anādaye* or *anādine*, and so forth. The remainder is like the word *vāri*. The word *pīlu* refers to the tree; its fruit is also called *pīlu*. In the expression *tasmai pīlune* ("to that pīlu [fruit]"), there is no masculine substitution because the cause of application differs.
SK 322: *asthidadhisakthyakṣṇām anaṅ udāttaḥ* (A 7.1.75). [In the neuter, for *asthi*, *dadhi*, *sakthi*, and *akṣi*, the substitute *anaṅ* is applied, and it is acute-accented.]

For these [words ending in *an*], *anaṅ* is substituted when followed by a case-ending beginning with *ṭ* or a vowel, and that [substitute] is udātta. There is elision (*allopa*) of the *an*. *dadhnā*, *dadhne*, *dadhnaḥ* (2), *dadhnoḥ* (2), *dadhi*, *dadhani*; the remainder is like *vāri*. Similarly for *asthi*, *sakthi*, and *akṣi*. *Anaṅ* is also substituted for those ending in such [words]. *atidadhnā* (from *atidadhan*). *sudhi*, *sudhinī*, *sudhīni*; *he sudhe*; *sudhinā*. *pradhyā*, *pradhinā*. *madhu*, *madhunī*, *madhūni*; *he madho*, *he madhu*. Similarly for *ambu* and others. For the word *sānu*, *snu* is optionally substituted.

*snūni*, *sānūni*; *priyakroṣṭu*, *priyakroṣṭunī*. By the application of the *tṛj-vat* rule, *num* occurs by way of prior contradiction (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*): *priyakroṣṭūni*. In the case of suffixes beginning with *ṭa*, when there is the option of treating [the word] like the masculine (*puṃvat*), one has *priyakroṣṭrā* or *priyakroṣṭunā*; *priyakroṣṭre* or *priyakroṣṭave*. In other cases, by the application of the *tṛj-vat* rule, *num* alone occurs by way of prior contradiction: *priyakroṣṭunā*, *priyakroṣṭune*. By the rule *num-acira-*, it is again the same: *sulvā*, *suluvā*, *sulunā*. *dhātṛ*, *dhātṛṇī*, *dhātṝṇi*.
*he dhātaḥ*, *he dhātṛ*, *dhātrā*, *dhātṛbhiḥ*; likewise for *jñātṛ*, *kartṛ*, and others.
A 1.1.48 states: "In place of an *ec* vowel, an *it* vowel is substituted when a short vowel is prescribed."

When short vowels are being prescribed, only *ig* (short *i*, *u*, or *ṛ*) should be understood. For example: *pradyu*, *pradyunī*, *pradyūni*, *pradyune*, and so on. Here, there is no *puṃvat* (masculine-like) substitution because *pradyu*, which ends in *ig*, lacks the quality of having been previously mentioned as masculine (*bhāṣitapuṃska*). Similarly, later on: *prari*, *prariṇi*, *prariṇā*. Because that which is modified in one part is not different from the original, the substitution of *ā* for *rāy-* occurs before a consonant (*hali*), resulting in *prarābhyāt* and *prarābhiḥ*. Regarding *prarāṇām*, Mādhava maintains that the *num* augment and the substitution of *ā* apply according to the rule *numacira-*.

In reality, however, by the technical rule (*paribhāṣā*) regarding the meeting [of sounds], the *nuṭ* augment does not trigger the substitution of *ā*. It has been stated that the lengthening prescribed by the rule *nāmi* overrides the technical rule due to the force of its specific formulation. Examples include: *prarīṇām*, *sunu*, *sununī*, *sunūni*, *sununā*, *sunune*, and so forth.
Thus ends the section on neuter nouns ending in vowels. Now begins the section on masculine nouns ending in consonants (11).

SK 324 *ho ḍhaḥ* (A 8.2.31): After the sound *h*, *ḍha* shall be substituted [for *h*] before a *jhal* consonant and at the end of a word. By the rule *halṅyābbhyaḥ* (A 6.1.68), there is elision of the case-ending *su*. Because it is at the end of a word, *ḍha* is substituted for *h*. Then the substitutions of *jaśtva* and *cartva* apply. [The forms of the root *lih* are: *liṭ*, *liḍ*; *lihaḥ*, *liham*; *lihau*, *lihaḥ*; *lihā*, *liḍbhyām*; *liṭsu*, *liṭsu*. SK 325 *dāder dhātor ghaḥ* (A 8.2.32): After a root beginning with *da* or *dh*, *gha* is substituted [for *ha*].

In the original formative instruction (*upadeśa*), the *h* of a root beginning with *d* shall be replaced by *gh*, before an affix beginning with a *jhal* consonant and at the end of a word. Why specify "in the original formative instruction"? [To ensure it applies] as in the case of *adhog-i* here; [otherwise, one might think it would not apply]. One desires for oneself a *dāmaliha* (a horse that licks the halter), thus *dāmalihyati*. From this, with the *kvip* suffix, we have *dāmaliṭ*. Here [the substitution] must not occur. [This is governed by] Pāṇini 8.2.37: *ekāco baśo bhaṣ jhaṣantasya sdhvoḥ* ("In place of a *baś* sound belonging to a monosyllabic root ending in a *jhaṣ* sound, there is *bhaṣ* before the suffixes *s* and *dhv*").

In place of *baś* that is part of a one-syllable verbal root (*dhātu*) ending in a *jhaṣ* consonant, there shall be *bhaṣ* when followed by the sound *s*, the word *dhva*, or at the end of a word (*padānta*). However, if the phrase "of a one-syllable root" were construed in grammatical apposition (*sāmānādhikaraṇya*), this rule would not apply here: *gardabham ācaṣṭe* → *gardabhayati*; from that, *kvip* [is added]; [then] the elision of *ṇi* [occurs], resulting in *dardhab*. [The condition] *jhalī* has ceased to apply, due to the force of the inclusion of *sdhvoh* [in the rule]. Therefore, it does not apply here: *dugdham*, *dogdhā*. Because it is considered a part of the root by virtue of being designated as such (*vyapadeśivadbhāva*), the *bhaṣ*-substitution occurs: *dhukṣu*. SK 327: *vā druhamuhaṣṇuhaṣṇihām* (A 8.2.33). [This rule states that for the roots *druh*, *muha*, *ṣṇuh*, and *ṣṇih*, the *bhaṣ*-substitution is optional.]

For these [roots], *gh* may optionally replace *h* before a *jhal* consonant and at the end of a word; alternatively, *ḍh* may be substituted. Thus: *dhruk*, *dhrug*; *dhruṭ*, *dhruḍ*; *druhau*; *druhaḥ*; *dhrugbhyām*, *dhruṅbhyām*; *dhrukṣu*, *dhruṭtsu*, *dhruṭsu*. The same applies to *muh*, *ṣṇuh*, and *ṣṇih*. *viśvāṭ*, *viśvāḍ*; *viśvavāhau*; *viśvavāhaḥ*; *viśvavāham*; *viśvavāhau*. SK 328: *igyaṇaḥ saṃprasāraṇam* (A 1.1.45).
An *iK* vowel that is employed in place of a *yaṇ* [consonant] shall bear the technical designation *saṃprasāraṇa*.
SK 329 *vāha ūṭh* (A 6.4.133): For the word *vāh*, when it is a *bha*-stem, the semivowel substitution (*saṃprasāraṇa*) becomes *ūṭh*.
SK 330 *saṃprasāraṇāc ca* (A 3.1.108).

When a vowel follows a *saṃprasāraṇa*, there shall be a single substitute in the form of the preceding sound. [This applies] before *eti*, *edhati*, and *ūṭh*. Examples: *viśvauhaḥ*, *viśvauhaḥ*, and so forth. According to the view that the suffix *ṇvi* occurs only in the Veda, [the forms are derived] from the causative (*ṇijanta*) of the root *vac*. SK 331: *caturanaḍuhorām udāttaḥ* (A 7.1.98).
The augment *ām* is added to these two [stems, *catur* and *anaḍuh*], in the place of a nominal ending (*sarvanāmasthāna*), and that [augment] is acute-accented (*udātta*).

SK 332 (*sāvanaḍuhaḥ*, A 7.1.82): The augment *num* shall be added to this [stem *anaḍuh*] when followed by the nominative singular suffix *su*. Because of the governing rule [from A 7.1.70] beginning with "ādi" (*ād*), this *num* follows after a vowel (*a*). Therefore, the *ām* [of A 7.1.94] is not superseded by the *num* even though the latter is prescribed as a specific rule; likewise, the *num* is not superseded by the *ām*. The *su* is elided. Due to the force of the rule prescribing *num*, the substitution of *da* [for *t*] as in *vasusraṃsu* (A 7.1.70) does not apply. Because the elision of the final consonant of the conjunct (*saṃyogāntalopa*) is considered non-existent (*asiddha*), the elision of the *n* [by A 6.4.24] does not apply. Thus: *anaḍvān*. SK 333 (*am saṃbuddhau*, A 7.1.99): [The suffix *su* is replaced by] *am* in the vocative case.

In the vocative case, *anaḍuh* takes the suffix *-auram*; this is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *-ām*. *he anaṅvan*, *anaḍvāhau*, *anaḍvāhaḥ*. *anaḍuhā*. By Pāṇini 8.2.72, *vasusraṃsudhva�svanaḍuhāṃ daḥ*:

after a word ending in *s* (including those ending in *vasu*), after *sraṃsu*, *dhvaṃsu*, and *anaḍuh*, the letter *d* is substituted [for the final consonant] at the end of a word (*padānte*). Examples include *anaḍudbhyām*, and so forth. Why is it specified "ending in *s*" (*sānta*)? Consider *vidvān* (where the *s* is not part of the stem-final). Why is it specified "at the end of a word" (*padānte*)? Consider *srastam* and *dhvastam* (where the substitution does not apply because they are not at the end of a word).

SK 335 *saheḥ sāḍaḥ saḥ* (A 8.3.56): For the *s* of the root *sah-* when it has the form *sāḍ*, there shall be a cerebral substitute (*mūrdhanya*). Thus: *turāṣāṭ*, *turāṣāḍ*, *turāsāhau*, *turāsāhaḥ*, *turāṣāḍbhyām*, and so forth. In the sense of "one who endures force" (*turaṃ sahate*), the suffix *ṇvi* is applied to *saha-* in the Vedic language (*chandasi*). In common usage (*loke*), however, the suffix *kvip* is applied to *sāhayati*. The lengthening of the preceding vowel occurs by the rule *anyeṣām api*. SK 336 *diva aut* (A 7.1.84): [The substitution of] *aut* [occurs] for *div*.

The substitution of *au* occurs for the nominal stem *div* when followed by the nominative singular suffix *su*. Because this is not a rule governed by an *al* (vowel), the status of being a *sthānivat* does not apply; therefore, the elision of *su* by the rule *halṅyābbhyaḥ* does not take place. Thus: *sudyauḥ*, *sudivau*, *sudivaḥ*, *sudivam*, *sudivau*. By the rule *diva ut* (A 6.1.131), the final letter of *div* is replaced by the vowel *u* at the end of a word. Thus: *sudyubhyām*, *sudyubhiḥ*. [The forms of] *catur* are: *catvāraḥ*, *caturaḥ*, *caturbhiḥ*, *caturbhyaḥ*.

SK 338: *ṣaṭracaturbhyaś ca* (A 7.1.55). After words designated as *ṣaṣ* and after *catur*, the augment *nuṭ* is added to the following case-ending *ām*. [In *catur + ām*,] there is the substitution of *ṇ* for *n*, and then doubling [of the *n*]. Thus: *caturṇṇām*. SK 339: *roḥ supi* (A 8.3.16). [The rule concerning the substitution of *ru* for *repha* applies when a *sup* suffix follows.]

When the seventh case plural (*saptamī-bahuvacana*) follows, the *visarjanīya* occurs only for the *ru* [of *catur*] and not for any other *repha*. [Then] the substitution of *ṣ* [occurs]. When the doubling of *ṣ* would otherwise apply, [Pāṇini’s rule] A 8.4.49 states: *śaro 'ci*—"Before a vowel (*aci*), the *śara* [consonants] do not become doubled. Thus: *caturṣu*, *priyacatvāḥ*, *he priyacatvaḥ*, *priyacatvārau*, *priyacatvāraḥ*. However, when [the word *catur*] is secondary (*gauṇatva*), the insertion of *nuṭ* is not desired; thus: *priyacaturām*. But when it is primary (*prādhānya*), it must indeed occur: *paramacaturṇām*. [The word] *kamal*, meaning "one who speaks of a lotus (*kamalaṃ*)" or "a lotus (*kamalāṃ*)" [is declined as]: *kamalau*, *kamalaḥ*. The substitution of *ṣ* occurs: *kamalaṣu*.

SK 341: *mo no dhātoḥ* (A 8.2.64). In place of the *m* of a verbal root (*dhātu*), there shall be *n* at the end of a word (*padānte*). Because the substitution of *n* for *m* is considered asiddha (non-existent for the purposes of subsequent rules), the elision of *n* (*nalopa*) does not occur. Thus, from the root *śam*, we have *praśān* (as in *praśāmyati*); *praśāmau*; *praśāmaḥ*; *praśānbhyām*, and so forth.
SK 342: *kimaḥ kaḥ* (A 7.2.103). In place of *kim*, there is *ka*.

*Kim-ah kaḥ su-ād vibhaktau*: After *kim*, when followed by the nominative singular suffix *su*, the substitute *kaḥ* is applied. This substitution applies even to *kim* when accompanied by the *akac* suffix. Thus: *kaḥ*, *kau*, *ke*; *kam*, *kau*, *kān*, and so forth, following the paradigm of *sarva*. *Idamo maḥ* (A 7.2.108):

When the nominative singular suffix *su* follows, the final phoneme of *idam* is replaced by *m*. This is an exception to the rule for the substitution of *yat* (the *tyadādyatva* change). Thus: *ayam*.

SK 344 *ido 'y puṃsi* (A 7.2.111): In the masculine, *idam* becomes *aya* before the nominative singular suffix *su*. [The rule] *sor lopaḥ* applies; then there is the substitution of *yatva* for the *tyad*-class stems and the substitution of the subsequent form (*pararūpatva*). SK 345 *daś ca* (A 7.2.109): [The *yatva* substitution occurs] also when followed by a *d*-sound.

In place of the *d* of *idam*, *ma* shall be substituted when followed by a case-ending (*vibhakti*). [Examples: *imau*, *ime*. It is a general rule (*utsarga*) that there is no vocative for words beginning with *tyad* and so forth. By A 7.2.112, *anāpyakaḥ*: in place of the *id* of *idam*, *an* shall be substituted before case-endings beginning with *āp* (the letter *ā*). The term *āp* is a pratyāhāra (abbreviated designation) formed from the letter *ā* in *ṭā* up to the letter *p* in *sup*. [Example: *anena*.

SK 347 *hali lopaḥ* (A 7.2.113): The *id-* of *idam*, when not followed by the letter *ka*, is elided even before a consonant-initial [suffix]. Regarding non-meaningful elements (*anarthaka*), the rule concerning the final letter of a stem does not apply, except in the case of modifications to a reduplicated syllable (*anabhyāsavikāra*).
SK 348 *ādyantavadekasmin* (A 1.1.21): With respect to a single entity, operations apply as if it were both the beginning and the end.
An operation performed upon one [element] should be regarded as having occurred both at the beginning and at the end. [From the word *idam*: **SK 349**: *nedamadasorakoḥ* (A 7.1.11).

For *idam* and *adas*, when they do not have the suffix *kakāra*, the substitution of *ais* for *bhisa* does not take place. [Instead, the following substitutions apply: The substitution of *etva* (change to *e*) occurs: *ebhiḥ*. The substitution of *atva* (change to *a*) occurs: *ebhiḥ*. Because it is a permanent rule (*nityatva*), the substitution of *smai* for *ṅe* occurs first; subsequently, there is the elision of the *hali* (consonant) portion: *asmai*. [From *idam* with dual endings: *ābhyām*. [With plural endings: *ebhyaḥ*. [With ablative singular: *asmāt*. [With dual: *ābhyām*. [With plural: *ebhyaḥ*. [With genitive singular: *asya*. [With dual: *anayoḥ*. [With plural: *eṣām*. [With locative singular: *asmin*. [With dual: *anayoḥ*. [With plural: *eṣu*. However, when there is the connection with the suffix *kakāra*, [the forms are]: *ayakam*, *imakau*, *imake*; *imakam*, *imakau*, *imakān*; *imakena*, *imakābhyām*, *imakaiḥ*.

SK 350: *idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudāttas tṛtīyādau* (A 2.4.32). In the context of a subsequent reference (*anvādeśa*), the enclitic *aś*, which is unaccented (*anudātta*), is the substitute for *idam* when followed by the third case and those that follow. This substitution of *aś* occurs when the third case and subsequent cases are present. The mention of *aś* is for the sake of including the form with the *k* suffix (*sākacka*). SK 351: *dvitīyāṭaussvena* (A 2.4.34). [The substitute *enad* is applied to *idam*] when followed by the second case endings and the nominative-accusative dual endings (*ṭaus*).

In the case of the second [pronoun], when followed by the dual endings *ṭā* and *ṅasi* (i.e., *bhyām* and *bhyas*), the substitutes *ena-* for *idam* and *etad* occur in the sense of *anvādeśa*. *Anvādeśa* is the re-mention of something already employed to prescribe a certain operation, in order to prescribe another operation; for example: "He has studied grammar; teach him prosody," or "The lineage of these two is pure; the wealth of these two is abundant. [The forms are: *enam*, *enau*, *enān*; *enena*, *enayoḥ*. From the root *gaṇayati* with the suffix *vic*: *sugaṇ* ("one who counts well"). *sugaṇ*, *sugaṇau*, *sugaṇaḥ*; *sugaṇṭhsu*.

*sugaṇ-su* / *sugaṇ-su* / [with] *kvip* [suffix], there is lengthening by the rule *anunāsikasya kvijhaloḥ*. *sugāṇ*, *sugāṇ-au*, *sugāṇ-aḥ*, *sugāṇ-ṭh-su*, *sugāṇ-ṭ-su*, *sugāṇ-su*. Because it is subsequent, there is lengthening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhādīrghaḥ*). Then, elision of the consonant and following vowels (*halṅyādilopaḥ*). After that, elision of the *n* (*nalopaḥ*). Thus: *rājā*. By the rule *na ṅisaṃbuddhyoḥ* (A 8.2.8).

The elision [of *an*] should not occur before the locative singular ending (*ṅi*) or in the vocative (*saṃbuddhi*). Examples for the locative (*ṅi*) are found in Vedic: *rājan*. Here, the elision of the case-ending (*ṅeḥ luk*) occurs by the rule *supāṃ suluk*. Due to the force of this prohibition, the presence of the suffix is still recognized (*pratyayalakṣaṇa*), as in *parame vyoman*. A prohibition must be stated when the locative ending is part of a compound (*uttarapada*): *carmaṇi tilā asya* → *carmatilaḥ*; *brahmaṇi niṣṭhā asya* → *brahmaniṣṭhaḥ*. In *rājānau*, *rājānaḥ*, *rājānam*, and *rājānau*, the *an* is elided (*alloponaḥ*), followed by the substitution of the sibilant (*ścutvam*). Nor is this elision (*al-lopa*) treated as if it were still present (*sthānivat*).

Because that [rule] is prohibited where a preceding rule is *asiddha*. Nor can it be argued that the *paribhāṣā* does not apply because the substitution of *ścu* (*ś*, *c*, *u*) is *asiddha*, resulting in the absence of an *antaraṅga* operation; for in *ajor jñaḥ* (P. 7.2.61), as in *rājñaḥ* and *rājñā*, the elision of *n* (*nalopaḥ*) applies by A 8.2.2: "The elision of *n* occurs before a case-ending (*sup*), in rules concerning accent (*svara*), technical names (*saṃjñā*), and the introduction of *tuṭ* or *kṛt* suffixes."

The elision of *n* (nalopa) is considered non-existent (*asiddha*) with respect to the rules for vowels (*svaravidhi*), technical designations (*saṃjñāvidhi*), and the application of the suffix *kṛt* and the augment *tuṅ*; but not in other cases, such as in "rājāśva" and the like. Because of this non-existence, the substitution of *āt*, *et*, and *aist* do not occur. [Thus we have: *rājabhyām*, *rājabhiḥ*, *rājñe*, *rājabhyaḥ*, *rājñaḥ*, *rājñoḥ*, *rājñām*, *rājñi*, *rājani*. [From the root *div* with the prefix *prati-*: "He plays against," thus *pratidivā*. [In the dual and plural: *pratidivānau*, *pratidivānaḥ*. When the elision of *al* (*allopa*) has been applied in its domain of occurrence...

For a verbal root ending in *r*, there is lengthening of the *ik* vowel in the penultimate position (*upadhā*) before a consonant (*hal*). Furthermore, the substitution of *al* (the elision of *n*) does not behave as if it were present (*sthānivadbhāva*), because that is prohibited in rules prescribing lengthening. The paribhāṣā regarding "external" (*bahiraṅga*) operations does not apply here due to the reasoning already stated. Examples: *pratidīvnaḥ*, *pratidīvnā*, etc.; *yajvā*, *yajvānau*, *yajvānaḥ*. SK 355 *na saṃyogād vamantāt* (A 6.4.137): [The suffix *niṣṭhā* is not replaced by *kta* after a root ending in a cluster (*saṃyoga*) that ends in *v* or *m*.]

There shall be no elision of the vowel *a* of the suffix *an* following a conjunct consonant ending in *va* or *ma*. For example: *yajvanaḥ*, *yajvanā*, *yajvabhyām*, and so forth; *brahmaṇaḥ*, *brahmaṇā*, *brahmabhyām*, and so forth. Regarding this, Pāṇini’s rule A 6.4.12 states: *inhanpūṣāryamṇāṃ śau* ("In the case of *in*, *han*, *pūṣan*, and *aryaman*, the penultimate vowel is lengthened only before the nominative plural suffix *śas*, and not elsewhere"). Thus, when the prohibition [of lengthening] would otherwise apply, [the following applies].

SK 357 *sau ca* (A 6.4.13): When the nominative singular suffix *su* follows, there is lengthening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) of words beginning with *han*. Thus, *vṛtrahā*; [in the vocative] *he vṛtrahan*. By the rule *ekāj-uttarapade* (Pāṇini 8.4.12), there is the substitution of *ṇ* for *n*: *vṛtrahaṇau*, *vṛtrahaṇaḥ*, *vṛtrahaṇam*, *vṛtrahaṇau*. SK 358 *ho hanter ñṇinneṣu* (A 7.3.54): In place of the *h* of the root *han*, there is the substitution of *gh* before suffixes marked with *ñ*, *ṇ*, or *ṅ*.
When a suffix marked with Ñ or Ṇ follows, or when the letter *n* follows, the substitution of *k* (kutva) occurs for the *h* of the root *han*.
[Pāṇini 8.4.22: *hanteḥ*]

The substitution of *ṇ* for the *n* of the root *han* occurs when it follows a cause (*nimitta*) situated in a prefix (*upasarga*). Thus, *prahaṇyāt*. By the rule *atpūrvasya* (A 8.4.22), the substitution of *ṇ* for the *n* of *han* occurs only when preceded by *at* (i.e., *a*), and not otherwise; thus, *praghnanti*. Due to the force of the separation of the rules (*yogavibhāga*), the maxim that "a rule or a prohibition applies only to what is immediately preceding" is set aside. Consequently, even the substitution of *ṇ* prescribed by *ekājuttarapade* is blocked. Furthermore, because of the force of the rule prescribing the change to a guttural (*kutva*) when *n* follows, the elision of *a* (*allopa*) is not treated as if it were still present (*na sthānivat*).

*vṛtraghnaḥ*, *vṛtraghnā*, and so forth. As for the optional substitution of *ṇ* for *n* in forms such as *vṛtryaghnaḥ* mentioned by Mādhava, that contradicts the Bhāṣya and the Vārttika. Similarly, in the case of *śārṅgin*, *yaśasvin*, *aryaman*, and *pūṣan*: although the suffix *in* in *yaśasvin* is devoid of meaning (*anarthaka*), it is nevertheless included under the rule *inhann* [Pāṇini 6.4.12]. This is because of the statement: "The mention of *an*, *in*, *as*, and *man* causes the application of the rule regarding what ends in them, whether the elements themselves are meaningful or meaningless. Thus: *aryamṇi* / *aryamaṇi*; *pūṣṇi* / *pūṣaṇi*. [Sūtra 360: *maghavā bahulam* (A 6.4.128).
Alternatively, there may be the substitution of *tṛ* for the word *maghavan*. [The substitute] is *ṛ*.
By A 7.1.70 (*ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ*), [the augment *num* is added].

The augment *num* shall be applied after a stem ending in a vowel other than a *dhātu*, after a stem ending in an *u*-vowel (*ugit*), and after the root *añc* when the nasal is elided, provided that a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix follows. There is lengthening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*). Thus, *maghavān*. In this case, when the lengthening is to be applied, the non-validity (*asiddhatva*) of the elision of the final consonant of the cluster (*saṃyogāntalopa*) does not apply, because of the use of the term "variously" (*bahulagrahaṇa*). Accordingly, the author of the *Mahābhāṣya* has rejected this sūtra by relying on the fact that both forms are established even in the common language (*bhāṣā*)—either through the specific grammatical derivation (*nipātana*) of *śvan* and *ukṣan*, or through the suffix *matup* added to the word *magha*.

"That Maghavan here eats the sacrificial oblation in the sacrifices without hesitation"—thus says Bhaṭṭi (BhK 18.19). [The forms are: *maghavantau*, *maghavantaḥ*; *he maghavan*; *maghavantam*, *maghavantau*, *maghavataḥ*; *maghavatā*, *maghavadbhyām*, and so forth. In the absence of the suffix *tṛ*, [the form is] *maghavā*. Regarding the suffix *van* in the rule *chandasi īvanipau ca*: that which ends in *van* is oxytone (*antodātta*) only in the Veda; however, the distinction is that that which is oxytone occurs in common usage (*loka*) as well. [The forms are: *maghavānau*, *maghavānaḥ*. In the presence of *su* [i.e., in the nominative singular], it follows the pattern of *rājan*.

Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.133 (*śvayuvamaghonāmataddhite*): For these [words] ending in *an* that bear the designation *bha*, there shall be vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) when a suffix other than a *taddhita* follows. And by Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.108 (*saṃprasāraṇācca*), there is *guṇa* substitution for the preceding vowel. Thus: *maghonaḥ*. Why "ending in *an*"? Consider: *maghavataḥ*, *maghavatā*; in the feminine: *maghavatī*. Why "other than a *taddhita*"? Consider: *māghavanam*, *maghonā*, *maghavabhyām*, and so forth. From *śvan*: *śunaḥ*, *śunā*, *śvabhyām*, and so forth. In the word *yuvan*, once the substitution of *u* for *va* has been made: Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.37 (*na saṃprasāraṇe saṃprasāraṇam*): When a vocalized element (*saṃprasāraṇa*) is being substituted, another vocalization is not substituted [in its place].

When a *saṃprasāraṇa* follows, there should not be a *saṃprasāraṇa* for the preceding semi-vowel (*yaṇ*). Thus, the *yakāra* does not undergo *it*-treatment. By this very indicator (*jñāpaka*), the *saṃprasāraṇa* occurs before the final *yaṇ*. Examples: *yūnaḥ*, *yūnā*, *yuvabhyām*, etc. *arvā*; *he arvan*. [Sūtra: *arvaṇastrasāvanañaḥ* (A 6.4.27).

For a stem ending in *arvan* that is not preceded by the negative particle *nañ*, the substitute *tṛ* shall be applied to the end of the base, but not before the nominative singular suffix *su*. Because it possesses the marker *u* (*ugit*), the augment *num* is added: *arvantau*, *arvantaḥ*, *arvantam*, *arvantau*, *arvataḥ*, *arvatā*, *arvadbhyām*, and so forth. Why "not preceded by *nañ*"? [Consider] *anarvā* (which is like *yajvan*). [A 7.1.85: For *pathin*, *maghavan*, and *ṛbhukṣan*, the letter *ā* is the final substitute when *su* follows. By the inclusion of the vowel *ā* (*ā-āt*) in the rule, the substitution is prescribed for the pure (non-nasalized) phoneme alone; therefore, there is no nasalization (*anunāsika*).
SK 366: In place of the *ik* vowel of *pathin* and so forth, there shall be *akāra* (*a*) when a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix follows.

SK 367 *yo nthaḥ* (A 7.1.87): In place of the *th* of *pathin* and *mathin*, the substitute *nth* shall occur when a *sarvanāmasthāna* follows. *panthāḥ*, *panthānau*, *panthānaḥ*; *panthānam*, *panthānau*. SK 368 *bhasya ṭer lopaḥ* (A 7.1.88): There is elision of the final phoneme (*ṭi*) of a *bha*-stem [when a *sarvanāmasthāna* follows].

There is elision of the final vowel of a nominal stem designated as *bha*, such as *pathin* and others. Thus: *pathaḥ*, *pathā*, *pathibhyām*, and so forth. Similarly for *manthāḥ* and *ṛbhukṣāḥ*. In the feminine, when the suffix *ṅīp* applies by virtue of the stem ending in *-n*, there is elision of the *ṭi* (the final vowel) because the stem is a *bha*-stem: *supathī*, *sumathī*, *nagarī*, *anṛbhukṣī senā*. [In the neuter,] the substitution of *ā* does not occur; or rather, it should be stated that the elision of the suffix *n* is optional by the rule *na lumatā* (Pāṇini 1.1.63). Thus: *he supathin* or *he supathi*.

Because the elision of *n* (*nalopa*) is considered non-existent (*asiddha*) with respect to the rules for *sup*-suffixes and accents, there is no *guṇa* substitution for the short vowel. In the dual, because it is a *bha*-stem, there is elision of the *ṭi* portion (*ṭilopa*). Thus: *supathi*. In the nominative plural (*śi*), because it is a *sarvanāmasthāna*, [the form is] *supanthāni*. Again: *supathi*, *supathī*, *supanthāmi*, *supathā*, *supathe*, *supathibhyām*, and so forth.
(SK 369) "Those ending in *ṣ* or *n* are called *ṣaṭ*. (A 1.1.24)

The number *ṣaṣ* (six), whether ending in a sibilant (*ṣ*) or a nasal (*ṇ*), shall be designated as *ṣaṭ*. [In the case of *ṣaṣ*,] there is elision (*luk*) after the dual endings. *pañca* (5), [dual] *pañca*. Why "number" (*saṃkhyā*)? [To exclude words like] *vipraṣuḥ* and *pāmānaḥ*. In the cases of *śatāni* and *sahasrāṇi*, there is no elision by virtue of the *saṃnipāta-paribhāṣā* (the rule that an operation caused by a specific combination does not destroy that combination), because the addition of *num* is effected by the presence of a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix and thus does not obstruct that very combination. The long vowel does not occur for the penultimate (*upadhā*) of the final member when *nām* follows. There is elision of *n*. [Examples: *pañcānām*, *pañcasu*, *paramapañca*, *paramapañcānām*. However, when [the word] is subordinate (*gauṇa*), the elision (*luk*) and the augment *nuṭ* do not apply: *priyapañcā*, *priyapañcān*, *priyapañcānaḥ*, *priyapañcām*. The same applies to *saptan*, *navan*, and *daśan*. SK 371: *aṣṭana ā vibhaktau* (A 7.4.84).
The substitution of *ā* occurs for *aṣṭan* before a case-ending (*vibhakti*) beginning with a consonant.

SK 372: *aṣṭābhya auś* (A 7.1.21). After the word *aṣṭan* when it has taken the form ending in *-ā*, the suffix *auś* shall replace the dual endings *jas* and *śas*. Although one could have simply said *aṣṭabhyaḥ*, the mention of the form with the vowel change (*ātva*) indicates that this vowel substitution applies specifically in the domain of *jas* and *śas*. Furthermore, this *ātva* of *aṣṭan* is optional, as evidenced by the inclusion of the term "long" (*dīrgha*) in the rule *aṣṭano dīrghāt* (A 7.2.84). Examples: *aṣṭau* (two), *paramāṣṭau* (two supreme eights). *aṣṭābhiḥ*, *aṣṭābhyaḥ* (two), *aṣṭānām*, *aṣṭāsu*. In the absence of *ātva*: *aṣṭa*, *aṣṭa*, etc., following the pattern of the number five (*pañcan*). However, when the word is used in a secondary sense (*gauṇatva*), in the absence of *ātva*, it follows the pattern of *rājan* (like a king).

In the case of *śasi* [the accusative plural], the substitution of *ā* for the final vowel of *priyāṣṭan-* occurs because, according to the *kāryakālapakṣa* (the view that a rule applies at the time its effect is to take place), the elision of the penultimate vowel (*al-lopa*)—being an external operation—is considered non-existent (*asiddha*). Thus, one forms *priyāṣṭnā*, and so forth. The substitution of *ā* for the final vowel (*ātva*), which is inferred from the rules for the nominative-accusative dual (*jas-śasoḥ*), applies only when the word is primary (*prādhānya*) and not when it is secondary (*gauṇatā*). Consequently, the optional substitution of *ā* for *priyāṣṭan-* occurs only before consonant-initial endings (*hal-ādi*). *priyāṣṭābhyām* / *priyāṣṭābhiḥ* / *priyāṣṭābhyaḥ* / *priyāṣṭāsu*. Like *rājan* [in the strong cases], everything else for *priyāṣṭan-* follows the pattern of *hāhā* before consonants. *budhā* / *budbhyām* / *bhutsu*. Pāṇini A 3.2.59 states: *ṛtvigdadhṛksragdiguṣṇigañcuyujikruñcāṃ ca* ("And [the suffix *kin* is added after the verbal roots] *ṛtviñ*, *dadhṛk*, *sraj*, *dik*, *uṣṇih*, *añcu*, *yuj*, and *kruñ*").

The suffix *kvin* shall occur after these [roots]. Through nipātana (irregular derivation), certain operations are obtained even though they are not indicated by formal rules. The suffix *kvin* occurs after the root *yaj* when it is without an upapada; [the resulting form is] *kanāvitau*.
SK 374: *kṛd atiṅ* (A 3.1.93).
When the governing context of "dhātu" (verbal root) is present, a suffix other than *tiṅ* shall bear the technical designation *kṛt*.
SK 375 *ver apṛktasya* (A 6.1.67):

There shall be elision (*lopa*) of an unreduplicated (*apṛkta*) suffix *v*. Because [the resulting form] is a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) by virtue of the rule *kṛttaddhita-samāsāś ca*, the case-endings (*svādayaḥ*) are applied.
SK 376 *yujer asamāse* (A 7.1.71): [The suffix *naṅ* is applied] after the root *yuj* when it is not in a compound.

The augment *num* shall be added to the root *yuj* before a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix, provided it is not in a compound (*asamāse*). [The following rules apply: there is elision of *su*; there is elision of the final member of a *saṃyoga* [consonant cluster]. By *kvinpratyayasya kuḥ* (A 8.2.62), when a *kvin* suffix follows, a guttural (*ka-varga*) substitute shall occur for the final sound of that [stem] at the end of a word (*padānte*). Because of this substitution of *ku* for *n*, the *num* becomes an *anusvāra* which is then subject to *parasavarṇa*. Since that [substitution] is considered as if non-existent (*asiddha*), the rule *coḥ kuḥ* does not apply [to change the *j* to *g*]. Thus: *yuñjau*, *yuñjaḥ*, *yuñjam*, *yuñjau*, *yujaḥ*, *yujā*, *yugbhyām*, and so forth. Why "provided it is not in a compound"? [Consider: *prayujau*.

SK 378: *coḥ kuḥ* (A 8.2.30). The *ku*-class (*kavarga*) shall replace the *cu*-class (*cavarga*) before a *jhal* consonant or at the end of a word. Thus, there is the substitution of *k* [for *c*]. However, because the rule *kvinpratyayasya* [which prescribes *kutva* for the suffix *kvin*] is considered *asiddha* (not having taken effect), [the following forms are derived differently]: *suyuk*, *suyug*; *suyujau*; *suyujaḥ*. The mention of *yujeḥ* in the Dhātupāṭha is an imitation (*anukaraṇa*) of the root as specified by its long vowel *ī* (*yuj-ī*), and not a reference (*nirdeśa*) by the short vowel *i*. Therefore, [the rule does not apply here]: *yujyate* ("he joins"), *samādhatte* ("he composes himself")—[from which we derive] *yuk*. The root *yuj* in the sense of "composing" belongs to the *divādi* class and is *ātmanepadī*. [In *suyuk*,] there is the elision of the final consonant of the *saṃyoga* cluster. *svan*: *svañjau*, *svañjaḥ*, and so forth.

By the rule *vraśca*, there is the substitution of *ṣ*; then *jaśtva* and *cartva* apply, resulting in *rāṭ*. Thus: *rāṭ*, *rāḍ*, *rājau*, *rājaḥ*, *rāṭsu*, *rāṭtsu*. Similarly: *vibhrāṭ*. *Deveṭ*, *devejaḥ*, *viśvasṛṭ*, *viśvasṛḍ*, *viśvasṛjau*, *viśvasṛjaḥ*. Here, it will be stated under the neuter section that the *kutva* substitution does not apply to the roots *sṛj* and *yaj*. *Parimṛṭ*. In the rule prescribing the substitution of *ṣ*, because of its association with the root *rāj*, only the root *ṭubhrājṛ* (meaning "to shine") belonging to the *phaṇādi* group is understood; however, for the root *ejṛ-bhre-jṛ-bhrājṛ* (also meaning "to shine"), there is indeed *kutva*. Thus: *vibhrāk*.

*vibhrāṭ*, *vibhrāgbhyām*, and so forth. *Parau vrajeḥ ṣaḥ padānte*: When *pari* is the preceding word (*upapada*), the root *vraj* takes the suffix *kvip*; there is lengthening of the vowel and the substitution of *ṣ* for the final consonant when at the end of a word. One who goes away, having abandoned everything, is a *parivrāj*. [Examples: *parivrājau*, *parivrājaḥ*. [From *viśvasya vasurāṭoḥ* (A 6.3.128): The substitution of *viśva-* for *sarva-* occurs before the words *vasu* and *rāṭ*.

The vowel *viśva* becomes long when followed by the word *vasu* or the word *rāṭ*. Thus, one whose wealth (*vasu*) is universal (*viśva*) is *viśvāvasuḥ*. The term *rāṭ* is intended as an indicator for the end of a word (*padānta*). The substitution of *c* for *ṭ* is not intended here. Examples include: *viśvārāṭ*, *viśvārāḍ*, *viśvarājau*, *viśvarājaḥ*, *viśvārāḍbhyām*, and so forth. (SK 380: A 8.2.29:
*skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca*) [The letters *s* and *k*, when at the beginning of a conjunct consonant (*saṃyoga*), are elided before a suffix beginning with a consonant, and also at the end of a word.]

When a *saṃyoga* (consonant cluster) occurs at the end of a word (*padānte*) or when a *jhal* (consonant) follows, there is elision of the initial *s* or *k* of that *saṃyoga*. *bhṛṣṭ* / *bhṛḍ*: After the elision of *ṣ*, *s* becomes *ś* by *ścutva*; that *ś* becomes *j* by *jaśtva*. Thus: *bhṛjau*, *bhṛjjaḥ*. By the rule *ṛtvig-ādi*, the suffix *kvin* is applied to the root *yaj* with *ṛtu* as an *upapada*. Because it ends in *kvin*, there is *kutva* (the substitution of *g*). Thus: *ṛtvik* / *ṛtvig*. *Ṛtvijau*, *ṛtvijaḥ*. Due to the restriction *rāt sasya*, there is no elision of the final consonant of the *saṃyoga*. *ūrk* / *ūrg*: *ūrj-au*, *ūrjaḥ*. [In the case of *tyad* etc.,] there is the substitution of *atva* and the subsequent form (*pararūpatva*).

SK 381: *tadoḥ saḥ sāvanantyayoḥ* (A 7.2.106). For the non-final *t* and *d* of the group beginning with *syad-* (the *tyadādi* pronouns), there is substitution of *sa-* when followed by the nominative singular suffix *su*. Examples: *syaḥ*, *tyau*, *tye*; *tyam*, *tyau*, *tyān*; *saḥ*, *tau*, *te*. Also: *paramasaḥ*, *paramatau*, *paramate*. [This applies] only to those ending in *dvi-*. Not here: *tvam*. Nor should it be said that [the substitution does not apply] because of the force of the explicit utterance of the letter *t*; for [the rule] finds its scope of application in the case of the secondary (*gauṇa*) form *atitvam*. Furthermore, when it is a technical name (*saṃjñā*) or when it is secondary, the substitutions of *atva* and *satva* do not occur. Examples: *tyad*, *tyadau*, *tyadaḥ*; *atityad*, *atityadau*.

*atityadaḥ*: *yaḥ*, *yau*, *ye*; *eṣaḥ*, *etau*, *ete*. But in the case of subsequent reference (*anvādeśa*), [the forms are]: *enam*, *enau*, *enān*; *enena*; *anayoḥ* (twice). (A 7.1.28): *ṅeprathamayor am*: After *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, the substitute *am* shall take the place of the suffix *ṅe* and of the first and second case endings.
Having introduced [the rule] *maparyantasya* (A 7.2.91),
[it continues with] *tvāhau sau* (A 7.2.94).
In place of the entire stem of *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, the substitutes *tva-* and *aha-* respectively occur when followed by the nominative singular suffix *su*;
otherwise, there is elision (*lopa*) of the remainder. (Pāṇini 7.2.90)

When a case ending other than those that cause the substitution of *āt* and *atv* follows, there shall be elision of the final letter of *yuṣmad* and *asmad*. Then, by the rule *ato guṇe ami pūrvaḥ*, [we obtain] *tvam* and *aham*. [Objection: But in the case of *tvaṃ strī* and *ahaṃ strī*, when *tva-am* and *aha-am* have been established, the substitution of the single preceding form (*ami pūrvarūpam*) should be set aside by the feminine suffix *ṭāp*, because the latter is more internal (*antaraṅga*). [Reply: True. However, *yuṣmad* and *asmad* are devoid of gender (*aliṅga*); therefore, due to the absence of femininity, *ṭāp* does not apply. Alternatively, in the rule *śeṣe*, the locative case indicates that the original base (*sthānin*) is intended as the locus (*adhikaraṇa*).

By that [rule], there is the elision of the portion *ad* following *maparyanta* according to the rule *ad-adaḥ*. And although that [elision] is subsequent, it applies once the internal operation (*antaraṅga*) of *ato guṇe* has taken effect. Consequently, because the finality in *a* is absent, the suffix *ṭāp* does not occur. Thus: *paramatvam*, *paramāham*, *atitvam*, *atyaham*.
SK 386: *yuvāvau dvivacane* (A 7.2.92). When two [persons] are expressed, *yuva* and *āva* replace the portion ending in *maparyanta* of *yuṣmad* and *asmad* before a case-ending.

SK 387: *prathamāyāś ca dvivacane bhāṣāyām* (A 7.2.88). Here, in the spoken language (*bhāṣā*), the vowel *ā* shall be the final substitute for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* in the dual of the nominative case. It would have been easier to state simply *auṅi*. Why specify "in the spoken language"? [Consider: *yuvaṃ vastrāṇi*, *yuvām*, *āvām*. Why say "of that which ends in *m*" (*maparyantasya*)? So that it does not apply to the form with the possessive suffix *kaC*: *yuvakām*, *āvakām*. [Otherwise,] in the cases *tvayā* and *mayā*, one would get *tvyā* and *myā*; furthermore, forms such as *yuvakābhyām* and *āvakābhyām* would not be established. SK 388: *yūyavayau jasi* (A 7.2.93). [In the spoken language, the forms] *yūyam* and *vayam* are substituted for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* respectively when followed by the suffix *jas*.

This is clear. [The forms] *yūyam*, *vayam*, *paramayūyam*, *paramavayam*, *atiyūyam*, and *ativayam* are examples. Here, under the view that "in the remaining cases, there is elision of the final letter" (*śeṣe lopo 'ntyalopaḥ*), the substitution of *śī* for *jas* would have applied. However, this does not occur because of the principle: "Once an operation dependent on a stem (*aṅgakārya*) has been performed, another operation dependent on that same stem is not repeated. Alternatively, it may be explained by reading an additional *m* into the rule *ṅeprathamayoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.28), so that only *am* remains when the stem ends in *m*, and it is not further modified. SK 389: *tvamāv ekavacane* (A 7.2.97). When expressing a singular, the substitutes *tvam* and *au* take the place of the portions of *yuṣmad* and *asmad* ending in *m* before a case-ending.

And in the second case (dvitīyā), there shall be the substitution of the vowel *ā* for *yuṣmad* and *asmad*. [Thus: *tvām*, *mām*, *yuvām*, *āvām*. And also in the nominative plural (*śas*). (A 7.1.29)

"No" [is used] without a case ending. After *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, the letter *na* shall replace *śas*. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to [the substitution of] *ām*. [The rule] "of the subsequent [element], it replaces the first [sound]" applies: there is elision of the final consonant cluster (*saṃyogāntalopa*). Thus: *yuṣmān*, *asmān*. SK 392: *yo 'ci* (A 7.2.89).
When a vowel beginning with a non-substitute (*anādeśa*) follows, the replacement of *ya* shall occur for these two [stems, *yuṣmad* and *asmad*]. Thus: *tvayā*, *mayā*.

SK 393 *yuṣmadasmador anādeśe* (A 7.2.83): When followed by a case-ending beginning with a consonant that is not a substitute, the long vowel *ā* is substituted for these two [stems *yuṣmad* and *asmad*]. [Examples: *yuvābhyām*, *āvābhyām*; *yuṣmābhiḥ*, *asmābhiḥ*. SK 394 *tubhyamahyau ṅayi* (A 7.2.95): When the dative singular ending *ṅe* follows, *tubhya-* and *mahya-* are substituted for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* respectively.

In these two [forms, *yusmad* and *asmad*], for the portion ending in *m*, there is the substitution of *tubhya* and *mahya* before the suffix *ṅe*. There is the replacement (*amādeśaḥ*). In the remaining cases, there is elision (*śeṣe lopaḥ*). Thus: *tubhyam*, *mahyam*; *pratumubhyam*, *paramamahyam*; *atitubhyam*, *atimahyam*; *yuvābhyām*, *āvābhyām*. SK 395: *bhyasaḥ bhyam* (A 7.1.30). For the suffix *bhyas*, there shall be the substitution of *bhyam* or *abhyam*. The former [substitution of *bhyam*] occurs only when the elision of the remainder (*śeṣe lopa*) is an elision of the final letter. In that case, by the *aṅgavṛttaparibhāṣā* (the maxim regarding operations within a stem), the substitution of *etva* (the change to *e*) does not take place. However, *abhyam* is correct in both alternatives. Thus: *yuṣmabhyam*, *asmabhyam*.

SK 396 *ekavacanasya ca* (A 7.1.32): After these two [words *yuṣmad* and *asmad*], the fifth case singular ending shall be replaced by *at*. Thus, *tvat* and *mat* are easily explained. Furthermore, it is well stated that [the same applies] after the ending *ṅasi*: *yuvābhyām*, *āvābhyām*. SK 397 *pañcamyā at* (A 7.1.31): [The ending of the fifth case is replaced by *at*].
From these two [words *yuṣmad* and *asmad*], the fifth case ending *bhyas* shall be *ābhyām*. [The forms are] *yuṣmad* and *asmad*. (SK 398) *tavamamau ṅasi* (A 7.2.96):
In the case of the fifth case ending *ṅasi*, the portions up to the final *m* of these two [words] are replaced by *tava* and *mama* respectively.
SK 399 *yuṣmadasmadbhyāṃ ṅaso 'ś* (A 7.1.27): This is clear. [The forms are] *tava*, *mama*, *yuvayoḥ*, and *āvayoḥ*. SK 400 *sāma ākam* (A 7.1.33).

The substitute *sām* shall take the place of the following [stem] after these two [words *yuṣmad* and *asmad*]. The mention of the form with the augment *suṭ* (*yuṣmān*, *asmān*) is for the purpose of excluding the future application of *suṭ*. Examples: *yuṣmākam*, *asmākam*; *tvayi*, *mayi*; *yuvayoḥ*, *āvayoḥ*; *yuṣmāsu*, *asmāsu*. When *yuṣmad* and *asmad* are being compounded and denote duality or singularity, the forms *yuvā-* and *āvā-* [are substituted], and likewise *tva-* and *ma-*. (Pāṇini 7.2.92) In the presence of the suffixes *su*, *jas*, *ṅe*, and *ṅasi*, these substitutes always occur: *tvā-* and *ah-*; *yūya-* and *vaya-*; *tubhya-* and *mahya-*; and also *tava-* and *mama-*. (Pāṇini 7.2.93–96)

2. These [substitutes *yuṣmad* and *asmad*] set aside *yuvā* and *āvā* in their own domain because they are subsequent; they also set aside *tvam* and *mām* by means of a prior counter-exception (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*). 3–4. The meaning of a compound possesses the number two or one, whereas *yuṣmad* and *asmad* possess a plural sense. Since those two do not have the sense of two or one, there is no application of *yuvā*, *āvā*, *tvam*, or *mām*. In the analysis (*vigraha*) "one who has surpassed you" (*tvām*) or "me" (*mām*), we have: *atitvam*, *atyaham*; *atitvām*, *atimām*; *atiyūyam*, *ativayam*; *atitvām* (dual), *atimām* (dual); *atitvān*, *atimān*.

*atitvayā* / *atimayā* / *atitvābhyām* / *atimābhyām* / *atitvābhiḥ* / *atimābhiḥ* / *atitubhyam* / *atimahyam* / *atitvābhyām* / *atimābhyām* / *atitvabhyam* / *atimabhyam*. In the cases of *ṅasi* and *bhyas*: *atitvat* (twice) / *atimat* (twice). In the case of *bhyām*, it is as before: *atitava* / *atimama*. In the genitive dual: *atitvayoḥ* / *atimayoḥ*. In the genitive plural: *atitvākam* / *atimākam*. In the locative singular: *atitvayi* / *atimayi*. In the locative dual: *atitvayoḥ* / *atimayoḥ*. In the locative plural: *atitvāsu* / *atimāsu*.

In the analysis (*vigraha*) "you two" or "we two" have passed by (*atikrāntaḥ*), the forms are as before in the cases *su*, *jas*, *ṅe*, and *ṅasi*. In the cases *au*, *am*, and *auṭ*: *atiyuvām* (3), *atyāvayā* (3); *atiyuvān*, *atyāvān*; *atiyuvayā*, *atyāvayā*; *atiyuvābhyām* (3), *atyāvābhyām* (3); *atiyuvābhiḥ*, *atyāvābhiḥ*. In the case *bhyas*: *atiyuvabhyam*, *atyāvabhyam*. In the cases *ṅasi* and *bhyas*: *atiyuvat* (2), *atyāvat* (2). In the case *osi*: *atiyuvayoḥ* (2), *atyāvayoḥ* (2); *atiyuvākam*, *atyāvākam*.

In the analysis *ati-yuṣmān-asmān-veti* ("he goes beyond you and us"), the forms in *su*, *jas*, *ṅe*, and *ṅasi* are as before. In the case of *au*, *am*, and *auṭ*: *atiyuṣmām* (3), *atyasmām* (3). [In the dual: *atiyuṣmān*, *atyasmān*. [In the singular instrumental: *atiyuṣmayā*, *atyasmayā*. [In the dual instrumental: *atiyuṣmābhyām* (3), *atyasmābhyām* (3). [In the plural instrumental: *atiyuṣmābhiḥ*, *atyasmābhiḥ*. [In the dative plural (*bhyas*): *atiyuṣmabhyam*, *atyasmabhyam*. [In the genitive singular (*ṅasi*) and dative-ablative plural (*bhyas*): *atiyuṣmat* (2), *atyasmat* (2). [In the genitive dual (*osi*): *atiyuṣmayoḥ* (2).
In the case of *ati* followed by *asmad* and *yuṣmad*: *atiyuṣmākam*, *atyasmākam*; *atiyuṣmayi*, *atyasmayi*; *atiyuṣmāsu*, *atyasmāsu*.
[Pāṇini 8.1.16] Regarding the end of a word (*pada*);
[Pāṇini 8.1.17] following a word (*padāt*).
Having introduced [the rule] SK 403: "Everything is unaccented except at the beginning of a metrical foot" (A 8.1.18), [the following applies]:
SK 404: "In place of the forms of *yuṣmad* and *asmad* standing in the sixth, fourth, or second case, *vām* and *nau* are substituted respectively" (A 8.1.20).

In place of these two [pronouns *yuṣmad* and *asmad*] when they follow a word and do not stand at the beginning of a metrical foot (*apādādau*), or when they are specified by the sixth case (*ṣaṣṭhī*) and so forth, there are the substitutes *vām* and *nau*, and these two are unaccented (*anudātta*).

According to A 8.1.21, *vas* and *nas* are the substitutes for the plural forms of those [two pronouns] ending in the sixth case and so forth, according to the aforementioned rule; this is an exception (*apavāda*) to *vām* and *nau*.
SK 406: For the singular case-ending, [the substitutes] *te* and *me* occur in place of these two aforementioned forms ending in the genitive and dative singular. SK 407:
*tvā* and *mā* occur in place of the accusative singular.

The forms *tvā* and *mā* are used for the second person singular and first person singular respectively. 1. May the Lord of Śrī protect you (*tvām*) and me (*mām*) here; may He also grant you (*te*) and me (*me*) happiness. That Hari, the Master, protects you (*vām*) and us (*nau*); may the All-pervading One also protect you two (*vām*) and us two (*nau*). 2. May the Lord grant happiness to you two (*vām*) and us two (*nau*); may Hari, the Master, [protect] you two (*vām*) and us two (*nau*). May He protect you (*vaḥ*) and us (*naḥ*); may He grant auspiciousness to you (*vaḥ*) and us (*naḥ*); He is to be served by you (*vaḥ*) and by us (*naḥ*) in this world. Why [is it said] "after a word"? So that it does not occur at the beginning of a sentence. [Examples: *tvāṃ pātu* (May he protect you); *māṃ pātu* (May he protect me). Why [is it said] "not at the beginning of a foot"? [Example: *tvāṃ pātu*. *māṃ pātu*. Why [is it said] "not at the beginning of a foot"? [Example: *apādādau kim*.

May Kṛṣṇa, who is to be known through all the Vedas, protect us at all times. [The rule applies] only when the case endings are actually heard due to their retention; not here: *hatiyuṣmatputro bravīti* (the son of you-here says), because [in this case] *asmāt* (from him) is the son who speaks. The elision (*nighāta*), as well as the substitutes for *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, must be stated to occur within a single sentence (*samānavākya*). A sentence consists of one finite verb (*ekatiṅ*). Therefore, there is no [elision] here: *odanaṃ eca tava bhaviṣyati* (rice will indeed be yours). But it would certainly occur here: *śālīnāṃ te odanaṃ dāsyāmi* (I shall give you rice of fine grains).

These substitutes—*etad*, *tvad*, *mad*, etc.—are optionally prescribed when there is no subsequent reference (*ananvādeśa*). However, in the case of a subsequent reference (*anvādeśa*), they must necessarily be used. For example: *dhātā te bhaktaḥ asti* or *dhātā tava bhaktaḥ asti*; [but] *tasmai te namaḥ* only.

By the rule *na cavāhāhaivayukte* (A 8.1.24), these substitutes do not occur when joined with the five beginning with *ca*. For example: *haris tvāṃ māṃ ca rakṣatu*; *kathaṃ tvāṃ māṃ vā na rakṣet* and so forth. Because of the inclusion of the word *yukta* ("joined"), this prohibition applies only when there is direct connection; however, in the case of an indirect relationship, the substitute would indeed occur. For example: *haro hariś ca me svāmī*.

SK 409 *paśyārthair anālocane* (A 8.1.25): When used in conjunction with verbal roots whose meaning is non-visual cognition (*acākṣuṣajñāna*), these substitutes shall not occur. For example: *cetasāṃ svāṃ samīkṣate* ("He perceives his own [nature] with the mind"). This prohibition applies even when there is an indirect connection (*paramparā-saṃbandha*). For example: *bhaktas tava rūpaṃ dhyāyati* ("The devotee meditates upon your form"). However, in the case of visual perception (*ālocana*), it is: *bhaktas tvā paśyati cakṣuṣā* ("The devotee sees you with his eyes"). SK 410 *sapūrvāyāḥ prathamāyā vibhāṣā* (A 8.1.26): [The substitution of *te* for *tubhyaṃ* and *tava* occurs optionally] after a nominative case ending (*prathamā*) that is preceded by another word.

When these two [pronouns] follow a word ending in the nominative case that has already appeared in the discourse, even in the case of an *anvādeśa* (subsequent reference), these substitutes may optionally occur. For example: *bhaktas tvam apy ahaṃ tena haris tvāṃ trāyate sa mām* ("You are a devotee, and I too; therefore Hari protects you and me"), or alternatively *tvā mā*. *Sāmantritam* (Pāṇini 2.3.48): That which ends in the first case when used in the sense of addressing (*saṃbodhana*) shall be designated as *āmantrita* (vocative).

It is clear that [the rule] *āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat* (Pāṇini 8.1.72) applies: *agne tava*, *devāsmān pāhi*, *agne naya*, *agna indra varuṇa*. In these cases, there is no substitution for *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, nor is there the low-pitched accent (*nighāta*) of a finite verb (*tiṅanta*), nor the low-pitched accent of the vocative (*āmantritanighāta*). However, in the case of *sarvadā rakṣa deva naḥ*, although the word *deva* behaves as if non-existent (*avidyamānavat*), the substitution [of *naḥ* for *asmad*] occurs by relying on the preceding word *rakṣa*.

Thus, in the mantra *evaṃ imaṃ me gaṅge yamune*, although the vocatives beginning with *yamune* are treated as non-existent (*avidyamānavat*) due to the preceding vocative, the *nighāta* (anudātta accentuation) of all [the following words] occurs by relying solely on the word *me*.
This is because of the rule: *nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam* (Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.1.73).

When followed by a vocative in grammatical apposition (*samānādhikaraṇa*), the qualified noun (*viśeṣya*) shall not be treated as non-existent. For example: *hare dayālo naḥ pāhi* ("O compassionate Hari, protect us!"); *agne tejasvin* ("O radiant Agni!"). Regarding this, the *Bhāṣya* states that the rule is optional when the qualifier is plural: "I shall state that it concerns the plural. Thus, a qualified noun ending in the plural may optionally be treated as non-existent when followed by a vocative qualifier in apposition. For example: *yūyaṃ prabhavaḥ* ("You are the lords") or *devāḥ śaraṇyāḥ* ("The gods are our refuge"); or *yuṣmān bhaje* ("I worship you") or *vo bhaje* ("I worship you").
Here, even in the case of subsequent mention (anvādeśa), the substitutes are optional: *supāt*, *supād*, *supādau*, *supādaḥ*, *supādam*, *supādau*.

SK 414 *pādaḥ pat* (A 6.4.130): When a base (*aṅga*) ending in the word *pād* is a *bha*-stem, the substitute *pad* shall take the place of that constituent word *pād*. Examples: *supadaḥ*, *supadā*, *supādbhyām*, and so forth. From the expression "he churns the fire" (*agniṃ manthati*), [the derivative] is *agnimat*, *agnimad*, *agnimathau*, *agnimathaḥ*, *agnimadbhyām*, and so forth. By the rule beginning with *ṛtvig-*, the suffix *kvin* is applied to the root *añc* when a *su*-ending follows as an upapada.

SK 415 *aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti* (A 6.4.24): [The long vowel is not substituted for the penultimate vowel of roots ending in a consonant and having no *it* marker, provided a suffix marked with *k* or *ṅ* follows.]

There is elision of the *n* of stems ending in a consonant (*hal*) that do not have *i* as their *it*, provided it is in the *upadhā* position, when followed by a suffix marked with *k* or *ṅ*. [In *prāṅ*,] the augment *num* is added by the rule *ugidacām*. There is elision of the final member of a *saṃyoga*. By the rule *kvinpratyayasya kuḥ*, the *n* of the *num* augment becomes a *ṅ* due to the substitution of *ku*. Thus: *prāṅ*. Then the *anusvāra* and *parasavarṇa* substitutions apply: *prāñcau*, *prāñcaḥ*, *prāñcam*, *prāñcau*. By the rule *acaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.138), there is elision of the vowel *a* of the stem *añc-* when its *n* has been elided, provided it is a *bha*-stem.

SK 417: When *añcu* follows, provided that the *a* or *n* has been elided, there is lengthening of the preceding *aṇ*. Thus: *prācaḥ*, *prācā*, *prāgbhyām*, and so forth. *pratyaṅ*, *pratyañcau*, *pratyañcaḥ*, *pratyañcam*, *pratyañcau*. Regarding the rule for the elision of *ac*, the *yaṇ* substitution does not take effect even though it is *antaraṅga*, by the metarule (*paribhāṣā*) "those which have not yet undergone [the application of] *vyūha* do not [themselves] undergo *vyūha*" (*akṛtavyūhāḥ*). *pratīcaḥ*, *praticā*. In the analysis (*vigraha*) "he goes toward that" (*amum añcati*), when we have reached the stage *adas-añc-*, [the following applies]: SK 418:
In the case of *viṣvak* and *deva*, as well as [the pronoun *adas*], the final phoneme (*ṭi*) is replaced by *adri* before the suffix *añcu*, provided it is not a *kṛt* suffix. (A 6.3.92)

In these two cases, as well as for a pronoun (*sarvanāman*), the final vowel (*ṭi*) is replaced by *adri* when followed by the suffix *añcu*, provided it does not end in a *pratyaya*. When *adadri-añca* is established, the *yaṇ* substitution occurs.
Regarding *adas-*: "In place of *adas-*, when the *si* case-ending follows, *dāt* is substituted for *ada-* and *do* is substituted for *da-*" (A 8.2.80). *maḥ* [is the augment]. SK 419.

In the word *adas*, for that which follows *d* and does not end in *s*, there are *u* and *t*; and for *d*, there is *m*. The term *u* is a collective dvandva compound of both the short and long vowels. By the principle of closest proximity (*āntaratamya*), the short vowel is substituted for the short vowel and the consonant, and the long vowel for the long vowel. Thus: *amum uyaṅ*, *amum uyañcau*, *amum uyañcaḥ*, *amum uyañcam*, *amum uyañcau*, *amum uricaḥ*, *amum uricā*, *amum uyagbhyām*, and so forth. Because the substitution of *m* (*mutva*) is considered as if non-existent (*asiddha*), the *yaṇ* sandhi does not apply.

In the opinion of those who, relying on the *paribhāṣā* "when there is an obstruction of the final [element], [the operation applies] to that which is in the position of the final," maintain that the substitution of *m* (*mutva*) applies only to the subsequent [element], they derive *adadryaṅ* from the analysis: *adas* + *uyaṅ*; and because of the analysis *aḥ seḥ*, meaning "that which has *s* in place of *si* is *asi*," they hold that the substitution of *m* occurs only in the domain of the *tyadādi* substitution (of *a* for *da*) and not elsewhere. And it has been said: "Some desire the substitution of *m* for *adra* in *adas* separately, like the substitution of *l* (*latva*). Some [desire it] for that which is in the position of the final; others say 'no,' for it is seen [to apply] to *asi*. [Question: What [is the purpose of the mention of] *viṣvak* and *deva*? [Answer: *aśvācī*.

What is the purpose of [specifying] *añcatu*? [Consider] *viṣvagyuk*. Why [is it said] "in the absence of an affix" (*apratyaye*)? [Consider] *viṣvagañcanam*. The mention of "the absence of an affix" indicates that, elsewhere, when there is a mention of a verbal root (*dhātu*), the rule applies to what begins with that [root]. By this, [we have] *ayaskāraḥ*; here, by [Pāṇini 8.3.46] *ataḥ kṛkami*, the *s* [substitutes for the *n*]. *udaṅ*, *udañcau*, *udañcaḥ*. In the case of vowels beginning with the [accusative plural] suffix *śas*: SK 420, *uda īt* (A 6.4.139).
After the word *udak*, the *a* of the stem (*bha*) of the root *añc-*—whose *n* has been elided—should be replaced by *ī*. Thus: *udīcaḥ*, *udīcā*, *udagbhyām*, and so forth.

SK 421: Before the suffix *añc*, when it ends in the *v*-suffix, the word *sama* becomes *sami*. Examples: *samyaṅ*, *samyañcau*, *samyañcaḥ*; [also] *samīcaḥ*, *samīcaḥ*. SK 422: For *saha*, the substitute *sadhr̥* is applied.

When the suffix *añc* ending in the *vap*-affix follows [the stem], [the following rules apply]: **SK 423:** *tirasas tir yalope* (A 6.3.94). When the suffix *añc* ending in the *vap*-affix follows, provided that the vowel *a* has not been elided, the substitute *tir* is applied in place of *tiras*. Examples: *tiryaṅ* *tiryañcau* *tiryañcaḥ* *tiryañcam* *tiryañcau* *tiraścaḥ* *tiraścā* *tiryagbhyām*, and so forth.

SK 424: *nāñceḥ pūjāyām* (A 6.4.30). For the root *añc-* when it has the sense of worship (*pūjā*), there shall be no elision of the *n* in its penultimate vowel. Because the *n* is not elided, the augment *num* does not apply. [The forms are: *prāṅ*, *prāñcau*, *prāñcaḥ*. Due to the absence of the elision of *n*, there is no elision of the vowel *a*. [Thus: *prāñcaḥ*, *prāñcā*, *prāṅbhyām*, *prāṅkṣu* or *prāṅṣu*. In this same way, *pratyaṅ* is cited as an example for the sense of worship. The root *kruñc-* is used in the senses of crookedness (*kauṭilya*) and becoming small (*alpībhāva*). Although the elision of *n* would normally occur by the rule for *ṛtvig* and others, here it is specifically prescribed (*nipātyate*) that it remains. [The forms are: *kruṅ*, *kruñcau*, *kruñcaḥ*, *kruṅbhyām*, etc. By the rule *coḥ kuḥ* (A 8.2.30), [the *c* of] *payomuc* becomes *k*. [The form is: *payomuk*.

*payomuk*, *payomucau*, *payomucaḥ*. By the rule *vraśca*, there is the substitution of *ṣ*; by *skoḥ*, there is the elision of *s*; then the substitutions of *jaśtva* and *cartva* apply: *suvṛṭ*, *suvṛḍ*, *suvṛścau*, *suvṛścaḥ*, *suvṛṭsu*, *suvṛṭtsu*. In the present tense, these words—*pṛṣat*, *mahat*, *bṛhat*, *jagat*, and those ending in the suffix *śatṛ*—are treated as irregular (*nipātyante*). They should undergo the grammatical operations of those ending in *śatṛ*. Because they possess the marker *u* (being *ugit*), the augment *num* is added. By the rule *sāntamahataḥ*, there is lengthening [of the vowel before the final *t*]. That which is magnified or honored is called *mahān* (great). [The forms are: *mahāntau*, *mahāntaḥ*, *he mahan*, *mahataḥ*, *mahatā*, *mahadbhyām*, and so forth.

SK 425: *atvasantasya cādhātoḥ* (A 6.4.14). When the nominative singular suffix *su* follows, which is not the vocative (*asaṃbuddhau*), there is lengthening of the penultimate vowel of a stem ending in short *a* (*at*) as well as of a non-verb root (*adhātu*) ending in long *ā* (*asan*). By the force of this explicit statement, the lengthening occurs first, overriding the subsequent and obligatory *num* augment; thereafter, *num* is applied. Thus: *dūmān*, *dhīmantau*, *dhīmantaḥ*; and in the vocative, *he dhīman*. From the accusative plural (*śas*) onwards, it is like *mahat*. There is also lengthening for a verbal root ending in short *a*. [The forms] *gomān* and *dhīmān* are derived from the desiderative (*kyajanta*) *gomant-iṣati* or from the denominative with *kvip* (*ācārakvibanta*) *gomān ivācarati*, followed by the agentive *kvip* suffix.

In the sūtra *ugidacām*, the mention of *aj* is for the purpose of restriction: if an operation conditioned by an *ugit* suffix applies to a verbal root, then it applies only to the root *añc*. Consequently, there is no [application of the rule] in cases such as *srat* and *dhvat*. However, the phrase *adhātoḥ* is intended to include even that which was previously not a verbal root, so that the augment *num* may apply; for example: *gomān*, *gomantau*, *gomantaḥ*, and so forth. From the root *bhā*, the suffix *ḍvatu* is applied: *bhavān*, *bhavantau*, *bhavantaḥ*. But in the case of the present participle (*śatṛnta*) [of *bhū*], because it lacks the sequence *at-ant*, the lengthening does not occur: *bhavan* (as in "being"). SK 426: *ubhe abhyastam* (A 6.1.5).
In the section concerning the doubling of the sixth [case-ending], those two which are prescribed are both designated as *abhyasta* when combined.
(Pāṇini 7.1.4–6). According to A 7.1.78, *nābhyastāc chatuḥ*:
there shall be no *num* after the suffix *śatṛ* (*śatṛ-pratyaya*) following an *abhyasta*. Examples: *dadat*, *dadad*; *dadatau*; *dadataḥ*.

SK 428: *jakṣityādayaḥ ṣaṭ* (A 6.1.6). Six verbal roots, beginning with *jakṣ*, and a seventh, *jakṣiti*, are designated as *abhyasta*. [Examples: *jakṣat*, *jakṣad*, *jakṣatau*, *jakṣataḥ*. Similarly: *jāgrat*, *daridrat*, *śāsat*, *cakāsat*. Although *dīdhī* and *vevī* are marked with the *ṅit* indicator, they take the *parasmaipada* ending by way of irregularity (*vyatyaya*) due to their Vedic character. [Examples: *dīdhyat*, *vevyat*. *gup*: *gub*, *gupau*, *gupaḥ*; *gubbhyām*, etc. SK 429: *tyadādiṣu dṛśo 'nālocane kañ ca* (A 3.2.60). After the pronouns beginning with *tyad*, the suffix *kañ* is added to the root *dṛś* when it does not mean "perceiving."

When words such as *tyad* and others are used as upapadas, the suffix *kañ* is applied after the root *dṛś* meaning "to see" or "to know," and optionally the suffix *kvin*; furthermore, the long vowel *ā* is substituted for the final vowel of a pronominal stem.
(Pāṇini 6.3.91)

The letter *ā* shall be the final substitute for a pronominal stem before the suffixes *dṛk*, *dṛś*, and *vat*. Because the substitution of *k* (for *t*) is considered asiddha, the rule *vraśca-* applies, resulting in *ṣ*. This becomes *ḍ* by the rule for *jaś*-substitution. That becomes *g* by the rule for *ku*-substitution. By the rule for *car*-substitution, it optionally becomes *k*. Thus: *tādṛk* / *tādṛg*; *tādṛśau*; *tādṛśaḥ*. According to the opinion of Kaiyaṭa, Haradatta, and others, however, because the substitution of *kh* (by *kutva*) takes precedence over the substitution of *ṣ* (*ṣatvāpavāda*), the sound *kh* alone is heard in the alternative case where *car*-substitution does not occur, and not *g*. This is because the substitution of *ku* is asiddha with respect to the substitution of *jaś*.

Alternatively, it should be understood that because of the rule *digādibhyo yat* (Pāṇini 5.1.97), there is no status of being "asiddha" (not yet established). By the rule *vraśca* (Pāṇini 8.2.36), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs; then by the rules for *jaśtva* and *cartva*, we have: *viṭ*, *viḍ*, *viśau*, *viśaḥ*, *viśam*. Regarding the rule *naśer vā* (A 8.2.63):

after the root *naś*, the guttural (*ka-varga*) may optionally be the substitute for the final sound at the end of a word. Thus: *nak*, *nag*, *naṭ*, *naḍ*, *naśau*, *naśaḥ*, *nagbhyām*, *naḍbhyām*, and so forth.

SK 432: *spṛśo ’nudake kvin* (A 3.2.58). When a word other than *udaka* follows as an upapada, the suffix *kvin* is applied after the root *spṛś*. [Examples: *ghṛtaspṛk*, *ghṛtaspṛg*; *ghṛtaspṛśau*; *ghṛtaspṛśaḥ*. Because the analysis *kvinaḥ pratyayo yasmāt* (that from which the suffix *kvin* arises) is adopted as a bahuvrīhi compound, the substitution of *k* for *s* (*kutva*) occurs even when the suffix is *kvip*. [The forms] *spṛk* etc. follow the same pattern as before regarding the six operations (*ṣaḍagaka*). The root *dhṛṣ* is used in the sense of "boldness" (*prāgalbhye*). From this root, the suffix *kvin* is applied according to A 3.2.59 (*ṛtvig-ādinā*), and the reduplication (*dvitva*) and the acute accent on the final syllable (*antodāttatva*) are prescribed by nipātana. Before the application of *kutva*, the substitution of *ḍ* for *s* occurs by *jaśtva*. Thus we have *gaḥ* and *kaḥ*. SK 444 *vā napuṃsakasya* (A 7.1.79): After an *abhyasta* [reduplicated] stem, the suffix *num* may optionally be inserted before the final vowel of a neuter noun ending in *śatṛ*, when a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix follows. Examples: *dadanti* or *dadati*; *tudat*. SK 445 *ācchīnadyor num* (A 7.1.80): The suffix *num* is inserted after a stem ending in long *ā*, and after the feminine suffixes *śī* and *nadī*, when a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix follows.

After a verbal stem ending in a vowel other than *a*, the augment *num* may optionally be inserted before the portion of the suffix *śatṛ* that follows it, when *śī* or *nadi* follow. Examples: *tudantī* / *tudatī*; *tudanti*. *bhāt* / *bhāntī* / *bhātī* / *bhānti*. *pacat*.
According to A 7.1.91 (*śapśyanor nityam*), [the augment *num* is] obligatory after the suffixes *śap* and *śyan*.

The final letter of that which ends in the *śatṛ* suffix (present participle) following the roots *śās* and *śyan* shall take the augment *num* when followed by the feminine suffixes *śī* and *nadyām*. Examples: *pacantī*, *pacanti*; *dīvyat*, *dīvyantī*, *dīvyanti*; *svap*, *svap*, *svapī*. Even though the *num* follows what is otherwise constant (*nitya*), the lengthening rule from *aptṛn* applies first because it is taught as a specific rule (*pratipadokta*). Thus: *svāmpi*. However, according to the view that "being taught as a specific rule" means "having no other scope," since that [lengthening] does not apply here, only *num* occurs: *svampi*. Furthermore: *svapā*. Regarding the form *svadbhyām*: the rule *apo bhi* applies. *svadbhyām* (Note: This is the correct form derived from *svap* + *bhyām*, where the *ap* is replaced by *at* before the case ending).

By the rule *arti-pṛ-vapi-ityādinā* [Uṇādi Sūtra 1.2], the suffix *um* is added to the root *dhan* (to sound). The substitution of *ru* for *n* occurs, resulting in *dhanuḥ*. In the dual, *dhanuṣī*. In the plural, because the stem ends in a consonant (*sānta*), the vowel is lengthened; then, by the rule *num-visarjanīya-*, the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs, yielding *dhanūṃṣi*. The instrumental singular is *dhanuṣā*; the dual is *dhanurbhyām*. Similarly, *cakṣus* (eye), *havis* (oblation), and others are formed. From the desiderative *pipaṭhiṣati* (he wishes to read), the suffix *kvip* is added. By the rule *rvoḥ* [Pāṇini 6.1.89], the vowel is lengthened, resulting in *pipaṭhīḥ*. In the dual, *pipaṭhiṣī*. Because the elision (*allopasya*) is treated as if it were still present (*sthānivattvāt*), the *num* augment—which is conditioned by a stem ending in a *jhal* consonant—does not apply. Furthermore, because there is no *sthānivadbhāva* with respect to a rule concerning its own form (*svavidhau*), the *num* augment conditioned by a stem ending in a vowel (*ajanta-lakṣaṇa*) also does not apply.

*pipaṭhiṣi*, *pipaṭhībhyām*, and so forth; *payaḥ*, *payasī*, *payāṃsi*; *payasā*, *payobhyām*, and so forth; *supum*, *supuṃsī*, *supumāṃsi*. For *adaḥ*, the operations of the case-endings apply: the substitution of *utva* and *matva* [yield] *amū* and *amūni*. The remainder is like the masculine.
Thus end the consonant-final neuter gender nouns. Section 14: Indeclinables.
SK 447: *svarādinipātam avyayam* (A 1.1.37).

The words beginning with *svara* and the particles (*nipāta*) shall receive the designation of indeclinable (*avyaya*). *svar*, *antar*, *prātar*, *punar*, *sanutar*, *uccais*, *nīcais*, *śanais*, *ṛdhak*, *ṛte*, *yugapat*, *ārāt*, *pṛthak*, *hyas*, *śvas*, *divā*, *rātrau*, *sāyam*, *ciram*, *manāk*, *īṣat*, *joṣam*, *tūṣṇīm*, *bahis*, *avas*, *samayā*, *nikaṣā*, *svayam*, *vṛthā*, *naktam*, *nañ*, *hetu*, *iddhā*, *addhā*, *sāmi*. [The following are included in the *gaṇa*:]* *brāhmaṇavat*, *kṣatriyavat*, *sanā*, *sanat*, *sanāt*, *upadhā*, *tiras*, *antarā*, *antareṇa*, *jyok*, *kam*, *śam*.

*Sahasā*, *vinā*, *nānā*, *svasti*, *svadhā*, *alam*, *vaṣaṭ*, *vauṣaṭ*, *anyat*, *upāṃśu*, *kṣamā*, *vihāyasā*, *doṣā*, *mṛṣā*, *mithyā*, *mudhā*, *purā*, *mithas*, *mithas*, *prāyas*, *muhus*, *pravāhukam*, *pravāhikā*, *āryahalam*, *abhīkṣṇam*, *sākam*, *sārdham*, *namas*, *hiruk*, *dhik*, *am*, *ām*, *pratām*, *praśān*, *pratān*, *mā*, *māṅ*. This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class).

*ca*, *vā*, *ha*, *aha*, *eva*, *evam*, *nūm*, *śaśvat*, *yugapat*, *bhūyam*, *kūpat*, *kuvit*, *net*, *cet*, *caṇ*, *kaccit*, *kiṃcit*, *yatra*, *naha*, *hanta*, *mākir*, *mākīm*, *nakiḥ*, *ākim*, *māṅ*, *nañ*, *yāvat*, *tāvat*, *tvai*, *dvai*, *rai*, *śrauṣaṭ*, *vauṣaṭ*, *svāhā*, *svadhā*, *tum*, *tathā*, *hi*, *khalu*, *kila*, *atho*, *atha*, *suṣṭhu*, *sma*, *ādaha*; as well as those that resemble prepositions (*upasarga*), case endings (*vibhakti*), accents (*svara*), and indeclinables (*pratirūpaka*).

*avadatta*, *ahayuḥ*, *astikṣīrā*, *a*, *ā*, *i*, *ī*, *u*, *ū*, *e*, *ai*, *o*, *au*, *paśu*, *śukam*, *yathākathāca*, *pāṭ*, *pyāṭ*, *aṅga*, *hai*, *he*, *bhoḥ*, *aye*, *dya*, *vipu*, *ekapade*, *yut*, *ātaḥ*; the group beginning with *ca* (*cādi*) is also an open-ended class (*ākṛtigaṇa*). (SK 448) A taddhita suffix that does not express all case-relations is also [an indeclinable]. (A 1.1.38)

That which does not take on any case-ending (*vibhakti*) should be an indeclinable (*avyaya*), provided it ends in a secondary suffix (*taddhita*). A complete enumeration must be made: *tasil* and others up to *pāśap*; *śas* and others up to the compound-final suffixes (*samāsānta*); *am*, *ām*; words having the sense of "having done" (*kṛtvortha*); *tas* and *vat*; and *nānā* and *añ*. Therefore, it is not [an indeclinable] here: *pacatikalpam* and *pacatirūpam*. **SK 449:** *kṛnmejantaḥ* (A 1.1.39).
That which ends in a *kṛt* suffix ending in *m* or *e* shall be an indeclinable. Examples: *smāraṃ smāram*, *jīvase*, *pibadhyai*.
SK 450: That which ends in *ktvā*, *tosun*, or *kasun* shall be an indeclinable (*avyaya*). Examples: *kṛtvā*, *udetoḥ*, *visṛpaḥ*.
SK 451: And the *avyayībhāva* compound is also [an indeclinable].

*adhihari* / [SK 452] *avyayād āpsupaḥ* (A 2.4.82): There shall be elision (*luk*) of the feminine suffix *āp* and of case endings (*sup*) prescribed after an indeclinable (*avyaya*). [Example: *tatra śālāyām* ("there, in the hall"). Because the rule specifies what is "prescribed" (*vihita*), there is no elision here: *atyuccaisau*. Although the extension of a grammatical operation to that which ends in a specific element (*tadantavidhi*) applies to the technical designation of "indeclinable," it nevertheless does not apply to secondary (*gauṇa*) usage. The mention of the suffix *āp* is redundant because indeclinables lack gender. As stated in the *Bhāṣya*: "That which remains unchanged across the three genders, all case-endings, and all numbers—that is an indeclinable. This scriptural definition intends to exclude the presence of gender, number, and case-role (*kāraka*).

Bhāguri maintains that there is the elision of *i* after the prefixes *ava* and *api*, as well as the substitution of *āp* for the final vowel of words ending in consonants, as in *vācā*, *niśā*, and *diśā*; likewise, [the forms] *vagāhaḥ* and *avagāhaḥ*, and *pidhānam* and *apidhānam*.
Section 15: The Section on Feminine Suffixes.
SK 453: *striyām* (A 4.1.3). [The suffix *ṭāp* is applied] in the feminine.
This is a governing rule (*adhikāra*); it extends as far as the word "of those capable" (*samarthānām*).
[Pāṇini 4.1.4: *ajādyataṣ ṭāp*.

The suffix *ṭāp* shall be applied when femininity—whether belonging to words beginning with *ajā-* or ending in short *a*—is to be expressed. The mention of *ajā-* and so forth is for the purpose of setting aside the application of *ṅīṣ* and *ṅīp*. Examples: *ajā*, [and] *khaṭvā* (from the rule *ataḥ*). Because the feminine gender is qualified by the group beginning with *ajā-*, it does not apply here: *pañcājī* (five goats). Here, the suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule *dvigoḥ*; for in this case, the feminine gender resides in the collective aggregate (*samāhāra*) which is the meaning of the compound. Examples where *ṅīṣ* would otherwise apply by the rule governing genus (*jāti*) are: *ajā*, *eḍakā*, *aśvā*, *caṭakā*, *mūṣikā*. Examples where *ṭāp* applies despite the presence of other conditions are: *bālā*, *vatsā*, *hoḍā*, *mandā*, *vilātā*.

In these cases, the suffix *ṅīp* is obtained because they denote age (*vayasi prathama*). [The following are examples: from *saṃ*, *bhastrā*, *ajina*, *śaṇa*, and *piṇḍa* followed by *phala*: *saṃphalā*, *bhastraphalā*. Here, the short vowel is applied by the rule *ṅyāpoḥ*. From *sat*, *ada*, *kāṇḍa*, *prānta*, *śata*, and *eka* followed by *puṣpa*: *satpuṣpā*, *prākpuṣpā*, *pratyakpuṣpā*. *Śūdrā* is used when it denotes a caste (*jāti*) and is not preceded by the word *mahat*; however, in the sense of a female connection with a male (*puṃyoga*), it is *śūdrī*. Why "not preceded by *mahat*"? [Example: *mahāśūdrī*. [Other examples: *kruñcā*, *uṣṇihā*, *devaviśā*, *jyeṣṭhā*, and *madhyamā*—these also apply even in the sense of a female connection with a male.

The word *kokilā* is also formed with the suffix *āp* after a class name (*jāti*). From the word *mūla*, the feminine suffix *āp* is applied by the rule *naño mūlāt*: *amūlā*. By the rule *ṛnnebhyo ṅīp*, we have *kartrī* and *daṇḍinī*. SK 455: *ugitaś ca* (A 4.1.6). The suffix *ṅīp* shall be applied in the feminine after a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) ending in an *ugit* vowel. Examples: *pacantī*, *bhavantī*, *dīvyantī*. [In these cases,] the augment *num* is added by the rule *śapśyanoḥ*. In the sūtra *ugidacām*, the mention of the term *aj* (vowel) restricts the application such that if an operation based on being *ugit* is to apply to a verbal root, it applies only to the root *añc*.
