*Madhyamaḥ* / [SK 1379] The suffix *a* may be added to the word *madhya* in the sense of "present" (*sāmpratika*) according to A 4.3.9. One who is devoid of excellence and deficiency is a "middling" (*madhya*) grammarian. "Middling wood" (*madhyaṃ dāru*) means neither too short nor too long.

SK 1380 *dvīpād anusamudraṃ yañ* (A 4.3.10): The suffix *yañ* is applied after the word *dvīpa* when it refers to an island situated near the ocean; for example, *dvaipyam* (m. or *dvaipyā* (f.). SK 1381 *kālāṭ ṭhañ* (A 4.3.11): The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word denoting time.

The suffix *ṭhañ* shall occur after words expressing time. Examples: *māsikam* (monthly), *sāṃvatsarikam* (annual), *sāyaṃprātikaḥ* (occurring at evening and morning), *paunaḥpunikaḥ* (repeated). How then are we to explain such usages as Kālidāsa’s *śārvarasya tamaso niṣiddhaye* ("for the warding off of the darkness of night") and Bhāravi’s *anuditauṣasarāga-* ("without the rising glow of dawn"), as well as expressions like *samānakālīnam* ("contemporary") and *prākkālīnam* ("belonging to a previous time")? Authoritative grammarians maintain that these are merely corruptions (*apabhraṃśas*). In this context, the governing rule "born therein" (*tatra jātaḥ*) applies up until the section on time (*kāla-adhikāra*). According to A 4.3.12, the suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after the word *śarad* when forming a derivative meaning "a *śrāddha* ceremony. This is an exception to the suffix *ṛtvaṇ*. Example: *śāradikaṃ śrāddham* ("a *śrāddha* performed in autumn").

SK 1383 *vibhāṣā rogātapayoḥ* (A 4.3.13): [The suffix *ṭhañ*] is optionally applied after the words *śarad* when meaning "disease" or "heat. Thus, one may say either *śāradikaḥ* or *śāradaḥ* for a disease or heat. Why [is it optional] in these two cases? [Because in other senses it is not optional: *śāradaṃ dadhi* ("autumnal curd"). SK 1384 *niśāpradoṣābhyāṃ ca* (A 4.3.14): [The suffix *ṭhañ* is optionally applied] also after the words *niśā* and *pradoṣa*. Thus, one may say either *naiśikaḥ* or *naiśaḥ*, and *prādoṣikaḥ* or *prādoṣaḥ*. Why [is it optional]? Because in other senses it is not optional: *naiśaṃ jyotiḥ* ("nocturnal light") and *prādoṣaṃ tamaḥ* ("the darkness of nightfall"). SK 1385 *śvasas tu ṭhañ* (A 4.3.15): After the word *śvas*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied [to denote what occurs on that day]. Thus, *śauvastikaḥ*. SK 1386 *kālāt ṭhañ* (A 4.3.11): The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word denoting time [to express what occurs at that time]. Thus, *māsikaḥ*, *sāṃvatsarikaḥ*. SK 1387 *tena nivṛttam* (A 4.3.12): The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word denoting time to express "completed within that [time]. Thus, *māsena nivṛttaṃ māsikam*, *sāṃvatsarikam*. SK 1388 *tasmai prabhavati saṃtāpādibhyaḥ* (A 4.3.13): The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after words such as *saṃtāpa* to express "capable of producing that. Thus, *saṃtāpikaḥ*, *vaiśvāsikaḥ*. SK 1389 *prakṛṣṭe ṭhañ* (A 4.3.14): The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word denoting time to express "excessive [in duration]. Thus, *māsikaḥ saṃtāpaḥ* ("an excessive fever lasting a month"), *sāṃvatsarikaḥ*. SK 1390 *so'sya nivāsaḥ* (A 4.3.89): The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word denoting time to express "this is his place of residence [for that duration]. Thus, *māsiko vyādhiḥ* ("a fever lasting a month"), *sāṃvatsarikaḥ*. SK 1391 *adhikam* (A 4.3.90): The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word denoting time to express "additional [by that amount]. Thus, *māsiko'dhiko vyādhiḥ* ("a fever exceeding a month"). SK 1392 *tad asyāṃ praharaṇam iti krīḍāyāṃ ṇaḥ* (A 4.2.57): The suffix *ṇa* is applied after a word denoting a weapon to form a feminine noun meaning "a game in which this is the weapon. Thus, *daṇḍāḥ praharaṇam asyāṃ krīḍāyāṃ dāṇḍā*. SK 1393 *śalabhakavadibhyaś ca* (A 4.2.58): The suffix *ṇa* is applied after words such as *śalabha* and *vada* to form a feminine noun meaning "a game in which these are used. Thus, *śālābhā*, *vadvā*. SK 1394 *gostriyor upasarjanasya* (A 1.2.48): A feminine base ending in *go* or a short vowel, when it is a subordinate member (*upasarjana*) in a compound, is shortened. Thus, *dvidaṇḍyā*, *triśaṅkuyā*. SK 1395 *na kroḍādibahvacaḥ* (A 4.1.56): The suffix *ṅīṣ* is not applied after a word beginning with *kroḍa* or a word having more than two syllables. Thus, *kroḍā*, *bahvacaḥ*. SK 1396 *nityaṃ saṃjñāchandasoḥ* (A 4.1.29): The suffix *ṅīṣ* is invariably applied after a word ending in *go* when it is a proper name or in Vedic literature. Thus, *gaurī nāma nadī*, *gaurī chandasi*. SK 1397 *pūtakratu-ādibhyaś ca* (A 4.1.36): The suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied after words such as *pūtakratu* to form a feminine noun. Thus, *pūtakratur nāma devatā pūtakratī*. SK 1398 *manor au vā* (A 4.1.39): For the word *manu*, the substitution of *au* is optionally applied before the suffix *ṅīṣ*. Thus, *manāvī* or *manuḥ*. SK 1399 *varṇād anudāttāt topadhāt to naḥ* (A 4.1.39): The suffix *ṭāp* is applied after a monosyllabic word denoting a color that is anudātta and has *t* as its penultimate letter; furthermore, *n* is substituted for the final *t*. Thus, *śoṇā*, *haritā*. SK 1400 *anyato ṅīṣ* (A 4.1.40): The suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied after a word denoting a color that is not covered by the previous rule. Thus, *kalmāṣī*, *piśaṅgī*. SK 1401 *jāter astrīviṣayād ayopadhāt* (A 4.1.63): The suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied after a word denoting a genus (*jāti*) that does not refer to a female, provided it does not have *y* as its penultimate letter. Thus, *brāhmaṇī*, *balākā*. SK 1402 *pākakarṇaparṇapuṣpaphalamūlavālottarapadāc ca* (A 4.1.64): The suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied after a word ending in *pāka*, *karṇa*, *parṇa*, *puṣpa*, *phala*, *mūla*, or *bāla* when they are the final members of a compound. Thus, *śitipācikā*, *śitipākkā*; *dīrghakarṇī*, *dīrghakarṇā*; *śālaparṇī*, *śālaparṇā*; *śaṅkhapuṣpī*, *śaṅkhapuṣpā*; *mūlaphalī*, *mūlaphalā*; *śaṣpamūlī*, *śaṣpamūlā*; *ekabālī*, *ekabālā*. SK 1403 *itaḥ
Or the suffix *ṭhañ* may be applied: *naiśikam* or *naiśam*; *prādoṣikam* or *prādoṣam*.
According to A 4.3.15, *śvasas tuṭ ca*, the suffix *ṭhañ* may optionally be applied after the word *śvas*, and the augment *tuṭ* is added to it.

SK 1386: And for *dvāra* and the others—namely *dvāra*, *svar*, *vyalkaśa*, *svasti*, *svara*, *sphayakṛt*, *svādu*, *mṛdu*, *śvas*, *śvan*, and *sva*—there is no *vṛddhi* [substitution], but rather the substitution of *aij*. [Example: *śauvastikam*. SK 1387:
The suffix *aṇ* is applied after words beginning with *saṃdhivelā*, as well as after names of seasons (*ṛtu*) and lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*).

The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied after words denoting seasons and asterisms that function as time-words, beginning with *saṃdhivelā*. For example: *sāndhivelam*, meaning "occurring at twilight" (*saṃdhivelā*). *Graiṣmam* ("belonging to summer"), *taiṣam* ("belonging to the month of Taiṣa"). [The relevant time-words are: *saṃdhivelā*, *saṃdhyā*, *amāvāsyā*, *trayodaśī*, *caturdaśī*, *paurṇamāsī*, and *pratipat*. After the word *saṃvatsara*, when referring to fruit or a festival (*parvan*), [the suffix *aṇ* is applied]: *sāṃvatsaram phalam* or *sāṃvatsaram parvam* ("fruit or festival occurring annually"). In other cases, the suffix *aṇ* becomes *u* by rule A 4.3.21: *sāṃvatsarūkam* ("occurring every year"). By rule A 4.3.17, *prāvṛṣ* takes the suffix *eṇya*: *prāvṛṣeṇyaḥ* ("belonging to the rainy season").

SK 1389: *varṣābhyaṣ ṭhak* (A 4.3.18). [The suffix] *ṭhak* is applied after the word *varṣā*. For example: *vārṣikaṃ vāsaḥ* ("garment suitable for the rainy season"). This is according to the rule *kālāt sādhupuṣpyatpacyamāneṣu*, which prescribes the suffix in the sense of "suitable for" (*sādhvarthe*). SK 1390: *sarvatrāṇ ca talopaś ca* (A 4.3.22). [The suffix] *aṇ* is applied everywhere [after words denoting time], and there is the elision (*lopa*) of the final syllable (*talopa*).

The suffix *aṇ* is applied after *hemanta*, with the elision of the final *t*, in the sense of the Vedas and common usage (*loka*). Because of the word "and" (*ca*), the suffix *ṛtvaṇ* optionally applies as well. Thus: *haimana* or *haimantam*. [From the sūtra: *sāyāṃciraṃprāhṇeprage 'vyayebhyaṣṭayuṭyulau tuṭ ca* (A 4.3.23): After the indeclinables *sāyam*, *ciram*, *prāhṇe*, and *prage*, the suffixes *ṭyu*, *ṭyuṭ*, and *yul* are applied, along with the augment *tuṭ*.

After the four indeclinables beginning with *sāyam* and other words denoting time, the suffixes *ṭyu* and *ṭyul* occur, and for these two, the augment *tuṭ* is added. The *tuṭ* is placed before the initial element [of the suffix], as indicated by the rule stating "in the non-today" (*anadyatane*) and so forth. Thus: *sāyantanam*, *cirantanam*. For *prāhṇa* and *prage*, the final vowel *e* is prescribed by nipātana (irregular substitution). Thus: *prāhṇetanam*, *prāgetanam*. It should be stated that after *doṣā*, *divā*, *cira*, *parut*, and *parāri*, the suffix *tna* occurs. Thus: *doṣātanam*, *divātanam*, *ciratnam*, *parutnam*, *parāritnam*. After *agra* and so forth, the suffix *ḍimac* occurs. Thus: *agrimam*, *ādimam*, *paścimam*. And also after *anta*: *antimam*.

SK 1392 *vibhāṣā pūrvāhṇāparāhṇābhyām* (A 4.3.24): After these two [words], the suffixes *ṭya* and *ṭyaka* optionally occur, and they have the augment *tuṭ*. In the alternative case, the suffix *ṭhañ* occurs. Examples: *pūrvāhṇetanaḥ* (where there is no elision of the final vowel by the rule *ghakālataneṣu*). However, when the analysis is "that which has endured the forenoon" (*pūrvāhṇaḥ soḍho 'sya*), the forms are *pūrvāhṇatanam*, *aparāhṇatanam*, *paurvāhṇikam*, and *āparāhṇikam*. SK 1393 *tatra jātaḥ* (A 4.3.25): [The suffixes taught from A 4.3.12 onwards occur after a word denoting time] in the sense of "born there."

SK 1407 (A 4.3.34): *śraviṣṭhā-phalgunī-anurādhā-svāti-tiṣya-punarvasu-hasta-viśākhā-aṣāḍhā-bahulāl luk*.

SK 1408 (A 4.2.49): *luk taddhitaluki*. When a secondary suffix (*taddhita*) is elided by *luk*, [the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is also elided].

One born under Śraviṣṭhā is called *śraviṣṭha*; likewise for *phalguna* and so forth. An addition [to the rule] is made regarding feminine forms derived from *citrā*, *revatī*, and *rohiṇī*: one born under *citrā* is *citrā*, *revatī*, and *rohiṇī*. When the suffix *taddhita* is elided by the rule "elision after these two when the *taddhita* is elided" (*ābhyāṃ luk taddhitaluki*), the feminine marker *ṅīṣ* is applied again because the group beginning with *pippalī* is an open-ended class (*ākṛtigaṇa*). Regarding *phalgunī* and *aṣāḍhā*, the suffixes *ṭāp* and *ṅīṣ* should be stated; this applies only in the feminine: *phalgunī*, *aṣāḍhā*. In the case of the *proṣṭhapadā* constellation, there shall be *vṛddhi* substitution for the first vowel of the second member (*uttarapada*) when a suffix beginning with *ñ*, *ṇ*, or *k* is added in the sense of "born under" (*jātārtha*). For example: *proṣṭhapadāsu jātaḥ* → *proṣṭhapādo māṇavakaḥ* ("a boy born under Proṣṭhapadā"). Why is it said "when [the suffix] *ñ* follows"? Consider: *proṣṭhapadāsu bhavaḥ* → *prauṣṭapadaḥ* ("existing under Proṣṭhapadā"). Because the plural number is used in the rule, the synonym (*paryāya*) is also included: *bhādrapādaḥ*. SK 1410: *sthānāntagośālasvaraśālāc ca* (A 4.3.35). There shall be elision (*luk*) of the suffix denoting "born under" after these: *go-sthāna*, *go-śāla*, *khara-śāla*, and *svara-śālā*. Examples: *go-sthānaḥ*, *go-śālaḥ*, *khara-śālaḥ*. When the word is neuter according to the rule *vibhāṣā senā-* etc., there is shortening of the final vowel.

SK 1411: *vatsaśālābhijidaśvayukśatabhiṣajo vā* (A 4.3.36). After these [words], there may optionally be elision (*luk*) of the suffix expressing the sense of "born under" (*jātārtha*). Examples: born under *vatsaśālā* is *vatsaśālaḥ* or *vātsaśālaḥ*, and so forth. Regarding the suffix *aṇ* which has been reintroduced for the sense of "born under," it should be stated that it may optionally take the augment *ḍi*. Examples: *śātabhiṣaḥ*, *śātabhiṣajaḥ*, or *śatabhiṣak*. SK 1412: *nakṣatrebhyo bahulam* (A 4.3.37). After words denoting lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*), the suffix expressing the sense of "born under" is diversely applied.

There is generally elision (*luk*) of the suffix expressing the sense of "born" (*jāta*). Examples: *rohiṇaḥ*, *rauhiṇaḥ*. By rule A 4.3.38, *kṛta-labdha-krīta-kuśalāḥ*, the suffix is applied in the sense of "located there" (*tatra*). Example: one who is made, obtained, bought, or skilled in *srughna* is called *sraughnaḥ*.

SK 1414 *prāyabhavaḥ* (A 4.3.39): [The suffix *ṭhak*] is applied after [a word denoting a place], provided that it means "mostly occurring there. For example, one who mostly (*prāyeṇa*) or frequently (*bāhulyena*) resides in *Srugghna* is called *sraughna*.
SK 1415 *upajānūpakarṇopanīveṣṭak* (A 4.3.40).
*aupajānukaḥ* (reaching to the knees), *aupakarṇikaḥ* (reaching to the ears), *aupanīvikaḥ* (reaching to the neck).

one who is born in Sṛghna is called *sraughnaḥ*.
SK 1417: The suffix *ḍhañ* is applied after the word *kośa*. Example:
*kauśeyaṃ vastram* ("silk cloth"). SK 1418: The suffix *ḍhañ* is applied after the word *kāla* when it refers to things that flower or ripen at the proper time.

*Haimanta* means a wall suitable for the winter season; *vāsantyaḥ* refers to jasmine creepers that bloom in spring; *śāradāḥ* refers to rice crops that ripen in autumn. And according to [Pāṇini] 4.3.44, *upte ca*:
*haimantāḥ* refers to barley seeds sown in winter.
SK 1420: After *āśvayujī*, the suffix *vuñ* [is applied] (A 4.3.45);
this is an exception to *ṭhañ*. *Āśvayujakā māṣāḥ* means "beans sown in the month of Āśvayuja.
SK 1421: After *grīṣma* and *vasanta*, [the suffix *vuñ* is applied] optionally (A 4.3.46).

In the sense of a lunar fortnight (*pakṣa*), the suffix *ṛtvaṇ* is applied: *gāiṣmakaṃ*, *graiṣmam*, *vāsantakaṃ*, *vāsantam*. Regarding what is to be given as a debt (*deyam-ṛṇe*), [the rule] "from time" (*kālāt*) applies: a debt to be paid in a month is *māsikam*.
Pāṇini 4.3.48: *kalāpy-aśvattha-yava-busāt vun*.

When peacocks (*mayūra*) possess their plumage (*kalāpa*), that time is metaphorically called "plumed" (*kalāpin*); a debt to be paid at that time is *kalāpaka*. The fruit of the *aśvattha* tree is called *aśvattha*; the time when it is possessed of such fruit is also called *aśvattha*. A debt to be paid at the time when the *aśvattha* trees bear fruit is *aśvatthaka*. A debt to be paid at the time when barley chaff (*yavabusam*) arises is *yavabusaka*. Pāṇini 4.3.49: *grīṣmā-varasamād vuñ*. [A debt to be paid] in the summer (*grīṣma*) or the latter part of the year (*avarasama*) is denoted by the suffix *vuñ*.

A debt to be paid in summer is *graiṣmaka*; [it is also] *āvarasamakam*. According to Pāṇini 4.3.50, *saṃvatsarāgrahāyaṇībhyāṃ ṭhañ ca*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied, and by the word "ca" (*and*), *vuñ* is also included: *sāṃvatsarikam* and *sāṃvatsarakam*; *āgrahāyaṇikam* and *āgrahāyaṇakam*.

SK 1426 *vyāharati mṛgaḥ* (A 4.3.51): After a word denoting time ending in the locative case, suffixes such as *aṇ* and others are applied in the sense of "he cries out," provided that the one who cries out is a wild animal (*mṛga*). For example: "He cries out at night" → *naiśo mṛgaḥ* ("a night-crying animal") or *naiśikaḥ*.
SK 1427 *tad asya soḍham* (A 4.3.52): [The suffix *khañ* is applied after a word denoting time ending in the locative case] in the sense of "that was endured by him."

[The suffix *ṭhañ*] is applied after [words denoting] time; thus, *niśā* refers to study associated with the night, and that which is endured during that [time] is *naiśa*. Similarly, *naiśika*. By the rule *tatra bhavaḥ* (A 4.3.53), from *srughna*, we have *sraughna*; likewise, *rāṣṭriya*.

SK 1429: The suffix *yat* is applied after words such as *diś* (direction), [yielding] *diśyam*; and after *varga* (class/group), [yielding] *vargyam*. SK 1430: The suffix *yat* is also applied after words denoting parts of the body.

*dantyam* / *karṇyam* / SK 1431: *prācāṃ nagarānte* (A 4.3.24). In the speech of the Easterners (*prācām*), when a member of a compound ending in *nagara* follows [the first member] in a region of the East, there is Vṛddhi substitution for the initial vowel of both the first member (*pūrvapada*) and the second member (*uttarapada*) before an affix marked with *ñ*, *ṇ*, or *k*. For example: that which exists in *Suhmanagara* is *sauhmanāgaraḥ*; *paurvanāgaraḥ*. Why "of the Easterners" (*prācām*)? *Managara* is in the North; that which exists there is *mānagaraḥ*.

SK 1432: For a *bahuvrīhi* compound ending in *jaṅgala*, *dhenu*, or *valaja*, the substitution of *vṛddhi* for the first vowel of the preceding member is optional before a suffix marked with *ñ*, *ṇ*, or *k*. In the case of a stem ending in *jaṅgala* and so forth, when it is the first member of a compound, *vṛddhi* is optionally substituted for the first vowel (*ac*) of that first member before a suffix beginning with *ñ*, *ṇ*, or *k*. Examples: *kurujaṅgale bhavam* ("produced in Kurujaṅgala") yields *kaurujaṅgalam* or *kaurujāṅgalam*. *vaiśvadhenavam* or *vaiśvadhainavam*. *sauvarṇavalajam* or *sauvarṇavālajam*. SK 1433: The suffix *ḍhañ* is applied after *dṛti*, *kukṣi*, *kalaśi*, *vasti*, *asthi*, and *ahi*.

*dārteya* (derived from *dṛti*, "leather bag"); *kaukṣeya* (from *kukṣi*, "belly"); *kalaśi* means a jar; that which is produced therein is *kālaśeya*; *bāsteya* (from *basti*, "bladder"); *āsteya* (from *āsi*, "sword"); *āheya* (from *ahi*, "serpent"). According to Pāṇini A 4.3.57, *grīvābhyo ’ṇ ca*: the suffix *aṇ* is added after *grīvā* ("neck"), and because of the word *ca* ("and"), the suffix *ḍhañ* is also applied. Thus: *graiveya* and *graiva*.

SK 1435 *gambhīrāñ ñyaḥ* (A 4.3.58): From the word *gambhīra*, the suffix *ñya* is applied [to form a word for what exists therein]. Thus, that which exists in the deep is *gāmbhīrya*. There is an extension of the rule to the word *pañcajana*. Thus, [one born from] the five people is *pāñcajanya*. SK 1436 *avyayībhāvāc ca* (A 4.3.59): And [the suffix *ñya* is applied] after an *avyayībhāva* compound.
*Pārimukhya* is derived from *parimukham bhavam*. This suffix is desired only after words such as *parimukha*; it does not apply here in the case of *aupakūlaḥ*.

By rule A 4.3.60, *antaḥ pūrvapadāt ṭhañ*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after an *avyayībhāva* compound; thus, from *veśmani*, we have *antarveśmam*. The suffix *ṭhañ* is intended to denote "that which exists therein" (*tatra bhavam*); hence, from *adhyātman*, we have *ādhyātmikam*.

The word *saupa* refers to a treatise (*grantha*) that explains the case endings (*sup*). Similarly, there are *taiṅa* and *kārta*. That which exists within the case endings is *saupam*. According to Pāṇini’s rule A 4.3.67, *bahvaco ’ntodāttāṭ ṭhañ*, the term *ṣatvaṇatva* refers to the grammatical rules (*śāstra*) that prescribe the substitution of *ṣ* and *ṇ*. A work that explains those rules, or that which pertains to them, is called *ṣātvaṇatvika*.

SK 1447: *kratuyajñebhyaś ca* (A 4.3.68). These two [terms] are well-known in the context of sacrifices accomplished by means of Soma. Since the desired result is established by the mention of either one, the fact that both are mentioned indicates that sacrifices not involving Soma (*asomaka*) are also included here. Examples: *āgniṣṭomikaḥ* (pertaining to the Agniṣṭoma), *vājapeyikaḥ*, *pākayajñikaḥ*, *nāvayajñikaḥ*. The plural number is for the purpose of excluding the application of the rule to the actual word-forms themselves. This rule is commenced for the sake of ensuring the final syllable is udātta. SK 1448: *adhyāyeṣv eva rṣaḥ* (A 4.3.69). [The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after words denoting Ṛṣis] only when they refer to chapters (*adhyāya*).

The suffix *ṭhañ* shall be applied after words denoting sages (*ṛṣi*)—which function as designations for the texts they have seen—to form a word meaning "in that [text]" or "the commentary thereon," provided it refers to a chapter (*adhyāya*). For example, a mantra seen by Vasiṣṭha is called *Vasiṣṭha*; a commentary on that, or something occurring therein, is a *Vāsiṣṭhika* chapter. Why "in chapters"? [To exclude cases such as: a *ṛc* verse belonging to Vasiṣṭha.

SK 1449 *pauroḍāśapuroḍāśāt ṣṭhan* (A 4.3.70): A mantra associated with the *puroḍāśa* is called *puroḍāśa*; that very [mantra] is *pauroḍāśa*. From that, the suffix *ṣṭhan* is applied. Thus: *pauroḍāśikaḥ*. SK 1450 *chandaso yad aṇau* (A 4.3.71).
*chandasya* / *chāndasaḥ*.

[SK 1451] *dvyaj-ṛg-brāhmaṇa-ṛk-prathamā-dhvara-puraścaraṇa-nāmākhyātāt ṭhak* (A 4.3.72): after a word consisting of two syllables, and after *ṛc*, *brāhmaṇa*, *ṛc*, *prathama*, *adhvara*, *puraścaraṇa*, a name, or a verb, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied. Examples: *aiṣṭikaḥ* (relating to the *iṣṭi*), *pāśukaḥ* (relating to the animal sacrifice); *cāturhotṛkaḥ* (relating to the *caturhotṛ* formulas); *brāhmaṇikaḥ* (relating to the *brāhmaṇa*); *ārcikaḥ* (relating to the *ṛc* collection), and so forth.

SK 1452 *aṇ-ṛgayanādibhyaḥ* (A 4.3.73): This is an exception (*apavāda*) to [the suffixes] beginning with *ṭhañ*. Examples: *ārgayanaḥ*, *aupaniṣadaḥ*, *vaiyākaraṇaḥ*. SK 1453 *tata āgataḥ* (A 4.3.74).
One who has come from Srughna is a *sraughna*. According to Pāṇini 4.3.75 (*ṭhak āyasthānebhyaḥ*), one who has come from a customs house (*śulkaśālā*) is a *śaulkaśālika*.

SK 1455: *śuṇḍikādibhyo ’ṇ* (A 4.3.76). This is an exception to [the suffixes] *ṭhak*, *cha*, and others [prescribed after words meaning] "place of business" (*āyasthāna*). Derived from *śuṇḍika* is *śauṇḍikaḥ*; *kārkaṇaḥ*; *tairthaḥ*. SK 1456: *vidyāyonisaṃbandhebhyo ’vuñ* (A 4.3.77). [The suffix] *vuñ* is applied after words denoting relationships through learning or birth.
*aupādhyāyakaḥ* ("belonging to a teacher"), *paitāmahakaḥ* ("belonging to a grandfather").

According to Pāṇini 4.3.78, *ṛtaṣ ṣṭhañ*, the suffix *ṣṭhañ* is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *vuñ*. Examples: *hautṛkam* ("the office of the *hotṛ* priest"), *bhrātṛkam* ("the office of a brother").

SK 1458: By the rule *pitur yac ca* (A 4.3.79), the suffixes *cha* and *ṭhañ* are applied [to the word *pitṛ*]. By the rule *rīṅ ṛtaḥ*, *ṛ* is replaced by *rī*. Then, by the rule *yasyeti ca*, the final vowel and following consonant are elided. Thus, we have *pitryam* and *paitṛkam*. SK 1459: According to the rule *gotrād aṅkavat* (A 4.3.80), [the suffixes taught for *gotra*] apply to words denoting lineage (*gotra*) in the same manner as they do for *aṅka*.
*Baiddam* (from Bida), *gārgam*, *dākṣam*, *aupagavakam*.

SK 1460: *nañaḥ śucīśvarakṣetrajñakuśalanipuṇānām* (A 7.3.30). When the negative particle *nañ* precedes the five words beginning with *śuci*, the first vowel of these five undergoes *vṛddhi* substitution, while the first vowel of the preceding member optionally does so, when a suffix beginning with *ñ* or *ñi* follows. Examples: *āśaucam* / *aśaucam* *ānaiśvaryam* / *anaiśvaryam* *ākṣaitrajñam* / *akṣaitrajñam* *ākauśalam* / *akauśalam* *ānaipuṇam* / *anaipuṇam*
SK 1461: After words denoting a cause (*hetu*) or a person (*manuṣya*), the suffix *rūpya* is optionally employed [in the sense of "come from" (*samāgata*)].

*Samād āgatam* → *samarūpyam* / *viṣamarūpyam*. In the alternative case, by virtue of belonging to the *gaha*-class, the suffix *cha* is applied: *samīyam* / *viṣamīyam*. [After a personal name: *devadattarūpyam* / *devadattīyam* / *daivadattam*. SK 1462:
And the suffix *mayaṭ* [is also employed after a word denoting a cause or a person in the same sense].
[The suffix *mayaṭ* is applied] after [words denoting] "consisting of equality," "consisting of inequality," or "consisting of Devadatta.

SK 1463: [The suffix *mayaṭ*] is also applied after a word denoting the source (*prabhava*), provided that the word *tataḥ* ("from that") is understood. For example: *haimavatī gaṅgā* ("the Gaṅgā originates from the Himavat").
SK 1464: *vidūrāñ ñyaḥ* (A 4.3.85). From *vidūra*, [the suffix] *ñya* [is applied].
A gem originating from Vidūra is a *vaidūrya* gem.
SK 1465: *tad-gacchati pathi-dūtayoḥ* (A 4.3.85). [The suffix *ñya* is applied after a word denoting a place] when it means "going to that" in the sense of a path or a messenger.

*sraughnaḥ* means "going to Srughna," referring to a path or a messenger. (SK 1466) *abhiniṣkrāmati dvāram* (A 4.3.86): with the word *tat* [implied], [the suffix *aṇ* is applied]. For example: *srughnam abhiniṣkrāmati sraughnam kānyakubjadvāram*, meaning "the gate of Kānyakubja that leads out toward Srughna."

SK 1467: *tad* [is used] in the sense of "composed concerning that" (A 4.3.87). For example: a work composed concerning the *Śārīraka* is called *Śārīrakīya*. However, the expression *Śārīraka-bhāṣya* (the Commentary on the Śārīraka) occurs by way of metaphorical identification (*abhedopacāra*).
SK 1468: The suffix *cha* is applied after [words ending in] *śiśukranda*, *yamasabha*, dvandva compounds, *indrajanana*, and so forth (A 4.3.88).

*Śiśukranda* refers to the crying of children; a treatise composed concerning that is called *śiśukrandīya*. *Yamasabha* is the assembly of Yama; the neuter gender is due to irregular derivation (*nipātana*). [A treatise concerning it is] *yamasabhīya*. [Other examples are] *kirātārjunīya*, and the group beginning with *indrajana* is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (a class defined by its form). [Examples include] *indrajana-nīya* and *viruddhabhojana-nīya*. SK 1469: *so 'sya nivāsaḥ* (A 4.3.89). [The suffix *cha* is applied after a word denoting a place when the sense is] "that is his residence. For example, one whose residence is *Srugghna* is *sraughna*.

SK 1470: *abhijanaś ca* (A 4.3.90). One whose *abhijana* is Srughna is called *sraughna*. The distinction is as follows: that where one dwells oneself is the *nivāsa*; that where one's ancestors have lived is the *abhijana*. SK 1471: *āyudhajīvibhyaś chaḥ parvate* (A 4.3.91). [The suffix *cha* is added after words denoting those who live by weapons when followed by the word *parvata*.]

The suffix *cha* shall be applied after a word denoting a mountain ending in the nominative case, when used as a word for "lineage" (*abhijana*), in the sense of "belonging to this. For example: *hṛdgola*. Those weapon-bearers whose lineage is the Hṛdgola mountain are called *hṛdgolīyāḥ*. Why "weapon-bearer"? [Consider: those twice-born ones whose lineage is the Ṛkṣoda mountain are called *ārkṣodā* brāhmaṇas.
By rule A 4.3.92, *śaṇḍikādibhyo ’ñyaḥ*: the suffix *añ* is applied after words such as *śaṇḍika*.
One whose lineage is Śaṇḍika is *śāṇḍikyaḥ*.

SK 1473: *sindhu-takṣaśilādibhyo ’ṇ-añ-au* (A 4.3.93). After *sindhu*, *takṣaśilā*, and so forth, the suffixes *aṇ* and *añ* are applied in the sense [of place of origin] already mentioned. From *sindhu*, [with *aṇ*] we have *saindhavaḥ*. From *takṣaśilā*, the city, being his native place (*abhijana*), [with *añ*] we have *tākṣaśilaḥ*. SK 1474: *tūdī-salātura-varmatī-kūcavārāḍ ḍhak-chaṇ-ḍhañ-yak-aḥ* (A 4.3.94). After *tūdī*, *salātura*, *varmatī*, and *kūcavāra*, the suffixes *ḍhak*, *chaṇ*, *ḍhañ*, and *yak* are respectively applied in the same sense.
*Tūdī* is his native land (*abhijana*); thus he is a *taudeya*, a *śālāturīya*, a *vārmateya*, or a *kaucavārya*.

(SK 1475) Regarding the suffix for "devotion" (*bhakti*): the phrase *so 'sya* ("that belongs to him") is understood to carry over. That which is resorted to or served is called *bhakti*. One whose devotion is to *Srugghna* is a *sraughna*.

SK 1476: After a word that does not denote a conscious being (*acitta*) and after words denoting non-places (*adeśa*) and non-times (*akāla*), the suffix *ṭhak* is applied [to form patronymics and designations of devotion]. *Apūpā bhaktir asya* ("this is his devotion to cakes") → *āpūpikaḥ*. *pāyasikaḥ*. Why "not denoting a conscious being"? [Example: *daivadattaḥ*. Why "non-place"? [Example: *sraughnaḥ*. Why "non-time"? [Example: *graiṣmaḥ*. SK 1477: After the word *mahārāja*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied [to form patronymics and designations of devotion].
The Mahārājika [deities].
SK 1478: After the words *vāsudeva* and *arjuna*, the suffix *vun* is applied [to form patronymics]. Examples: *vāsudevakaḥ*, *arjunakaḥ*.
SK 1479: After words denoting a *gotra* (lineage) or a *kṣatriya* (warrior), the suffix *vuñ* is applied diversely.

This is an exception to the rule for *aṇ*. Because it is subsequent [in the order of rules], it subverts the suffix *cha* prescribed after *vṛddha* stems. For example: *glucukāyaniḥ* is his devotion (*bhakti*) → *glaucukāyanakaḥ*; *nākulakaḥ*. Due to the inclusion of the term "optionally" (*bahulagrahaṇāt*), it does not apply here: *pāṇinaḥ* is his devotion → *pāṇinīyaḥ*. SK 1480: For those whose names are derived from a country (*janapadinām*), everything [including gender and number] is like that of the country itself, provided they have the same form as the name of the country when expressed in the plural. (A 4.3.100)

When words denoting the lords of a country (*janapada*) are used in the plural, they behave like words denoting the country itself—provided they are homophonous (*samānaśruti*)—in that both the suffix and the base apply in the same manner as they do for the country. The suffixes taught in the section beginning with *janapadatadavadhyoś ca* are extended here by analogy. For example: *aṅgā* (the country of Aṅga) is his devotion; thus, *aṅgakaḥ*. Or: *aṅgāḥ* (the Kṣatriyas of Aṅga) are his devotion; thus, *aṅkaḥ*. Why "of those denoting a country" (*janapadinām*)? Consider: *pañcālāḥ* (the Brāhmaṇas of Pañcāla) are his devotion; thus, *pāñcālaḥ*. Here, the word denotes people, not the country. Why "by a country" (*janapadena*)? Consider: *pauravaḥ* (the king Paurava) is his devotion; thus, *pauravīyaḥ*. Here, the word denotes a person, not a country.
SK 1481: By the rule *tena proktam* (A 4.3.101), that which was proclaimed by Pāṇini is called *pāṇinīya*.
SK 1482: By the rule *tittirivaratantukhaṇḍikokhāc chaṇ* (A 4.3.102).
The term *chandobrāhmaṇāni* refers to that [subject matter]. Those who study what was proclaimed by Tittiri are called *taittirīya*.
According to Pāṇini’s rule A 4.3.103 (*kāśyapakauśikābhyām ṛṣibhyām ṇiniḥ*), those who study what was proclaimed by the sages Kāśyapa and Kauśika are called *kāśyapinaḥ*.

SK 1484: *kalāpivaiśampāyanāntevāsibhyaś ca* (A 4.3.104). [The suffix *cha* is applied] after the names of pupils of Kalāpin and Vaiśampāyana. [Example: *haridruṇā proktam adhīyate* ("they study what was taught by Haridru") → *hāridraviṇaḥ*. After the names of pupils of Vaiśampāyana: *ālambinaḥ*. SK 1485: *purāṇaprokteṣu brāhmaṇakalpeṣu* (A 4.3.105). [The suffix *cha* is applied] after [the name of a teacher] in reference to Brāhmaṇas and Kalpas proclaimed in ancient times.

The suffix *ṇini* occurs after a word ending in the third case in the sense of "proclaimed by"; provided that what is proclaimed are Brāhmaṇas or Kalpas that have been proclaimed by ancient sages (*purāṇaproktāḥ*). [The word] *purāṇa* means "ancient. Examples: *bhallu*, *bhāllavinaḥ*; *śāṭyāyana*, *śāṭyāyaninaḥ*. Regarding the *kalpa*: *paiṅgī kalpaḥ* ("the Kalpa proclaimed by Piṅga"). Why say "ancient" (*purāṇa*)? [Counter-examples: *yājñavalkyāni brāhmaṇāni* ("Brāhmaṇas [proclaimed by] Yājñavalkya"), *āśmarathaḥ kalpaḥ* ("the Kalpa [proclaimed by] Āśmaratha"). [In these cases, the suffix is *aṇ*, and there is elision of the *ya* of the patronymic suffix according to A 6.4.151. Pāṇini’s rule A 4.3.106 states: *śaunakādibhyaś chandasi* ("after *śaunaka* and others, the suffix *ṇini* is used in the Veda").
When the Vedic literature (*chandas*) is the object to be expressed, the suffix *ṇini* is applied after these [words]. Those who study what was proclaimed by Śaunaka are called *śaunakinaḥ*.
Regarding A 4.3.107, *kaṭhacarakāl luk*:
there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix applied to that which was proclaimed by Kalāpin. Those who study what was proclaimed by Kaṭha are *kaṭhāḥ*; likewise, *carakāḥ*.

SK 1488: *kalāpino ’ṇ* (A 4.3.108). Those who study what was taught by Kalāpin are called *Kālāpāḥ*. Regarding the elision of the suffix *ṭi* for words ending in *n*, there is an extension (*upasaṃkhyāna*) stating: "The elision of *ṭi* applies to *sabrahmacārin*, *pīṭhasarpi*, *kalāpin*, *kauthumin*, *taitilin*, *jājali*, *lāṅgali*, *śilālin*, *śikhaṇḍin*, *sūkara*, *sadman*, and *suparvan*"; by virtue of this extension, the *ṭi* is elided. SK 1489: *chagalino ḍhinuk* (A 4.3.109). [Those who study what was taught by Chagalin are called *Chāgalinaḥ*.]
Those who study what was proclaimed by Chāgali are called Chāgaleyins. According to Pāṇini 4.3.110, *pārāśarya-śilālibhyāṃ bhikṣu-naṭa-sūtrayoḥ*:
those mendicants who study the mendicant-sūtra (*bhikṣusūtra*) proclaimed by Pārāśarya are called Pārāśariṇa mendicants; the actors are called Śailālins.

SK 1491: *karmandakṛśāśvādibhya iniḥ* (A 4.3.111). This applies only to the words *bhikṣu* and *naṭa*. Those who study what was taught by Karmanda are *karmandinaḥ* monks; those who [study] what was taught by Kṛśāśva are *kṛśāśvinaḥ* actors.
SK 1492: *tenaikadik* (A 4.3.112).
*Saudāmanī* [is derived] from *sudāmān* with the suffix *aṇ* and the word *adri*; it means "in the same direction as Mount Sudāman.
By the rule *tasiś ca* (A 4.3.113), and because it is listed among the *svarādi* group, it is an indeclinable (*avyaya*). *Pīlumūlataḥ* means "in the same direction as the root of the *pīlu* tree."
SK 1494 *uraso yac ca* (A 4.3.114): The suffix *yasi* is also applied after *uras*. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *aṇ*. Examples: *urasā ekadik* → *urasyaḥ*; *urastaḥ*.
SK 1495 *upajñāte* (A 4.3.115).
"By him" (*tena*) is used in this very sense. That which was first conceived by Pāṇini is "Pāṇinīya.
According to A 4.3.116, *kṛte granthe* ("when a book is made"), a book composed by Vararuci is called "Vāraruca."

SK 1497 *saṃjñāyām* (A 4.3.117): [The suffix *aṇ* is applied] after [the word denoting the agent] as stated by "by that" (*tena*). This is for the sake of non-technical (non-scriptural) meaning. Honey produced by bees is *mākṣika*. SK 1498 *kulālādibhyo vuñ* (A 4.3.118).
When [the suffix] *añ* is applied in the sense of "made by that" to form a proper name: *kaulālakam* ("made by a potter"), *vāruḍakam* ("made by a basket-maker").

SK 1499: After the words *kṣudrā*, *bhramara*, *vaṭara*, and *pādapa*, the suffix *añ* is applied in the sense of "made by that" to form a proper name: *kṣaudram* ("made by bees"), *bhrāmaram* ("made by bees"), *vāṭaram* ("made by a *vaṭara*"), *pādapam* ("made by a tree").

SK 1500 *tasyedam* (A 4.3.120): "This belongs to him. *aupagava-*: [the son] of Upagu. *vaha-* with the suffix *turaṇiṭ* and the augment *iṭ*: *sāṃvahitra-*: the property of one who carries (*saṃvoḍhṛ*). *agnīdh-* with the suffix *raṇ* and the replacement of *bha* [by *idh*]: *āgnīdhra-*: [a place] where the *agnīdh* priest maintains the fire; his station is the *āgnīdhra*. Because it is located there (*tātsthyāt*), he too is called *āgnīdhra*. With the suffix *ṣeṇyaṇ* in the sense of "placing fuel" (*samidh-ādhāna*): *sāmidhenya-*: a mantra for kindling the fire; *sāmidhenī*.
SK 1501 *rathād yat* (A 4.3.121): [The suffix] *yat* [is applied after *ratha*].
The wheel of a chariot (*rathyaṃ cakraṃ*).
[By the rule] *patrapūrvād añ* (A 4.3.122), *patra* means a vehicle. This belongs to a horse-chariot, thus it is *āśvaratha*.

SK 1503: After *patra*, *adhvaryu*, and *pariṣad*, the suffix *añ* is applied [to form words denoting "the duty of"]. After *patra*, it means "external" (*bāhya*). For example: *āśvam* ("the duty of carrying a horse"), *ādhvaryavam* ("the duty of an *adhvaryu* priest"), *pāriṣadam* ("the duty of an assembly"). SK 1504: After *hala* and *sīra*, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied [to denote "the duty of"].

*hālikam* / *sairikam*. According to Pāṇini 4.3.125, *dvandvād vun vairamaithunikayoḥ*: *kākolūkikā* (the enmity between crows and owls); *kutsakuśikikā* (the enmity between Kutsa and Kuśika). Regarding enmity (*vaira*), there is a prohibition [of the suffix] after words such as *devāsura*: *daivāsuram* (the enmity between gods and demons).

SK 1506: The suffix *vuñ* is applied after [words denoting] a lineage (*gotra*) and a school (*caraṇa*). Example: *aupagavakam*. It should be stated that [the suffix *vuñ* is applied] after a school (*caraṇa*) when referring to its *dharma* or *āmnāya*. Example: *kāṭhakam*. SK 1507: The suffix *aṇ* replaces the suffixes *añ*, *yañ*, and *iñ* when [the patronymic denotes] a group (*saṅgha*), a part (*aṅka*), or a characteristic mark (*lakṣaṇa*).

The mention of *ghoṣa* (a hamlet) must also be made. [Examples: from *añ*: *gārgaḥ* (a descendant of Garga), *gārgam* (the hamlet of the Gargas); from *iñ*: *dākṣaḥ* (a descendant of Dakṣa), *dākṣam* (the hamlet of the Dākṣas). An *aṅka* (a settlement) is a connection through lineage, whereas a *lakṣaṇa* (a village) is a direct designation. Regarding *śākalād vā* (A 4.3.128): when the aforementioned meaning is expressed, the suffix *aṇ* is optionally used; alternatively, because it belongs to the category of *caraṇa* (Vedic schools), the suffix *vuñ* may be applied. Those who study what was proclaimed by Śākala are called *Śākalas*; their *saṅgha* (corporation), *aṅka*, or *ghoṣa* is *śākalaḥ*. [With *vuñ*: *śākalakaḥ*. In the sense of a *lakṣaṇa*, the word is neuter.

SK 1509: *chandogaukthikayājñikabahvṛcanāṭāñ ñyaḥ* (A 4.3.129). From the words *chandoga*, *aukthika*, *yājñika*, *bahvṛca*, and *naṭa*, the suffix *ñya* is applied. *Chandogya* refers to the dharma or the sacred tradition (*āmnāya*) of the chanters of the Sāmaveda; likewise, *aukthikya*, *yājñikya*, *bāhvṛcya*, and *nāṭya*. Since it has been stated that [the suffix applies] "to the dharma and the sacred tradition derived from a *caraṇa* (Vedic school)," by association with those two, the same suffix is applied to the word *naṭa* as well, in the sense of those two alone.

SK 1510: The suffix *vuñ* is not applied after the word *daṇḍa* when it refers to *māṇava* (young students) or *antevāsin* (resident pupils). For example, *daṇḍapradhānā māṇavāḥ* means "students for whom punishment is primary"; in such cases, when referring to those pupils, *vuñ* does not occur. Thus, *dākṣā daṇḍamāṇavāḥ* (or *śiṣyāḥ*) [means "the staff-bearing students of Dakṣa"]. SK 1511: The suffix *cha* is applied after words beginning with *raivatika*.

In the sense of "this belongs to him," this is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *vuñ*. Examples: *raivatikīyaḥ*, *baijavāpīyaḥ*. By the rule *kaupiñjalahāstipadād aṇ* (A 4.3.132): the descendant of *Kupiñjala* is [formed with] *aṇ*. Here, by virtue of a specific grammatical irregularity (*nipātana*), there is *aṇ*; and from that which ends in *aṇ*, there is again *aṇ*. Thus: *kaupiñjalaḥ*. This is an exception to the *vuñ* used for lineage (*gotra*). The descendant of *Hastipāda* is *Hāstipāda*; his [descendant] is *Hāstipadaḥ*.

SK 1513: *ātharvaṇikasyekalopaś ca* (A 4.3.133). The suffix *aṇ* shall be applied [after the word *ātharvaṇika*], with the elision of the single phoneme *i*. Thus, that which belongs to an *ātharvaṇika* is called *ātharvaṇa*, whether it be the Dharma or the sacred tradition (*āmnāya*). This is an exception to the suffix *vuñ* [prescribed after words denoting Vedic schools]. The secondary suffixes (*śaiṣika*) are concluded.
This concludes the section on *taddhita* suffixes pertaining to the period prior to the division of time (*prāgdīvyatīya*). 29.

SK 1514: Regarding the rule *tasya vikāraḥ* (A 4.3.134), it should be stated that there is the elision of the *ṭi* suffix when [the suffix *aṇ*] denotes a modification of stone (*aśman*). Thus, a modification of stone is *āśmaḥ*; likewise, *bhāsmanaḥ* and *mārtikaḥ*.

SK 1515: And [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] after words denoting parts of living beings, herbs, and trees (A 4.3.135); and by the word "and" (*ca*), also in the sense of a modification (*vikāra*). For example: *māyūraḥ* means a part or a modification of a peacock; *maurvaṃ* means a stalk or ashes of the *mūrvā* plant; *paippalam*. SK 1516: The suffix *aṇ* is applied after words beginning with *bilva* (A 4.3.136).
*Bailvam* / [SK 1517] *kopadhāc ca* (A 4.3.137): the suffix *aṇ* [is applied after a word ending in *ka*]. This is an exception to *añ*. Examples: *tarku*, *tārkavam*; *taittiḍīkam*.
SK 1518: *trapu-jatunoḥ ṣuk* (A 4.3.138).
After these two, the suffix *aṇ* occurs in the sense of a derivative product (*vikāra*), and there is also the augment *ṣuk*. Examples: *trāpuṣam*, *jātuṣam*.
SK 1519: *or añ* (A 4.3.139). [The suffix *añ* occurs after a word ending in *u* in the sense of a derivative product.]
*daivadāravam* (made from Devadāru wood); *bhādradāravam* (made from Bhādradāru wood).
According to A 4.3.140, *anudāttādeś ca*:
*dādhittham* (a collection of wood-apple trees); *kāpittham* (a collection of wood-apple trees).
SK 1521: Optionally after *palāśa* and others [the suffix *cha* is applied]. (A 4.3.141) Examples:
*pālāśam*, *kārīram*. SK 1522: After *śamī*, the suffix *ṣlañ* is applied. (A 4.3.142)

*Śāmīla* means ash. Because it ends in *ṣ*, the suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied; thus, *śāmīlī* means a ladle (*sruk*). SK 1523: *mayaḍvaitayor bhāṣāyām abhakṣyācchādanayoḥ* (A 4.3.143). In common usage (*bhāṣā*), the suffix *mayaṭ* may optionally be added after the mere base (*prakṛti*) to denote a modification (*vikāra*) or a part (*avayava*), except when referring to food or clothing. Examples: *aśmamayam* or *āśmanam* (made of stone). Why say "except for food" and so forth? [Counter-examples: *maudgaḥ sūpaḥ* (bean soup); *kārpāsam ācchādanam* (cotton clothing).

SK 1524: *nityaṃ vṛddha-śarādibhyaḥ* (A 4.3.144). [The suffix *mayaṭ* is applied] after words with a vṛddhi vowel in the first syllable and after *śara*, etc., invariably: *āmramayam* ("made of mangoes"), *śaramayam* ("made of reeds"). After words consisting of a single vowel, it is also invariably applied: *tvaṅmayam* ("made of skin"), *vāṅmayam* ("consisting of speech"). How then is the form *āpyamammayam* explained? It is derived from the word ending in *aṇ* (*āpya*) by adding the suffix *ṣyañ* in the sense of the base itself (*svārthe*), according to the rule *tasyedam*.
SK 1525: After *go*, [the suffix *mayaṭ* is applied] in the sense of "excrement," as in *goḥ purīṣam* = *gomayam* ("cow-dung"). SK 1526: [The suffix *mayaṭ* is applied] also after *piṣṭa*.

The suffix *mayaṭ* occurs in the sense of a modification (*vikāra*). For example: *viṣṭamayaṃ bhasma* ("ashes made from cow-dung"). How then is there the form *paiṣṭī surā* ("liquor made from flour")? When the general sense is intended, the suffix *aṇ* is applied according to the rule *tasyedam*. By the rule *saṃjñāyāṃ kan* (A 4.3.147), the suffix *kan* is added after *piṣṭa* alone. A specific modification of flour is called *piṣṭaka*; it may also be termed *pūpa*, *apūpa*, or *piṣṭaka*.

SK 1528: After *vrīhi*, when *puroḍāśa* follows, *mayaṭ* shall be applied (A 4.3.148). This is an exception to *yaṇ* [which would apply] after *bilva*. Example: *brīhimayaḥ puroḍāśaḥ* ("a sacrificial cake made of rice"). The form *vraihabhamyat* is an error. SK 1529: When not used as a technical name (*asaṃjñāyām*), [the suffix *mayaṭ* is applied] after *tila* and *yava* (A 4.3.149).

[The suffix *mayaṭ* is applied] after *tila* and *yava* [to form *tilamaya* and *yavamaya*]; however, when used as a conventional name (*saṃjñā*), [the forms are] *taila* and *yāvaka*. SK 1530: After *tāla*, [the suffix *mayaṭ* is applied] in the sense of a bow (*dhanus*). This is an exception to [the application of] *añ* and *mayaṭ*. In the sense of a bow: *tālaṃ dhanuḥ* ("a palm-tree bow"). In other cases: *tālamayam* ("made of palm wood") and *aindrāyudham* ("a rainbow").

SK 1531: After words meaning "gold" (*jātarūpa*), the suffix *aṇ* is used when expressing a measure (*parimāṇa*). Because the plural is used, synonyms are included. Examples: *hāṭaka-niṣkaḥ*, *tāpanīya-niṣkaḥ*, or *sauvarṇa-niṣkaḥ*. Why "when expressing a measure"? Example: *hāṭakamayī yaṣṭiḥ* ("a staff made of gold"). SK 1532: After words denoting living beings (*prāṇin*) and after *rajata* ("silver") and so forth, the suffix *añ* is used [to denote a measure].
*Śauka*, *bāka*, *rājata*. (SK 1533) *Ñitaś ca tatpratyayāt*:

after a word ending in a suffix that denotes a modification (*vikāra*) or a part (*avayava*), the suffix *añ* shall be applied, provided those same two meanings [of modification or part] are intended. This is an exception to *mayaṭ*. For example: *śāmīla* from *śāmīla*; *dādhittha* from *dādhittha*; *kāpittha* from *kapittha*. Why "ending in *ñ*" (*ñitaḥ*)? Consider *bailvamaya* (made of *bilva*).

SK 1534: *krītavat parimāṇāt* (A 4.3.156). Beginning from *prāgvahateṣ ṭhañ* (A 4.3.153), those suffixes which are prescribed for the sense of "purchased" (*krīta*) by means of a specific condition (*upādhi*) when applied to a measure (*parimāṇa*), are extended (*atidiśyante*) in the same manner to the sense of "modification" (*vikāra*). This is an exception (*apavāda*) to [suffixes] such as *aṇ*. *niṣkeṇa krītam* ("bought for a *niṣka*") → *naiṣkikam*. Likewise, a modification of a *niṣka* is also *naiṣkikaḥ*. A modification of a hundred (*śata*) is *śatyaḥ* or *śatikaḥ*. SK 1535: *uṣṭrād vuñ* (A 4.3.157). [The suffix *vuñ* is applied after the word *uṣṭra* in the senses of "purchased" and "modification"].
This is an exception (*apavāda*) to *prānyañ*. *Auṣṭrakaḥ*.
By A 4.3.158, *umorṇayor vā*, there are the forms *aumam* and *aumakam*, as well as *aurṇam* and *aurṇakam*. In the absence of the suffix *vuñ*, the suffixes *aṇ* and *añ* apply respectively.
SK 1537: By the rule *eṇyā ḍhañ* (A 4.3.159), [the suffix] *ḍhañ* is applied after *eṇī*; thus, *aiṇeyam*. However, after *eṇa*, [the suffix] *aṇ* is applied, resulting in *aiṇam*.
SK 1538: By the rule *gopayasor yat* (A 4.3.160), the suffix *yat* is applied after the words *go* and *payas*.
*gavyam* (derived from *go*), *payasyam* (derived from *payas*).
According to Pāṇini A 4.3.161, *droś ca*:
*dravyam* is a modification or a part of a tree (*dru*)—that is, a wooden object.

SK 1540 *māne vayaḥ* (A 4.3.162): [The suffix *vaya* is applied] after the word *dru*, provided it refers to a measure. *Druvayam*. The three terms *yautavam*, *druvayam*, and *pāthyam* have the sense of "measure. SK 1541 *phale luk* (A 4.3.163): [The suffix *phala* is applied with] elision (*luk*) [of the suffix].

The suffix denoting a modification or a part shall be elided when the word refers to the fruit. Thus, *āmalakyāḥ phalam* becomes *āmalakam*. However, in the case of *plakṣa* and other such words, the elision does not occur due to the force of the specific rule prescribing the suffix *aṇ* (Pāṇini 4.3.164); hence, *plākṣam*.
And for *nyagrodha* alone (A 7.3.5), there is no *vṛddhi* [strengthening] and the augment *auC* is applied: *naiyagrodham*.
Or, by A 4.3.165, from *jambū*: [the suffix *aṇ* is optionally applied].

From the word *jambū*, there may be the suffix *phal* [denoting the fruit], as in *jāmbavam*; alternatively, by the suffix *añ* with the elision (*luk*) of that [suffix], it becomes *jambu*. According to A 4.3.166, *lup ca*: "And [the suffix] *lup* [is applied]."

The suffix *pratyaya* may optionally be elided (*lup*) after *jambū* when it refers to its fruit. When there is elision (*lupi*), the word behaves like the base it is derived from (*yuktavat*); thus, the fruit of the *jambū* tree is called *jambū*. An addition (*upasaṃkhyāna*) should be made for words ending in *phala*, *pāka*, and *śuṣa*: *vrīhayaḥ* (rice), *mudgāḥ* (mung beans). Regarding flowers and roots, the elision is frequent (*bahulam*): the flower of the *mallikā* is *mallikā*; the [flower] of the *jāti* is *jātī*; the root of the *vidārī* is *vidārī*. Because of the mention of "frequently," it does not occur here: *pāṭalāni puṣpāṇi* (Pāṭala flowers), *sālvāni mūlāni* (Sālva roots). Due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), there is sometimes elision (*luk*): *aśoka*, *karavīra*. (SK 1546) *harītakyādibhyaś ca* (A 4.3.167).

The *lup* elision of the suffix denoting the "fruit" (*phala-pratyaya*) shall occur after these [words beginning with *harītakī*]. For *harītakī* and the others, the gender remains exactly as in the base word (*prakṛti*). The fruits of the *harītakī* are called *harītakyaḥ*. A 4.3.168 states: *kaṃsīyaparaśavyayor yaññau luk ca*. After the words *kaṃsīya* and *paraśavya*, the suffixes *yañ* and *ñya* are applied, and there is also *luk* elision of the suffixes *cha* and *yat*. That which is beneficial for bell-metal (*kaṃsa*) is *kaṃsīya*; its modification (*vikāra*) is *kāṃsya*. That which is beneficial for an axe (*paraśu*) is *paraśavya*; its modification is *pāraśava*. Thus end the suffixes belonging to the *prāgdīvyatīya* group.
In the section on secondary suffixes (taddhita), there is the governing rule for the suffix *ṭhak*. 30.

SK 1548: *prāgvahateṣ ṭhak* (A 4.4.1). The suffix *ṭhak* is applied from the rule *tadvahati* onwards. There is an addition (*upasaṃkhyāna*) for words such as *māśabda* in the sense of "he says that": one who says "the word *mā* must be used" is called a *māśabdika*. SK 1549: *svāgatādīnāṃ ca* (A 7.3.7). [The final vowel of these words is lengthened.]

*ai* would not occur. One who says "welcome" is a *svāgatika*. A *svādhvarika* [is one who says "well-sacrificed"]. The offspring of *svaṅga* is *svāṅgiḥ*; the offspring of *vyaṅga* is *vyāṅgiḥ*; the offspring of *vyaḍa* is *vyāḍiḥ*. One who acts according to legal procedure is *vyāvahārika*. That which is good for one's own master is *svāpateyam*. Regarding the verb *ā-hve* ("to call"), [the suffix applies] after words such as *prabhūta*: one who calls out abundantly is *prābhūtika*; [so too is] a *pāryāptika*. Regarding the verb *praccha* ("to ask"), [the suffix applies] after words such as *susnāta*: one who asks about bathing well is *sausnātika*; [so too is] a *saukhaśāyanika*.

The *anuśatikādi* group [is as follows]: from *paradāra* and others, when combined with *gacchati* ("goes to"), [the suffix *ṭhak* is applied]. *pāradārikaḥ* ("one who goes to another's wife"); *gaurutalpikaḥ*. SK 1550: [The suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after [words denoting an instrument] in the sense of "one plays with that," "one digs with that," "one wins with that," or "that which has been won. *ākṣikaḥ* ("one who plays with dice"); one who plays with dice (*akṣaiḥ dīvyati*). *ābhrikaḥ* ("one who digs with a spade"); one who digs with a spade (*abhryā khanati*). *ākṣikaḥ* ("one who wins with dice"); one who wins with dice (*akṣair jayati*). *ākṣikam* ("that which has been won with dice"); that which has been won with dice (*akṣair jitam*).
SK 1551 *saṃskṛtam* (A 4.4.3):
That which is prepared with curd is *dādhikam*; that which is prepared with *mārīca* is *mārīcikam*.
SK 1552 *kulatthakopadhād aṇ* (A 4.4.4): The suffix *aṇ* is applied after a word ending in *kulattha* or having it as its penultimate element.
This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ṭhak*. That which is prepared with *kulattha* beans is *kaulattham*; likewise, *taittiḍīkam*.
[By the rule] "He crosses" (*tarati*), one who crosses by means of a raft (*uḍupa*) is an *auḍupikaḥ*.
SK 1554: After *gopuccha*, the suffix *ṭhañ* [is applied] (A 4.4.6):
*gaupucchikaḥ*. SK 1555:
After *nau* and words consisting of two syllables, the suffix *ṭhan* [is applied] (A 4.4.7).

*nāvikaḥ* (boatman); *ghaṭikaḥ* (water-carrier). From a word ending in the third case, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied in the senses of "crosses by means of" (*carati*) or "eats" (*bhakṣayati*). For example: one who moves by means of an elephant is *hāstikaḥ*; one who moves by means of a cart is *śākaṭikaḥ*; one who eats with curd is *dādhikaḥ*. A woman who crosses with her arms is called *bāhukā*. (SK 1556, Pāṇini 4.4.8) *Carati*: the suffix *ṭhak* occurs after a word in the third case when the meanings "goes by means of" or "eats" are intended. *Hastinā carati* → *hāstikaḥ*; *śākaṭikaḥ*; *dadhnā bhakṣayati* → *dādhikaḥ*.

SK 1557: *ākārṣāt ṣṭhal* (A 4.4.9). *Ākarṣaḥ* means a touchstone. There is an alternative reading, *ākaṣāt*. From that [reading], one who moves about [with it] is an *ākarṣikaḥ*. Because of the suffix being marked with *ṣ*, there is the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*: *ākarṣikī*. SK 1558: *parpādibhyaḥ ṣṭhan* (A 4.4.10).

He moves with a *parpa* [crutch]; hence *parpikaḥ* (masculine) and *parpikī* (feminine). That seat (*pīṭha*) upon which the lame move is called a *parpa*. [Similarly: *aśvikaḥ* (one who moves by horse), *rathikaḥ* (one who moves by chariot).
A 4.4.11 states: *śvagaṇāṭ ṭhañ ca*; because of the word "ca" (and), there is also *ṣṭhan*.

SK 1560: In the case of *śvan* and others before the suffix *iñ*, [the substitution of] *aiC* does not occur. The offspring of *śvabhastra* is *śvābhastriḥ*; [the offspring of *śvadaṃṣṭra* is] *śvādaṃṣṭriḥ*. This very rule is the indicator (*jñāpaka*) for the application of the rule regarding "beginning with that" (*tadādividhi*). It should be stated that [the substitution occurs] before a suffix beginning with the vowel *i*: [one who moves with] a pack of dogs is *śvāgaṇikaḥ* (masc. or *śvāgaṇikī* (fem.); [one who moves with] a pack of dogs is *śvagaṇikaḥ* (masc. or *śvagaṇikī* (fem.). SK 1561: Optionally, [the substitution of *aiC* for the final *a* of *śvan* occurs] when it is at the end of a word (*padāntasya*). (A 7.3.9)

The *ai* and *au* diphthongs (*aij*) are optionally substituted for the final vowel of the word *śvan* when it is a member of a compound ending in the word *pada*. Thus, "belonging to this dog" is *śvāpadam* or *śauvāpadam*.

SK 1562: The suffix *ṭhak* is added after words such as *vetana* in the sense of "one who lives by means of that. For example, "one who lives by wages" is *vaitanikaḥ*; "one who lives by the bow" is *dhānuṣkaḥ*.

SK 1563: *vasna-kraya-vikrayāt ṭhan* (A 4.4.13). From the words *vasna*, *kraya*, and *vikraya*, the suffix *ṭhan* is added [to form a word for one who lives by that]. One who lives by means of *vasna* (price/value) is a *vasnikaḥ*. The inclusion of *kraya* and *vikraya* is for the sake of including both the compound and its individual components. Thus: *krayavikrayikaḥ*, *krayikaḥ*, and *vikrayikaḥ*. SK 1564: *āyudhāc cha ca* (A 4.4.14). From the word *āyudha* (weapon), the suffix *cha* is also added [along with *ṭhan*].
The suffix *ṭhan* [is applied after the word *āyudha*]. One who lives by means of weapons is *āyudhīyaḥ* or *āyudhikaḥ*.
According to Pāṇini 4.4.15, *haraty utsaṅgādibhyaḥ*:
one who carries [something] by means of the lap is *autsaṅgikaḥ*.

SK 1566: *bhastrādibhyaḥ ṣṭhan* (A 4.4.16). From *bhastrā* and so forth, the suffix *ṣṭhan* is applied. [Example: *bhastrikah* ("one who carries with a carrying-net"). Because it has the marker *ṣ*, the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is added: *bhastrikī*. SK 1567: *vibhāṣā vivadhāt* (A 4.4.17). [The suffix *ṣṭhan* is applied] optionally after *vivadha*.

One who carries by means of a *vivadha* (a yoke for carrying loads on both shoulders) is a *vivadhika*. In the alternative, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied, resulting in *vaivadhika*. Because a word that has undergone a partial modification is not considered different from the original, the suffix *ṣṭhan* may also be applied after *vīvadha*, yielding *vīvadhika* and *vīvadhikī*. The words *vivadha* and *vīvadha* refer to a wooden pole carried on the shoulders with slings at both ends. By the rule *aṇ kuṭilikāyāḥ* (A 4.4.18), the suffix *aṇ* is added after *kuṭilikā*. *Kuṭilikā* refers to a specific mode of movement used by hunters, as well as an iron hook used as a tool for catching game. One who catches deer or charcoal by means of a *kuṭilikā* is a *kauṭilika* hunter or a smith.
SK 1569: After the word *nirvṛtta* [the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied] following words such as *akṣadyūta*. (A 4.4.19) For example:
*akṣadyūtena nirvṛttam ākṣadyūtikam vairam* ("a feud brought about by a game of dice"). SK 1570: The suffix *mam* is always applied after the word *tri*. (A 4.4.20)

The suffix *map* is always applied after a word ending in the third case, provided that the base ends in a *tri*-suffix (*tr*), in the sense of "produced therefrom" (*nirvṛtta*). That which is produced by means of an action (*kṛtyā*) is called *kṛtrimam* ("artificial") or *paktrimam* ("cooked"). It should be stated that the suffix *ima* is added after a base ending in an abstract suffix (*bhāvapratyaya*). For example: produced by cooking (*pākena*) is *pākimam*; produced by abandoning (*tyāgena*) is *tyāgimam*. A 4.4.21: After the words *apamitya* and *yācita*, the suffixes *ka* and *kan* respectively [are applied].
*Apamitya* is a word ending in a gerund (*lyap*). Produced by having obtained on credit (*apamitya*) is *āpamityakam*; produced by what has been asked for (*yācitena*) is *yācitakam*.
SK 1572 (A 4.4.22): *saṃsṛṣṭe* — that which is mixed with curd is *dādhika*.
SK 1573 (A 4.4.23): *cūrṇādiniḥ* — [the suffix *ini* is added after *cūrṇa* and others].
SK 1574: *lavaṇāt luk* (A 4.4.24). [The suffix *cha* is elided after *lavaṇa*. Example:
*lavaṇena saṃsṛṣṭaḥ lavaṇaḥ sūpaḥ* ("soup mixed with salt"); *lavaṇaṃ śākam* ("salted vegetable").
SK 1575: *mudgād aṇ* (A 4.4.25). [The suffix *aṇ* is applied after *mudga*.]
*Maudga odanaḥ* (rice with mung beans).
According to *Pāṇini* 4.4.26, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied when something is "sprinkled over" (*upasikta*) with seasonings (*vyañjana*). Thus, that which is sprinkled over with curd is *dādhikam*.
SK 1577: *ojaḥ-saha-ambhasā vartate* (A 4.4.28). [The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after these words when they mean "subsisting by means of"].

*ojasā vartate* → *aujasikaḥ śūraḥ* ("a hero who subsists by means of his own vigor"); *sāhasikaś cauraḥ* ("a thief who subsists by means of violence"); *āmbhasiko matsyaḥ* ("a fish that subsists in water"). SK 1578: *tat-prati-anu-pūrvam īpa-loma-kūlam* (A 4.4.29). [The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after the word *īpa*, *loman*, and *kūla* when preceded by *prati* or *anu*].

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after a word ending in the second case in the sense of "he acts toward that. It is the second case because [the words] function as adverbs (*kriyāviśeṣaṇa*). Examples: *pratīpaṃ vartate* → *prātīpikaḥ*; *ānvīpikaḥ*; *prātilomikaḥ*; *ānulomikaḥ*; *prātikūlikaḥ*; *ānukūlikaḥ*. By the rule *parimukhaṃ ca* (A 4.4.29), [the suffix is applied] after *parimukham*. Example: *parimukhaṃ vartate* → *pārimukhikaḥ*. Due to the word *ca* ("and"), [the suffix is also applied] after *pāripārśvam*: *pāripārśvikaḥ*.

SK 1580: The suffix *cha* is applied after the word *garhya* when it means "that which one receives back as a double or triple amount" (*dviguṇārthaṃ triguṇaṃ tatpratyacchati*). Examples: *dvau guṇau* [of principal] = *dviguṇaḥ*; *trayo guṇāḥ* = *traiguṇaḥ*. It should be stated that the substitution of *vṛddhuṣi* for *vṛddhi* occurs: *vṛddhiḥ* = *vārdhuṣikaḥ* ("one who lives by usury"). SK 1581: The suffixes *ṣṭhan* and *ṣṭhac* are applied after the words *kusīda* and *daśaikādaśa*. (Pāṇini 4.4.31)

From these two words, *gārha* and *artha*, these two suffixes occur in the sense of "he gives. *Kusīda* means interest; the substance for that purpose is *kusīda*. One who gives that is a *kusīdikaḥ* (moneylender); likewise, *kusīdikī*. Because it has the meaning of "eleven," in the analysis (*vigraha*) "those eleven and, in reality, those ten," the suffix *aka* as a compound-final element (*samāsānta*) is prescribed by this very rule. Thus: *daśaikādaśikaḥ*; likewise, *daśaikādaśikī*. In the analysis "he gives eleven [for the price of] ten," here too the meaning of the secondary derivative (*taddhita*) is simply the creditor. By the rule *uñchati* (A 4.4.32): one who gathers wild fruits (*badara*) is a *bādarikaḥ*.
SK 1583 *rakṣati* (A 4.4.33):
one who protects the assembly is a *sāmājika*.
SK 1584 *śabdadarduraṃ karoti* (A 4.4.34): [one who makes a sound like a frog].

One who makes a sound is a *śābdika* (grammarian); one who makes the sound of a frog is a *dārdurika*. [Pāṇini 4.4.35] states: "He kills birds, fish, or deer. There is the inclusion of both the actual forms and their synonyms, as well as their specific varieties. Among the synonyms for fish, only *mīna* is accepted according to the Bhāṣya. One who kills birds is a *pākṣika*, a *śākunika*, a *māyūrika*; one who kills fish is a *mātsyika*, a *mainika*; one who kills birds is a *śākunika*; one who kills deer is a *mārgika*, a *hāriṇika*, or a *sāraṅgika*.
SK 1586: *paripanthaṃ ca tiṣṭhati* (A 4.4.36).

The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after this word ending in the accusative case, in the sense of "standing" or "striking. A thief who stands obstructing the path, having avoided or pervading it, is called *pāripanthikaḥ*. One who strikes at the path is also *pāripanthikaḥ*.
SK 1587: *mātha-uttara-pada-padavy-anupadam dhāvati* (A 4.4.37).

A *mātha* that has the form of a staff is a "staff-path" (*daṇḍamātha*). One who runs along the staff-path is a *dāṇḍamāthika*. [Likewise: *pādavika* ("one who runs along the path") and *ānupadika* ("one who runs along the track").
SK 1588: *ākrandāt ṭhañ ca* (A 4.4.38). [The suffixes *ṭhak* and *ṭhañ* are added after the word *ākranda* in the sense of "running toward"].

The suffix *ṭhañ* shall occur after this [word], and *ṭhak* shall occur after *āṭ*, in the sense of "running toward. For example, one who runs toward a place of weeping (*ākranda*)—a location where the sorrowful cry out—is called *ākrandikaḥ*. By the rule *padottarapadaṃ gṛhṇāti* (A 4.4.39), [the suffixes occur] in the sense of "grasping the preceding word" (*pūrvapadaṃ gṛhṇāti*) and "grasping the following word" (*uttarapadaṃ gṛhṇāti*). Thus: *paurvapadikaḥ* and *auttarapadikaḥ*.

SK 1590 *pratikaṇṭhārthalalāmaṃ ca* (A 4.4.40): after these words, when meaning "he grasps," the suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied. *pratikaṇṭhaṃ gṛhṇāti* → *prātikaṇṭhikaḥ*; *ārthikaḥ*; *lālāmikaḥ*. SK 1591 *dharmaṃ carati* (A 4.4.41): [the suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after the word *dharma*, when meaning "he practices."
One should state [the suffix] after *dharma* as well: *adharmāt* → *ādharmikaḥ*. A 4.4.42: *pratipatham eti ṭhaś ca* (he goes along the path);
*pratipatham eti* → *prātipathikaḥ*.
SK 1593: By [the rule] *samavāyāṃśca samavaiti* (A 4.4.46), [the suffix *ṭhak* is applied to form] *sāmavāyikaḥ* ("belonging to a collection") and *sāmūhikaḥ* ("belonging to a multitude"). SK 1594:
By [the rule] *pariṣado ṇyaḥ* (A 4.4.44), [the suffix *ṇya* is applied to form *pāriṣadyaḥ* ("a member of an assembly")."

One who belongs to an assembly is *pāriṣadya*. According to Pāṇini 4.4.45, the suffix *ṇya* may optionally be used after the word *senā*, in which case *ṭhak* is also applied: *sainyāḥ* or *sainikāḥ*.

SK 1596: *saṃjñāyāṃ lalāṭakukkuṭyau paśyati* (A 4.4.46). One who looks at the forehead is a *lālāṭika*, a servant [who watches his master’s face]. By the word *kukkuṭī*, a small area suitable for a hen to perch upon is indicated. A *kaukkuṭika* is a mendicant [who watches for scraps]. SK 1597: *tasya dharmyam* (A 4.4.47). [The suffix *ṭhak* is added after a word denoting a person] to form a term meaning "that which is his duty" (*dharmya*).
*Āpaṇika* means "relating to a shop" (*āpaṇa*), [formed] by the suffix *aṇ* according to Pāṇini 4.3.120.
By rule A 4.4.48, *mahiṣy-ādibhyaḥ*, [the suffix *aṇ* is applied]: *māhiṣa* means "relating to a buffalo-cow" (*mahiṣī*); likewise, *yājamāna*.

SK 1599: After the word *ṛtu*, the suffix *añ* [is applied]. From *yātu*, [the form] *yātram* is derived, meaning "consistent with the law (*dharmya*) of a journey. It should be stated that [the suffix applies] after *nara* as well; thus, *narasya dharmyā* becomes *nārī*. It should be stated that for *viśasitṛ*, there is both the elision of *iṭ* and the suffix *añ*; thus, *viśasitur dharmyam* becomes *vaiśastram*. For *vibhājayitṛ*, it should be stated that there is the elision of *ṇi* and the suffix *añ*; thus, *vibhājayitur dharmyam* becomes *vaibhājitram*.

SK 1600 *avakrayaḥ* (A 4.4.50): The suffix *ṭhak* shall be applied after a word ending in the genitive case when the sense is "rent" (*avakraya*). For example, *āpaṇasyāvakrayaḥ* becomes *āpaṇikaḥ*. "Rent" (*avakraya*) refers to the property to be collected by the king. SK 1601 *tad asya paṇyam* (A 4.4.51): [The suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after a word denoting that which is his merchandise (*paṇya*).
One whose merchandise is cakes (*apūpa*) is an *āpūpika*;
[by the rule] *lavaṇāt ṭhañ* (A 4.4.52), one whose merchandise is salt is a *lāvaṇika*.

SK 1603: *kisarādibhyaḥ ṣṭhan* (A 4.4.53). From *kisara* and others, the suffix *ṣṭhan* is applied. One for whom *kisara* is the merchandise is a *kisarika*. Because the suffix is marked with *ṣ*, there is the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*: *kisarikī*. The words beginning with *kisara*—such as *kisara*, *uśīra*, *balada*, and so forth—are all names for specific fragrant substances. SK 1604: *śalāluno ’nyatarasyām* (A 4.4.54). [The suffix *ṣṭhan* is optionally applied after *śalālu*.]
In the alternative case, there shall be the suffix *ṭhak*. [Examples: *śalālukaḥ* / *śalālukī*; *śālālukaḥ* / *śālālukī*. *Śalālu* is a specific kind of fragrant substance.
SK 1605: Regarding "craft" (*śilpam*, A 4.4.55).
One whose craft is playing the *mṛdaṅga* drum is a *mārdaṅgikaḥ*.

SK 1606 *maḍḍukajharjharādaṇ anyatarasyām* (A 4.4.56): If playing the *maḍḍuka* drum is his craft, he is a *māḍḍukaḥ* or a *māḍḍukikaḥ*; [if playing the *jhārjhara* drum, he is] a *jhārjharaḥ* or a *jhārjharikaḥ*. SK 1607 *praharaṇam* (A 4.4.57): [The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after a word denoting a weapon when it signifies one who uses that weapon as his profession.]
The suffix *ka* is applied in the sense of "this belongs to him. For example: *asi-praharaṇam asya* ("the sword is his weapon") results in *āsikaḥ*; *dhānukaḥ*.
According to Pāṇini 4.4.48, *paraśvadha* takes the suffix *ṭhañ*:
*pāraśvadhikaḥ*.

SK 1609: After *śakti* and *yaṣṭi*, the suffix *īkak* is applied [to form nouns denoting one who uses them as a weapon]. Examples: *śāktīkaḥ* ("a spearman"), *yāṣṭīkaḥ* ("a staff-bearer"). SK 1610: The suffix *matup* is applied after the words *asti*, *nāsti*, and *diṣṭam* [to denote one whose opinion it is that such is the case]. Examples: *āstikaḥ* ("one who believes in the existence of the afterlife"), *nāstikaḥ* ("an atheist"), *daiṣṭikaḥ* ("one who believes in fate").

The suffix *tad-as-ya* is used in this way: one whose conviction is "the other world exists" is an *āstika*; one whose conviction is "it does not exist" is a *nāstika*; one whose conviction is "it is destiny" is a *daiṣṭika*. According to Pāṇini 4.4.61, the suffix *śīla* [is added after a word denoting an action]:
one whose habit is eating cakes is an *āpūpika*.
SK 1612: The suffix *ṇa* is applied after words such as *chatra* (A 4.4.62).
A *chatra* is that which covers the faults of a teacher; one whose character is such is a *chātra* (pupil).

SK 1613 *kārmastācchīlye* (A 6.4.172): In the sense of habitual disposition (*tācchīlya*), the form *kārma* is derived by applying the suffix *ṇa*, and the elision of the *ṭi* portion is prescribed as an irregularity (*nipātana*). One whose habitual disposition is action (*karmaśīlaḥ*) is called *kārmaḥ*. Although this would have been established by the rule *na staddhite* (Pāṇini 6.4.144), which prohibits the elision of the final vowel before a *taddhita* suffix, [the specific mention here] is for the sake of ensuring that the elision occurs even when the suffix *ṇa* is applied in the sense of habitual disposition. By this, forms such as *caurī* ("one whose habit is stealing") and *tāpasī* ("one whose habit is asceticism") are established. Why "in the sense of habitual disposition"? Consider *kārmaṇaḥ* ("pertaining to action"). SK 1614 *krnādhyayane vṛttam* (A 4.4.63).

The suffix *ṭhak* occurs after a word ending in the nominative case in the sense of the genitive (*ṣaṣṭhī*), provided that the action performed during study is the meaning of that nominative. For example: *aikānyikaḥ*. This refers to one who, having engaged in study, committed exactly one error consisting of a mispronunciation at the time of examination. By rule A 4.4.64, *ṭhañ* is used after a compound whose prior member consists of many syllables (*bahvac*) in the same sense as the preceding [suffix]. For example: *dvādaśānyikaḥ*. This means one for whom twelve errors occurred during study; that is, twelve misreadings (*apapāṭha*) have taken place in his study.
SK 1616 *hitaṃ bhakṣāḥ* (A 4.4.65):
"Bread-eating is beneficial for him" → *āpūpikaḥ*.
SK 1617 *tad asmai dīyate niyuktam* (A 4.4.66).
The suffix *ika* is applied after the word *āgrabhojana* to form *āgrabhojanika*, meaning "to whom the first portion of food is invariably given.
According to A 4.4.67, the suffix *ṭiṭhan* is added after *śrāṇā*, *māṃsa*, and *odana*.

Thus, *śrāṇā* [meaning "soup"] invariably given to him is *śrāṇikaḥ*; the feminine form is *śrāṇikī*. The inclusion of both *māṃsaudana* (as a compound) and its separate members (*māṃsa* and *odana*) is for the sake of including both the compound and its constituent parts: *māṃsaudanikaḥ*, *māṃsikaḥ*, and *odanikaḥ*.
SK 1619 *bhaktād-aṇ-anyatarasyām* (A 4.4.68): optionally, the suffix *aṇ* is applied after *bhakta*.

In the alternative case, *ṭhak* is applied. *bhaktam asmai niyuktaṃ dīyate* ("food is assigned to him for his portion") results in *bhāktaḥ* or *bhāktikaḥ*. SK 1620 *tatra niyuktaḥ* (A 4.4.69): [the suffixes taught from A 4.4.65 onwards are applied] after a word denoting a location, in the sense of "appointed to that."
One appointed to a mine is an *ākārika*. According to Pāṇini 4.4.70 (*agārāntāt ṭhan*),
one appointed to a temple of the gods is a *devāgārika*.

SK 1622: After words denoting prohibited places or times, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied [to form a word] for one who studies there. For example: *śmaśāne ’dhīte śmāśānikaḥ* ("one who studies in a cremation ground"); *caturdaśyām adhīte cāturdaśikaḥ* ("one who studies on the fourteenth day").
SK 1623: The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after words ending in *kaṭhina*, as well as after *prastāra* and *saṃsthāna*, [to denote] one who deals in them.

In this context, it is exactly so. One who deals with bamboo-mats (*vaṃśakaṭhina*) is called a *vāṃśakaṭhinika*. "Bamboo" (*vaṃśa*) means reeds; that place where they are abundant is a "bamboo-thicket" (*vaṃśakaṭhina*). The meaning is that he performs in that very same manner whatever action is to be performed in that place. [Similarly: *prāstārika* (one who deals with grass mats), *sāṃsthānika* (one who deals with formal assemblies).
According to Pāṇini 4.4.73, *nikaṭe vasati* ("he dwells near"), one who dwells nearby is a *naikaṭika* mendicant.

SK 1625: *āvasathāt ṣṭhal* (A 4.4.74). From *āvasatha*, [the suffix] *ṭhal* is applied: one who dwells in a lodging is *āvasathikaḥ*. Because it is marked with *ṣ*, there is the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*: *āvasathikī*. [The following six suffixes are taught: from *ākara*, *parpa* and others, from *bhastra* and others, and from *kusīda-sūtra*; from *āvasatha*, *kisara* and others—these six are marked with *ṣ* under the heading of *ṭhak*. (Verse 1) The meaning of "six" is that they are prescribed by six sūtras. However, the actual suffixes are seven. The limit for *ṭhak* is thus concluded.
Among the secondary suffixes (taddhita), those beginning with the suffix -īya (prāg-hītīyāḥ) [are treated as having the same accent as their base].
SK 1626: That which is governed by *prāgghatāt* (Pāṇini 4.4.75), namely from the rule *tasmai hitam* (4.4.74) onwards, is the subject matter here.
SK 1627: [The suffix *cha*] is applied after [stems ending in] *ratha*, *yuga*, *prāsaṅga*, and *aṅga* in the sense of "it carries that" (*tadvahati*).

*rathyaḥ* means "one who draws a chariot"; *yugyaḥ* means "one who draws a yoke. At the time of training calves, a piece of wood is placed upon their shoulders; that is called a *prāsaṅga*. One who draws that is *prāsaṅgayaḥ*. Regarding the rule *dhuro yaḍḍhakau* (A 4.4.77), although the lengthening [of the vowel] would have applied by the rule *hali ca*, [it does not occur here].

SK 1629 *na bhakurchurām* (A 8.2.79): In the case of a *bha*-stem, as well as for the words *kūrca* and *kūra*, there shall not be lengthening of the penultimate vowel. Examples: *dhuryaḥ*, *dhaureyaḥ*. SK 1630 *khaḥ sarvadhurāt* (A 4.4.78): The suffix *kha* [in the sense of "one who bears"] is applied after the word *sarvadhura*.
One who bears every burden (*sarvadhurām vahati*) is called *sarvadhurīṇaḥ*. According to A 4.4.79, *ekadhurāl luk ca*:
one who bears a single burden (*ekadhurām vahati*) is called *ekadhurīṇaḥ* or *ekadhuraḥ*.

SK 1632: The suffix *aṇ* is applied after *śakaṭa* [to form a word meaning "that which carries"]. A bull that carries a cart is called *śākaṭa*. SK 1633: The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after *hala* and *sīra* [to form a word meaning "that which carries"].
The plowman (*hālika*) or the sower (*sairika*) draws the plow.
According to A 4.4.82, *janya* is used as a technical term (*saṃjñā*); *janī* means a bride (*vadhū*), and that which carries her—that is, brings her—is called *janya*.

SK 1635 *vidhyaty adhanuṣā* (A 4.4.83): The suffix *yat* occurs after a word ending in the second case in the sense of "pierces," provided that a bow (*dhanus*) is not the instrument therein. Example: *padyāḥ śarkarāḥ* ("gravel that pierces the feet"). SK 1636 *dhanagaṇaṃ labdhā* (A 4.4.84): [The suffix *ya* occurs after the words *dhana* and *gaṇa*] in the sense of "one who has obtained."
This [suffix] ends in *tṛn*. One who has obtained wealth is *dhanya*; one who has obtained a group is *gaṇya*. According to Pāṇini 4.4.85, *annaṇ* [is applied]:
one who has obtained food is *ānna*.
*vaśaṃ gataḥ* (Pāṇini 4.4.86): *vaśyaḥ*, one who acts according to the will of another.
SK 1639: *pada* [is used] in this sense when it means "visible" (*dṛśya*).
*padyaḥ kardamaḥ* ("mud that is visible"); the meaning is "not completely dry. SK 1640: *mūla* [is used] when it means "not removed" (*abarhi*).
*Ābarhaṇa* means pulling out or uprooting; that which possesses this is *ābarhin*. Those for whom the root has been pulled out (*mūla-ābarhin*) are *mūlyā* mung beans.

Regarding the rule *saṃjñāyāṃ dhenuṣyā* (Pāṇini 4.4.89), the augment *puK* and the suffix *ya* are prescribed after the word *dhenu* in its own sense when it is a proper name (*saṃjñā*). Thus, *dhenuṣyā* refers to a cow kept as collateral.
By [the rule] *gṛhapatinā saṃyukte ñyaḥ* (Pāṇini A 4.4.90): the *gārhapatya* fire is that which is connected with the householder (*gṛhapati*), who is the sacrificer (*yajamāna*).

SK 1643: [The suffix *ya* is applied after the words] *nau*, *vayaḥ*, *dharma*, *pathin*, *viṣa*, *mūla*, *sītā*, *tulā*, *abhyasta*, *tārya*, *tulya*, *prāpya*, *vadha*, *ānāmya*, *sama*, and *samita*.

*nāvā tāryam* = *nāvyam* (crossable by boat). *vayasā tulyaḥ* = *vayasyaḥ* (equal in age). *dharmeṇa prāpyam* = *dharmyam* (attainable through dharma). *viṣeṇa vadhyaḥ* = *viṣyaḥ* (to be killed by poison). *mūlena ānāmyam* = *mūlyam* (to be bent down by the root-price). *mūlena samaḥ* = *mūlyaḥ* (equivalent to the price). *sītayā saṃmitam* = *sītyam* kṣetram (a field measured by the furrow). *tulayā saṃmitam* = *tulyam* (measured by a scale). SK 1644: [The suffix *ya* is applied after the words] *dharma*, *pathin*, *artha*, and *nyāya* when meaning "not deviating from" (*anapeta*). *dharmād anapetam* = *dharmyam* (not departing from dharma). *patho 'napetam* = *pathyam* (not deviating from the path). *arthād anapetam* = *artham* (not departing from the purpose). *nyāyād anapetam* = *nyāyyam* (not departing from justice).
That which does not deviate from *dharma* is *dharmya*, meaning wholesome (*pathya*), noble (*ārthya*), or logical (*nyāyya*).
According to A 4.4.93, *chandaso nirmite*: that which is fashioned by *chandas* is *chandasya*; the meaning is "that which is made according to one's wish."

SK 1646 *uraso ṇyaś ca* (A 4.4.94). Because of the word "ca" [in the sūtra], the suffix *yat* is also applied. That which is produced from the chest (*uras*) is *aurasaḥ* (legitimate son); also *urasyaḥ*.
SK 1647 *hṛdayasya priyaḥ* (A 4.4.95). [The suffix *yat* is applied after *hṛdaya* when the meaning is "beloved"].
The word *hṛdya* means "a place dear to the heart. Regarding the substitution of *hṛd* for *hṛdaya*, [Pāṇini] states:

"In the sense of binding, after the word *hṛdaya* ending in the genitive case, when a mantra is to be expressed in the Veda" (A 4.4.96). Thus, *hṛdayasya bandhanaḥ* becomes *hṛdyaḥ*, meaning a mantra used for subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*).
SK 1649: After *mata*, *jana*, and *hala*, the suffix *ya* is applied in the sense of instrument (*karaṇa*), discourse (*jalpa*), and drawing (*karṣa*) respectively (A 4.4.97).

Knowledge is *mata*; its instrument, state, or means is *matya*. The discourse of people is *janya*. The drawing of a plough is *halya*. SK 1650: The suffix *ya* is applied after a word denoting a place in the sense of "skilled therein" (*tatra sādhuḥ*) (A 4.4.98).

*Agre sādhuḥ* results in *agryaḥ*. *Sāmasu sādhuḥ* results in *sāmanyaḥ*; the original stem remains (*prakṛtibhāvaḥ*) by the rule *ye cābhāvakarmaṇoḥ*. [Examples: *karmaṇyaḥ*, *śaraṇyaḥ*. SK 1651: *pratijanādibhyaḥ khañ* (A 4.4.99). *Pratijanaṃ sādhuḥ* results in *prātijanīnaḥ*. *Sāṃyugīnaḥ*, *sārvajanīnaḥ*, *vaiśvajanīnaḥ*.

SK 1652 *bhaktāṇṇaḥ* (A 4.4.100): [The suffix] *ṇa* is applied after the word *bhakta*. For example: *bhakte sādhavaḥ bhāktāḥ śālayaḥ* ("rice that is suitable for a meal"). SK 1653 *pariṣado ṇyaḥ* (A 4.4.101): [The suffix] *ṇya* is applied after the word *pariṣad*.

*Pāriṣadyaḥ*: by means of a *yogavibhāga* (splitting of a rule) from the word *pariṣad*, there is also the suffix *ṇa*; thus [we have] *pāriṣadaḥ*. There is also the reading *parṣadaḥ*, from which [we derive] *pārṣadaḥ*. SK 1654 states: "The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after words such as *kathā*. Thus, one who is skilled (*sādhu*) in discourse (*kathā*) is a *kāthikaḥ*.

SK 1655: *guḍādibhyaṣ ṭhañ* (A 4.4.103). [The suffix] *ṭhañ* is applied after [words beginning with] *guḍa*. Example: *gauḍika ikṣuḥ* ("sugarcane suitable for molasses"); *sāktukā yavāḥ* ("barley suitable for *saktu* flour"). SK 1656: *pathyatithivasatikhapater ḍhañ* (A 4.4.104). [The suffix] *ḍhañ* is applied after the words *pathin*, *atithi*, *vasati*, and *khapati*.

That which is good for a journey is *pātheya* (provisions for a journey). That which is good for a guest is *ātitheya* (hospitality). That which is good for dwelling (*vasana*) or staying (*vasati*) is *vāsateyī*, as in "the night. Wealth is *svāpateya*.
According to A 4.4.145, that which pertains to an assembly (*sabhā*) is *sabhya* (a member of an assembly).
SK 1658: *samānatīrthe vāsī* (A 4.4.107). The word *sādhuḥ* is no longer in force. One who dwells is a *vāsī*. One who dwells with a teacher at the same sacred site (*tīrtha*) is a *satīrthyaḥ*.
SK 1659: *samānodare śayitaño codāttaḥ* (A 4.4.108). [The suffix *cha* is applied after *samānodara*, and the *ñ* of the suffix *añ* is also udātta.]
One who has lain and remained in the same womb is a uterine brother (samānodarya).
SK 1660: *sodarād yaḥ* (A 4.4.109).
*Sodaryaḥ*. The meaning is as before. Thus ends the section on suffixes beginning with *hit*.
Regarding the secondary suffixes (*taddhita*), the rule for *cha* and *yat* is as follows:
