SK 2117: *kṛbhvastiyoge saṃpadyakartari cvih* (A 5.4.50). It should be stated that [this rule applies] when there is a transition from one state to another (*abhūtatadbhāve*). When the base undergoes a change toward the nature of the suffix *ci*, the suffix *cvi* may optionally be added in its own sense (*svārthe*) to a word denoting the modified form (*vikāraśabda*), provided it is used in conjunction with the verbs *kṛ*, *bhū*, or *as*.
SK 2118: *asya cvau* (A 7.4.32). Before the suffix *cv-* [in the sense of "becoming"], the vowel *a* is replaced by *ī*.

There is elision of the *v* [of *cv-*]. Because it ends in *cv-*, it is an indeclinable (*avyaya*). [Examples: *akṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sampadyate taṃ karoti* ("he makes that which was not black into black") → *kṛṣṇīkaroti*; *brahmībhavati* ("he becomes a Brahmin"); *gaṅgīsyāt* ("may he become the Gaṅgā"). It should be stated that for an indeclinable, the substitution of *ī* does not occur before *cv-*. [Examples: *doṣābhūtam ahaḥ* ("the day became evening"); *divābhūtā rātriḥ* ("the night became day"). This was stated in the *Bhāṣya* on the rule *avyayībhāvaś ca* (A 2.4.18). SK 2119: *kyacvyoś ca* (A 6.4.152). [The substitution of *ī* for the final vowel of the penultimate syllable occurs] also before the denominative suffix *kyac* and the suffix *cv-*.

There is elision of the *y* of an affix denoting descent (*apatya*) when it follows a consonant (*hal*), provided that *kyac* or *cvī* follows. *gārgībhavati*. Regarding *cvau ca* (A 7.4.23): when *cvī* follows, there is lengthening of the preceding vowel. *śucībhavati*; *paṭū syāt*. Some say there is no lengthening for indeclinables; however, that is without foundation. As for *svasti syāt*, this is established by the absence of *cvī* due to the Great Option (*mahāvibhāṣā*). If it is argued that *svastī syāt* should also occur as an alternative, let it be so. If it is not desired, then let it be that *cvī* simply does not arise at all because of non-usage (*anabhidhāna*). *rīṅ ṛtaḥ*: [The substitution of] *rīṅ* occurs for *ṛt* [before *cvī*]. *mātrīkaroti*.
SK 2121: *arur-manas-cakṣuḥ-cetas-raho-rajasām lopaś ca* (A 5.4.51).

There is elision of these [stems] when the suffix *cvi* follows. Examples: *arūkaroti* ("he makes [the body] woundless"), *unmanīsyāt* ("may he become free from anxiety"), *uccakṣūkaroti* ("he makes [the eyes] look upward"), *cicetīkaroti* ("he makes [the mind] conscious"), *virahīkaroti* ("he makes [the place] devoid of passion"), *virajīkaroti* ("he makes [the mind] free from passion").
SK 2122: *vibhāṣā sāti kārtsnye* (A 5.4.52). The suffix *sāti* is optionally applied after a word denoting a part of the whole, provided that the sense of "entirety" (*kārtsnya*) is intended.
In this context, *sāti* may optionally be used in the sense of totality (*sākalya*).

[By the rule] *sātpadādyoḥ* (A 8.3.111), the change to *ṣ* for the *s* would not occur. Examples: *dadhi siñcati* ("he pours curd"); *kṛtsnaṃ śastram agniḥ saṃpadyate* ("the entire weapon becomes fire"), expressed as *agnisādbhavati* or *agnībhavati*. By the great option (*mahāvibhāṣā*), a full sentence may also be used. Why "in the sense of totality"? [Consider: *ekadeśena śuklībhavati paṭaḥ* ("the cloth becomes white in one part").

SK 2124: *abhividhau saṃpadā ca* (A 5.4.53). When used with the word *saṃpad* and with the roots *kṛ*, *bhū*, and *as*, the suffix *sāt* may optionally be applied to express pervasion (*abhividhi*). In the alternative case, when used with *kṛ*, *bhū*, and *as*, the suffix *cvi* is applied. However, when used with *saṃpad*, there is only the formation of a sentence [without a formal suffix]. Examples: *agnisāt saṃpadyate*, *agnisādbhavati* — "The weapon becomes fire. *agnībhavati*. *jalasāt saṃpadyate*, *jalībhavati* — "The salt becomes water. "Totality" (*kārtsnya*) refers to the transformation of a single individual entity through the modification of all its constituent parts. "Pervasion" (*abhividhi*), on the other hand, refers to the alteration of many individual entities through the modification of only some of their parts.

SK 2125: The suffix *sāti* is applied after a word denoting that which is dependent on another, when used in conjunction with the roots *kṛ*, *bhū*, *as*, or the verb *saṃpad*. Examples: *rājasātkaroti*, *rājasātsaṃpadyate*. The meaning is "dependent upon the king. SK 2126: When the sense is "to be given," the suffix *trā* is also applied [after a word denoting that which is dependent].

When that which is to be given (*deya*) is dependent on someone, the suffixes *trā* and *sāti* are used after the words *kṛ*, *bhū*, and others. For example: *viprādhīnaṃ deyaṃ karoti* (he makes the gift dependent on the Brahmin), *vipratrā karoti*; *vipratrā saṃpadyate* (it becomes dependent on the Brahmin); and optionally, *viprasātkaroti*. Why "when it is to be given"? [Consider: *rājasādbhavati rāṣṭram* (the kingdom becomes dependent on the king). SK 2127: *deva-manuṣya-puruṣa-purumartyebhyo dvitīyā-saptamyor bahulam* (A 5.4.56).

After these words ending in the second or seventh case, the suffix *trā* is used diversely. For example: *devatrā vande rame vā* (I praise or I delight in the gods). Because of the mention of "diversely" (*bahula*), it occurs elsewhere as well: *bahutrā jīvato manaḥ* (the mind of the living being is in many places).

Pāṇini A 5.4.57: *avyaktānukaraṇād dvyajavarārdhādanitau ḍāc* (Ḍāc follows an imitation of an indistinct sound which has two syllables as its minimum, provided it does not end in *it*, when used with the roots *kṛ*, *bhū*, or *as*). "Two-syllable" (*dvyac*) means "at least two," but not less than that; that is to say, it must have more than one vowel (*anekāj*). Ḍāc is added after such a word whose second half consists of [more than one syllable], when used in conjunction with *kṛ*, *bhū*, or *as*. When Ḍāc is intended, reduplication (*dvirvacana*) occurs diversely (*bahulam*). It should be stated that reduplication is obligatory when Ḍāc is intended. When the reduplicated form follows Ḍāc, the single substitute for both the preceding and following sounds shall be the latter form (*pararūpa*). Thus, for the *t* and *p* sounds, the substitute is *p*. Example: *paṭapaṭākaroti*. Why "imitation of an indistinct sound"? Example: *dṛṣatkaroti* ("he makes a stone").

Why [is the condition] "consisting of at least two vowels" (*dvyajavarārdha*) stated? [Consider: *śratkaroti*. Why [is the condition] "in the latter part" (*avara*) stated? [Consider: *kharaṭakharaṭākaroti*, *trapatrapaṭākaroti*. It would have been more appropriate to formulate the rule simply as "having more than one vowel" (*anekāca*). For in this way, in the case of *dāci*, it would be easier to explain that the locative case in *pare* refers to the subsequent element (*parasaptamī*) when reduplication occurs; this should be noted. Why [is the condition] "not followed by *i*" (*anitau*) stated? [Consider: *paṭiti karoti*. SK 2129: After the words *dvitīya*, *tṛtīya*, *śamba*, and *bīja*, the suffix *ṇamul* is applied to the root *kṛ* in the sense of ploughing (*kṛṣau*). (A 5.4.58)

The suffix *ḍāc* occurs after words beginning with "dvitīya" when used in conjunction with the root *kṛ* alone, in the sense of ploughing. Because of the frequent occurrence [of this rule], there is no reduplication for anything other than an unexpressed imitation (*avyaktānukaraṇa*) when used with the root *dāñ*. Examples: *dvitīyam karṣaṇam karoti* → *dvitīyākaroti*; *tṛtīyam karṣaṇam karoti* → *tṛtīyākaroti*. The word *śamba* means "contrary" (*pratiloma*). When one ploughs a field that was already ploughed in the regular direction (*anuloma*) again in the contrary direction, it is *śambākaroti*. When one ploughs together with the sowing of seed, it is *bījākaroti*. [This is governed by] A 5.4.59: *saṃkhyāyāś ca guṇāntāyāḥ*.

When used in conjunction with the root *kṛ* ("to do"), the suffix *ḍāc* occurs after the word *kṛṣi* ("plowing"). Example: *dviguṇākaroti kṣetram*. The meaning is: "he performs a double plowing of the field," that is, he performs the action of plowing the field twice over. (Pāṇini 5.4.59). The rule for *ḍāc* after *kṛṣi* has ceased to apply. When used in conjunction with the root *kṛ*, the suffix *ḍāc* occurs after the word *samaya* ("time"). Example: *samayākaroti*. The meaning is: "he lets time pass," that is, he delays. (Pāṇini 5.4.60).

SK 2132: *sapattraniṣpattrādativyathane* (A 5.4.61). *sapatrākaroti mṛgam* ("he makes the deer 'with-feather'"). The meaning is that by inserting an arrow together with its feathers (*sapuṅkha*), he makes it "with-feather" (*sapatra*). *niṣpattrākaroti*. The meaning is that because the arrow emerges from the other side along with its feathers, he makes it "featherless" (*niṣpattra*). Why "when causing excessive pain"? [Because otherwise: he makes the ground "with-feather" or "featherless. SK 2133: *niṣkulān niṣkoṣaṇe* (A 5.4.63).

He makes the pomegranate seedless (*niṣkulākaroti dāḍimam*). The suffix *ḍāc* is applied to the *bahuvrīhi* compound *niṣkula*, meaning "that from which the *kula*—the collection of internal parts—has gone out.
According to A 5.4.63, *sukha-priyād ānulomye*:
he makes the teacher happy (*sukhākaroti*) or dear (*priyākaroti*), meaning he gladdens him by acting in a favorable manner.
SK 2135: After *duḥkha*, when used in the sense of being contrary [to the usual state], [the suffix *ṇic* is applied].
*duḥkhākaroti svāminam* ("he makes the master suffer"); the meaning is "he torments. SK 2136: After *śūla*, in the sense of cooking.
*Śūlākaroti māṃsam*: it means he cooks the meat on a spit (*śūlena pacati*).
(SK 2137) *Satyādaśapathe* (A 5.4.66):

*satyākaroti bhāṇḍaṃ vaṇik*—the merchant makes the merchandise "true," meaning he declares it as something that ought to be purchased. However, regarding an oath, *satyaṃ karoti vipro*—the Brahmin makes [his word] true.

SK 2138: *madrāt parivāpaṇe* (A 5.4.67). The word *madra* signifies auspiciousness (*maṅgala*). *Parivāpaṇa* means shaving (*muṇḍana*). *Madrākaroti* means "he performs [the rite]"; the sense is that he consecrates [someone] by means of an auspicious shaving. It should be stated that this also applies after *bhadra*: *bhadrākaroti*. The meaning is as before. Why "in the case of shaving"? [Consider: *madraṃ karoti* ("he does what is pleasing") and *bhadraṃ karoti* ("he does what is auspicious"). Thus ends the section on *tadrāja* suffixes among the secondary derivatives (*taddhita*). Section 40: The Procedure for Reduplicated Forms (*dvirukta-prakriyā*).
With reference to the rule *sarvasya dve* (A 8.1.1),
[the rule] *nityavīpsayoḥ* (A 8.1.4) applies.

When frequency (*ābhīkṣṇya*) or distributive repetition (*vīpsā*) is to be indicated, a word is reduplicated. Frequency applies to forms ending in *tiṅ* suffixes and to those ending in *kṛt* suffixes that are designated as indeclinables (*avyaya*). Examples: *pacati pacati* ("he cooks repeatedly"); *bhuktvā bhuktvā* ("having eaten repeatedly"). Regarding distributive repetition: *vṛkṣaṃ vṛkṣaṃ siñcati* ("he waters tree after tree"); *grāmo grāmo ramaṇīyaḥ* ("every village is beautiful"). SK 2141: *parervarjane* (Pāṇini A 8.1.5). When *pari* is used in the sense of exclusion (*varjana*), it is reduplicated. Example: *pari pari vaṅgebhyo vṛṣṭo devaḥ* ("the god has rained excluding the Vaṅgas"). The meaning is "having avoided the Vaṅgas. There is an optional rule (*vāvacana*) regarding *pari* when used in the sense of exclusion: *pari vaṅgebhyaḥ*.

SK 2142: *upary-adhy-adhasaḥ sāmīpye* (A 8.1.7). *upa-upari grāmam* ("near the village"). The meaning is: "a place near the village, above the village. *adhi-adhi sukham* ("near happiness"). The meaning is: "suffering at a time near [immediately following] happiness, after happiness. *adhaḥ-adho lokam* ("near the world"). The meaning is: "a place near the world, below the world. SK 2143: *vākyāder āmantritasyāsūyā-saṃmati-kopa-kutsana-bhartsaneṣu* (A 8.1.8). [The doubling of the first word occurs when it is a vocative at the beginning of a sentence, provided it expresses envy, consent, anger, reproach, or threat.]

In the sense of envy (*asūyā*): "O handsome one, handsome one! Your beauty is in vain. In the sense of approval (*saṃmati*): "O King, King! You are worthy of worship. In the sense of anger (*kopa*): "O ill-behaved one, ill-behaved one! Now you shall know [the consequences]. In the sense of censure (*kutsana*): "O archer, archer! Your bow is in vain. In the sense of reproach (*bhartsana*): "O thief, thief! I shall have you executed. [Pāṇini 8.1.9] states: "A single [word] used in apposition functions like a *bahuvrīhi* compound."

A word that is repeated twice shall be treated like a *bahuvrīhi* compound. By this rule, there is the elision of the case-ending (*sup*) and the substitution of the masculine form (*puṃvadbhāva*). For example: *ekaikam akṣaram*. Here, since the case-endings of both members have been elided, the status of being a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) arises precisely because of the treatment as a *bahuvrīhi*; thus, a case-ending is added to the entire aggregate. In *ekaikayā āhutyā*, because of the masculine substitution in the first member, there is a specific difference regarding the *avagraha* (the pause between words). Furthermore, the explicit mention of "in a *bahuvrīhi*" in the rule *na bahuvrīhau* is for the purpose of obtaining the primary *bahuvrīhi* (as opposed to a secondary one).

Therefore, the ancients maintain that the status of being a *sarvanāman* (pronoun) certainly exists in a *bahuvrīhi* by extension (*atideśa*). However, in reality, according to the view of the *Bhāṣya*, this has been rejected. Even according to the view of the *Sūtra*, since the prohibition applies to the non-technical (*alaukika*) analytical statement (*vigraha*) regarding the meaning of a *bahuvrīhi*, but not to the *bahuvrīhi* compound itself, there is no possibility of raising the doubt of extension here at all. "Give to each one" (*ekaikasmai dehi*). By A 8.1.10, *ābādhe ca*, when affliction is to be indicated, a word is doubled and it behaves like a *bahuvrīhi*. Thus: *gatagataḥ*. This is the utterance of one who is tormented by separation. Because of the treatment as a *bahuvrīhi*, there is elision of the case-ending (*subluk*). [In the feminine: *gatagatā*. Here, the masculine form is applied (*puṃvadbhāva*).

SK 2146: *karmadhārayavad uttareṣu* (A 8.1.11). In the subsequent reduplications from this point forward, the operations of a *karmadhāraya* compound apply. The purposes [of this rule] are the elision of case-endings (*sublopa*), the masculine form (*puṃvadbhāva*), and the acute accent on the final syllable (*antodāttatva*). SK 2147: *prakāre guṇavacanasya* (A 8.1.12). [The same operations apply when a word denoting a quality (*guṇavacana*) is used in the sense of a manner.]

When similarity (*sādṛśya*) is to be expressed, a word denoting a quality (*guṇavacana*) is reduplicated, and that [compound] is treated like a *karmadhāraya*. Because of the governing rule "after a *karmadhāraya* [the following words...]," there is the *puṃvadbhāva* (masculine stem form) of the first member, as well as the oxytone accent (*antodāttatva*) of the compound according to the rule "of the compound. Examples: *paṭupaṭvī* (a woman who is somewhat clever), *paṭupaṭuḥ* (something that is somewhat clever). That is to say, it means "one who is slightly clever. Here, both words denoting a substance with a subordinate quality (*guṇopasarjana-dravyavācin*) and those denoting a quality alone (*kevalaguṇavācin*) are included. Examples: *śuklaṃ śuklaṃ rūpam* (a white-white color), *śuklaśuklaḥ paṭaḥ* (a white-white cloth).

Two [instances] are to be expressed in succession; [the word] is thick at every root. When an action proceeds with intensity, its repeated application in various ways as desired is established by logical principle (*nyāyasiddha*). For example: "Sarpa! Sarpa! Wake up! or "Sarpa! Wake up! And [this rule applies] in the case of the intensification of an action (*kriyāsamabhihāra*): "He cuts, he cuts"—thus indeed he cuts. Since this is already established by the rule *nityavīpsayoḥ*, this present rule is intended for the sake of expressing intensity (*bhṛśārtha*). Alternatively, it is intended so that even in the case of frequency (*paunaḥpunya*), the suffix may acquire the capacity to indicate [that meaning] when combined with the imperative (*loṭ*).

When there is a reciprocal action (*karmavyatihāra*), two forms of the pronoun are to be expressed, and they may optionally be treated like a compound (*samāsavat*); this is due to the inclusion of the term "frequently" (*bahula*). Because of the mention of "frequently," this treatment as a compound does not apply to *anya* and *para*. However, for the word *itara*, it is mandatory. When the treatment as a non-compound (*asamāsavadbhāva*) occurs, the case-ending (*sup*) of the first member should be stated as *su*. Examples include: *anyonyaṃ viprā namanti* (the Brahmins bow to one another), *anyonyau*, *anyonyān*, *anyonyena kṛtam*, *anyonyasmai dattam*, and so forth. Māgha [wrote]: *anyonyeṣāṃ puṣkarair āmṛśantaḥ*. The same applies to *parasparam*.

Here, by virtue of the *kaskādi* group, the visarga is replaced by *s*, as in *itaretaram* and *itaretareṇa*, etc. It should be stated that for feminine and neuter [stems], the case-ending situated in the second member of the compound undergoes the substitution of *ām*. Thus: *anyonyām*, *anyonyam*; *parasparām*, *parasparam*; or *itaretarām*, *itaretaram*—these two Brahmin women, or these two families, feed [one another]. Regarding this, some maintain that the substitute *ām* occurs only for the accusative case, because it is cited in that very way in the *Bhāṣya* and other works.

Therefore, they say that even for feminine and neuter bases, the form is exactly like the masculine in the third case (*tṛtīyā*) and subsequent cases. Others, however, because the example given is merely illustrative, state that there is the substitution of *ām* for all case-endings. The absence of the suffix *ṭāp* in both members [of the compound], the absence of the augment *ṭāp* in the neuter in the nominative singular (*svamau*), and the non-elision (*aluk*) of the nominative suffix (*su*) in a compound—all this is established by way of irregularity (*bāhulakāt*). For instance, in the expressions *anyonyam* and *parasparam*, the suffix *ṭāp* would have been required for both members; yet, the rule "a pronoun undergoes masculinization (*puṃvadbhāva*) in all derivative formations (*vṛtti*)" does not apply here.

Because the status of not being treated as a compound (*asamāsavadbhāva*) does not apply to *anya* and *para*, and because reduplication alone is not the *vṛtti* (compound formation), there would be an over-extension (*atiprasaṅga*) in cases such as "whichever timid-eyed woman her lover gazed upon, she [became] that [woman]," and so forth. Furthermore, in the case of *anyonya* and *itaretara*, the suffix *adḍ* would be required by the rule *adḍ ṛtādibhyaḥ*. In examples such as *anyonyasaṃsaktamahastriyāmam*, *anyonyāśrayaḥ*, *parasparākṣisādṛśyam*, and *adṛṣṭaparasparaiḥ*, the elision of the nominative case ending (*suluk*) would also be required. All of this must be resolved through the principle of diversity (*bāhulaka*).

The example from the *Vārttika* and *Bhāṣya* on the present topic, as well as the *Bhāṣya* statement "that [is mutual dependence]" under the rule *striyām* (Pāṇini 4.1.3), serve as the authority here.
Regarding the rule *akṛcchre priyasukhayor anyatarasyām* (A 8.1.13):

one gives *priyapriyeṇa* or *priyeṇa*; one gives *sukhasukhena* or *sukhena*. Because of the application of the *karmadhārayavat* treatment when there is reduplication, the case-ending (*sup*) is elided, and then that very same word-form is used again. The meaning is: "one gives even a very dear object without effort."

SK 2149 *yathāsve yathāyatham* (A 8.1.14): *yathāsvam* is an *avyayībhāva* compound used in the sense of distributive repetition (*vīpsā*). That which is the self (*ātman*) and that which belongs to the self (*ātmīya*)—that is *yathāsvam*. In this case, the word *yathā* is prescribed as being doubled and as having the neuter gender. *Yathāyathaṃ jñātā*: one who knows according to [each thing's] own nature; the meaning is "according to its own nature" (*yathāsvabhāvam*), or alternatively, "according to what belongs to itself" (*yathātmīyam*). SK 2150 *dvandvaṃ rahasyamaryādāvacanavyutkramaṇayajñapātraprayogābhivyaktiṣu* (A 8.1.16): The word *dvandva* is prescribed as being doubled in the following senses: secrecy (*rahasya*), the expression of a limit (*maryādāvacana*), transgression (*vyutkramaṇa*), the employment of sacrificial vessels (*yajñapātraprayoga*), and manifestation (*abhivyakti*).

In these senses, the reduplication of the word *dvi*, the substitution of *ambh-* for the first member (*pūrvapada*), the substitution of *at* for the second member (*uttarapada*), and the neuter gender are prescribed as irregularities (*nipātyate*). Among these, "secret" (*rahasya*) is the expressed meaning (*vācya*) of the word *dvandva*; the others are its domains of application (*viṣaya*). *Dvandvaṃ mantrayate* means "he consults in secret. *Maryādā* is the non-transgression of established limits. *Ācaturaṃ hīme paśavo dvandvaṃ mithunīyanti* means "these animals mate in pairs even up to the fourth generation"; that is, the mother mates with her son, her grandson, and even her great-grandson.

*Vyutkramaṇa* means standing separately. *Dvandvaṃ vyutkrāntāḥ* means they are situated separately by virtue of being connected in pairs. "He employs the sacrificial vessels in pairs" (*dvandvaṃ yajñapātrāṇi prayunakti*). "The two, Saṃkarṣaṇa and Vāsudeva, [are] in pair" (*dvandvaṃ saṃkarṣaṇavāsudevau*); the meaning is that they are manifested through association. By means of a formal division of rules (*yogavibhāga*), the term *dvandva* is also desired in other instances. Thus ends the section on reduplicated formations. Thus ends the first half of the *Siddhāntakaumudī* composed by the venerable Bhaṭṭojidīkṣita.
The second half [of the section on verbal roots];
the *bhvādi* class within the section on verbal endings (tiṅanta). 41.

Though praised day and night by great sages who possess the qualities of those learned in the Vedas and worthy of offerings, the All-pervading Lord, whose very nature is excellence, is ever more victorious. // 1 //
The suffixes occurring in the fourth and fifth chapters have been explained in the first half [of this work]; now, those belonging to the scope of the third chapter are being explained. (2)
First, the ten *lakāras* are presented here: *laṭ*, *liṭ*, *luṭ*, *lṛṭ*, *leṭ*, *loṭ*, *laṅ*, *luṅ*, *lṛṅ*. Among these, the fifth *lakāra* (*leṭ*) has as its domain only the Vedic meters.
*A 3.2.123*: "In the sense of the present, *laṭ* [is used].
The suffix *laṭ* occurs after a verbal root that expresses a present action. [The augment] *aṭ* is elided.
SK 2152: *laḥ karmaṇi ca bhāve cākarmakebhyaḥ* (A 3.4.69).

The *l*-suffixes [denote] the object (*karman*) as well as the agent (*kartṛ*) after transitive verbs (*sakarmaka*), and they denote the state (*bhāva*) as well as the agent after intransitive verbs (*akarmaka*). SK 2153: *lasya* (A 3.4.77).
This is the heading.

SK 2154: *tiptasjhisipthasthamibvasmastātāṃjhathāsāthāṃdhvamiḍvahimahiṅ* (A 3.4.78). These eighteen are the substitutes for *la*. SK 2155: *laḥ parasmaipadam* (A 1.4.99). [The *la*-substitutes] are the *parasmaipada*.
The substitutes for *l* shall be designated as *parasmaipada*. (A 1.4.100) *taṅ*, *āna*, and *āna* shall have this designation (*ātmanepada*). This is an exception to the preceding designation.
SK 2157: *anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam* (A 1.3.12).

The *ātmanepada* endings shall occur in place of *L* after a verbal root that is marked with an indicatory low-pitched vowel (*anudātta*) in its original enunciation (*upadeśa*), or which ends in an indicatory nasal (*ṅit*).

SK 2158: *svaritañitaḥ kartrabhiprāye kriyāphale* (A 1.3.72). [The *ātmanepada* endings occur] after a root marked with an indicatory circumflex vowel (*svarita*) or an indicatory nasal (*ṅit*), when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent.
The *ātmanepada* suffixes shall occur after a root that has a circumflex (*svarita*) accent on its indicatory letter (*ñit*), provided the fruit of the action accrues to the agent.

(A 1.3.72) "From the remainder, the *parasmaipada* suffixes occur when the agent is expressed" (A 1.3.78): after a root that lacks the causes for *ātmanepada*, the *parasmaipada* suffixes shall occur when the agent is expressed.

SK 2160: *tiṅas trīṇi trīṇi prathamamadhyamottamāḥ* (Pāṇini 1.4.101). Of the *tiṅ* suffixes in both voices (*parasmaipada* and *ātmanepada*), the three triplets [of suffixes] are respectively designated by these names: first, middle, and last. SK 2161: *tāny ekavacanadvivacanabahuvacanāny ekaśaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.4.102). These [triplets] are respectively termed singular, dual, and plural.

The three numbers of each of the *tiṅ* suffixes, having received their respective designations as "first" (*prathama*) and so forth, shall each individually receive the designations "singular" (*ekavacana*) and so on. (Pāṇini 1.4.102) When *yuṣmad* is present as a coreferential (*samānādhikaraṇa*) word, even if it is not actually employed, the second person (*madhyama*) [suffix] is used. (Pāṇini 1.4.105) When *yuṣmad*, which denotes the grammatical participant (*kāraka*) expressed by the *tiṅ* suffix, is either employed or not employed, the second person suffix shall be used.

SK 2163: *prahāse ca manyopapade manyater uttama ekavac ca* (A 1.4.106). When a verbal root has *manya-* as its subordinate word (*upapada*), the second person (*madhyama*) shall be used provided that the sense of jest (*prahāsa*) is understood; however, for the root *manya-*, the third person (*uttama*) shall be used, and it shall express a single entity. SK 2164: *asmady uttamaḥ* (A 1.4.107). [The third person is used] when the word *asmat* ("we") is present.

In such a case, the *uttama* (first person) [ending] should be used. According to Pāṇini 1.4.108, *śeṣe prathamaḥ* ("the first person is used for the remainder"), the *prathama* (third person) should be used when neither the *madhyama* (second person) nor the *uttama* (first person) is applicable. The root *bhū* is used in the sense of "existence" (*sattā*). When the agent (*kartṛ*) is intended to be expressed, and the form *bhū ti* has been established:

SK 2166: *tiṅ-aśit sārvadhātukam* (A 3.4.113). Both *tiṅ* affixes and those beginning with *ś* that are mentioned under the heading of "dhātu" (verbal root) shall receive this designation (*sārvadhātuka*). SK 2167: *kartari śap* (A 3.1.68). [The suffix] *śap* is applied when the agent (*kartṛ*) is expressed.

When a *sārvadhātuka* suffix follows in the sense of an agent, the affix *śap* is added to the root. In *śap*, the letters *ś* and *p* are indicatory (*it*). By the rule *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* (A 7.3.84), when these two [suffixes] follow, there is *guṇa* substitution for a stem ending in an *iṭ* vowel. There is the substitution of *ava*. Thus: *bhavati*, *bhavataḥ*.

SK 2169 *jho 'ntaḥ* (A 7.1.3): For a *jh*-sound that is a constituent of an affix, there shall be the substitution of *ant*. [Thus, by *ato guṇe*: *bhavanti*, *bhavasi*, *bhavathaḥ*, *bhavatha*. SK 2170 *ato dīrgho yañi* (A 7.3.101): A long vowel is substituted for *at* before an affix beginning with *yañ*.

Therefore, there shall be lengthening of the stem when a sārvadhātuka suffix beginning with *yañ* follows. *bhavāmi* (I am), *bhavāvaḥ* (we two are), *bhavāmaḥ* (we are). *sa bhavati* (he is), *tau bhavataḥ* (they two are), *te bhavanti* (they are). *tvaṃ bhavasi* (you are), *yuvāṃ bhavathaḥ* (you two are), *yūyaṃ bhavatha* (you all are). *ahaṃ bhavāmi* (I am), *āvāṃ bhavāvaḥ* (we two are), *vayaṃ bhavāmaḥ* (we are). "Come, I think you will eat rice"—but it was eaten by the guests. "I think you two will eat this rice," or "you [plural] will eat this. "I will eat."

The meaning is "we two shall eat" (*bhokṣyāvahe*), "we [all] shall eat" (*bhokṣyāmahe*), "you think" (*manyase*), "you two think" (*manyethe*), "you [plural] think" (*manyadhve*), and so forth. The rule *yuṣmady upapade* ("when *yuṣmad* is the accompanying word") and others continue to apply; therefore, it does not apply here: *etu bhavān manyate odanaṃ bhokṣye iti bhuktaḥ so 'tithibhiḥ* ("Come, sir; you think 'I shall eat rice,' but it has been eaten by the guests"). What is the purpose of the term *prahāse* ("in jest")? It is so that it does not apply when stating the facts as they are, such as: *ehi manyase odanaṃ bhokṣye iti bhuktaḥ so 'tithibhiḥ* ("Come; you think 'I shall eat rice,' but it has been eaten by the guests," etc.). **SK 2171**: *parokṣe liṭ* (A 3.2.115).

The suffix *liṭ* occurs after a verbal root whose meaning refers to a past time that is not of today (*anadyatana*) and is beyond the range of direct perception (*parokṣa*). For *la*, the substitutes *tiP* and so forth are applied.

SK 2172 *liṭ ca* (A 3.4.115): A substitute for *liṭ* shall have the designation *ārdhadhātuka* only, and not the designation *sārvadhātuka*. Consequently, [the suffixes] *śap* and so forth do not apply. SK 2173 *parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatususthalathusaṇalvamāḥ* (A 3.4.82).
For the nine suffixes beginning with *tiP* of the *liṭ* [perfect], nine substitutes beginning with *ṇal* shall occur. When *bhū a* is established, [the rule] *bhuvo vug luṅ-liṭoḥ* (A 6.4.88) applies:
the augment *vuk* shall occur for the root *bhū* before a vowel in the *luṅ* and *liṭ* tenses. Because it is obligatory (*nitya*), *vuk* subverts both *guṇa* and *vṛddhi*.
Having introduced [the rules] "ekāco dve prathamasya" (A 6.1.1) and "ajāder dvitīyasya" (A 6.1.2):

SK 2177: *liṭi dhātor anabhyāsayasya* (A 6.1.8). When *liṭ* follows, the first monosyllabic (*ekāc*) constituent of a verbal root that has not yet undergone reduplication (*anabhyāsa*) becomes doubled; however, for that which follows the initial vowel, the second [monosyllabic] constituent is doubled. When the form *bhūv bhūv a* is established: SK 2178: *pūrvo 'bhyāsaḥ* (A 6.1.4). The preceding [portion] is called the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).
In this context, of the two [substitutions] that are prescribed, the former shall be designated as "abhyāsa" (reduplication).
By the rule *halādi śeṣaḥ* (A 7.4.60), the initial consonant (*hal*) of the reduplication is retained, while the other consonants (*hal*) are elided; thus, there is the elision of the *v*.
SK 2180 *hrasvaḥ* (A 7.4.59): The vowel of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) shall be short. SK 2181 *bhavater aḥ* (A 7.4.73): [The substitute] *a* [is applied] to the root *bhū*.
In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, the *u* of the reduplicated syllable of the root *bhū* shall become *a*.

According to Pāṇini 8.4.54, *abhyāse carcā*, in a reduplicated syllable, the *car* sounds shall replace the *jhal* sounds, as well as the *jaś* sounds; specifically, the *jaś* sounds replace the *jhaś* sounds, and the *car* sounds replace the *jhaś* sounds. Furthermore, among those, the *jaś* sounds of the original form (*prakṛti*) are replaced by *jaś* sounds, and the *car* sounds of the original form are replaced by *car* sounds—this distinction is made according to the principle of closest proximity (*āntaratamya*).

SK 2183: *asiddhavad atrābhāt* (A 6.4.22). From here until the end of the chapter (*āpādaparisamāpteḥ*), [the rules] belong to the *ābhīya* section. When that [operation] which has a common locus (*samānāśraya*) is to be performed, this [preceding rule] shall be treated as if it were unestablished (*asiddha*). Thus, since the *vuk* augment would be unestablished, *uvaṅ* would be applicable; therefore, it must be stated that *vuk* and *yuṭ* are established (*siddha*) in relation to *uvaṅ* and *aṇ*. [Examples: *babhūva*, *babhūvatuḥ*, *babhūvuḥ*. SK 2184: *ārdhadhātukasyeḍvalādeḥ* (A 7.2.35). [The augment *iṭ* is added] to an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant.
The augment *iṭ* shall be added to an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix following roots such as *bal* and others. [Examples: *babhūvitha*, *babhūvathuḥ*, *babhūva*, *babhūva*, *babhūviva*, *babhūvima*.
SK 2185: *anadyatane luṭ* (A 3.3.15). The suffix *luṭ* shall be applied after a verbal root when the sense is future (*bhaviṣyat*) but not pertaining to the current day (*anadyatana*).

SK 2186: *syatāsī lṛluṭoḥ* (A 3.1.33). The term *lṛ* here is a designation for both *lṛṅ* and *lṛṭ*. After a verbal root (*dhātu*), these two suffixes, *sya* and *tāsī*, occur when *lṛṅ* and *lṛṭ* follow; they serve as exceptions to [the addition of] *śap* and other such affixes. SK 2187: *ārdhadhātukaṃ śeṣaḥ* (A 3.4.114). All remaining [suffixes] are termed *ārdhadhātuka*.
A suffix prescribed after a verbal root (dhātu) other than those [ending in] tiṅ or śit shall receive this technical designation (kṛt). [The suffix] iṭ.

According to A 2.4.85, *luṭaḥ prathamasya ḍāraurasaḥ*, the suffixes *ḍā*, *rau*, and *ras* shall respectively replace the first person endings. By virtue of the marker *ṭ* [in *ḍā*], there is elision of the final phoneme (*ṭi*) even though it does not belong to a nominal stem (*abha*).

SK 2189: *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* (A 7.3.86). Guṇa shall be substituted for the *ik* vowel of a root ending in a *pu*-class consonant (*pu-ganta*) or of a stem having a light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadha*), when followed by a *sārvadhātuka* or *ārdhadhātuka* suffix. According to the authority of this rule, even when there is an intervention by that which does not cause the elision of a letter (*nāvyavadhāna*), [the substitution applies]. Therefore, in forms such as *bhinatti*, the *ik* vowel is not subject to guṇa because it is separated by one intervening element. In the form *bhavit-ā*, guṇa would apply to the single *ik*. SK 2190: *dīdhīvevīṭām* (A 1.1.6). [The prohibition of guṇa applies] to the roots *dīdhī* and *vevī*, and to the augment *iṭ*.
The *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* substitutions do not occur for the roots *dīdhī* and *vevī*, nor for the augment *iṭ*. [Example: *bhavitā*.
(A 7.4.50) *tāsastyor lopaḥ*:
There is elision (*lopa*) of the root *tās* and of the root *as* when followed by an affix beginning with *s*.

SK 2192 *ri ca* (A 7.4.51): Before an affix beginning with *r*, [the substitution of *ar* for *as*] is as stated previously. *bhavitārau*, *bhavitāraḥ*; *bhavitāsi*, *bhavitāsthaḥ*, *bhavitāstha*; *bhavitāsmi*, *bhavitāsvaḥ*, *bhavitāsmaḥ*. SK 2193 *lṛṭ śeṣe ca* (A 3.3.13): The suffix *lṛṭ* is used in the remaining cases as well.

The suffix *lṛṭ* occurs after a verbal root denoting a future action, whether or not there is another action performed for the sake of that [future] action. [The augment] *sya* is added, followed by *iṭ*. [Examples: *bhaviṣyati*, *bhaviṣyataḥ*, *bhaviṣyanti*; *bhaviṣyasi*, *bhaviṣyathaḥ*, *bhaviṣyatha*; *bhaviṣyāmi*, *bhaviṣyāvaḥ*, *bhaviṣyāmaḥ*. SK 2194: *loṭ ca* (A 3.3.162).
The suffix *loṭ* occurs after a verbal root in the senses of injunction (*vidhi*) and so forth.
SK 2195: The *liṅ* and *loṭ* [suffixes] are used in the sense of benediction (*āśis*).
SK 2196: For the *e* of the *loṭ*, there shall be *u*. [Thus: *bhavatu*.

SK 2197: *tuhyoḥ tātaṅ āśiṣy anyatarasyām* (A 7.1.35). In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), *tātaṅ* may optionally replace *tu* and *hi*. Because it consists of more than one phoneme (*anekāl*), it is a replacement for the whole (*sarvādeśa*). Although this [rule] is an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule *ṅic ca* [which states that a substitute ending in *ṅ* replaces only the final phoneme], it nonetheless finds its scope of application in cases like *anaṅ* and others where the *ṅ*-mark serves no other purpose. Thus, when *tātaṅ*—whose *ṅ*-mark has a valid function such as the prohibition of *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* or the occurrence of *saṃprasāraṇa*—is encountered, it proceeds slowly and is superseded by the subsequent rule, because here even the general rule (*utsarga*) and the exception (*apavāda*) possess equal force. [Examples: *bhavatāt*. SK 2198: *loṭo laṅvat* (A 3.4.85). [The suffixes of] *loṭ* are treated like those of *laṅ*.

The *loṭ* [imperative] should undergo the same operations as the *laṅ* [imperfect]. Consequently, *tām* and the other suffixes are substituted, and there is elision of the *s*. For it is thus stated: "In place of *ta*, *thas*, *tha*, and *mi*, there shall be *tām*, *tam*, *ta*, and *am* respectively" (A 3.4.101).
Thus, for the four *ṅit* endings, *tām* and the others are substituted in their respective order.

SK 2200 *nityaṃ ṅitaḥ* (A 3.4.99): There must always be elision of the final *s* of the third person plural ending (*uttama*) when it ends in *s* and is marked with the *ṅ*-sign. By the rule *alo 'ntyasya*, there is elision of the final *s*. [Thus we get] *bhavatām* and *bhavantu*. SK 2201 *ser hy apic ca* (A 3.4.87): [The substitution of *hi* for *si* occurs] before a root beginning with *h* and before endings that do not have an indicatory *p*.
In place of the imperative suffix *si*, *hi* shall be substituted, and that [suffix] is also elided.
(SK 2202) By the rule *ato heḥ* (A 6.4.105), there is elision (*luk*) of the *hi* following an *at* vowel. Thus: *bhava*; *bhavatāt*; *bhavatam*; *bhavata*.

SK 2203: *mer niḥ* (A 3.4.89). For the imperative (*loṭ*), *niḥ* shall be substituted for *me*. SK 2204: *āḍuttamasya pic ca* (A 3.4.92). And for the first person (*uttama*), there is the augment *āṭ*, and it is also treated as having the marker *p*.

The augment *āṭ* shall be added to the first person of the imperative (*loṭ*), and it shall be treated as having the marker *p*. By virtue of the phonetic capacity of the vowel *i*, there is no substitution of *u* for the *i* in *hi* and *ni*. [Examples: *bhavāni*, *bhavāva*, *bhavāma*.
SK 2205: *anadyatane laṅ* (A 3.2.111).
The suffix *laṅ* shall be applied after a verbal root that functions to express a past sense not belonging to the current day.
SK 2206: *luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣvaḍudāttaḥ* (A 6.4.71).
When these [suffixes] follow, the augment *aṭ* is added to the stem, and it is acute (*udātta*). SK 2207:
*itaś ca* (A 3.4.100). [The suffix *aṭ* is also added] after [a verbal root ending in] *i*.
The *ik* ending of that which is *lasya parasmaipada* shall be elided. *abhavat*, *abhavatām*, *abhavan*; *abhavaḥ*, *abhavatam*, *abhavata*; *abhavam*, *abhavāva*, *abhavāma*.

(SK 2208) The *liṅ* [suffix] is used in the sense of injunction (*vidhi*), invitation (*nimantraṇa*), entreaty (*āmantraṇa*), request (*adhīṣṭa*), inquiry (*saṃpraśna*), and supplication (*prārthana*). (A 3.3.161)

When these meanings—whether as indicated (*dyotya*) or as expressed (*vācya*)—are to be conveyed, the optative suffix (*liṅ*) shall be used. *Vidhi* is an instigation; *preraṇa* is the urging of a subordinate, such as a servant; *nimantraṇa* is the performance of a duty, the engaging of a daughter's son and others in necessary acts such as a *śrāddha* meal; *āmantraṇa* is permission to act according to one’s own will; *adhīṣṭa* is an activity preceded by respect. It would have been sufficient simply to say "the optative is used for instigation" (*pravartanāyāṃ liṅ*). The separate mention of the four [sub-varieties] is for the sake of elaboration. [The rule] *yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅic ca* (A 3.4.103).

The augment *yāsuṭ* shall be added to the *parasmaipada* endings of the *liṅ*; it is both acute (*udātta*) and marked with the *ṅ*-sign (*ṅit*). From the mention of the *ṅ*-sign, it is understood that in some instances of operations dependent on an indicatory letter (*anubandha*), the prohibition "not when there is a rule concerning a letter" (*analvidhau*) applies. Furthermore, the fact that the substitute *śānac* for *śnā* is marked with the *ś*-sign (*śit*) is also an indicator here [of this principle].

By the rule *suṭ tothoḥ* (A 3.4.107), *suṭ* is added to the *takāra* and *thakāra* of the *liṅ*. *Yāsuṭ* is not superseded by *suṭ*, because their domains differ: *yāsuṭ* is added to the *liṅ*, whereas *suṭ* is added to the *takāra* and *thakāra* [of the *liṅ*].

SK 2211: *liṅaḥ salopo ’nantyasya* (A 7.2.79). There is elision of the non-final *s* of the *liṅ* suffixes belonging to the *sārvadhātuka* class. Thus, there is the disappearance of both *s* sounds. However, the *suṭ* augment is heard in the *āśīr-liṅ* (the benedictive mood), and it is even more clearly audible there in the *ātmanepada*. SK 2212: *ato yeyaḥ* (A 7.2.80). [The *iy* substitute takes the place of the *ārdhadhātuka* affix *liṭ* following a verbal root ending in short *a*.]

Therefore, for the *y* that is part of a subsequent *sārvadhātuka* suffix, *iy* should be substituted. [Then] *guṇa* [applies], and there is the elision of *y*. Thus: *bhavet*. Why "in a *sārvadhātuka* suffix"? [Consider: *cikīrṣyāt*. For, by the rule of "an exception [blocks] what intervenes," only the elision of *a* (*ato lopa*) is blocked. However, in cases such as *bhaved*, the long vowel (*dīrgha*) would occur because it is a subsequent rule. [Thus: *bhavetām*. SK 2213: *jher jus* (A 3.3.18).
*jus* should be substituted for the *jh* of the *liṅ* [suffix]. [The *ja* is elided. *it*.

SK 2214: *usy apadāntāt* (A 6.1.96). When *uṣ* follows a non-final *a*-vowel, there shall be a single substitute of the form of the subsequent [vowel]. This being the case, the ancient teachers maintain that because it is both subsequent (*paratva*) and obligatory (*nityatva*), the rule *ato yeyaḥ* applies. Even though, by virtue of being internal (*antaraṅga*), the substitution of the subsequent form (*pararūpa*) would be more logical, nevertheless, this [rule] should be explained as *iy* replacing *yās*. Thus, *iy* is an exception (*apavāda*) to the elision of *s* (*salopa*). However, in the rule *ato yeyaḥ*, the euphonic combination (*sandhi*) is archaic (*ārṣa*). [Examples: *bhaveyuḥ*, *bhaveḥ*, *bhavetam*, *bhaveta*, *bhaveyam*, *bhaveva*, *bhavema*.
SK 2215: *liṅ āśiṣi* (A 3.4.116). [The suffix *liṅ* is used in the sense of benediction.]
In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), the *liṅ* verbal suffix shall have the designation *ārdhadhātuka*.
By the rule *kid āśiṣi* (A 3.4.104), the *yāsuṭ* augment of the *liṅ* in the sense of benediction shall be *kit*. By the rule *skoḥ—*, there is the elision of the *s*.

SK 2217 *kṅiti ca* (A 1.1.5): When *gi*, *kit*, or *ṅit* suffixes are present, the *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* substitutions caused by an *ik*-vowel do not take place. *bhūtāt* / *bhūyāstām* / *bhūyāsuḥ* / *bhūyāḥ* / *bhūyāstam* / *bhūyāsta* / *bhūyāsam* / *bhūyāsva* / *bhūyāsma*. SK 2218 *luṅ* (A 3.2.110).
The *luṅ* suffix shall be used after a verbal root (*dhātu*) expressing an event that has already occurred.
By the rule *māṅi luṅ* (A 3.3.175), *luṅ* is an exception (*apavāda*) to all other tense and mood suffixes (*lakāra*).
SK 2220: *smottare laṅ ca* (A 3.3.176).
When *māṅ* follows *smṛ*, the *laṅ* suffix shall be used, and optionally the *luṅ* suffix as well.
SK 2221: *cli luṅi* (A 3.1.43). [The augment] *cli* is applied when the *luṅ* suffix follows.
The exception [to the substitution] of *śa* and so forth:
by A 3.1.44, *sic* is substituted for *cli*;
and in this case, the *i* and *c* are *it*.

SK 2223: *gāti-sthā-ghu-pā-bhū-bhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (A 2.4.77). After these roots, there shall be elision (*luk*) of the suffix *sic* when followed by *parasmaipada* endings. Here, *gā* and *pā* are understood as the substitutes (*ādeśa*) for *iṇ* and *pibati*.
SK 2224: *bhūsuvos tiṅi* (A 7.3.88). [The substitution of *guṇa* occurs] for the roots *bhū* and *su* before a *tiṅ* suffix.
In the case of these two roots, *bhū* and *sū*, there shall be no *guṇa* substitution when followed by a *sārvadhātuka* *tiṅ* affix.

Regarding *astisico 'pṛkte* (A 7.3.96): *sic* and *as* form a collective *dvandva* compound. The status of *bha* for the word *sic* is based on Vedic usage (*sautra*). The term *asti* forms a *karmadhāraya* with the [root] *as*. Then, there is the Vedic elision (*luk*) of the fifth case ending. Thus, the augment *īṭ* is applied to a single-consonant (*apṛkta*) consonant following *sic* or *as* when they are present. Therefore, *īṭ* does not apply here [in the example below] because *sic* has been elided. *abhūt* (he became). Why "after a consonant" (*halaḥ*)? Consider *aidhiṣi* (I prospered). Why "of a single-consonant" (*apṛktasya*)? Consider *aidhiṣṭa* (he prospered) and *abhūtām* (they two became).

SK 2226 *sijabhyastavidibhyaś ca* (A 3.4.109): After the suffix *sic*, after a reduplicated stem (*abhyasta*), and after a stem ending in two consonants (*dvic*), there shall be *jus* in place of *jhi* when it is related to a *ṅit* affix. This being the case, [the following applies]: SK 2227 *ātaḥ* (A 3.4.110).
The suffix *jus* shall replace *jhi* only after a root ending in a vowel that has lost its *sij* augment. Examples: *abhūvan*, *abhūḥ*, *abhūtam*, *abhūtaḥ*, *abhūvam*, *abhūva*, *abhūma*.
According to Pāṇini A 6.4.74 (*na māḍyoge*), the augments *aṭ* and *āṭ* do not occur when used in conjunction with the prohibitive particle *mā*. Examples:
*mā bhavān bhūt*, *mā sma bhavat*, or *mā sma bhūt*.

SK 2229: *liṅnimitte lṛṅ kriyātipattau* (A 3.3.139). When there is a cause for the conditional (*liṅ*), such as the relation of cause and effect (*hetu-hetumadbhāva*) and so forth, the conditional suffix (*lṛṅ*) shall be used in the sense of the future, provided that the non-actualization of the action is understood. Examples: *abhaviṣyat*, *abhaviṣyatām*, *abhaviṣyan*; *abhaviṣyaḥ*, *abhaviṣyatam*, *abhaviṣyata*; *abhaviṣyam*, *abhaviṣyāva*, *abhaviṣyāma*. SK 2230: *te prāg dhātoḥ* (A 1.4.80). Those [suffixes] occur before the verbal root.
Those [words] designated as *gati* and *upasarga* must be employed only before the verbal root. (SK 2231) *Āni loṭ* (A 8.4.16):

Following a cause situated in an *upasarga*, the *ṇ* shall replace the *ṇ* of the substitute *āni* for the imperative (*loṭ*). Example: *prabhavāṇi*. It should be stated that there is a prohibition of the status of *upasarga* for *dus* in the rules concerning the substitution of *ṣ* and *ṇ*. Examples: *duḥsthitiḥ*; *durbhavāni*. The status of *upasarga* for the word *antar* should be stated in the rules concerning the suffix *aṅ*, the suffix *ki*, and the substitution of *ṇ*. Examples: *antardhā*; *antardhiḥ*; *antarbhavāṇi*.

SK 2232: *śeṣe vibhāṣākakhādāvaṣānta upadeśe* (A 8.4.18). When followed by a verbal root other than those beginning with *ka*, *kha*, etc., and ending in *ṣa*, in its original form (*upadeśe*), the *ṇatva* (nasalization to *ṇ*) of the *n* of *ni* may optionally occur after a cause situated in a prefix (*upasarga*). For example: *praṇibhavati* or *pranibhavati*. Here, even though the prefixes are not compounded, their *saṃhitā* (euphonic junction) is obligatory. As it has been said: "The *saṃhitā* is obligatory within a single word and between a verbal root and a prefix; it is obligatory in a compound, but in a sentence, it depends on the speaker's intention. Furthermore, the mention of meanings such as "existence" (*sattā*) and so forth is merely illustrative (*upalakṣaṇa*).

In expressions such as "Heaven results from sacrifice" (*yāgāt svargo bhavati*), the meaning is that [heaven] "arises" (*utpadyate*) and so forth; however, prefixes (*upasarga*) serve to indicate specific nuances of meaning. This is because in cases such as *prabhavati*, *parābhavati*, *saṃbhavati*, *anubhavati*, *abhibhavati*, *udbhavati*, and *paribhavati*, a distinct meaning is understood. And it has been said: "By means of a prefix, the meaning of a verbal root is forcibly perceived as something else, just as in the case of striking (*prahāra*), eating (*āhāra*), gathering (*saṃhāra*), wandering (*vihāra*), and avoiding (*parihāra*). [The root] *edh* (to increase) follows. The thirty-six roots ending in *kattha* are anudātta-its.
SK 2233: *ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere* (A 3.4.79).

For those *ātmanepada* endings that have a *ṭi*-marker, the final vowel (*ṭeḥ*) shall be replaced by *a*. [Thus: *edhate*. SK 2234: *sārvadhātukam apit* (A 1.2.4). A *sārvadhātuka* suffix that is not marked with *p* is *ṅit*.

Furthermore, a sārvadhātuka [affix] should be treated as having the marker ṅ. According to A 7.2.81, *āto ṅitaḥ*, the vowel *ā* of those [sārvadhātuka affixes] that have the marker ṅ following an *a* [of the verbal root] shall be replaced by *iy*. Thus: *edhete*, *edhante*.

SK 2236: *thāsaḥ se* (A 3.4.80). For the *thās* of the *laṅ* [ending] that follows a suffix marked with *ṭ*, there shall be *se*. [Examples: *edhase*, *edhe*, *edhadhve*. [In *edhāthe*: by *ato guṇe* (A 6.1.97),] *edhe*. [Examples: *edhāvahe*, *edhāmahe*. SK 2237: *ijādeś ca gurumato ’nṛcchaḥ* (A 3.1.35). [The suffix *ām* is applied after a verbal root beginning with *i* or *ī* that has a heavy vowel (*gurumat*), provided it does not end in *ṛcch*.]

Any root beginning with *ij* that possesses a heavy vowel (*guru*) takes the suffix *ām* in place of *liṭ*, except for those roots ending in *ṛ*. The *m* of *ām* does not become nasalized (*it*). This is known from the rule prescribing *ām* after the roots *ās* and *kās*.
According to A 2.4.81, *āmaḥ*: there is elision (*luk*) of what follows *ām*.

SK 2239: *kṛñ cānuprayujyate liṭi* (A 3.1.40). After a root ending in *ām*, the roots *kṛ*, *bhū*, and *as* are employed as subsequent suffixes (*anuprayoga*) when followed by the *liṭ* suffix. From the force of the inclusion of the term *kṛñ* in the rule *āmpratyayavat kṛño 'nuprayogasya*, it is understood that the subsequent suffixation applies to others as well. Consequently, from the rule *kṛño dvitīya-*—where the *ñ* serves as a *pratyāhāra* (abbreviation) for the group beginning with *kṛñ*—the inclusion of *bhū* and *as* is obtained. Because these [roots] denote general action while the bases of the *ām*-formation denote specific action, there is a relation of non-difference (*abhedānvaya*) between their respective meanings.

Although *saṃpad* is included within *pratyāhāra*, it is not employed because its meaning is not [properly] connected [to the context]. As for the root *kṛ*, since the *parasmaipada* endings would otherwise apply when the fruit of the action accrues to another, [the rule] applies: "The subsequent employment (*anuprayoga*) of *kṛ* is like the suffix *ām*" (A 1.3.63). SK 2240.

The compound *ām-pratyayo yasmāt* is a *bahuvrīhi* of the *atadguṇasaṃvijñāna* type [meaning "that from which the suffix *ām* arises"]. The *ātmanepada* should also occur after the verb *kṛ*, when it is employed following a form identical to the base of the *ām*-formation. Here, the word *pūrvavat* is carried over and connected through a split in the sentence (*vākyabheda*): "the *ātmanepada* occurs exactly as before, and not its opposite. Consequently, even when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, the *taṅ* (the *ātmanepada* endings) does not occur in forms such as *indāṃcakāra*. [This is governed by] A 3.4.81: *liṭas tajhayor eś irec*.

In place of the *ta* and *tha* substitutes of the *liṭ* [perfect], *eś* and *irec* respectively occur. The pronunciation of the vowel *e* is an indicator (*jñāpaka*) that the final phoneme (*ṭi*) of the *taṅ* substitutes does not undergo the substitution of *a*. Consequently, this does not apply to *ḍā*, *rau*, and *ras*. When the form *kṛ-e* is established, [the rule] SK 2242, *asaṃyogāl liṭ kit* (A 1.2.5), applies: a *liṭ* suffix following a non-conjunct consonant is marked with the *kit* designation. Due to the prohibition [of *guṇa*] by the rule *kṅiti ca*, there is no *guṇa* substitution by the rule *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*. Since *yaṇ* would apply after the doubling [of the root], [the following is considered].

SK 2243 *dvirvacane 'ci* (A 1.1.59): When a vowel (*ac*) that causes reduplication follows, a substitute for a vowel (*ac-ādeśa*) shall not take effect when reduplication (*dvitva*) is to be performed. SK 2244 *urat* (A 7.4.66).

The *abhyāsa* (reduplicated syllable) of a consonant shall become *at* when followed by an affix (*pratyaya*). [This results in] *sparatvam*. [Then] *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* [applies]. Why "when followed by an affix"? [Consider] *vavraś ca*.
By *kuhoś cuḥ* (A 7.4.62), there is the substitution of a *cavarga* for the *abhyāsa* *kavarga* and *hakāra*. [Thus: *edhāṃcakre*, *edhāṃcakrāte*, *edhāṃcakrire*.

A 7.2.10: *ekāca upadeśe ’nudāttāt* (from a root that is monosyllabic and has an anudātta vowel in its original enunciation). No *iṭ* augment shall be added to a *val*-beginning *ārdhadhātuka* suffix following a root that is monosyllabic and bears an anudātta accent in its original enunciation (*upadeśa*). The term "in the original enunciation" (*upadeśe*) applies to both [the root and the accent]. Why specify "monosyllabic"? So as to exclude cases where the suffix is elided (*saṅluk*). For they say: "With *śtip*, with *śap*, with a suffix having an indicatory letter (*anubandha*), with a class-marker (*gaṇa*), and where there is the mention of 'monosyllabic' (*ekāj*)—these five do not apply when there is *yaṅluk*. And this very point is made known here by the inclusion of the term "monosyllabic" (*ekāj*).

Since this is already established by the mention of "that which possesses [the vowel]" (*tadvat*) with the intention of expressing singularity (*ekatva*), the explicit mention of "single" (*eka*) serves to exclude the teaching of those that have multiple vowels (*anekāc*). Consequently, there is no prohibition for *vadhi* even though it is taught as having a single vowel in its base form (*upadeśa*), because it becomes polysyllabic (*anekāctva*) in its substituted form (*ādeśa*). Furthermore, the anudātta vowels will be collected immediately below. [Examples: *edhāṃcakṛṣe*, *edhāṃcakrāthām*. Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.3.78: *iṇaḥ ṣīdhvaṃluṅliṭāṃ dho 'ṅgāt* ("The substitute *dh* takes the place of *dhi* after an element ending in *iṇ*, before the suffixes *ṣīdhvam*, *luṅ*, and *liṭ*").

The dental *dha* of the affixes *ṣīdhvam*, *luṅ*, and *liṭ* following an *aṅga* ending in *iṇ* (the palatal class) shall be replaced by a cerebral (*mūrdhanya*). Thus: *edhāṃcakṛḍhe*, *edhāṃcakre*, *edhāṃcakṛvahe*, *edhāṃcakṛmahe*; and *edhāṃbabhūva*. By virtue of the capacity of the subsequent application (*anuprayoga*), the substitution of *bhū* for *as* does not occur here. For otherwise, he would have stated "after *kṛ*" or "after *kṛ-bhv*" in the rule *kraś cāniṭi prayujyate*. [Pāṇini 7.4.70: *ata ādeḥ*] [Translation of the Sūtra: In place of the initial vowel of a root, a long vowel is substituted when followed by an affix marked with *K* or *N*. [This applies to the examples above.]

Therefore, a long vowel shall be substituted for the initial [vowel] of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*). This is an exception to *pararūpa* (the substitution of the subsequent form). Examples include *edhāmāsa*, *edhāmāsatuḥ*, and so forth. [In the future tense: *edhitā*, *edhitārau*, *edhitāraḥ*; *edhitāse*, *edhitāsāthe*. SK 2249: *dhi ca* (Pāṇini A 8.2.25):
When a suffix beginning with *dh* follows, there is elision of the *s* [of the root]. [Example: *edhitādhve*.

In place of the *s* of the roots *tās* and *as*, there shall be *h* when followed by *eti*. *edhitāhe* / *edhitāsvahe* / *edhitāsmahe* / *edhiṣyate* / *edhiṣyete* / *edhiṣyante* / *edhiṣyase* / *edhiṣyethe* / *edhiṣyadhve* / *edhiṣye* / *edhiṣyāvahe* / *edhiṣyāmahe* / SK 2251 *āmetaḥ* (A 3.4.10): [The substitution of] *ā* occurs in place of the *me* [of the first person singular].
In the imperative (*loṭ*), *e* may optionally become *ā*. [Thus we have: *edhatām*, *edhetām*, *edhantām*. According to A 3.4.91, *savābhyāṃ vāmau*:
after *sa* (the first person ending) and *va* (the second person ending), the *e* of the imperative is respectively replaced by *va* and *am*. [Thus we have: *edhasva*, *edhethām*, *edhadhvam*.

SK 2253: *eta ai* (A 3.4.93). In the first person plural of the imperative (*loṭ*), *eta* is replaced by *ai*. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to [the substitution of] *āma*. Examples: *edhāvahe*, *edhāmahe*. SK 2254: *āḍ ajādīnām* (A 6.4.102). The augment *āṭ* is added to the beginning of verbal roots that begin with a vowel.

The augment *āṭ* shall be applied to roots beginning with vowels (*aj-ādi*) in the *luṅ* and subsequent tenses; it is an exception (*apavāda*) to *aṭ*. And [the augment *āṭ* is added] before the suffix *liṅ*. *aidhata*, *aidhetām*, *aidhanta*; *aidhathāḥ*, *aidhethām*, *aidhadhvam*; *aidhe*, *aidhāvahi*, *edhāmahi*. By rule A 3.4.102, *sīyuṭ* is added to the *liṅ* suffixes. There is elision (*lopa*) of the *s*. *edheta*, *edheyātām*.
SK 2256 *jhasya ran* (A 3.4.105):
For the *jh* [of the suffixes] of the *liṅ*, *ran* shall be substituted. *edheran*; *edhethāḥ*; *edheyāthām*; *edhedhvam*.
SK 2257 *iṭo 't* (A 3.4.106): [The *at* substitution applies] for the *it* [augment].

The augment *iṭ* of the substitutes for *liṅ* shall be replaced by *at*. [Thus: *edheya*, *edhevahi*, *edhemahi*. In the *āśīr-liṅ* (precative), because it is *ārdhadhātuka*, there is no elision of the *s* of *liṅ*. Since *sīyuṭ* and *suṭ* are parts of the affixes, they undergo *ṣatva* (the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*). [Thus: *edhiṣīṣṭa*, *edhiṣīyāstām*, *edhiṣīran*; *edhiṣīṣṭhāḥ*, *edhiṣīmahi*. [In the imperfect: *aidhiṣṭa*, *aidhiṣātām*. [By the rule] "In the *ātmanepada* endings, [the *s* of *liṅ* is elided] after a stem ending in *a*" (A 7.1.5).

When followed by a suffix beginning with a non-vowel (anakāra) in the *ātmanepada* voice, the substitute *at* shall take the place of *jha*. Thus: *aidheṣata*, *aidheṣṭhāḥ*, *aidhiṣāthām*. Regarding the rule *iṇaḥ ṣīdhvaṃluṅliṭāṃ dho ’ṅgāt*: according to the view that only the *iṇ* [root] distinct from *iṭ* is understood here, the form is *aidhiḍhvam*. However, according to the opinion that *iṇ* is understood here even when accompanied by *iṭ*, the form is *aidhidhvam*. Due to the optional doubling of the *ḍha* and *dha* sounds, as well as the *va* and *ma* sounds, there are sixteen forms. [The remaining forms are: *aidhiṣi*, *aidhiṣvahi*, *aidhiṣmahi*; [and in the conditional: *aidhiṣyata*, *aidhiṣyetām*, *aidhiṣyanta*, *aidhiṣyathāḥ*.

*aidhiṣyethām*, *aidhiṣyadhvam*, *aidhiṣye*, *aidhiṣyāvahi*, *aidhiṣyāmahi*. Because [the root] is udātta, the augment *iṭ* is applied before suffixes beginning with a consonant (*valādi*). In this context, the anudātta roots are collected as follows: "Excluding those ending in *ṛ* or *u*, the roots *yau* (yauti), *ru*, *kṣṇu*, *śīṅ*, *snu*, *nu*, *kṣu*, *śvi*, *ḍīṅ*, *śri*, *vṛṅ*, and *vṛñ*—among the single-vowel (*ekāc*) roots ending in vowels, these are traditionally recorded as being anudātta. [The following roots are also anudātta: *śaklṛ*, *pac*, *muc*, *ric*, *vac*, *vic*, *sic*, *pracch*, *tyaj*, *nijir*, and *bhaj*.

*bhañj*, *bhuj*, *bhrasj*, *masj*, *yaj*, *yuj*, *ruj*, *rañj*, *vijir*, *svañj*, *sañj*, *sṛj* // 2 // *ad*, *kṣud*, *khid*, *chid*, *tudi*, *nudaḥ*, *padya*, *bhid*, *vidyati*, *vinad*, *śad*, *sadī*, *svidyati*, *skandi*, *hadī*, *krudh*, *kṣudhi*, *budhyatī* // 3 // *bandhir*, *yudhi*, *rudhī*, *rādhir*, *vyadh*, *śudhaḥ*, *sādhi*, *siddhyātī*, *manya*, *han*, *nāp*, *kṣip*, *chupi*, *tap*, *tip*, *stṛpyati*, *dṛpyatī* // 4 //

*lip*, *lup*, *vap*, *śap*, *svap*, *sṛp*, *yabh*, *rabh*, *labh*, *gam*, *nam*, *yam*, *ram*; *kruś*, *daṃś*, *diś*, *dṛś*, *mṛś*, *riś*, *ruś*, *liś*, *viś*, *spṛś*, and *kṛṣ*. (5) *tviṣ*, *tuṣ*, *dviṣ*, *duṣ*, *puṣ*, *piṣ*, *viṣ*, *śiṣ*, *śuṣ*, *śliṣ*, *yat*, *ghas*, *vas*, *darh*, *dihi*, *duh*, *nah*, *miha*, *ruh*, *lih*, and *vah*. (6) There are one hundred and two roots ending in *h* that have anudātta [accent] in the *tudādi* class, as well as those that exist according to different opinions in the *curādi* class. (7)

The roots *tṛp* and *dṛp* are taught with the *śyan* affix in order to exclude [the addition of] *vikaraṇa* affixes; furthermore, *svid*, *pad*, *sidh*, *budh*, *man*, *puṣ*, and *śliṣ* are also taught with *śyan*. (8) The root *vas* is taught with the *śap* affix and the elision (*luk*) [of the *vikaraṇa*] to exclude others; likewise, *ṇijir*, *vijir*, and *śaklṛ* are taught with their indicatory letters (*anubandhas*). (9) The root *vindati* is accepted by the followers of Candra, Durga, and others, and it is also seen in the *Bhāṣya*; however, Vyāghrabhūti and others did not include it here—this is the established position. (10)

*rañji*, *masjī*, *adi*, *padī*, *tud*, *kṣudh*, *śuṣi*, *ṣuṣī*, *śiṣi*—these have not been mentioned in the *Bhāṣya*, yet they are stated here because they are accepted by Vyāghrabhūti and others. (11) *Spardha* means rivalry (*saṃgharṣa*). Rivalry is the desire to overcome another. Because its meaning is already included within the root's own sense, it is intransitive (*akarmaka*). One rivals (*spardhate*). [In this context,] the rule *śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ* (A 7.4.61) applies.

In the case of reduplication (*abhyāsa*), the consonants preceded by *ś* are retained; this is an exception to the rule "the initial consonant remains" (*halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*). *spardhe* (he vied); *spardhitā* (he will vie); *spardhiṣyate* (he will vie); *spardhatām* (let him vie); *aspardhata* (he vied); *spardheta* (he might vie); *spardhiṣīṣṭa* (may he vie); *aspardhiṣṭa* (he vied [past]); *aspardhiṣyata* (he would have vied). 4. *gādhṛ* is used in the senses of standing firm (*pratiṣṭhā*), desire to obtain (*lipsā*), and tying (*grantha*). *gādhate* (he stands firm/desires to obtain/ties); *jagādhe* (he stood firm/desired to obtain/tied). 5. *bādhṛ* means to strike or repel (*loḍana*). Striking (*loḍana*) is resistance (*pratighāta*). *bādhate* (he strikes/resists). 6. *nāthṛ* and 7. *nādhṛ* are used in the senses of begging (*yācñā*), affliction (*upatāpa*), sovereignty (*aiśvarya*), and benediction (*āśis*).

The term *nātha* should be stated [as having an indicatory *ṅ*] when used in the sense of a benediction (*āśis*). In this sense of benediction alone, the *ātmanepada* ending shall apply: *nāthate*. In other cases, it takes the *parasmaipada*: *nāyati*, *nādhate*. 8. *dadh* in the sense of "holding" (*dhāraṇa*): *dadhate*. Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.120: *ata ekahalmadhye 'nādeśāder liṭi*. When a root has *liṭ* as its cause, and the substitute [vowel] does not begin with a substituted [consonant], then for that stem (*aṅga*) which contains a single *hal* between two [consonants], there shall be the substitution of *e* for the vowel *a* situated between non-conjunct *hal*s, and there shall be the elision of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsalopa*), provided the *liṭ* suffix is a *kit*. [Example: *dadhe* (from *dadh* + *liṭ*). In this case, the *liṭ* suffix is a *kit*, and the stem *dadh-* contains the vowel *a* between two *hal*s (*d-a-dh-*); thus, *e* replaces the *a* and the reduplication is elided. The result is *dadhe*.

SK 2261: *thali ca seṭi* (A 6.4.121). That which was previously mentioned [the substitution of *et* and the elision of the reduplication] shall apply here as well. And in this context, only that substitute which brings about a change in form (*vairūpya*) is accepted, based on the indicative power (*jñāpaka*) of the prohibition stated for the roots *śas*, *sidh*, and others. Therefore, even when the original *jaś*-sounds are present, the substitution of *et* and the elision of the reduplication do indeed occur. Examples: *dedhe*, *dedhāte*, *dedhire*. Why [is it specified] "after a short vowel" (*ataḥ*)? [Counter-example: *didivatuḥ*. Why [is it specified] "followed by *t*" (*taparaḥ*)? [Counter-example: *rarāse*. Why [is it specified] "beginning with a single consonant" (*eka-ityādi*)? [Counter-example: *tatsaratuḥ*. Why [is it specified] "not beginning with a substitute" (*anādeśādeḥ*)? [Counter-example: *cakaṇatuḥ*. Because the term "substitute" (*ādeśa*) qualifies the *liṭ* suffix, the rule applies here [in the following cases]: *nemitha*, *sehe*.
9. *Skudi* means *āpravaṇa*; *āpravaṇa* means leaping up and lifting up.

SK 2262: *idito num dhātoḥ* (A 7.3.58). From the root *skand*: *skandate*, *cuskunde*. 10. *viśvad* in the sense of whiteness; it is intransitive (*akarmaka*). *śvindate*, *śiśvinde*. 11. *vad* in the sense of salutation and praise: *vandate*, *vavande*. 12. *bhad* in the sense of auspiciousness and happiness: *bhandate*, *babhande*. 13. *bhad* in the sense of praise, joy, intoxication, sleep, beauty, and motion: *mandate*, *mamande*. 14. *spad* in the sense of slight movement: *spandate*, *paspande*. 15. *klid* in the sense of lamenting; that is, sorrow. It is transitive (*sakarmaka*).
*klindate* (he is desirous); *ciklinde*. 16. *mud* in the sense of joy: *modate*. 17. *dada* in the sense of giving: *dadate*.

According to A 6.4.126 (*na śasadadavādiguṇānām*), there is no substitution of *et* (for the final vowel) nor elision of the reduplication for the *a* of *śas*, *dad*, those beginning with *va*, and that which has been affected by a term denoting *guṇa*. Thus: *dadade*, *dadadāte*, *dadadire*. 18. *ṣvad*; 19. *svarda* in the sense of tasting. This [root] is transitive when it means experiencing, and intransitive when it means liking.

SK 2264 *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* (A 6.1.64): The *ṣ* at the beginning of a verbal root (*dhātu*) shall become *s*. [This is stated because] there is a prohibition against the substitution of *ṣ* by the rule *sātpadādyoḥ*. *anusvadate*; *sasvade*. *svardate*; *sasvarde*. 20. *urda* in the sense of pride and play. SK 2265 *upadhāyāṃ ca* (A 8.2.79).

A long vowel shall replace the *ik* vowels (i, u, ṛ, ḷ) when they follow a root-final *repha* (r) or *vakāra* (v) that serves as an *upadhā* (penultimate) and is followed by a consonant (*hal*). Examples: *ūrdate* (he leaps); *ūrdāñcakre* (he has leaped). 21. *kurda*, 22. *khurda*, 23. *gurda*, 24. *guda*—these roots mean "to play" (*krīḍā*) only. *kūrdate* (he plays); *cukūrde* (he has played). *gūrdate*; *godate*; *jugude* (he has played). 25. *ṣūda* means "to flow" (*kṣaraṇa*). *sūdate*; *suṣūde*. ---The roots *sek* (sic), *sṛp*, *sṛ*, *stṛ*, *sṛj*, *stṝ*, and *styai* have dental stops (*dantya*) as their final letters, and their initial *sa* (*sādi*) is not a palatal (*ca*).

The roots with a single vowel that have *ṣ* as their upadeśa (original form) are: *ṣvaṣk*, *svid*, *svada*, *svañj*, *svap*, and *smi*. (1) [In this context,] "dental" refers to a pure dental sound and not even a labio-dental, because the separate mention of *ṣvaṣk* and the others serves as an indicator (*jñāpaka*) of this rule. 26. *hrād* in the sense of indistinct sound: *hrādate*; *jahrāde*. 27. *hlādī* in the sense of pleasure; and by the word "and" (*ca*), also in the sense of indistinct sound: *hlādate*. 28. *svāda* in the sense of tasting: *svādate*. 29. *parda* in the sense of contemptible sound; that is, the sound of the bowels: *pardate*. 30. *yatī* in the sense of effort.

*yatate*, *yete*. 31. *yutṛ* and 32. *jutṛ* in the sense of shining: *yotate*, *yuyute*; *jotate*, *jujute*. 33. *vithṛ* and 34. *vethṛ* in the sense of begging: *vivithe*, *vivethe*. 35. *śrathi* in the sense of loosening: *śranthate*. 36. *grathi* in the sense of crookedness: *granthate*. 37. *kattha* in the sense of boasting: *katthate*. The roots beginning with *edh* ending in anudātta vowels have been completed. Now follow the thirty-eight [roots] ending in the dental class (*tavargīya*), which have a following *ru*-upadhā vowel. 38. *ata* in the sense of continuous motion: *atati*. By the rule *ata ādeḥ*: *āta*, *ātatuḥ*, *ātuḥ*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), when the form *āti-s-ī-t* is established...

SK 2266 *iṭa iṭi* (A 8.2.28): There is elision of the *s* following an *iṭ* augment when another *īṭ* follows. It should be stated that the elision of the *sic* is established (*siddha*) when there is a single-substitute (*ekādeśa*). *ātīt*, *ātiṣṭām*, *ātiṣu*.
SK 2267 *vadavrajahalantasyācaḥ* (A 7.2.3): [The substitution of *iṭ* occurs] after the vowel of roots containing *v*, *d*, *vraj*, or a consonant ending in a *hal*.

When [the rule] *vṛddhir ād-añ-ṇiti* (A 1.1.1) applies—[stating that] "there shall be vṛddhi in place of the vowel of a root ending in *hr-* or of a verbal base (*aṅga*) before the suffix *sic*, when followed by a parasmaipada personal ending"—this is obtained.

However, by *neṭi* (A 7.2.4), "when *sic* begins with *iṭ*, what was previously stated shall not take place. Thus: *mā bhavān atīt*, *atiṣṭām*, *atiṣuḥ*. 40. *citī* in the sense of perceiving: *cetati*; *ciceta*; *acetīt*; *aceṣṭām*; *aceṣuḥ*. 41. *cyuti* in the sense of sprinkling; sprinkling means making moist. [The prefix] *āṅ* is used in the sense of slightness and pervasiveness. It should be stated that the vowel *i* has the technical designation *it*. [Thus]: *cyotati*; *cucyota*.

SK 2269: *irito vā* (A 3.1.57). After a root ending in *ir*, the suffix *aṅ* may optionally be used for *cli* when followed by a *parasmaipada* ending. Examples: *acyutat* / *acyotīt*. 41. *ścyutir* in the sense of "flowing. *ścyotati*; *cuścyota*; *aścyutat* / *aścyotīt*. This root is also without the letter *y*: *ścotati*. 42. *mantha* in the sense of "churning" (*viloḍana*). Churning is a striking or agitation. *manthati*; *mamantha*. Because of the *kittva* [of the suffix] by the rule *yāsuṭaḥ kidāśiṣi*, there is the elision of the nasal [by the rule] *aniditām...* [in the benedictive]. Example: *mathyāt*.

43. *kuthi*, 44. *puthi*, 45. *luthi*, 46. *mathi*—in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*) and affliction (*saṃkleśana*). Because they are marked with the indicator *it*, there is no elision of the nasal (*na-lopa*). Thus: *kunthyāt*; *manthyāt*. 47. *ṣidha* in the sense of motion (*gati*). *sedhati*. *siṣedha*. *sedhitā*. *asedhīt*. When the prohibition [of *ṣatva*] by the rule *sāt padādyoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.111) would apply, [the following applies]: SK 2270: *upasargāt sunotisuvatisyatistautistobhatisthāsenayasedhasicasañjasvañjām* (A 8.3.65). After a prefix (*upasarga*), the *s* of these roots—*sunoti*, *suvati*, *syati*, *stauti*, *stobhati*, *sthā*, *senayati*, *sedhati*, *sica*, *sañja*, *svañja*—is replaced by *ṣ*. Thus, [the *s* in *asedhīt* becomes *ṣ*].
SK 2271: *sadir aprateḥ* (A 8.3.66). When preceded by a prefix other than *prati*, the *s* of the root *sad* becomes *ṣ*.
SK 2272: *stanbheḥ* (A 8.3.67). [The *s* of the root *stambh* becomes *ṣ* when preceded by a prefix.]

In the case of the root *stanbh* as taught in the Sūtras, the dental *s* should become the retroflex *ṣ*. The separation of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) is for the sake of what follows. Furthermore, the term *aprater* does not carry over [from the previous rule]. Example: *bāhupratiṣṭambhavivṛddhamanyuḥ* ("his anger increased by the bracing of his arms"). A 8.3.68: *avāccālambanāvidūryayoḥ*:
In the presence of the prefix *ava*, the change to *ṣ* occurs for the root *stanbh* when these two meanings are present: support (*ālambana*) and proximity (*avidūrya*).
SK 2274: And after *va*, the *s* of the root *svan* becomes *ṣ* when the object is food. SK 2275:
After *puri*, *ni*, and *vi*, the *s* of the roots *sev*, *sit*, *say*, *si*, *vus*, *saha*, *suṭ*, *stu*, and *svañj* becomes *ṣ*.
The *ṣ* of these [roots] following the prefixes *pari*, *ni*, and *vi* shall be *ṣ*.

(SK 2276) Regarding the rule *prāksitādaḍvyavāye ’pi* (A 8.3.63), which states that for those roots beginning with *sū* (such as *sū*, *sev*, *sit*, etc. that precede the word *sita*, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs even when there is an intervention by the augment *aṭ*: *nyaṣedhat*, *nyaṣedhīt*, *nyaṣedhiṣyat*.
SK 2277: *sthādiṣv abhyāsena cābhyāsasya* (A 8.3.64).

Before the suffix *sit*, even when there is an intervention by the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*), the substitution of *ṣ* shall occur for the root-initial *s* in the case of the roots beginning with *sthā*; however, this applies only to the reduplicated syllable of these [roots], and not to the roots beginning with *su*. Examples: *niṣiṣedha*, *niṣiṣidhatuḥ*. SK 2278:
*sedhater gatau* (A 8.3.113). [The substitution of *ṣ* does not occur] for the root *sidh* when it means "to go."

The substitution of *ṣ* for *s* in the root *sedh* meaning "to go" would not occur [in the following case]: *gaṅgānāṃ visedhati*. [The root] *ṣidhū* is used in the sense of "instruction" (*śāsana*) and "auspiciousness. Here, "instruction" means teaching. Pāṇini Sūtra 7.2.44: *svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūdito vā*.

An augment *iṭ* may optionally be added to a *valādi* (beginning with a consonant other than *y*) *ārdhadhātuka* suffix that follows roots beginning with *svarati*, *sūti*, *sūyati*, *dhūñ*, and those marked with the *ūdit* designation.

SK 2280 *jhaṣas tathor dho ’dhaḥ* (A 8.2.40): After a *jhaṣ* [consonant], the sounds *t* and *th* are replaced by *dh*, but not in the case of the root *dhā*. [The substitution of] *jaś* [occurs]. *siṣeddha*, *siṣedhitha*, *seddhā*, *sedhitā*, *setsyati*, *sedhiṣyati*, *asaitsīt*. SK 2281 *jhalo jhali* (A 8.2.26).

There is elision of *s* following a *jhal* [consonant] when a *jhal* [consonant] follows. *asaiddhām*, *asaitsuḥ*, *asaitsīḥ*, *asaiddham*, *asaiddha*, *asaitsam*, *asaitsva*, *asaitsma*. In the alternative [view], *asedhīt*, *asedhiṣṭām*, and so forth. 50. *khādṛ* in the sense of eating. The vowel *ṛ* is indicatory (*it*). *khādati*; *cakhāda*. 50. *khada* in the sense of steadiness and injury; by the word "and" (*ca*), also in the sense of eating. In the sense of steadiness, it is intransitive. *akhadait*. SK 2282: *ata upadhāyāḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.116).
There is *vṛddhi* substitution for the penultimate (*upadhā*) *a* when a suffix marked with *ñ* or *ṇ* follows. *cakhāda*.

SK 2283: *ṇaluttamo vā* (A 7.1.91). The final *ṇal* augment of the last [conjugational] suffix may optionally be treated as having the *ṇit* designation. Examples: *cakhāda* or *cakhada*. SK 2284: *ato halāder laghoḥ* (A 7.2.7). [The *guṇa* substitute is applied for the *iṭ* augment after a light vowel that is preceded by a consonant.]

In the case of a light *a* belonging to roots beginning with *ha*, there is optionally a *vṛddhi* substitute before the *sic* affix when it begins with *iṭ* and is followed by a *parasmaipada* ending. Thus: *akhādīt* or *akhadīt*. 51. *bada* [meaning] steadiness; it begins with a labial (*pa-vargīya*). *badati*; *babāda*; *bedatuḥ*; *beditha*; *babāda*; *babada*; *abādīt*; *abadīt*. 52. *gada* [meaning] distinct speech. *gadati*. SK 2285:
*ner gadanadapatapadaghumāsyatihantiyātivātidrātipsātivapativahatiśāmyaticinotidegdhiṣu ca* (Pāṇini A 8.4.17). [The augment *ṇiṅ* is applied after the prefix *ni-* before these verbs.]

The *ṇ* of the prefix *ni-* shall be substituted for *n* when it follows a cause (*nimitta*) situated in a preverb (*upasarga*), provided that the root begins with *gad-* and so forth. *praṇigadati* ("he speaks clearly"); *jagāda* ("he spoke"). 53. *rada* in the sense of "scratching" (*vilekhana*). Scratching means tearing apart. *rarāda* ("he scratched"); *redatuḥ* ("the two of them scratched"). 54. *ṇada* in the sense of indistinct sound. SK 2286: *ṇo naḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.65). [This rule prescribes the substitution of *na* for *ṇa* at the beginning of a verbal root.]

The initial *ṇ* of a verbal root shall become *n*. According to the *Bhāṣya*, those roots taught with an initial *ṇ* (*ṇopadeśa*) are: *anard*, *naṭ*, *nāthin*, *nādh*, *nand*, *nakk*, *nṝ*, and *nṛt*. Because of the exclusion of *nāṭ*—which is eligible for lengthening—it follows that *ghaṭ* and others are indeed taught with an initial *ṇ*. Some authorities, however, state that *nādh* (ending in a fourth letter of the *tavarga*), as well as *nṝ* and *nṛd*, are taught with an initial *ṇ*. [Pāṇini 8.4.14] states: "After a prefix, the *ṇ* of a root taught with an initial *ṇ* becomes *n*, even in a non-compound."*SK 2287* *upasargād asamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya* (A 8.4.14).

In a compound, as well as outside of a compound, the *ṇ* of a root that is taught with an initial *ṇ* (ṇopadeśa) shall be changed to *ṇ* when it follows a cause (*nimitta*) situated in a prefix (*upasarga*). Examples: *praṇadati*, *praṇinadati*. 55. The root *ard* means "to go" and "to beg. [The rule] *ata ādeḥ* [applies].

SK 2288: *tasmān nuḍ dvihalaḥ* (A 7.4.71). The augment *nuṭ* is applied after the vowel *a* which has been lengthened, provided that it follows a root consisting of two consonants (*dvihala*). Examples: *ānardata*, *ārdīt*. [Roots: 56. *narda* and 47. *garda* in the sense of "sound. Because these are not designated as having an initial *ṇ* (*ṇopadeśa*), the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* does not occur. Examples: *pra-nardati*, *gardati*, *jagarda*. 58. *tarda* in the sense of "injury. Example: *tardati*. 59. *karda* in the sense of "contemptible sound," specifically a guttural sound. Example: *kardati*. 60. *khada* in the sense of "biting" (*dandaśūka*). This means an action of biting or injuring characteristic of a venomous creature. Example: *khardati*, *cakharda*.

61–62. *ati* and *adi* in the sense of binding (*bandhane*): *antati*, *ānanta*; *andati*, *ānanda*. 63. *idi* in the sense of supreme sovereignty (*paramaiścarye*): *indati*, *indāṃcakāra*. 64. *bidi* in the sense of making a part (*avayave*). It begins with the third letter of the labial class (*pavargatṛtīyādi*). *bindati*; the meaning is "he makes a part. There is an alternative reading, *bhidī*. 65. *gaḍi* in the sense of a part of the face (*vadanaikadeśe*): *gaṇḍati*. Kāśyapa says that these five, beginning with the last one [of this group], do not have the scope of the *tiṅ* (verbal) suffixes; others, however, desire them even for *tiṅ*. 66. *ṇidi* in the sense of censure (*kutsāyām*): *nindati*, *praṇindati*. 67. *ṭunadi* in the sense of prosperity (*samṛddhau*).

SK 2289: *ādir ñiṭuḍavaḥ* (A 1.3.5). In the original instruction (*upadeśa*), these letters—*ñ*, *ṭ*, *ḍ*, and *v*—at the beginning of a verbal root (*dhātu*) are markers (*it*). [Examples: *nandati*. Because of the marker *id*, there is no elision of the *n*. [Optative: *nandyāt*. 68. *cad* in the sense of delighting: *cacanda*. 69. *trad* in the sense of movement: *tatranda*. 70. *kad*, 71. *krad*, 72. *klad* in the senses of calling out and weeping: *cakanda*, *cakranda*, *caklanda*. 73. *klid* in the sense of lamenting: *ciklinda*. 74. *śundh* in the sense of purification: *śuśundha*. [With the marker *ṇ*: elision of *n*. [Optative: *śudhyāt*.

Now, there are forty-two roots ending in consonants of the *ku*-class (*kavarga*) that have an anudātta accent on their final vowel. 75. *śīkṛ* (meaning "to sprinkle"); it begins with a palatal (*tālavya*). Some say it begins with a dental (*dantya*). Example: *śiśīke*. 76. *lokṛ* (meaning "to see"); example: *lokate*, *luloke*. 77. *ślokṛ* (meaning "to compose" or "to collect"). "Composition" (*saṃghāta*) refers to a literary work (*grantha*). Here, this refers either to the activity of that which is being composed or to the activity of the composer. In the first sense, it is intransitive; in the second, it is transitive. Example: *ślokate*. 78. *drekṛ*; 79. *dhrekṛ* (both meaning "to sound" and "to exert oneself"). "Exertion" (*utsāha*) means increase or arrogance. Example: *didreke*.

*didhreke* / 80 *rekṛ* in the sense of apprehension (*śaṅkā*): *rekate*. 81 *sekṛ*, 82 *srekṛ*, 83 *srakī*, 84 *śrakī*, 85 *ślakī* in the sense of motion (*gati*). Three [roots] begin with dentals; two begin with palatals. Because they are not taught with an initial *ṣ* (*aṣopadeśatvāt*), there is no substitution of *ṣ*.
