[Example: *siseke*. 86 *śakī* in the sense of apprehension: *śaṅkate*; [perfect: *śaśaṅke*. 87 *akī* in the sense of marking (*lakṣaṇa*): *aṅkate*; [perfect: *ānaṅke*. 88 *vakī* in the sense of crookedness (*kauṭilya*): *vaṅkate*. 89 *makī* in the sense of adorning (*maṇḍana*): *maṅkate*. 90 *kakī* in the sense of fickleness (*laulya*). Fickleness includes pride (*garva*) and childishness (*āpatya*). [Example: *kakate*.

*ca*k (91), *ku*k (92), and *vṛ*k (93) mean "to take. *kokate*, *cukuke*, *varkate*, *vavṛke*. By a prior counter-exception (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*) to the rule for *guṇa*, roots with a short *ṛ* as their penultimate vowel (*ṛdupadha*) cause the *liṭ* suffix to be treated as having the *kit* designation. *ca*k (94) means "to be satisfied" and "to strike back. *cakate*, *ceke*. *kak* (95), *vak* (96), *śvak* (97), *trak* (98), *ḍaukṛ* (99), *traukṛ* (100), *ṣvaṣk* (101), *vaṣk* (102), *maṣk* (103), *ṭikṛ* (104), *ṭīkṛ* (105), *tikṛ* (106), *tīkṛ* (107), *raghi* (108), and *laghi* (109) have the meaning "to go. *kaṅkate*, *ḍuḍhauke*.

*Tutruke*: A prohibition of *satva* (the substitution of *s*) must be stated for roots ending in *ṣ*, *dhātu*, *ṣṭhivu*, *ṣvaṣka*, and *tṛ*. [Examples: *ṣvaṣkate*, *ṣavaṣke*. Regarding this, some say that the third [consonant] begins with a dental (*d*). *Laghi* also means "cessation from eating. 109 *adhi*, 110 *vadhi*, 111 *maghi*: [meaning] "to urge" (*ākṣepa*) in motion; *ākṣepa* here means "reproach. Others say it means "in motion" and "at the commencement of motion. [Examples: *aṅghate*, *ānaṅghe*; *vaṅghate*; *maṅghate*. *Maghi* also means "gambling" (*kaitava*). 112 *rāghṛ*, 113 *lāghṛ*, 114 *drāghṛ*: [meaning] "capability" (*sāmarthya*). [Example: *rāghate*.
*lāghate*; some also say *dhrāghṛ*. *drāghṛ* [is used] in the sense of extension (*āyāma*); extension means length. *drāghate*. 115. *ślāghṛ* in the sense of boasting (*katthana*); *ślāghate*.

Now follow fifty roots ending in *parasmaipada*. 116. *phakka* (to go low). "Going low" means moving slowly or improper conduct. *phakkati*; *paphakka*. 117. *taka* (to laugh). *takati*. 118. *taki* (to live with difficulty). *taṅkati*. 119. *bukka* (to bark). Barking is the sound of a dog. *bukkati*. 120. *kakha* (to laugh). *pra-ni-kakhati*. 121. *okhṛ*, 122. *rākhṛ*, 123. *lākhṛ*, 124. *drākhṛ*, 125. *dhrākhṛ* (in the senses of drying up and being able).

*lokhati*; *lokhāṃcakāra*. 126. *śākhṛ*, 127. *ślākhṛ*: in the sense of pervading (*vyāpti*). *śākhati*. 128. *ukha*, 129. *ukhi*, 130. *vakha*, 131. *vakhi*, 132. *makha*, 133. *makhi*, 134. *ṇakha*, 135. *ṇakhi*, 136. *rakha*, 137. *rakhi*, 138. *lakha*, 139. *lakhi*, 140. *ikha*, 141. *ikhi*, 142. *īkhi*, 143. *valgā*, 144. *ragi*, 145. *lagi*, 146. *agi*, 147. *vagi*, 148. *magi*, 149. *tagi*, 150. *tvagi*, 151. *śragi*, 152. *ślāgi*, 153. *igi*, 154. *rigi*, 155. *ligi*: these have the meaning of motion (*gati*).

There are fifteen [mantras] ending in the accusative case and thirteen ending in the instrumental case. Here, regarding those ending in *khā*, some also recite four others: *rikha*, *trakha*, *trikhi*, and *śikhi*.

SK 2290: *abhyāsasyāsavarṇe* (A 6.4.78). In the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*), when followed by a vowel (*ac*) that is not homogeneous (*asavarṇa*), the vowels *i* and *u* undergo the substitutions *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ*. [Examples: *uvokha*; *ūkhatur*; *ūkhuḥ*. By the *sannipāta-paribhāṣā*, the suffix *am* [of the third person plural] does not apply after a root beginning with *ij* (i.e., *ūkh*). Here, because the long vowel resulting from *savarṇa-dīrgha* is included within the term "reduplicated syllable" (*abhyāsagrahaṇa*), the shortening [prescribed by A 7.4.59] does not apply. This is because the rule has already applied once; for, due to its status as an *aṅga* operation, it proceeds like a rain-cloud (*parjanya-vat*), and once the shortening is effected, the lengthening follows. This is according to the maxim *vārṇād āṅgaṃ balīyaḥ* ("an *aṅga* operation is stronger than a phonetic one") and because it is subsequent in the order of rules.

*uṅkhati*, *vavakhatu*, *vaṅkhati*, *mekhatuḥ*; *tvagi* and *kampane* [mean] "to tremble. 156. *yugi*, 157. *jugi*, 158. *bugi* [mean] "to avoid"; *yuṅgati*. 159. *ghagha* [means] "to laugh"; *ghaghati*; [the perfect form is] *jaghāgha*. 160. *maghi* [means] "to adorn"; *maṅghati*. 161. *śighi* [means] "to smell"; *śiṅghati*.

Now follow those ending in the *ca*-class (*cavargīya*). Among them, twenty-one are *anudātta* (unaccented) roots. 162. *varc* (in the sense of shining): *varcate*. 163. *ṣac* (in the sense of sprinkling and serving): *sacate*, *sece*, *sacitā*. 164. *locṛ* (in the sense of seeing): *locate*, *luloce*. 165. *śac* (in the sense of distinct speech): *śece*. 166. *śvaca* and 167. *śvaci* (in the sense of moving): *śvacate*, *śvañcate*. 168. *kac* (in the sense of binding): *kacate*. 169. *kaci* and 170. *kāci* (in the sense of shining and binding): *cakañce*, *cakāñce*.

171. *maca* and 172. *muci* in the sense of *kalkana*. *Kalkana* means deceit (*dambha*) and guile (*śāṭhya*); others say it means "speaking" (*kathana*). [Roots] *mece* and *mumuñce*. 173. *muci* in the senses of holding, rising, and honoring. *mamance*. 174. *eci* in the sense of making manifest. *pañcate*. 175. *ṣṭuca* in the sense of satisfaction. *stocate*; *tuṣṭuce*. 176. *ṛja* in the senses of going, standing, acquiring, and gaining. *arjate*. In the rule for the insertion of *nuṭ*, the letter *ṛ*—which is a portion of the vowel *ṛ*—is taken as a consonant (*hal*). Therefore, because it has two consonants (*dvihaltva*), *nuṭ* is inserted: *ānṛje*.

177. *ṛji* and 178. *bhṛjī* in the sense of parching. *ṛñjate*. By the rule "after a prefix, [the vowel] becomes *ṛ*" (*upasargād ṛte*), there is *vṛddhi*: *prārñjate*. *ṛñjāñcakre*. *ārñjiṣṭa*. *bharjate*. *babhṛjje*. *abharjiṣṭa*. 179. *rjṛ*, 180. *bhrejṛ*, 181. *bhrājṛ* in the sense of shining. *ejāñcakre*. 182. *īja* in the sense of going and censuring. *ījāñcakre*.

Now, the roots ending in *ś* that take the *parasmaipada* endings: 183. *śuc* (to grieve): *śocati*. 184. *kuc* (to sound loudly): *kocati*. 185. *kuñc* and 186. *kruñc* (in the senses of crookedness and becoming small). By the rule *aniditām...* [Pāṇini 6.4.24], there is elision of the nasal (*n*). [The optative forms are] *kucyāt*, *krucyāt*. 187. *luñc* (to remove): *lucyāt*. 188. *añc* (in the senses of motion and honoring). [The optative forms are] *acyāt*; however, in the sense of motion, there is elision of the nasal, [yielding] *acyāt*; but in the sense of honoring, [the form is] *añcyāt*.

189 *vañcu*, 190 *cañcu*, 191 *tañcu*, 192 *tvañcu*, 193 *mruñcu*, 194 *muñcu*, 195 *bhrucu*, 196 *mucu*—these have the sense of "going. [The forms] *vacyāt*, *cacyāt*, *tacyāt*, *tvacyāt* [are derived from these]. [The aorist forms] *amruścīt*, *amluñcīt* [are formed]. According to Pāṇini A 3.1.58: *jṛ-stambhu-mrucu-grucu-glucu-gluñcu-śvibhyaś ca*.

After these roots, the suffix *aṅ* may optionally occur. *amrucat* / *amrocīt*; *amlucat* / *amlocīt*. 197. *grucu*, 198. *glucu*, 199. *kuju*, 200. *khuju*: in the sense of committing theft. *jugroca*; *agrucat* / *agrocīt*; *jugloca*; *aglucat* / *aglocīt*; *akujīt*; *akhojīt*. 201. *gluñcu*, 202. *ṣasja*: in the sense of going. With *aṅ*: *aglucat*; *agluñcīt*. Due to the rule of *ścutva*, the *s* becomes *ś*; due to the rule of *jaśtva*, it becomes *j*. *sajjati*. This root is also used in the Ātmanepada.

203. *sajjate* (and *kuji*, *guji*) mean "in an indistinct sound"; [thus] *guñjati*, *guñjyāt*. 204. *arca* means "in worship"; [thus] *ānarca*. 205. *mleccha* means "in an indistinct sound"; the meaning is "in an unclear or incorrect word. [Thus] *mlecchati*, *mimleccha*. 206. *laccha*, 207. *lācchi* mean "in marking" (*lakṣaṇe*). [Thus] *lalaccha*, *lalāccha*. 208. *vācchi* means "in desiring" (*icchāyām*). [Thus] *vāñchati*. 209. *ācchi* means "in stretching" (*āyāme*). [Thus] *āñchati*.

Therefore, in the rule *ata ādiḥ*, the addition of the marker *t* (in *at*) is for the purpose of including the natural short vowel (*hrasva*). Consequently, because there is no long vowel [in the root], *ānāñcha* does not occur. 210. *hrīccha* in the sense of shame: *jihrīccha*. 211. *hurcchā* in the sense of crookedness (*kauṭilya*). Maireya states that "crookedness" means "stepping aside. By the rule *upadhāyāṃ ca*, the vowel is lengthened: *hūrcchati*. 212. *murchā* in the sense of fainting (*moha*) and rising up (*samucchrāya*): *mūrcchati*. 213. *sphurcchā* in the sense of expansion (*vistṛti*): *sphūrchati*. 214. *yuccha* in the sense of negligence (*pramāda*): *yucchati*.

215. *ucchi* (to glean). *Uñcha* means taking [grain] grain by grain; Yādava says it is the gathering of ears of corn (*kaṇiśa*) and so forth, which is called *śila*. [Examples: *uñchati*; *uñchāṃcakāra*. 216. *ucchī* (to finish). *Vivāsa* means completion. This root is generally preceded by the prefix *vi-* (*vyucchati*). 217. *dhraja*, 218. *dhraji*, 219. *dhṛja*, 220. *dhṛji*, 221. *dhvaja*, 222. *dhvaji* (to move). [Examples: *dhrajati*, *dhrañjati*, *dharjati*, *dhṛñjati*, *dhvajati*, *dhvañjati*. 223. *kūja* (to make an indistinct sound). [Example: *cukūja*.

224. *arja* (225) *ṣarja*, in the sense of acquisition (*arjane*). [Examples: *arjati*; *ānarja*. *sarjati*; *sasarja*. 226. *garja*, in the sense of sound (*śabde*). When *caṅ* follows, the first monosyllabic (*ekāc*) portion of a verbal root that is not part of a reduplicated stem is reduplicated; however, if it begins with a vowel (*aj-ādi*), the second syllable is reduplicated.
Furthermore, when *caṅ* follows and is preceded by a light vowel (*laghu*), the penultimate vowel is treated as if it were followed by *san*, provided there is no elision of *an*. (Pāṇini 7.4.93)

*caṅpare* is a *bahuvrīhi* compound. Both [the terms] *sa* and *aṅgasya* recur. That is to say: when a *ṇi*-affix follows immediately after that which causes the designation of *aṅga* (*aṅgasaṃjñānimitta*) and is followed by *caṅ*, then for the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) of the *aṅga* that follows that light [vowel], the same operation as in the case of *san* should take place, provided there is no elision (*aglopa*) of the *ṇi*. Alternatively, *aṅgasya* does not recur; rather, it means: when a *ṇi*-affix followed by *caṅ* is present, for the reduplication of that *aṅga* which has a light vowel following it, and so forth, as before. *Sanyataḥ* (A 7.4.79): In the presence of *san*, the vowel *a* of the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) should be replaced by *i*.

SK 2318: *dīrgho laghoḥ* (A 7.4.94). In the scope of the *sanvadbhāva* operation, there should be lengthening of a light (*laghu*) reduplicated syllable. Examples: *acīkamata*. In the alternative view where the *ṇiṅ* suffix is absent, it should be stated that *caṅ* follows the root *kamu* after the *cli* suffix. Because the *ṇi* suffix is absent, there is neither lengthening nor *sanvadbhāva*: *acakamata*. Mādhava holds that because the technical designation (*saṃjñā*) applies at the time the operation occurs (*kāryakālatva*), the lengthening and *sanvadbhāva* apply only where the entire stem (*aṅga*) is reduplicated, and not in cases involving multiple syllables (*anekākṣu*). In roots such as *cakāsti*, *arthāpayati*, and *ūrṇoti*, it is not the entire stem that is reduplicated, but rather a portion of it.

Someone [says]: "Therefore, this twofold [application] applies to a single syllable (*ekākṣu*) [only]. In reality, that which is the repetition (*abhyāsa*) of a verbal base (*aṅga*) is [meant] from the perspective of the phoneme (*varṇa*). We consider that in the case of *ūrṇau* (the root *ūrṇu*), when it is applied to the meaning of 'covering' (*arthāpayati*), there is a long vowel, and thus the twofold [application] occurs. "But in the case of *cakās-* (the root *cakās*), both of these would not apply; yet they would apply by way of a specific restriction (*vyavasthayā*). For Kaiyaṭa himself has described the alternative interpretations [as follows]: either the element to be qualified by the suffix *ṇi* is what is proximate, or it is the verbal base (*aṅga*) itself, because of the rule *laghūni* (Pāṇini 7.4.91). Thus, even when there is elision of *ṇi* (*aglope*), the connection [to the rule for lengthening] remains for the sake of establishing forms such as *tvagitām*. (Verse 5)

Therefore, for the general sense of action, one has forms such as *vanati*, etc.; *pravanayati*. However, it will be stated that for the unprefixed form, there is an option regarding its being a *mit* root. 804. *jval* in the sense of "to blaze. This root, which is to be recited for the sake of the *ṇic* suffix, is restated here for the sake of its being a *mit* root: *prajvalayati*. 805. *hval*; 806. *hmla* in the sense of "to move. *prahvalayati*; *prahmalayati*.

807. *smṛ* in the sense of *ādhyāna* (longing remembrance). This is a restatement for the sake of the *mit* designation (*mittva*) of the root that will be taught in the sense of *cintā* (thinking); *ādhyāna* is remembrance preceded by longing. 808. *dṝ* in the sense of fear. This is a restatement for the sake of the *mit* designation of the root *dṝ* "to tear" belonging to the *krādi* class; *darayati* means "he causes one who is tearing to move [out of fear]. In a sense other than fear, it is *dārayati*. According to the view that this is indeed a different root, we have forms such as *darati*, etc.

Some read *dṛ* as a short vowel in place of the long one in the rule *at smṛdṛtvarasrambha...* regarding words such as *ghaṭa*; Mādhava says that this is not correct. 809. *nṛ* "to lead": this is a restatement of the root which will be read later among the roots beginning with *trai*. Other than in the sense of leading, it forms *nārayati*. 810. *śrā* "in cooking": this is a general representation of both *śrai*, which has undergone *ātva* (the change to *ā*), and *śrā*, which belongs to the first class (*bhvādi*). Between a root with a *luk*-suffix and one with a non-*luk* suffix, the non-*luk* suffix is preferred. Between a term defined by a general rule and one stated by its specific form, only the specifically stated one is taken.

Thus, by these two technical rules (*paribhāṣā*), [the causative] *śrapayati* means "he causes to cook" or "he causes to soften. In contexts other than cooking, *śrāpayati* means "he causes to sweat. Regarding the rule *māraṇatoṣaṇaniśāmaneṣu jñā*: Mādhava states that *niśāmana* is visual perception (*cākṣuṣajñāna*). Others say it means mere making known (*jñāpanamātra*). There is an alternative reading, *niśāneṣu*, where *niśāna* means sharpening. In these very senses, the root *jñā* takes the suffix *mit*. In the *curādigaṇa*, there is the root *jñap* with the suffix *mic*; its meaning is making known and killing, etc.

"How does the causative suffix *ṇic* achieve its result when applied to the roots meaning 'to inform' (*vijñā*)? To this, the Teacher says: "Listen. According to the opinion of Māghava, there is no *mit*-designation for the non-visual cognition [of the root *jñā*]. However, according to the view that *mit*-designation applies to the mere act of making known, it is the root *jñā* belonging to the *curādigaṇa* (the tenth class), because verbal roots have multiple meanings. Furthermore, according to Haradatta and others who read the root as *niśā* (in the sense of sharpening), there is no impossibility regarding the form *kāṣya*. The root *cali* means 'to shake'; *cala* in the sense of shaking belongs to the *jvalādi* group. [Example: *calayati śākhām* ('he shakes the branch')."

But in a sense other than "shaking," *cālayati* means "he makes otherwise" (i.e., he alters); Master [Pāṇini] says it means "he takes away. It also means "he moves a Sūtra"; that is, "he casts it aside. *Chadi* is used in the sense of "afflicting" (*ūrjan*). And for the root *chad* meaning "concealing" belonging to the *curādika* group, this restatement is for the sake of its being a *mittva* root when the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is absent in its own sense. Because roots have multiple meanings, it functions here in the sense of "afflicting. One employs that which ends in *chad* as *chadayati*; the meaning is "one causes another to conceal."

But when the causative suffix *ṇic* is applied in its own sense (*svārthe*), it means "he covers," "he becomes powerful," "he becomes vital," or "he wards off. Regarding *laḍi* in the sense of "tongue-torment" (*jihvonmathane*): this is a restatement for the sake of [establishing] the *mittva* (causing the *ṇic* to have the *mit* designation) of the root *laḍ*, which is listed as meaning "to sport" (*vilāsa*). "Torment" (*unmathana*) here means making known (*jñāpana*). The compound *jihvā-unmathanam* is a genitive *tatpuruṣa*: "the torment of the tongue. Thus, *laḍayati jihvām*. Alternatively, it is a third-case *tatpuruṣa*: "he torments by means of the tongue," i.e., *laḍayati jihvayā*. Others, however, hold that by the word "tongue" (*jihvā*), its activity is indicated; this is a collective *dvandva* compound.

*laḍayati śatrum* (he deceives the enemy); *laḍayati dadhi* (he stirs the curd). In other cases, *lāḍayati putram* (he fondles the son). 815. *madī* [is used] in the senses of "rejoicing" (*harṣa*) and "depressing" (*glepana*). *Glepana* means "wretchedness" (*dainya*). This is a restatement for the purpose of indicating that this root belongs to the *divādigaṇa* and is marked with the *mit* designation. *Madayati* means "he causes to rejoice" or "he causes to be depressed. In other cases, *mādayati* means "he produces a transformation of the mind. 813. *dhvana* [is used] in the sense of "sound. This is restated for the purpose of indicating that it is marked with the *mit* designation. *Dhvanayati ghaṇṭām* (he makes the bell sound). In other cases, *dhvānayati*.

The meaning is that one utters [the word] with indistinct syllables. On this point, Bhoja recited: *dali*, *vali*, *skhali*, *raṇi*, *dhvani*, *trap*, and *kṣapa*. Among these, *dhvani* and *raṇi* have been illustrated. *Dala* (in the sense of splitting), *vala* (in the sense of covering), *skhala* (in the sense of moving), and *trapūṣ* (in the sense of shame)—these are included. In their case, with the causative suffix (*ṇau*), we have: *dalayati*, *valayati*, *skhalayati*, and *trapayati*. Regarding *kṣai* (in the sense of wasting away), which will be mentioned later, there is a reference to it after it has undergone *ātvam* and been provided with the augment *puk*; thus, *kṣapayati*.

*svana* [is used] in the sense of "adorned" (*avataṃsane*) and "sound" (*śabde*); this is a restatement of what will be recited [later]. *Svanayati*; elsewhere, *svānayati*. *Ghaṭādayo mitaḥ*: the meaning is that they have the designation *mit*. *janījṝṣknasurañjo 'mantāś ca*: the term *mit* is understood to carry over. Because of the indication of the *ṣit* quality in *jṝṣ*, there is the inclusion of the root *jṝ* (to grow old). However, for *jṛṇāti*, it is *jārayati*. Some, however, having read *janī jṝ ṣṇasu*, cite the *ṣṇasu* belonging to the *divādigaṇa* in the sense of "casting away" (*nirasane*).

Regarding the rule *jvala-hvala-hmala-nama-ām anupasargād vā*: for these roots, the designation *mit* is optional. This is an option that applies where [the *mit* designation] would otherwise be mandatory. Thus: *jvalayati* or *jvālayati*. However, when a prefix (*upasarga*) is present, the *mit* designation is obligatory: *prajvalayati*. [Question: How then is it that one says *prajvālayati*? [Answer: It is derived from the root *nam* with the suffix *ghañ*, and then the causative suffix *ṇic* is applied in the sense of "he causes that to happen" (*tat karoti*). [Question: How then is it that one says *saṃkrāmayati*? [Answer: The author of the *Vṛtti* explains that this is due to the application of a restricted option (*vyavasthita-vibhāṣā*), by carrying over the word "optionally" (*vā*) from the rule *mitāṃ hrasvaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.92), which itself carries over the word "optionally" (*vā*) from the preceding rule *vā cittavirāge* (Pāṇini 6.4.91). Thus, the shortening does not necessarily occur here.

By this [rule], the following is explained: *rajo viśrāmayan rājñāṃ dhuryān viśrāmayeti saḥ*, etc. Regarding the roots *glāsnu* and those ending in *-vam*: there is an option (*vibhāṣā*) for these to have the *mit* designation when they are not preceded by a prefix (*anupasarga*). For the first two, the *mit* designation was not previously established; for the other two, it was already established. Thus, the rule provides an option. The roots *kam*, *am*, and *cam* do not [have the *mit* designation]. Since they end in *-am*, the *mit* designation would have applied by default, but it does not apply here. Examples: *kāmayate*, *āmayati*, *cāmayati*. Regarding the root *śam* in the sense of "seeing" (*darśane*): the root *śam* (as *śāmyati*) shall not have the *mit* designation in the sense of seeing. Example: *niśāmayati rūpam* ("he observes the form").

But elsewhere, in the case of *praṇayin*, the wife listens to the stories; here, the root *ni-śam* belongs to the *cur*-class (caurādika). Because verbal roots have multiple meanings, its function here is "hearing," just as in the case of *śāmyati*. Regarding *yamo 'pariveṣaṇe*: the root *yacchati* shall not take the suffix *min* when it does not mean "serving food. Thus, *āyāmayati* means "he lengthens" or "he occupies with activity. However, in the sense of serving food, one says *yamayati brāhmaṇān*, meaning "he feeds the Brahmins."

Regarding the phrase "paryavasitaṃ niyamayan" and so forth, it should be understood that due to the word *niyama*, the suffix *ṇic* is applied in the sense of "he performs that" (*tat karoti*). [The rule] *skhadiravaparibhyāṃ ca* [is explained as follows]: it is indeed *min* (the *m* is an *it*), not otherwise. Thus: *avaskhādayati*, *pariskhādayati*. The author of the *Nyāsa* says [the rule applies] after *apa*, *ava*, and *pari*. However, Svāmī, not repeating the negative particle *na* from the following three sūtras, [interprets] *śama adarśane* [as meaning] he cuts off [the *m-it* quality]. But Yama states that there is the status of being *mit* (causing the shortening of the penultimate vowel) except in the sense of serving food (*apariveṣaṇe*).

In his view, the restriction [of the rule] beginning with "niyamayan" and so forth is indeed correct. Because of the restriction that "for a root preceded by *ava* and others, [the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs] if it is in its own domain (*svadeśe*)," he says "praskhādayati. Therefore, in the two sūtras, a reversal of the examples and counter-examples results. Furthermore, this opinion is to be disregarded because it contradicts the Vṛtti, the Nyāsa, and other authorities. [Root] 821: *phaṇa* (to move). The word "not" (*na*) has ceased [to apply] because it is impossible [in this context]. This [root] was not recited prior to the prohibition [of the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*], in accordance with the grammatical operations (*kārya*) beginning with *phaṇ*.
[Sūtra A 6.4.125: "And [the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs] after the seven roots beginning with *phaṇ*. (SK 2354).

For these [roots], there is optionally the elision of the penultimate vowel (*abhyāsa-lopa*) before a *kit* suffix in the perfect tense (*liṭ*), as well as before a *seṭ* suffix in the *thal* ending. Thus: *pheṇatuḥ*, *pheṇuḥ*, *pheṇitha*; or *paphaṇatuḥ*, *paphaṇuḥ*. From the causative stem: *phaṇayati*. The *vṛt* group, beginning with *ghaṭ*, is completed. According to some, the *vṛt* designation applies only prior to *phaṇ*; in their view, only *phaṇayati* is formed. 822. *rājṛ* (to shine). This root is marked with the *svarita* accent. *rājati*, *rājate*. *rejatuḥ*, *rarājatuḥ*; *reje*, *rarāje*. Although the word *ataḥ* ("from *at*") is understood [in the rule], by virtue of the specific formulation, the change of *āt* to *et* occurs here.

823. *ṭubhrājṛ*, 824. *ṭubhrāśṛ*, 825. *ṭubhlāśṛ*—these roots mean "to shine. They are *anudāttet* (unaccented on the root syllable). The inclusion of *bhrāj* here is for the sake of the grammatical operations pertaining to the *phaṇādi* group; however, its placement earlier [in the *phaṇādi* list] was for the purpose of preventing the substitution of *ṣ* in the *vraścādi* group. For in that context, due to association with *rāj*, only those belonging to the *phaṇādi* group are understood. *bhreje*, *babhrāje*. By the rule *vā bhrāśa-* etc., the suffix *śyan* is optionally applied: *bhrāśyate*, *bhrāśate*; *bhreśe*, *babhrāśe*. [Similarly: *bhlāśyate*, *bhlāśate*; *śleśe*, *babhlāśe*. Both of these [roots, *bhrāś* and *bhlāś*] belong to the *phaṇādi* group.

The two ending in the palatal (*tālavya*) [consonants] are: 826 *syamu*, 827 *svana*, 828 *dhvana*—meaning "to sound. From *syam* up to the end of *kṣar*, these roots are *parasmaipada*. [Examples: *syematuḥ*; *sasyamatuḥ*; *asyamīt*. *svenatuḥ*; *sasvanatuḥ*; *asvānīt*; *asvanīt*. *viṣvaṇati*; *avaṣvaṇati*—the meaning is "he eats with noise. The substitution of *ṣ* occurs by the rule *veś ca svanaḥ*. The roots beginning with *phaṇ* have been dealt with. *dadhvanatuḥ*. 829 *ṣama*, 830 *ṣṭama*—meaning "not to be deficient" (*avaikalye*). *sasāma*; *tastāma*.

831 *jvala* in the sense of blazing; hence, with the suffix *lrānta*, *ajvālīt*. 832 *cala* in the sense of shaking. 833 *jala* in the sense of sharpening (*dhātana*); *dhātana* means keenness. 834 *ṭala*; 835 *dvala* in the sense of unsteadiness. 836 *ṣṭhala* in the sense of standing. 837 *hala* in the sense of plowing or scratching. 838 *ṇala* in the sense of odor; some say in the sense of binding. 839 *pala* in the sense of going; *palati*. 840 *bala* in the sense of breathing and enclosing grain; *balati*; *belatuḥ*; *beluḥ*. 841 *pula* in the sense of greatness; *polati*.

842. The root *kula* is used in the sense of gathering (*saṃstyāna*) and among kinsmen (*bandhu*). *Saṃstyāna* means a collection. By the word *bandhu*, its activity is understood. [Examples: *kolati*, *cukola*. 843. *śala*, 844. *hula*, 845. *patḷ*—these roots mean "to go. [Examples: *śaśāla*, *juhola*, *papāta*, *petatuḥ*, *patitā*. SK 2355: After the root *pat*, the augment *pum* [is inserted before the suffix *ktvā*]. (A 7.4.19)

When *aṅ* follows: *apaptat*. By the rule *ner gad-* [Pāṇini 8.4.17], there is *ṇatva*: *praṇyapaptat*. 846. *kvath* in the sense of boiling (*niṣpāka*). *kvathati*; *cakvātha*; *akvathīt*. 847. *path* in the sense of going. *apathīt*. 848. *math* in the sense of churning (*viloḍana*). *methatuḥ*; *amathīt*. 849. *ṭuvam* in the sense of vomiting (*udgiraṇa*). According to Sudhākara, the substitution of *ṛ* by *i* occurs here due to a specific grammatical exception (*nipātana*). *vavāma*; *vavamatuḥ*. Because it belongs to the *vadi* group, the substitution of *e* for *a* and the elision of the reduplication do not occur. 850. *bhram* in the sense of moving (*calana*). By the rule *vā bhrāśa-* [Pāṇini 3.1.70], the suffix *śyan* is optionally applied. *bhramyati*; *bhramati*. However, the form *bhrāmyati* will be explained as belonging to the *divādi* class.

SK 2356: *vā jṝbhramutrasām* (A 6.4.124). For these roots (*jṝ*, *bhram*, *tras*), there is optionally the substitution of *e* for the root vowel and the elision of the reduplication when followed by a *kit* suffix, as well as in the case of the *seṭ* suffix *thali*. Examples: *bhrematuḥ* or *babhramatuḥ*; *abhramīt*. 851. *kṣara* in the sense of "moving. Example: *akṣārīt*. Now, two roots are *anudātta* (unaccented): 852. *ṣaha* in the sense of "endurance. By the rule *parinivibhyaḥ...* (A 8.3.70), there is the substitution of *ṣ* for the initial *s*. Examples: *pariṣahate*, *sehe*, *sahitā*. By the rule *tīṣasaha...* (A 7.2.48), there is optionally the augment *iṭ*. In the absence of *iṭ*, there is the substitution of *ḍha* for *sa*, then *dha* for *ḍha*, then *ṣṭu* for *ṣṭa*, and finally the elision of *ḍha*.
SK 2357: *sahivahor od-avarṇasya* (A 6.3.112):
When there is elision of the letter *ḍh*, the vowel *o* shall replace the *o*-vowel of these two roots (*sah* and *vah*).

In *soḍhrūpa* (the form of the root *sah*), the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* shall not occur. *parisoḍhā*. According to A 8.3.71, *sivādīnāṃ vāḍvyavāye ’pi*, the *s* of roots beginning with *siv* that follow *pari*, *ni*, or *vi* may optionally become *ṣ*, even when there is an intervention by *aṭ*. Thus: *paryasahata* or *paryaṣahata*. 853. *ram* in the sense of sporting: *reme*, *remiṣe*, *rantā*, *raṃsyate*, *raṃsīṣṭa*, *araṃsta*.
Now follow the roots ending in *ka*, which take the *parasmaipada* endings: 854. *ṣadl* (to perish, to go, to sink down).

**SK 2360:** *piba-jighra-dhama-tiṣṭha-mana-ya-chapaśya-rccha-dhau-śīya-sīdāḥ* (A 7.3.78). The substitutes beginning with *piba* shall take the place of the roots beginning with *pā* when followed by an affix beginning with a *s* that has the marker *it*. *sīdati* (he sits); *sasāda* (he sat); *sedatuḥ* (they two sat); *seditha* (you sat); *sasattha* (you [Vedic] sat); *sattā* (future participle); *satsyati* (he will sit). Because it is marked with *ḷ*, the suffix is *aṅ*: *asadat* (he sat). *sadir aprateḥ* (A 8.3.66): The substitution applies to the root *sad* when not preceded by the prefix *pra*. *niṣīdati* (he sits down); *nyaṣīdat* (he sat down). **SK 2361:** *sadeḥ parasya liṭi* (A 8.3.118). [The substitution of *sa* for *sa* occurs] after the root *sad* when followed by the *liṭ* affix.

Due to the practice of *sader*, there shall not be the substitution of *ṣ* for the following [consonant] in the *liṭ* [perfect tense]. Examples: *niṣasāda*, *niṣedatuḥ*. 855. *śadḷ* [is used] in the sense of falling away (*śātana*). This [root] refers to the state of being shattered (*viśīrṇatā*); however, "falling away" (*śātana*) is mentioned as its scope of application.

SK 2362 *śadeḥ śitaḥ* (A 1.3.60): The ātmanepada suffixes shall occur after this root when followed by a *śit* affix. *śīyate*; *śaśāda*; *śedatuḥ*; *śeditha*; *śaśattha*; *śattā*; *aśadat*. 856 *kruśa* in the sense of calling out and weeping: *krośati*; *kroṣṭā*. [In the case of the *liṭ* suffix: *cleḥ ksaḥ* [Pāṇini 3.1.45]; *akrukṣat*. 857 *kuc* in the sense of rubbing together, crookedness, obstruction, and scratching: *kocati*; *cukoca*. 858 *budha* in the sense of understanding: *bodhati*; *bodhitā*; *bodhiṣyati*. 859 *ruha* in the sense of the germination of seeds and manifestation: *rohati*.
*ruroha*, *rurohitha*, *roḍhā*, *rokṣyati*, *aruksat*. 860 *kasa* (to go): *akāsīt*, *akasīt*. 7. *vṛt*: The *kvādi*-group is completed.

Now, those ending in *ghu* have a circumflex (*kharita*) accent on their final vowel. 861. *hikka* (to make an indistinct sound): *hikkati*, *hikkate*. 862. *añcu* (to go and to beg): *añcati*, *añcate*. Some say the root is *acu*; others say it is *aci*. 863. *ṭuyācṛ* (to beg): *yācati*, *yācate*. 864. *reṭṭa* (to revile): *reṭati*, *reṭate*. 865. *cata* and 866. *cade* (to beg): [Present: *cacāta*, *cete*; [Aorist: *acatīt*, *acedīt*. 867. *prothṛ* (to be sufficient): [Perfect: *puprotha*.

*puprotha* / 868 *midṛ*, 869 *medṛ*: in the senses of "to be fat" and "to injure. *mimeda*, *mimide*, *mimede*. These two [roots] end in *th*, according to Svāmī; *mimetha*. According to Nyāsa, they end in *dh*. 870 *medhṛ*: also in the sense of "to join. *medhati*, *mimedha*. 871 *ṇidṛ*, 872 *ṇedṛ*: in the senses of "censure" and "proximity. *nineda*, *ninidatuḥ*, *ninida*; *ninede*. 873 *śṛdhu*, 874 *mṛdhu*: in the sense of "moistening"; moistening means wetting. *śardhati*, *śardhate*; *śardhitā*. *mardhati*.

*mardhate* / 875 *budh* in the sense of awakening: *bodhati*, *bodhate*. Because it belongs to the *harita* group, the suffix *aṅ* optionally applies: *abudhat*, *abodhīt*, *abodhiṣṭa*. The rule "after *dīp*, *jana*, etc. does not apply here [to form *abuddha*], because by virtue of the association with what precedes and follows, only the root belonging to the *divādi* class is understood there. 876 *ubund* in the sense of perceiving (*niśāmana*). Perceiving means knowledge. *bubunde*, *abudat*, *abundīt*. 877 *veṇṛ* in the senses of moving, knowing, thinking, perceiving, and grasping musical instruments: *veṇati*, *veṇate*. This root also ends in *n*. 878 *khanu* in the sense of digging: *khanati*, *khanate*.
In the presence of an affix marked with K or Ṅ, except for anaṅ, there is elision of the final phoneme of the roots gam, han, jan, khan, and ghas.

There shall be elision of the *upadhā* (penultimate vowel) of these [roots] before an affix beginning with a vowel that is marked with *k* or *ṅ*, but not before the *aṅ* augment. Examples: *cakhnatuḥ*. Regarding the roots beginning with *ye* (*yā* etc.), there is an option (*vibhāṣā*): *khāyāt* or *khanyāt*. 879. *cīvṛ* in the sense of taking and covering: *cicīva*, *cicīve*. 880. *cāyṛ* in the sense of honoring and perceiving. 881. *vyay* in the sense of going: *avyayīt*. 882. *dāśṛ* in the sense of giving: *dadāśa*, *dadāśe*. 883. *bheṣṛ* in the sense of fear; some say also in the sense of going: *bheṣati*, *bheṣate*. 884. *bhreṣṛ*; 885. *bhleṣṛ* in the sense of going. 886. *as* in the senses of going, shining, and taking: *asati*.

*āsate*, *āsa*, *āse*; this [root] also ends in *ṣ*. 887. *spaś* in the sense of "afflicting" and "touching"; touching means binding. *spaśati*, *spaśate*. 888. *laṣ* in the sense of "desire. By the rule *vā bhrāśa-bhlāśa-bhramu-kasaya-ruṣa-raṭa-laṣaḥ*, there is optionally the affix *śyan*. *laṣyati*, *laṣati*; *leṣe*. 889. *caṣ* in the sense of "eating. 890. *chaṣ* in the sense of "injuring. *cacchaṣatuḥ*, *cacchaṣe*. 891. *jhaṣ* in the sense of "taking" and "concealing. 892. *bhrakṣ* and 893. *bhlakṣ* in the sense of "eating. Maitreya says [the root is] *bhakṣ*. 894. *dāsṛ* in the sense of "giving. 895. *māhṛ* in the sense of "measuring. 896. *guhū* in the sense of "concealing."

SK 2364: *ūdupadhāyā gohaḥ* (A 6.4.89). For the root *guh*, there shall be *ū* in place of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) before an affix beginning with a vowel that causes *guṇa*. Thus: *gūhati* (he hides) or *gūhate* (he hides). Because it is marked with *ūd*, *iṭ* is optional. [Thus: *gūhitā* (he will hide) or *goḍhā* (he will hide); *gūhiṣyati* (he will hide) or *ghokṣyati* (he will hide). [Optative: *gūhet* (he may hide) or *guhyāt* (may he hide). [Aorist: *agūhīt* (he hid). In the absence of *iṭ*: [the suffix] *ksa*. [Thus: *adhukṣat* (he hid). SK 2365: *lug vā duhadihalihaguhām ātmanepade dantye* (A 7.3.73). SK 2373: *dā-dhā-ghv-adāp* (A 1.1.20). Verbal roots having the form of *dā* or the form of *dhā*, with the exception of *dāp* and *daip*, shall bear the technical designation *ghu*. SK 2374: *er liṅi* (A 6.4.67). [The substitution of *ī* for the final *e* of a root occurs] before the suffix *liṅ*.

SK 2376 *vibhāṣā ghrādheṭśācchāsaḥ* (A 2.4.78): After these roots (*ghrā*, *dheṭ*, *śā*, *chā*, *sā*), there may optionally be the elision (*luk*) of the suffix *sic* when a *parasmaipada* ending follows. Examples: *adhāt*, *adhātām*, *adhuḥ*.
SK 2377 *yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca* (A 7.2.73): After the roots *yam*, *ram*, *nam*, and *mā*, the augment *sak* is added [to the root] before the suffix *sic*.

For these [roots], *sak* may be substituted; for these [roots], *iṭ* shall be added to *sic* in the *parasmaipada* endings. *adhāsīt*, *adhāsiṣṭām*, *adhāsiṣuḥ*. *glai* and *mlai* [mean] "in the waning of joy"; "waning of joy" means "waning of vitality. *glāyati*; *jaglau*; *jaglitha*; *jaglātha*. 920–921. The roots *pai* and *ovai* mean "to dry. *pāyāt* (optative); *apāsīt* (aorist). SK 2379: *ṛtaś ca saṃyogāder guṇaḥ* (A 7.4.10). Guṇa is substituted for a stem ending in ṛ that begins with a conjunct consonant when followed by the suffix *liṭ*. [Thus we get: *jahvāra*, *jahvaratuḥ*, *jahvaruḥ*, *jahvartha*. [In the future tense: *hvartā*. [Regarding the rule] *ṛddhanoḥ*: SK 2380: *guṇor tisaṃyogādyḥ* (A 7.4.29). Thus: *hvaryāt*; *ahvārṣīt*; *ahvārṣṭām*. 932. The root *svṛ* means "to sound" and "to heat. By the rule *svarati-sūti-* etc., the augment *iṭ* is optional. Thus: *sasvaritha* or *sasvartha*. However, regarding the roots *vam* and *mā*, [the following applies]: SK 2381: *śryuk kiti* (Pāṇini 7.2.11). [This rule states that the long vowel *ī* is substituted for the final *u* of a root ending in *u* or *ū* when followed by an *ārdhadhātuka* affix beginning with a *kit* suffix.]

The augment *iṭ* shall not occur after the root *śri*, when followed by suffixes marked with the indicators *ṅ* or *k*. Since this prohibition is established by the force of commencing the section on prohibitions (*pratiṣedha-kāṇḍa*) earlier in the treatise—thereby overriding even the subsequent optional rules such as those concerning *svarati*—the augment *iṭ* would be prohibited by this rule; however, because of the restrictive rule for roots beginning with *krī* (*krādiniyama*), *iṭ* is applied invariably. Thus: *sasvariva*, *sasvarima*. Because of the subsequent rule "after roots ending in *ṛ* or *dhā*" (*ṛddhanoḥ*), *iṭ* is invariably applied: *svariṣyati*, *svaryāt*, *asvārīt*, *asvārīṣṭām*, *asvārṣīt*, *asvārṣṭām*. 933. *smṛ* in the sense of recollection. 934. *vṛ* in the sense of covering.

935 *sṛ* in the sense of "going. Because it belongs to the *krād-varga*, there is no *iṭ* augment. [Forms: *sasārtha*, *sasṛva*. [In the optative,] *riṅ* [substitution applies]: *sriyāt*. [In the aorist: *asārṣīt*, *asārṣṭām*. SK 2382: *sarti-śāsty-artibhyaś ca* (A 3.1.56). SK 2383: *ṛcchaty-ṛtām* (A 7.4.11). In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], there shall be *guṇa* substitution for the root *ṛcch*, which belongs to the *tud*-class, as well as for roots ending in *ṛ*. *iḍ-atty-arti-vyayatīnām* (A 7.2.66). [The augment *iṭ* is added after the *liṭ* suffixes] following roots ending in *i*, the root *ad*, the root *ṛ*, and the root *vyay*.

[This is governed by] A 6.4.87: *huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke*.

In place of the vowel *u* of the root *hu*, which ends in the suffix *śnu* and has more than one syllable (*anekāc*), as well as in place of the vowel *u* of a stem (*aṅga*) that does not have a conjunct consonant (*asaṃyoga-pūrva*) preceding it, there shall be *yaṇ* substitution before an *sārvadhātuka* affix beginning with a vowel. Examples: *śṛṇvanti*, *śṛṇomi*, *śṛṇvaḥ*, *śṛṇuvaḥ*, *śṛṇmaḥ*, *śṛṇumaḥ*; *śuśrotha*, *śuśruva*; *śṛṇu*; *śṛṇavāni*; *śṛṇuyāt*; *śrūyāt*; *aśrauṣīt*. 943. *dhru* in the sense of steadiness (*sthairye*). It forms *dhravati*. This [root] also belongs to the *kuṭādi* group and means "to go. 944. *du* and 945. *dru* in the sense of going. [Examples: *dudotha*, *dudavitha*.

*dudaviva*, *dudrotha*, *dudruva*. By the rule *ṇi-śri-... caṅ*, [the form] *adudruvat* is derived. (946) *ji*, (947) *jri*—in the sense of "overpowering" (*abhibhava*). Overpowering consists of both making something inferior (*nyūnīkaraṇa*) and becoming inferior oneself (*nyūnībhavana*). In the first sense, it is transitive (*sakarmaka*): "He conquers his enemies" (*śatrūn jayati*). In the second sense, however, it is intransitive (*akarmaka*): "He is defeated by his studies" (*adhyayanāt parājayate*). The meaning is that he becomes weary of studying. By the rule *viparābhyāṃ jeḥ*, the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied. By the rule *parāher asoḍhaḥ*, the studies are treated as the ablative (*apādāna*) because they are not endured.

Now follow the roots ending in *ḍīṅ* that are marked with the *ṅit* indicatory letter: 948. *ṣmiṅ* (to smile slightly): *smayate*, *siṣmiye*, *siṣmiyiḍhve* / *siṣmiyidhve*. 949. *guṅ* (inarticulate sound): *gavate*, *juguve*. 950. *gāṅ* (motion): *gāte*, *gāte*, *gāte*. The commentary states that the doubling [of the consonant] is intended to be superseded by the designation *digya*. Thus: *digye* (SK 2389), according to A 1.2.17:
*sthādhvor ic ca*.

In place of these two [roots], there shall be the substitution of *ad*, and *sic* shall be *kit* when followed by *taṅ*. Examples: *adita*, *adithāḥ*, *adiṣi*. 963. *śyaiṅ* in the sense of going: *śyāyate*; *śaśye*. 964. *pyaiṅ* in the sense of growth: *pyāyate*; *papye*; *pyātā*. 965. *traiṅ* in the sense of protecting: *trāyate*; *tatre*. 966. *pūṅ* in the sense of purifying: *pavate*; *pupuve*; *pavitā*. 967. *mūṅ* in the sense of binding: *mavate*. 968. *ḍīṅ* in the sense of moving through the air: *ḍayate*; *ḍiḍye*; *ḍayitā*. 969. *tṝ* in the senses of floating and crossing:
[By rule A 1.1.100, *ṛta iddhātoḥ*: the substitute *it* is applied in place of the final *ṛ* of a root.]

The vowel *i* shall be substituted for the final *ṛ* of a verbal root that constitutes an *aṅga*. In case of conflict between the substitution of *i* or *u* and the rules for *guṇa* or *vṛddhi*, the former prevails. *tarati*: here, by the rule *ṛcchatyṝtām*, *guṇa* applies; by *tṝphalabhajām ām akiti*, *etva* applies. *teratuḥ*; *teruḥ*. **SK 2391**: *vṝto vā* (A 7.2.37).

After the roots *vṛṅ* and *vṛñ*, and after a root ending in *ṛ*, the long vowel may optionally be substituted for the *iṭ* augment, except in the *liṭ* (perfect tense). *tarītā*; *taritā*. Why say "except in the *liṭ*" (*aliṭi*)? Consider *teritha*: here, by the rule *hali ca*, the long vowel is applied. *tīryāt*.
SK 2392: *sici ca parasmaipadeṣu* (A 7.2.40). Here, the long vowel [substitution] for the *iṭ* augment after roots ending in *vṛt* does not occur. Examples: *atāriṣṭām*.

Now, eight [roots] are *anudātta-it* (unaccented in their indicatory vowel): 790 *gup* in the sense of protecting; 791 *tij* in the sense of sharpening; 792 *mān* in the sense of honoring; 793 *badh* in the sense of binding.

SK 2393: *guptijkidbhyaḥ san* (A 3.1.5). SK 2394: *mānbadhadānśānbhyo dīrghaś cābhyāsasya* (A 3.1.6). The suffix *san* occurs after the roots mentioned in these two rules; furthermore, there is lengthening of the vowel *i* in the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) of the roots beginning with *mān*. *gup* [takes *san*] in the sense of reproaching (*nindā*). *tij* [takes *san*] in the sense of enduring (*kṣamā*). *kit* [takes *san*] in the sense of counteracting disease, restraint, removal, destruction, and doubt. *mān* [takes *san*] in the sense of desiring to know (*jijñāsā*). *badh* [takes *san*] in the sense of a mental disturbance (*cittavikāra*). *dān* [takes *san*] in the sense of straightforwardness (*ārjava*). *śān* [takes *san*] in the sense of sharpening (*niśāna*). By the rule *sanādyantāḥ...* [Pāṇini 3.1.32], these forms possess the status of verbal roots (*dhātutva*).

SK 2395: *sanyaṅoḥ* (A 6.1.9). For a root ending in *san* (Desiderative) and one ending in *yaṅ* (Intensive), the first monosyllabic (*ekāc*) portion is reduplicated; however, for a root beginning with a vowel (*aj-ādi*), the second syllable is reduplicated. Subsequently, the operations pertaining to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa-kārya*) apply. Roots such as *gup* and others—excluding those marked with the *kṛt* suffix *kit*—which signify censure (*nindā*) and so forth, are *anudātta-it* (have a low-pitched indicatory vowel); likewise, *dāna* and *śāna* are *svarita-it* (have a circumflex indicatory vowel). These necessarily take the *san* suffix. However, when used in a different sense, they belong to the *curādigaṇa* and lack an indicatory vowel (*ananubandhaka*). Since an indicatory vowel has no function when the root stands alone, the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are applied after the form ending in *san*. Because the suffix *san* is not prescribed here by the rule *dhātoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.91), it does not possess the status of an *ārdhadhātuka* (semi-vocalic) suffix in this context.

By that [rule], the *iṭ* augment does not occur: *jugupsate*, *jugupsāṃcakre*, *titikṣate*, *mīmāṃsate*. In these [roots], there is the elision of the *ś* when followed by the suffix *ap*. Thus: *svajate*, *pariṣvajate*. After the prefix *vi*, the root *skand* takes *ṣ* [for *s*], except in the case of the past passive participle (*aniṣṭhāyām*). (A 8.3.73)

Or rather, there would be *ṣatva* [the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*]. As stated in the *Bhāṣya*: "First the root is joined with the prefix; thereafter, it is joined with the suffix."

According to another school of thought (*matāntara*), there is no substitution of *ṇ* for *n* when preceded by a *sādhana* (instrumental case). 980. *yabh* (to copulate): *yebhitha*, *yayabdha*, *yabdhā*, *yapsyati*, *ayāpsīt*. 981. *ṇam* (in bowing and sound): *nemitha*, *nanantha*, *nantā*, *anaṃsīt*, *anaṃsiṣṭām*. 982. *gamḷ* and 983. *sṛpḷ* (to go).

However, some maintain that this extension (*atideśa*) applies only to what is taught under the heading of *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes; according to their view, the *yaṇ* substitution does not occur. Thus says Bhaṭṭi:

Regarding the phrase "studying the *samītayaḥ* of the two Rāghavas" (BhK 3.18): the root *vī* is used in the senses of motion, pervasion, procreation (*prajana*), beauty, throwing (*asana*), and eating. *Prajana* means conception (the taking of an embryo). *Asana* means casting or throwing. [Conjugations of *vī*:]* *veti*, *vītaḥ*, *viyanti*; *veṣi*, *vemi*, *vīhi*; *avet*, *avītām*, *aviyan*. Some maintain that because there is the augment *aṭ* and [the root] has more than one vowel (*anekāctvāt*), the substitution of *yaṇ* occurs [resulting in *aviyan*]. Others hold that here the vowel *ī* is also included as a separate root (*dhātvantara*) [yielding *avyan*]. [Conjugations of *i*:]* *eti*, *ītaḥ*, *iyanti*; *īyāt*, *aiṣīt*. 1049. *Yā* in the sense of reaching (*prāpaṇa*). Here, reaching means motion. [Conjugations:]* *praṇiyāti*, *yātaḥ*, *yānti*.

SK 2463: According to Śākaṭāyana alone, the *jus* substitute may optionally occur for *jhi* following the *laṅ* [aorist] when it follows a root ending in long *ā*. Examples: *ayuḥ* / *ayān*. *yāyāt* / *yāyātām* / *yāyāstām*. 1050. *vā* in the senses of motion and scenting (*gandhana*); *gandhana* means indicating (*sūcana*). 1051. *bhā* in the sense of shining (*dīpti*). 1052. *ṣṇā* in the sense of cleansing (*śauca*). 1053. *śrā* in the sense of cooking (*pāka*). 1054. *pā* in the sense of protecting (*rakṣaṇa*). Example: *pāyāstām*. Aorist: *apāsīt*. 1057. *rā* in the sense of giving (*dāna*). 1058. *lā* in the sense of taking (*ādāna*). Candra states that both [roots] mean "giving. 1059. *dāp* in the sense of cutting (*lavana*). Present: *praṇidāti* / *pranidāti*. Precative: *dāyāstām*. Aorist: *adāsīt*.

1060 *khyā* in the sense of "to tell" (*prakathane*). This [root] has as its domain only the *sārvadhātuka* suffixes. The evidence for this is the *vārttika* "There is homogeneity (*sasthānatva*) with *na* in the case of *namas khyātre*" and its commentary (*bhāṣya*). "Homogeneity" refers to the *jihvāmūlīya* sound. The meaning is that the purpose of the substitution of *khyāñ* [for *khyā*] is to prevent [the *jihvāmūlīya*] from occurring when [the root] belongs to the *khaśādi* group. The author of the *Nyāsa* states that there is no usage of *khyāti* preceded by the prefix *sam*. 1061 *prā* in the sense of "filling" (*pūraṇe*). 1062 *mā* in the sense of "measuring" (*māne*). It is intransitive (*akarmaka*). As Māgha says: "The enemies of Kaiṭabha did not measure themselves (*mamur*) there in their own bodies."

By the force of a prefix (*upasarga*), [the root *mā*] takes an object in another sense: *udaraṃ parimāti muṣṭinā* ("he measures the belly with his fist"). It is not included here in the rule *ner gada-* (Pāṇini 7.3.73); thus we have *praṇimāti* and *pranimāti*. 1063. *vaca* in the sense of speaking: *vakti*, *vaktaḥ*. This [root] is not used followed by the suffix *anti*. Others say it is not used followed by the plural suffixes; others say it is not used followed by the suffix *jhi*. [Optative: *vagdhī*, *vacyāt*, *ucyāt*. [Imperfect: *avocat*. 1064. *vida* in the sense of knowing. [Pāṇini 3.4.83 states:
*vido laṭo vā* ("after the root *vid*, the present tense suffixes are optionally [replaced by the perfect suffixes]").

In the case of the *laṭ* [present tense] for the *parasmaipada* endings, *ṇal* and the other substitutes may optionally occur. *veta* (*veda*), *vidatuḥ*, *viduḥ*; *vettha*, *vidathuḥ*, *vida*; *veda*, *vidva*, *vidma*. In the alternative [when the substitutes do not apply], *vetti*, *vittaḥ*, etc. *viveda*, *vividatuḥ*. By the rule *uṣavidajāgṛbhyo 'nyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 3.1.38), the suffix *ām* is optionally used; in the *ām*-alternative, because of the irregular substitution (*nipātana*) of *videt* ending in *a*, there is no *guṇa* strengthening of the light penultimate vowel. *vidāñcakāra*. *veditā*. According to *vidāṅkurvantv ity anyatarasyām* (A 3.1.41), [the form *vidāṅkurvantu* is used].

In the place of the *loṭ* [imperative], there is the absence of the *guṇa* vowel; the elision (*luk*) of the *loṭ* suffix and the optional employment (*anuprayoga*) of the verb *kṛ* ending in *loṭ* are prescribed as irregularities (*nipātyate*). Because of the word "iti," neither person (*puruṣa*) nor number (*vacana*) is intended to be expressed.

SK 2466: *tanādikṛñbhya uḥ* (A 3.1.79). The suffix *u* shall be applied after the roots beginning with *tan* and after *kṛ*. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to *śap*. Since the desired form would have been established by the fact that *kṛ* belongs to the *tan*-class, the explicit mention of *kṛ* is a *liṅga* (indicative mark) that operations pertaining to the [verbal] classes (*gaṇakārya*) are not invariably obligatory (*anitya*). By this, forms such as *na viśvased aviśvastam* ("one should not trust the untrustworthy") are established. [Examples: *vidāṃkarotu*. SK 2467: *ata ut sārvadhātuke* (A 6.4.110). [The substitution of] *u* for the final *a* of a verbal root occurs before an affix beginning with a vowel that is part of a *sārvadhātuka* suffix.

The vowel *u* shall be substituted for the *a* of the root *kṛ*, when it ends in the suffix *upratyaya*, before a *sārvadhātuka* affix marked with *k* or *ṅ*. Because of the force of the *tapara* notation in *ud*, there is no *guṇa* substitution. *vidāṃkurutāt* / *vidāṃkurutām* / By the rule *utaś ca*, there is elision (*luk*) of the imperative suffix *hi*; because this elision is considered "unestablished" (*asiddha*) due to its being a rule pertaining to the *ābhīya* class, the substitution of *u* takes place. *vidāṃkuru* / *vidāṃkaravāṇi* / *avet* / *avittām* / By the rule *sijabhyasta-*, *jus* is substituted for *jhi*. *aviduḥ* / By the rule *daś ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.75), when *sip* follows, the final *d* of a verbal root may optionally become *ru*. *aveḥ* / *avet* / 1065. The root *as* meaning "to be": *asti* /

SK 2469 *śnasor allopaḥ* (A 6.4.111): There is elision (*lopa*) of the vowel *a* of both the suffix *śna* and the root *as*, when followed by a *sārvadhātuka* affix marked with *k* or *ṅ*. [Examples: *staḥ*, *santi*. By the rule *tāsastyoḥ...* (A 7.4.50), there is elision of *s*. [Examples: *asi*, *sthaḥ*, *stha*, *asmi*, *svaḥ*, *smaḥ*. Under the governing heading (*adhikāra*) "in an *ārdhadhātuka* affix" (A 6.4.46): SK 2470 *aster bhūḥ* (A 6.4.52).
*babhūva*, *bhavitā*, *astu*, *syāt*, *stām*, *santu*.

SK 2471: *dhvasoreddhāv abhyāsalopaś ca* (A 6.4.119). [In the case of the roots *dhu* and *sas*, when the suffixes *liṭ* and *luṅ* with the augment *āṬ` follow, the substitution of *et* occurs for the final vowel and the following consonant, and there is the elision of the reduplicated syllable.]

In the case of the root *as* (to be), when followed by the suffix *dhi* (the second person singular imperative ending), the substitution of *e* for *a* occurs, and there is the elision (*lopa*) of the *abhyāsa* (reduplication) and the *s*. Because this substitution of *e* is considered "unestablished" (*asiddha*) by virtue of being an *ābhīya* operation, the rule *dheḥ dhiḥ* applies. Furthermore, by the rule *śnasoḥ*, there is the elision of the vowel (*al-lopa*). Thus: *edhi*. In the alternative where the substitute *tātaṅ* is used, the substitution of *e* does not occur, because it is superseded by the subsequent *tātaṅ*; this is according to the maxim *sakṛdgatau vipratiṣedhe yad bādhitaṃ tad bādhitam eva* ("when a conflict has occurred once, that which is superseded remains superseded"). [The forms are: *stāt*, *stam*, *sta*, *asāni*, *asāva*, *asāma*. By the rule *astisico 'pṛkte*, the augment *iṭ* is added. [Thus: *āsīt*. Since the elision of the vowel (*al-lopa*) by the rule *śnasoḥ* is "unestablished" (*asiddha*) due to its *ābhīya* status, the augment *āṭ* is applied. [Thus: *āstām*, *āsan*. [Optative forms: *syāt*, *bhūyāt*. [Aorist: *abhūt*. Because the presence of the suffix *sic* and the root *as* serves as a qualifier, the augment *iṭ* is not applied [in the counter-example *āsiṣṭa*].

SK 2472: *upasargaprādurbhyām astir yacparaḥ* (A 8.3.87). When preceded by an *upasarga* or *prādur*, the *s* of the root *as* becomes *ṣ* when followed by a suffix beginning with *y* or a vowel (*ac*). Examples: *niṣyāt*, *prāduḥṣyāt*; *niṣanti*, *prāduḥṣanti*. Why "followed by *y*" (*yacparaḥ*)? [Consider: *abhistaḥ*. 1066: *mṛj* in the sense of purification. SK 2473: *mṛjer vṛddhiḥ* (A 7.2.114). [The substitute *vṛddhi* occurs in place of the final vowel and following consonant of the root *mṛj* before an affix marked with *K* or *Ṅ*.]

The vowel *i* of the root *mṛj* undergoes *vṛddhi* when followed by an affix beginning with a consonant that has an indicatory *k* or *ṅ*, provided it begins with a vowel. By the rule *vaśca*, the *j* becomes *ṣ*. Thus: *mārṣṭi*, *mṛṣṭaḥ*, *mṛjanti*, *mārjanti*. Perfect: *mamārja*, *mamārjatuḥ*, *mamṛjatuḥ*, *mamārjitha*, *mamārṣṭa*. Future: *mārjitā*, *mārṣṭā*. Imperative: *mṛḍḍhi*. Aorist: *amārṭ*, *amārjam*, *amārjīt*, *amārkṣīt*. 1067. *rudir* in the sense of shedding tears.
According to A 7.2.76 (*rudādibhyaḥ sārvadhātuke*), [the augment *īṭ* is added after the roots beginning with *rud* before an affix of the *sārvadhātuka* class].

The augment *iṭ* shall be applied to a *sārvadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant (*valādi*) following the roots *rud*, *svap*, *śvas*, *an*, and *jakṣ*. Thus: *roditi*, *ruditaḥ*. In the case of the second person singular ending *hi*, because it is subsequent [in the order of rules], *iṭ* is applied first, and thus the substitution of *dhi* does not occur; hence: *ridihi*. [Rule 2475: *rudaś ca pañcabhyaḥ* (A 7.3.98): The augment *īṭ* shall be applied to a *sārvadhātuka* suffix that begins with a consonant (*halādi*), consists of a single phoneme (*apṛkta*), and ends in *p* (i.e., the third person singular ending *-ti*), following the five roots beginning with *rud*. Thus: *roditī*.

SK 2476 *aḍ gārgyagālavayoḥ* (A 7.3.99): *arodīt*, *arodat*, *aruditām*, *arudan*, *arodīḥ*, *arodaḥ*. Because they depend on specific bases (*prakṛti*) and suffixes (*pratyaya*), the augment *yāsuṭ* applies by virtue of being *antaraṅga* (internal) relative to the augments *aṭ* and *iṭ*. [Thus]: *rudyāt*, *arudat*, *arodīt*. 1068 *ñiṣvap śaye* (to lie down): *svapiti*, *svapitaḥ*, *suṣvāpa*, *suṣupatuḥ*, *suṣupuḥ*, *suṣvapitha*, *suṣvaptha*.
SK 2477 *suvinirdurbhyaḥ supisūtisamāḥ* (A 8.3.88).

In these cases, the *s* of the *sup* suffixes beginning with a vowel shall become *ṣ*. First, the verbal root is joined with the prefix (*upasarga*). In the case of the *liṭ* (perfect) affix marked with *k*, because it is subsequent [to the rules for reduplication], the semivowel-vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) and the change to *ṣ* are performed first; then, reduplication occurs. According to the principle that "what is established earlier is not considered valid for the purpose of reduplication," we have *suṣuṣupatuḥ* and *suṣuṣupuḥ*. However, in the case of an affix not marked with *k*, the semivowel-vocalization of the reduplicated syllable occurs after the reduplication. Because the change to *ṣ* is not yet established at that point, the rule *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* (retaining only the initial consonant of the reduplicated syllable) applies before it, and this is due to its obligatory nature (*nityatva*). Consequently, since the form *sup-* no longer exists, the change to *ṣ* does not take place. Thus, we have *susuṣvāpa* and *susvaptā*.

*asvapīt*, *asvapat*, *avapyāt*, *supyāt*, *suṣupyāt*, *asvāpsīt*. 1069 *śvasa* (to breathe): *śvasiti*, *śvasitā*, *aśvasīt*, *aśvasat*, *śvasyātām*, *śvasyāstām*. By the rule *hmyantakṣaṇa-*, there is no *vṛddhi*: *aśvasīt*. 1070 *ana* (and [the root *an*]): *aniti*, *āna*, *anitā*, *ānīt*, *ānat*. SK 2478 (*aniteḥ*): After a cause situated in a prefix, the *n* of *ani* is replaced by *ṇ*. *prāṇiti*. 1071 *jakṣa* (to eat and to laugh): *jakṣati*, *jakṣitaḥ*.

SK 2479: *ad abhyastāt* (A 7.1.4). After a reduplicated (*abhyasta*) root ending in a consonant (*jha*), *at* shall be substituted for [the *s* of the suffix]. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule concerning the final letter. *jakṣati*. By the rule *sijabhyasta-*, *jus* is substituted [for *at*]: *ajakṣuḥ*. Ujjvaladatta was mistaken in thinking that this [root *jakṣ*] begins with a semivowel (*antasthā*). The five roots beginning with *rud* have been completed. 1072. *jāgṛ* (to wake, to cease from sleep). *jāgarti*. *jāgṛtaḥ*. *jāgrati*. By the rule *uṣavidajāgṛbhyo 'nyatarasyām*, *ām* is optionally added: *jāgarāṃcakāra*. Alternatively, *jajāgāra*.

SK 2480 *jāgro 'viciṇṇalṅitsu* (A 7.3.85): The *guṇa* substitution shall apply to the root *jāgr-* in cases other than those requiring *vṛddhi* or *pratiṣedha* (prohibition), except before the suffixes *vi*, *ciṇ*, and *ṅit*. Examples: *jajāgaratuḥ*; *ajāgaḥ*; *ajāgṛtām*. Because it is an *abhyasta* (repeated) stem, the suffix *jus* is applied [by SK 2481]. SK 2481 *jusi ca* (A 7.3.83): [The *guṇa* substitution applies] also before the suffix *jus*.

When followed by a suffix beginning with *aj* (vowels), there shall be *guṇa* substitution for a stem ending in *ī*. Examples: *ajāgaruḥ*. Why "beginning with *aj*"? Consider *jāgṛyuḥ*. But in the benedictive (*āśis*), we have *jāgaryāt*, *jāgāryāstām*, *jāgaryāsuḥ*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *ajāgarīt*. In the form *jāgṛ im*, *yaṇ* substitution would have been applicable; that is superseded by the *sārvadhātuka-guṇa*. That [guṇa] is superseded by the *vṛddhi* rule in the *sic* suffix. That [vṛddhi] is superseded by the *guṇa* of the root *jāgarti*. Once that has been applied, the *vṛddhi* conditioned by the stem ending in a consonant (*halanta-lakṣaṇā*) would have been applicable, but it is prohibited by the rule *neṭi*.

Then, setting aside the rule *ato halādeḥ* (P. 6.4.71), the rule *ato lrāntasya* (P. 6.4.66) becomes applicable, but it is negated by *hmyanta* (P. 6.4.9). Regarding this, they say: "Guṇa, Vṛddhi, Guṇa, Vṛddhi, prohibition, option, again prohibition of Vṛddhi, and the application of *yaṇ* after *at*: there are nine possibilities. The root *daridrā* means "to be in distress. It forms *daridrāti*. By the rule *iddaridrasya* (A 6.4.114), the *ikāra* (the vowel *i*) is substituted for the final portion of *daridrā* before a *sārvadhātuka* affix beginning with a consonant (*dhakārādi*) that has *k* or *ṅ* as an *it*. Thus: *daridritaḥ*.

SK 2483: *śnābhyas tayor ātaḥ* (A 6.4.112). There is elision of the *ā* of these two [roots] before a *sārvadhātuka* affix beginning with *k* or *ṅ*. *daridrati*. Because it has more than one vowel (*anekāctvāt*), there is the insertion of *ām*: *daridrāṃcakāra*. In the rule *āta au ṇalaḥ*, although the form would have been established by simply saying *o*, the prescription of *au* is for the purpose of its being heard after the elision of the *ā* of *daridrāti* has taken place. On account of this very indicator (*jñāpaka*), some say that *ām* is inserted. Thus: *dadaridrau*, *dadaridratur*, etc. As for the form *dadaridra* in the *ṇal* suffix, that is entirely without foundation. When an *ārdhadhātuka* affix is intended to follow *daridrāti*, the elision of the *ā* should be stated; or else, [the elision] occurs in the *luṅ* tense.

The augment *ṇ* is not applied when the suffixes *ṇvul* or *lyuṭ* follow. *daridritā* / *adaridrāt* / *adaridritām* / *adaridruḥ* / *daridriyāt* / *daridryāt* / *adaridrīt*. The augments *iṭ* and *sak* are added: *adaridrāsīt*. 1074. The root *cakāsṛ* means "to shine. *cakāsti*. [By the rule *jhasya at*,] *at* replaces the *jh* [of the first person plural]: *cakāsati*. *cakāsāṃcakāra*. According to the rule *dhica*, there is elision of *s*; some say this applies only to the *sic* [augment]. *cakāddhi*. The *Bhāṣya* states only *cakādhī*. By the rule *tipyanasteḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.73), *d* replaces the *s* at the end of a word before the suffix *tip*, but not for the root *as*. *acakāt* / *acakād*. *acakāsuḥ*.

SK 2485: *sipi dhāto rur vā* (A 8.2.74). After a verbal root ending in *s*, there is optionally *ru* [before the suffix *sip*]. In the alternative case, *da* occurs by virtue of the *jaś*-rule. Thus: *acakāḥ* or *acakāt*. 1075: *śāsu* in the sense of "instruction. [The present indicative third-person singular is] *śāsti*. SK 2486: *śāsa id aṅ-haloḥ* (A 6.4.34). [The substitute *i* is applied to the final vowel of the root *śās* before the augment *aṅ* and before suffixes beginning with a consonant.]

The substitution of *it* shall take place for the penultimate vowel of the root *śās* before an affix beginning with a consonant (*hal*) that has an indicatory *k* or *ṅ*, as well as before the affix *aṅ*. By the rule *śāsivasighasām—*, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs [for the *s*]. Thus: *śiṣṭaḥ*; *śāsati*; *śaśāsatuḥ*; *śāstu*; *śiṣṭāt*; *śāsatu*. [And] by *śā hau* (A 6.4.35):
[the substitution of *u* for the final vowel of *śās* occurs before the imperative ending *hi*].

The substitution of *śā* for the root *śās* occurs when followed by the suffix *dhī*. Because that [substitution] is *abhīya*, it is considered asiddha; consequently, *dhi* replaces *dhī*. *śādhi* (imperative). *aśāt* (imperfect, singular). *aśiṣṭām* (imperfect, dual). *aśāsuḥ* (imperfect, plural). *aśāḥ* (imperfect, second person singular). *aśāt* (imperfect, second person dual). *śiṣyāt* (precative). By the rule *sarti-śāsty-artibhyaś ca*, the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *aśiṣat* (imperfect). *aśāsiṣyat* (conditional). 1076. *dīdhīṅ* in the sense of shining and playing. These five roots beginning with this one are Vedic (*chāndasa*). *dīdhīte* (present, third person singular). By the rule *eranekācaḥ*, the *yaṇ* substitute is applied. *dūdhyāte* (present, third person dual). [Note: By the rule *yīvarṇayor dīdhīvevyoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.53), [the elision of the penultimate vowel applies].

According to the rule "there is elision of the final [vowel] of these two before *ya* and an *i*-vowel," one might expect elision; however, that is superseded by the substitution of *e* for the final vowel (*ṭi*), because it is a mandatory (*nitya*) rule. Thus: *dīdhye*. By the rule *dīdhye-vevīṭām*, there is a prohibition of *guṇa*. *dīdhyāñcakre*. *dīdhitā*. *dīdhiṣyate*. 1077. *vevīṅ* has the same meaning as *veti*; that is to say, it occurs in the sense of moving, which is the same as the root *vī* meaning "to go."

Now follow three roots that take the *parasmaipada* endings: 1078 *ṣasa* and 1079 *sasti*, meaning "to sleep. *sasti*, *sastaḥ*, *sasanti*. *sasāsa*, *sesatuḥ*. *sastu*, *sadhi*. Because the elision of *s* (the *salopa*) is considered "not established" (*asiddha*) by the rule *pūrvatrāsiddham*, the elision of *hi* (by the rule *ato heḥ*) does not occur here. *asat*, *asastām*, *asaḥ*, *asat*. *sasyāt*. *a-sāsīt*, *a-sasīt*. *santi*. Since the root is marked with the *idit* designation, *num* is added. When the form *saṃstaḥ* is thus established, the *s* is elided by the rule *skoḥ saṃyogādyor...*. Then, by the rule *jharo jhari savarṇe*, there is optionally the elision of the *t* sound.

*Santaḥ* (they are); *saṃstanti* (they continue). Because one does not accept that the technical term "conjunction" (*saṃyoga*) applies to two [consonants] when there is a cluster of many, the elision [of the *t*] by the rule *skoḥ—* does not occur. Some say [the forms are] *saṃsti* and *saṃstaḥ*. 1080. *vaś* (to desire); "desire" means longing. *vaṣṭi* (he desires); *uṣṭaḥ* (they two desire); *uśanti* (they desire). *vakṣi* (thou desir-est); *uṣṭaḥ* (you two desire). *uvāśa* (he desired); *ūśatuḥ* (they two desired). *vaśitā* (the state of having desired). *vaṣṭu* (let him desire); *uṣṭāt* (may he desire); *uḍḍhi* (do thou desire). *avaṭ* (he desired); *avaḍ* (he desired). *auṣṭām* (they two desired); *auśan* (they desired). *avaśam* (I desired). *uśyātām* (may they two desire); *uśyāstām* (may they two desire). *avāśīt* (he desired); *avaśīt* (he desired). And [there is] the *carkarīta* (reduplicated present) formation.

The forms without the *yaṅ* suffix (*yaṅluganta*) should be understood as belonging to the *ad*-class (second class). 1082. *hnuṅ* in the sense of "removing": *hnute*, *juhnuve*, *hnuvīta*, *hnoṣīṣṭa*, *ahnoṣṭa*. Thus end the *ad*-class verbs.
The affixes *jho* and so forth occur after verbal roots ending in personal endings (*tiṅ*).

The root *hu* is used in the senses of giving (*dāna*) and taking (*ādāna*); some say it is also used in the sense of eating (*prīṇana*), according to the Bhāṣya. Here, "giving" (*dāna*) means the act of pouring; and by its very nature, this is understood to be the offering of oblation (*havis*) into a Vedic receptacle (*ādhāra*). From here on, four roots are *parasmaipada*. SK 2489: *jhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ* (A 2.4.75).
After the roots beginning with *hu*, there shall be *ślu* [elision] of *śap* (the present tense marker).

SK 2490 (A 6.1.10): In the *ślau* state, there is reduplication of the root. *juhoti*, *juhutaḥ*. By [the rule] *ad abhyastāt*, *at* is substituted for the ending.
