Some read [the root] as *sphara* with the vowel *a* as its penultimate; hence: *pasphāra*. 1392 *sphuḍa*, 1393 *cuḍa*, 1394 *vṛḍa*: in the sense of covering. 1395 *kruḍa*, 1396 *bhṛḍa*: some say in the sense of sinking. 1397 *gurī*: in the sense of exertion. It is *anudātta-it*. *gurate*; *jugure*; *guritā*. 1398 *ṇū*: in the sense of praising. It ends in a long vowel (*dīrghānta*). *pariṇūtaguṇodayaḥ*. From here on, four [roots] take the *parasmaipada* endings. *nuvati*; *anuvīt*.

1399. *dhū* in the sense of shaking (*vidhūnana*). [Present stem: *dhuvati*. 1400. *gu* in the sense of voiding excrement (*purīṣotsarga*). [Perfect forms: *juguvitha*, *jugutha*. [Future: *goṣyati*. [Aorist: *agoṣīt*. [By the rule *hrasvād aṅgāt*: dual] *agutām*; [plural] *aguṣuḥ*. 1401. *dhru* in the senses of motion (*gati*) and steadiness (*sthairya*). There is an alternative reading *dhru*. For the first [root], [forms such as] *dhruvati* etc. are like those of *guvati*. The second, however, is *seṭ* (having an *iṭ* augment). [Perfect: *dudhruvitha*. [Future: *dhruvitā*. [Present stem: *dhruvati* etc., like *guvati*. But the second [root] is *seṭ*: [Vedic perfect dual] *dudhruviṣṭām*. 1402. *kuṅ* in the sense of sound (*śabda*).

Kaiyaṭa and others hold that [the root *ku*] ends in a long vowel; thus: *kuvītā*, *akuviṣṭa*. The author of the Nyāsa holds it to end in a short vowel; thus: *kutā*, *akuta*. The roots beginning with *kuṭ* have been explained. 1403. *pṛṅ* (to exert oneself). Preceded by *vyā* in the sense of effort (*prāyaṇa*). [Substitution of] *riṅ*; [substitution of] *iyaṅ*. *vyāpriyate*, *vyāpapre*, *vyāpaprāte*, *vyāpariṣyate*, *vyāpṛta*, *vyāpṛṣātām*. 1404. *mṛṅ* (to die). SK 2538: *mriyater luṅliṅoś ca* (A 1.3.61).

After the roots *mṛ* and *liṅ*, and after those ending in *śit*, the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) suffixes are used; not otherwise. The *ṅ*-marking is for the sake of accent. *mriyate*; *mamāra*; *mamārtha*; *mamṛva*; *martāmi*; *mariṣyati*; *mṛṣīṣṭa*; *amṛta*. Now, seven [roots] that take the *parasmaipada* endings: 1405 *ri* and 1406 *pi* in the sense of "going. Because it is antaranga, *iyaṅ* is applied: *riyati*; *piyati*; *retā*; *petā*. 1407 *dhi* in the sense of "holding"; 1408 *kṣi* in the senses of "dwelling" and "going"; 1409 *ṣū* in the sense of "impelling": *suvati*; *savitā*.

1410 *kṝ* in the sense of scattering (*vikṣepa*). [Present tense: *kirati*, *kirataḥ*. [Perfect tense: *cakāra*, *cakratuḥ*. [Future tense: *karitā*, *karītā*. [Precative: *kīryāt*. [Aorist: *akārīt*. SK 2539: According to A 6.1.104, the augment *suṭ* is applied to the root *kṝ* when preceded by the prefix *upa-* in the sense of cutting (*lavane*). Thus: *upaskarati*. It should be stated that even when there is an intervention by the augment *aṭ* or the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*), *suṭ* occurs before the consonant *k*. Examples: *upāskirat*, *upacaskāra*.

SK 2540: *suṭ* is added before *kṛ* when preceded by *prati* or *upa*, provided that the sense is "injury. Thus: *upaskirati* and *pratiskirati*. 1411: *gṝ* in the sense of "swallowing. SK 2541: Before an *ac*-affix, [the substitution of *guṇa*] is optional. (A 8.2.21)

The substitution of *l* for the *r* of the root *gṛ* may optionally occur when followed by a vowel-initial suffix. Thus: *girati* or *gilati*; *jagāra* or *jagāla*; *jagaritha* or *jagalitha*; *garitā* or *garītā*, *galitā* or *galītā*. 1412. *dṛṅ* (to respect): *ādriyate*; *ādriyete*; *ādadre*; *ādadriṣe*; *ādartā*; *ādariṣyate*; *ādṛṣīṣṭa*; *ādṛta*; *ādṛṣātām*. 1413. *dhṛṅ* (to remain steadfast): *dhriyate*.

Now follow sixteen roots that take the *parasmaipada* endings. 1414. *praccha* (to ask), in the sense of desiring to know (*jñīpsā*). *prcchati*. *papraccha*. *papracchatuḥ*. *papracchitha*. *papraṣṭha*. *praṣṭā*. *prakṣyati*. *aprākṣīt*. The section beginning with *kṛ* (1408) and ending with *vṛt* has been completed. 1415. *sṛja* (to emit, create). By the rule *vibhāṣā sṛjidṛśoḥ*, there is optionally the substitution of *sa* for *sṛ* before the *thali* affix: *sasṛjitha*. *sasraṣṭa*. *sraṣṭā*. *srakṣyati*. By the rule *sṛjidṛśor jhaly am akiti*, the augment *am* is added before an affix beginning with a *jhal* consonant that does not have *k* or *it* as an indicatory letter: *sṛjet*. *sṛjyāt*. *asrākṣīt*. 1416. *ṭumasjo* (to cleanse, purify).

*majjati* (he sinks). *mamajja* (he sank). By the rule *masjinaśor jhali*, the augment *num* is added; it should be stated that *num* is placed before the final letter of the root *masj*. There is the elision of the first consonant of the conjunct (*saṃyogādilopa*). *mamaṅktha* / *mamajjitha* (you sank). *maṅktā* (he will sink). *maṅkṣyati* (he will sink). *amāṅkṣīt* / *amāṅktām* / *amāṅkṣuḥ* (he sank, they two sank, they sank). 1417. *ruj* in the sense of breaking. *roktā* (he will break). *rokṣyati* (he will break). *araukṣīt* / *arauktām* (he broke, they two broke). 1418. *bhuja* in the sense of crookedness. Like *ruj*. 1419. *chup* in the sense of touching. *choptā* (he will touch). *acchaupsīt* (he touched). 1420. *ruśa* and 1421. *riśa* in the sense of injury.

The two ending in *tālavya* (palatals): *roṣṭā*, *rokṣyati*; *reṣṭā*, *rekṣyati*. 1422. *liś* in the sense of going: *alikṣat*. 1423. *spṛś* in the sense of touching: *spraṣṭā*, *sparṣṭā*; *sprakṣyati*, *sparkṣyati*; *asprākṣīt*, *aspārkṣīt*, *aspṛkṣat*. 1424. *viccha* in the sense of going: [by *gupū-dhūpa-ādayaḥ*] the suffix *āya* is added; optionally before an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix: *vicchāyati*; *vicchāyāṃcakāra*; *viviccha*. 1425. *viś* in the sense of entering: *viśati*; *veṣṭā*. 1426. *mṛś* in the sense of touching/grasping.

*Āmarśanam* means touching. [The forms] *amrākṣīt*, *amārkṣīt*, and *amṛkṣat* [are derived from the root *mṛj*]. 1427. *ṇud* in the sense of impelling. This is read again for the purpose of ensuring the *parasmaipada* even when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. 1428. *ṣadḷ* in the senses of falling apart, going, and sinking. Forms such as *sīdati* etc., follow the *bhūvādigaṇa*. Its inclusion here is for the purpose of making the *num* augment optional. [Thus we have] *sīdati*, *sīdantī*. However, its reading in the *jvalādigaṇa* is for the purpose of forming the causative (*ṇic*). [Furthermore, it serves] for the sake of accentuation: in the *śap* [present tense], it is *anudātta*; in the *śa* [perfect tense], it is *udātta*. 1429. *śadḷ* in the sense of cutting off.
The repetition [of the root] is solely for the sake of the *svarita* accent; however, there is no [augment] *śatṛ*, because the *ātmanepada* is prescribed by the rule "śadeḥ śitaḥ" (Pāṇini 3.1.60).

Now, six [roots] have the *svarita* accent: 1430 √mil (in the sense of meeting) and √mil (in the sense of joining); the repetition of that which was previously recited is for the purpose of the *taṅ* (*ātmanepada*) endings when the action benefits the agent. [Examples: *milati*, *milate*; *mimela*, *mimile*. 1431 √mucḷ (in the sense of releasing). [Rule SK 2542: *śe mucādīnām* (Pāṇini 7.1.59).

[The forms] *muñcet*, *muñcati*, *muñcate*, *moktā*, *mucyāt*, *mukṣīṣṭa*, *amucat*, *amukta*, *amukṣātām* [are derived from the root *muc*]. 1432. *lukḷ* in the sense of cutting: *lumpati*, *lumpate*, *alupat*, *alupta*. 1433. *vidḷ* in the sense of obtaining: *vindati*, *vindate*, *viveda*, *vivide*. According to the opinion of Vyāghrabhūti and others, this [root] is *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*): *veditā*. According to the opinion of the Bhāṣya and others, it is *aniṭ* (not taking *iṭ*): *vettā*. [From the same root with the prefix *pari-*: *parivettā*. [The prefix] *pari-* is used in the sense of exclusion (*varjana*).

The meaning is that he obtained wives and fires, having abandoned his elder [brother]. [The suffixes] *tṛn* and *tṛc* [are applied]. 1434. *lip* (to smear); "smearing" means growth. [He] smears (*limpati*), [he] smears himself (*limpate*). [The agentive form is] *leptā*. By the rule *lipisici...* [the suffix] *aṅ* is applied. But in the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) voice, there is an option: *alipat*, *alipata*, or *alipta*. 1435. *ṣic* (to pour); [he] pours (*siñcati*), [he] pours for himself (*siñcate*). *asicat*, *asicata*, *asikta*. [With the prefix *abhi*: he] consecrates (*abhiṣiñcati*). *abhyaṣiñcat*, *abhiṣiṣeca*.

Now follow three roots that take the *parasmaipada* endings. 1436. *kṛtī* (meaning "to cut"): *kṛntati*, *cakarta*, *kartitā*, *kartiṣyati*, *kartsyati*, *akartīt*. 1437. *khid* (meaning "to afflict"): *khindati*, *cikheda*, *khettā*. This root is also used in the sense of "dejection" (*dainya*) in the *divādi* and *rudhādi* classes. 1438. *piś* (meaning "to form parts" or "to fashion"): *piṃśati*, *peśitā*. This root is also used in the sense of "illuminating. [End of section: "May Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms. The *muc*-class and the *tud*-class have been completed. Thus ends the *tudādayaḥ*.
The *rudh*-class [of roots] ending in verbal suffixes (tiṅanta). 47.
1439 *rudhir* in the sense of obstructing; nine [roots] are svarita-accented, and [the rest] are udātta-accented. (SK 2543) *śnam* is added after the roots beginning with *rudh*. (A 3.1.78)

This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the *śap* suffix. Because it is marked with the *mit* designation, it follows after the final vowel. Due to its obligatory nature (*nityatva*), it overrides the *guṇa* substitution. Thus: *ruṇaddhi*. In the case of *ruṇatsi*, there is the elision of the *a* of *śnas* (*allopaḥ*). Since the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* (*ṇatva*) is considered non-existent (*asiddha*), the *anusvāra* undergoes the *parasavarṇa* substitution. Because that [substitution] is also considered non-existent, the substitution of *ṇ* does not occur by the rule "not at the end of a word" (*na padānta...*), and thus the elision of the *a* is not treated as *sthānivadbhāva* (as if it were the original). Hence: *rundhaḥ*; *rundhanti*. In the middle voice: *rundhe*. Future: *roddhā*. Future: *rotsyati*. Imperative: *ruṇaddhu*. Imperative: *rundhāt*. Imperative: *rundhi*. Imperative: *ruṇadhāni*. Imperative: *ruṇadhai*. Aorist: *aruṇat*.

*arundhām*, *aruṇat*, *aruṇaḥ*, *aruṇadham*, *arudhat*, *arautsīt*, *aruddha*. 1440 *bhidir* (to split): *bhinakti*, *bhinte*, *bhettā*, *bhetsyati*, *bhetsyate*, *abhinat*, *abhintām*, *abhinadam*, *abhinta*, *abhidat*, *abhaitsīt*, *abhitta*. 1441 *chidir* (to cut/divide): *acchidat*, *acchaitsīt*, *acchitta*. 1442 *ricir* (to empty/separate): *riṇakti*, *riṅkte*, *rireca*, *ririce*.

*rekte*, *ariṇak*, *aricat*, *araikṣīt*, *arita*. 1443. *vicir* in the sense of separation: *vinakti*, *viṅkte*. 1444. *kṣudir* in the sense of crushing: *kṣuṇatti*, *kṣunte*; future *kṣottā*; aorist *akṣudat*, *akṣautsīt*, *akṣutta*. 1445. *yujir* in the sense of joining: future *yoktā*. 1446. *ucchṛdir* in the senses of shining and playing: present *chṛṇatti*, *chṛnte*; perfect *caccharda* (with optional *iṭ* by the rule *sesici*); *cacchṛdiṣe*, *cacchṛtse*; future *charditā*, *chardiṣyati*, *chatsyati*.

*acchṛdat*, *acchardīt*, *acchardiṣṭa*. 1447. *utṛdī* in the sense of injury and disregard. Forms such as *tṛṇatti* follow the pattern of *chṛṇatti*. 1448. *kṛtī* in the sense of enveloping; it takes the *parasmaipada* endings. *kṛṇatti*; in the *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes, it follows the *tud*-class. 1449. *ñi indhī* in the sense of flaming; these three take the *ātmanepada* endings. According to Pāṇini 6.4.23, *śnān nalopaḥ*, there is elision of the *n* of the *śnā* affix.

There is elision of the *n* of the suffix *śna*. There is elision of the vowel of *śnas*. [Examples: *indhe*, *hantse*, *indhitā*, *inadhai*, *aindha*, *aindhāḥ*. 1450. *khid* in the sense of dejection: *khinte*, *khettā*. 1451. *vid* in the sense of deliberation: *vinte*, *vettā*.

Now, the roots ending in *parasmaipada* (active voice): 1452. *śiṣḷ* (to distinguish, leave as a remainder). *śinaṣṭi* (he leaves/teaches). *śiṃṣṭaḥ* (they two leave). *śiṃñanti* (they leave). *śiśeṣitha* (you left—thematic perfect). *śeṣṭā* (he will leave—future). *śekṣyati* (he will leave—periphrastic future). In the imperative, *hi* is replaced by *dhi*. By the rule of *jaśtva*, *ṣ* becomes *ḍ*. By *ṣṭutva*, *d* becomes *ṭ*. Then, by the rule *jharo jhari savarṇe*, there is optionally the elision (*lopa*) of *ḍ*. Subsequently, the *anusvāra* and its corresponding *parasavarṇa* are applied. Thus: *śiṇḍhi* or *śiṇḍḍhi*. *śinaṣāṇi* (let me leave—first person singular imperative). *aśinaṭ* (he left—imperfect). Because it is marked with *ḷ* and *it*, the suffix *aṅ* is used: *aśiṣat* (he left—imperfect with *aṅ*). 1453. *piṣḷ* (to grind, crush). It is conjugated like *śiṣḷ*: *pinaṣṭi* (he grinds). 1454. *bhañjo* (to break, crush). *bhanakti* (he breaks). *babhañjitha* (you broke—thematic perfect).

*babhaṅktha*, *bhaṅktā*. 1455. *bhuja* in the senses of protecting and eating: *bhunakti*, *bhoktā*, *bhokṣyati*, *abhunak*. 1456. *tṛha*, 1457. *hiṃsi* in the sense of injuring. [By rule A 7.3.92: *tṛṇaha* becomes *im*.

When the suffix *śnam* is applied to the root *tṛh*, the augment *ś* is added before a *pit* suffix beginning with a consonant. Thus: *tṛṇeḍhi*, *tṛṇḍhaḥ*, *tatarha*, *tarhitā*, *atṛṇeṭ*. The root *hiṃs* (to injure): *hinasti*, *jihiṃsa*, *hiṃsitā*. 1458. The root *undī* (in moistening): *unatti*, *untaḥ*, *undanti*; *undāñcakāra*; *aunat*, *auntām*, *aundan*; *aunaḥ*, *aunat*, *aunadam*. 1459. The root *añjū* (in manifestation, smearing, luster, and motion):
*anakti*, *aṅktaḥ*, *añjanti*; *ānañja*, *ānañjitha*, *ānaṅktha*; *aṅktā*, *añjitā*; *aṅgdhi*; *anajāni*; *ānak*.

SK 2546: *añjeḥ sici* (A 7.2.71). After the root *añj*, the augment *iṭ* is obligatory before the suffix *sic*. Example: *āñjīt*. 1460. *tañcū* in the sense of contraction (*saṅkocana*). Present: *tanakti*. Future: *taṅktā* or *tañcitā*. 1461. *ovijī* in the senses of fear and trembling (*bhayacalana*). Present: *vinakti*, *viṅktaḥ*. By the rule *vija iṭ* [Vārttika], the marker *ṅ* is applied [to the root], resulting in the form *vivijitha*. Future: *vijitā*. Aorist: *avinak* or *avijīt*. 1462. *vṛjī* in the sense of avoiding or excluding (*varjana*). Present: *vṛṇakti*. Future: *varjitā*. 1463. *pṛcī* in the sense of contact (*saṃparka*). Present: *pṛṇakti*. Perfect: *paparca*. Thus ends the section on the *rudhādi* roots.
The *tan*-class and others [of roots] belong to the section on verbal suffixes (*tiṅanta*). 48.

Now, there are seven roots with the svarita accent: 1464. *tanu* (to extend). By the rule *tanādikṛñbhya uḥ*, the suffix *u* is added: *tanoti*, *tanvaḥ*, *tanuvaḥ*; *tanute*. [Perfect: *tatāna*, *tene*. [Vedic forms: *tanu*, *atanīt*, *atānīt*. [By the rule *tanādibhyas tathāsoḥ* (A 2.4.79), the substitution of *iṭ* for *th* and *as* occurs.]

There may be the elision (*luk*) of *sic* after roots beginning with *tan*, etc., when followed by *tathās*. Because of its association (*sāhacarya*) with *thās*, the singular form of the suffix *ta* is understood here; therefore, it does not apply in this case: *yūyam ataniṣṭa*. By the rule "anudāttopadeśa... (Pāṇini 6.4.37), there is the elision of the nasal. In the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) voice: *atata*, *ataniṣṭa*, *atathāḥ*, *ataniṣṭhāḥ*. 1465. The root *ṣaṇu* (in the sense of giving): *sanoti*, *sanute*. By the rule "ye vibhāṣā" (Pāṇini 6.4.44), [the substitution of *ī* for *ya* is optional]: *sāyāt*, *sanyāt*. By the rule "janasana... (Pāṇini 6.4.42), there is the substitution of *ā* [for the final vowel]: *asāta*, *asaniṣṭa*, *asāthāḥ*, *asaniṣṭhāḥ*.

1466. *kṣaṇu* in the sense of injury. *kṣaṇoti*; [aorist] *akṣata*, *akṣaṇiṣṭa*; [perfect] *akṣathāḥ*, *akṣaṇiṣṭhāḥ*. 1467. *kṣiṇu* also [in the sense of injury]. The *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel caused by the suffix *u* does not take place, according to Ātreya and others, on the principle that "a rule conditioned by a technical designation (*saṃjñā*) is not necessarily permanent. Others hold that it certainly does take place. [Present] *kṣiṇoti*, *kṣeṇoti*; [future] *kṣeṇitāsi*, *kṣeṇitāse*; [aorist] *akṣeṇīt*, *akṣita*, *akṣeṇiṣṭa*. 1468. *ṛṇu* in the sense of motion. [Present] *ṛṇoti*, *arṇoti*; [present dual] *arṇutaḥ*; [present plural] *arṇvanti*; [perfect] *ānarṇa*.
*ānṛṇe*, *arṇitāsi*, *ārṇīt*, *ārta*, *ārṇiṣṭa*, *ārthāḥ*, *ārṇiṣṭhāḥ*. 1469. *tṛṇu* (to eat): *tṛṇoti*, *tarṇoti*, *tṛṇute*, *tarṇute*. 1470. *ghṛṇu* (to shine): *jagharṇa*, *jaghṛṇe*.

Now, there are two [roots] with anudātta [indicatory vowel]. 1471. *vanu* in the sense of "begging": *vanute*, *vavane*. According to the opinion of Candra, it is parasmaipada: *vanoti*, *vavāna*. 1472. *manu* in the sense of "perceiving": *manute*, *mene*. 1473. *ḍukṛñ* in the sense of "making": *karoti*. [In *kurutaḥ*,] *u* is substituted for the *a* before a sārvadhātuka suffix; then *yaṇ* [substitution of *u* for *u*] occurs. There is no lengthening by the rule *na bhakurchurām* [Pāṇini 7.3.59]. [Thus: *kurvanti*. [By the rule] *nityaṃ karoteḥ* (A 6.4.108).

The *u* of the suffix following the root *kṛ* is always elided when *m* or *v* follow: *kurvaḥ*, *kurmaḥ*; *cakartha*, *cakṛva*, *cakṛṣe*; *kartā*; *kariṣyati*. By *ye ca* (A 6.4.109), there is elision of the *ṛ* of *kṛ* before a suffix beginning with *y*: *kuryāt*. In the sense of benediction (*āśis*): *kriyāt*, *kṛṣīṣṭa*. *akārṣīt*. In the absence of *luk* by *tanādibhyaḥ* (A 6.4.43), there is elision of *sic* by *hrasvād aṅgāt* (A 8.2.27): *akṛta*, *akṛthāḥ*.

SK 2550: *saṃ* and *pari* are prefixed to the root *kṛ* when it means "adornment" (A 6.1.137). SK 2551: Also when it means "gathering together" (A 6.1.138). The augment *suṭ* is added to the root *kṛ* preceded by *saṃ* and *pari* when the meaning is "adornment" or "forming a group. *saṃskaroti*: the meaning is "he adorns. *saṃskurvanti*: the meaning is "they gather together. In some cases, *saṃ* is prefixed with *suṭ* even when it does not mean "adornment," as evidenced by the rule *saṃskṛtaṃ bhakṣāḥ* ("prepared food"). By the rule *parinivibhyaḥ*, the sibilant becomes *ṣ*. *pariṣkaroti*. According to the rule *sivādīnāṃ vā*, there is optionally no change: *paryaṣkārṣīt* or *paryaskārṣīt*.
SK 2552: After *upa*, [the suffix *kha* is applied] in the sense of refinement (*pratiyatna*), transformation (*vaikṛta*), and ellipsis (*vākyādhyāhāra*). (A 6.1.139)

The augment *suṭ* is added after the prefix *upa* before the root *kṛ*, in these senses, as well as in the two senses previously mentioned: *pratiyatna* (the imparting of a quality), *vaikṛta* (a transformation, i.e., that which is changed), and *vākyādhyāhāra* (the supplying of an ellipsis, i.e., the filling of a required part of a sentence). *Upaskṛtā kanyā*: "A girl adorned. The meaning is "decorated. *Upaskṛtā brāhmaṇāḥ*: "The Brahmins assembled. The meaning is "gathered together. *Edho dakasyopaskurute*: "The fuel improves the water. The meaning is "it imparts a quality [to it]. *Upaskṛtaṃ bhuṅkte*: "He eats prepared food. The meaning is "transformed [food]. *Upaskṛtaṃ brūte*: "He speaks with an ellipsis. The meaning is "he speaks by supplying the missing part of the sentence."

SK 2553: *suṭ* is placed before *kāt* (A 6.1.135). It has been stated that this occurs even when there is an intervention by *aṭ* or the reduplication (*abhyāsa*). Examples include *saṃcaskāra*. However, the rule "before *kā*" and so forth has been rejected in the *Bhāṣya*. For instance: first, the root is joined with the prefix (*upasarga*); because it is *antaraṅga*, *suṭ* is applied; then follows reduplication. Thus, in *saṃcaskaratuḥ*, the rule *ṛtaś ca saṃyogādeḥ* provides for *guṇa*. Furthermore, regarding the rules *kṛsṛbhṛ-* and *ṛto bhāradvājasya*, it must be stated that the prohibition applies to *kṛñ* when *suṭ* is present. Consequently, the augment *iṭ* occurs after [the root] followed by *suṭ*: *saṃcaskaritha*, *saṃcaskariva*.

In the rule *guṇortti*, the word *nityam* (always) is carried over from the rule *nityaṃ chandasi*. Therefore, by implication, there is no *guṇa* substitution for that [root] which always begins with a consonant cluster (*saṃyoga*) when followed by *suṭ*; as in *saṃskriyāt*. Furthermore, by the rule *ṛtaś ca saṃyogādeḥ*, there is no *iṭ* augment in the case of the suffixes *liṅ* and *sic*; this is because, carrying over the word *upadeśe* from the rule *ekāca upadeśe*, the interpretation is "that which begins with a consonant cluster in its original enunciation" (*upadeśe*). Thus: *saṃskṛṣīṣṭa*, *samaskṛta*, *samaskṛṣātām*. These are the roots beginning with *tan*.
The section on verbal roots beginning with *kry* (the tenth class) consists of those ending in verbal suffixes (*tiṅanta*). 49.

1474. *ḍukrīñ* [is used] in the sense of "exchanging goods" (*dravyavinimaya*). By A 3.1.81, *kryādibhyaḥ śnā*, the suffix *śnā* is applied: *krīṇāti*. By the rule *ī halyaghoḥ*, the vowel *ī* is substituted [for the radical *i*] before endings beginning with *haL* that do not begin with *ghu*: *krīṇītaḥ*. Because this substitution of *ī* is subsequent (*paratva*), obligatory (*nityatva*), and internal (*antaraṅgatva*), it takes precedence; thus, the substitution of *ad* for *jhi* occurs first. Then, by the rule *śnābhyastayoḥ*, there is elision (*allopa*) of the *ā* of *śnā*. [The forms are: *krīṇanti*; *krīṇīte*, *krīṇāte*, *krīṇate*. Periphrastic perfect: *cikrāya*; *cikriyatuḥ*; *cikriyitha* or *cekretha*; *cikriyiva*; *cikriyiṣe*. Future: *kretā*; *kreṣyati*. Precative (āśīrliṅ): *krīyāt*; *kreṣīṣṭa*. Aorist: *akraiṣīt*; *akreṣṭa*.

1475. *Prīñ* in the sense of satisfying and longing; longing (*kānti*) means desire. *Prīṇāti*, *prīṇīte*. 1476. *Śrīñ* in the sense of cooking. 1477. *Mīñ* in the sense of injury. [The forms] *hinu*, *mīnā*, *pramīṇāti*, *pramīṇītaḥ* occur. By the rule *mīnātiminoti* etc., there is substitution of *ā* in place of the root vowel when an affix beginning with *ej* follows. *Mamau*, *mimyatuḥ*, *mamitha*, *mamātha*, *mimye*. *Mātā*, *māsyati*, *mīyāt*, *māsīṣṭa*, *amāsīt*, *amāsiṣṭām*, *amāsta*. 1478. *Ṣiñ* in the sense of binding. *Sinīte*, *siṣāya*, *siṣye*, *setā*. 1479. *Skuñ* in the sense of cutting or tearing.
After the roots *stambh*, *stumbh*, *skambh*, *skumbh*, and *skuñ*, the suffix *śnu* is also applied [in addition to *śnā*].

And [the suffix] *śnā* [is applied after the root *sku*]: *skunoti*, *skunute*; *skunāti*, *skunīte*; *cuskāva*, *cuskave*; *skotā*; *askauṣīt*, *askoṣṭa*. The four roots beginning with *stambh* are Vedic (sautra). Some say that all of them have the meaning "to obstruct. Mādhava, however, says that the first and third have the meaning "to support," the second has the meaning "to extract," and the fourth has the meaning "to hold. All of them take the *parasmaipada* endings. [By the rule] *nalopaḥ*, [we have] *viṣṭabhnoti*, *viṣṭabhnāti*; *avaṣṭabhnoti*, *avaṣṭabhnāti*.

*avataṣṭambha*; [from the roots] *jṝ* and *stambh*, the suffix *aṅ* is optionally applied: *vyaṣṭabhat* or *vyaṣṭambhīt*. [In the present tense: *stubhnoti* or *stubhnāti*. SK 2556: *ve skabhnāter nityam* (A 8.3.77). After the prefix *vi-*, the *s-* of the root *skabh* is necessarily changed to *ṣ-*. Thus: *viṣkabhnoti* or *viṣkabhnāti*. [Similarly: *skubhnoti* or *skubhnāti*.

SK 2557: *halaḥ śnaḥ śānaj jhau* (A 3.1.83). After a consonant, the substitute *śānac* shall take the place of *śna* when *jh* follows. *stabhāna*, *stubhāna*, *skabhāna*, *skubhāna*; alternatively, *stabhnuhi*, etc. 1480. *yuñ* in the sense of binding. *yunāti*, *yunīte*. Future: *yotā*. 1481. *knūñ* in the sense of sounding. *knūnāti*, *knūnīte*. Future: *knavitā*. 1482. *drūñ* in the sense of injuring. *drūṇāti*, *drūṇīte*. 1483. *pūñ* in the sense of purifying. SK 2558: *pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ* (A 7.3.80). [The short vowel is substituted for the radical vowel of roots beginning with *pv*.]

With the suffix *śit* (indicating the *ātmanepada*), [the roots] *pūñ* and *māñ* take the forms *punāti*, *punīte*, *pavitā*. 1484. *lūñ* in the sense of cutting: *lunāti*, *lunīte*. 1485. *stṝñ* in the sense of covering: *stṛṇāti*, *stṛṇīte*; *tastāra*, *tastaratuḥ*; *staritā*, *starītā*; *stṛṇīyāt*, *stṛṇīta*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), [the form is] *stīryāt*. By the rule *liṅsicoḥ* (Pāṇini 1.2.11), there is optionally *iṭ*; however, in the benedictive, by the rule *vṝto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.39), the long vowel does not occur for *iṭ* in the benedictive. Thus: *stariṣīṣṭa*. By the rule *uś ca* (Pāṇini 1.2.12), there is *kittva* (the *sic* suffix is treated as having the *kit* marker). Thus: *stīrṣīṣṭa*. And by the rule *sici ca parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.40), there is no lengthening [of the vowel] in the *parasmaipada* forms.

*astārīt*, *astāriṣṭām*, *astariṣṭa*, *astarīṣṭa*, *astīrṣṭa*. 1486. *kṝñ* in the sense of harming: *kṛṇāti*, *kṛṇīte*; *cakāra*, *cakare*. 1487. *vṛñ* in the sense of choosing: *vṛṇāti*, *vṛṇīte*; *vavāra*, *vavare*; *varitā*, *varītā*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), by the rule *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya vūryāt*: *variṣīṣṭa*, *vūrṣīṣṭa*. *avārīt*, *avāriṣṭām*; *avariṣṭa*, *avarīṣṭa*, *avūrṣṭa*. 1488. *dhūñ* in the sense of shaking: *dhotā*, *dhavitā*. By the rule *stusudhūmbhyaḥ...* [the augment *iṭ* is applied]: *adhāvīt*; *adhaviṣṭa*, *adhoṣṭa*.

Now follow the roots ending in *ṝ* that take the *parasmaipada* endings. 1489. *śṝ* in the sense of "injuring. By the rule *śṝdṝprāṃ hrasvo vā*, there is optionally a short vowel; in the case of the short vowel, *yaṇ* substitution occurs. Otherwise, by the rule *ṛcchaty ṝtām*, there is *guṇa*. [The forms are] *śaśratuḥ* (with short vowel) and *śaśaratuḥ* (with *guṇa*). Regarding the prohibition [of *guṇa*] by the rule *śryukaḥ kiti*, it is set aside by the restriction of the *krādi* group. [The form is] *śaśariva*. [The aorist form is] *aśāriṣṭām*. 1490. *pṝ* in the senses of "protecting" and "filling. [The forms are] *papratuḥ* and *paparatuḥ*. In the benedictive: *pūryāt*. 1491. *vṝ* in the sense of "choosing"; some say "supporting. 1492. *bhṝ* in the sense of "threatening."

Some [read] *bhṛ* as well. 1493 *mṛ* in the sense of injury: *mṛṇāti*, *mamāra*. 1494 *dṛ* in the sense of tearing apart: *dadaratuḥ*, *dadratuḥ*. 1495 *jṛ* in the sense of decay of age; some read *jhṛ*, others *dhṛ*. 1496 *nṛ* in the sense of leading. 1497 *kṛ* in the sense of injury. 1498 *ṛ* in the sense of motion: *ṛṇāti*; *arāṃcakāra*; *aritā*, *arītā*; *ārṇāt*, *ārṇītām*; *īryāt*; *ārīt*, *āriṣṭām*. 1499 *gṛ* in the sense of sound. 1500 *jyā* in the sense of decay of age; [subject to] *grahijyā-* [substitution]; by *halaḥ* (A 6.4.2).

When a *saṃprasāraṇa* follows a consonant (*hal*) after a member of the verbal base (*aṅga*), there shall be lengthening of that base ending in such a *saṃprasāraṇa*. Once the lengthening has been applied, the rule "the short vowel for roots beginning with *pv*" (*pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ*) applies. Thus: *jināti*, *jijyau*, *jijyatuḥ*. 1501. *rī* (to go, to seek). *Reṣaṇa* means the howling of a wolf. 1502. *lī* (to cling, to adhere). Regarding the root *lī*, there is optionally an *ā*-substitution (*ātva*) when an affix marked with *eṅ* follows, according to the rule *vibhāṣā līyateḥ*. Thus: *lalau* or *lilāya*; *lātā* or *letā*. 1503. *blī* (to choose). *blināti*. 1504. *plī* (to go). [End of section. The roots beginning with *lv* have been concluded.

Some say that *pv* and others [also belong here]. 1507. *kṣī* in the sense of "injury. In these three, there is shortening; however, according to some, it does not occur. 1508. *jñā* in the sense of "cognition. In the forms *jānāti*, *jānīte*, etc., [the root vowel is replaced by] *jā* because of *jñā* and *jan*. Due to the force of the explicit mention of the long vowel (*dīrgha*), there is no shortening. 1509. *bandh* in the sense of "binding. [Present: *badhnāti*; [Perfect: *babandha*; [Aorist 2nd sg. Parasmaipada: *babandhitha*; [Aorist 1st du. Parasmaipada: *bandhā*; [Aorist 1st pl. Parasmaipada: *bandhāma*; [Future: *bhantsyati*; [Imperative: *badhāna*; [Aorist 3rd sg. Parasmaipada: *abhāntsīt*. Because of the rule *pūrvatrāsiddham*, the elision of *sic* (by *jhalo jhali*) occurs before the substitution of *bhaṣ* (i.e., *dh* for *t*).

By virtue of the rule regarding the characteristics of suffixes (*pratyayalakṣaṇa*), the substitution of *bhaṣ* does not occur based on the suffix beginning with *s*, because the elision of the *sic* suffix is considered non-existent (*asiddha*) for the purpose of applying the rule concerning the characteristics of suffixes. Examples: *abāndhām*, *abhāntsuḥ*. 1510. The root *vṛṅ* (to choose/share). * vṛṇīte* * vavre* * vavṛṣe*, *vavṛḍhve* * varitā*, *varītā* * avariṣṭa*, *avarīṣṭa* * avṛta* 1511. The root *śranth* (in the senses of loosening and rejoicing). From here onwards, the roots take the *parasmaipada* terminations. * śrathnāti*

Haradatta and others maintain that in the alternative view where the suffix is *kitt*, the substitution of *et* (for *i*) and the elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsa-lopa*) must also be stated here; thus [the forms] are *śrethatuḥ* and *śrethuḥ*. According to the opinion of Sudhākara, this *kittva* applies even when the suffix is *pit*; hence [the form] is *śrethitha*. Even in this view, in the case of the *ṇal* suffix, [the form] is *śaśrātha*. But in the first person singular (*uttama*), Mādhava says it is *śaśrātha* or *śaśratha*; the source for this must be sought. 1512. *mantha* in the sense of churning. 1513. *śrantha* and 1514. *grantha* in the sense of stringing together or composing.

The repetition [of the root] is due to a difference in meaning; however, its form has already been stated. 1515. *kuntha* in the sense of "to join together"; some say in the sense of "to afflict. One conjugates: *kuthnāti*, *cukuntha*. Durga says *kutheti*; [another form is] *cukotha*. 1516. *mṛda* in the sense of "to crush. One conjugates: *mṛdgāti*, *mṛdāna*. 1517. *mṛḍa* also [in this sense]. This [root] also means "to delight. There is the substitution of *ṣṭu*. One conjugates: *mṛḍṇāti*. 1518. *gudha* in the sense of "anger. One conjugates: *gudhnāti*. 1519. *kuṣa* in the sense of "extracting. One conjugates: *kuṣṇāti*. The future participle is *koṣitā*.

SK 2560 *niraḥ kuṣaḥ* (A 7.2.46): After the prefix *nir*, the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied to a following *ārdhadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant (*val*) after the root *kuṣ*. [Examples: *niṣkoṣitā* / *niṣkoṣṭā*; *nirakoṣīt* / *nirakukṣat*. 1520 *kṣubha* in the sense of "shaking" or "agitating": In the list of *kṣubhnādi* words, we have *kṣubhnāti*, *kṣubhnītaḥ*, *kṣobhitā*, *kṣubhāna*. 1521–1522 *ṇabha* and *tubha* in the sense of "injury": With the suffix *śap*, we have *nabhnāti* and *tubhnāti*; with *śap*, *nabhate* and *tobhate*; with *śyan*, *nabhyati* and *tubhyati*. 1523 *kliśū* in the sense of "afflicting": By the rule *śād* [A 8.2.36], there is a prohibition of the substitution of *ścutva* (the change of *ś* to *ṣ*).

*kliśnāti* / *kleśitā* / *kleṣṭā* / *akleśīt* / *aklikṣat* / 1524 *aśa* (to eat): *aśnāti* / *āśa* / 1525 *udhrasa* (to glean): the letter *u* is an *it*. *dhrasnāti*; some say the letter *u* is part of the verbal root (*dhātu*). *udhrasāṃcakāra* / 1526 *iṣa* (in the sense of repetition): repetition (*paunaḥpunya*) or intensity (*bhṛśārtha*) is "repeated action" (*ābhīkṣṇya*). *iṣṇāti*.

Regarding the rule *tīṣasaha-* (Pāṇini 7.2.48), they say that because of its association (*sāhacarya*) with the root *sah*, only the root *iṣ* belonging to the *tud*-class (which takes the suffix *ak*), namely *iṣ* in the sense of "desiring," is understood there, and not the roots *iṣ* ("to go") or *iṣṇāti*. Thus, [the form] is *eṣitā*. However, in reality, the optional insertion of the augment *iṭ* is appropriate for *iṣṇāti* as well. Accordingly, the Vārttika states: "There is a prohibition [of the augment *iṭ*] after the suffix *śyan* when the root *iṣ* ends in *t*. 1527. *viṣ* (in the sense of) separation: *viṣṇāti*; [future] *veṣṭā*. 1528. *praṣu* and 1529. *pluṣa* (in the senses of) unctuousness, service, and filling: *pruṣṇāti*; *pluṣṇāti*.

1530 *puṣ* in the sense of nourishing (*puṣṭi*): *poṣitā*. 1531 *muṣ* in the sense of stealing (*steya*): *moṣitā*. 1532 *khac* in the sense of the manifestation of what has come into being (*bhūtaprādurbhāva*). "Manifestation of what has come into being" means arising after having transcended [the previous state]. *khacñāti*. Some say that this [root] ends in *-vān*. [This is governed by] Pāṇini 6.4.19: *cch-ṭ-ś-ṣ-ṭu-raḥ ṣ-ṭu-raḥ* (and when a nasal follows).

In place of *cha* and *va* followed by *tuka*, the substitutes *śa* and *ūṭh* respectively occur before an affix beginning with a nasal (*anunāsika*) or a consonant (*jhal*) that has *k* or *ṅ* as an indicatory letter (*kit/ṅit*). [Examples: *khauṇāti*, *cakhāva*, *khavitā*. Because *uṭh* is applied later than *śānac*, the root no longer ends in a consonant; therefore, *śānac* does not apply. 1534. *graha* (to seize). It is marked with the *svarita* accent. [By *grahijyā-* (Pāṇini 6.1.16), the *samprasāraṇa* occurs. *gṛhṇāti*, *gṛhṇīte*. SK 2562: *graho 'liṭi dīrghaḥ* (A 7.2.37): In the case of the root *grah*, there is lengthening of the vowel before the *liṭ* affixes, except for those that are *liṭ*. [Example: *jagrāha*.]

The long vowel substitute shall apply to the augment *iṭ* prescribed after the root *grah*, provided it consists of a single vowel, but not when the *liṭ* (perfect) suffix follows. [Examples: *grahītā* (he will seize). However, in the *liṭ*, [it is] *jagrahitha* (you seized). [Optative: *gṛhyāt* (may he seize); *grahīṣīṣṭa* (may he be about to seize). By the rule "roots ending in *h*, *m*, or *y*" (*hmyanta-*) there is no *vṛddhi* [substitution]. [Aorist: *agrahīt* (he seized); *agrrahīṣṭām* (they two seized); *agrahīṣṭa* (he seized); *agrahīṣātām* (they two seized); *agrahīṣata* (they all seized). Thus end the roots beginning with *kry*.
The section on the *cur*-class [of roots] ending in verbal suffixes (tiṅanta). 50.

SK 2563: *satyāpapāśarūpavīṇātūlaślokasenālomatvacavarmavarṇacūrṇacurādibhyo ṇic* (A 3.1.25). The suffix *ṇic* shall be applied after these [words]. Since the formation would already be established by the rule "after nominal stems ending in *cūrṇa*, in the sense of verbal activity" (*prātipadikād dhātvarthe*), their inclusion here is for the sake of elaboration (*prapañca*). However, in the case of the *cur*-group and others, it occurs in its own meaning (*svārthe*). By the rule *pugantalaghūpadhasya guṇaḥ*, there is *guṇa*; by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ*, there is the status of being a verbal root (*dhātutva*); then *tiP*, *śap*, and so on; and finally *guṇa* and *āy-ādeśa*. Thus: *corayati*. SK 2564: *ṇicaś ca* (A 1.3.74). [The *ātmanepada* endings are used] also after a stem ending in *ṇic*.

The *ātmanepada* ending shall occur after a root with the causative suffix (*ṇic*) when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. Examples: *corayate*, *corayāmāsa*, *corayitā*, *coryāt*, *corayiṣīṣṭa*. By the rule *ṇi-śri-*, the suffix *caṅ* is applied [in the aorist]. By the rule *ṇau caṅi*, there is shortening of the penultimate vowel. Then reduplication occurs. By the rule *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*, all consonants except the first are elided. By the rule *dīrgho laghoḥ*, the long vowel is substituted for the reduplicated syllable. Thus: *acūcurat*, *acūcurata*. 1536. The root *cit* (meaning "to remember") forms *cintayati*. The aorist form is *acicintat*. The form *cinteti* is taught; the inclusion of the *it*-marker (*idit*) is an indication that the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is optional in this case.

Therefore, in forms such as *cintyāt* (from the root *cit*) and *cintyate*, there is no elision of the nasal (*n*). One says *cintati* and *cintet*. Some maintain that this is an indicator (*jñāpaka*) that depends on the general rule (*sāmānya*). Others hold that it depends on a specific rule (*viśeṣa*), because in the section beginning with *ata ekahal-* (Pāṇini 6.4.120), the author of the Vṛtti cited *jagāṇa* and *jagaṇatuḥ* as examples. For this very reason, the rule *ādhṛṣād vā* (Pāṇini 6.1.15) is not rendered redundant. 1537. *yatṛ* in the sense of contraction: *yantrayati*; one may also read *yantre*.

As for what Mādhava stated—that [the root *yantr*] is derived from the addition of the marker *idit*—that is to be reconsidered. The same applies to *kudr*, *trim*, and *matri*. 1538. *sphuḍi* (in the sense of joking): *sphuṇḍayati*. Because of the addition of the marker *idit*, [it also takes the form] *sphuṇḍati*. *Sphuṭī* is an alternative reading; [from this, one forms] *sphuṇḍayati*. 1539. *lakṣa* (in the senses of seeing and marking). 1540. *kudri* (in the sense of speaking untruth): *kundrayati*. 1541. *laḍa* (in the sense of fondling/serving): *lāḍayati*. 1542. *midi* (in the sense of moistening/affection): *mindayati*, *mindati*.

1543. *olaḍi* in the sense of throwing up: *olaṇḍayati*, *olaṇḍati*. Some say that the vowel *o* is replaced by *i*; thus: *laṇḍayati*, *laṇḍati*. Others say that this root begins with *u*; thus: *ulaṇḍayati*. 1544. *jala* in the sense of covering: some say it is *laja*. 1545. *pīḍa* in the sense of pressing or plunging: *pīḍayati*. [According to] Pāṇini 7.4.3: "In the case of *bhrāja*, *bhāsa*, *bhāṣa*, *dīpa*, *jīva*, *mīla*, and *pīḍa*, the substitution of *niṣṭhā*-nasal (*ṇ*) is optional. (SK 2565).

For these roots, there may optionally be a short vowel for the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) when followed by a *ṇi*-affix that itself is followed by *caṅ* (the reduplication of the aorist). Examples: *apīpiḍat* or *apipīḍat*. 1546. *ṇaṭ* in the sense of leaping down; leaping down is acting on the stage (*nāṭyam*). 1547. *śrath* in the sense of exertion; some say it means setting out (*prasthāna*). 1548. *badh* in the sense of restraining; *bādhayati*. According to Cāndra, the root is *bandh*. 1549. *pṝ* in the sense of filling; *pārayati*. The lengthening of the vowel is a sign that the addition of the *ṇic* affix is optional; for that [lengthening] serves to ensure the presence of the *iṭ* augment.

And thus, although *parita* and so forth are established from the roots *pṛṇāti* and *piparti*, the forms *parati* and *parata* and so forth are also established. [Root 1550] *ūrj* means strength and life-sustenance. [1551] *pakṣ* means to embrace or accept. [1552–1553] *varṇ* and *cūrṇ* mean to impel; some say *varṇ* means to describe. [1554] *prath* means to become famous; one causes to become famous (*prāthayati*). Because it will be stated later that "others are not *mit* when there is no causal suffix," this root does not have the *mit* designation.

SK 2566: *atsmṛdṝtvaraprathamradastṝspaśam* (A 7.4.95). When followed by a *ṇi*-affix that is itself followed by *caṅ*, the substitute *at* is applied to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) of these roots. This is an exception to the substitution of *it*. Example: *apaprathat*. [Note: The root] *pṛth* in the sense of "scattering" is *parthayati*. SK 2567: *ur ṛt* (A 7.4.7). [The substitute *u* is applied to the reduplicated syllable of a root ending in *ṛ* when followed by a *ṇi*-affix that is itself followed by *caṅ*.]

In place of an *ṛ*-vowel that follows an *upadhā* (penultimate vowel), *ṛt* may optionally be substituted when a *ṇi*-affix follows that is itself followed by a *caṅ* (the reduplication of the aorist). *Prātipadikād dhātvarthe bahulam iṣṭhavañ ca*: After a nominal stem (*prātipadika*), the suffix *ṇic* may optionally be added in the sense of verbalizing that stem, just as in the case of the superlative suffix *iṣṭhan*. Just as in the case of the superlative suffix, the following operations apply to the nominal stem after *ṇic*: masculine gender substitution (*puṃvadbhāva*), the elision of the *ra* sound (*rabhāva*), the elision of the *ṭi* portion (*ṭilopa*), the elision of the suffixes *vin* and *matup*, the elision of *yaṇ*-class vowels and so forth, the replacement of *pra-stha* and *sphā* etc., and the designation of the element as *bha*. These same operations should also apply after *ṇic*. For example: *paṭum ācaṣṭe* (he describes as clever) becomes *paṭayati*. Because the rule for *vṛddhi* substitution takes precedence, the *ṭi*-portion is elided once *vṛddhi* has occurred. Thus, *apīpaṭat* (he caused to describe as clever). However, in the *Mahābhāṣya* on the rule *ṇau caṅi*, it is established that the elision (*lopa*) is stronger than *vṛddhi*.

*apapaṭat*. It performs that [action], it describes that [action]. This is an elaboration (*prapañca*) of the preceding [sūtra]. In "he causes to do" (*karoti*) and "he causes to describe" (*ācaṣṭe*), the meaning of the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is merely the meaning of the verbal root; the meaning of the present tense marker (*laṭ*) is not intended to be expressed. Therefore: *atikrāmati* (he overcomes); *aśvena atikrāmati* (he overcomes by means of a horse) becomes *aśvayati*; *hastinā atikrāmati* (he overcomes by means of an elephant) becomes *hastayati*. And there is the form of the verbal root: the base of the causative (*ṇic*) reverts to the form of the verbal root. The word *ca* ("and") has the sense of including what has not been explicitly stated. And so says the Vārttika:

The *kṛt* suffix expresses that which has been accomplished through narration; there is elision of the *kṛt* suffix and restoration of the original form (*prakṛti-pratyāpatti*), and the *kāraka* (participant in the action) remains as it was in the original base. Thus, "he narrates the killing of Kaṃsa" becomes *kaṃsaṃ ghātayati*. Here, when the stage *kaṃsaṃ han i* is reached, [the rule] *hanasto 'ciṇṇaloḥ* (A 7.3.32) applies.

Regarding the list beginning with *puccha*, it is already established that the meaning of the verbal root itself applies, because of the rule of diversity (*bahulavacana*) even from the causative stem. Let the ātmanepada ending be so; let there be no need for the specific rule for *ṇiṅ* regarding *puccha* and *bhāṇḍa*. The word "siddha" at the end of the treatise is for the sake of auspiciousness. Thus ends the section on the *cur*-class verbs.
The formation of *ṇi*-derived stems in the section on verbal suffixes (tiṅanta):
51. SK 2575. *tatprayojako hetuś ca* (A 1.4.55).
The instigator (*prayojaka*) of the agent shall have both the designation of "instigator" (*hetu*) and the designation of "agent" (*kartṛ*).

SK 2576 *hetumati ca* (A 3.1.26): When the activity of an instigator (*prayojaka*), such as commanding (*preṣaṇa*) and so forth, is to be expressed, the suffix *ṇic* shall be added to a verbal root. For example: *bhavantam prerayati* → *bhāvayati*. And by the rule *ṇicaś ca* (A 1.3.74), the Ātmanepada ending is used when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent; thus: *bhāvayate*. Also: *bhāvayāṃ babhūva*. SK 2577 *oḥ puyaṇjyapare* (A 7.4.80).

When *san* follows, the *it* (short *i*) substitution shall occur for the vowel *u* of the reduplicated syllable belonging to that stem, provided that *pa*, *ya*, *ṇa*, or *ja*—followed by an *a*-vowel—follows. Examples: *abībhavat*, *apīpavat*; *mūṅ*: *amīmavat*; *yā*: *ayīyavat*; *rī*: *arīravat*; *lī*: *alīlavat*; *jī*: *ajījavat*.
(SK 2578) There is an option for the roots *sravati*, *śṛṇoti*, *dravati*, *pravati*, *plavati*, and *cyavati*. (A 7.4.81)

In these cases, when there is the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) of a root ending in *s*, the vowel *i* may optionally replace it before a consonant followed by a vowel, provided that a verbal root-final (*dhātu-akṣara*) follows. Examples: *asisravat*, *asusravat*. [The rule] "not after a root that loses its penultimate vowel" (*nāglopi*) prohibits the shortening of the reduplicated vowel. Examples: *aśaśāsat*, *aḍuḍhaukat*, *acīcakāsat*. According to another opinion: *acacakāsat*. The term "one that loses its penultimate vowel" (*aglopi*) will be illustrated later in the section on roots ending in *su*. Regarding a causative (*ṇic*) derived from a causative: because it is an exception (*apavāda*) or due to a prior contradiction (*pūrva-vipratiṣedha*), the elision of the causative suffix (*ṇilopa*) prevails over the Vṛddhi strengthening. Example: *vīrayati*. [In this case,] the shortening of the reduplicated vowel occurs according to the rule "when there is *caṅ* following a causative" (*ṇau caṅi*).

The long vowel [is substituted] for the short [vowel]. Nor is there an impossibility of both [substitutions] occurring because of the elision of the penultimate (*aglopi*), since the rule is stated in reference to the general form (*ākṛti*) of the suffix *ṇi*. Example: *acūcurat*. According to A 6.1.31, *ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ*: when followed by the causative suffix *ṇi* which is itself followed by *san* or *caṅ*, the semivowel of the root *śvi* may optionally undergo *saṃprasāraṇa*. By the statement that "the *saṃprasāraṇa* and the operation dependent upon it are stronger," the *saṃprasāraṇa* takes place, resulting in the single substitution of the preceding form (*pūrvarūpa*). Example: *aśūśavat*. Because the vowel is not light (*alaghutva*), the long vowel is not substituted. Example: *aśiśvayat*.

SK 2580: *stambhu-sivu-saha-ām caṅi* (A 8.3.116). When *caṅ* follows, the *s* of these roots [stambh, siv, sah] preceded by a prefix does not become *ṣ*. Examples: *avātastambhat*, *paryasīṣivat*, *nyasīṣahat*. In *āṭiṭat* and *āśiśat*, the shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasva*) occurs even though it is extrinsically conditioned (*bahiraṅga*), because it applies prior to reduplication; this is indicated by the fact that the root *oṇ* is marked with the *ṛt* indicator. *Mā bhavān ididhat*: Since the rule for *vṛddhi* substitution is prescribed only for roots beginning with *eC* when followed by *edh*, there is no *vṛddhi* here. *Mā bhavān predidhat*: By the rule *na ndrāḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.3), there is no reduplication of the *n*, *d*, or *r* sounds. Examples: *aundidat*, *āṅḍiḍat*, *ārcicat*.

The root *ubj* means "to straighten. In the context of grammatical instruction (*upadeśa*), it has *da* as its penultimate letter. According to the rule *bhujanyubjau pāṇyupatāpayoḥ*, the *da* is replaced by *va* due to a specific grammatical irregularity (*nipātana*). Although this substitution is an internal operation (*antaraṅga*), it takes effect only after the reduplication (*dvitva*) has occurred—specifically, after the reduplication of the syllable *ji*—and not prior to it, because of the prohibition *na ndrāḥ*. This is due to the functional power (*sāmarthya*) of the explicit pronunciation of the letter *da*. Examples: *aubjijat*. [This applies] only to roots beginning with a vowel (*ajādi*). Not here: *adidrapat*. Sūtra 2581: *rabher aśabliṭoḥ* (A 7.1.63).
The augment *num* is added to the root *rabh* before a vowel, except when followed by the suffixes *śap* or *liṭ*.

SK 2582: *labheś ca* (A 7.1.64). *alalambhat*, *alalambhat*. Because the word *acaṅi* is stated in the sūtra *heracaṅi*, there is no *kutva* [substitution]. *ajīhayat*. [The rule] *atsnṛdṝtvaraprathamradastṝspaśām* [applies]. *asasmarat*, *adadarat*. Due to the force of the *tapara* [specification], there is no lengthening of the short vowel here. SK 2583: *vibhāṣā veṣṭiceṣṭyoḥ* (A 7.4.96).

The substitution of *ā* for the penultimate vowel (*atva*) may optionally occur when a *ṇi*-affix follows that is itself followed by *caṅ*. Thus: *avaveṣṭat* or *aviveṣṭat*; *acaceṣṭat* or *aciceṣṭat*. By the rule *bhrājabhāsa-* etc., the penultimate vowel is optionally shortened: *abibhrajat* or *ababhrājat*. It should be stated that this applies to the group beginning with *kāṇ*. Six roots—*kaṇ*, *raṇ*, *bhaṇ*, *śraṇ*, *lup*, and *heṭh*—ending in *ṇi* are mentioned as *kāṇyādi* in the Bhāṣya. Four more—*hvāyi*, *vāṇi*, *loṭi*, and *lopaya*—are added in the Nyāsa. *Vāṇi* and *loṭhi* are also found elsewhere. Thus, there are twelve. Examples: *acīkaṇat* or *acakāṇat*. [Rule A 6.1.18: *svāpeś caṅi* ("and after *svap*, when *caṅ* follows").
There shall be vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) for the causative of *svap* when followed by *caṅ*. Example: *asūṣupat*.

(Pāṇini 7.3.37) The suffix *yuk* is added after the roots *śā*, *chā*, *sā*, *hve*, *vye*, and *ve* when followed by a causative (*ṇic*). This is an exception to the addition of *puk*. Examples: *śāyayati*, *hvāyayati*.

SK 2586 *hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam* (A 6.1.32): When followed by the causative suffix *ṇiC* which is itself followed by *san* or *caṅ*, there shall be vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the root *hve*. Examples: *ajūhavat*, *ajuhāvat*.

SK 2587 *lopaḥ pibater īc cābhyāsasya* (A 6.4.4): In the case of the root *pā* (*pibi*), there is elision of the penultimate vowel, and the substitute *īC* is applied to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).

There is elision of the penultimate vowel of the root *pā* (*pibati*), and the substitution of *ī* for the reduplicated syllable, when followed by a *ṇi*-affix that is itself followed by *caṅ*. Thus: *apīpyat*. By the rule *arti-hrī-* etc., the augment *puK* is added: *arpayati*, *hrepayati*, *vlepayati*, *repayati*. There is elision of *y*: *kopayati*, *kṣmāpayati*, *sthāpayati*.
By the rule *tiṣṭhater it* (A 7.4.5), the substitution of *i* for the penultimate vowel of the root *sthā* occurs when followed by a *ṇi*-affix that is itself followed by *caṅ*. Thus: *atiṣṭhipat*.

SK 2589: Or, after the root *ghrā* (to smell), [the substitution of *ap* for *aṭ* is optional] (A 7.4.3). Examples: *ajighripat* or *ajighrapat*. [In the case of the roots *kṝ*, *kṝt*, *vṛt*, *bhṛj*, and *mṛj*, the substitution of *ur* for *ṛt* is applied before the suffix *aṅ*:

*acīkṛtat*; *acikīrtat*; *avīvṛtat*; *avavartat*; *amībhṛjat*; *amamārjat*. Regarding the root *pā* (to protect): it should be stated that there is elision (*luk*) [of the augment *pu*] when followed by the causative suffix *ṇi*. This is an exception to the rule for *puk*. Example: *pālayati*. SK 2590: After the root *vā*, when meaning "shaking," the suffix *juk* is added [before *ṇic*] (A 7.3.38).

The augment *juk* is optionally applied after the root *vā* before an affix marked with *ṇ*, when the meaning is "to shake. Examples: *vājayati*. Why "when the meaning is to shake"? [Counter-example: *keśān vāpayati* ("he causes the hair to be cut"). Regarding the root *lī*: there is an option (*vibhāṣā*). According to A 7.3.39, *nuk* and *luk* are optionally substituted for the *li* of *lī* and *līṅ* respectively, in the sense of "causing the flow of oil" (*snehavipātana*).

In the sense of "becoming soft" (*snehadrava*), after the roots *lī* and *lā*, the augment *nuK* or the substitution of *a* for *ī* respectively may optionally occur before the causative suffix *ṇiC*. Thus: *vilīnayati*, *vilāyayati*, *vilālayati*, or *vilāpayati* "he causes the ghee to melt. Because of the elision (*praśleṣa*) of the vowel *ī* in *lī-ī*, the augment *nuK* does not apply in the case where *ā* is substituted. Why "in the sense of becoming soft"? Consider: *lohaṃ vilāpayati* "he melts the metal"; [here one says] *vilāyayati*. It should be stated that for the root *lī*, the substitution of *ā* for *ī* is obligatory before a suffix beginning with a non-vocalic consonant (*aśit*) when it means "deceiving," "overpowering," or "honoring. This is based on the rule: *liyaḥ saṃmānanaśālīnīkaraṇayoś ca* (A 1.3.70).

The *ātmanepada* ending shall be used after the roots *lī* and *līṅ* when followed by the causative suffix (*ṇic*), even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, provided the meaning is "worship," "overpowering," or "deceiving. *Jaṭābhir lāpayate*: "He causes [himself] to be worshipped by means of matted locks"; the meaning is that he attains worship. *Śyeno vartikām ullāpayate*: "The hawk overpowers the quail"; the meaning is that he overcomes her. *Bālam ullāpayate*: "He deceives the child"; the meaning is that he cheats him. SK 2593: *bibheter hetumaye* (A 6.1.56).
The substitution of *ā* for the *e* of the root *bhī* may optionally occur when it is caused by an instigator, provided the fear arises from that instigator.

Pāṇini 1.3.68: *bhīsmyor hetubhaye*. The Ātmanepada suffix occurs after these two roots (*bhī* and *smi*) when they are followed by the causative suffix *ṇic*, provided that the fear or wonder arises from a cause. In the rule, the mention of "fear" (*bhaya*) is an illustration for the meaning of the verbal root itself. Example: *maṇḍo bhāpayate* ("The gruel causes [people] to be afraid"). Pāṇini 7.3.40: *bhiyo hetubhaye ṣuk*. [The augment *ṣuk* is added after the root *bhī* when it is followed by the causative suffix *ṇic* and the fear arises from a cause.]

The vowel *ī* is elided [from the root *bhī*]. The augment *ṣuk* is added to the root *bhī*, which ends in *ī*, when followed by the causative suffix *ṇi* in the sense of causing fear. Thus, *bhīṣayate*.
According to A 6.1.57, the augment *ṣuk* is applied invariably to the root *smi* (*nityaṃ smayateḥ*).

In the case of *smi* (to smile), when used with the causal suffix *ṇic* in the sense of "causing wonder," the substitution of *ā* for the root vowel occurs invariably. Thus, one forms *vismāpayate*. This is because it is stated that [the rule applies] "if fear or wonder is caused by a motive (*hetu*). Therefore, it does not apply here: *kuñcikayainaṃ bhāyayati* ("he frightens him with a key") and *vismāyayati* ("he causes him wonder"). [Objection: How then is one to explain the phrase *vismāpayan vismitam ātmavṛttāv iti* ("causing wonder while recounting his own deeds")? [Response: For in that case, the wonder arises precisely from the fact that the speaker is a human being (*manuṣyavāc*). Otherwise, the suffix *śānac* would also have been possible. [Reply: True. The traditional scholars maintain that the correct reading is simply *vismāyayan*. Alternatively:

The human voice is the indirect agent (*prayojyakartṛ*); it causes astonishment. Thus, in the expression "the lion causes astonishment by means of that [voice]," it should be explained as being derived from the causative form of the root *vismi* with the suffix *śatṛ*.
According to A 7.3.41, *sphāyo vaḥ*, the letter *v* is substituted for the final vowel of the root *sphāy* when followed by the causative suffix *ṇic*: *sphāvayati*.

SK 2598: *śader agatau taḥ* (A 7.3.42). In the causative (*ṇi*) of the root *śad*, the substitution of *t* for the final letter occurs, except when the meaning is "to go. Examples: *śātayati* ("he causes to fall"). But in the sense of "to go": *gāḥ śādayati govindaḥ* ("Govinda makes the cows go"; the meaning is *gamayati*). SK 2599: *ruhaḥ po 'nyatarasyām* (A 7.3.43). In the causative of the root *ruh*, the substitution of *p* for the final letter optionally occurs.
In the case of the causative suffix *ṇic*: *ropayati* and *rohayati*.
According to A 6.1.48, *krīṅjīnāṃ ṇau*, these [roots] alone undergo the substitution of *ā* for their final vowel before the causative suffix *ṇic*: *krāpayati*, *adhyāpayati*, *jāpayati*.

SK 2601: *ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ* (A 2.4.51). When followed by a *ṇi*-affix that is itself followed by a *san* or a *caṅ*, the substitution of *gāṅ* for *iṅ* may optionally take place. Examples: *adhyajīgapat* or *adhyāpipat*. SK 2602: *sidhyater apāralaukike* (A 6.1.49). [The substitution of *siddha* for *siddha* applies] when the root *sidh* does not refer to a matter concerning the next world.

In the case of the root *sidh* meaning "to accomplish" (*sādhana*) with respect to a worldly matter (*aihikalaukika*), the vowel *a* is replaced by *ā* when followed by the causative suffix *ṇic*. Example: *annaṃ sādhayati*, meaning "he prepares food. Why say "not pertaining to the next world" (*apāralaukika*)? Consider: *tāpasaḥ siddhyati*, meaning "the ascetic attains realization" (*tattvaṃ niścinoti*). If one prompts him [to do so], it is *sedhayati tāpasaṃ tapaḥ*, "he causes the ascetic to perform penance. By rule A 6.1.55, *prajane vīyateḥ*: for the root *vī* in the sense of procreation (*prajana*), the vowel *e* is optionally replaced by *ā* when followed by the causative suffix *ṇic*. Example: *vāpayati* or *vāyayati gāḥ purovātaḥ*, meaning "the east wind causes the cows to conceive," that is, "it causes them to take up the embryo. By rule A 6.4.89, *ūdupadhāyā gohaḥ*: for the root *guh*, the vowel *u* is substituted for the penultimate vowel when followed by the causative suffix *ṇic*. Example: *gūhayati*.

SK 2604 *doṣo ṇau* (A 6.4.90): It is better to state *duṣ-* [instead of *doṣ-*, as the root is *duṣ*]. After the root *duṣ*, the substitute *ūt* occurs for the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) when followed by the suffix *ṇi*. [Thus: *dūṣayati*.
SK 2605 *vā cittavirāge* (A 6.4.91).

*Virāga* is a lack of delight. Desire (*kāma*) corrupts or defiles the mind. *Mita* is short; those [roots] beginning with *bhū* and *cur* are stated to be *mita*. [Examples: *ghaṭayati*; from *janījṛṣ*: *janayati*, *jarayati*; but from *jṛṇāti*: *jārayati*. Regarding the root *rañj* in the causative (*ṇau*), it should be stated that there is the elision of *na* when referring to the hunting of deer (*mṛgaramaṇa*). Hunting (*mṛgaramaṇa*) means the chase. [Example: *rajayati mṛgān* (he causes the deer to be colored/pleased). Why "deer"? [Counter-example: *rañjayati pakṣiṇaḥ* (he pleases the birds). But elsewhere than in the context of pleasure (*ramaṇāt*), as in *rañjayati mṛgāṃs tṛṇadānena* (he pleases the deer by giving them grass), [the elision does not apply].

Among the *cur*-class roots, *ciñ* belongs to the *jñapādi* subgroup. It is stated that for *ci* and *sphur*, when followed by the causative suffix *ṇic*, the forms are *capayati* and *cāyayati*. However, for the root *cinoti*, the forms are *cāpayati* and *cāyayati*; for *sphur*, they are *sphārayati* and *sphorayati*. Regarding the forms *apupphurat* and *aputpharam*: SK 2606 (*ubhau sābhyāsasya*, A 8.4.21): When a cause [for substitution] is present, both *ṇakāra*s of the root *an* together with its reduplicated syllable undergo the substitution of *ṇ*. Thus, we have *prāṇiṇat*.

SK 2607: *ṇau gamir abodhane* (A 2.4.46). In the context of the causal suffix *ṇic*, *gam* shall be substituted for *iṇ*. Thus, *gamayati*. However, in the sense of "making known," one says *pratyāyayati*. The root *iṅ* is treated like *iṇ*: *adhigamayati*. Regarding *han*: *to 'ciṇṇaloḥ* (A 7.3.32). By the rule *ho hanteḥ* (A 7.3.54), there is *kutva* (the substitution of *gh* for *h*). Thus, *ghātayati*. Regarding *īrṣy*: It should be stated that [the doubling occurs] of the third [consonant] of *īrṣy*. This means either "of the third consonant" or "of the third single-consonant [vowel]. In the first interpretation, this [sūtra] is intended to prevent the doubling of the letter *c*. In the second, however, it operates within the domain of the desiderative (*sannanta*) as an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule *ajāder dvitīyasya* (A 6.1.2).

*airṣyiyat*; *airṣiṣyat*. According to the second explanation, when the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is added and then the *caṅ* (reduplication) affix follows, only the letter *ṣ* is heard in the reduplicated syllable because of the rule *halādiḥśeṣaḥ* (the first consonant remains). However, doubling occurs only of the second [consonant], because the present Vārttika does not apply due to the absence of a third [consonant]. When the sense of instigation has ceased, the meaning of the root with the causative suffix (*hetumaṇṇic*) is identical to that of the simple root. By this, forms such as *prārthayanti śayanotthitaṃ priyāḥ* ("the beloveds entreat him who has risen from his bed") are established. This should be inferred for all transitive roots in this manner. Thus ends the section on the formation of causative stems (*ṇyantaprakriyā*). Now begins the section on the formation of desiderative stems (*sannantaprakriyā*) within the section on verbal suffixes (*tiṅanta*). 52.
After a verbal root expressing an action that has the same agent [as the desirer], the suffix *san* may optionally be used to express desire. (A 3.1.7)

The suffix *san* may optionally occur after a verbal root (*dhātu*) that has an object (*karman*) and shares the same agent (*ekakartṛka*), in the sense of desire (*icchā*). Because it is prescribed after a verbal root, *san* here possesses the status of an *ārdhadhātuka*. [Thus, the augment] *iṭ* is applied. [Then] reduplication (*dvitva*) occurs. By the rule *sanyataḥ*, [the vowel of the reduplicated syllable is replaced by *i*]. He desires to read: *pipaṭhiṣati*. Why "that which has an object"? To prevent [the application of *san*] from an instrument (*karaṇa*), as in "he desires by means of going" (*gamanenecchati*). Why "sharing the same agent"? To exclude cases such as "the teacher desires that the pupils should read" (*śiṣyāḥ paṭhantv itīcchati guruḥ*). Due to the inclusion of the word "optionally" (*vā*), the sentence form also occurs in the alternative case. [In *pipaṭhiṣati*, the augment] *iṭ* is not applied because of the rule *luṅsanorghasṭerekāca upadeśe*.

The reality of grain: *jighatsati* (he wishes to eat). Regarding *īrṣyati*, because it belongs to the third [class], there is reduplication for the suffixes *san* and *yan*: *īrṣyiyiṣati*; *īrṣyiṣiṣati*.

(Pāṇini 1.2.8) After these roots—*rud*, *vid*, *muṣ*, *grah*, *svap*, and *racch*—the suffixes *san* and *ktvā* are both *kit*. Thus: *rurudiṣati* (he wishes to weep), *vividiṣati* (he wishes to know), *mumuṣiṣati* (he wishes to steal).

SK 2610: *sani grahaguhoś ca* (A 7.2.12). After the roots *grah* and *guh*, and after a root ending in *u*, the augment *iṭ* shall not be added to the suffix *san*. By the rule *grahijyā-*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). Because the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* in *san* is considered *asiddha*, the substitution of *bhaṣ* occurs [resulting in *gh*]. Thus: *jighṛkṣati*; *suṣupsati*. SK 2611: *kiraś ca pañcabhyaḥ* (A 7.2.75). [The augment *iṭ* is also not added to *san*] after the five roots beginning with *kṝ*.

The augment *iṭ* shall be applied after the suffix *san* following the roots *kṝ*, *gṝ*, *dṛṅ*, *dhṛṅ*, and *pracch*. Thus: *pipṛcchiṣati*, *cikariṣati*, *jigariṣati*, *jigaliṣati*. In this context, lengthening of the *iṭ* is not desired; thus: *didariṣate*, *didhariṣate*. [Question: How is it that we have *uddidhīrṣuḥ*? [Answer: Understand that it refers to the two roots *dhṛṅ* and *dhṛñ* belonging to the *bhūvādika* class. (Pāṇini 1.2.9: *iko jhal*).

After a verbal root ending in a short vowel (*iganta*), a *san* suffix beginning with a *jhal* consonant shall be marked with the *kit* designation. Thus, from *bhū*, one forms *bubhūṣati*. From *dīṅ*: "he wishes to give" is *didīṣate*. Because it does not fall within the scope of the rule for *ej*-beginning roots, the substitution of *ā* as prescribed by *mīnātiminoti...* does not apply. For this very reason, in the rule *sani mīmā...* (Pāṇini 7.4.54), the root *mī* is mentioned separately from the root *mā*. [Also applicable is] A 1.2.10: *halantāc ca*.

A *san* suffix beginning with a *jhal* consonant following a *hal* consonant immediately after an *ik* vowel shall be treated as *kit*. *guhū*: *jughukṣati*. *bibhitsati*. Why "after an *ik* vowel"? Consider *yiyakṣate*. Why "beginning with a *jhal* consonant"? Consider *vivardhiṣate*. The mention of *hal* refers to the class [of consonants]. *nṛnhū*: *titṛkṣati*, *titṛṃhiṣati*. **A 6.4.16**: *aj-jhan-gamāṃ sani* (In the presence of a *san* suffix beginning with a *jhal* consonant, there is lengthening for roots ending in *ac*, for *han*, and for the substitute *gam*. Lengthening occurs for roots ending in *ac*, for *han*, and for the substitute *gam*, when followed by a *san* suffix beginning with a *jhal* consonant. Regarding *ji* in the sense of *san* and *laṭ*: *jigīṣati*. Optionally so for *ci*: *cikīṣati*, *cicīṣati*. *jighāṃsati*.

SK 2615 *sani ca* (A 2.4.47): After the root *iṇ*, there shall be the substitute *gami* before the suffix *san*, but not when it means "to understand. Examples: *jigamiṣati* ("he wishes to go"). When meaning "to understand," [the substitute is not applied]: *pratīṣiṣati*. The root *ik* is treated like *iṇ*: *adhijigamiṣati*. In the passive (*karmaṇi*), the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are used. Because of the statement "in the parasmaipada endings," the augment *iṭ* is not added. Before a suffix beginning with a *jhal* consonant, there is lengthening by the rule *sani* (A 6.4.16): *jigāṃsyate*; *adhijigāṃsyate*. Because of the statement "of that which is not an *ajādeśa*," there is no lengthening for the root *gam* [when it is not a substitute]: *jigaṃsyate*; *saṃjigaṃsate*. SK 2616 *iṅaś ca* (A 2.4.48).
The root *gam* shall take the place of *iṅ* when followed by the suffix *san*. Example: *adhijigāṃsate*. [Pāṇini 1.2.26:
After a root beginning with a consonant (*hal*), having *v* or *y* as its penultimate letter (*vy-upadha*), the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied before the suffixes *sa* and *san*.

The suffixes *ktvā* and *san* (desiderative) are optionally treated as *kit* after a root ending in *r* or *l*, provided they are followed by a consonant (*hal-ādi*) and take the augment *iṭ*. There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) for the roots *dyut* and *svāpi*. Examples: *didyutiṣate* / *didyotiṣate*; *ruruciṣate* / *rurociṣate*; *lilikhiṣati* / *lilekhiṣati*. Why "ending in *r* or *l*" (*ralaḥ*)? Consider *dideviṣati*. Why "having *u* or *i* as a penultimate" (*vy-upadhāt*)? Consider *vivartiṣate*. Why "followed by a consonant" (*hal-ādeḥ*)? Consider *eṣiṣiṣati*. In this case, even though reduplication (*dvitva*) is obligatory, it is superseded by the *guṇa* strengthening.

For the operation caused by the *upadha* (penultimate vowel) is stronger because it applies when there is a pair [of vowels]. This is because the marking of the root *oṇ* with the *ṛt* diacritic (*ṛdit*) serves as an indicator (*jñāpaka*) based on a general consideration.

(A 7.2.49) *sanīvantardhabhrasjadambhuśrisvṛyūrṇubharajñapisanām*: After roots ending in *i*, *u*, or *ṛ*, and after the group beginning with *ṛdh*, the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied to the suffix *san*. In the absence of *iṭ*, the suffix is marked as *kit* by the rule *halantāc ca*. By the rule *chvoḥ—*, *ūṭh* is substituted for *v*. Then the *yaṇ* substitution and reduplication take place. Thus: *dudyuṣati*; *dideviṣati*. Due to the restriction to be stated later—*stautiṇyor eva*—the change to *ṣ* does not occur here. *susyūṣati*; *siseviṣati*.

SK 2619: For the roots *āp*, *jñap*, and *ṛdh*, the vowel *i* is substituted for the [root-final] vowel when followed by a *san* suffix beginning with a consonant. SK 2620: In this context, there is elision of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*).

Regarding what was stated starting from *sani mīmā-* (Pāṇini 7.4.54), there should be the elision (*lopa*) of the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) therein. He desires to obtain: *īpsati*. He desires to split: [from *ardh*]—there is substitution of *ra* for *ṛ* (*raparatva*), then the substitution of *ca* for *ja* (*cartva*): *īrtsati*. He desires to split repeatedly: *ardidhiṣati*. [From *bhṛj*] he desires to fry repeatedly: *bibhrajjiṣati*, *bibharjiṣati*, *bibhrakṣati*, *bibharkṣati*. SK 2621: *dambha ic ca* (A 7.4.56).

After the root *dambh*, the augment *it* (which is also *ī*) is inserted before a *san* suffix beginning with a consonant; there is elision of the reduplication. It has been stated that in the rule *halantāc ca*, the mention of *hal* refers to the class (*jāti*). Consequently, because the *san* suffix is marked with *k* (indicating it is *kit*), there is elision of the nasal (*n*). Thus: *dhīpsati* or *dhīpsati*; *didambhiṣati*. [Similarly: *śiśrīṣati* or *śiśrayiṣati*. Regarding the rule *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya*: *susvūrṣati* or *sisvariṣati*; *yuyūṣati* or *yiyaviṣati*; *ūrṇunūṣati*, *ūrṇunuviṣati*, or *ūrṇunaviṣati*.

Nor should it be argued that because the substitutes for the *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* vowels would be subsequent [to the original], the vowel *u* would not be heard in the reduplication; for by the rule *dvirvacane 'ci*, when reduplication is to be performed, there is either an extension of the form of the original (*sthānin*) or a prohibition of the substitute (*ādeśa*). Nor should it be asked how the desiderative suffix (*san*) can serve as a cause (*nimitta*) for reduplication since it is itself the object of the operation (*kāryin*); for an element is not treated as a cause by virtue of undergoing an operation, but rather by not undergoing one. And here, the *san* does not undergo reduplication—as in *bubhūrṣati*.

*bibhariṣati*. The root *jñap* is marked with *mit* and ends in *p*; it belongs to the *curādigaṇa*. In the absence of *iṭ*, there is no *guṇa* substitution because the suffix is *kit* by the rule *iko jhal*. The lengthening [of the vowel] by the rule *ajjhanagamāṃ sani* is superseded by the elision of *ṇi* (*ṇilopa*), as it is subsequent. By the rule *āpjñapyṛdhāmīt*, the vowel becomes *ī*: *jñīpsati*. In the case of *jijñapayiṣati*, [the *ṇi* is present]. But when it is not *mit* [as in the case of *jñā*], it is *jijñāpayiṣati*. By the rule *janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ*, there is *ātva* [substitution of *ā* for *a*]: *siṣāsati* and *sisaniṣati*. Regarding the roots *tan*, *pat*, and *garī* (from *glai*), it should be stated that *iṭ* is optional after *san*: SK 2622. By the rule *tanoter vibhāṣā* (A 6.4.17), [the *iṭ* is optional].

In place of the penultimate vowel of this [root], a long vowel may optionally occur before an affix beginning with *jhal* when followed by *san*. Thus: *titāṃsati*, *titaṃsati*, or *titaniṣati*. It should be stated that *san* is used in the sense of apprehension (*āśaṅkā*). For example: *śvā mumūrṣati* ("the dog is about to die") and *kūlaṃ pipatiṣati* ("the bank is about to fall"). In the presence of *san*, the vowel *i* is substituted for the vowel of the roots *mī*, *mā*, *dhū*, *rabh*, *labh*, *śak*, *pat*, and *pad* (Pāṇini 7.4.54).

For these [roots], *is* should be substituted when a suffix beginning with *s* follows; there is elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsalopa*). By the rule *skoḥ—*, there is elision of *s*. Thus: *pitsati*; *didaridriṣati*; *didaridrāsati*. From the roots *ḍu-miñ* and *mīñ*, the suffix *san* is added. Since even *minoti* has the form *mī* after the lengthening has occurred, *is* is applied without distinction. By the rule *saḥ si—*, *t* is substituted for *s*. Thus: *mitsati*; *mitsate*. From *mā* in the sense of measuring: *mitsati*. From *māṅ* and *meṅ*: *mitsate*. From *do* and *dāṇ*: *ditsati*; from *deṅ*: *ditsate*; from *dāñ*: *ditsati*; *ditsate*. From *dhēṭ*: *dhitsati*; from *dhāñ*: [the same].

*dhitsati*, *dhitsate*; *ripsate*, *lipsate*. The root *śakl* [is used]; *śikṣati*, *śikṣate*. The root *śak* meaning "to endure" belongs to the *divādi* class; it is marked with the *svarita* accent. Thus: *śikṣati*, *śikṣate*. *pitsate*. Regarding the root *rādh* in the sense of "injury," it should be stated that the suffix *san* is applied optionally. Thus: *ritsati*. Why "in the sense of injury"? [Consider: *ārirātsati*. SK 2624:
For the root *muc* when it is intransitive (*akarmaka*), there is optionally the substitution of *guṇa*. (A 7.4.57)

When *san* follows a root beginning with a vowel, there is elision of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa-lopa*). Thus, *mokṣate* or *mumukṣate vatsaḥ svayam eva* ("the calf desires to release itself"). Why "of an intransitive verb" (*akarmakasya*)? [Consider: *mumukṣati vatsaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ* ("Kṛṣṇa desires the calf to release [him]"). [The suffix *iṭ* is not added] after the four roots beginning with *vṛt*: *vivṛtsati*. But when *taṅ* (ātmanepada) follows, it is *vivartiṣate*. By the rule *se 'sici—*, *iṭ* is optional: *ninartiṣati* or *ninṛtsati*. SK 2625: *iṭ sani vā* (A 7.2.41). When *san* follows, *iṭ* is optionally inserted.

After the roots *vṛṅ* and *vṛñ*, as well as after a root ending in *ṝ*, the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied before the suffix *san*. Thus: *titariṣati*, *titarīṣati*, *titīrṣati*; *vivariṣati*, *vivarīṣati*, *vuvūrṣati*. From *vṛṅ*: *vuvūrṣate*, *vivariṣate*, *vuvūrṣate*. [Pāṇini 7.2.74 states: "The augment *iṭ* is applied after the roots *smi*, *pūṅ*, *rañj*, and *vaś* when *san* follows. *SK 2626*.

The augment *iṭ* is applied after the roots *smi*, *pūṅ*, *ṛ*, *añjū*, and *aś* when followed by the suffix *san*. Thus: *sismayiṣate*, *pipaviṣate*, *aririṣati*. Here, there is reduplication of the syllable *ri*; since the portion *is* of the suffix *san* is what undergoes the grammatical operation, it cannot serve as the cause for that operation, and thus the rule *dvirvacane 'ci* does not apply. [Examples: *añjijiṣati*, *aśiśiṣate*. By the rule *ubhau sābhyāsasya*, [we have] *prāṇiṇiṣati*. In *ucchecchati*, there is the substitution of *c* for *t* (*cutvam*). Because of the principle *pūrvatrāsiddhīyam advirvacane*, the reduplication applies to the entire sequence including the augment *iṭ* along with the letters *c* and *ch*.

*Halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* (P. 7.4.60): *ucicchiṣati*. However, the principle that "when the cause disappears, the effect also disappears" is not universally valid (*anitya*). This is known from the inclusion of the augment *tuK* in the rule *cchvoḥ—* (P. 6.1.16); or else, it is known from the statement regarding the restoration of the original form (*prakṛtipratyāpatti*) [in P. 6.1.11]. By the two rules *ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ* (P. 6.1.31–32), the substitution of *gāṅ* for *iṅ* and the semivowel-consonant contraction (*saṃprasāraṇa*) for *śvi* are optional. Thus: *adhijigāpayiṣati* or *adhyāpipayiṣati*; *śiśvāyayiṣati* or *śuśāvayiṣati*. For the root *hve*, there is contraction: *juhāvayiṣati*.

Because it has been stated that no substitution for a vowel (*ac*) occurs prior to reduplication (*dvitva*), there is reduplication of the vowel *u*: *pusphārayiṣati*, *cukṣāvayiṣati*. Regarding the rule *oḥ puyaṇjyapare* [Pāṇini 7.4.80]: *pipāvayiṣati*, *bibhāvayiṣati*, *yiyāvayiṣati*, *rirāvayiṣati*, *lilāvayiṣati*, *jijāvayiṣati*. Why say *puraṇji*? [To exclude cases like] *nunāvayiṣati*. Why say *apare*? [To exclude cases like] *bubhūṣati*. Regarding *sravati*, there is optionally the substitution of *i* (*itva*): *sisrāvayiṣati*, *susrāvayiṣati*, etc. Only when *apare* follows does this apply; otherwise, as in *śuśrūṣate*. [The rule] *stautiṇyor eva ṣaṇy abhyāsāt* [Pāṇini 8.3.61] applies.

In the case of the roots *stu* and *ṇi*, when followed by a *san* that has become *ṣan*, the *s* of the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) becomes *ṣ*; this does not apply to any other root. *tuṣṭūṣati* ("he desires to praise"). By the rule *dyutisvāpyoḥ...* [Pāṇini 7.4.67], there is the substitution of *u* for the vowel. *susvāpayiṣati* ("he desires to cause to sleep well"). *sisādhayiṣati* ("he desires to accomplish"). Why "of *stu* and *ṇi*"? Consider *sisikṣati* ("he desires to sprinkle"). However, because of the rule *upasargāt tu sthādiṣv abhyāsena ca* [Pāṇini 8.3.65], the *s* becomes *ṣ*. *pariṣiṣikṣati* ("he desires to sprinkle around"). Why "in the case of *ṣan*"? Consider *tiṣṭhāsati* ("he desires to stand") and *suṣupsati* ("he desires to sleep well"). Because of the mention of "from the reduplication" (*abhyāsāt*), the prohibition does not apply here. *iṇ*: *pratīṣiṣati* ("he desires to go toward"). *ik*: *adhīṣiṣati* ("he desires to study"). SK 2628: *saḥ svidisvadisahīnāṃ ca* (A 8.3.62). [The *s* of the reduplication becomes *ṣ* after a prefix for the roots *svid*, *svad*, and *sah* when followed by *ṣan*.]

In the case of these roots ending in *ṇic*, when there is repetition (*abhyāsa*), the *s* of the root remains *s* and does not become *ṣ* before a following *ṣaṇ* suffix: *sisvedayiṣati*, *sisvādayiṣati*, *sisāhayiṣati*. This is because of the restrictive rule that "in the case of *sthā* and others, [the change occurs] due to the reduplication. Therefore, it does not apply here in *abhisusūṣati*. Regarding the rule: "A secondary derivative (*śaiṣika*) suffix having the sense of the possessive suffix (*matubarthīya*), and another secondary derivative having the sense of the possessive suffix, which is similar in form (*sarūpa*), is not desired [to be applied]. (Bhāṣya). A similar secondary derivative is not applied after another secondary derivative; therefore, for the meaning "existing in Śālīya," one must simply use the sentence itself.

But [the suffix] *cha* does not follow after [a word ending in] *śānta*. Why "of the same form" (*sarūpa*)? [Consider: *āhicchatraḥ*, meaning "one who lives in Ahicchatra"; and *āhicchatrīyaḥ*, meaning "one who lives in Ahicchatra. [In the latter case,] *cha* follows after that which ends in *aṇ*. Likewise, [the suffix] of the same form does not follow after a word expressing possession (*matvartha*). [For example: "He possesses wealth" (*dhanavān asyāsti*). Here, *matup* does not follow after a word already ending in *matup*. However, if the forms are different (*virūpa*), it certainly occurs: *daṇḍimatī śālā* ("a hall possessing staffs"). The term "of the same form" (*sarūpa*) is understood to carry over [from the previous rule]. Its meaning is similarity by way of the sense (*artha*). Therefore, *san* does not follow after a desiderative (*sannanta*) [ending in] *icchā*; however, it certainly occurs after a desiderative [ending in] *san* that expresses its own meaning (*svārtha*): *jugupsiṣate*, *mīmāṃsiṣate*. Thus concludes the section on the formation of desideratives (*sannantaprakriyā*).
The formation of the intensive (yaṅ) in the verbal suffixes (tiṅanta): 53.

Pāṇini A 3.1.22: *dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ*—the suffix *yaṅ* occurs after a root that has a single vowel and begins with a consonant when there is "intensive repetition of action" (*kriyāsamabhihāra*).
This intensive repetition of action consists of frequency (*paunaḥpunya*) and intensity (*bhṛśārtha*), and *yaṅ* is used to indicate that.
Pāṇini A 7.4.82: *guṇo yaṅlukoḥ*—a *guṇa* substitution takes place before *yaṅ* and its elision (*yaṅluk*).

The quality of reduplication (*abhyāsa*) occurs when the *yaṅ* affix or its elision (*yaṅluk*) follows. Because [the base] is a verbal root by virtue of the rule *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ*, the *laṭ* and other suffixes are applied. Due to the presence of a *ṅit* ending, the *ātmanepada* voice is used. Thus: it becomes again and again or intensely—*bobhūyate*; *bobhūyāñcakre*; *abobhūyiṣṭa*. Why "of a verbal root" (*dhātoḥ*)? So that it may be treated as an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix; hence [rules such as] *bruvo vaciḥ* apply. Why "having a single vowel" (*ekācaḥ*)? [Example: he wakes up repeatedly—*punaḥpunar jāgarti*. Why "beginning with a consonant" (*halādeḥ*)? [Example: he looks intensely—*bhṛśam īkṣate*.

Regarding the statement "it shines intensely" (*bhṛśaṃ rocate śobhate*), the *Bhāṣya* states that the *yaṅ* suffix does not apply here; however, it would certainly apply in the sense of repetition (*paunaḥpunye*). Thus we have *rorucyate* and *śośubhyate*. It should be stated that *yaṅ* is added after the roots *sūci*, *sūtri*, *mūtri*, *aṭi*, *arti*, *aśu*, and *ūrṇoti*. The first three are found in the *curādi* class and end in short *a*. Thus: *sosūcyate* and *sosūtryate*. Because they have multiple vowels (*anekāctva*), they are not taught with an initial *ṣ* (*aṣopadeśa*), and therefore there is no change to *ṣ*. Thus: *momūtryate*. [The rule] *yasya halaḥ* (A 6.4.49) applies.

The term *yasya* refers to the mention of a cluster [of sounds]. There shall be elision (*lopa*) of the sound *ya* following a *hal* consonant when an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix follows. [By the rule] *ādeḥ parasya*, this applies to the initial [sound] of the subsequent element. [Then by] *ato lopaḥ*, there is elision of the *a*. Thus: *sosūcāñcakre*, *sosūcitā*, *sosūritā*, *momūtritā*. SK 2632: *dīrgho 'kitaḥ* (A 7.4.83).
