In the case of *yaṅ* and *yaṅluk*, there shall be lengthening of the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) that does not contain the augment *kit*. Thus: *aṭāṭyate*.

In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, there is *guṇa* substitution for the *ṛ* of the root *ṛ*, as well as for the *ṛ* of roots beginning with a consonant cluster (*saṃyoga*). There is no prohibition of doubling for the *r* that follows the *y*. This is because the *Bhāṣya* provides the example *arāryate*. [Examples: *arāritā*, *aśāśitā*, *ūrṇonūyate*, *bebhid-y-ate*. Because the elision (*alopa*) is treated as *sthānivadbhāva*, there is no *guṇa* substitution for the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*). [Resulting forms: *bebhiditā*. SK 2634: *nityaṃ kauṭilye gatau* (A 3.1.23). [The *yaṅ* suffix is applied] invariably when expressing crookedness of movement.

After a root meaning "to go," the suffix *yaṅ* occurs only in the sense of crookedness (*kauṭilya*) and not in the sense of repetition of action (*kriyāsamabhihāra*). For example: *vāvrajyate* ("he moves crookedly").

(A 3.1.24) *lupasadacarajapajabhadahadaśagṛbhyo bhāvagarhāyām*: After these roots—*lup*, *sad*, *car*, *jap*, *jabh*, *dah*, *daś*, and *gṛ*—the suffix *yaṅ* occurs only when there is censure of the meaning of the verbal root (*dhātvarthagarhā*). For example: *lolupyate* ("he cuts in a censurable manner"), *sāsadyate*.

SK 2636 *caraphalor ca* (A 7.4.87): For these two roots (*car* and *phal*), the augment *nuk* shall be added to the vowel *a* of the reduplicated syllable when the suffix *yaṅ* or *yaṅluk* follows. By the rule *nug-*, an anusvāra is indicated; and that [anusvāra] should be treated as if it were at the end of a word (*padāntavat*), so that the rule *vā padāntasya* may apply. SK 2637 *utparasyātaḥ* (A 7.4.88): [The substitute *u* is applied] to the subsequent *a* [of the reduplicated syllable].

Due to the repetition (*abhyāsa*) of the roots *car* and *phal*, the suffix *yaṅ* occurs after the vowel *a*, as well as its elision (*yaṅluk*). By the rule *hali ca*, there is lengthening of the vowel. Thus: *cañcūryate* / *caṃcūryate*; *pamphulyate* / *puṃphulyate*. SK 2638: *japajabhadahadaśabhañjapaśāṃ ca* (A 7.4.86). For these roots—*jap*, *jabh*, *dah*, *daś*, *bhañj*, and *paś*—the augment *nuk* is added to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) when *yaṅ* or *yaṅluk* follows. Examples include: he performs recitation in a censurable manner (*garhitaṃ japati*); *jañjapyate*, and so forth.

SK 2639 *gro yaṅi* (A 8.2.20): In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, the substitution of *l* for the *r* of the root *gṛ* occurs. *garhitaṃ gilati* (he swallows what is censurable); *jegilyate*. By the rule *ghumāsthā-*, there is the substitution of *ī*; then *guṇa* [vṛddhi]. *dedīyate*, *pepīyate*, *seṣīyate*. [By the rule] *vibhāṣā śveḥ*: *śośūyate*, *śeśvīyate*. [By the rule] *yaṅi ca*: *sāsmaryate*. [By the rule] *rīṅ ṛtaḥ*: *cekrīyate*. [With the addition of] *suṭ*: *saṃceskrīyate*. SK 2640 *sico yaṅi* (A 8.3.112).

The substitution of *ṣ* for the *s* of *sic* should not occur in the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix. *nisesicyate*. (SK 2641) There is no substitution of *c* for the reduplicated syllable of *kavati* in the *yaṅ* suffix. *kokūyate*. However, for *kau* and *kuvati*, it is *cokūyate*.

SK 2642: *nīg vañcu-sraṃsu-dhvaṃsu-bhraṃsu-ka-sapa-tapa-da-skandām* (A 7.4.84). For these roots, the augment *nīg* is added to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) in the *yaṅ* and *yaṅluk* formations. Because it is stated [in the rule] that this applies "not when there is *kit*" (*akitaḥ*), there is no lengthening. There is elision of the *n*. Thus: *vādīdacyate*, *sanīsrasyate*, and so forth.
SK 2643: *nug ato ’nunāsikāntasya* (A 7.4.85). The augment *nuk* is added after the reduplicated syllable of a root ending in a nasal (*anunāsika*).

For a stem ending in a nasal (*anunāsika*), the *nuk* augment shall be added to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) that ends in *a*. It has been stated that by the presence of *nuk*, an *anusvāra* is indicated. Examples: *yaṃyamyate* / *yaṃyamyate*. Because of the force of the marker *t* in the rule, this does not apply even to a long vowel that existed previously. From the root *bhām* in the sense of anger: *bābhāmyate*. According to the rule *ye vibhāṣā*: *jājāyate* / *jañjanyate*. Regarding the root *han* in the sense of injury, it should be stated that there is a substitution of *ghnī* when *yaṅ* follows. Example: *jeghnīyate*. Why "in the sense of injury"? [Counter-example: *jaṅghanyate*. SK 2644: *rīgṛdupadhasya ca* (A 7.4.90). [This rule states that] the augment *rīk* is added to a reduplicated syllable whose penultimate (*upadhā*) is a short *ṛ*.

The augment *rīg* is added to the reduplicated syllable of a root that has a light vowel (*ṛt*) as its penultimate letter, when the suffix *yaṅ* or *yaṅluk* follows. *varīvṛtyate*. Because it belongs to the *kṣubhna*-class, there is no substitution of *ṇ* for *n*. *narīnṛtyate*. *arīgṛhyate*. In both cases, there is the substitution of *l* for *ṛ*. *calīkḷpyate*. It should be stated that *rīg* is added to a root ending in *ṛt*. *varīvṛścyate*. *parīpṛcchyate*. (A 6.1.19) *svapisyamivyeñāṃ yaṅi*:
There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the roots *svap*, *syam*, and *vyeñ* when *yaṅ* follows. *soṣupyate*. *sesimyate*. *vevīyate*.
SK 2646: [The substitution of] *va* for *vaś* does not occur;
thus, *vāvaśyate*.
SK 2647: [The substitution of] *kī* occurs for *cāy*.
He is made to tremble.
SK 2648: Before the suffix *ya*, [the vowel *i* is substituted for the final vowel] of the roots *ghrā* and *dhmā* (A 7.4.31).
Thus: *jeghrīyate*, *dedhmīyate*.
SK 2649: Before a suffix beginning with *y* that has *k* or *ṅ* as an indicatory letter (*yi kṅiti*), [the vowel *a* is substituted for the final vowel of a root] (A 7.4.22).

The substitution of *ayaṅ* for the root *śīṅ* occurs when followed by an affix beginning with *y* that has the markers *k* or *ṅ*. Thus: *śāśayyate*. There is shortening of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*), and then *guṇa* substitution. Thus: *ḍoḍhaukyate*, *totraukyate*. This concludes the derivation of the *yaṅ*-intensive forms.
Now begins the derivation of the *yaṅluk* (elided *yaṅ*) forms within the section on verbal suffixes (*tiṅanta*).

Pāṇini 2.4.74: *yaṅo 'ci ca*. After a *yaṅ*-intensive base, there shall be elision (*luk*) when the suffix *ac* follows; because of the word "ca," this elision occurs diversely even without that suffix. This [elision] is unconditional (*anaimittika*); because it is an internal operation (*antaraṅga*), it takes effect first. Thereafter, by the rule of suffixal characterization (*pratyayalakṣaṇa*), since the base ends in *yaṅ*, reduplication occurs. Then the operations pertaining to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) take place. Because it is now a verbal root (*dhātu*), the *laṭ* and other tense-affixes apply. By the rule *śeṣāt kartari—*, the *parasmaipada* endings are used. However, the rule *anudāttaṅita—* does not apply here, because since the property of being marked with *ṅ* (*ṅittva*) is common to both suffixes and non-suffixes, the rule of suffixal characterization does not operate [to trigger the *anudāttaṅita* rule].

For that [suffix] applies only where the unique form (*asādhāraṇa-rūpa*) of the suffix is relied upon. For this very reason, in the example *sudṛṣat-prāsāda*, the rule *atvasantasya* (Pāṇini 6.4.14) does not apply to produce a long vowel. Furthermore, it does not apply even to roots such as *spardh* and *śīṅ*, which are marked with the anubandha *ṅ* (indicating they are *anudātta-ṅit*), because of the specific mention of the anubandha *ṅ* in the rule *anudātta-ṅitaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.12). Moreover, in that context, there is a prohibition by the rule *śtipā śapā* (Pāṇini 3.1.89). For this same reason, suffixes such as *śyan* do not apply, because they are mentioned by their class name (*gaṇa*). Rather, only *śap* applies. However, in cases such as *car-karītam*, there is elision (*luk*) of *śap* due to its being read in the list beginning with *car-karītam ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.12). Regarding the suffix *yaṅ*: [the rule] *yaṅo vā* (Pāṇini 7.3.94).

The augment *īṭ* may optionally be applied to a *pitt* sārvadhātuka suffix beginning with a consonant that follows a stem ending in *yaṅ*. Regarding the prohibition of *guṇa* by the rule *bhusuvoḥ...* (Pāṇini 7.3.88), it does not apply in the case of the elision of *yaṅ* (*yaṅluk*) in the spoken language (*bhāṣā*). This is because forms such as *bobhūtu* and *tetikte* are established as archaic (*chandasi*) irregularities (*nipātana*). For this very reason, the form is established even in the spoken language when there is *yaṅluk*. Nor should it be argued that the absence of *guṇa* should be established as an irregularity (*nipātana*) specifically for cases where *yaṅluk* occurs and [the rule] would otherwise not apply. This is because a base form (*prakṛti*) includes its *yaṅluk* derivative as well, according to the established principle (*siddhānta*) that "doubling (*dvirvacana*) consists in the double utterance [of the root]. Thus, the rule applies to the *yaṅluk* form as well.

*bobhavīti*, *bobhoti*, *bobhūtaḥ*, *bobhuvati*; *bobhavāñcakāra*; *bobhavitā*; *abobhavīt*, *abobhot*, *avobhūtām*, *abobhavuḥ*; *bobhūyāt*, *bobhūyātām*, *bobhūyāstām*. By the rule *gātisthā-*, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *sic*. In the alternative where the augment *iṭ* is applied by the rule *yaṅo vā-*, the *ṭuk* augment applies because it is obligatory (*nitya*), overriding the *guṇa* substitution. Thus: *abobhūvīt*, *abobhot*, *abobhūtām*. By the rule *abhyastāśrayo jus*, the *jus* is substituted; because it is obligatory, the *guk* substitution takes effect. Thus: *abobhūvuḥ*. Similarly, *abobhaviṣyat*, etc.

*pāspardhīt* / *pāspardhi* / *pāspardhaḥ* / *pāspardhati*. In the *laṅ*: *apāspart* / *apāspard*. With the suffix *sip*, in the alternative where there is *rutva* (the substitution of *r*), by the rule *ro ri*, [it becomes] *apāspāḥ*. *jāgāddhi* / *jāghātsi*. In the *laṅ*: *ajāghāt*. With the suffix *sip*, in the alternative where there is *rutva*, [it becomes] *ajāghāḥ*. *nāthṛ*: *nānātti* / *nānāttaḥ*. *dadha*: *dādaddhi* / *dādaddhaḥ* / *dādhatsi*. In the *laṅ*: *adādhat* / *adādaddhām* / *adādadhuḥ* / *adādhaḥ* / *adādhat*. In the *luṅ*: *adādādhīt* / *adādadhīt*.

*coṣkūyate*, *coṣkūyante*; *acoṣkūt*, *acoṣkūtām*, *acoṣkūḥ*; *momudyate*, *momutti*, *momodāñcakāra*, *momuditā*, *amomudīt*, *amomot*, *amomuttām*, *amomuduḥ*, *amomudīḥ*, *amomoḥ*, *amomot*; [in the *luṅ* tense with *tip*: *acokūrt*, *acokūrdīt*; in the alternative form (*sippakṣe*): *acokūḥ*, *acokhūḥ*, *ajogūḥ*; *vanīvañcyate*, *vanīvaṅkti*, *vanīvaktaḥ*, *vanīvacati*, *avanīvañcīt*, *avanīvan*; *jaṅgamīti*.

*jaṅganti*. By the rule *abudāttopadeśa-* (Pāṇini 6.4.7), there is the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika-lopa*). *jaṅgataḥ*, *jaṅgmati*. [In the first person singular,] by the rule *mvoś ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.65), we have *jaṅganmi*, *jaṅganvaḥ*. Because the prohibition of *iṇ* has already been stated by the mention of "a single vowel" (*ekāj-grahaṇa*), there is no prohibition of *iṇ* here. *jaṅgamitā*. Since the elision of the nasal is considered *asiddha* (not yet established) according to the rule *abhīyatva*, there is no elision of *hi* (the imperative suffix). *jaṅgahi*. By the rule *mo no dhātoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.64), *m* becomes *n*: *ajaṅgan*. Because of the mention of the *anubandha* (indicatory letter), there is no *aṅ* substitution for *cli*. By the rule *hmyanta-*, there is no *vṛddhi* increment: *ajaṅgamīt*, *ajaṅgamiṣṭām*. [Likewise,] from the root *han* with *yaṅ*-elision (*yaṅ-luk*).

Regarding the statement "and from repetition" (*abhyāsāc ca*), although *kutva* (the substitution of *k*) was prescribed following the rule *ho hanteḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.54) by carrying forward the word *hanteḥ*, nevertheless, the author of the *Nyāsa* maintains that it indeed occurs in the case of *yaṅluk*. The sense is that the prohibition [of *kutva*] by the rule *śtipā śapā* (Pāṇini 1.2.4) is non-eternal (*anitya*), because there is an indicator (*jñāpaka*) based on a general consideration in the rule *guṇo yaṅlukoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.82). [Examples: *jaṅghanīti*, *jaṅghanti*, *jaṅghataḥ*, *jaṅghnati*, *jaṅghanitā*. Because of the mention with the suffix *śtip*, the substitution of *j* [for *han*] does not take place. *jaṅghahi*. *ajaṅghanīt*. *ajaṅghan*. *jaṅghanyāt*.

In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), however, we have *vadhyāt*, *avadhīt*, *avadhiṣṭām*, and so forth. There is no doubling (*dvitva*) of the substitute *vadh* because of the prohibition [by Pāṇini 1.1.59], "not for a non-reduplicated stem" (*anabhyāsasya*), due to its being a *sthānivadbhāva*. For that [term *anabhyāsasya*] is a qualifier of the verbal root (*dhātu*) in apposition, by virtue of the force of the *bahuvrīhi* compound. However, when preceded by the prefix *āṅ*, the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) applies by the rule *āṅo yamahanaḥ*; thus we have *ājaṅghate*, and so on. By the rule *utparasya...* (Pāṇini 7.4.89), there is no *guṇa* substitution because of the presence of the phoneme *t* (in *tapara*). But by the rule *hali ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.2), lengthening (*dīrgha*) would indeed occur.

Because that [substitution] is not established, it cannot be excluded by the rule regarding *tapara* (a vowel followed by *t*). *cañcurīti*, *cañcūrti*, *cañcūrtaḥ*, *cañcurati*, *acañcūrīt*, *acañcūḥ*. *caṅkhanīti*, *caṅkhanti*. By the rule *janasana-*, there is the substitution of *ā*. *caṅkhātaḥ*. By the rule *gamahana-*, there is the elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhālopa*). *caṅkhnati*, *caṅkhāhi*, *caṅkhanāni*, *acaṅkhanīt*, *acaṅkhan*, *acaṅkhātām*, *acaṅkhnuḥ*. By the rule *ye vibhāṣā*: *caṅkhāyāt*, *caṅkhanyāt*, *acaṅkhanīt*.

*a-caṅkṣānīt*. In the rule *uto vṛddhiḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.89), because of the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the prohibition *nābhyastasya* (Pāṇini 7.3.87), there is no vṛddhi after *ut*: *yoyoti*, *yoyavīti*, *ayoyavīt*, *ayoyot*, *yoyuyāt*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), there is lengthening: *yoyūyāt*. *ayoyāvīt*. *nonavīti*, *nonoti*. *jāheti*, *jāhāti*. Regarding *ī halyaghoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.113): *jāhītaḥ*. Here, for the root *jahāti*, none of these five rules apply: neither the *ātvam* [of *jahāti*] before *hi*, nor the elision [of the penultimate vowel] before *ya*, nor the *ghu*-designation, nor the *mā-sthā-* rule, nor the *er liṅi* rule. This is because of the specific mention (*nirdeśa*) using the *śtip* affix. Thus: *jāhati*, *jāhāsi*.

*Jāheṣi*, *jāhīthaḥ*, *jāhītha*, *jāhīti*; *ajāhet*, *ajāhāt*, *ajāhītām*, *ajāhuḥ*; *jāhīyāt*; in the benedictive (*āśis*), *jāhāyāt*; *ajāhāsīt*, *ajāhāsiṣṭām*; *ajāhiṣyat*. When [the suffix] is elided by *luk*, because there is no application of the rule for suffixal characteristics (*pratyayalakṣaṇa*), the substitution of *u* (as in *svapisyam*) does not occur. Because it is specified by its inclusion in the *rudādi* group, the augment *iṭ* is not applied. *Sāsvapīti*, *sāsvapti*, *sāsvaptaḥ*, *sāsvapati*; *asāsvapīt*, *asāsvap*; *sāsvapyāt*. However, in the benedictive, by the rule *vacisvapi-*, the substitution of *u* occurs: *sāsupyāt*. *Asāsvāpīt*, *asāsvapīt*.

SK 2652: *rug-rikau ca luki* (A 7.4.92). When there is elision (*luk*) [of *yaṅ*], the augmentments *ruk*, *rik*, and *rīk* are applied to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) of a root that has *ṛ* as its penultimate letter (*ṛdupadha*). SK 2653: *ṛtaś ca* (A 7.4.92). [The augment *iṭ* is also applied] after a root ending in *ṛ*.

The same applies even after a root ending in *ṛ*: *varvṛtīti*, *varivṛtīti*, *varīvṛtīti*; *varvarti*, *varivarti*, *varīvarti*; *varvṛtaḥ* (3), *varvṛtati* (3); *varvartāmāsa* (3); *varvartitā*. Because it is specified by its inclusion in the *gaṇa*, the rule *na vṛdbhyaś caturbhyaḥ* does not apply. *varvartiṣyati* (3); *avarvṛtīt* (3); *avarvart* (3). In the case where *s* is replaced by *r* according to *sipi daś ca*, the *r* is dropped by *ro ri*, resulting in *avarvāḥ* (3). Because it is specified by its inclusion in the *gaṇa*, the suffix *aṅ* is not applied; thus, *avarvartīt*. *carkarīti*.

3 / *carkarti* / *carikarti* / *carīkarti* / *carkṛtaḥ* 3 / *carkrati* 3 / *carkarāṃcakāra* 3 / *carkaritā* 3 / *acarkarīt* / *acarkaḥ* 3 / *carkṛyāt* 3 / [In the sense of a benediction (*āśiṣi*), *riṅ* is substituted: *carkriyāt* 3 / *acakārīt* 3 / [The rule] *ṛtaś ca* [does not apply here] because of the *tapara* (the short *ṛ*) vowel; [this applies to] *kṝ* in the sense of scattering (*vikṣepe*): *cākarti* / *tātarti* / *tātīrtaḥ* / *tātirati* / *tātīrhi* / *tātarāṇi* / *atātarīt* / *atātaḥ* / *atātīrtām* / *atātaruḥ* / *atātārīt*.

*atātāriṣṭām*, etc. [The derivation is as follows: From the root *ṛ* (to go), when the *yaṅ* suffix is elided (*yaṅluk*), after doubling, the *abhyāsa* (reduplicated syllable) undergoes substitution of *a* for *u* (*urat*), followed by replacement with *r* (*raparatvam*). Then, by the rule *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*, all but the first consonant of the reduplication is dropped. Next, the augment *ruk* is added. However, because of the rule *rigriko tu abhyāsasyāsavarṇe*, the vowel *i* replaces the *ṛ* of the *abhyāsa* (yielding *iy*). Thus we have *ararti* and *ariyarti*. In the third person singular present indicative: *ararīti* and *ariyarīti*. For the dual: *arṛtaḥ* and *ariyṛtaḥ*. In the plural: the suffix *jhi* becomes *at*. By *yaṇ* (vowel substitution), the *ṛ* is replaced by *ar*. Then, by the rule *ro ri*, the preceding *r* is elided. Note that this elision does not cause the *yaṇ* substitute to be treated as *sthānivat* (as if it were the original *ṛ*) when the subsequent operation is to be performed, because of the prohibition: "That which is *asiddha* (not yet established) regarding a preceding operation is not subject to the rules concerning *sthānivat*. Thus we have *ārati* and *ariyrati*.

Because of the mention of *śtip* in the rule for the *liṅ* (optative) suffix, there is no *guṇa* substitution by the rule *arti-rīṅ-...*, so [the root vowel remains] *ṛ*. Then there is *ṛ*-lopa, followed by lengthening: *āriyāt*, *ariyriyāt*, *arārīt*, *āriyārīt*. Regarding the root *gṛhū* in the sense of seizing: *jargṛhīti* (3), *jargarḍhi* (3), *jargṛḍhaḥ* (3), *jargṛhati* (3), *ajargharṭ* (3). But for the root *gṛhṇāti*: *jāgrahīti*, *jāgrāḍhi*. When *ṅit* suffixes beginning with *t* follow, there is *saṃprasāraṇa*. Because that [substitution] is *asiddha* due to being *bahiraṅga*, the *rug* and other substitutions do not apply. Thus: *jāgṛḍhaḥ*, *jāgṛhati*.

*Jāgrahīṣi*, *jāghrakṣi*. In the *luṭ* [future], *jāgrahitā*; however, there is no lengthening by the rule *graho 'liṭi*, because the term *ekācaḥ* (of a monosyllabic root) is understood as a governing factor (*anuvṛtti*) there. Mādhava, however, asserts lengthening, which contradicts the Bhāṣya. The root *gṛdh* [is used] in the sense of longing. *jargṛdhīti* (3x); *jargarddhi* (3x); *jargṛddhaḥ* (3x); *jargṛdhati* (3x); *jargṛdhīṣi* (3x); *jarghartsi* (3x). *Ajargṛdhīt* (3x): in the absence of the augment *īṭ*, there is *guṇa* substitution; then the elision of the *hal-ṅy-ādi* suffixes; then the substitution of *bhaṣ* [for the dental]; and finally the substitutions of *jaś* and *car*. Thus: *ajarghart* (3x).

*ajargṛddhām* (3). By the rule *sipi daś ca*, there is optionally *ru*-substitution, yielding *ajarghāḥ* (3). *ajargardhīt* (3). *ajargardhiṣṭām* (3). Regarding *pāpracchīti*: [the forms are] *pāpraṣṭi*. In the case of suffixes beginning with *ta* and so on, the *saṃprasāraṇa* substitution [of *ṛ* for *ṝ*] does not occur because of the mention [of the root] with the *śtip* affix (*pāpracchīti*). By the rule *cchvoḥ śūḍ*, *ś* is substituted [for the *ch*]. By the rule *vraśca*, *ṣ* is substituted [for the *ch*]. Thus: *pāprṣṭaḥ*. *pāpracchati*. *pāpraśmi*. *pāpracchvaḥ*. *pāpraśmaḥ*.

It is indicated in the *Bhāṣya* on the rule *cchvoḥ* that there is no *yaṅluk* for roots ending in *yakāra* or *vakāra* that undergo the substitution of *ūṭh*; this was made explicit by Kaiyaṭa. This [restriction] regarding the substitution of *ūṭh* applies specifically to the scope of the rule *cchvoḥ*. However, it is logical and in agreement with Mādhava and others that *yaṅluk* does indeed exist for the roots *sriv* and *mav*, which undergo the substitution of *ūṭh* according to the rule *jvaratvara-*; *mavya* (meaning "to bind") ends in *yakāra* and undergoes the substitution of *ūṭh*. Roots such as *tevṛ* and *devṛ* (meaning "to play" or "to sport") end in *vā*. *Haya* (meaning "to go") forms *jāhayīti* and *jāhati*.

*jāhataḥ* / *jāhayati* / *jāhayīṣi* / *jāhasi* / when the suffix *val* is elided, there is lengthening before suffixes beginning with *yañ*: *jāhāmi* / *jāhāvaḥ* / *jāhāmaḥ*. The root *harya* means "to move" and "to desire. *jāharyīti* / *jāharti* / *jāhartaḥ* / *jāharyati*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *jāharhi*. [In the imperfect: *ajāhaḥ* / *ajāhartām* / *ajāharyuḥ*. The root *mava* means "to bind. According to Pāṇini 6.4.20 (*jvaratvarasrivyavimavām upadhāyāś ca*), [the vowel is lengthened] for these roots as well as for the penultimate vowel [of the suffix].

In the case of roots such as *jvar* and others, when the suffixes *kvip* or *kvi* follow, provided they are characterized by a *jhal* consonant or an *anunāsika* (nasal) sound, the substitution of *ūṭh* occurs for the penultimate vowel and the following semivowel (*upadhā-vakāra*). Here, the condition *kṅiti* does not apply, as is seen in the form *otur* derived from the root *ava-* with the suffix *tun*. Furthermore, the term *anunāsika* is understood to carry over [from the previous rule]. This is seen in the form *om*, where the suffix *man* is added to *ava-*, resulting in the elision of the *ṭi* portion. In the absence of the augment *īṭ* and with the presence of *ūṭh*, there is *guṇa* substitution before a *pit* suffix. Thus: *māpnoti*, *māmavīti*, *māmūtaḥ*, *māmavati*, *māmoṣi*, *māmomi*, *māmāvaḥ*, *māmūmaḥ*, *māmūhi*, and *māmavāni*.
*amāmot*, *amāmoḥ*, *amāmoḥ*, *amāmavam*, *amāmāva*, *amāmūm*. [The root] *turvī* is used in the sense of "to injure. [In the intensive form] *totūrvīti*:

by *SK 2655 rāl lopaḥ* (A 6.4.21), there is elision of *ch* and *v* following a *repha* (*r*) when a suffix beginning with a *jhal* consonant and having an *anunāsika* follows. Thus, there is elision of the *v*. [Then] the *guṇa* substitution of the light penultimate vowel occurs.

SK 2656: *na dhātulopa ārdhadhātuke* (A 1.1.4). When an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix follows that causes the elision of a portion of the verbal root (*dhātu*), the *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* substitutions for the *ik* vowels do not occur; however, this prohibition does not apply here [in the following examples], because *tiP* and other such suffixes are not *ārdhadhātuka*. *totorti*: by *hali ca*, there is lengthening. *totūrtaḥ*. *totūrvati*. *tothorti*. *dodorti*. *murchā*: *momūrcchīti*, *momorti*, *mobhurtaḥ*, *momūrchatī* and so forth. The term *ārdhadhātuke* is a locative of scope (*viṣaya-saptamī*). Therefore, when the *yaṅ* is intended, *ajervī* applies: *vevīyate*. There is no *yaṅ-luk* (elision of *yaṅ*) for this [root].

Because the elision (*luk*) [of the suffix] removes the status of being a grammatical object (*viṣayatva*), the substitution of *vī* does not apply. Thus ends the section on the formation of the *yaṅ*-luṅ (reduplicated) stems.
This concludes the section on the formation of nominal roots (*nāmadhātu*) within the section on verbal suffixes (*tiṅanta*). 55.
Pāṇini 3.1.8: *supa ātmanaḥ kyac*.

The suffix *kyac* may optionally occur after a word ending in a case-suffix (*subanta*) that denotes the object of a desire (*iṣikarman*) and is related to the desirer (*eṣitṛ*), in the sense of "desiring. Because it is a part of a verbal root (*dhātu*), the case-suffix is elided by Pāṇini 2.4.71. Pāṇini 7.4.33: *kyaci ca*. [The penultimate vowel of the base is lengthened before *kyac*.]

The augment *īt* may optionally occur after this [root *i*]. He desires a son for himself: *putrīyati*. When the suffix *yi* follows, the final *v* and *ā* are elided: *gavyati*, *nāvyati*. However, the rule "the elision of *n* according to Śākalya" (*lopaḥ śākalyasya*) does not apply here, because it is not at the end of a word (*apadāntatvāt*). For it is stated: "In the domain of *kyac*, *naṭ* [is substituted for *nas*]" (*naḥ kye*).

In the *kyac* and *kyaN* affixes, only a word ending in *-n* (nānta) undergoes this change, and no other. By the *sannipāta-paribhāṣā*, the elision (*lopa*) of the *y* in *kyac* does not occur. Examples: *gavyāñcakāra*, *gavyitā*; *nāvyāñcakāra*, *nāvyitā*. [The elision of] *n*: *rājīyati*. And [the elision occurs] before an affix and in a subsequent member of a compound (*uttarapada*): *tvadyati*, *madyati*. Only when they have a single meaning (*ekārtha*). Examples: *yuṣmadyati*, *asmadyati*. And before a consonant (*hal*): *gīryati*, *pūryati*. Only after a verbal root (*dhātu*). Not here: *divamicchati* → *divyati*.

Regarding the statement by Mādhava that *puri* means "he wishes for a city" (*puram icchati puryati*), this counter-example is to be reconsidered, as it is identical to *pūḥ* (the root *pū*). As for the form *dīvyati*, the lengthening [of the vowel] is merely a mistake of the Easterners. *adasyati*. By the rule *rīṅ ṛtaḥ*: *kartrīyati*. And by the rule *kyac-vyoś ca*: *gārgīyati*; *vācyati*. The lengthening occurs by the rule *akṛt-sārvadhātuka-*. *kavīyati*; *samidhyati*.

SK 2660 *kyasya vibhāṣā* (A 6.4.50): After a consonant, the elision (*lopa*) of *kyac* and *kyaṅ* may optionally occur before an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix. By the rule *ādeḥ parasya*, the initial [portion] is affected; by *ato lopaḥ*, the *a* is elided. Because that [elision] is treated as if it were still present (*sthānivadbhāva*), the *guṇa* substitution for a light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadha*) does not take place. Examples: *samidhitā*, *samidhyitā*. The suffix *kyac* is not applied after a *subanta* (inflected noun) whose stem ends in *m*, nor after an indeclinable (*avyaya*). Examples: *kim icchati*, *idam icchati*, *svar icchati*. SK 2661 *aśanāyodanyadhanāyā bubhukṣāpipāsāgardheṣu* (A 7.3.34): The forms *aśanāyā*, *udanyā*, and *dhanāyā* are derived with *kyac* in the senses of hunger, thirst, and greed, respectively.

Derivatives ending in *kyac* are irregularly formed (*nipātita*). Examples: *aśanāyati*, *udanyati*, *dhanāyati*. Why [is this rule] stated for cases such as hunger? [Counter-examples: *aśanīyati*, *udakīyati*, *dhanīyati*. SK 2662: After the words *aśva*, *kṣīra*, *vṛṣa*, and *lavaṇa*, the suffix *kuñc* is applied when expressing one's own pleasure (*ātmaprīti*).

The augment *asuk* shall be added to these before the suffix *kyac*: to *aśva* and *vṛṣa* when there is a desire for sexual intercourse; thus, *aśvasyati vaḍavā* (“the mare desires [to mate with] the horse”) and *vṛṣasyati gauḥ* (“the cow desires [to mate with] the bull”). To *kṣīra* and *lavaṇa* when there is intense longing (*lālasā*); thus, *kṣīrasyati bālaḥ* (“the child longs for milk”) and *lavaṇasyati uṣṭraḥ* (“the camel longs for salt”). For all nominal stems (*prātipadika*) before *kyac* in the sense of longing, the augments *suk* and *asuk* are applied; thus, *dadhisyati* or *dadhyasyati* (“he longs for curd”), and *madhusyati* or *madhvasyati* (“he longs for honey”). [Pāṇini 3.1.9:
*kāmyac ca* (“and the suffix *kāmyac* [is applied after a nominal stem to express the agent’s desire for that object]”).

The suffix *kāmyac* shall occur in the sense already mentioned [i.e., "desiring"]. He desires a son for himself: *putrakāmyati*. Here, the elision [of the final consonant] by the rule *yasya halaḥ* does not apply, because [the suffix *kāmyac*] is devoid of meaning (*anarthakatva*). It has been stated that the term *yasya* refers to a cluster of sounds (*saṃghāta*). He desires glory: *yaśaskāmyati*. He desires clarified butter: *sarpiṣkāmyati*. This suffix should indeed occur even after words ending in *mām* and indeclinables (*avyaya*): *kiṃkāmyati*; *svaḥkāmyati*. A 3.1.10: *upamānād ācāre* ("After a word used as a standard of comparison, [the suffix *kvip* occurs] in the sense of behaving like that").

The suffix *kyac* occurs after a noun ending in a case-suffix (*subanta*) that functions as a standard of comparison (*upamāna*), in the sense of "behaving like" (*ācāra*). For example: *putram ivācarati* → *putrīyati chātram* ("he behaves toward the pupil as if toward a son"); *viṣṇum ivācarati* → *viṣṇūyati dvijam* ("he behaves toward the twice-born as if toward Viṣṇu"). It should be stated that this also applies after a word denoting a locus (*adhikaraṇa*): *prāsādīyati kuṭyāṃ bhikṣuḥ* ("the mendicant behaves in the hut as if on a palace") and *kuṭīyati prāsāde* ("he behaves in the palace as if in a hut"). [Pāṇini 3.1.11] *kyaṅ* occurs after a word denoting the agent (*kartṛ*), and there is the elision of the final *s*. (A 3.1.11) *kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaś ca*.

The suffix *kyaṅ* may optionally occur after a word ending in a case-suffix (*subanta*) that expresses a standard of comparison (*upamāna*), when the sense is "acting like" (*ācāra*). However, for a word ending in *-s* that denotes the agent, the elision (*lopa*) of that *-s* may optionally occur. Because it is stated "optionally *kyaṅ*," there is also a construction in the alternative case (e.g., a full sentence). The elision of the final *-s*, however, is taught as being conditioned by the occurrence of *kyaṅ* (*sanniyogaśiṣṭa*). And that [elision] is restricted (*vyavasthita*): it is obligatory for *ojas-* and *apsaras-*, while for others it is optional. He behaves like Kṛṣṇa: *kṛṣṇāyate*. In the context of grammatical function (*vṛtti*), the word *ojas-* refers to one who possesses vigor (*tadvat*): *ojāyate*. *Apsarāyate*. *Yaśāyate*. *Yaśasyate*.

*vidvāyate*, *vidvasyate*; *tvadyate*; *madyate*. However, when the roots have multiple meanings (*anekārthatva*), one has *yuṣmadyate* and *asmadyate*. Regarding the suffixes *kyaṅ* and *mānin*: [the following examples apply]: He acts like a young girl: *kumārāyate*. She acts like a doe: *haritāyate*. She acts like a teacher: *gurūyate*. She acts like a co-wife: *sapatnāyate*, *sapatīyate*, or *sapatnīyate*. She acts like a young woman: *yuvāyate*. They two act like the clever and the soft: *paṭvīmṛdūyate*. [The suffix *kyac*] is not applied after a word ending in a penultimate *ka*: *pācikāyate*.

In the sense of "conduct" (*ācāra*), the suffix *kvip* should optionally be stated after the roots *avagalbh*, *klīb*, and *hoḍ*. Because of the mention of the word "optionally" (*vā*), the suffix *kyaṅ* is also applied. The words *avagalbha* and so on end in the suffix *ac* (by *pacādyac*). By the rule of co-occurrence (*sanniyoga*) with *kvip*, it is declared that the suffix *ac* is both *anudātta* (unaccented) and nasalized (*anunāsika*). Consequently, the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) endings are used: *avagalbhate*, *klībate*, *hoḍate*. Even from a root that was previously polysyllabic (*anekāc*), the suffix *ām* is applied, by virtue of the force of the commencement of this specific Vārttika. Nor is the establishment of forms such as *avagalbhate* the sole result [of this rule].

Since verbal roots have multiple meanings (*anekārthatva*), the formation of a derivative (*vṛtti*) is possible even from the simple roots themselves in their usage; for example: *avagalbhāṃcakre*, *klībāṃcakre*, and *hoḍāṃcakre*. Mādhava and others maintain that because the word *ava* is specifically listed in the Vārttika, the suffix *kyaṅ* occurs only after this [specific root] when preceded by the prefix *ava*, as well as when preceded by other prefixes. However, it is more appropriate to say that the *taṅ* (the Ātmanepada endings) do not occur. It should be stated that *kvip* is optionally added to all nominal stems (*prātipadika*). As for the previous Vārttika, however, it is intended for the purpose of attaching an indicatory letter (*anubandha`); therein, *kvip* is merely restated.

Because of the mention of the *prātipadika* (nominal stem), the term *sup* (case ending) is not connected here; therefore, it does not undergo word-level operations (*padakārya*). *kṛṣṇa-iva ācarati* → *kṛṣṇati*: By the rule *ato guṇe*, there is a single substitute for the final vowel of the root and the initial vowel of the suffix *śap*. *a-iva ācarati* → *ati*: [The suffix] *at*. *ataḥ*, *anti*: [The suffixes] *at* and *anti*. Having removed the requirement for the mention of a suffix (*pratyayagrahaṇa*), the form *anekāc* is stated, resulting in *nām*. *au*, *atuḥ*, *uḥ*: [The suffixes] *au*, *atus*, and *u*. There is reduplication. By *ato guṇe* and *ata ādeḥ*, there is lengthening. By *ṇal*, there is *vṛddhi*. However, in the case of *atus* and the others, by *āto lopa iṭi ca*, there is elision of the long *ā*.

*Mālāti* means "she acts like a garland" (*mālā ivācarati*). By the *paribhāṣā* regarding gender-distinction (*liṅgaviśiṣṭaparibhāṣā*), or because the single-substitute (*ekādeśa*) is treated as the end of the preceding element (*pūrvāntatva*), the suffix *kvip* is applied. [In the perfect tense: *mālāṃcakāra*. In the *laṅ*: *amālāt*. Here, there is no elision by the rule *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal* (P. 6.1.68), because the elision of *s* after *āp* is prescribed only for the nominative singular (*su*) due to its association with *gi* (as in *gīḥ*). With the addition of *iṭ* and *suk*: *amālāsīt*. Like a poet (*kavi*), he acts like a poet: *kavayati*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *kavīyāt*.

Regarding the rule *sicivṛddhiḥ* ("vṛddhi [substitution] occurs before the suffix *sici*"), Kaiyaṭa and others maintain that by carrying forward (*anuvartana*) the term "root" (*dhātu*) from the previous context and interpreting it as "only that which is a root is a root," there is no *vṛddhi* for denominative roots (*nāmadhātu*). Examples include *akavāyīt*. However, Mādhava maintains that *vṛddhi* does occur even for denominative roots; examples include *akavāyīt*, *vir iva vayati* ("he weaves like a bird")—from which *vivāya*, *vivyatuḥ*, *avayīt*, and *avāyīt*—and *śrīr iva śrayati* ("he rests like Śrī")—from which *śiśrāya* and *śiśriyāt*—as well as *bhūr iva bhavati* ("he exists like the earth").

In this context, the rules *gāti-sthā-*, *bhuvo vuk*, and *bhavateraḥ* do not apply, because only that which is present in the Dhātupāṭha is understood there by virtue of being explicitly manifested [as a verbal root]. Thus: *bubhāva*; *abhāvīt*. In *drur iva dravati* ("he runs like a tree"), the suffix *caṅ* does not occur after the causative marker *ṇi* due to the rule *ṇi-śri-*. Thus: *adrāvīt*. [This is governed by] A 6.4.15: *anunāsikasya kvijhaloḥ kṅiti*.

A long vowel shall be substituted for the penultimate vowel of a stem ending in a nasal (anunāsika) before a *kvip* suffix and before a *kṅit* suffix beginning with a *jhal* consonant. Examples: *idam ivācarati* → *idāmati* (he acts like this). *rājeva* → *rājānati* (he acts like a king). *panthā iva* → *pathīnati* (he acts like a path). *mathīnati* (he acts like a mathematician). *ṛbhukṣīṇati* (he acts like Indra). *Mādhava* says that *dyaur iva* → *devatī* (she acts like heaven), but in this case, it is more appropriate to say *dyavatī* after the substitution of *ūṭh*. *ka iva* → *kati* (he acts like "who"?). Haradatta says that *cakāv* [is derived from *ka*] by applying *kvip*. However, Mādhava, based on the rule *ṇyallopau*, states that the form is *caka* because the *vṛddhi* is blocked by the *ṇal* suffix and the subsequent elision (*lopa*) of the vowel *a*.
*sva* becomes *svati*, *sasvau*, and *sasva*. As for the statement that "the master (*svāmī*) caused himself to swell (*svāṃcakāra*)," that is simply without authority.
[This is according to] A 3.1.12: *bhṛśādibhyo bhuvyacver lopaś ca halaḥ*.

The suffix *kyaṅ* occurs after words such as *bhṛśa* (intense) and others that signify the transformation from one state to another (*abhūtatadbhāva*), provided they end in a consonant; furthermore, there is elision (*lopa*) of these [words]. For example: *abhṛśo bhṛśo bhavati* ("that which was not intense becomes intense") results in *bhṛśāyate*. By virtue of the exclusion (*paryudāsa*) of the word *acveḥ* ("not ending in a vowel"), it is understood that this applies specifically to the "transformation from one state to another. Therefore, it does not apply here: *kva divā bhṛśā bhavanti* ("Where do the intense ones become so by day?"). The meaning is: "Where do those stars and other luminaries that are intense at night become [so] during the day? In the case of *sumanas*, there is elision of the *s*: *sumanāyate*.

In the *curādi* class, the root *saṃgrām* is recited in the sense of "fighting. Here, *saṃgrāma* is a nominal stem (*prātipadika*). From that, the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is established by the rule *tat karoti*. Along with that [suffix], the indicatory letter (*anubandha*) is attached. Even though it is stated, "the word *grāma* which occurs in the sense of fighting," the specific recitation of *saṃgrāma* indicates—by virtue of the contextual force—that when a suffix that triggers the designation "verbal root" (*dhātu*) is intended, a preceding member that has the same form as a prefix (*upasarga*) is separated [from the following part].

From that [rule], [the suffix] *āṬ* follows after the word *manas*: *svamanāyate*, *unmanāyate*, *udamanāyata*. In the same way, it should be understood that in cases such as *avāgalbhata* and *avāgalbhiṣṭa*, there is a separation of the element *ava*. Furthermore, this indicative authority (*jñāpaka*) applies to its own class of similar forms. Therefore, the separation occurs only where the entire form of the prefix is heard and has not been replaced by a substitute. And thus, in *ā ūḍhaḥ = oḍhaḥ*, acting like one who is so (*oḍhāyitvā*), there is no *lyap* suffix, unlike in the cases of *unmanāyya* and *avagalbhyā*.

Regarding the fact that an indicator (*jñāpaka*) has a specific scope, the sixth-century *Vārttika* and its commentary (*bhāṣya*) serve as the authority. To explain: there is a prohibition of *āṭ* after *usi*, *om*, and *āṅ*. That is to say, when *usi*, *om*, or *āṅ* follow, the single-substitute (*pararūpa*) [prescribed by A 6.1.94] for *āṭ* does not occur. Thus, *ausrīyat* (he wished for a cow), *auṅkārīyat* (he wished for the sound *oṃ*), and *auḍhīyat* (he wished for the sound *auḍh*) are formed. It is established in the sixth book (*ṣaṣṭha*) that this is accomplished because the word "and" (*ca*) in the rule *āṭaś ca* (A 6.1.90) serves to re-enjoin the rule for *vṛddhi*.
SK 2668: *lohitādi-ḍājbhyaḥ kyaṣ* (A 3.1.13). The suffix *kyaṣ* occurs after the group beginning with *lohita* and after words ending in *ḍāc*, in the sense of "becoming that."

SK 2669: *vā kyaṣaḥ* (A 1.3.90). After a verbal base ending in *kyaṣ*, the *parasmaipada* endings may optionally occur. [Examples: *lohitāyati*, *lohitāyate*. Here, by the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the rule *acveḥ*, it is established that the scope is restricted to cases of "becoming what one was not" (*abhūtatadbhāva*). That [restriction] is a qualifier of the word *lohita* alone, and not of the suffix *ḍāc*, because [the formation of a *ḍāc*-derivative] is impossible; nor does it apply to those [bases] included under the word "and so forth" (*ādi*), because that [extension] has been rejected. Thus says the Vārttika: "The addition of *kyaṣ* after *lohita* and *ḍāc*-derivatives [is prescribed]; the others [are included] among the *bhṛśādi* group."

Nor should it be argued that, as in the case of *kāmyac*, the *k* of *kyaṣ* would likewise be audible due to the power of its pronunciation; for that [the audibility of *k*] is also refuted in the Bhāṣya. [Examples: *paṭapaṭāyati*, *paṭapaṭāyate*. Here, *ḍāc* occurs even without connection to the roots *kṛ*, *bhū*, or *as*, because of the power of the rule prescribing *kyaṣ* after a stem ending in *ḍāc*. As for the verse: "Red, dark-blue, and suffering; joy, pride, and happiness; Fainting, sleep, pity, smoke, compassion, and constant cruelty. (1)

Having recited this, some cite two forms ending in *kyaṣ* even for roots such as *śyām-*; however, that contradicts the Bhāṣya and the Vārttika. Therefore, from those roots, only *kyaṅ* applies. By the paribhāṣā regarding words qualified by gender (*liṅgaviśiṣṭaparibhāṣā*), *kyaṣ* also applies after the word *lohinī*: *lohinīyati*, *lohinīyate*. [Pāṇini 3.1.14: *kaṣṭāya kramaṇe*.

The suffix *kyaṅ* occurs after the word *kaṣṭa* ending in the fourth case (*caturthyanta*) in the sense of "endeavoring" (*utsāha*). *Kaṣṭāya kramate* becomes *kaṣṭāyate*; the meaning is that he endeavors to commit an evil act. It should be stated [as a rule] that *kyaṅ* occurs after *satra*, *kakṣa*, *kaṣṭa*, *kṛcchra*, and *gahana* in the sense of desiring to perform an evil act (*kaṇvacikīrṣā*). *Kaṇva* means "evil. In the context of grammatical derivation (*vṛtti*), these words—*satra* and the others—signify "evil. From these, when they end in the second case (*dvitīyānta*), *kyaṅ* occurs in the sense of desiring to perform [an evil act]. The analysis (*vigraha*) of "desiring to perform an evil act" is not expressed by its own constituent parts (*asvapadavigraha*). Thus: *satrāyate*, *kakṣāyate*, and so forth.

SK 2671: *karmaṇo romanthatapobhyāṃ varticaroḥ* (A 3.1.15). After the two objects *romantha* and *tapas*, the suffix *kyaṅ* is applied respectively in the senses of "turning over" (*vartanā*) and "wandering" (*caraṇa*). *romanthaṃ vartayati* becomes *romanthāyate*. It should be stated that this refers to the movement of the jaw. The meaning is "chewing again after drawing back what has been chewed. In this case, [the rule does not apply to] "the insect turns over its *romantha*. Here, *romantha* refers to the substance that has emerged from the region of the anus; the meaning is "it eats that," says Kaiyaṭa. The author of the Nyāsa and Haradatta say the meaning is "he makes it round."
And for the root *tap*, the *parasmaipada* endings are used. He performs penance: *tapaś carati* → *tapasyati*.

(A 3.1.16) After the two [words] *bāṣpa* and *ūṣman*, when meaning "to emit," the suffix *kyaṅ* is applied. He emits steam: *bāṣpam udvamati* → *bāṣpāyate*; *ūṣmāyate*. It should be stated that it also applies after *phena*: *phenāyate*.

SK 2673: *śabdavairakalahābhrakaṇvameghebhyaḥ karaṇe* (A 3.1.17). From these [words] as objects, the suffix *kyaṅ* occurs in the sense of "doing" (*karoti*). One makes sound: *śabdāyate*. According to the *Nyāsa*, it is also accepted that the causative suffix *ṇic* applies in the sense of "doing that," as in *śabdayati*. Also from *sudinadurdinanīhārebhyaḥ*: *sudināyate*. SK 2674: *sukhādibhyaḥ kartṛdevanāyām* (A 3.1.18). [The suffix *kyaṅ* occurs after words beginning with *sukha* when the agent is the object of play.]

The suffix *kyaṅ* may be added after the words *sukha* and others when they function as objects in the sense of "feeling," provided that these [words] denote the feeling itself as the agent. For example: *sukhaṃ vedayate* ("he feels pleasure"). Why is the mention of the "agent" (*kartṛ*) necessary? [To exclude cases like: *parasya sukhaṃ vedayate* ("he causes another to feel pleasure"). By the rule *namas-varivas-citraṅaḥ kyac* (A 3.1.19), with the word "instrument" (*karaṇe*) understood from the previous context, [the suffix *kyac* is added] in the sense of a specific action: namely, worship (*pūjā*), service (*paricaryā*), and wonder (*āścarya*). Examples: *namasyati devān* ("he pays homage to the gods")—the meaning is "he worships. *varivasyati gurūn* ("he serves his teachers")—the meaning is "he attends upon them. *citrīyate*—"he is amazed"—the meaning is "he is struck with wonder. Others say it means "he causes wonder."

SK 2676: *puccha-bhāṇḍa-cīvara-ṇiṅ* (A 3.1.20). After the words *puccha*, [the suffix] *ṇiṅ* is applied in the senses of tossing up (*udasanam*), scattering (*vyasanam*), and turning over (*paryasanam*). Tossing up is lifting up in various or contrary ways. Examples: *utpucchayate*, *vipucchayate*, *paripucchayate*. After *bhāṇḍa*, [it is used] in the sense of collecting together (*samācayanam*). Example: *saṃbhāṇḍayate*. This means he collects the goods; the meaning is that he makes them into a heap. Example: *samavabhāṇḍata*. After *cīvara*, [it is used] in the senses of acquiring (*arjanam*) and wearing (*paridhānam*). Example: *saṃcīvarayate* a monk. This means he acquires robes or he puts them on.
The causative suffix *ṇic* is applied after the words *muṇḍa*, *miśra*, *ślakṣṇa*, *lavaṇa*, *vrata*, *vastra*, *hala*, *kala*, *kṛta*, and *tūsta*. (A 3.1.21)

In the sense of the root *kṛ* (to do/make): *muṇḍam karoti* becomes *muṇḍayati* (he shaves). From *vrata* (vow), in the sense of eating or abstaining from food: *payaḥ* or *śūdrānnam vratayati* (he takes milk or the food of a Śūdra as his vow). From *vastra* (clothing), in the sense of dressing: *saṃvastrayati* (he dresses). From *hali* and others, in the sense of seizing: *hali* and *kali* undergo the irregularity (*nipātana*) of having their final vowel dropped; thus, *halim* or *kalim gṛhṇāti* becomes *halayati* (he seizes a plough) or *kalayati* (he seizes strife). *Hali* means a large plough. Because the rule for Vṛddhi replacement would apply later, yet by the principle of "acting as if desired" (*iṣṭavadbhāva*), only the suffix *a* is elided; therefore, the rules for *sanvadbhāva* and lengthening do not apply.

*ajahalat*, *acakalat*; he takes what has been done (*kṛtam gṛhṇāti*), *kṛtayati*; he pulls out the *tūsta*s (tufts), *vitūstayati*. Some say *tūsta* means "hair," others say it means "matted hair," and others say it means "sin. It would have been more appropriate to read *muṇḍa* and the others in that very same rule [Pāṇini 3.1.25], *satyāpapāśa-*, etc., since the formation is already established by the rule "from a nominal stem, in the sense of verbal action" (*prātipadikād dhātvarthe*). The inclusion of some of them is for the sake of adding the causative suffix (*ṇic*) even when they are used dependently: *muṇḍayati māṇavakam* ("he shaves the boy"), *miśrayaty annam* ("he mixes the food"), *ślakṣṇayati vastram* ("he smooths the cloth").

"Lavaṇayati" means "to season a condiment. [The mention of] *halika* and *kalika* is for the sake of showing that they end in short vowels; [the mention of] *satya* is for the sake of showing the insertion of *āpuk*; however, for some, it is for the sake of elaboration (*prapañca*). One who makes true or declares what is true is "satyāpayati. The suffix *āpuk* should also be stated after *artha* and *veda*: *arthāpayati*, *vedāpayati*. One who releases a noose is "vipāśayati. One who sees a form is "rūpayati. One who sings along with a lute is "upavīṇayati. One who scrapes along with cotton is "anutūlayati."

The meaning is that he touches the tip of a blade of grass with cotton. He praises with verses; thus, one says *upaślokayati*. He marches against with an army; thus, one says *abhiṣeṇayati*. According to the rule "after a prefix, [the *s* of] *sunoti* etc. becomes *ṣ*," we have *abhyaṣeṇayat*. According to the rule "before a suffix beginning with *s* which has an indicatory *k* or *ṅ*," we have *abhiṣiṣeṇayiṣati*. According to the rule "in the case of roots beginning with *sthā* and others, as well as after a reduplication, [the *s* becomes *ṣ*]," we have *ṣ*. He strokes the hairs; thus, one says *anulomayati*. The root *tvac* is used in the sense of covering. With the suffix *gha*, we have *tvac* (skin). He takes hold of the skin; thus, one says *tvacayati*. He equips himself with armor; thus, one says *saṃvarmayati*.

One takes up color (*varṇa*) or describes it; one scatters with powders (*cūrṇa*) or covers with them. By the extension [of rules] as if they were desired (*iṣṭavat*), there is the substitution of the masculine form (*puṃvadbhāva*) and so forth. One describes a dark woman (*enī*) as *etayati*; one describes a Darada woman as *dāradayati*. One makes broad (*pṛthu*) wide, *prathayati*. When the vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) occurs, the suffixal *ṭi* is optionally elided first: *apiprathat* or *apaprathat*. One makes soft (*mṛdu*) pliable, *mradayati*; [the aorist is] *amimradat* or *amamradat*. For *bhṛśa*, *kṛśa*, and *dṛḍha*: one makes intense, *bhraśayati*; one makes thin, *kraśayati*; one makes firm, *draḍhayati*; [the aorist is] *ababhraśat*.

*acakraśat*, *adadraḍhat*, *parivraḍhayati*, *paryavavraḍhat*, *aujiḍhat* (from *ūḍhim ākhyat*). Because the substitution of *ḍha* and so forth is considered *asiddha* (unestablished) [for the purposes of reduplication], there is reduplication of the word *hūti*. It has been stated that the rule "that which is *asiddha* in a preceding operation does not apply when reduplication is involved" is non-permanent (*anitya*). According to others, there is reduplication of the syllable *ḍhi*; thus [the forms] *auḍiḍhat* (from *ūḍham ākhyat*) and *aujaḍhat* (from *oḍham ākhyat*), *auḍaḍhat* (from *oḍham ākhyat*). In the rule *oḥ puyaṇjyapare* (Pāṇini 7.4.80), the inclusion of the class-consonant (*varga*) and the *pratyāhāra* *ja* is an indicative mark (*liṅga*).

Regarding the formation of the dual number, it was stated in the discussion on *ūnayati* that there is no substitution for the *ac* (the penultimate vowel) when the causative suffix *ṇic* is applied. [The rule] *prakṛtyaikāc* applies; [then] the *vṛddhi* and *puk* augmentations follow. Thus, *svāpayati*. In the case of *tvāpayati* ("he causes you to speak") and *māpayati* ("he causes me to speak"), where *tvām* and *mām* are the objects, the forms *tvam* and *mam* are substituted for them. Because the *ṭilopa* (elision of the final *am*) is obligatory (*nitya*), it occurs prior to the *pararūpa* (single-substitute) operation. Then the *vṛddhi* and *puk* are applied, resulting in *tvādayati* and *mādayati*. However, this is not correct; rather, *tvāpayati* and *māpayati* are the proper forms. This is because the *pararūpa* is internal (*antaraṅga*) and is applied first; once it has been applied, the *prakṛtibhāva* (preservation of the original form) takes effect by the rule *prakṛtyaikāc*.

One should not fall into the error of thinking that the *prakṛtibhāva* (the preservation of the original form) has been rejected in the Bhāṣya; for the Bhāṣya merely intends to show that [the rule] is otherwise established (*anyathāsiddhi*) in specific examples such as *preṣṭha*. [Examples: From *yuvām* or *āvām*, one forms *yuṣmayati* or *asmayati*. From *śvan*, one forms *śāvayati*; here, there is elision of the *ṭi* by the rule *na staddhite*. However, the *prakṛtibhāva* does not subvert the rule *ṭeḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.143) according to the maxim *yena nāprāpte*, because that [maxim] applies specifically to that [rule]. Due to its being a *bha*-stem, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). Others, however, maintain that the rule *na staddhite* is not extended here.

Because [the suffix] *iṣṭhan* is not seen [in such cases], and because in examples such as *brahmiṣṭhaḥ*, the rule *ṭeḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.155) applies by virtue of its higher status, they say that the form is *śunayati*. Regarding *vidvāṃsam ācaṣṭe* ("he describes one who knows"), it becomes *vidayati*. Some hold that, by the *aṅgavṛttaparibhāṣā* (the metarule concerning operations within a base), there is no *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization). Others hold that after *saṃprasāraṇa*, *vṛddhi*, and the substitution of *āv*, it is *vidāvayati*. Others again hold that because the *ṭilopa* (elision of the final vowel) is obligatory, *saṃprasāraṇa* occurs before it; then, because it is *antaraṅga* (internal), the *pūrvarūpa* (single-substitute replacement) occurs first, followed by *ṭilopa*, resulting in *vidayati*. Thus say others.

He describes one who is facing upward (*udañc*): *udīcayati*; [in the past tense] *udaicicat*. [He describes one who is facing] toward (*pratyañc*): *pratīcayati*; [in the past tense] *pratyacicat*—this is according to the alternative view of *prakṛtibhāva* (the preservation of the original form) by the rule *iko ’savarṇe*. Alternatively, [according to the other view], *pratiacicat*. He describes one who is facing together (*samyañc*): *samīcayati*; [in the past tense] *samyacicat* or *samiacicat*. He describes one who is facing crosswise (*tiryañc*): *tirāyayati*. Even though the suffix *ṭi* is elided by the rule for *añc*, the substitution of *tiras* for *tiri* takes place because the elision of *ṭi* is considered *asiddha* (non-existent) due to its being *bahiraṅga* (external). By the maxim of *ciṇ* in the *luṅ* [tense]—namely, "that which is *asiddha* here"—the first elision of *ṭi* is treated as non-existent.

Therefore, there is no elision of the *ṭi* [the final vowel and following consonant] again, either by the *aṅgavṛttaparibhāṣā* (the maxim that what occurs during the formation of a stem is considered as having already taken effect) or otherwise. Because it is not an *aglopi* (one whose suffixal portion is elided) in the *caṅ* [reduplication], the shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhāhrasva*) does not apply. Thus: *atitirāyat*. He speaks of one who is turned together (*sadhryañcam*): *sadhrāyayati*; *asasadhrāyat*. Of one who is turned everywhere (*viṣvadryañcam*): *aviviṣvadrāyat*. Of one who is turned toward the gods (*devadryañcam*): *devadrāyayati*; *adidevadrāyat*. Of one who is turned toward the mountains (*adadryañcam*): *adadadrāyat*. Of one who is turned toward that person (*adamuyañcam*): *adamuāyayati*; *ādadamuāyat*. Of one who is turned toward that person over there (*amumuyañcam*): *amumuāyayati*. In the *caṅ*: *āmumuāyayat*.

He causes the earth to exist: *bhāvayati*. He caused it to exist: *abībhavat*. He causes the brow to exist: *bhruvam abubhravat*. He causes prosperity to exist: *śriyam aśiśrayat*. He causes a cow to exist: *gām ājūgavat*. He causes wealth to exist: *rāyam arīrayat*. He causes a boat to exist: *nāvam anūnavat*. He causes his own self to exist: *svasvam svāśaśvat*. [In the case of] indeclinables, there is the elision of the *ṭi* (the final vowel and following consonant) when the suffix *bha* follows: *svayati*. He caused it to exist: *asasvat*, *asisvat*. He causes many to exist: *bahūn bhāvayati*; others say *bahayati*. There is elision by the rule *vinmator luk*. He causes one who possesses a garland (*sragvin*) to possess a garland: *srajayati*; because the formation is based on a technical designation (*saṃjñāpūrvakatva*), there is no *vṛddhi* strengthening. He causes one who is prosperous (*śrīmatī* or *śrīmanta*) to possess prosperity: *śrayayati*.

*aśiśrayat* / *payasvinīm* / *parisayati*. Here, there is no elision of the suffix *ṭi*, because the *luk*-elision, which is an exception to it, has taken effect. *sthūlam* becomes *sthavayati*; *dūram* becomes *davayati*. How then is it that one says *dūrayaty avanate vivasvatī*? [The meaning is: she stretches out to a distance, or she goes to a distance; the sense is "making it far-reaching. *yuvānam* becomes *yavayati* or *kanayati*; or, by the rule *yuvālpayoḥ...* [the suffix] *kan* is applied. *antikam* becomes *nedayati*; *bāḍham* becomes *sādhayati*; *praśasyam* becomes *praśasyayati*.

In this context, *śrajyau* do not [apply], because of the separation of the prefix. [Examples: *vṛddhaṃ jyāpayati* (he causes the aged to grow), *varṣayati* (he causes to rain); *priyaṃ prāpayati* (he causes to reach what is dear); *sthiraṃ sthāpayati* (he causes to stand firm); *sphiraṃ sphāpayati* (he causes to expand); *uruṃ varayati* (he causes to become wide) or *vārayati*; *bahulaṃ baṃhayati* (he causes to increase); *guruṃ garayati* (he causes to become heavy); *tṛpraṃ trāpayati* (he causes to become soft); *dīrghaṃ drāghayati* (he causes to lengthen); *vṛndārakaṃ vṛndayati* (he treats as a distinguished person). Thus ends the derivation of denominative verbs (*nāmadhātuprakriyā*).

Under the section on verbal suffixes (*tiṅanta*), the *kaṇḍvādi* group [is treated]: A 3.1.27 states that the suffix *yak* is added after the roots *kaṇḍū* and others. After these roots, *yak* is invariably applied in the sense of the root itself (*svārtha*). Why "after roots" (*dhātubhyaḥ*)? So that it does not apply after nominal stems (*prātipadika*). For the *kaṇḍvādi* items are of two kinds: they are both roots and nominal stems. 1945. *kaṇḍūñ* in the sense of scratching the body. *kaṇḍūyati*, *kaṇḍūyate*. 1946. *mantu* in the sense of offense. Some say it means "anger. *mantūyati*. Candragomin, however, says it is marked with Ñ (*ñit*), thus: *mantūyate*. 1947. *valgu* in the sense of worship and sweetness. *valgūyati*. 1948. *asu* in the sense of lack of distress. *asū*.

Some [say] *asūn*: *asyati*, *asūyati*, *asūyate*. 1949 *leṭ* (1950 *loṭ*): in the sense of theft, prior existence, and dreaming; some say "in the sense of shining. *leṭyati*, *leṭitā*; *loṭyati*, *loṭitā*. 1951 *lelā*: in the sense of shining. 1952 *iras*, 1953 *iraj*, 1954 *irañ*: in the sense of envy. *irasyati*; *irajyati*—[here] there is lengthening by the rule *hali ca*; *īryati*, *īryate*. 1955 *uṣas*: in the sense of the state of dawn. 1956 *veda*: in the sense of theft and dreaming.

1957. *medhā* in the sense of quick apprehension: *medhāyati*. 1958. *kuṣubha* in the sense of throwing: *kuṣubhyati*. 1959. *magadha* in the sense of surrounding; others say "acting as a low servant. 1960. *tanta* and 1961. *pampas* in the sense of suffering. 1962. *sukha* and 1963. *duḥkha* in the sense of performing those [actions]. 1964. *sapara* in the sense of honoring. 1965. *arara* in the sense of the work of spokes (or a spoke). 1966. *bhiṣaj* in the sense of medical treatment. 1967. *bhiṣṇaj* in the sense of service. 1968. *iṣudha* in the sense of holding arrows. 1969. *caraṇa* and 1970. *varaṇa* in the sense of going.

1971. *curaṇ* in the sense of stealing (*caurye*). 1972. *turaṇ* in the sense of haste (*tvarāyām*). 1973. *bhuraṇ* in the sense of supporting and nourishing (*dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*). 1974. *gadgada* in the sense of faltering speech (*vākskhalane*). 1975–1977. *elā*, *kelā*, and *khelā* in the sense of play (*vilāse*). 1978. Others say *ilā* [is used] in this sense. 1979. *lekhā* in the sense of stumbling (*skhalane*) as well. Others say this root ends in a vowel (*adanta*); thus, [the form] is *lekhayati*. 1980. *liṭ* in the sense of smallness and censure (*alpakutsanayoḥ*); [the form] is *liṭyati*. 1981. *lāṭa* in the sense of living (*jīvane*). 1982. *hṛṇīṅ* in the sense of anger (*roṣaṇe*) and shame (*lajjāyām*). 1983. *mahīṅ* in the sense of honoring (*pūjāyām*); [the form] is *mahīyate*.

The meaning is "he receives worship. 1984 *rekhā* [is used] in the sense of praise and attainment. 1985 *dravas* in the sense of heating and attending to. 1986 *tiras* in the sense of disappearance. 1987 *agada* in the sense of being free from disease. 1988 *uras* has the sense of strength; *urasyati* means "he becomes strong. 1989 *taraṇa* in the sense of going. 1990 *payas* in the sense of spreading. 1991 *saṃbhūyas* in the sense of becoming abundant. 1992 *aṃbara* and 1993 *saṃvara* in the sense of gathering or supporting. This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class). Thus end the *kaṇḍvādigaṇa* roots. [Section on] the series of suffixes in the section on verbal endings (*tiṅanta*). 57.

Regarding the desiderative (*san*) of *kaṇḍūy* (to scratch): when the doubling of the first monosyllabic element (*ekāc*) is about to occur by the rule *sanyaṅoḥ*, it should be stated that for roots beginning with *kaṇḍū*, the third [element] is doubled. Thus: *kaṇḍūyiyiṣati*. From a root ending in *kyac*: "In nominal stems (*nāmadhātu*), there is doubling of whichever one is desired among the first three. This means that among the first three elements, any one may be doubled. However, for those beginning with a vowel (*ajādi*), it is the one other than the first that is doubled. Thus: *puputrīyiṣati*, *putitrīyiṣati*, *putrīyiyiṣati*; *aśiśvīyiṣati*, *aścīyiyiṣati*.

When nasals are conjoined, there is a prohibition of doubling for the vowel that follows them. From the root *indrīya* with the suffix *san*, there is doubling of either the syllable *drī* or the syllable *yi*. Thus: *indridrīyiṣati*, *indrīyiyiṣati*, *cicandrīyiṣati*, *candridrīyiṣati*, *candrīyiyiṣati*. He desires to urge someone who is in the process of announcing or declaring what is dear: *piprāpayiṣati*, *prāpipayiṣati*, *prāpayiyiṣati*. He desires to cause [something] wide to be opened: *vivārayiṣati*, *vārirayiṣati*, *vārayiyiṣati*.

The three forms beginning with *sisādhayiṣati* are indeed valid; however, there is no change of *s* to *ṣ*, because it is stated that the substitute is the letter *s*. Thus: from *yaṅ*, *san*, and the causative (*ṇic*) suffix comes *bobhūyiṣayiṣati*; from *yaṅ*, *ṇic*, and the desiderative (*sannanta*) followed by *ṇic* comes *bobhūyayiṣayatī*, and so forth.
This concludes the series of suffixes (*pratyayamālā*).
The section on the formation of the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) endings in verbal conjugation (58).
The *ātmanepada* endings are used for roots marked with an *anudātta* accent or the suffix *ṅ*. Examples: *āste*, *śete*. [Regarding the rule] A 1.3.13 *bhāvakarmaṇoḥ*:
*babhūve*, *anubabhūve*.

SK 2680 *kartari karmavyatihāre* (A 1.3.14): When the reciprocal exchange of actions (*kriyāvinimaya*) is to be expressed, the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) shall be used in the active sense (*kartari*). Example: *vyatilunīte*. The meaning is that one person performs the act of cutting suitable for another. [In *lunāti*,] there is the elision of the *a* of *śn* and *as* [by A 6.4.111]. *vyatiste*; *vyatiṣāte*; *vyatiṣate*. [In the present indicative,] there is the elision of *s* by the rule *tāsastyoḥ...* [A 7.4.50]: *vyatise*. [In the second person plural,] by the rule *dhi ca* [A 8.2.25]: *vyatidhve*. [In the first person singular,] by the rule *ha eti* [A 8.2.35]: *vyatihe*. [In the imperfect: *vyatyasai*; *vyatyāsta*; *vyatiṣīta*; *vyatirāte*; *vyatibhāte*; *vyatibabhe*. SK 2681 *na gatihiṃsārthebhyaḥ* (A 1.3.15): [The middle voice is not used] after roots whose meanings involve motion (*gati*) or injury (*hiṃsā*).

[The verb *vyati*] undergoes [the substitution of *ātmanepada* endings]. [The rule] "in the sense of prohibition" requires the addition of *hasa* and others as examples. *Hasa* and the like refer to types of laughter, which are vocal actions: *vyatihasanti* ("they laugh at each other"), *vyatijalpanti* ("they converse with each other"). There is no prohibition for the root *hṛ* ("to seize"): *saṃpraharante rājānaḥ* ("the kings attack one another"). SK 2682: It should be stated that [the *ātmanepada* ending is used] also when *itaretara*, *anyonya*, and *paraspara* are the accompanying words (*upapada*). [Examples: *itaretarasya*, *anyonyasya*, or *parasparasya vyatilunanti* ("they cut each other's [hair]").
SK 2683 *nerviśaḥ* (A 1.3.17):
[the ātmanepada ending is used] after the root *viś* when preceded by *ni*.
SK 2684 *parivyavebhyaḥ kriyaḥ* (A 1.3.18): [the ātmanepada ending is used] after the root *kṛ* when preceded by *pari*, *vi*, or *ava*.
This [sūtra] is for the purpose of expressing that the result does not accrue to the agent (*akartrabhiprāya*). [Examples: *parikrīṇīte*, *vikrīṇīte*, *avakrīṇīte*.
According to A 1.3.19, *viparābhyāṃ jeḥ*:
*vijayate*, *parājayate*.

SK 2686: *āṅo do 'nāsyaviharaṇe* (A 1.3.20). After the root *dā* preceded by *āṅ*, when it occurs in a sense other than "opening the mouth," the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) shall apply. Example: *vidyām ādatte* ("He acquires knowledge"). Why say "other than opening the mouth"? Example: *mukhaṃ vyādadāti* ("He opens his mouth"). The mention of "mouth" (*āsya*) is not intended to be restrictive; thus: *vipādikāṃ vyādadāti* ("He opens a cracked foot"). A crack in the foot is called *vipādikā*. Example: *nadī kūlaṃ vyādadāti* ("The river opens its bank"). There is no prohibition [of the middle voice] when the action concerns another's body part: *vyādadate pipīlikāḥ pataṅgasya mukham* ("The ants open the mouth of the moth"). SK 2687: *krīḍo 'nusaṃparibhyaś ca* (A 1.3.21). [The middle voice applies after the root *krīḍ* preceded by *anu*, *sam*, *pari*, and *ca* ("and").]

[The suffix *ātmanepada* is applied] after the root *krīḍ* when preceded by the prefixes *anu*, *sam*, *pari*, and *ā*. However, it is not so when preceded by *anu* used as a *karmapravacanīya*. This is because [the rule] associates with a prefix (*upasarga*). For example: *māṇavakam anukrīḍati* ("he plays along with the boy"). The meaning is "with him" (*tena saha*); thus, these two [prefixes] function as *karmapravacanīyas*. [The suffix is applied] after *sam* when not meaning "making a sound. Example: *saṃkrīḍate* ("he plays together"). But when meaning "making a sound," one says *saṃkrīḍati cakram* ("the wheel makes a clattering sound"). [The suffix is applied] after *ā-gam* in the sense of "endurance" (*kṣamā*). This refers to the causative form (*ṇyanta*). Example: *āgamayasva tāvat* ("wait for a moment").

"Do not hasten"—this is the meaning. With *śikṣ* used in the sense of "desire to know" (*jijñāsā*): *dhanuṣi śikṣate*. The meaning is that he desires to become capable in the knowledge of archery. Regarding *nāth* used in the sense of "blessing" (*āśis*): it has been stated that the Vārttika [saying] "only in the sense of blessing" is for the purpose of restriction. *sarpiṣo nāthate*. The meaning is that he prays, "May clarified butter be mine. How then is one to explain the verse: *nāthase kimu patiṃ na bhūbhṛtām*? It should be read as *nādhase*. With *hṛ* used in the sense of "manner" (*gata*) when there is a habit (*tācchīlya*). "Manner" (*gata*) means a way or mode.

Horses imitate their father. It should be stated that the root *kṛ* [is used] in the sense of "scattering" (*kirati*) when referring to joy, livelihood, or making a nest. Joy and the others are the objects; therein, joy is the cause of scattering, while the others are the results.
A 6.1.142: *apāt ca tuṣpāc-chakuniṣv ālekhanē*.

The suffix *suṭ* is applied after the root *kirati*. It should be stated that *suṭ* also occurs only in the sense of joy (*harṣa*) and so forth. Examples: *apaskirate vṛṣo hṛṣṭaḥ* (the bull, being joyful, wallows); *kukkuṭo bhakṣārthī* (the cock, seeking food); *śvā āśvayārthī ca* (and the dog, seeking its own gain). Why "in the sense of joy and so forth"? Example: *apakirati kusumam* (he scatters a flower). In this case, neither the *taṅ* (ātmanepada) nor *suṭ* apply. They say that although *taṅ* would be applicable if one intends to express mere joy and so forth, it is not desired here because of the absence of *suṭ*: *gajo 'pakirati* (the elephant scatters). [The rule] *āṅi nupracchyoḥ*: *ānute*, *āpṛcchate*. [The rule] *śapa upālambhe* (the root *śap* takes *taṅ* in the sense of reproaching).

The meaning is that the *ātmanepada* ending should be prescribed after a verb meaning "to revile" (*ākrośa*) when it is marked with a *svarita* accent, even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, provided the sense is that of an oath (*śapatha*). Example: *kṛṣṇāya śapate* ("he swears an oath against Kṛṣṇa"). (A 1.3.22) *sam-ava-pra-vi-bhyaḥ sthaḥ*: After the prefix *stha*, the *ātmanepada* is used following *sam*, *ava*, *pra*, and *vi*. *sthā-dhvor ic ca*: The vowel *i* is substituted for the final vowel of *sthā* and *dhā* [when followed by *liṭ*]. *samasthita*; *samasthiṣātām*; *samasthiṣata*. *avatiṣṭhate*; *pratiṣṭhate*; *vitiṣṭhate*. There is an extension of the rule for *āṅ* in the sense of a formal proposition (*pratijñā*): *śabdaṃ nityam ātiṣṭhate* ("he maintains that sound is eternal"). The meaning is that he formally asserts its eternity.
SK 2690 *prakāśanastheyākhyayoś ca* (A 1.3.23):

"The cowherd woman stands for Kṛṣṇa" (*gopī kṛṣṇāya tiṣṭhate*). The meaning is that she reveals her intention. "He who, having doubted, stands for Karṇa and others" (*saṃśayya karṇādiṣu tiṣṭhate yaḥ*). The meaning is that he relies upon Karṇa and others as his arbiters. SK 2691 *udo 'nūrdhvakarmaṇi* (A 1.3.24).

The suffix *ap* is used after [a word denoting] liberation (*mukti*) when it means "to rise. Why say "not upward" (*anūrdhva*)? [Because otherwise one would say: "He rises from a seat" (*pīṭhād uttiṣṭhati*). It is used only in the sense of effort (*īhā*); not here: "One hundred [coins] arise from the village" (*grāmāc chatam uttiṣṭhati*). A5.4.49: After [the root] *upa*, [the suffix *ap* is used] when a mantra is the instrument.

One worships the *āgnīdhra* shed with the *āgneyī* [verse]. What is the purpose of using a mantra here? [It is for the sake of] "worshipping the husband with youth. It should be stated that the prefix *upa-* is used in the senses of worshiping a deity (*devapūjā*), forming an association (*saṅgatikaraṇa*), making a friend (*mitrakaraṇa*), and on paths (*pathi*). [Examples: "He worships the sun" (*ādityam upatiṣṭhate*). How then is one to explain the phrase: "Sarasvatī worshipped the praiseworthy one with meaningful hymns"? [This is because] he is superimposed as a deity, or because the king possesses a portion of divinity (*devatāṃśatva*). "The Gaṅgā approaches the Yamunā"—the meaning is that she clings to it (*upaśliṣyati*). "He attends upon the chariot-warriors" (*rathikān upatiṣṭhate*).

The meaning is "he makes friendly. *Panthāḥ srughnam upatiṣṭhate* ("The path approaches Srughna") means "it reaches. It should be stated that [the suffix *ātmanepada* is used] in the sense of desiring to obtain (*lipsā*). *Bhikṣuḥ prabhum upatiṣṭhate* or *upatiṣṭhate* ("The mendicant attends upon the master"): the meaning is that he approaches out of a desire to obtain [favor]. SK 2693: *akarmakāc ca* (A 1.3.26).

The *ātmanepada* suffix shall be used after the root *sthā* preceded by *upa-* when it is intransitive (*akarmaka*). *Bhojanakāle upatiṣṭhate* ("He attends at the time of eating"): the meaning is that he is present.

SK 2694 *udvibhyāṃ tapaḥ* (A 1.3.27). [The rule applies] only when the root is intransitive (*akarmaka*). Examples: *uttapate*, *vitapate*. The meaning is "shines. It should be stated that [the rule applies] when the object is one's own limb (*svāṅga*). "One's own limb" (*svāṅga*) is defined as a limb belonging to oneself, but not one that is liquid (*adrava*). Examples: *pāṇim uttapate* or *vitapate* ("he warms his hand"). Not here: *suvarṇam uttapati* ("he heats gold"), which means "he causes it to glow" or "he melts it. Example: *caitro maitrasya pāṇim uttapati* ("Caitra warms Maitra's hand"), which means "he causes it to glow. SK 2695 *āṅo yamahanaḥ* (A 1.3.28).

[The rule applies] to *āyacchate* and *āhate* when [the verb] is intransitive or has its own body part (*svāṅga*) as its object; thus, it does not apply here in *parasya śira āhanti* ("he strikes the head of another"). How then is one to explain Bhāravi’s *ājaghne viṣamavilocanasya vakṣaḥ* ("he struck the chest of the three-eyed god") and Bhaṭṭi’s *āhadhvaṃ mā raghūttamam* ("do not strike the best of the Raghus")? The *Bhāgavṛtti* states that these are simply errors. Alternatively, one may supply the word *prāpya* ("having reached"). Or, regarding the rule "the ablative is used when there is an elision of a *lyap*-suffix" (*lyablope pañcamī*), this refers to cases where the meaning of that suffix is understood even without the presence of a form ending in *lyap*.
Or one may supply a form ending in *tumun*, such as *bhettum* ("in order to pierce"), or interpret it as *samīpam etyeti* ("he goes near").

SK 2696 (A 2.4.44): *ātmanepadeṣv anyatarasyām*—the substitute *vadha* optionally replaces *han* when the *ātmanepada* endings follow in the *luṅ* tense. [Examples: *avadhiṣṭa*, *avadhiṣātām*. SK 2697 (A 1.2.14): *hanaḥ sic*—the suffix *sic* follows *han*.
What would [the result] be? There would be the elision of the nasal (*anunāsikalopa*). [Examples: *āhata*, *āhasātām*, *āhasata*. Rule SK 2698: *yamo gandhane* (A 1.2.15).

The suffix *sic* is marked as *kit* when following the root *yam* in the sense of "hinting" (*gandhana*). Hinting (*gandhana*) means suggesting or exposing the faults of others. [Example: *udāyata*. Why "in the sense of hinting"? [Counter-example: *udāyaṃsta pādam*. The meaning here is "he dragged."
SK 2699: After the roots √gam and √ṛcch, [the suffix -yañ is applied] provided they are intransitive (A 1.3.29). For example: *saṃgacchate*.
SK 2700: Optionally after the root √gam [the suffix -yañ is applied] (A 1.2.13).

The suffixes *liṅ* and *sic*, when following a root beginning with a consonant (*jhal*), are optionally *kit* after the root *gam*. [Examples: *saṃgasīṣṭa* or *saṃgaṃsīṣṭa*; *samagata* or *samagaṃsta*. [Future: *samṛcchiṣyate*. Why "after intransitive roots"? [Counter-example: *grāmaṃ saṃgacchati* ("he goes to the village"). There is an extension [of this rule] for the roots *vid*, *pracch*, and *svar*. Only the root *vid* is intended here. [Examples: *saṃvitte*, *saṃvidāte*. According to A 7.1.7, *vetter vibhāṣā*: [the substitution of *samprasāraṇa* is optional].

The augment *ruṭ* may optionally be added after the root *vetteḥ* (*vid*) when it is followed by a substitute *jha* (the 3rd person plural ending) beginning with *a*. Thus: *saṃvidrate* or *saṃvidate*; *saṃvidratām* or *saṃvidatām*; *samavidrata* or *samavidata*. [Likewise for other roots: *saṃpṛcchate*, *saṃsvarate*. It should be stated that [the augment *ruṭ* is also applied] after the roots *ṛ*, *śru*, and *dṛś*. Regarding *ṛ*, both [roots *ṛ* and *ṛ*] are included; however, it has been stated that in the rule for the formation of *aṅ* suffixes, only *iyarti* is intended. Thus: *mā samṛta*, *mā samṛṣātām*, *mā samṛṣata* (from the root *ṛ*); and *samārta*, *samārṣātām*, *samārṣata* (from the root *ṛ* belonging to the *bhvādi* class).

But here [the forms] are *mā samarata*, *mā samaretām*, *mā samaranta*, *samārata*, *samāretām*, and *samāran*—and likewise *saṃśṛṇute* and *saṃpaśyate*. [The rule applies] only when the verb is intransitive (*akarmaka*). For this very reason, they say that the usage by Murāri, "rakṣāṃsīti purāpi saṃśṛṇumahe" ("we have heard even before that there are Rākṣasas"), is erroneous; or else, they say, it is due to an ellipsis (*adhyāhāra*), as in [the phrase] "kathayadbhyaḥ" (from those who were telling). Now, if it is asked how verbs such as *han* (to strike) and *gam* (to go) can be intransitive within this section concerning intransitives, listen: [they become so when used in specific senses].

An action is considered "intransitive" (akarmikā) when the verbal root functions in a sense other than its primary meaning, when the object is included within the meaning of the root itself, when it is so established by convention, or when the object is not intended to be expressed. (1) *Vahati bhāram* ("he carries a load")—this is transitive. *Nadī vahati* ("the river flows")—the meaning is *syandate* ("it flows"). *Jīvati* ("he lives"), *nṛtyati* ("he dances")—these are examples of actions that are intransitive by convention. *Megho varṣati* ("the cloud rains")—this is an example where the object is not intended to be expressed. *Sa kiṃprabhuḥ yo hitān na saṃśṛṇute* ("What kind of master is he who does not listen to beneficial advice"?). It should be stated: "After a prefix, [the roots] *as* and *ūh* are optionally [intransitive]. The term "from an intransitive [root]" (*akarmakāt*) is no longer in force here.
Examples: *Bandhaṃ nirasyati* ("he casts off bondage") and *nirasyate*; *samūhati* and *samūhate*.
SK 2702: After a prefix, the root *ūh* [takes the substitute *ūḍ*] before an affix beginning with *y*, provided it is marked with *k* or *ṅ*. Example: *brahma samuhyāt*; *agniṃ samuhya*. SK 2703:
The root *hve* [takes the augment *ātmanepada*] after the prefixes *ni*, *sam*, *upa*, and *vi*. (A 1.3.30)
He calls out. According to A 1.3.31, *nihvayate* is used in the sense of rivalry (*spardhā*).
For example: "Kṛṣṇa challenges Cāṇūra. Why specify "in the sense of rivalry"? [Consider: "He calls his son."

SK 2705: The verb *kṛ* [takes the genitive case for its object] in the senses of perfuming (*gandhana*), throwing down (*avakṣepaṇa*), serving (*sevana*), violence (*sāhasikya*), preparation (*pratiyatna*), speaking (*prakathana*), and employment (*upayoga*). (A 1.3.32)

*Gandhana* means injury; it signifies "to expose" or "to indicate. Indeed, exposing [a fault] is itself a form of injury because it is conducive to the separation from life. *Avakṣepaṇa* means reviling. As in: "The hawk *udākurute* the quail," which means "it reviles it. *Upakurute harim*: "He serves Hari. *Prakurute paradārān*: "He acts violently toward another's wife"; he engages with them by force. *Prakathayati*: "He speaks at length. *Prakurute śatam*: "He employs a hundred [pieces of money]" for the sake of dharma. In these cases, why [is the rule not applied]? [Answer: *Kaṭaṃ karoti* ("He makes a mat"). (A 1.3.33) *Adheḥ prasahane* ("After *adhi*, in the sense of overcoming").

*Prasahana* means endurance and overcoming, based on the grammatical rule that the root *ṣaha* is used in the senses of "to endure" and "to overcome. It governs the object *śatru* (enemy); the meaning is "he endures" (*śamate*) or "he overcomes" (*abhibhavati*). According to A 1.3.34, *veḥ śabdakarmaṇaḥ*, [the verb *kṛ*] is used with the prefix *vi-* when the action concerns sound;
the meaning is "he utters sounds" (*svarān vikurute*), i.e., he pronounces them. Why specify "when the action concerns sound"? [Consider: *kāmaś cittam vikaroti* ("desire agitates the mind").

SK 2708: *akarmakāc ca* (A 1.3.35). [The suffix *ātmanepada* is used] after the root *kṛ* following the prefix *vi-* when it is intransitive (*akarmaka*). Example: *chātrā vikurvate*. The meaning is: "they undergo a transformation" (*vikāraṃ labhante*). SK 2709:

*saṃmānanotsañjanācāryakaraṇajñānabhṛtivigaṇanavyayeṣu niyaḥ* (A 1.3.36). [The suffix *ātmanepada* is used after the root *nī* when it signifies] honoring, lifting up, acting as a teacher, knowing, wages, counting, or spending.

In this context, *utsañjana* (lifting up), *jñāna* (making known), and *vigaṇana* (reckoning) are the meanings to be expressed by the root *nī*; the others are merely contextual adjuncts (*prayogopādhi*). For instance: in the technical treatise (*śāstra*), one says *nayati* [the root]; the meaning is that one causes the established doctrine (*siddhānta*) residing in the treatise to reach the students. And by that, the honoring of the students is implied as the result. In the sense of lifting up: *daṇḍam unnayate*; the meaning is that one raises the staff. In the sense of bringing near: *māṇavakam upanayate*; the meaning is that one causes the boy to reach one's own presence according to the prescribed rule.

For by teaching preceded by the initiation ceremony (*upanayana*), the status of an *ācārya* is established in the initiator. In the sense of "knowledge," it means he leads to reality; that is, he ascertains it. "He initiates laborers" means he brings them into his own presence by providing wages. "Settling accounts" refers to the repayment of debts and the like. "He settles the tax" means he clears the portion to be given to the king. "He settles a hundred" means he applies it for the sake of dharma. (Pāṇini 1.3.37:
*kartṛsthe cāśarīre karmaṇi*) [The agent is designated as the object when the action resides in the agent, provided the object is not part of the body.]
