*sthāvaraḥ*, *īśvaraḥ*, *bhāsvaraḥ*, *presvaraḥ*, *kasvaraḥ*.

SK 3156 (*yaś ca yaṅaḥ*): The suffix *varac* may be applied after a reduplicated form (*yaṅanta*) of the root *yā*. By the rule *ato lopaḥ*, the *a* is elided. When the status of being a "substitute" (*sthānivadbhāva*)—based on the rule *acaḥ parasmin*—would otherwise apply, [it is noted that] when the final element of a word (*padasya caramāvayava*) or operations such as doubling (*dvirvacana*) are to be performed, a substitute for a vowel (*ajādeśa*) caused by a subsequent element (*paranimitta*) is not treated as a "substitute" (*na sthānivat*). This is because there is a prohibition against its being treated as a substitute with respect to the elision of *y* and *v* (*yalopa*). Thus, by the rule *lopo vyoḥ*, the *y* is elided. If one were to rely on the status of the elision of *a* (*allopa*) as being a "substitute," the elision of the *ā* [of *yā*] would follow. However, [the rule] *vare luptaṃ na sthānivat* states that what is elided before the suffix *vara* is not treated as a "substitute. Thus, *yāyāvaraḥ* is formed.
SK 3157: After the roots *bhrāj*, *bhās*, *dhurv*, *vidyut*, *ūrj*, *pū*, *dṛś*, *jū*, *grāva*, and *stu*, the suffix *kvip* is applied [to form nouns].

*vibhrāṭ* (shining), *bhāḥ* (light), *bhāsau* (two lights); *dhūḥ* (burden), *dhurau* (two burdens); *vidyut* (lightning); *ūrk* (nourishment); *pūḥ* (city), *purau* (two cities). Because the mention of *dṛś* is drawn back [from the previous rule], there is lengthening for the root *jū*: *jūḥ* (speed), *juvau* (two speeds), *juvaḥ* (many speeds). Regarding the word *grāva*, its composition with the verbal root is prescribed as an irregularity (*nipātana*) in the Sūtra; from that, *kvip* is applied: *grāvastut* (one who praises the pressing-stones). SK 3158: The suffix *kvip* is seen after other [roots] as well.

The mention of *kvip*, *chit*, *bhid*, and *dṛśi* is for the purpose of including other rules. In some cases there is lengthening; in some cases there is no *saṃprasāraṇa*; in some cases there is reduplication; and in some cases there is shortening. And so says the Vārttika: "In the case of *kvi*, *vac*, *pracch*, *āyata*, *stu*, *kaṭapru*, *ju*, and *śrī*, there is lengthening and no *saṃprasāraṇa*. Since this is established for some roots by the Uṇādi-sūtra beginning with *kvi-vaci-*, the mention in the Vārttika is intended to ensure that these forms do not fall under the rule for the suffix *tṛn* when denoting one who habitually performs an action (*tacchīla*), etc., thereby preventing its sublation. Thus: *vaktīti vāk* ("she speaks, hence speech"); *pṛcchatīti prāṭ* ("she asks, hence an asker").

*Āyatastūḥ*: one who praises what is extended. *Kaṭaprūḥ*: one who moves toward a mat. *Jūḥ*: said to be [from *ju*]. *Śrīḥ*: she who causes to resort (*śrayati*). For the roots *dyuti*, *gami*, and *hu*, there is also reduplication. Because of the inclusion of *dṛśi*, it receives the technical designation of "reduplicated" (*abhyāsa*). *Didyut*. *Jagat*. From *hu*, there is also lengthening: *juhūḥ*. From *dṛ* in the sense of fear, there is also shortening: *dadṛt*. From *dhyai*, there is also vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*): *dhīḥ*. A 3.2.179: *bhuvaḥ saṃjñāntarayoḥ* ("After the root *bhū*, [the suffix *kvip* occurs] when a name or a different thing is expressed").

A certain person named *mitrabhū* is one who stands between a creditor and a debtor for the sake of providing security; he is a *pratibhū* (surety). According to A 3.2.180, *viprasaṃbhyo ḍvasaṃjñāyām*, the suffix *ḍu* is applied after these [prefixes] following the root *bhū*, but not when it is a proper name (*saṃjñā*). Thus, *vibhū* means "all-pervading"; *prabhū* means "lord" or "master"; *saṃbhū* means "progenitor. However, when it is a proper name, there is someone named *vibhū*. There is an extension [of the rule] to *mitadru* and others: *mitadruḥ* ("that which flows measuredly"), *śatadruḥ* ("flowing in a hundred ways"), and *śambhū* ("source of happiness"). Here, the root *bhū* has the causative sense (*ṇyartha*) inherent within it.

SK 3161: *dhaḥ karmaṇi ṣṭran* (A 3.2.181). The suffix *ṣṭran* occurs after the roots *dheṭ* and *dhāñ* in the sense of the object (*karman*). [The word] *dhātrī* is used for "mother," "myrobalan tree" (*āmalakī*), "earth" (*vasumatī*), and "nurse. SK 3162: *dāmnīśasayuyujastutudasisicamihapatadaśanahaḥ karaṇe* (A 3.2.182). The suffix *ṣṭran* occurs after the roots *dām*, *nī*, *śas*, *yu*, *yuj*, *stu*, *tud*, *si*, *sic*, *mih*, *pat*, *daś*, and *naha* in the sense of the instrument (*karaṇa*).

The suffix *ṣṭran* shall be applied after roots such as *dā* in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇa*). [Examples: that by which they cut is a *dātra* (sickle); *netra* (eye/lead-rope). Pāṇini Sūtra 7.2.9 states: "And [the substitution of *iṭ*] does not occur before these ten *kṛt* suffixes: *ti*, *tu*, *tra*, *ta*, *tha*, *si*, *su*, *sa*, *ra*, and *ka*. [Examples: *śastra* (weapon), *yotra* (rope), *yoktra* (yoking-rope), *stotra* (hymn), *setra* (fetter), *sektra* (sprinkler), *meḍhra* (penis), *patra* (leaf/vessel), *daṃṣṭrā* (fang), *naddrī* (river).

SK 3164: After the roots *pū* (in the sense of purifying) and *pūñ* (in the sense of cleansing), the suffix *ṣṭran* occurs when the instrument (*karaṇa*) is a part of a plough (*hala*) or a boar (*sūkara*). [The resulting forms are] *halasya potram* or *sūkarasya potram*, meaning "the snout. SK 3165: After the roots *ṛt*, *lū*, *dhū*, *sū*, *khan*, *sah*, and *car*, the suffix *itra* occurs.
*aritra*, *lavitra*, *dhavitra*, *savitra*, *khanitra*, *sahitra*, *caritra*.
According to Pāṇini 3.2.185 (*puvaḥ saṃjñāyām*), [the suffix *itra* is added after the root *pū*] when it denotes a name:
*pavitra*. That by which clarified butter (*ājya*) is purified, and that which is the ring worn on the ring finger.

SK 3167: *kartari carṣidevatayoḥ* (A 3.2.186). The suffix *itra* occurs in the sense of the agent when the object is either a seer (*ṛṣi*) or a deity (*devatā*). A seer is a Vedic mantra; this is seen from the statement, "It was seen by a seer" (*ṛṣiṇā dṛṣṭaḥ*). That by which one is purified is *pavitra*. As for the deity, [the example is]: "Agni is the purifier; may he purify me. Thus ends the section on primary derivatives (*kṛdanta*) formed with preceding elements.
The Section on Uṇādi Suffixes, Number 65.
The first quarter-verse.

1. The suffix *uṇ* is added after the roots *kṛ*, *vā*, *pā*, *ji*, *svad*, *sādh*, and *śū*. One who acts (*karoti*) is a *kāruḥ*—an artisan or an agent. [By the rule] *āto yuk ciṇ-kṛtoḥ*, [we have] *vāti* (he blows), thus *vāyuḥ* (wind). *Yāyuḥ* is the anus. It conquers (*jayati*), that is, overcomes diseases; thus *jāyuḥ* is medicine. It measures (*minoti*), that is, it injects heat into the body; thus *māyuḥ* is bile (*pitta*). *Svāduḥ* (sweet). He accomplishes the work of others (*sādhnoti parakāryam*), thus *sādhuḥ* (virtuous). It pervades quickly (*āśu*); thus *āśuḥ* is the *vrīhi* rice known as *pāṭala*. 2. In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *iṇ* [is added] after the root *mā*. "May it not come to us" (*mā na āyau*).

3. The suffix *ñuṇ* is added after the roots *dṝ*, *sanijani*, *car*, and *caṭi*. That which is split (*dīryate*) is *dāru* (wood). *Snuḥ* means a ridge or table-land; it is used in the masculine and neuter (*sānu*). *Jānu* (knee); *jānunī*. Here, the prohibition [of *guṇa*] by the rule *janivadhyoś ca* does not apply, due to the force of the two indicatory letters (*anubandha*s). *Cāru* means beautiful. *Cāṭu* means a pleasing word. Because it belongs to the *mṛgayvādi* group, there is also the form *caṭ* with the suffix *kupratyaya*. 4. The suffix *u* is added to the root *śri* after the words *kim* and *jara*. That which hears what? (*kiṃ śṛṇoti*) is *kiṃśāruḥ*, meaning the awn of grain or an arrow. That which goes toward old age (*jarām eti*) is *jarāyuḥ*, meaning the womb or fetal membrane.

The *garbhāśaya* (womb) is the *jarāyu* (chorion). 5. From the roots *tṛ*, *ra*, and *lṛ*, [the suffix *u* is added]. Because the castes (*varṇas*) cross over by means of this, it is the *tālu* (palate). 6. From the root *vac* preceded by *kṛka*, the letter *ka* is inserted. Because he speaks with the *kṛka* (throat), he is the *kṛkavāku*. According to the *Viśvakośa*: "The *kṛkavāku* refers to a peacock, a lizard, and a cock. 7. From the roots *bhṛ*, *mṛ*, *śī*, *tṝ*, *car*, *tṛ*, *tan*, *dhan*, *mi*, and *masj*, the suffix *u* is added. He supports or sustains, thus he is the *bharu*—both the master and Śiva. In him beings die, thus the *maru* is a waterless region. These [roots also yield] *śayu* (serpent) and *ajagara* (python).

*Taru* means a tree (*vṛkṣa*). *Caru* is that which the deities consume; thus it is called *caru*. *Tsaru* refers to the handle of a sword or similar object. *Tanu* means small or slight. *unatti induḥ* // 13. *īṣeḥ kic ca* // From the root *īṣ*, the suffix *u* occurs, and it is *kit*; furthermore, there is the substitution of *i* for the initial [radical]. Thus, *īṣate* (he moves) becomes *iṣuḥ* (an arrow), which means "that which strikes. *Iṣuḥ* is used in both genders. 14. *skandeḥ salopaś ca* // [From *skand*,] there is the elision of *s*. Thus, *kanduḥ* (a small vessel). 15. *sṛjer asum ca* // By the word "ca" (and), there is the elision of *s* and the suffix *up*. Thus, *rajjuḥ* (a rope). 16. *kṛter ādyantaviparyayaś ca* // There is an inversion of the first and last [consonants], namely, a transposition of the *k* and *t*. Thus, *tarkuḥ* (a spinning wheel for winding thread). 17. *na avaṅceḥ* // [The rule applies] except for *avañc*. Due to being included in the *nyaṅkv-ādi* group, there is the substitution of *ku* (i.e., *ṅ*) for the final consonant.

The word *nyaṅku* means a deer; it is derived from the root *añc* with the suffix *niyatam* (meaning "fixedly" or "constantly"). Regarding the rule *phalipāṭinamimanijanāṃ guk paṭinākidhataś ca*: - From the root *phal*, the suffix *guk* is added: *phalgu*. - From the root *pāṭ*, the suffix *paṭi* is added: *paṭu*. One who causes to split (*pāṭayati*) is called *paṭu*. - From the root *nam*, the suffix *āk* is added: *nāku*, meaning an anthill (*valmīka*). - From the root *man*, the suffix *u* is added: *madhu*. - From the root *jan*, the suffix *u* is added: *jatu*. Regarding the rule *valer guk ca*: - From the root *val* (meaning "to cover," *saṃvaraṇe*), the suffix *guk* is added: *valgū*. Regarding the rule *śaḥ kit sanvac ca*: - From the root *śyai* (to flow/coagulate), the suffix *u* is added, and that suffix is both *kit* and behaves like *san*. Thus: *śiśu*, meaning a child. Regarding the rule *yo dve ca*: - [From the root *śyai*,] the suffix *yu* is added, and the root is reduplicated. Thus: *śyāyū*.

The horse fit for the *aśvamedha* sacrifice went away. The repetition of the word "two" (*dve*) in the context of the rule *sanvat* is for the purpose of excluding the suffix *it*. 22. *Kuru* and *bhruś*. *Babhru* occurs as a name of a certain sage; in the sense of Viṣṇu, *babhru* means a mongoose and tawny. There is *ku*-substitution (the substitution of *u*) for the three [roots], and there is the elision of the *s* of the root *bhrasj*. Thus: *pṛthuḥ* (broad), *mṛduḥ* (soft). Because they belong to the *nyaṅkv-ādi* group, there is *ku*-substitution. He who fries (*bhṛjjati*) by means of ascetic heat is *bhṛguḥ*. 29. There is also the elision of the nasal (*na*) of the roots *laṅgh* and *baṃh*. Thus: *laghuḥ* (light). 30. In the words *vāla*, *mūla*, *laghu*, *alpa*, and *aṅguli*, the *l* optionally undergoes the change to *r*. Thus: *raghuḥ* (a certain king); *bahuḥ* (much). 31. From the root *ūrṇ* (to cover), there is the elision of the nasal (*nu*). Thus: *ūruḥ* (the thigh). 32. In the sense of "great," there is also the substitution of the short vowel (*u* for *o*). Thus: *uru* (great). 33. From the root *śliṣ*, there is also the suffix *ka*. Thus: *śleṣkaḥ* (an embrace).

The suffix *ku* is applied after the root *śliṣ*, meaning "to cling," to form *ślīku*, which denotes a servant; it also forms *udyatu*, meaning "effulgent. (34) After the roots *khana* ("to dig") and *śṛ* ("to crush"), with the prefix *ā-* or *para-*, the suffix *ku* is applied, and it is also marked as having an indicatory letter *ḍ*. From *ā-khanati* comes *ākhu*, meaning a rat. From *paraṃ śṛṇāti* comes *paraśu*, meaning an axe. Due to its inclusion in the *pṛṣodarādi* group, there is also the form *parśu* through the elision of the vowel *a*. (35) After the root *dru* ("to run") when *hari* or *mita* are the preceding words, the suffix *ku* is applied, and it is also marked as having an indicatory letter *ḍ*. From the root *dru* in the sense of "going," when *hari* and *mita* are the accompanying words, *ku* is added and is marked as *ḍit*. *Haribhir drūyate* results in *haridrur vṛkṣaḥ*, a tree. *Mitaṃ dravati* results in *mitadruḥ*, the ocean. (36) And also when *śata* [is the preceding word].

It flows in a hundred ways, thus it is *śatadru* (the "Hundred-flower"); this [formation] occurs even from a single root by virtue of the rule of abundance (*bāhulaka*). It flows upwards, thus *dru* is a tree and its branch; that which possesses these is a *druma* (tree). 37. *Kharu*, *śaṅku*, *pīyu*, *nīlaṅgu*, and *liṅgu*: these five are derived as irregular forms (*nipātana*) ending in the suffix *ku*. From the root *khan* ("to dig"), the letter *r* is substituted for the final [nasal], resulting in *kharu*: meaning desire (*kāma*), a cruel person (*knūra*), a fool (*mūrkha*), and a horse (*aśva*). *Śaṅku* is masculine, meaning a wedge (*kīla*) and an arrow-head (*śalya*). 38. From the root *pibati* ("to drink"), there is the substitution of *i* for the vowel and the addition of the augment *yuk*, resulting in *pīyu*: meaning a crow (*vāyasa*), time (*kāla*), and gold (*suvarṇa*).

From the root *lagi* meaning "to go," preceded by the prefix *ni*, there is the substitution of *ku* for *ni* and the lengthening of the vowel. Thus, *nīlaṅguḥ* refers to a specific kind of worm or a jackal. There is an alternative reading, *nīlāṅguḥ*, in which case the lengthening applies to the root as well. From the root *lage* meaning "to cling," there is the substitution of *it* for the final *a*. That which clings is the mind (*citta*); thus, *liguḥ* means a fool. (39) *Mṛgayu* and others: these are derived with the suffix *ku* and are treated as irregular forms (*nipātana*). One who goes after (*yāti*) game (*mṛga*) is a hunter (*mṛgayuḥ*). A righteous person is a *devayuḥ*. One who is conversant with the ways of the world is a *mitrayuḥ*.

This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class of words). 40. From the roots *mandi*, *vāśi*, *mathi*, *cati*, *caṅki*, and *aṅki*, the suffix *urac* is added. *mandurā*: a stable for horses. *vāśurā*: the night. *mathurā*: [the city of] Mathurā. *caturaḥ*: clever. *caṅkuraḥ*: a chariot. *aṅkuraḥ*: a sprout. Due to its inclusion in the *kharjūrādi* group, *aṅkūraḥ* is also valid. 41. From the root *vyathi*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) and the suffix *kic*. *vithuraḥ*: a thief or a demon. 42. *makura-* and *dardura-*. *mukuraḥ*: a mirror. By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), *makuraḥ* is also valid. The root *dṝ* means "to tear apart."

There is reduplication of the root, the augment *ruk* for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*), and the elision of the suffixal *ṭi*. According to the *Viśva-kośa*: "The word *dardura* refers to a cloud, a frog, a type of musical instrument, and a kind of mountain; *dardurā* refers to Caṇḍikā; and *dardura* also refers to a network of villages. (Verse 43) Furthermore, words such as *madgura* and others are derived through irregular formation (*nipātana*) ending in the suffix *urac*. From the root *mādyati*, the suffix *guk* is applied: *madgura* denotes a specific kind of fish. From the root *kabṛ* (in the sense of color), there is the augment *ruk*: *karbura* means white or a Rākṣasa. From the root *badhnāti*, the suffix *ūra* is also applied because it belongs to the *kharjūra* group.

*Bandhūra* and *bandhura* are used for "bending" and "beautiful," respectively; according to Rantideva, they are also used in the three genders [as adjectives]. (44) For *kokata*, there is optionally *kuk*: *kukkuraḥ* or *kukuraḥ*. (45) For *asa*, there is *uran*: *asuraḥ*. With the suffix *aṇ* [from the *prajñādi* group], it is *āsuraḥ*. (46) And for *masi*: In the fifth chapter (*pāda*), it will be stated that *ūrann* follows *masi*. [Thus: *masūrāḥ* or *masurāḥ* refer to a type of grain; *masūrā* or *masurā* refers to a courtesan. *Masūrā* or *masurā* (feminine) refers to a courtesan or a type of grain. *Masūrī* refers to a disease of the foot; furthermore, [the word] *masūra* is masculine when referring to a pillow.

"Masūra and Asura are two"—thus [states] the Viśva-kośa. (47) *Śāvaśer āptau*: *śu* has the sense of "quickly. *Śvaśuraḥ*. Regarding this, Amara says: "The mother of the husband and wife is *śvaśrūḥ*; the father of those two is *śvaśuraḥ*. (48) *Avimahyoṣ ṭiṣac*: *aviṣaḥ*, *mahiṣaḥ*. (49) *Amer dīrghaś ca*: *āmiṣam* is not feminine; it refers to meat as well as an object of enjoyment. (50) *Ruher vṛddhiś ca*: *raṅku*, *śambara*, *rauhiṣaḥ*.

*Rauhiṣa* may refer to a species of deer, and *rauhiṣa* is considered to be a type of grass; thus says the *Saṃsārāvarta*. (51) *Tav-i*, with the augment *ṇit*, is optional. *Tave-* is a root found in the *Sūtra* [of Pāṇini]. *Taviṣa* and *tāviṣa* mean "water" and "heaven. In the feminine, *taviṣī* and *tāviṣī* mean "river," "celestial maiden," and "earth. According to the Vedic commentary (*Vedabhāṣya*), *taviṣī* means "strength. (52) From the root *vyath-* with the negative prefix *nañ*: *avyathiṣa* refers to the ocean and the sun; *avyathiṣī* refers to the earth and night. (53) From the root *kil-*, there is the substitution of *buk*: *kilbiṣam*.

54. After the roots *iṣ*, *mad*, *mud*, *khid*, *chid*, *bhid*, *mand*, *candi*, *tim*, *mi*, *hi*, *muh*, *muc*, *ruc*, *rudh*, *bandh*, and *śuṣ*, the suffix *kirac* is applied. *iṣiraḥ* means fire (*agni*). *madirā* means liquor (*surā*). *mudiraḥ* means a lover (*kāmuka*) and a cloud (*abhra*), according to the *Viśva* and *Medinī* lexicons. *khidiraḥ* means the moon (*candra*). *chidiraḥ* means a sword (*asi*) and an axe (*kuṭhāra*). *bhidiram* means a thunderbolt (*vajra*). *mandiram* means a house (*gṛha*). It is also feminine; the *Viśva* lexicon states: "The word *mandira* may also mean liquor (*madirā*). *candiraḥ* means the moon (*candra*) and an elephant (*hastin*). *timiraḥ* means darkness (*tamas*) and a disease of the eye (*akṣiroga*).

*mihiraḥ* means the sun; *muhiraḥ* refers to one who is desirable or refined; *muciraḥ* means a giver. *Ruciram*, *rudhiram*, and *badhiraḥ* [are derived from their respective roots]. From the root *śuṣ* (to dry): *śuṣiram* means a hole or cavity; others say it means *śuṣkam* (dry). 55. After the root *aś* (to eat), the suffix *iran* is added with the augment *ṇit*. *Āśiraḥ* refers to fire or a demon (*rakṣasa*). 56. *Ajira*, *śiśira*, *śithila*, *sthira*, *sphira*, *sthavira*, and *khadira* [are formed with the suffix *iran*]. In *ajira*, there is an absence of the substitution of *vī* for the root *aj*. *Ajiram* means a courtyard. In *śiśira*, the penultimate vowel undergoes *itva* (shortening). *Śiśiram* denotes a specific season (the cool season), as well as frost, cold, or other things of that nature.

Now, in the case of *mocana*, there is the substitution of *i* for the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) and the elision of the letter *r*. There is the substitution of *l* for the *r* of the suffix. *Śithilaṃ* (loose). From the roots *sthā* and *sphāyi*, there is the elision of the letter *ṣṭi*. *Sthiraṃ* (firm) means motionless; *sphiraṃ* (motionless) means abundant. From the root *tiṣṭhati*, there is the addition of the suffix *vuk* and the shortening of the vowel: *sthaviraḥ* (an elder). *Khadiraḥ* (the catechu tree). By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), from the root *śīṅ* there is the addition of *vuk* and the shortening of the vowel: *śibiraṃ* (a camp). 57. From the roots *sal*, *kal*, *ani*, *mahi*, *bhaḍi*, *bhaṇḍi*, *śaṇḍi*, *piṇḍi*, *tuṇḍi*, *kuki*, *bhū*, [the suffix] *ilac* is added.

It flows and goes downward, thus it is *salila*. [Examples: *kalila*, *anila*, *mahilā*; and because it belongs to the class beginning with *pṛṣodara*, there is also *mahelā*. *Bhaḍ* is a root belonging to the *sūtra* (Vedic) tradition. *Bhaḍila* refers to brave attendants; *bhaṇḍila* means a messenger and also auspiciousness; *śaṇḍila* is a sage; *piṇḍila* is an accountant; *tuṇḍila* is a talkative person; *kokila* is a cuckoo; *bhavila* is one who is likely to become; by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), there is *kuṭila*. 58. After the root *kam*, *pa* is substituted for the final vowel. [Result: *kapila*. 59. After the roots beginning with *gup*, the suffix is *kit*. [Result: *gupila* is a king.

*Tijila* means the moon; *guhila* means a forest. 60. And *mithilā* and others [are formed with the suffix *ilac*]. *Mithilā* is the city where enemies are crushed (*mathyante*); *pathilaḥ* and *pathikaḥ* mean a traveler. 61. From the roots *pati*, *kaṭhi*, *kuṭhi*, *gaḍi*, *guḍi*, and *daṃśi*, the suffix *erak* is added. *Eteraḥ* means a bird or a goer; *chaṭheraḥ* means one who lives in hardship; *kuṭheraḥ* is the *parṇāśa* plant. Due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), there is no nasal augment (*num*): *gaḍeraḥ* means a cloud; *guḍeraḥ* means a small ball; *daṃśeraḥ* means a harmful creature. 62. From *kubi*, there is also the elision of the letter *n*: *kuberaḥ*.

63. And *śada* [takes the suffix] *ista*. *Śateraḥ* means an enemy (*śatruḥ*). 64. *Mūlera-* and others: words ending in the suffix *era* are irregularly formed (*nipātyante*). *Mūleraḥ* means one with matted hair (*jaṭā*). *Gudheraḥ* means a protector (*goptā*). *Guheraḥ* means a blacksmith (*lohaghātakaḥ*). *Muheraḥ* means a fool (*mūrkhaḥ*). 65. From *kapi*, [the suffix] *ota* is added, and *pa* is substituted for [the final *i*]. *Kapotaḥ* means a bird (*pakṣī*). 66. From *bhāti*, [the suffix] *ḍavatu* is added. He who shines is *bhavān*. 67. From *kaṭhi* and *caki*, [the suffix] *oran* is added. *Kaṭhoraḥ* (hard). *Cakoraḥ* (a type of bird). 68. *Kiśora-* and others [are also irregular formations].

From the root *śṛ* preceded by *kim*, there is the suffix *iṣṭi* with elision [of the suffix], and the final letter of *kim* is dropped; thus *kiśora* means a young horse. From *sah* and *ṛ*, the suffix *u* is added; *sahoru* means virtuous. 69. From the roots *kapi*, *gaḍi*, *gaṇḍi*, *kaṭi*, and *paṭi*, the suffix *olac* is added. Because of the specific mention of *kapi*, there is no elision of the nasal (*na*); thus *kapola* (the cheek). *Gaḍola* and *gaṇḍola* are synonyms for a small ball (*guḍaka*). *Kaṭola* means pungent (*kaṭu*). *Paṭola* is the name of a plant. 70. From the root *mī* (to measure), the suffix *ūran* is added; thus *mayūra* (peacock). 71. From the root *syand*, there is also vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*); thus *sindūra* (vermilion). 72. From the roots *si*, *tan*, *gam*, *mas*, *sic*, *vyadh*, *dhā*, *kuś*, the suffix *tun* is added. That which binds (*sinoti*) is a *setu* (bridge).

The suffix *na* is applied after the roots *tita*, *tru*, and *tra*. Thus: *tantuḥ* (a thread), *gantuḥ* (a goer). *Mastu* means the scum of curd. That which is ground is *saktuḥ* (groats); it belongs to the *ardharca*-class of compounds. By the rule *jvaratvara-*, the substitution *ūṭh* occurs; however, according to the view that the condition *kṅiti* (before an affix marked with *k* or *ṅ*) continues to apply here, it occurs by virtue of the word being included in the *bahulaka* (diverse) category. Thus: *otur* (a cat, a wildcat), *dhātuh* (a jackal). 73. After the root *pā* ("to drink"), the suffix *tu* is applied, and it is *kit*. Thus: *pitur* (fire, the sun). 74. And after the root *ṛ* ("to go"), the suffix *tu* is applied. Thus: *artuḥ* (the sun).

The suffix *tu* may optionally be applied after the root *kṛ*, and it becomes *kit*. The word *ṛtu* denotes both the menses of a woman and a season. From the roots *kam*, *man*, *jan*, *gā*, *bhā*, and *yāhi*, the suffix *tu* occurs. *Kantu* means Cupid (*kandarpa*) and the mind (*citta*). *Mantu* means an offense (*aparādha*). *Jantu* means a living being (*prāṇī*). *Gātu* means a male cuckoo, a bee, a *gandharva*, and also a leader (*nāyana*). *Bhānu* means the sun (*āditya*). *Yātu* means a traveler (*adhvaga*) and time (*kāla*); it is neuter when it means a demon (*rakṣas*). *Hetu* means a cause (*kāraṇa*). After the root *ci* (in the form *cāya*), the suffix *ki* occurs. *Ketū* means a planet (*graha*) and a banner (*patākā*). The suffix *aptu* [is added after the root *vas*] to form *vāstu*, meaning "site" (78). The suffix *tun* [is added after the root *vas*] to form *vastu*, meaning "thing" (79). When meaning "dwelling," the suffix *ṇic* is also added; thus *veśma*, *bhū*, and *vāstu* denote "house" and are not feminine (80). The suffix *katu* is added after the root *kṛ* to form *kratu*, meaning "sacrifice" (81). The suffix *tu* is also added after the roots *edh* and *vah*; thus *edhatuḥ* means "man," and *vahatuḥ* means "ox" (82). The suffix *ātu* is added after the root *jīv* to form *jīvātu*, which is not feminine and means "food," "life," or "life-giving medicine" (83). The suffix *ātṛkan* is also added after *jīv*, with *vṛddhi* strengthening of the vowel; thus *jaivātṛka* refers to the moon, a physician, one who is long-lived, or a farmer.

84. From the roots *kṛṣi*, *cam*, *tan*, *nidhā* (from *dhā*), *nisṛj*, and *kharj*, the suffix *ū* is added. *karṣūḥ*: In the masculine, it means a fire of dried cow-dung (*karīṣāgni*); in the feminine, it is considered a river. *camūḥ*: An army. *tanūḥ*: The body. *dhanūḥ*: A weapon (bow). *sarja* in the sense of "emitting" (*sarjane*): *sarjūḥ* means a merchant. *kharja* in the sense of "affliction" (*vyathane*): *kharjūḥ* means scabies (*pāmā*). 85. After the root *mṛj*, there is the suffix *ū* and the substitution of *guṇa*. *marjūḥ*: One who performs purification. 86. After the root *vah*, there is the suffix *ū* and the substitution of *dha* for the root-final. *vadhūḥ*: A wife, a daughter-in-law, or a woman in general. 87. After the root *kaṣ*, there is the suffix *ū* and the substitution of *cha* for the root-final. *kacchūḥ*: Scabies. 88. The suffix *ū* is added after the roots *kas*, *pad*, and *ṛ* with the augment *ṇit*. *kasūḥ*: A sword. *patsūḥ*: A foot. *artsūḥ*: A year.

*kāsūḥ* means a spear (*śakti*). *pādūḥ* means that which bears feet (*caraṇadhāriṇī*). *ārūḥ* means tawny (*piṅgala*). [Pāṇini 5.2.127: "After *aṇ*, there is also *ḍa*. *āḍūḥ* is a substance that floats on water (*jalaplavadravya*). [Amara-kośa 2.4.136: "Both *tumbī* and *alābū* are the same. [Pāṇini 5.2.128: "When *nañ* is present, there is the elision of *n* after *labi*. According to Amara, both *tumbī* and *alābū* are identical. [Pāṇini 5.2.129: "After *ke*, there is *ū* and *eraṅ* for this [root]. When the word *ka* is an upapada, there is *ū* after the root *śṛṇāti*, and *eraṅ* is the substitute. *Keśarūḥ* is a grass-root (*tṛṇakanda*) and is feminine. By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), with the suffix *up*, *kaśeruḥ* is both neuter and masculine. [Pāṇini 5.2.130: "After *tṝ*, there is *ū* and *duṭ*. There is *ū* after the root *tṝ*, and *duṭ* is its augment.

*tardūḥ* would be *dāruhastakaḥ* (a wooden shovel). [The suffix] *ū* is added to the root *daridrāti*, and there is the elision (*lopa*) of both *ya* and *ā*. *Dardrūḥ* is a specific type of leprosy (*kuṣṭha*). [The suffix] *kū* is added to the roots *nṛt* and *śṛdh*. *Nṛtūḥ* is a dancer; *śṛdhūḥ* is drinking. [The suffix] *kū* is added to the root *ṛti*, and there is also the augment (*āgama*) *am*. *Ṛti* is a root belonging to the *sautra* (grammatical) tradition. From that, *rantūḥ* is formed with the augment *am*; it means a river of play (*devanadī*) and one who speaks the truth (*satyavāk*). *Andū*, *dṛmbhū*, *jambū*, *phelū*, *karkandhū*, and *didhiṣū*: these are irregularly formed (*nipātita*) words ending in the suffix *kū*.

*dṛndhū-*: from the root *dṛbh* (to tie). Due to a grammatical irregularity (*nipātana*), the augment *num* is added; thus, *dṛmbhūḥ*. Some say that the absence of the nasal (*anusvāra*) is also due to irregularity, resulting in *dṛnbhūḥ*. Pāṇini 3.2.97: *janer buk*: [The suffix] *buk* is added after the root *jan* (to be born). Thus, *jambūḥ*. Some say it is derived from the root *jam* (to eat), with the suffix *u*. Due to the rule of multiplicity (*bāhulaka*), there is also a short vowel, resulting in *jambuḥ*. *Kaphelūḥ*: [it] takes (*lāti*) phlegm (*kapha*). It refers to the *śleṣmātaka* tree. Due to irregularity, the vowel *e* is substituted for *i*. *Karkandhūḥ*: [it] holds (*dadhāti*) the *karka* fruit. It refers to the jujube tree (*badarī*). Due to irregularity, the augment *num* is added. *Didhiṣūḥ*: [she] abandons (*syati*) steadfastness (*didhi*, i.e., *dhairya*). It refers to a remarried woman (*punarbhū*).

Some, however, read *andūdṛmphūjambūkambū*. [The root] *dṛmph* means "to cause agitation"; *dṛmphūḥ* is a species of snake. (98) After the root *kam*, the suffix *buk* is added; *kambūḥ* is one who steals the property of others. (99) After the roots *mṛ* and *gṛ*, the suffix *ati* is added; *marut* [means wind], and *garut* means "wing. (100) After the root *gṛ*, the suffix *ati* is added along with the augment *muṭ*; *garmut* is gold and a particular kind of grass. (101) After the root *hṛṣ*, the suffix *alac* is added; *hṛṣulaḥ* means "deer" or "libidinous. And by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), after the root *caṭ*, [the suffix *alac* is added]; *caṭulam* means "beautiful."

102. From the roots *hṛ*, *sṛ*, *ruh*, and *yuṣ*, the suffix *iti* is applied. *Harit* means "direction" (*kakubh*), "color," and two specific types of grass. *Sarit* means "river. *Rohit* refers to the female of a particular species of deer; *yuṣ* is a root mentioned in the *Sūtra* (Pāṇini). According to the *Bhāṣya*: "The *rohit* is the female of the *ṛśya* [deer]; the *yoṣit* is the female of the *puruṣa*. 103. From the root *taḍ*, there is the elision of the causative suffix (*ṇiluk*). That which strikes or causes to strike is *taḍit* (lightning). 104. From the root *śam*, the suffix *ḍa* is applied. By virtue of the rule of "excessive abundance" (*bāhulaka*), the technical designation *it* does not apply, nor is there the substitution of *ey* for the root vowel, nor the augment *iṭ*. *Śaṇḍha* denotes a male cowherd (*gopati*) or a eunuch (*klība*). 105. From the root *kam*, the suffix *aṭha* is applied.

*kamaṭhaḥ*: According to the *Medinīkośa*, *kamaṭhaḥ* is masculine when meaning "tortoise," and neuter when meaning "a type of vessel. By way of irregularity (*bāhulaka*), [from the root *jṛ*] we have *jaraṭhaḥ*. 106. *Vṛddhi* is also applied to the root *ram*. *Rāmaṭham* means asafoetida (*hiṅgu*). 107. From the root *śam*, the suffix *kha* is added. *Śaṅkhaḥ* (conch). 108. From the root *kaṇ*, the suffix *ṭha* is added. *Kaṇṭhaḥ* (throat). 109. The suffix *kala* is added to the root *tṛp*; and because of the word "ca" (and), it is also added to *tṛph*. *Tṛpalā* is a creeper. *Triphalā*, however, refers to the group of three fruits. 110. From the root *śap*, the letter *ba* is substituted for the radical *śa*. *Śabalaḥ* (variegated). 111. The suffix *cit* is added after roots beginning with *vṛṣ*.

*vṛṣalaḥ* (a low-born man); *palalam* (meat)—here the *guṇa* substitution occurs by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*). *saralaḥ* (straight); *taralaḥ* (trembling). 112. After the root *gam*, the suffix *buk* is added. *kambalaḥ* (a woolen blanket). From the root *mus* (to crush), *musalam* (a pestle). 113. After the root *laṅg*, there is also a *vṛddhi* strengthening. *lāṅgalam* (a plough). 114. After the roots *kuṭi*, *kaśi*, and *kuti*, the augment *muṭ* is added to the suffix. *kuṭamalaḥ* (a bud); also from *kuḍ*, *kuḍmalaḥ* (a bud). *kaśmalam* (distress). By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), there is *guṇa*: *komalam* (tender). 115. After the root *mṛj*, there is the elision of the *ṭi* (the final vowel and following consonant). *malam* (dirt). 116. After the root *cup*, the penultimate vowel is replaced by *a*. *capalam* (fickle).

117. After the roots *śak* and *śam*, the suffix *niC* is applied. [Examples: *śakalam* (a piece), *śamalam* (impurity). 118. After the root *chā*, *guK* is the augment and the vowel is shortened. [Example: *chagalaḥ* (a goat). Because it belongs to the *prajñādi* group, *chāgalaḥ* is also formed. 119. After a root ending in *Ñ* or *Ṇ*, the suffix *aC* is applied. [Examples: *daṇḍaḥ* (a staff), *raṇḍā* (a widow), *khaṇḍaḥ* (a fragment), *bhaṇḍaḥ* (a rogue), *vaṇḍaḥ* (one with severed hands), *aṇḍaḥ* (an egg/testicle). Due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), there is the substitution of *sa* for *ṣa*: *ṣaṇḍaḥ* (a multitude/group); others say it begins with the palatal *ś*. [Examples: *śaṇḍaḥ*, *gaṇḍaḥ* (a boil), *caṇḍaḥ* (fierce), *paṇḍaḥ* (a eunuch); *paṇḍā* (intellect). 120. After the roots beginning with *kvā*, the suffixes are marked with the *k* indicatory letter (*kit*).

After verbal roots beginning with the *ka*-group (*kavarga*), the suffix *ḍha* is added as a *kit*. Examples: from *kuṇḍ*, *kuṇḍam*; from *kāṇḍ*, *kāṇḍam*; from *guṅ*, *guḍaḥ*; from *ghuṇ* (meaning "to wander"), *ghuṇḍaḥ* (a bee). 121. After the roots *sthā*, *cat*, and *mṛj*, the suffixes *ālaj*, *ūvalaj*, and *ālīyac* respectively are added. From *sthā*, *ālac*: *sthālam* (a vessel) and *sthālī* (a pot). From *cat*, *ūvalaj*: *catvālaḥ* (a sacrificial pit). From *mṛj*, *ālīyac*: *mārjālīyaḥ* (a cat). 122. From the roots *pat* and *caṇḍi*, the suffix *ālañ* is added. Examples: *pātālam* (the netherworld); *cāṇḍālaḥ* (an outcaste). Some say that because it belongs to the *prajñādi* group, the form *cāṇḍālaḥ* is also derived by adding the suffix *aṇ*.

123. The suffix *kālan* is added after the roots *tam*, *viś*, *biḍ*, *mṛṇ*, *kul*, *kap*, *pal*, and *pañc*. [Examples: *tamālaḥ*, *viśālaḥ*, *biḍālaḥ*, *mṛṇālam*, *kulālaḥ*, *kapālam*, *palālam*, *pañcālāḥ*. 124. The suffix *aṅgac* is added to the root *pat* when referring to a bird. [Example: *pataṅgaḥ*. 125. The suffix *aṅgac* is also added after the roots beginning with *tṛ*. [Examples: *taraṅgaḥ*, *lavaṅgam*. 126. The suffix *aṅgac* is added after the roots beginning with *viḍ*, and it is marked as *kit*. [Example: *viḍaṅgaḥ*.

*viḍaṅgaḥ*, *mṛdaṅgaḥ*, *kuraṅgaḥ*; and by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), there is also the substitution of *u* for *ṛ*. 127. After the roots *sṛ* and *vṛñ*, there is also *vṛddhi*. Thus: *sāraṅgaḥ* (a spotted deer); *vāraṅgaḥ* (the hilt of a sword or similar weapon). 128. From the roots *gam* and *ad*, [the suffix *aṅ* is applied]. Thus: *gaṅgā* (the Ganges); *adgaḥ* (a sacrificial cake, *puroḍāśa*). 129. After the roots *chā*, *pū*, and *khaḍi*, the suffix is *kit*. Thus: *chāgaḥ* (a goat); *pūgaḥ* (a betel-nut tree or a multitude); *khaḍgaḥ* (a rhinoceros or a sword). By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), after the root *ṣiṭ* in the sense of "disregard," there is no change of *ṣ* to *s*. Thus: *ṣiḍgaḥ* (a fickle or wanton man). Regarding this, Māgha says: "He was addressed thus with agitation by the *ṣiṅgas* (wanton men), 'She is alone! (Śiśupālavadha 3.46).

130. After the root *bhṛ* (to carry), the suffix *kin* is applied, along with the augment *nuṭ*. After *bhṛ*, *gan* is applied as *kit*, and there is the augment *nuṭ* for that [suffix]. *Bhṛṅgāḥ* refers to bees, parrots, and hornbills. 131. After the root *śṛ* (to crush), there is also the shortening of the vowel. *Śṛṅgam* (a horn). 132. In the sense of a bird (*śakuni*), after the root *śṛ*, the suffix *gan* is applied. The augment *nuṭ* is understood [from the previous rule]. *Śārṅgaḥ* (a kind of bird). 133. After the roots *mud* and *gṛ*, the suffixes *gak* and *ga* are applied respectively. *Mudgaḥ* (a bean); *Gargaḥ* (a proper name). 134. The suffix *aṇḍan* is applied after the roots *kṛ*, *sṛ*, *bhṛ*, and *vṛ*. *Karaṇḍaḥ* (a basket); *Saraṇḍaḥ* (a type of bird); *Bharaṇḍaḥ* (a master); *Varaṇḍaḥ* (a disease of the mouth). 135. The suffix *adi* is applied after the roots *śṝ*, *dṝ*, and *bhas*. *Śarad* (autumn).

[The suffix *u* is added to the roots *dṛ* and *dhṛ*] when meaning "the two banks of the heart" (*daraddhṛdayakūlayoḥ*). [The form] *bhasajjaghanam* [is derived from *bhasajjaghana*]. 136. From the root *dṛ*, [the suffix *asun* is added], and there is a short vowel [for the radical *r*]: *dṛṣat* (stone). 137. From the roots *tyaj*, *tan*, and *yaj*, [the suffix *ḍit* is added]: *tyad* (that), *tad* (that), *yad* (which). These belong to the class beginning with *sarva*. 138. From the root *i*, [the suffix *asun* is added] with the augment *tuṭ*: *etad* (this). 139. From the root *sṛ*, [the suffix] *aṭi* [is added]: *saraṭ* occurs in the sense of wind and cloud. However, in the Vedic commentary on the mantra "yābhiḥ kṛśānum," it is explained as "from the *saraṭ*s, i.e., honey-bees. 140. From the root *laṅgh*, [the suffix *aṭi* is added] and the nasal is replaced by *l*: *laghaṭ* means wind.

141. From the root *pṛ* (to cross over), the suffix *aji* is applied. *Pāraka* means gold. 142. After the root *prath*, the suffix *kit* is applied and there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). *Pṛthak*. Because it is listed among the words beginning with *svar*, it is an indeclinable (*avyaya*). 143. After the root *bhī* (to fear), the suffix *ṣuk* is applied and the vowel is shortened. *Bhiṣaj* (physician). 144. From the roots *yuṣ* and *as*, the suffix *madik* is applied. *Yuṣ* is a root belonging to the *sautra* class. *Yuṣmad* (you); *asmad* (we); *tvam* (you, singular); *aham* (I). 145. From the roots *ṛ*, *tu*, *su*, *hu*, *sṛ*, *dhṛ*, *bhikṣ*, *bhī*, *yā*, *vā*, *pad*, *yakṣ*, and *nī*, the suffix *man* is applied. The suffix *man* is added to these fourteen roots. *Arma* is an eye disease.

*Stoma* means a collection; *soma*; *homa* (an oblation); *sarma* means going; *dharma* means security, welfare, or linen (*kṣauma*); from the root *kṣu* with the suffix *aṇ*, it also becomes *kṣauma*; *bhāma* means the sun; *yāma*; *vāma* means beautiful or wicked; *padma*; from the root *yakṣ* in the sense of worship, *yakṣama* means the king of diseases (consumption); *nema*. 146. From the root *jahāti* (to abandon), there is the suffix *man* with the reduplication as in the desiderative (*san-vat*) and the elision of the vowel *ā*. *Jihma* means crooked or slow. 147. From the root *avati* (to protect), there is the suffix *man* with the elision of the *ṭi* (the final vowel and following consonant). This elision of the *ṭi* applies to the suffix *man*, not to the verbal base (*prakṛti*). *Avama* means low or inferior.

Otherwise, one would have simply said *ḍit*. [In the rule] *jvaratvara-*, the suffix *ūṭh* is applied; when its lengthening is performed, *guṇa* substitution occurs. Ujjvaladatta claims that because it is listed among the *ca*-group, it has the status of an indeclinable (*avyaya*), but that is not correct, because those [items in the *ca*-group] denote non-substantiality (*asattvārthatva*). In reality, however, its status as an indeclinable arises from its inclusion in the *svarādi* group. From the root *ava*, [with the suffix *man*], we derive *om*. 148. After the root *gras*, there is also the vowel *ā*. [Thus: *grāṃaḥ*. 149. After the roots *avi*, *si*, *vi*, and *śuṣ*, the suffix *man* is *kit*. [Thus: *ūmaṃ* (a city); *syūmaḥ* (a rein); *simaḥ* (all); *śuṣmam* (fire and proximity).

150. From the roots *iṣ*, *yudh*, *indh*, *das*, *śyā*, *dhū*, and *sū*, the suffix *man* is applied. *Īṣmaḥ*: desire and spring (*vasanta*). In the reading *īṣī*, it begins with a long vowel. *yudhmaḥ*: an arrow and a warrior. *idhmaḥ*: sacrificial fuel (*samit*). *dasmaḥ*: a sacrificer (*yajamāna*). *śyāmaḥ*: smoke. *sūmaḥ*: the atmosphere (*antarīkṣa*). By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), *īrmaṃ* means a wound (*braṇa*). 151. From the roots *yuj*, *uc*, and *tij*, the suffix *man* is applied, and *ku* is substituted for the final consonant. *yugmam*: a pair. *rukmaṃ*: gold. *tigmaṃ*: sharp. 152. From the root *han*, *hi* is substituted [for the final *n*], and the suffix *man* is applied. *himaṃ*: snow or frost. 153. From the root *bhī*, the syllable *ṣuk* is optionally substituted [for the final *ī*], and the suffix *man* is applied. *bhīmaḥ*: terrifying. *bhīṣmaḥ*: formidable. 154. [From the root *ghṛ*,] *gharmaḥ* [is formed]. (The heat of the sun; the hot season.)

The suffix *magguṇa* is also applied as a *nipātana* (irregular formation) to the root *ghṛ*. 155. *grīṣmaḥ* ("summer"). This is a *nipātana* derived from the root *pra-sṛ*. 156. From the root *pṛth*, the suffix *ṣivan* is applied, along with *saṃprasāraṇa* (vowel substitution). *pṛthivī* ("earth"). Some say the suffix is *ṣavan*. According to the *Śabdārṇava*: "pṛthavī, pṛthivī, pṛthvī. 157. From the roots *aś*, *pruṣ*, *laṭ*, *kaṇ*, *khaṭ*, and *viś*, the suffix *kvan* is applied. *aśvaḥ* ("horse"). *pruṣ* means "to sprinkle" and so on; *pruṣvaḥ* refers to a season or the sun; *pruṣvā* refers to a drop of water. *Laṭ* refers to a species of bird or a fruit. *Kaṇva* means "evil."

By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), *kiṇva*, *khaṭvā*, and *viśva* are also [formed with the suffix *van*]. 158. From the roots *iṇ* and *śī*, the suffix *van* [is added]. *Evaḥ* means "one who goes. In the phrase *ye ca evā marutaḥ*, this is a particle (*nipāta*) not denoting a substance (*asattve*). *Śevam* [means] "auspiciousness" for Mitra and Varuṇa. 159. The forms *sarva*, *nighṛṣva*, *ariṣva*, *laṣva*, *śiva*, *paṭva*, and *prahva* are irregularly formed (*nipātana*) with the suffix *van* when they do not denote an agent (*asvatantre*). These are introduced as irregular forms when they are not agents. Because everything has been traversed by it, it is called *sarvam*. There is also an absence of *guṇa* substitution after the prefix *ni-* in the root *ṛṣ*; thus, that by which something is rubbed is *nighṛṣvaḥ*, meaning a hoof. *Riṣvaḥ* means "injurious."

Others say *laṣva*. In that case, there is also the substitution of *i* for the penultimate vowel. *Śiva* means "Auspicious" (*śambhu*), because everything rests (*śete*) in him; there is shortening of the vowel in the root *śīṅ*. *Paṭva* refers to a chariot and the world of earth (*bhūloka*). *Prahva* means "one who is called forth" (*prahūyate*); there is the elision of the vowel *ā* and the consonant *v* from the root *hveñ*, or alternatively, the elision of *ā* from the root *jahāti*. From the root *īṣ* with the suffix *vun*, we get *īṣva*, meaning "teacher" (*ācārya*). Others say *iṣva*. Why [is the suffix used] when [the agent] is not independent? [Answer: *sartā* (a mover) and *sārakaḥ* (a driver). By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), from the root *hras* we derive *hrasva* (short). 160. *śauva-vaya-vajra-jihvā-grīvā-pv-amīvāḥ*.

The suffix *śeva* is for the purpose of making the final syllable udātta. They go by means of this: *vahvaḥ*; there is a short vowel and the augment *huk*. They lick with this: *jihvā*; the letter *l* becomes *j*, and there is an absence of *guṇa*. They swallow with this: *grīvā*; there is the augment *īḍ*. That which reaches is *āpvā*, namely the wind (*vāyu*). *Mīvā* is a stomach-worm; others say it is the wind. 161. From the roots *kṝ*, *gṝ*, *śṝ*, and *dṛ*, the suffix *va* is added. *Karvaḥ* means desire (*kāma*) and also a rat (*ākhu*). *Garvaḥ*. *Śarvaḥ*. *Darvaḥ* is a Rākṣasa. 162. The suffix *kanin* is added after the roots *yu*, *vṛṣi*, *takṣi*, *rāj*, *dhinv*, *dyut*, and *pratidiv*.

He joins (*yunakti*) is *yuvan*; *vṛṣan* is Indra; *takṣan* is a carpenter; *rājan* is a king; *dhanvan* is a desert; *dhanus* is a bow; *dyuvan* is the sun; they gamble (*pratidīvanti*) upon it, thus *pratidivan* is a day. 163. After the roots *sap* and *aś*, the suffix *kan* is added, along with the augment *tuṭ*. Thus: *sapta* (seven) and *aṣṭa* (eight). 164. After the root *jahāti* when preceded by the negative particle *nañ*, [the suffix *kan* is added]. Thus: *ahan* (day). 165. *śvan*, *ukṣan*, *pūṣan*, *plīhan*, *klēdan*, *snehana*, *mūrghan*, *majjan*, *aryaman*, *viśvapsan*, *parijman*, *mātariśvan*, and *maghavan*: these thirteen words ending in the suffix *kan* are irregularly formed (*nipātyante*).

It swells, thus it is *śvā* (the dog). *Ukṣā* is Pūṣan. [From] the root *plih* "to go," there is the lengthening of the vowel *i*: it swells, thus *plīhā*, a disease of the belly. [From] *klidū* "to become moist": it becomes moist, thus *kledā*, the moon. From *snihyati*, there is the substitution of *guṇa*: it is affectionate, thus *snehā*, a friend and the moon. They faint when struck here; thus *mūrdhā* (the head). After the root *muha*, there is the lengthening of the penultimate vowel, the substitution of *dha* for the final letter, and the addition of the augment *ram*. It sinks into the bones, thus *majjā*, the marrow, the essence of the bone. Preceded by *arya*, the root *māṅ* [becomes] *aryamā*.

Agni is called *viśvapsā* because he devours (*psāti*) everything (*viśvam*). *Parijmā* is Agni; he is born everywhere (*parijāyate*) and is radiant (*candraḥ*). [In this formation], there is elision of the penultimate vowel of the root *jan-* and the substitution of *ma* for the final letter. He swells (*śvayati*) in the mother, the intermediate space (*antarikṣe*), thus he is *mātariśvā*. There is elision of the vowel *i* from the root. From the root *maha* in the sense of "worship" (*pūjāyām*), the *h* becomes *gh*, and with the addition of the augment *vuK*, one obtains *maghavān*, namely Indra. Thus ends the first quarter of the *auṇādika* suffixes.
The second chapter.

166. From the roots *kṛ* (to do) and *hṛ* (to take), the suffix *eṇu* is applied. *Kareṇuḥ* (an elephant); *hareṇuḥ* (a fragrant substance). 167. From the roots *han* (to strike), *kuṣ* (to tear), *nī* (to lead), and *kāś* (to shine), the suffix *kthan* is applied. *Hathaḥ* (one who is dejected); *kuṣṭhaḥ* (the plant Kuṣṭha); *nīthaḥ* (a leader); *rathaḥ* (a wooden chariot). 168. After the root *bhṛ* (to carry) preceded by the prefix *ava*, [the suffix *kthan* is applied]. *Avabhṛthaḥ* (the final purificatory bath at the end of a sacrifice). 169. From the roots *uṣ* (to burn), *kuṣ* (to tear), and *gā* (to sing), the suffix *sthan* is applied. *Oṣṭhaḥ* (the lip); *koṣṭham* (the interior of a chest); *gāthā* (a verse or meaningful expression). By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), *śothaḥ* (swelling) is also formed. 170. From the root *sṛ* (to go) with the augment *ṇit*. *Sārthaḥ* (a caravan or a multitude). 171. From the roots *jṝ* (to grow old) and *vṛñ* (to choose), the suffix *ūthan* is applied. *Jarūtham* (flesh).

*Varūtha* is a masculine term meaning the protection of a chariot. (172) The suffix *tak* is applied after the roots *pā*, *tṛ*, *div*, *vac*, *ric*, and *sic*. Thus: *pītha* means the sun, clarified butter (*ghṛta*), and a drinking vessel. *Tīrtha* is well known in three senses: a sacred scripture, a sacrificial altar, and a holy bathing place; it is also used for a spiritual teacher (*upādhyāya*), a descent point (*avatāra*), one frequented by sages (*ṛṣijuṣṭa*), and the menses of a woman—so says the *Viśva* lexicon. *Tutha* is Agni. *Uktha* is a specific type of *Sāman*. *Riktha*: by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), the suffix is also applied after the root *ṛc*. Thus *riktha* or *ṛktha* means wealth or property. *Siktha* [is honey-foam]. (173) The suffix *niti* is applied after the root *ar*. Thus *nirṛtha* is a *Sāman*.

174. *Niśītha*, *gopītha*, and *avagatha*. *Niśītha* means midnight or the night in general. *Gopītha* means a bathing place (*tīrtha*). *Avagatha* means one who has bathed in the morning. 175. *Gaś cedi* (if there is *ga*). *Udgītha* is a specific portion of the *Sāman* chant. 176. *Samīṇaḥ*. *Samītha* means fire (*bahni*) and battle (*saṃgrāma*). 177. *Titha-pṛṣṭha-gūtha-yūtha-prothāḥ*. [The suffix *tha* is added] after the root *tij* with the elision of the vowel *ja*. *Titha* means fire (*anala*) and desire (*kāma*). *Pṛṣṭha* means the back. *Gūtha* means excrement (*viṣṭhā*). *Yūtha* means a herd or multitude (*samūha*). *Protha* means the nostrils.

*Protha* is not feminine; it refers to the horse's snout, and *protha* is said to mean "set out. The suffix *rak* occurs after thirty-two roots: *sphāyi*, *tañci*, *vañci*, *śaki*, *kṣipi*, *kṣudi*, *sṛpi*, *tṛpi*, *dṛpi*, *vand*, *undi*, *śvit*, *vṛti*, *aji*, *nī*, *pad*, *mad*, *mudi*, *khidi*, *chidi*, *bhidi*, *mand*, *candi*, *dahi*, *das*, *dambh*, *vas*, *vāś*, *śīṅ*, *has*, *sidhi*, and *śubh*. *Rak* is added to these thirty-two [roots]. In the case of *vali*, there is the elision of *y*. *sphāram* (vast). Due to belonging to the *nyaṅkvādi* group, there is the substitution of *k* for *t* (*kutva*). *takram* (buttermilk). *vakram* (crooked). *śakraḥ* (Indra). *kṣipram* (quickly). *kṣudraḥ* (mean/small). *sṛpraḥ* (the moon).

*Tṛpraḥ* means a sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*). *Dṛpraḥ* means strong or powerful. *Vandraḥ* means one who worships. From the root *undī*, *undraḥ* means a water-dweller. *Śvitram* means leprosy. *Vṛtraḥ* refers to an enemy, sound, darkness, a mountain, a wheel, and a demon (*dānava*). From the root *aj* with the suffix *vī*, *vīraḥ* is formed. *Nīram* means water. *Padraḥ* means a village. *Mandraḥ* means joy and a particular region. *Mudrā* is that which produces conviction or recognition. *Khidraḥ* means disease and a poor person. *Chidram* means a hole or opening. *Bhidram* means a thunderbolt. *Mandraḥ* and *candraḥ* [are also formed thus]; *candaḥ* is also [formed] by adding the suffix *ac* to the root *cad*.

Himāṃśu, Candramas, Candra, Śaśin, and Canda denote the moon; himadyuti means "having the luster of snow. Dahana denotes fire (agni). Dasra and Svarvaidya denote the two divine physicians (the Aśvins). Dambhra denotes the ocean and also something very small. [The forms] Vasman and Vatsara are derived from the root vas with vocalization of the semivowel.

SK 3168 / 179 / *na raparasṛpisṛjispṛśispṛhisavanādīnām* (A 8.3.110): A cerebral (*mūrdhanya*) substitution shall not occur for the *s* that follows a *r*, nor for the *s* of roots such as *sṛp*, *sṛj*, *spṛś*, *spṛh*, or words beginning with *savana*. The commentary (*vṛtti*) states that this rule is intended to prohibit what would otherwise have been obtained by the rule *pūrvapadāt* (8.3.106). Therefore, even what would have been obtained by the rule *śāsivasi-* (8.3.60) does not apply here. Examples: *usraḥ* (a ray of light); *usrā* (a cow); *vāśraḥ* (the day); *vāśram* (a dwelling); *śīraḥ* (a python); *hasraḥ* (a fool); *sidhraḥ* (a virtuous person); *śubhram* (bright). 180. *muser ak*: [The suffix] *ak* is added after the root *mus*. Example: *musram*. By virtue of the principle of multiplicity (*bāhulaka*), [the suffix *ak* is also applied] to form *aśruḥ* (a tear).

181. In the case of the roots *cakram* and *ruk*, the vowel *u* is substituted for the penultimate vowel. *Cukra* means a sour substance; *rukra* means reddish-brown. 182. After the prefix *vi*, the root *kas* [takes the same substitution]. *Vikusra* means the moon. 183. After the prefixes *ā* and *tam*, there is also lengthening of the vowel. *Āmra*; *tāmra*. 184. After the root *nid*, there is also the elision of the nasal (*n*). *Nidrā*. 185. After the root *ard*, there is also lengthening of the vowel. *Ārdra*. 186. After the root *śuc*, there is also the substitution of *da*. *Śūdra*. 187. After the prefix *dur*, there is the elision of the nasal in the root *iṇ*. That which is reached with difficulty is *dūra*. 188. After the root *kṛt*, there is the substitution of *cha* and *krū*. *Kṛcchra*; *krūra*.

189. *ṇiluk* and *ca*. [The suffix] *ṇi* is elided after the root *rud*, and [the suffix *ac* is added]. Thus, he who causes to weep (*rodayati*) is *rudraḥ*. 190. *Bahulam anyatrāpi saṃjñāchandasoḥ*. The elision of *ṇi* occurs diversely in other cases as well, both in names (*saṃjñā*) and in Vedic meters (*chandas*). [The rule] "elision of *ṇi*" applies here as well. For example: "The winds blow that wither the leaves; thereafter others are leaf-shedders (*parṇamuc*). 191. *Jorī ca*. After the root *jṝ*, there is the suffix *ī*. Thus, *jīraḥ* means "minute" (*aṇu*). Some say there is also the suffix *ya*. 192. *Susūdhāgṛdhibhyaḥ kran*. After the roots *su*, *sū*, *dhā*, and *gṛdh*, the suffix *kran* is added. Thus: *suraḥ*, *sūraḥ*; *dhīraḥ*; *gṛdhraḥ*. 193. *Śusicimīnāṃ dīrghaś ca*. After the roots *śu*, *si*, *ci*, and *mī*, the suffix *kran* is added and the vowel is lengthened. *Śu* is a root found in the *sūtra* (Vedic). Thus: *śūraḥ*; *sīram*; *cīram*; *bhīraḥ* (the ocean).

194. From the roots *ci* (to gather) and *dhi* (to hold), the suffix *ran* is applied; thus, *vodhraṃ* means "pure" (*vimalam*). 195. From the roots *vṛdh* (to grow) and *vap* (to sow/sprout), the suffix *ran* is applied; thus, *vardhraṃ* means "leather," and *vapraḥ* means "a rampart. 196. The nineteen words ending in the suffix *ran*—namely *ṛjra*, *indra*, *agra*, *vajra*, *vipra*, *kṛtra*, *cubra*, *kṣura*, *khura*, *bhadra*, *ugra*, *bhera*, *bhela*, *śukra*, *śukla*, *gaura*, *vamra*, *rāma*, and *lāla*—are irregularly formed (*nipātana*) with the absence of *guṇa* substitution. *Ṛjra* means "a leader. From the root *idi* (to rule), *indraḥ*. In *agra* (from the root *aṅg*), there is the elision of the nasal (*nalopa*). *Vajraḥ* (masculine/neuter) means "diamond" or "thunderbolt. From the root *ḍu-vap* (to sow), the penultimate vowel becomes *i* (*itvam*); thus, *vipraḥ*.

In *kumbi* and *cumbi*, there is the elision of *n*. *Kubram* means "forest"; *cubram* means "face. In the root *kṣur* (in the sense of "cutting"), there is the elision of *r*; there is no *guṇa* strengthening: *kṣuraḥ*. In the root *khur* (in the sense of "cutting"), there is the elision of *r* and the absence of *guṇa*: *khuraḥ*. In the root *bhand*, there is the elision of *n*: *bhadram*. In the root *uc* (in the sense of "gathering"), *c* becomes *g*: *ugraḥ*. In the root *ñibhī*, [the suffix] *ī* [is added]: *bherī*. Optionally, *l* [is substituted for *b*]: *bhelaḥ* (an object for crossing water). In the root *śuc*, *c* becomes *k*: *śukraḥ*. Optionally, *l* [is substituted for *c*]: *śuklaḥ*. In the root *guṅ* (in the sense of "growth"), [there is the substitution of *au*]: *gauraḥ* (meaning reddish-brown, white, or yellow).

The roots *vana* and *vabhra* mean "to divide. There is an absence of *guṇa* in the root *iṇ*. *Irā* means "intoxicating drink" and "water. *Mā* means "to measure"; hence *mālā*. (197) With the suffix *ukan*, [the root] *sam-kaś* is used; *kaś* means "to go. Because people flee from him properly (*samyak*), he is called *saṅkasuka*, meaning a wicked person and one who is unstable. (198) After the roots *pac* and *naś*, there are the suffixes *ṇukan* and *kanum*. From *pac*, the suffix *ka* is added: *pākuka* means a cook (*sūpakāra*). From *naś*, with the augment *num*: *naṃśuka*. (199) After the root *bhī*, the suffix *krukan* is added: *bhīruka*.

200. After the roots *kvi*, *śilpī* (craftsman), and *saṃjñā* (name), [the suffix] *akan* is applied even to those not previously mentioned. *rajakaḥ* (washerman); *ikṣukuṭṭakaḥ* (sugarcane crusher); *carakaḥ* (wanderer). From the root *caṣ* (to eat): *caṣakaḥ* (cup); *śunakaḥ* (dog); *bhaṣakaḥ* (barker). 201. After the root *ram*, *ra* is substituted for *ra*, or *la* optionally. *ramakaḥ* (one who delights, a voluptuary); *lamakaḥ*. 202. After the root *jahāti* (to abandon), two [letters] are added [at the beginning]. *jahakaḥ* (one who abandons, a renouncer) and *kālaḥ* (time). 203. After the root *dhmā*, *dham* is substituted for *dhmā*. *dhamakaḥ* (a blacksmith). 204. After the root *han*, *vadha* is substituted for *han*. *vadhakaḥ* (a killer). [The suffix *akan* is applied] diversely (*bahulam*) in other cases as well. From the root *kuh* (to deceive): *kuhakaḥ* (a deceiver); *kṛtakam* (a forgery).

205. For the root *kṛṣ*, there is also the suffix *vṛddhi* (vr̥ddhi-vowel substitution) according to the Eastern grammarians. *Kārṣakaḥ*; *kṛṣkaḥ*. 206. And [the word] *udaka* is for the sake of providing an example (*prapañca*). 207. After the roots *vṛśc* and *kṛṣ*, the suffix *kikan* is applied. *Vṛścikaḥ*; *kṛṣikaḥ*. 208. After the roots *pra-āp* and *pra-ā-kṛṣ*, the suffix *ikaṣ* is applied. *Prāpaṇikaḥ* means a seller of merchandise; *prākaṣikaḥ* means one who lives off the wives of others. 209. After the root *muṣ*, there is also lengthening of the vowel. *Mūṣikaḥ* means a rat. 210. After the root *syam*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*), and by the word "and" (*ca*), there is also lengthening. *Sīmikaḥ* is a type of tree. 211. After the root *krī*, the suffix *ikan* is applied. *Krayikaḥ* means a buyer.

212. After the roots *paṇi*, *pani*, *pati*, and *khan*, with the prefix *āṅ*, [the suffix *ini* is applied]. *āpaṇikaḥ* (a merchant); *āpanikaḥ* (a merchant); *indranīlaḥ* (sapphire) and *kirātaḥ* (a Kirāta hunter). *āpatikaḥ* (a hawk) and that which is dependent on fate (*daivāyatta*). *ākhanikaḥ* (a mouse) and a boar. 213. After the roots *śyai*, *styai*, *hṛ*, and *ava*, the suffix *inaC* is applied. *śyenaḥ* (a hawk); *styenaḥ* (a thief); *hariṇaḥ* (a deer); *avinaḥ* (an Adhvaryu priest). 214. After the root *vṛj*, [the suffix *inaC* is applied] and it is also *kit*. *vṛjinam* (crookedness/sin). 215. After the root *aj*, [the suffix *inaC* is applied] and there is also the substitution of *aja* for the root. This is for the purpose of preventing the *vībhāva* (vocalization). *ajinam* (skin/deer-skin). 216. [The suffix *inaC* is applied] diversely (*bahulam*) in other cases as well. *kaṭhinam* (hardness); *nalinam* (lotus); *malinam* (dirtiness).

From the root *kuṇḍ* (to surround), *kuṇḍinam*. From *div* (to play/shine), *dyateḥ*; in the sense of a person, *dinam*; *dinam* also means "day. From *dru* (to run) and *dakṣi* (to be able), with the suffix *inin*: *draviṇam* (wealth); *dakṣiṇaḥ* (right-hand, clever); *dakṣiṇā* (a gift). From *ṛ* (to go), with the suffix *in*, it is *kit* and *i* is substituted: *iriṇam* (a barren spot, a desert). From *vep* (to tremble) and *tuhi* (to be cold), there is also a shortening of the vowel: *vipinam* (a forest); *tuhinam* (snow, frost). From *tali* and *puli*, also: *talinaṃ* (thin, sparse, small, clear—*talinaṃ* is used in three genders); *pulinaṃ* (a sandbank). From *gurvī* (to be heavy), *a* is replaced by *u* and the suffix *in*: because it belongs to the *gaurādi* group, the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied: *gurviṇī* (pregnant); *garbhiṇī* (pregnant).

223. And from the root *ruh* [the suffix *ini* is added]. Thus: *rohiṇaḥ*. 224. From the root *maha*, the suffixes *inaṇ* and [by force of *ca*,] *inan* are added. Thus: *māhinan*. *Mahinam* means "sovereignty. 225. After the roots *vac*, *pracch*, *śri*, *sru*, *dru*, *pru*, and *ju*, the suffix *kvip* is added; there is lengthening of the vowel and no vocalization (*asaṃprasāraṇa*). Thus: *vāk* (speech); *prāṭ* (one who asks); *śrīḥ* (prosperity); *srūḥ*—that from which clarified butter and the like flow, namely a sacrificial vessel; *drūḥ*—gold; *kaṭaprūḥ*—a caterpillar that changes form at will and a certain insect; *jūḥ*—the sky, Sarasvatī, a female Piśācī, and a swift woman. 226. From the root *āp*, the vowel is shortened [before *kvip*]. Thus: *āpaḥ*; *apaḥ*.

*adbhiḥ*; *adbhyaḥ*. 227. *parau vrajeḥ ṣaś ca padānte*: After the prefix *pari*, the root *vraj* takes the suffix *kvip* and [the final vowel] becomes long at the end of a word (*padānte*), and the letter *ṣ* is substituted [for the *j*]. *paribrāṭ*; *parivrājau*. 228. *huvaḥ śluvac ca*: For the root *hve* (to call), there is the suffix *kvip* as if by elision (*ślu*). *juhūḥ*. 229. *sruvaḥ kaḥ*: For the word *sruva*, the suffix *ka* is applied. *sruvaḥ*. 230. *cik ca*: The suffix *cik* is also applied [to *srū*]. The vowel *i* is for the sake of pronunciation (*uccāraṇārtha*). By the rule *ka it kutvam*, the change to *k* occurs. "Cleanse both the *sruva* and the *sruca* ladles. 231. *tanoter anaś ca vaḥ*: From the root *tan*, the suffix *cik* is applied, and for the syllable *an*, the substitute *va* is applied. *tvak* (skin).

232. From the roots *glai* (to fade) and *nau* (to praise), the suffix *ḍau* is applied. Thus: *glauḥ* (the moon) and *nauḥ* (a ship). 233. A word ending in the suffix *cvi* is an indeclinable (*avyaya*). [The rule] "ḍau" applies here as well. Thus: *glaukaroti* (he makes something like the moon). Although this is already established by the rule *kṛnmejantaḥ* (words ending in *kṛt* suffixes with a final vowel or *m* are indeclinables), this [present rule] is for the sake of restriction: that words ending in *uṇādi* suffixes are indeclinables only when they end in *cvi*. 234. From the root *rā* (to give), the suffix *ḍau* is applied. Thus: *rāḥ* (wealth). [Declension: *rāyau*, *rāyaḥ*. 235. From the root *gam* (to go), the suffix *ḍo* is applied. Thus: *gauḥ* (a cow). [Note: *Gauḥ* refers to the sun, a bull, a ray of light, and a specific sacrifice. In the feminine (*strī*), however, it denotes the direction (the quarter), Sarasvatī, the earth, and also a fragrant substance.

The suffix *ḍo* is applied after the roots *nṛ*, *strī*, and *dyut* (in the sense of heaven, thunderbolt, water, ray, eye, arrow, and hair), by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*). Thus, *dyauḥ* (feminine) means heaven and the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*). By the addition of the suffix *ḍū* after the root *bhram*, we have *bhrūḥ* (the eyebrow). By the force of the word "and" (*ca*), it is also added after the root *gam*: *agregūḥ* (one who goes at the head). From the root *dam*, the suffix *ḍosi* is applied: *doḥ* (arm); dual: *doṣau*. From the root *paṇi*, the suffix *ij* is applied, and the letter *j* is replaced by *v*: *vaṇik* (merchant). The suffix *aṇ* is added in the sense of the base itself (*svārthe*): *naigamaḥ*, *vāṇijaḥ*, or *vaṇik*. After the root *vaś*, the suffix *kit* is applied: *uśig* (fire, and also clarified butter). After the root *bhṛ*, the suffix *ūc* is applied: *bhūri* (earth).

241. From the roots *jas*, *sah*, and *ur*, the suffix *i* is applied. Thus: *jasuriḥ* means "vajra" (thunderbolt); *sahuriḥ* means "Āditya" (the sun) and "the earth"; *uririḥ* [is formed]. 242. After the roots *su*, *yu*, *ru*, and *vṛñ*, the suffix *yuc* is applied. Thus: *savanaḥ* means "the moon"; *yavanaḥ*; *ravaṇaḥ*; *kokilaḥ* (cuckoo); *varaṇaḥ*. 243. After the root *aś*, the suffix *yuc* is applied and *aś* is replaced by *raś*. Thus: *raśanā* means "girdle. However, when it denotes the tongue, it contains a dental *s*. 244. After the root *und*, there is elision of the nasal (*n*). Thus: *odanaḥ* (boiled rice). 245. After the root *gam*, the suffix *yuc* is applied and *ga* is the substitute. Thus: *gaganam* (the sky).

The suffix *yuc* may occur abundantly after other roots as well: *syandanaḥ*, *rocanā*. 246. After the root *rañj*, the suffix *kyun* occurs: *rajanam*. 247. In the Veda, [the suffix *kyun* occurs] after the roots *bhū*, *sū*, *dhū*, and *bhrasj*: *bhuvanam*; *suvana* refers to the sun; *dhanavaḥ* refers to fire; *nidhuvanam* refers to sexual intercourse; *bhṛjjanam* refers to a frying pan. 248. The suffix *kyu* occurs after the roots *kṝ*, *pṝ*, *vṛj*, *mand*, and *dhā*: *kiraṇaḥ*; *puraṇaḥ* refers to the ocean; *vṛjanam* refers to the intermediate space; *mandanam* refers to a hymn of praise; *nidhanam*. 249. After the root *dhṛṣ*, the substitution of *dhiṣ* for *dhṛṣ* occurs when a name is formed.

*Dhiṣaṇa* is a heavy [name]. *Dhiṣaṇā* is wisdom (*dhī*). 250. In the sense of the present tense, the words *pṛṣat*, *bṛhat*, *mahat*, and *jagat* are formed, and they behave like words ending in the *śatṛ* suffix (i.e., they are treated as present participles). *Pṛṣu* means "to sprinkle"; there is an absence of *guṇa* [strengthening], resulting in *pṛṣanti*. *Bṛhat* means "great. From the root *gam*, there is the substitution of *jagad*; thus, *jagat*. 251. *Saṃścat*, *tṛpat*, and *vehat* are irregularly formed (*nipātita*). The separate mention [of these] is for the purpose of preventing their being treated like words ending in *śatṛ*. From *saṃcinoti*, there is the prefix *suṭ* and the elision of the vowel *i*; thus, *saṃścat* means a deceiver. *Tṛpat* means a parasol (*chatra*). From *han* preceded by *vi*, there is the elision of the *ṭi* (the final syllable); thus, *vehat* (a cow that miscarries).

And these [are the forms]: *vehad* (a cow that miscarries) and *garbhopaghātinī* (one who destroys the fetus). 252. After the roots *chand*, *as*, *śuc*, and *ṝ*, the suffix *asānac* is applied: *śavasānaḥ panthāḥ* (the path is powerful), *urasānaḥ puruṣaḥ* (a man is broad-chested). 253. After the roots *ṛñj*, *vṛdh*, *mand*, and *sah*, the suffix *asānac* is applied with the *k*-marker: *ṛñjasāno meghaḥ* (a cloud is stretching forth), *vṛdhasānaḥ puruṣaḥ* (a man is growing), *mandasāno 'gnir jīvaś ca* (fire and a living being are rejoicing), *sahasāno yajño mayūraś ca* (the sacrifice and a peacock are prevailing). 254. After the root *ṛ*, there is *guṇa* substitution and the prefix *śuṭ*: *arśasāno 'gniḥ* (fire is spreading). 255. After the root *stu*, the suffix *sam-yān-ac* is applied: *saṃstavāno vāgmī* (an eloquent speaker is praising).

256. After the roots *yudh* (to fight), *budh* (to wake/understand), and *dṛś* (to see), the suffix *kvan* is added, and it is also marked with the *kit* designation. Examples: *yudhānaḥ*, *budhānaḥ*, and *dṛśānaḥ* as a name for a world-protector (*lokapālaka*). 257. After the root *hurch* (to bend/crook), when followed by the suffix *saN*, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix and elision (*lopa*) of the *ch*. Example: *juhurāṇaḥ* as a name for the moon (*candramas*). 258. After the root *śvit* (to become white), the *da* is substituted [for the *t* of the suffix], and the suffix is *kvan*. Example: *śiśvidānaḥ* as one who performs meritorious deeds (*puṇyakarman*). 259. The suffixes *tṛn* and *tṛc* are added after the group of roots beginning with *śaṃs* (to praise) and the group beginning with *kṣad* (to cut), respectively, when used as proper names (*saṃjñā*), and they do not take the augment *iṭ*. Thus, *tṛn* and *tṛc* are added after *śaṃs* and the others respectively, and they are without the *iṭ* augment. Examples: *śaṃstā* (one who praises/a singer), *śaṃstarau*, *śaṃstaraḥ*.

The root *kṣadi* is a Vedic (sautra) root meaning "to split" and "to eat"; it is anudātta (unaccented). This is known from the mantra *vṛkye cakṣadānam* ("splitting for the wolf") and from the Brāhmaṇa passage *ukṣāṇaṃ vā vehataṃ vā kṣadante* ("they eat a bull or a cow in heat"). The suffix *tṛn* forms the following: *kṣattā* occurs in the sense of a charioteer, a door-keeper, and a son born of a Kṣatriya woman by a Śūdra father. It is used diversely (*bahulam*) in other senses as well. Examples include: *man* → *mantā*; *han* → *hantā*, and so forth. 260. The following are irregularly formed with the suffix *tṛn*: *naptṛ* (grandson), *neṣṭṛ* (officiating priest), *tvaṣṭṛ* (the artisan deity), *hotṛ* (priest who recites the Ṛgveda), *potṛ* (priest who recites the Yajurveda), *bhrātṛ* (brother), *jāmātṛ* (son-in-law), *mātṛ* (mother), *pitṛ* (father), and *duhitṛ* (daughter).

By this [suffix], *naptṛ* (grandson), *pautra* (grandson), and *dauhitra* (daughter’s son) are formed; from the root *nī*, there is the substitution of *ṣu* and the *guṇa* strengthening, resulting in *neṣṭṛ*. From the root *tviṣ*, the vowel *i* is replaced by *at*, resulting in *tvaṣṭṛ*. *Hotṛ* is the name of a priest. *Potṛ* is a specific type of officiating priest (*ṛtvij*). From the root *bhrāj*, there is the elision of *ja*, resulting in *bhrātṛ*. One who measures out the wife is *jāmātṛ*; from the root *mā* in the sense of honoring, there is the elision of *na*. *Mātṛ* is the mother. From the root *pā*, the vowel *ā* is replaced by *i*, resulting in *pitṛ*. From the root *duh* with the suffix *tṛc*, there is the absence of *iṭ* and the absence of *guṇa*, resulting in *duhitṛ*. 261. From the roots *su* and *as*, the suffix *ṛn* is added, resulting in *svasṛ* (sister). 262. From the root *yat*, there is also *vṛddhi* strengthening, resulting in *yātṛ* (mother-in-law).

The wives of one's brothers are called *yātaraḥ* (sisters-in-law) among themselves. (Pāṇini 3.1.134) Regarding the rule *nañi ca nandeḥ*: [the suffix *rak* is applied after the root *nand* when preceded by the negative particle *nañ*]. That which does not rejoice (*na nandati*) is *nanāndā*. Here, the rule for *vṛddhi* (vowel strengthening) does not apply; thus, one [scholar] says *nanāndā*. However, the *Śabdārṇava* states: "The *nanāndā* is the sister of the husband; she is also called *nanandā* and *nandinī*. (Pāṇini 3.1.135) From the root *div*, the suffix *ṛ* is applied: *devāḥ* (husband's brother). [In the dual and plural,] *svāminaḥ devṛ* becomes *devarau* and *devarāḥ*. (Pāṇini 3.1.136) From the root *nī*, the suffix *ḍi* is applied: *nā*, *narau*, *naraḥ*. (Pāṇini 3.1.137) In the Vedic language, the suffix *cha* is applied after the root *sthā* when preceded by *savya*.

Regarding the form *ambāmba*, there is an extension (*upasaṃkhyāna*) of the rule to include the suffixes *stha*, *sthin*, and *sthūṇa*. [Examples: *savyeṣṭhā* (the charioteer); *savyeṣṭharau*; *savyeṣṭharaḥ*. 267. *artisṛdhṛdhamyaśyavitṝbhyo 'niḥ*: The suffix *ani* shall be applied after these eight roots: *ṛ*, *sṛ*, *dhṛ*, *dhmā*, *aś*, *av*, and *tṛ*. [Examples: *araṇiḥ* (the source of fire); *saraṇiḥ*; *dharaṇiḥ*; *dhamaniḥ*; *amanir gatiḥ* (the path of movement); *aśaniḥ*; *avaniḥ*; *taraṇiḥ*. By virtue of the principle of multiplicity (*bāhulakāt*), [we also have] *rajanīḥ*. 268. *āṅi śuṣeḥ sanaś chandasi*: In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *sani* is applied after the root *śuṣ* when preceded by the prefix *āṅ*. [Example: *āśuśukṣaṇiḥ*, referring to Agni or the Wind.

269. After the root *kṛṣ*, there is the substitution of *ca* for the initial consonant. *Carṣaṇiḥ* means "people. 270. After the root *ad*, there is the augment *muṭ*. *Admanir* means "fire. 271. Also after the root *vṛt*. *Vartaniḥ*. Govardhana, however, says that due to the inclusion of the letter *ca* [in the rule], there is the augment *muṭ*, resulting in *vartmanir*. 272. After the root *kṣip*, there is also the suffix *ki*. *Kṣipaṇiḥ* means "weapon. 273. From the roots *arc*, *śuci*, *hu*, *sṛp*, *chad*, and *chardi*, the suffix *isi* is applied. *Arciḥ* means "flame"; this word also ends in *i*. "The flames of fire shine" (*agner bhrājante arcayaḥ*). *Śociḥ* means "light. *Haviḥ* means "clarified butter" (*sarpiḥ*); the vowel is shortened by the rule *isman-*. *Chadiḥ*.

*Paṭala*: [The suffix *ilac* is applied after the root *paṭ*]. *Chardi*: [The word] *chardi* means vomiting or the disease of emesis. [The suffix *ilac* is applied after roots ending in *i*, and it is also applied after *chard*]. Example: *chardy-atīsāra-śūla-vān*. (274) *Bṛṃheḥ* [the suffix *ilac* is applied after the root *bṛṃh*, and there is the elision of the nasal (*n*)]. Example: *barhiḥ* (meaning *kuśa* grass or sacrificial fuel). (275) *Dyuteḥ* [the suffix *isin* is applied after the root *dyut*, and *ja* is substituted for the initial *i*]. Example: *jyotiḥ* (light). (276) *Vasau* [the suffix *isin* is applied after the root *ruc* when forming a proper name]. Example: *vasurociḥ* (the sacrifice). (277) *Bhuvaḥ* [the suffix *isin* is applied after the root *bhū*, and it is *kit*]. Example: *bhuviḥ* (the ocean). (278) *Sahaḥ* [the suffix *isin* is applied after the root *sah*, and *dha* is substituted for the final *h*]. Example: *sidhiḥ* (an ox without a tail). (279) *Pibateḥ* [the suffix *isin* is applied after the root *pā*, and *thuk* is inserted]. Example: *pāthiḥ* (the eye or the ocean). (280) *Janeḥ* [the suffix *usi* is applied after the root *jan*].

*Januḥ* means birth (*jananam*). 281. *Maner dhaś chandasi*: [The suffix] *dha* is applied after the root *man* in the Vedic language; [the form is] *madhuḥ*. 282. *Artipṛvapiyajitanidhanitapibhyo nit*: [The suffix] *u*, with the augment *niṭ*, is applied after the roots *ṛ*, *pṛ*, *vap*, *yaj*, *tan*, *dhana*, and *tap*. [The forms are: *aruḥ* (wound), *paruḥ* (knot), *vapuḥ* (body), *yajuḥ* (sacrificial formula), *tanuḥ* (body). [Dual and plural: *tanuṣī*, *tanūṃṣi*. *Dhanuḥ* (bow) is not feminine. Even if one is of pure lineage (*dhanurvaṃśaviśuddha*), what will he accomplish if he lacks merit (*nirguṇa*)? This is a form ending in either *s* or *u*. *Tapuḥ* refers to the sun, fire, or an enemy. 283. *Eter ṇic ca*: [The suffix] *u* is applied after the root *i*, and the causative marker (*ṇic*) is also added; [the form is] *āyuḥ* (life). [Dual: *āyuṣī*. 284. *Cakṣeḥ śic ca*: [The suffix] *u* is applied after the root *cakṣ*, and the augment *śic* is also added; [the form is] *cakṣuḥ* (eye).

285. *muh-* takes the suffix *kic* [with the augment *u*]. *Muhur* is an indeclinable. It occurs abundantly (*bahulam*) in other instances as well: *ācakṣuḥ*, *paricakṣuḥ*. 286. From the roots *kṝ*, *gṝ*, *śṝ*, *vṛñ*, and *cati*, the suffix *ṣvarac* is applied. *Karvara* refers to a tiger or a demon (*kṣasa*). *Garvara* means one who is arrogant. *Śarvarī* means night. *Varvara* means a common person. *Catvara* means a square or courtyard. 287. After the root *sad-* preceded by *ni-*, [the suffix *ṣvarac* is applied]. *Niṣadvara* means mud. *Niṣadvarī* means night. Thus ends the second quarter in the *Uṇādi* [section].
The third quarter.

288. *chitvara*, *chatvara*, *dhīvara*, *pīvara*, *mīvara*, *cīvara*, *tīvara*, *nīvara*, *gahvara*, *kaṭvara*, and *saṃyadvara*—these eleven [words] ending in the suffix *ṣvarac* are irregularly formed (*nipātita*). In the case of the roots *chidir* (to cut) and *chad* (to cover), there is the substitution of the letter *t* for the final [consonant], and in the case of *chidir*, there is the absence of *guṇa*. *Chitvara*: a rogue. *Chatvara*: a house or a bower. *Dhīvara*: a fisherman. *Pīvara*: stout. *Mīvara*: a killer. In the case of the root *ci* (to gather), there is also lengthening [of the vowel]. *Cīvara*: the robe of a mendicant.

*Tīvara* is a specific type of caste; *nīvara* is a wandering mendicant (*parivrāj*). [The suffix] *vara* is applied after the root *gāh*, with shortening of the vowel, forming *gahvara*. After the root *kaṭ* (meaning "to rain" and so forth), *vara* forms *kaṭvara*, meaning "curd. After the root *yam*, the letter *d* is substituted [for *m*], forming *saṃyadvara*, meaning "king. Some say that after the root *pad*, *vara* forms *saṃpadvara*. 289. From the roots *iṇ*, *siñj*, *dīṅ*, *uṣ*, and *av*, the suffix *na* is applied. *Ina* means "sun," "king," or "lord. *Sina* means "one-eyed. *Jina* means "Arhat. *Dīna* means "miserable. *Uṣṇa* means "hot. *Ūna* means "deficient. 290. *Phena* and *mīna* are irregularly formed (*nipātita*). From the root *sphāy*, *phena* is formed; *mīna* is formed from the root *mī*.

291. After the root *kṛṣ*, [the suffix] *na* is applied in the sense of color (*varṇa*). *kṛṣṇaḥ* ("black"). 292. After the root *bandh*, [the suffix *na* is applied], and there is the substitution of *bradh* or *bdh* for *bandh*. *bradhnaḥ*; *bdhnaḥ*. 293. After the roots *dhā*, *pṛ*, *vas*, *aj*, and *ati*, the suffix *na* is applied. *Dhānāḥ* refers to parched barley grains (feminine plural). *Parṇam* means a leaf; *parṇaḥ* means the *kiṃśuka* tree. *Vasnaḥ* means price or wages. After *aj*, *vī* is substituted: *venaḥ*; here it refers to the Sun (*ādityaḥ*). By virtue of the rule of "abundance" (*bāhulakāt*), from the root *śṛ*, *śroṇaḥ* is formed, meaning a lame person. 294. After the root *lakṣ*, the augment *aṭ* is added. From the root *lakṣ* (belonging to the *curādi* class and ending in the causative marker *ṇi*), the suffix *na* is applied, and there is the augment *aṭ*. Some say that by the word "and" (*ca*) in the rule, the augment *muṭ* is also included.

*Lakṣaṇa* and *lakṣmaṇa* are used in the senses of "mark" and "sign. *Lakṣṇa* and *lakṣmaṇa* refer to Rāma’s brother. *Lakṣā* refers to the female swan (*haṃsayoṣā*) and the female crane (*sārasa*). 295. From the root *van*, the suffix *na* is added, and the penultimate vowel is replaced by *i*. *Vennā* is the name of a river. 296. From the roots *siv* and *ṣṭhā*, the suffix *yū* is added. Due to the force of the long vowel pronunciation, there is no *guṇa* substitution. *Syūna* means the sun. By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), the suffix *na* alone is also applied. [The *u* of *ṣṭhā* becomes] *ūṭh*; because it is an internal operation (*antaraṅga*), *yaṇ* replacement occurs first, then *guṇa*. Thus, *syona*. 297. From the roots *kṝ*, *vṝ*, *jṝ*, *sidru*, *pani*, *ani*, and *svapi*, the suffix *na* is added as a *nit* (causing *vṛddhi*). *Karṇaḥ* (ear). *Varṇaḥ* (color).

From the root *jṛ*, the suffix *na* is applied to form *jarṇa*, meaning "the moon" and "a tree. From *si*, *senā* ("army"); from *dru*, *droṇa* ("a wooden vessel"). From *pad*, *panna* ("lowly movement"). From *ad*, *anna* ("cooked rice"). From *svap*, *svapna* ("sleep"). 298. From the root *dhēṭ*, the suffix *na* is applied and the vowel is replaced by *i*; thus, *dhenaḥ* means "ocean," and *dhenā* means "river. 299. From the roots *tṛṣ*, *śuṣ*, and *ras*, the suffix *na* is applied as a *kit* (causing guṇa/vṛddhi substitution); thus, *tṛṣṇā* ("thirst"); *śuṣṇaḥ* means "the sun" and "fire"; *rasnaṃ* means "substance. 300. From the root *sū*, the suffix *na* is applied and the vowel is lengthened; thus, *sūnā* means "place of slaughter. 301. From the root *ram*, the suffix *na* is applied and the final syllable is replaced by *ta*; thus, that which causes delight is *ratnam* ("jewel"). 302. [The following are formed with the suffix *na*: *rāsnā*, *sāsnā*, *sthūṇā*, and *vīṇā*. *Rāsnā* is a fragrant substance.

*Sāsnā* means the dewlap of a cow; *sthūṇā* means a house-pillar; *vīṇā* means a lute (*vallakī*). 303. With the suffix *iṣṇuc* after the roots *gā* and *dā*: *goṣṇuḥ* means a singer; *deṣṇuḥ* means a giver. 304. With the suffix *ksna* after the roots *kṛt* and *aś*: *kṛtsnam*; *akṣṇam* means unbroken. 305. After the root *tij*, there is lengthening [of the vowel]: *tīkṣṇam*. 306. After the root *śliṣ*, the penultimate vowel is replaced by *a*: *ślakṣṇam*. 307. With the suffix *yuc* after the roots *yaj*, *man*, *śundh*, *das*, and *jan*: *yajyuḥ* means an Adhvaryu priest; *manyuḥ* means dejection, a sacrifice, or anger; *śundhyuḥ* means fire.

*dasyu* means a thief; *janya* means a corporeal being (one possessing a body). 308. From the roots *bhuj* and *mṛ*, the suffixes *yu* and *yuk* [are applied]. *Bhujyu* means a vessel; *mṛtyu* means death. 309. From the root *sṛ*, the suffix *ayu* [is applied]. *Sarayu* is a river. There is an alternative reading, *ayūḥ*; [from this] *sarayūḥ*. 310. From the roots *pā*, *nī*, and *viṣ*, the suffix *pa* [is applied].
