Because one protects (*pāti*) oneself from it, it is *pāpa* (evil); through connection with that, one is *pāpa* (sinful). *Nepa* is a domestic priest (*purohita*). By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), through the substitution of *guṇa*, in the sense of "state" (*bhāva*), *nīpa* is a specific type of tree. *Veṣpa* means water. 311. From the root *cyu*, [the suffix *pa* is applied] and it is also *kit*. *Cyupa* means the mouth.

312. From the roots *stu* and *dṛ*, the suffix *apa* is added, and [the vowel] is lengthened. Thus, *stūpaḥ* means "an elevation" or "a stupa. 313. After the prefixes *su-* and *suṣ-* (as well as *su-*), the suffix *apa* is added, and it is marked with the *k*-diacritic (*kit*). Thus, *sūpaḥ* ("soup"). By virtue of the rule of multiplicity (*bāhulaka*), there is the substitution of *ū* for the vowel; thus, *śūrpam* ("winnowing basket"). 314. Also after the roots *ku* and *yu*, [the suffix *apa* is added]. Because frogs (*maṇḍūkāḥ*) move about (*kurvanti*) in it, it is called *kūpaḥ* ("well"). Because they bind (*yuvanti*) or tether the sacrificial animal (*paśum*) in it, it is called *yūpaḥ*, the sacrificial post. 315. The seven words *khaṣaḥ*, *aśilaḥ*, *śilpaḥ*, *śaṣpam*, *bāṣpaḥ*, *rūpam*, and *talpaḥ* are irregularly formed (*nipātyante*) by taking the suffix *apa*. In the case of the root *khan* ("to dig"), the *n* is changed to *ṣ*. [Thus, *khaṣaḥ* "a mountain"]. [The others are formed accordingly.]

*Khaṣpa* and *kāra* are derived from the root *kṣai* (to waste) with the suffix *auṇādika* *au*, [the vowel] being shortened by the rule of *śīli*. *Śilpa* means skill or craft. From the root *śas* (to injure), the change to *ṣ* occurs by irregular derivation (*nipātana*); *śāṣpa* refers to young grass and the loss of creative intuition (*pratibhākṣaya*). From the root *bādh* (to oppress), the change to *ṣ* occurs; *bāṣpa* refers to tears and the heat of steam. *Bāṣpa* also [means this]. From the root *ru* (to cry out), the vowel is lengthened; *rūpa* refers to essential nature and beauty. From the root *pṝ* (to fill), *parpa* means a house, young grass, and a stool for the lame. In the sense of "establishing a base" (*talapratiṣṭhākaraṇa*), the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is elided; *talpa* refers to a bed, a platform, and a wife.

316. After the roots *stan*, *hṛṣ*, *puṣ*, *gad*, and *mad*, the suffix *ṇi* takes the augment *itnuc*. By the rule *ay-āmanta-*, the substitution of *ay* for *ṇi* occurs. Thus: *stanayitnuḥ* (thunder), *harṣayitnuḥ* (one who causes joy), *poṣayitnuḥ* (one who nourishes), *gadayitnuḥ* (one who speaks much), and *madayitnuḥ* (intoxicating liquor). 317. After the roots *kṛ* and *han*, the suffix *ktnu* is added. *Kṛtnuḥ* means an artisan; *hatnuḥ* means disease or a weapon. 318. After the root *gam*, the suffix *ktnu* is added, and it is treated as if it were *san* (causative). Thus: *jigatnuḥ* (one who goes repeatedly). 319. After the roots *dā* and *bhā*, the suffix *nu* is added. *Dānuḥ* means a giver; *bhānuḥ* means light or the sun. 320. After the root *vac*, the suffix *nu* is added, and *ga* is substituted for *va*. Thus: *vagnuḥ* (a speaker). 321. After the root *dhēṭ*, the suffix *nu* is added, and *i* is substituted for *dhā*. Thus: *dhenuḥ* (a cow).

A *dhenu* is so called because she "suckles" (*dhayati*) her offspring. (322) With the suffix *kit*, [from the root *sū*] we have *sūnuḥ*; it means son, younger brother, and the sun. (323) From the root *jahāti*, there is the suffix *u* and the elision of the final vowel; thus, *jahnuḥ*. (324) From the root *sthā*, the suffix *ṇu* [is added]; *sthāṇuḥ* means a peg, something stable, and Śiva. (325) From the roots *aj*, *vṛ*, and *rī*, the suffix *niC* [is added]. From *aj*, [the prefix] *vi-* is added; thus, *veṇuḥ*. *Varṇuḥ* refers to a type of river and a specific region. *Reṇuḥ* is masculine-feminine dual; as a feminine noun, it means dust. (326) From the root *viṣ*, the suffix *kic* is added; thus, *viṣṇuḥ*. (327) From the roots *kṛ*, *ādhṛ*, *aci*, and *kali*, the suffix *ka* is added. Due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), the suffix *ka* does not receive the technical designation *it*.

*Karka* means a white horse; *dāka* means a giver; *dhāka* means a bull and a support; *rākā* means the full moon day; *arka* [means the sun]; *alka* means a wicked person, sin, deceit, and also excrement. (328) From the roots *sṛ*, *vṛ*, *bhū*, *śuṣ*, and *muṣ*, the suffix *kak* is applied. *Sṛk* means a blue lotus and wind; *vṛka* means a beast of prey and a crow; *bhūka* means a hole; *śuṣka* [is formed from *śuṣ*]; *muṣka* means a testicle. (329) *Śuka*, *valka*, and *ulkā* [are formed as follows]: from the root *śubh*, there is elision of the final letter, resulting in *śuka*; *valka* means bark or rind, used in both genders; from the root *uṣ* meaning "to burn," the *ṣ* is changed to *l*, [resulting in *ulka*].

*Ulkā* (a meteor). 330. From the roots *iṇ*, *bhī*, *kṛ*, *pā*, *śal*, *at*, *mṛc*, and *arc*, the suffix *kan* is applied. *Eka* means "principal," "one," or "exclusive. According to the *Viśva* and *Medinī* lexicons, *bheka* refers to a frog or a ram. *Kāka* (a crow). *Pāka* means a child. *Śalka* means a splinter. *Atka* means a traveler or a limb of the body. *Marka* means the vital air of the body. 331. After the root *hā* (to abandon), the suffix *kan* is applied when preceded by *nau*. Thus, *nihākā* means a lizard. 332. When *sad* (to sit) is preceded by *nau*, the suffix *kan* is applied and the root vowel receives the *ḍit* designation. *Niṣka* (neuter) means gold or a specific weight of gold. 333. After the root *syam* (to sound), the suffix *kan* is applied and the augment *īṭ* is added.

*Syamīka* refers to an anthill and a species of tree. According to some, there is a short vowel before the suffix *iṭ*, resulting in *syamika*. From the roots *aji*, *yudh*, and *nī*, the suffix *vīka* is added, and the vowel is lengthened: *vīka* means a wind or a bird; *yūkā* (a louse); *dhūka* (the wind); *nīka* (a specific type of tree). From the root *hrī*, the suffix *ra* is added, and the letter *l* optionally replaces it: *hrīkā* or *hlīkā* is considered to mean shame. From the root *śak*, the four suffixes *una*, *unta*, *unti*, and *uni* are added: *śakunaḥ*, *śakuntaḥ*, *śakuntiḥ*, and *śakuniḥ* (all meaning "bird"). The suffix *jhi* is added to the root *bhū*.

The suffix *bhanti* forms the word *bhavanti*, meaning "the present time," by virtue of the rule of abundance (*bāhulaka*) and the substitution of *ava* for *bhū*. From the root *av*, we have *avanti*; from *vad*, *vadanti*. *Kiṃvadantī* means "rumor" or "public report. 338. After the roots *kṣip* and *bhū*, the suffix *anyuc* is added; by the force of "and" (*ca*), it is also added after *bhū*. Ujjvaladatta states that *kṣipaṇyu* means "spring" (*vasanta*). *Bhavanyu* denotes both "master" (*svāmin*) and "sun" (*sūrya*). 3339. After the roots *nad* and *kṣip*, the suffix *anuṅ* is added; by the force of "and" (*ca*), it is also added after *kṣip*. *Nadanu* means "cloud"; *kṣipaṇu* means "wind. 340. After the roots *kṛ*, *vṛ*, and *dāri*, the suffix *unan* is added. *Karuṇa* may denote a particular kind of tree, while *karuṇā* is considered to mean "compassion. [From *vṛ*] we have *varuṇa*.

*dāruṇam* (341). After the root *tṛ*, *ra* is optionally substituted for *la*: *taruṇaḥ*, *talunaḥ* (both meaning "young"). (342) After the roots *kṣudh*, *piś*, and *mith*, [the suffix *una*] is added as a *kit*: *kṣudhunaḥ* (a type of barbarian), *piśunaḥ* (an informer), *mithunam* (a pair). (343) After the root *phal*, *guk* is added: *phalgunaḥ* (Pārtha). With the suffix *aṇ* [from the *prajñādi* group], it is *phālgunaḥ*. (344) After the root *aś*, *laśa* is added: *laśunam* (garlic). (345) After the root *arj*, the *ṇi* is elided: *arjunaḥ*. (346) When designating a kind of grass, [the suffix *una*] is added with the *cit* marker; because of the *cit* marker, it is udātta on the final syllable: *arjunam* (a type of grass). (347) Also after the root *ṛ*: *aruṇaḥ* (reddish-brown).

348. From the roots *aj*, *mi*, *śīṅ*, and others, [the suffix *sa* is applied]: *vayunaṃ* (wisdom), *devamandiraṃ* (temple), *yamunā* (the river Yamunā); from *śyai*, *śayunaḥ* (a python). 349. From the roots *vṛ*, *tṛ*, *vad*, *han*, *kam*, *kaś*, and others, [the suffix *sa* is applied]: *varṣaḥ* (rain), *tarsaḥ* (thirst), *plava-samudrayoḥ* (in the sense of a boat and the ocean); *vatsaḥ* (a calf), *vatsam* (a calf); *vakṣaḥ* (the breast); *haṃsaḥ* (a swan); *kaṃsaḥ* (a drinking vessel, not feminine); *kakṣaṃ* (a constellation). 350. From the root *pluṣ*, [the suffix *sa* is applied] and the penultimate vowel is replaced by *a*: *plakṣaḥ* (the Plakṣa tree). 351. From the root *man*, [the suffix *sa* is applied] and there is lengthening [of the vowel]: *māṃsam* (flesh). 352. From the root *aś*, [the suffix *sa* is applied] with the substitution of *da* for the root-initial: *akṣaḥ* (an axle, a die).

353. After the roots *snu*, *vṛśc*, *kṛt*, and *ṛṣi*, [the suffix] *kit* is added. *Snuṣā* (daughter-in-law); *vṛkṣaḥ* (tree); *kutsam* (water); *ṛkṣam* (constellation). 354. After *ṛṣi* when denoting a genus (*jāti*). *Ṛkṣaḥ* is used for a type of rock and for a bear. 355. Also after the roots *und*, *guth*, and *kuṣ*. *Utsaḥ* (spring, fountain); *gutsaḥ* (cluster of blossoms); *ukṣaḥ* (belly). 356. After *gṛdh* and *paṇi*, *dak* is also [the suffix]. *Gutsaḥ* (Kāmadeva); *pakṣaḥ* (wing, side). 357. After *aś*, *sara* is [the suffix]. *Akṣaram* (syllable). 358. And after *vas*, [the suffix is *sara*]. *Vatsaraḥ* (year). 359. When preceded by *sa*, it is marked with the *cit* accent.

*Saṃvatsaraḥ*. [The suffix] *kit* is added after the roots *kṛ*, *dhū*, and *adhi*; due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), there is no *ṣatva* change. *Kṛsaraḥ* refers to rice mixed with sesame. *Dhūsaraḥ*. *Matsaraḥ*. It should be known that *matsarā* is a fly, and it is also considered to be a cricket (*bhambharālī*). 361. After these [roots], the suffix *ra* is replaced by *la*. *Patsalaḥ* means a path. 362. After the roots *tan* and *ṛṣi*, the suffix *ksaran* is added. *Tasaraḥ* refers to a shuttle for winding thread. *Ṛkṣaraḥ* refers to a priest (*ṛtvij*). 363. After the roots *pīyū* and *kvaṇi*, the suffix *kālan* is added; there is shortening of the vowel and vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). *Pīyū* is a root found in the *sūtra* (Vedic grammar).

*Piyāla* is a species of tree; *kuṇāla* is a region. 364. From the roots *kaṭi* and *kuṣ*, [the suffix] *kāku* is added. *Kaṭāku* is a bird; *kuṣāku* is fire and the sun. 365. From the root *sṛ*, [the suffix] *dāku* is added, and there is the substitution of *du*. *Sṛdāku* refers to wind and a river. 366. From the root *vṛt*, there is also [the substitution of] *vṛddhi*. *Vārtāku*. By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), the vowel *u* becomes *a*: *dhārtāka*. 367. From the root *pard*, [the suffix] *dāku* is added as a *nit* (causing *vṛddhi*), with *saṃprasāraṇa* and the elision of the penultimate vowel (*al-lopa*). *Pṛdāku* refers to a scorpion, a tiger, a leopard, and a reptile. 368. From the roots *sṛ*, *yu*, and *vac*, the suffixes *anyuc*, *āgūc*, and *ajnak* are added respectively.

The suffix *ān* (forming *anyu*, *āgu*, and *aknu*) occurs respectively after these roots: *sṛ* [in the sense of] *saraṇyu* (a cloud or wind), *yavāgu* (gruel), and *vacaknu* (a wise man or an archer). 369. After the roots *śīṅ* and *bhī*, the suffix *ānaka* is added: *śayānaka* (a python) and *bhayānaka* (terrible). 370. After the roots *lu*, *dhu*, *śighi*, and *dhāñ*, the suffix *āṇaka* is added: *lavāṇaka* (a sickle), *dhavānaka* (wind), and *śiṅghāṇaka* (phlegm); in the latter case, the elision of *k* occurs optionally because it belongs to the *pṛṣodarādi* class; *śiṅghāṇa* (nasal mucus), and *dhāṇaka* (a portion of a dīnāra coin). 371. It is also used after the roots *ulmuka* (a firebrand), *darvi* (a ladle), and *homin* (one who performs oblations).

From the root *uṣ* (to burn), with *la* substituted for *ṣ* and the suffix *muk*, we have *ulmukaṃ* (a glowing coal). From *dṛ* (to split), the suffix *vi*: *darviḥ* (a ladle). From *hu* (to sacrifice), the suffix *mini*: *homī* (one who sacrifices). 372. After the root *hrī* (to be ashamed), the suffix *kuk* is added, and *ra* optionally replaces *l*. Thus, *hākuḥ* (shame) and *hrīkuḥ* (one who is modest). 373. From the ten roots *has*, *mṛ*, *gṛ*, *ṇī*, *vā*, *mi*, *dam*, *lū*, *pū*, and *dhurv*, the suffix *tan* is added. The suffix *tan* occurs after these ten. By the rule *ti-tu-tra-*, there is no *iṭ* augment. *hastaḥ* (hand), *martaḥ* (mortal), *gartaḥ* (pit), *etaḥ* (a goat), *kurvaraḥ* (a type of grass), *vātaḥ* (wind), *dantaḥ* (tooth), *antaḥ* (end). *Lotaḥ* is used in the sense of impurity and a mark.

From *pu* and *tṛ*, the suffix *u* is added; *pūtaḥ* means "purified" or "carried by a child. From *dhurv*, the suffix *ta* is added; *dhūrtaḥ* means "rogue. By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), however, there is lengthening of the vowel before the suffix *si*; *tūstam* means "evil," and *dhūliḥ* means "dust" or "matted hair. 374. After the roots *āp* and *nañ*, the augment *iṭ* is added; *nāpitaḥ* means "barber. 375. After the roots *tan* and *mṛ*, the suffix *kic* is added; *tatam* and *mṛtam*. 376. After the roots *añj*, *ghṛ*, and *si*, the suffix *kta* is added; *aktam*, *ghṛtam*, and *sitam*. 377. After the roots *du* and *tan*, the suffix *ta* is added and the vowel is lengthened; *dūtaḥ* and *tātaḥ*. 378. After the root *ji*, the augment *muṭ* is added, which is udātta-accented; *jīmūtaḥ* ("cloud"). 379. *Loṣṭaḥ* ("clod") and *palitaḥ* ("grey-haired") [are formed with the suffix *ta*].

The suffix *kta* is added to the root *lunāti*; for that [root], there is the augment *suṭ* and *guṇa* of the root [applies]: *loṣṭam* (a clod) and *palitam* (grey hair). 380. From the roots *hṛ* and *śyā*, the suffix *itan* is added: *harita* and *śyeta* are two distinct colors. 381. After the root *ruh*, the letter *r* is optionally changed to *l*: *rohita* refers to a deer or a fish; *lohita* means red. 382. After the root *piś*, the suffix *ki* is added and it is also *kit*: *piśitam* means flesh. 383. After the roots *śru*, *dakṣ*, *spṛh*, and *gṛh*, the suffix *āyya* is added: *śravāyya* is a sacrificial animal; *dakṣāyya* is Garuḍa and a vulture; *spṛhayāyya*; *gṛhayāyya* is the master of a house. 384. *didhiṣāyya*.

From the root *dhā*, there is reduplication, the substitution of *i* for the radical vowel, and the suffix *ṣuk*: *didhiṣāyyaḥ*, meaning "one who is to be cherished like a friend. 385. From the root *vṛ*, the suffix *eṇya*: *vareṇyaḥ* ("to be chosen" or "excellent"). 386. From the root *stu*, the suffix *kṣeyya* occurs in the Vedic language (*chandas*): *stuṣeyyaṃ puruvarpasam* ("I shall praise the one of many forms"). 387. From the root *rāj*, the suffix *anya*: *rājanyo vahniḥ* ("the royal fire-priest"). 388. Also from the roots *śṝ* and *ram*, [the suffix *anya*]: *śaraṇyam* ("a refuge") and *ramaṇyam* ("delightful"). 389. From the root *ṛ*, with the substitution of *ni* for the radical vowel: *araṇyam* ("a forest"). 390. *Parjanyaḥ*. From the root *pṛṣu* (meaning "to sprinkle"), the radical *ṣ* is replaced by *j*: *parjanyaḥ*, which denotes both Indra and the rain-cloud. 391. From the root *vad*, the suffix *ānya*: *vādānyaḥ* ("generous" or "munificent").

The suffix *atran* is added after the roots *vad*, *dānī*, *styai*, *vac*, and *minakṣiyajivadhipati*. *Amatraṃ* means a vessel; *nakṣatram* (a star); *yajatraḥ* (one worthy of sacrifice); *vadhatram* (a weapon); and *patatram* (a feather). After the root *gaḍi*, the initial [of the root] is replaced by *ka*. *Kaḍatram*; because of the traditional rule regarding the identity of *ḍa* and *la*, it is also *kalatram*. After the root *vṛñ*, the suffix is *atran* with the *cit* marker. *Varatrā* is a leather thong. After the root *suvid*, the suffix *katra* is added. *Suvidatram* is a family. After the root *kṛt*, there is also the insertion of *num*. *Kṛntatram* is a plough.

397. The suffix *atac* occurs after ten roots: *bhṛ*, *mṛ*, *dṛś*, *yaj*, *parv*, *pac*, *am*, *tam*, *nam*, and *hary*. [The following forms] occur with *atac*: *bharataḥ* (a supporter); *marataḥ* (death); *darśataḥ* (referring to the moon or the sun); *yajataḥ* (a priest); *parvataḥ* (a mountain); *pacataḥ* (fire); *amataḥ* (disease); *tamataḥ* (thirst); *namataḥ* (one who bows); *haryataḥ* (a horse). 398. The suffix *kit atac* occurs after the roots *pṛṣ* and *rañj*. *Pṛṣataḥ* means a deer or a drop; *rajatam* means silver. 399. [The word] *khalatiḥ* [is formed with this suffix].

There is the elision of the *s* of *khalati*, and there is the substitution of *i* for the final vowel of that which ends in the suffix *atac*. *Khalati* means one whose head is hairless. (Uṇādi Sūtra 400) The suffix *atha* occurs after the seven roots *śīṅ*, *śapi*, *ru*, *gam*, *i*, *vañci*, *jīvi*, and *prāṇi*. After these seven, the suffix *atha* is applied. *Śayatha* is a python (*ajagara*). *Śapatha* is an oath. *Ravatha* is a cuckoo (*kokila*). *Gamatha* is a traveler and also a path (*panthā*). *Vañcatha* is a rogue (*dhūrta*). If the reading is *vandī*, then from the sense "he is praised" (*vandyate*), *vandatha* means both a singer of praise (*stotā*) and one worthy of praise (*stutya*). *Jīvatha* is long-lived (*āyuṣmān*). *Prāṇatha* is strong (*balavān*).

By virtue of the rule of general applicability (*bāhulaka*), [the suffix *tha*] is added after the roots *śam* and *dam*. Thus: *śamatha* is *śama*, *śānti*; *dānti* is *damatha*, *dama*. (401) After the root *bhṛ*, [the suffix *tha*] has the augment *cit*: *bharatha* is a world-protector (*lokapāla*). (402) After the roots *rud* and *vid*, [the suffix *tha*] is marked with *ṅit*. That which weeps is *rudathaḥ*; [this refers to] a child (*śiśuḥ*). That which knows is *vidathaḥ*. (403) After the root *vas* when preceded by a prefix (*upasarga*): *āvasatha* is a house; *saṃvasatha* is a village. (404) After the thirteen roots—*at*, *av*, *ci*, *mi*, *tam*, *ram*, *labh*, *nabh*, *tap*, *pat*, *pan*, *paṇ*, and *mah*—the suffix *asac* occurs. The suffix *asac* shall apply after these thirteen.

*Atasa* means "he extends," referring to the wind and the self (*ātman*). *Atasa* also means "he protects," referring to a king and the sun (*bhānu*). *Camasa* is a vessel for drinking soma; it is so called because "one sips" (*camati*) within it. *Tamasa* is darkness, so called because "one is distressed" (*tāmyati*) within it. *Namasa* means favorable. *Rabhasa* refers to speed and joy. *Labhasa* refers to wealth and a beggar. *Nabhasa* is the sky, derived from *nabhati* or *nabhyati*. *Tapasa* refers to a bird and the moon. *Pataṣa* refers to a bird. *Panasa* is the jackfruit tree (*kaṇṭakiphala*). *Paṇasa* refers to merchandise. *Mahasam* refers to knowledge.

405. From the root *veñ*, the suffix *tuṭ* is added; by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), there is no substitution of *ā*. Thus, *vetasaḥ* (the rattan cane). 406. From the roots *vah* and *yu*, the suffix *ṇit* is added. *Vāhasaḥ* means a python; *yāvasaḥ* means a heap of grass. 407. And from the root *vaya* (in the sense of "going"). *Vāyasaḥ* means a crow. 408. From the root *div*, the suffix is *kit*. *Divasam* or *divasaḥ* (day). 409. From the roots *kṝ*, *śṝ*, *śal*, *kali*, and *gard*, the suffix *abhac* is added. *Karabhaḥ* (a young elephant); *śarabhaḥ* (a kind of deer); *śalabhaḥ* (a locust); *kalabhaḥ* (a young elephant); *gardabhaḥ* (a donkey). 410. From the roots *ṛṣi* and *vṛṣi*, the suffix is *kit*. *Ṛṣabhaḥ* (a bull); *vṛṣabhaḥ* (a bull). 411. From the root *ruṣ*, the suffix is added and *ni* is substituted for *lu*. [Thus, *roṣabhaḥ*].

The root *ruṣ* means "to injure. From this root, the suffix *abhac* with the augment *nit* occurs, and there is a substitution of *luṣ*. *Luṣabha* refers to an elephant in rut. 412. Also from the roots *rās* and *vall*: *rāsabhaḥ* (donkey); *vallabhaḥ* (beloved). 413. From the roots *jṝ* and *viś*, the suffix *jhac* occurs: *jarantaḥ* (an old buffalo); *veśantaḥ* (a pond). 414. From the roots *ruh*, *nandi*, *jīv*, and *prāṇ*, the suffix *ṣid* occurs when expressing a blessing (*āśis*). *Rohantaḥ* is a type of tree; *nandantaḥ* is a son; *jīvantaḥ* is a medicinal herb; *prāṇantaḥ* is wind. Because of the marker *ṣit*, the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied: *rohantī*.

415. After the ten roots *tṛ*, *bhū*, *vah*, *vas*, *bhās*, *sādh*, *gaḍi*, *maṇḍi*, and *jani*, the suffix *jhac* is applied, and it is marked with the *ṣit* designation. *tarantaḥ* (the ocean), *tarantī* (a boat); *bhavantaḥ* (time); *vahantaḥ* (wind); *vasantaḥ* (the season); *bhāsantaḥ* (the sun); *sādhantaḥ* (a monk). Regarding *gaḍi*: because it belongs to the *ghaṭādi* group, it takes the *mit* designation, resulting in a short vowel. By the rule *ayāmanta-*, the *ṇi* is replaced by *aya*. Thus: *gaṇḍayantaḥ* (a cloud); *maṇḍayantaḥ* (an ornament); *jayantaḥ* (the son of Śakra).

The suffix *na* is added after the root *nand*, and the form is *nandaka* (one who causes joy). 416. After the root *han*, the suffix *muṭ* is added and the root-final *h* is replaced by *gh*; thus, *hemantaḥ* (winter). 417. After the root *bhand*, there is elision of the nasal (*n*); thus, *bhadantaḥ* (a renunciant). 418. After the root *ṛcch*, the suffix *ara* is added; thus, *ṛccharā* (a prostitute). By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), forms such as *jarjara* (worn out) and *jharjhara* (a type of musical instrument) are derived. 419. After the six roots *ṛ*, *kam*, *bhram*, *cam*, *di*, and *vās*, the suffix *ara* is added with the augment *cit*. Thus, from these six, *ara* occurs with the *cit* augment: *araram* (a door-panel), *kamaraḥ* (a lustful man), *bhramaraḥ* (a bee), *camaraḥ* (a yak), *devaraḥ* (a husband's brother), and *vāsaraḥ* (a day). 420. After the root *ku*, the suffix *kraran* is added.

*Kurara* is a species of bird. (Uṇādi Sūtra 421) From the roots *aṅg*, *mad*, and *mand*, the suffix *āran* is added: *aṅgāraḥ* (coal), *madāraḥ* (boar), *mandāraḥ* (the Mandāra tree). (Uṇādi Sūtra 422) From the root *gaḍ*, *kaḍa* is substituted [for the root]: *kaḍāraḥ* (tawny). (Uṇādi Sūtra 423) *Śṛṅgāra* and *bhṛṅgāra*: from the roots *śṝ* and *bhṛñ*, the suffix *āran* is added, with the augment *num*, the *guk* augment, and a short vowel [for the penultimate]. *Śṛṅgāraḥ* is an aesthetic sentiment (*rasa*); *bhṛṅgāraḥ* is a golden water-pot. (Uṇādi Sūtra 424) From the roots *kañj* and *mṛj*, the suffix *cit* is added. *Kañj* is a Vedic (sautra) root. *Kañjāraḥ* is a peacock; *mārjāraḥ* is a cat. (Uṇādi Sūtra 425) From the root *kam*, the suffix *kit* is added, and the penultimate vowel is changed to *u*.

The word *cit* is udātta on the final syllable due to its recurrence [in the rule]. *Kumāraḥ*. 426. *Tuṣāra-* and others: *tuṣāraḥ* (frost), *kāsāraḥ* (a lake), *sahāraḥ* (a variety of mango). 427. From the root *dīṅ*, there is the augment *nuṭ*: *dīnāraḥ* (a gold ornament). 428. From the root *sṛ*, with the suffix *ap* and the augment *ṣuk*: *sarṣapaḥ* (mustard seed). 429. From the roots *uṣi*, *kuṭi*, *dali*, *kaci*, and *khaji*, the suffix *kapan* is applied: *uṣapaḥ* (fire or the sun); *kuṭapaḥ* (a measure-vessel); *dalapaḥ* (a weapon); *kacapaṃ* (a leaf of vegetables); *khajapaṃ* (clarified butter).

430. After the root *kvaṇ*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). [The word is] *kuṇapa*. 431. And according to Ākravarmaṇa, there is also the suffix *kapa*. There is a difference in accent. 432. *viṭapa*, *piṣṭapa*, *viśipa*, and *ulapa*: these four end in the suffix *kapan*. [The root] *viṭ* means "to sound. *Viṭapa* (branch); [from] *viśati*, the initial [vowel] becomes *pa*; the suffix has the augment *tuṭ*; [the *s*] becomes *ṣ*. *Piṣṭapa* is the world; [from] *viśati*, the initial [vowel] of the suffix becomes *i*. *Viśipa* is a palace. 433. From the root *val*, there is vocalization. *Ulapa* is tender grass. 434. From the root *vṛt*, the suffix *tikana* [is added].

435. The suffix *vartikā* is added after the roots *kṛ*, *bhid*, and *dilati*, with the augment *kit*. From *kṛ*: *kṛttikā*; from *bhid*: *bhittikā* (which is synonymous with *bhitti*, "a wall"); *lattikā* means "a lizard. 436. The suffix *takan* is added after the roots *iṣ* and *aś*. *iṣṭakā* ("brick"); *aṣṭakā* ("the eighth day of the lunar fortnight"). 437. The suffixes *taśan* and *taśasun* are added after the root *iṇ*. *etaśaḥ* means "a Brāhmaṇa"; the same word [with the suffix *taśasun*] is *etaśāḥ*. 438. The suffix *tan* is added after the roots *vī* and *pat*. *Vī* is used in the sense of "motion" and so forth. *Vetanam* ("wages"); *pattanam* ("a city"). 439. The suffix *bha* is added after the roots *dṝ* and *dal*. *Darbhaḥ* ("the sacred grass *darbha*"); *dalbhaḥ* may mean either "a sage" or "a wheel. 440. The suffix *bhan* is added after the roots *ṛ* and *gṝ*. *Arbhaḥ* ("small"); *garbhaḥ* ("womb," "embryo").

441. From the root *iṇ*, with the suffix *kit*: *ibhaḥ* (an elephant). 442. From the roots *as* and *sañj*, with the suffix *kthin*: *asthi* (bone) and *sakthi* (thigh). 443. From the roots *pluṣ*, *kuṣ*, and *śuṣ*, with the suffix *ksi*: *plukṣiḥ* (fire), *kukṣiḥ* (belly), and *śukṣiḥ* (wind). 444. From the root *aś*, with the suffix *ksi* which is *nit*: *akṣi* (eye). 445. From the root *iṣ*, with the suffix *ksu*: *ikṣuḥ* (sugarcane). 446. From the roots *av*, *tṛ*, *stṛ*, and *tantr*, with the suffix *ī*: *avīḥ* (a woman in her menses), *tarīḥ* (a boat), *starīḥ* (smoke), and *tantrīḥ* (the string of a lute, etc.). 447. From the roots *yā* and *pā*, with the suffix *ī*, there is the substitution of *ke* for the root vowel and reduplication: *yayīḥ* (a horse); *papīḥ* may denote both the moon and the sun.
The suffix *muṭ* is added after the root *lakṣ*. [Thus] *lakṣmīḥ*. Thus ends the third quarter of the *Uṇādi* [sūtras].
Now begins the fourth quarter.

449. *vātapramīḥ*: When the word *vāta* is used as an *upapada*, the suffix *ī* is added to the root *mā*, and it is *kit*. Thus, *vātapramīḥ*. This [term] applies to both feminine and masculine. 450. From the twelve roots *ṛ*, *tan*, *añj*, *vi-añj*, *añj*, *ṛṣ*, *mad*, *yat*, *aṅg*, *ku*, *yu*, and *kṛś*, there arise respectively the suffixes *katnic*, *yatuc*, *jalic*, *jiṣṭhuc*, *isan*, *yan*, *thinic*, *ul*, *yas*, *ās*, and *ānuk*. From the root *ṛ* with the suffix *katnic*, *yaṇ* [substitution occurs]: *aratniḥ*. A hand with the fist clenched is an *aratni*; that same hand with the fingers extended is an *aratni*. From the root *tan* with the suffix *yatuc*: *tanyatuḥ*, meaning wind or night.

From *añj* (to anoint), *alic* [is added], forming *añjaliḥ* (a joined palm). From *van* (to desire), *iṣṭuc* [is added], forming *vaniṣṭu*, meaning "the thick intestine. From *añj*, *iṣṭuc* [is added], forming *añjiṣṭhaḥ*, meaning "the sun. From *arpayati* (to fix), *isan* [is added], forming *arpisaḥ*, meaning "the prime meat. From *mad* (to rejoice), *syan* [is added], forming *matsyaḥ* (fish). From *at* (to go), *ithin* [is added], forming *atithiḥ* (guest). From *aṅg* (to move), *uli* [is added], forming *aṅguliḥ* (finger/toe). From *kaut* (to shine), *asa* [is added], forming *kavasaḥ*. Some say that after *ac* [the suffix *asa* is added], forming *kavacam* (armor). From *yu* (to join), *āsa* [is added], forming *yavāsaḥ*, meaning "durālabhā" (a medicinal plant). From *kṛś* (to become thin), *ānuk* [is added], forming *kṛśānuḥ*. 451. From *śrā* (to cook), *karan* [is added].

In the subsequent sūtra, because of the inclusion of *kiṭ*, the letter *ka* here does not take the augment *it*. *Śarkarā*. (452) *puṣaḥ kit*: [The suffix] *ara* after the root *puṣ* is *kit*. *Puṣkaram*. (453) *kalaś ca*: [The suffix] *ala* also [is added]. *Puṣkalam*. (454) *gameḥ iniḥ*: The suffix *ini* after the root *gam*. One who will go is a *gamī*. (455) *āṅi ṇit*: [The suffix *ini* after *gam*] is *ṇit* when preceded by *āṅ*. An approaching person is an *āgāmī*. (456) *bhuvaś ca*: [The suffix *ini*] also after the root *bhū*. One who will be is a *bhāvī*. (457) *pre sthaḥ*: [The suffix *ini*] after the root *sthā* preceded by *pra*. One who sets out is a *prasthāyī*. (458) *parame kit*: [The suffix *ini*] after [the root *sthā*] preceded by *parama* is *kit*. One who stands in the highest place is a *parameṣṭhī*. (459) *manthaḥ*: The suffix *ini* is *kit* after the root *manth*. Because it is *kit*, there is the elision of the letter *na*. *Manthāḥ*, *manthānau*, *manthānaḥ*.

460. From the root *path*, [the suffix] *at* is applied: *panthaḥ* (path), *panthāḥ* (paths), *panthānau* (two paths). 461. From the root *khaj*, the suffix *āka* is applied: *khajākaḥ* (a bird). 462. *Balākā* and others are also [formed with this suffix]: *balākā* (crane), *śalākā* (pin), *patākā* (banner). 463. *Pināka* and others are also [formed with this suffix]. After the root *pāt*, there is the substitution of *it* and the addition of *num*. *Pinākaḥ* occurs in the neuter and masculine genders, meaning "trident" and "Śiva’s bow" respectively. From the root *taḍ* (to strike), [with the suffix *āka*]: *taḍākaḥ* (lake). 464. From the roots *kaṣ* and *dūṣi*, the suffix *īkan* is applied. *Kaṣikā* is a species of bird. *Dūṣikā* is the secretion from the eyes or nose. 465. From the roots *ani* and *hṛṣi*, the suffix *īkan* is applied, and it is also *kit*. *Anīkam* (army/front).

*hṛṣīkam* [is derived from *hṛṣ*]. 466. *caṅkaṇaḥ* and *kaṅkaṇaḥ*. From the root *kaṇ* in the sense of "sound," with the suffix *īkan* after the *yaṅ*-lopped form (*yaṅluganta*), there is the substitution of *kaṅkaṇa* for the root. *Kaṅkaṇīkā* is a small bell; it is also called *pratisarā*. 467. After the roots *śṝ*, *pṝ*, and *vṛñ*, the suffix *īkan* is applied, and the vowel of the reduplicative syllable (*abhyāsa*) becomes *u*. *Śarkarīkaḥ* means a violent person. *Parparīkaḥ* means the sun. *Varvarīkaḥ* means one with curly hair. 468. *Parpharīka* and others. From the root *sphur* in the sense of "throbbing," the suffix *īkan* is applied, and there is the substitution of *parphara* for the root. *Parpharīkam* means a young sprout.

The suffix *īka* is added after the roots *dṛ*, *hṛ*, *tiṭṭi*, and *car*, with the augment *nuṃ*. *dardarīka* means a musical instrument; *jharjharīka* means a body; *tittiḍīka* is a type of citron; *cañcarīka* means a bee; *marmarīka* means a low-born person; *karkarīkā* means a small water-pot. After the root *puṇ*, [the suffix *īka* is added]. *puṇḍarīka* means a musical instrument; *puṇḍarīka* also refers to a tiger, fire, and a cardinal elephant. After the root *īṣ*, the suffix *īka* is added, it is marked as *kit*, and the vowel is shortened. *iṣīkā* means a thin splinter or stalk. After the root *ṛji*, [the suffix *īka* is added]. *ṛjika* means one who is struck down or afflicted. After the root *sṛ*, the augment *num* is added [along with the suffix *īka*]. *sṛṇikā* means saliva.

472. From *mṛḍ* [the suffixes] *kīkac*, *kaṅkaṇ*, *mṛgīka*, *mṛga*, *mṛḍaṅkaṇa* are applied; [respectively] *mṛḍaḥ* means a child, *kīkacaḥ* and *kaṅkaṇaḥ* mean a certain joint, *mṛḍīkaḥ* means a deer, and *mṛgaḥ* means a child. 473. And *alīka* and others: words ending in *kīkac* are irregularly formed (*nipātita*). From the root *ala* (in the sense of adorning, etc.), *alīkam* means falsehood. With the prefix *vi-*, *vyalīkam* means that which is unpleasant or distressing. *Valīkam* refers to the edge of a roof-covering, and so forth. 474. From the roots *kṝ* and *tṝ*, the suffix *īṣan* is applied. *Karīṣaḥ* (masculine/neuter) means dried cow-dung; *karīṣaḥ* also means a swimmer. 475. From the roots *śṝ* and *pṝ*, the suffix *kic* is applied. *Śirīṣaḥ* (the Śirīṣa tree); *purīṣam* (excrement). 476. From the root *arj*, the suffix *īṣan* is applied and *arj* is replaced by *ṛj*. *Arjīṣaḥ* (the Arjīṣa tree).

*Ṛjīṣaṃ* means a flour-pot. (477) *Ambarīṣaḥ*: this is an irregular formation (*nipātyate*). From the root *abi* in the sense of "sound," *ambarīṣaḥ* is masculine and means a frying pan. (478) From the roots *kṝ*, *śṝ*, *pṝ*, *kaṭi*, *paṭi*, and *śauṭi*, the suffix *īran* is added: *karīraḥ* is a bamboo shoot; *śarīram* is the body; *parīram* is fruit; *kaṭīraḥ* is a cave and the region of the hips; *paṭīraḥ* is sandalwood, a thorn, and desire; *śauṭīraḥ* refers to one who is generous or heroic. Because it belongs to the *brāhmaṇādi* group, the suffix *ṣyañ* is applied: *śauṭīryam*. (479) From the root *vaś*, with the suffix *kit*: *vaśīram*.

480. From the root *kaś*, the suffix *muṭ* is added; the country is *kāśmīra*. 481. From the root *kṛ*, the vowel *u* is substituted [for the radical vowel] and the suffix *ra* is added; *kurīra* means sexual intercourse. 482. From the root *ghas*, the suffix *ki* is added and the radical vowel is changed; *kṣīra* (milk). 483. The words *gabhīra* and *gambhīra* [are derived from the root *gabh*]; optionally, *bha* is substituted for *gabh*, and in that case, the nasal augment (*num*) is inserted. 484. *Viṣā* and *vihā* are formed by adding the suffix *ā* to the roots *syati* and *jahāti* preceded by the prefix *vi*; *viṣā* means intellect, and *vihā* means heaven. These two are indeclinables. 485. From the root *pac*, the suffix *elimac* is added; *pacelima* refers to fire that is not extinguished. 486. From the root *śīṅ*, the suffixes *dhuk*, *lak*, *valañ*, and *vālana* are added.

There are four [meanings for the term] *pratyaya*: *śīdhu* means liquor; *śīla* means inherent nature (*svabhāva*); *śaivala* means moss (*śevāla*). Due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), the *va* may also become *pa*; thus *śevāla*, *śaivala*, and *śepāla* (not feminine) mean moss, while *jalanīlikā* is a specific type of aquatic plant. 487. From the roots *mṛ* and *kaṇi*, the suffixes *ūka* and *okaṇa* are added. *Marūka* means a deer; *kāṇūka* means a crow. 488. From the root *val*, the suffix *ūka* is added. *Valūka* means a bird and also the root of the blue lotus (*utpala*). 489. *Ulūka* and others [are formed similarly]. From *val*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) and the suffix *ūka*. *Ulūka* refers to the owl and the peacock. *Vāvadūka* means a speaker.

*bhallūkaḥ* (bear). 490. From *śam*, with the suffix *buk*: *śambūkaḥ* (a freshwater mussel). 491. From *śali* and *maṇḍi*, the suffix *ūkaṇ*: *śālūkam* (a type of bulbous root); *maṇḍūkaḥ* (frog). 492. From *ni*, the suffix *mi*: *nemiḥ* (felly of a wheel). 493. From *ṛ*, with the augment *ūc*: *ūrmiḥ* (wave). 494. From *bhū*, the suffix *ki* (which is *kit*): *bhūmiḥ* (earth). 495. From *āś*, with the replacement of *ś* by *ra*: *raśmiḥ* (ray of light and also a rope). 496. *dalmiḥ*. From *dal* in the sense of "crumbling apart": *dalmiḥ* (Indra’s weapon). 497. From *vī*, *jyā*, and *jvari*, the suffix *ni*; the nasalization (*ṇatvam*) occurs by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulakāt*).

*Veṇiḥ* and *praveṇī* both denote the arrangement of hair; these two are feminine. [The suffix *ini* is applied] after the roots *jyā*, *jū*, and *ṝ*. *Jyāniḥ* and *jūrṇaḥ* [are derived thus]. 498. After the roots *sṛ* and *vṛṣ*, the suffix *ini* is added with the *kit* designation. *Sṛṇiḥ* means a goad; *vṛṣṇiḥ* means a Kṣatriya or an arrow. 499. After the root *aṅg*, there is elision of the nasal (*na-lopa*). *Agniḥ*. 500. After the roots *vah*, *śrī*, *śru*, *yu*, *dru*, *glā*, *hā*, *at*, and *ari*, the suffix *ini* is added with the *nit* designation. *Vahniḥ*; *śreṇiḥ*; *śroṇiḥ*; *yoniḥ*; *droṇiḥ*; *glāniḥ*; *hāniḥ*; *tūrṇiḥ*. By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), *mlāniḥ* is also formed. 501. *Ghṛṇi*, *pṛśni*, *pārṣṇi*, *cūrṇi*, and *bhūrṇi*: these five are irregularly formed (*nipātita*).

*Ghṛṇiḥ* means a ray; there is elision of the *s* from the root *spṛś*. *Pṛśniḥ* means one with a small body; there is also the *vṛddhi* strengthening of the root *pṛṣ*. *Pārṣṇiḥ* means the sole of the foot. From the root *car*, the penultimate vowel becomes *u*: *cūrṇiḥ* means a hundred cowries. From the root *bibharti* (to support), there is the change to *u*: *bhūrṇiḥ* means the earth. 502. After the roots *vṛ* and *dṛ*, the suffix *vin* is applied: *varviḥ* means a consumer of food; *darviḥ* means a ladle. 503. After the roots *jṝ*, *śṝ*, *stṝ*, and *jāgṛ*, the suffix *kvin* is applied: *jīrviḥ* means a rib; *śīrviḥ* means a harmful creature; *stīrviḥ* means an officiating priest (*adhvaryu*); *jāgṛviḥ* means a king.

504. From the root *div*, [the suffix] *u* is added, and the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) becomes long: *dīdiviḥ*, meaning heaven and liberation. 505. [The following are derived from their respective roots: *kṛvi*, *ghṛṣvi*, *chavi*, *sthavi*, and *kikīdivi*. *Kṛvi* means the material for a weaver; *ghṛṣvi* means a boar; *chavi* (from *chā*) has its vowel shortened and means luster; *sthavi* means a weaver; and from the root *div* preceded by *kikī*, one gets *kikīdivi* (a woodpecker). 506. From the root *pat*, the suffix *ḍati* is added: *patiḥ* (lord/master). 507. From the root *śak*, the suffix *ṛtin* is added: *śakṛt* (excrement). 508. From the root *am*, the suffix *ati* is added: *amatiḥ*, meaning time. 509. From the roots *vah*, *vas*, and *ṛti*, the suffix *cit* is added [with the acute accent on the final syllable].

*Vahatiḥ* means wind; *vasatiḥ* means a house or night; *aratiḥ* means anger. 510. After the root *añc*, there is optionally *ki*. Thus, *aṅkatiḥ*; alternatively, *añcatiḥ* means wind. 511. After the root *han*, there is *ati*, and the root undergoes the substitution of *aṃha*. Thus, *aṃhatiḥ* is derived from *han*; it means that by which one destroys evil, i.e., a gift, a bestowal, a distribution, a relinquishment, or a donation. 512. After the root *ram*, there is the augment *nit*. Thus, *ramatiḥ* means time or desire. 513. After the root *sūṅ*, there is *kri*. Thus, *sūriḥ*. 514. After the roots *ad*, *śad*, *bhū*, and *bhī*, there is *krin*. Thus, *adriḥ* (mountain) and *śadriḥ* (a type of tree).

*Śarkarā* (gravel/sugar). *Bhūri* means abundant or much. *Śubhribrahmā*. 515. *Vaṅkri* and others are also irregularly formed (*nipātita*) with the suffix *in*. *Vaṅkri* refers to a type of musical instrument, a beam of a house, and a rib-bone. *Vapriḥ* means a field. *Aṃhri* and *aṅghri* mean a foot. *Tadi* is a root belonging to the *sautra* (grammatical) roots. *Tandriḥ* means delusion; the *guṇa* vowel change occurs here by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*). *Bheriḥ* (a drum). 516. From the roots *rā* and *śad*, the suffix *trip* is applied. *Rātriḥ* (night). *Śantriḥ* (an elephant). *Kuñjaraḥ* (elephant). 517. From the root *ad*, the suffixes *trin* and *niś* are applied. By the word "and" (*ca*), *antrip* is also included. *Antrī*; *antriṇau*.

From the root *antr*, [the suffix] *in* is applied: *antrin*, *antriḥ*, *antrī*, *antrayaḥ*. (518) From the roots *pat* and *atṛ*, [the suffix] *in* is applied: *patatriḥ* means "bird. (519) From the roots *mṛ* and *kaṇi*, [the suffix] *īci* is applied: *marīciḥ* means "ray" or "pallava," and *kaṇīciḥ* means "sound. (520) From the root *śvi*, [the suffix] *īci* is applied with the augment *cit*: *śvayīciḥ* means "disease. (521) From the root *veñ*, [the suffix] *īci* is applied with the augment *ḍit*: *vīciḥ* means "wave"; in a negative compound (*nañ-samāsa*), *avīciḥ* refers to a specific hell. (522) From the roots *ṛ* and *han*, [the suffix] *ūñan* is applied: *arūṣaḥ* means "the sun"; *hanūṣau* means "a Rākṣasa. (523) From the root *pur* [meaning] "to go before," [the suffix] *kuṣan* is applied: *puruṣaḥ*.

For other roots as well—the vowel is long: *pūrṣaḥ*. [Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.1.52] From the roots *pṛ*, *naha*, and *kali*, the suffix *uṣac* is added: *uruṣam*, *nahuṣaḥ*, *kaluṣam*. [Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.1.53] From the root *pīy*, the suffix *ūṣan* is added; *pīy* is a root found in the Sūtra (sautra-dhātu). *pīyūṣam*. By virtue of the rule regarding diversification (*bāhulaka*), there is *guṇa* substitution, resulting in *peyūṣaḥ*, meaning fresh milk. [Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.1.54] From the root *masj*, the augment *num* is also applied: *mañjūṣā*. [Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.1.55] Also from the root *gaḍ*: *gaṇḍūṣaḥ*; *gaṇḍūṣā*. 529. From the root *kuṭ*, the suffix *ki* is applied, and [the vowel] is lengthened (*kic*). *Kuṭaru* means a tent or cloth-hut. The purpose for applying the suffix *kit* should be considered. 530. From *śaka* and other roots, the suffix *aṭan* is applied. *Śakaṭa* (a cart) is not feminine. The root *śaki* has the meaning of "going. *Kaṅkaṭa* means armor. *Devata* means an artisan. *Karaṭa* and so forth. 531. From *kṛ*, *kad*, *ikaḍi*, and *kaṭi*, the suffix *ambac* is applied. *Karamba* means mixed. *Kadi* and *kaḍi* are Vedic (sautra) roots. *Kadamba* is a species of tree. *Kaḍamba* means the tip or front part. *Kaṭamba* means a musical instrument. 532. From the root *kada*, with the suffix *ṇit*, [the word *kāda*] refers to a bird.

From the roots *kad* and *amb*, *kala* and *haṃsa*: *kādamba* means a type of goose (*kalahaṃsa*). From the roots *kāl* and *kard*, with the suffix *am*: *kālamaḥ* and *kardamaḥ*. From the roots *kuṇ* and *puli*, with the suffix *kindac*: *kuṇ* means sound or instrument; *kuṇindaḥ* is a sound. *Pulindaḥ* is a specific tribe. From the root *kup*, optionally with *va* as the penultimate letter: *kupinda* and *kuvinda* both mean a weaver. From the root *ṣañj* preceded by *ni*, with the suffix *ghathin*: *niṣaṅgathih* means one who embraces. From the root *udyart*, with the suffix *cit*: *udarathiḥ* means the ocean. From the root *sṛ*, with the causative suffix (*ṇic*) and the suffix *i*: *sārathiḥ* (charioteer).

539. From *kharju*, *piñj*, and others, the suffixes *ūru* and *lac* are added. *Kharjūraḥ* (date palm); *karpūraḥ* (camphor); *vallūraṃ* (dried meat); *piñjūlaṃ* (a bundle of *kuśa* grass). From *laṅg*, there is also vṛddhi: *lāṅgūlam* (tail). *Kusūlaḥ* (granary). From *tam*, *bum* is added and there is vṛddhi: *tāmbūlam* (betel). From *śṛṇāti*, *duk* is added and there is vṛddhi: *śārdūlaḥ* (tiger). From *duka*, *kuk* is added: *dukūlam* (fine silk); *kukūlam* (a pit for burning chaff). 540. From *kuvaś*, *caṭ* is added and the vowel is lengthened: *kūcī* (a painting brush). 541. From *sam-iṇ*, [the suffix *caṭ* is added]: *samīcaḥ* (meeting); *samudraḥ* (ocean). *Samīcī* (a female deer).

542. *siveṣṭer ū ca*: From the root *siv* (to sew), the suffix *u* is added, and the vowel is replaced by *ū*. *Sūcu* means a blade of *darbha* grass; *sūcī* means a needle. 543. *śamer ban*: From the root *śam* (to be quiet), the suffix *ban* is added. *Śamba* means a pestle (*musala*). 544. *ulbādayaś ca*: Words beginning with *ulba* are derived as nouns ending in the suffix *ban*, through irregular derivation (*nipātana*). From the root *uc* (to collect), the letter *c* is replaced by *l*, and there is an absence of *guṇa* strengthening. *Ulba* means the womb (*garbhāśaya*); *śulba* means copper; *bimba* means a reflection or an image. 545. *sthaḥ sto 'mbajabakau*: To the root *sthā* (to stand), the suffixes *ambac* and *abaka* are added, and the root *sthā* is replaced by *sta*. *Stamba* means a cluster of grass or the like; *stabaka* means a cluster of flowers.

546. The suffix *dan* is added after the roots *śas* and *pā*. [The forms are] *śāda*, meaning "mud" (*jambāla*) and "grass" (*śāṣpa*). 547. And *abdādayaḥ* (words beginning with *abda*). [For example: *śabdaḥ* ("sound"). [From the root *śad* with *ab-* as prefix: *aśabdaḥ* ("not sounding," "silent"). 548. The augment *num* is added after the root *kauti*. [The form is] *kundaḥ* ("jasmine"). 549. The suffix *kayan* is added after the roots *vali*, *mali*, and *tani*. [The forms are] *valayam* ("bracelet"), *malayaḥ* ("the Malaya mountain"), and *tanayaḥ* ("son"). 550. After the roots *vṛ* and *hṛ*, the augments *ṣuk* and *duk* are respectively added. [The forms are] *vṛṣayaḥ* ("resort") and *hṛdayam* ("heart"). 551. The suffix *ru* is added after the roots *mi* and *pī*. [The forms are] *meruḥ* ("Mount Meru") and *peruḥ* ("the sun"). By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), it is also applied to the root *pā*: "He whose body is the year, the protector (*pāruḥ*), the pervader (*peruḥ*), the wielder of the sword, the leader of the day."

552. And *jatru* and so forth: *jatru*, *jatruṇī*; *aśru*, *aśruṇī*. 553. From the roots *ru* and *śāti*, the suffix *krun* is applied: *ruru* is a species of deer; *śatru* (enemy), because he "cuts down" (*śātayati*). The short vowel [of the root] occurs due to its inclusion in the *prajñādi* group. 554. From the roots *jan*, *dā*, *cyu*, *sṛ*, *vṛ*, *mad*, *iṣ*, *nam*, *bhṛ*, the suffixes *itvan*, *tvan*, *naṇ*, *knin*, *śak*, *sthaḍ*, *haḍ*, *aṭ*, and *aṭac* are applied respectively: *janitvau* refers to mother and father; *dātvaḥ* refers to a giver; *cyautnaḥ* refers to a goer; *aṇḍajaḥ* refers to one born from an egg and one whose merit is exhausted; *sṛṇiḥ* refers to a sprout, a sword, the moon, the sun, or the wind.

*Vṛśaḥ*, *ārdrakam*, and *mūlakam*; *matsyaḥ*; *ṣaṇḍhaḥ*. Due to the presence of the letter *ṭ*, there is the elision of the suffix *ṭi*. One who bows is a *naṭaḥ*, a stage-player (*śailūṣaḥ*). One who supports is a *bharaṭaḥ*: a potter (*kulālaḥ*) and a hired laborer (*bhṛtakaḥ*). 555. These are seen [as derivatives] from other roots as well: *petvam*, *amṛtam*, *bhṛśam*. 556. From the root *kusu*, the suffixes *umbha*, *meda*, and *ta* [are applied]: *kusumbham*, *kusumam*, *kusīdam*. A country is called *kusitaḥ*. 557. *Sānasi*, *varṇasi*, *paṇasi*, *taṇḍula*, *aṅkuśa*, *caṣāla*, *elvala*, *palvala*, *dhiṣṇya*, and *śalya*.

The suffix *asi* is added to the root *san*, with vṛddhi of the penultimate vowel: *sāṃsiḥ* (gold). To the root *vṛñ*, the suffix *asi* is added along with the augment *nu*: *varṇasiḥ* (water). To the root *pṝ*, the suffix *asi* is added: *parṇasiḥ* (the vessel for holding water). To the root *taḍ* (to strike), the suffix *asi* is added: *taṇḍulāḥ* (rice grains). To the root *ak* (to mark), the suffix *uśac* is added: *aṅkuśaḥ* (a goad). To the root *caṣ*, the suffix *ālac* is added: *caṣālaḥ* (the ring at the top of a sacrificial post). *Ilvalaḥ* is a specific type of demon; *palvalam* (a small pond). From the root *dhṛṣ* (with the *ñi* marker), the vowel *ṛ* is changed to *i*: *dhiṣṇyam*. From the root *śal*, the suffix *ya* is added: *śalyam* (an arrowhead); optionally it is masculine: *śalyaḥ* or *śaṅkuḥ* (a stake). 558. The suffix *kla* is added to the roots *mū*, *śak*, and *ab*: *mūlam* (root).

*Śuklaḥ* (white) and *priyaṃvadaḥ* (affable). From the root *aml*, due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), we have *amlaḥ* (sour). 559. From the roots *mā*, *chā*, and *sas*, the suffix *ya* is added: *māyā* (illusion), *chāyā* (shadow), and *sasyam* (grain). Due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), from the root *su* (to press), we have *savyam* (left; also meaning "favorable" or "right"). 560. From the root *jan* (to be born), the suffix *yak* is added. According to the rule *ye vibhāṣā*, [the suffix *ya* is optionally applied]: *janyam* (battle), and *jāyā* (wife). 561. Words such as *aghnyā* and others are irregularly formed with the suffix *ya*. From the root *han* (to kill), the augment *yuk* is added, there is the prefix *aṭ*, and the elision of the penultimate vowel: *aghnyā* (a cow), *aghnyaḥ* (Prajāpati). From the root *kan* (to shine), we have *kanyā* (a maiden).

The identity of *ba* and *va*. *vandhyā* (barren woman). 562. The suffix *vanip* is added after the roots *snā*, *mad*, *pad*, *ṛ*, *pṛ*, and *śaki*. *snāvā* means one who has bathed; *madvā* means Śiva; *padvā* means a path; *arvā* means a horse or one who is censurable; *parvā* means a knot or a section; *śakvā* means an elephant. The feminine suffixes *ṅī* and *īp* are applied: *śakvarī* means a finger. 563. The suffix *kvanip* is added after the roots *śīṅ*, *kruś*, *ruh*, *ji*, *kṣi*, *sṛ*, and *dhṛ*. *śīvā* means a python; *kruśvā* means a jackal; *ruhvā* means a tree; *jitvā* means a conqueror; *kṣitvā* means the wind; *sṛtvā* means Prajāpati.

564. After the roots *dhṛ* and *dhyai*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). *Dhīvā* means a laborer; *pīvā* means stout. 565. After the root *ad*, there is also the substitution of *dh*. *Adhvā* (path). 566. After the roots *pra-īr* and *pra-śad*, there is the addition of the suffix *tuṭ*. *Preitvā* and *praśatvā* mean the ocean; *pretvarī* and *praśatvarī* mean a river. 567. The suffix *in* occurs after all verbal roots. *Paciḥ* means fire; *tuḍiḥ*; *tuṇḍiḥ*; *valiḥ*; *vaṭiḥ*; *yajiḥ*; *devayajiḥ*. That which shines is *kāśiḥ*. *Yatiḥ*; *malliḥ*; *keliḥ*. *Masī* in the sense of measuring.

*masiḥ*; by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), there is *guṇa*: *koṭiḥ*, *heliḥ*, *bodhiḥ*, *nandiḥ*, *kaliḥ*. 568. And from *hṛ*, *piṣ*, *ruh*, *vṛt*, *vid*, *chid*, and *kīrti*: *hariḥ*—it is proclaimed [to denote] Viṣṇu, fire, Indra, a frog, a lion, a horse, the sun, the moon, a wedge, a monkey, Yama, and the wind; *peṣiḥ* is a thunderbolt; *rohiḥ* is one who observes a vow; *vartiḥ*; *vediḥ*; *chadiḥ* is a cutter; *kīrtiḥ*. 569. From a root with a semivowel (*ig*) as its penultimate (*upadha*), the suffix is marked with *kit*: *kṛṣiḥ*, *ṛṣiḥ*, *śuciḥ*, *lipiḥ*.

By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), the suffix *lib* is applied after the root *bat*; from *tūla* in the sense of "extracting," we have *tūliḥ*; *tūlī* means a brush. 570. After the root *bhram*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). *Bhṛmiḥ* means wind; by virtue of the rule of diversity, *bhramiḥ* is also formed. 571. After the roots *kram*, *tam*, *śas*, and *stambh*, the suffix *in* is applied, and the vowel *a* is replaced by *i*. *Krimiḥ* [is a worm]; because the rule for vocalization continues to apply, *kṛmiḥ* is also used. *Timiḥ* is a species of fish. *Śitiḥ* means dark-blue or white. *Stimbhiḥ* is the ocean. 572. After the root *man*, the vowel *u* is substituted [for the radical vowel], and the suffix *in* is applied. *Maniḥ* (jewel). 573. After the root *varṇ*, the suffix *in* is applied, and *bali* is substituted [for the root], provided it does not refer to gold. *Varṇiḥ* is a word found in the Sūtra collection.

The word *bali* is derived from the root *bal*. It is masculine when referring to a tax or an offering; it is feminine when denoting a part of a living being; and it is neuter when meaning gold (where it is also called *varṇi* or *suvarṇa*). [From the roots] *vas*, *vap*, *yaj*, *rāj*, *vraj*, *sad*, *han*, *nāś*, and *vāś*, the suffix *iñ* is applied: - From *vas*: *vāsi* means an instrument for cutting. - From *vap*: *vāpi* or *vāpī* means a pond. - From *yaj*: *yājī* means a sacrificer. - From *rāj*: *rājī* means a line or row. - From *vraj*: *vrājī* means a swarm of bees. - From *sad*: *sādī* means a charioteer. - From *han*: *nighāti* means a hammer used by a blacksmith. - From *vāś*: *vāśī* means fire. - From *vad*: *vādī* means a learned man or speaker. - From *vṛ*: *vārī* means a female elephant’s tethering post; it is neuter when meaning water.

By virtue of the rule of general application (*bāhulaka*), the suffix *vāri* is added after the root *path* to form *pathavāri*, meaning a multitude of travelers. 575.
