*na-bha-s-* (661): From the root *iṇ*, with the suffix *asun*; and [the word] *āgas* means "sin" and "offense. *ā-ga-s-* (662): From the root *am*, with the augment *huk* and the suffix *asun*; *aṃhas* [means sin]. *ra-me-ś-ca* (663): And from the root *ram*, [with the same suffix]; *raṃhas* [means speed]. *de-śe-ha-ca* (664): In the sense of "place," *ha* is substituted for *ra*; they delight in this, thus *rahas* [means a secret or secluded place]. *añci-añji-yuji-bhṛjibhyaḥ kuñ-ca* (665): From these roots, with the suffix *asun* and the substitution of the guttural class (*ku*) at the end; *aṅka* means a mark or the body; *aṅka* also means a bird; *yoga* means meditative absorption (*samādhi*); *bhargas* means splendor (*tejas*). *bhūrañjibhyāṃ kit* (666): From the roots *bhū* and *rañj*, with the suffix *asun* marked as *kit*; *bhuvas* [means the world]; *rajas* [means dust or passion]. *vaseḥ ṇit* (667): From the root *vas*, with the suffix *asun* marked as *ṇit*.

*vāsaḥ* means clothing (*vastra*). 668. From *chand*, there is the substitution of *cha*. *chandaḥ* (verse). 669. From the roots *pac* and *vac*, there is also the augment *suṭ*. *pakṣasī* are known as the two wings (*pakṣau*). *vakṣaḥ* is the heart (*hṛdayam*). 670. After the roots *vah*, *hā*, and *dhā*, [the suffix *asun* occurs] in the Vedic language (*chandasi*). *vakṣāḥ* is an ox (*anaḍvān*); *hāsāḥ* is the moon (*candra*); *dhāsāḥ* is a mountain—so say the ancients (*prāñcaḥ*). But in reality, the term *ṇit* is understood [from the previous rule], not *suṭ*. Therefore, there is vocalic strengthening (*vṛddhi*) of the penultimate vowel of *vah*; for the other two, the suffix *yuk* is applied by the rule *āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ*. "The ruddy, bold ones, the bearers of men" (*śoṇā dhṛṣṇū nṛvāhasā*).

"May he who hears the call of the singer, who bears the hymns, who is all-pervading, who brings strength, and who is vast—he who, like a god, has sustained the earth as its universal sustainer, the supporter, the one of manifold nourishment," and so forth. (671) *iṇ* with the suffix *asi*: *ayāḥ*, meaning "the bearer. It is an indeclinable because it is listed among the *svar-ādi* group. (672) Regarding the term *mithuna*, the suffix *asi* is applied as before, and everything else remains the same. A verbal root qualified by a prefix is called *mithuna*; in that case, *asi* is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *asun*. Its purpose is for the sake of the accent (*svarārtha*).

673. When the negative particle *nañ* is present, [the suffix] *han* becomes *eha*. Thus: *anehāḥ*, *anehasau*. 674. After the root *dhā*, [the suffix] *vidha* is substituted for *vedha*. One who ordains (*vidadhāti*) is *vedhāḥ*. 675. After the root *nu*, [the suffix] *dhuṭ* is added. Thus: *nodhāḥ*. 676. When a word denoting motion (*gati*), an agent (*kāraka*), or a subordinate word (*upapada*) precedes, there is also the preservation of the original accent (*prakṛtisvara*) of the preceding member. For example: *asiḥ*, *sutapāḥ*, *jātavedāḥ*. Since the rule "a *kṛt*-suffix following a word denoting motion, an agent, or an *upapada*" prescribes that the final syllable of the second member retains its original accent, and this would result in the rest of the word becoming unaccented (*anudātta*), this [present sūtra] is intended as an exception to that. 677. In the case of *candra*, the suffix *ma* is treated as having an indicatory letter *ḍ* (*ḍit*).

The suffix *asi* shall follow the root *māṅ* when preceded by *candra*, and that suffix is marked with the *ḍi*-sign. Example: *candramāḥ* (the moon). 678. After the root *dhā*, [the suffix *asi* is applied] in the sense of age (*vayas*). Example: *vayodhāḥ* (a youth). 679. Also after *payas*. Example: *payodhāḥ* (the ocean and the cloud). 680. Also after *puras*. Example: *purodhāḥ* (a domestic priest). 681. *purūravāḥ*. The lengthening of the word *puru* and the suffix *asi* after the root *ru* are irregularly prescribed (*nipātyate*). 682. After the root *cakṣ*, the suffix *śi* is frequently applied. Example: *nṛcakṣāḥ* (one who watches over men). 683. After the particle *u*, [the suffix *asi* is applied] as a *kit*. Example: *uṣaḥ* (dawn). 684. After the root *dam*, the suffix *unas* is applied. Example: *saptārcir damunāḥ* (the seven-flamed fire; a name of Agni).

685. From the root *aṅg* (to move), there is the suffix *asi*, and the augment *ruṭ* is added: *aṅgirāḥ*. 686. From the root *sṛ* (to go) preceded by *ap*, there is the suffix *asi*: *apsarāḥ*. This word generally occurs in the plural: *apsarasaḥ*. 687. From the roots *vid* (to know) and *bhuj* (to enjoy), with the prefix *viśva*, there is the suffix *asi*: *viśvavedāḥ* (all-knowing) and *viśvabhojāḥ* (all-enjoying). 688. From the root *vaś* (to desire), there is the suffix *kanasi*; there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*): *uśanāḥ*. Thus ends the fourth quarter of the *Uṇādi* [Sūtras]. Now begins the fifth quarter.

689. From the root *ad-bhū* (to eat and become), the suffix *ḍutac* is applied: *adbhutam* (a marvel). 690. From the root *guh* (to hide), the suffix *ūma* is applied: *godhūmaḥ* (wheat). 691. From the root *mas* (to measure), the suffix *ūran* is applied: *masūraḥ* (lentil). This was explained under the first *pāda* [of Pāṇini 3.3.56] in the rule *aser ūran maseś ca*. 692. From the root *sthā*, the suffix *kic* is applied: *sthūraḥ* (a stout man). 693. From the root *pā* (to protect), the suffix *ati* is applied: *pātiḥ* (a protector, a master); *saṃpātiḥ* (the king of birds). 694. From the root *vā* (to blow), the suffix *nit* is applied: *vātiḥ* (the sun or the moon). 695. Also from the root *ṛ* (to go), the suffix *ati* is applied: *aratiḥ* (distress, agitation). 696. From the root *tṛh* (to injure), the suffix *kna* is applied with the elision of the *h*: *tṛṇam* (grass).

697. From the roots *vṛ*, *luṭhi*, *tan*, and *taḍ*, the suffix *ulac* is added, and *taṇḍa* is substituted [for the root-final consonant]. Because they are chosen (*vriyante*), rolled (*luṭyante*), stretched (*tanyante*), or struck (*tāḍyante*), they are called *taṇḍulāḥ*. 698. From the root *daṃs*, the suffixes *iṣṭan* and *na* are added, and the vowel *a* is substituted for the radical vowel. *Dāsaḥ* denotes a servant or a Śūdra. 699. Also from the root *daṃś*, [the suffix *iṣṭan* is added]. *Dāśaḥ* means a fisherman. 700. With the prefix *ud*, the suffix *ḍaisi* is added to the root *ci*. Due to its inclusion in the list beginning with *svar* (A 1.1.37), it is an indeclinable. *Uccaiḥ* (highly). 701. With the prefix *ni*, [the suffix *ḍaisi* is added] and the vowel is lengthened. *Nicaiḥ* (lowly). 702. With the prefix *su*, the suffix *kta* is added to the root *ram*, and when the sense is "in a house" (*dame*), the vowel of the preceding member is lengthened. *Sūrataḥ* (well-disposed).

The suffix *kta* is applied after the root *ram* preceded by *su*, when the sense of "self-restraint" (*dama*) is to be expressed. Due to its *kit* status, there is the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika*). Thus, *sūrata* means "tranquil" (*upaśānta*) and "compassionate" (*dayālu*). 703. After the root *pū*, the suffix *yat* is added with the *ṇuk* augment and the vowel is shortened. [Resulting in] *puṇya*. 704. After the root *sraṃs*, *śi* is substituted, and the suffix *yat* is added as *kit*, with the augment *kuṭ*. [Resulting in] *śikya* (a loop or swing). 705. After the root *ṛ*, the suffix *kyu* is added, and the vowel is changed to *u*. [Resulting in] *uraṇa*, meaning "ram" (*meṣa*). 706. After the root *hiṃs*, the suffixes *īran* and *īrac* are added. *Hiṃsīra* refers to both a tiger and a wicked person (*duṣṭa*).

707. From the root *dṛṇāti*, with the suffix *u* and the elision of the final letter of the preceding member, we get *udara* (belly). 708. From the root *khan*, with the suffix *ḍit* [the suffix *u*], there is the augment *muṭ*, and that is acute-accented (*udātta*). The suffix *ac* is also *ḍit* after the root, and there is the augment *muṭ*, which is acute-accented. Thus, *mukha* (mouth). 709. From the root *am*, with the suffix *san*. Thus, *aṃsa* (shoulder). 710. From the root *muha*, with the suffix *kha*, there is the substitution of *mūr* for the root. Thus, *mūrkha* (fool). 711. From the root *naha*, with the suffix *kha*, there is the elision of the *hal* (consonant) [of the root]. Thus, *nakha* (nail). 712. From the root *śīṅ*, with the suffix *kha*, there is also the substitution of a short vowel. Thus, *śīkhā* (crest/topknot). 713. From the root *māṅ*, with the suffix *ūkha*, there is the substitution of *maya* for the root. Thus, *mayūkha* (ray). 714. From the roots *kali* and *gali*, with the suffix *phak*, there is the substitution of *as* for the root vowel. [Thus, *kālika* and *gāliphaka*].

*Kalpa* means a limb of the body or a disease. *Gulpha* means the ankle. (Pāṇini 3.2.54) After the root *spr̥ś*, the suffixes *śvan* and *śun* are applied, and there is the substitution of *pṛ*. *Pārśva* (masculine/neuter) refers to the area below the armpits; *parśu* is a weapon. (Pāṇini 3.2.55) After the root *śri* with the prefix *śman*, the suffix *ṭun* is applied. The word *śman* denotes the mouth. That which rests upon the mouth (*mukham āśrayate*) is *śmaśru* (beard). (Pāṇini 3.2.56) *Aśru* and others are also [formed in this manner]. *Aśru* is the water of the eyes. (Pāṇini 3.2.57) After the root *jan*, the suffix *ṭan* is applied and there is elision [of the nasal]. *Jaṭā* (matted hair). (Pāṇini 3.2.58) There is the suffix *ac*, and *jaṅgha* is substituted for [the root]. *Jaṅghā* (shank).

From the root *jan*, the suffix *an* is applied, and the vowel is replaced by *ac*; thus, *jaṅghā* (the shank). 720. From the root *han*, when referring to a part of the body, the suffix *an* is applied and the root is reduplicated; thus, *jaghanam* (the buttocks). The term *nitamba* refers to the hindquarters of a woman, while *jaghana* is used for the front part of the hips in the neuter gender. 721. From the root *kliś*, the suffix *an* is applied with the elision (*lopa*) of the letter *l*; thus, *keśaḥ* (hair). 722. From the root *phal*, the suffix *itac* is applied, and the initial *p* is substituted for the *ph*; thus, *palitam* (gray hair). 723. From roots such as *kṛ*, the suffix *vun* is applied when forming proper nouns (*saṃjñā*); thus, *karakaḥ* (a water-jar), *karakā* (hailstone), *kaṭakaḥ* (bracelet), *narakaḥ* (hell), and *narakam* (hell).

*Naraka* and *nāraka* constitute a dual form (*dvirūpakośa*). *Saraka* means the sky. *Koraka* and *koraka* [mean a bud]. (724) From the root *cīk*, there is a reversal of the initial and final [phonemes]; *kīcaka* is a type of bamboo. (725) From the roots *pac* and *mac*, the vowel *i* is substituted for the penultimate vowel; thus, *pecaka* and *mecaka*. (726) From the root *jan*, the suffix *ara* is added and the final syllable is replaced by *ṛṣṭha*; thus, *jaṭhara*. (727) From the roots *vac* and *man*, the suffix *ic* is added; thus, *vaṭhara* meaning a fool, and *maṭhara* meaning a sage or a drunkard. By virtue of belonging to the *bidādi* group, *māṭhara* [is formed]; by virtue of belonging to the *gargādi* group, *māṭharyaḥ*.

728. From the root *dṛ* (to tear), the suffixes *alac* and *ac* are added, with the elision of the final letter of the preceding stem; thus, *ūrdaraḥ*, meaning "hero" or "demon. 729. *Kṛdarādayaś ca*: [The words] beginning with *kṛdara* are formed [irregularly]. *Kṛdaraḥ* means "granary"; *mṛdaram* means "a pleasure-grove"; *sṛdaraḥ* means "serpent. 730. After the root *han* (to kill), when followed by suffixes beginning with *na* or ending in *t*, the substitution of *gh* for *h* and *t* for *n* occurs; thus, *ghātanaḥ*, meaning "a slayer. 731. From the roots *krami*, *gami*, and *kṣami*, the suffix *tun* is added, along with the increase (*vṛddhi*) of the vowel; thus, *krāntuḥ* means "bird"; *gāntuḥ* means "traveler"; *kṣāntuḥ* means "mosquito. 732. From the root *haryati*, the suffix *kanyan* is added, and *hira* is substituted [for the root]; thus, the suffix *kanyan* is applied.

733. From the root *kṛ* (to do/make), the suffix *pāsa* is applied: *karpāsaḥ* (cotton). Because it belongs to the *bilva* group, the word *kārpāsam* means "cotton cloth. 734. In the case of the root *jan* (to be born), *ra* is substituted for the final letter, and the suffix *tu* is applied: *jartuḥ* means "an elephant" and "the womb. 735. From the root *ūrṇoti* (to cover), the suffix *ḍa* is applied: *ūrṇā* (wool). 736. From the root *dadhāti* (to place/hold), the suffix *yat* is applied with the augment *nuṭ*: *dhānyam* (grain). 737. From the root *jṝ* (to grow old), the suffix *krin* is applied with *ra* substituted for the final letter: *jivriḥ* occurs in the sense of a "small bird" (*kalapakṣin*). Due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*), the lengthening of the vowel prescribed by the rule *hali ca* does not take place here. 738. From the root *mavyati*, there is elision of *ya*, *ma* is substituted for the final letter, and the suffixes *ap*, *tuṭ*, and *ala* are applied: [the resulting form is *mātulaḥ*].

The suffix *āla* shall be added to the root *mavyati*; there is the augment *at-uṭ* for that [suffix], the elision of *ya* from the root, and the final *m* is replaced by *a*. Thus: *mamāpatāla* in the sense of "in the domain. 739. The suffix *kīkan* is added to the root *ṛji*. *Ṛjīka* means Indra and smoke. 740. The suffix *ḍau* is added to the root *tanoti*, and it is treated as if it were *san* (causing reduplication). *Titau* is both masculine and neuter. 741. *Arbhaka*, *pṛthuka*, and *pāka* are used in the sense of age. From the root *ṛdh* (to increase), the suffix *vun* is added; *bhakāra* is the substitute for the final letter. From the root *prath* (to spread), the suffix *kukan* is added with vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). From the root *pibati*, the suffix *kan* is added. 742. *Avadya*, *avamā*, *adhama*, and *arvara* are formed with the suffix *ra*.

The suffix *yat* is applied after the root *vad* when it is preceded by the negative particle *nañ* in the sense of "blameworthy": *avadyam*. After the root *ava*, the suffix *ama* is applied; optionally, *dha* is substituted for *va*, resulting in *avamaḥ* or *adhamaḥ*. After the root *ṛ*, the suffix *van* is applied: *arvā*. 743. After the root *riph* belonging to the *tudādi* class, the suffix *a* is applied: *rephaḥ*. 744. After the roots *lī* and *rīṅ*, a short vowel is substituted [for the final], and the suffix *puṭ* is added when the suffixes *ta* and *ra* follow in the senses of "adhering" and "blame," respectively. The suffixes *ta* and *ra* are applied to the root in sequence, the root-final vowel is shortened, and the suffix receives the augment *puṭ*. Thus: *liptam* (adhered) and *śliṣṭam* (adhered); *ripram* (blameworthy). 745. After the root *kliś*, the suffix *kan* is applied, the penultimate vowel *ī* is replaced by *īc*, the letter *l* is elided, and the *n* is replaced by *m*: [resulting in *klīmaḥ*].

The suffix *kan* is applied after the root *kliś*; there is the substitution of *ī* for the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*), the elision of the *la* (the suffix marker), and the augment *nām*. Thus, *kīnāśaḥ* means "Yama. The result of the *kittva* (the *k*-marker) should be considered [elsewhere]. 746. After the root *aś*, when meaning "to eat quickly," the suffix *varaṭ* is applied. By the force of the letter *ca* [in the rule], there is the substitution of *ī* for the penultimate vowel. Thus, *īśvaraḥ*. 747. After the root *cat*, the suffix *uran* is applied. Thus, *catvāraḥ* ("four"). 748. After the root *prādat*, the suffix *aran* is applied. Thus, *prātaḥ* ("morning"). 749. After the root *am*, the augment *tuṭ* is added. Thus, *antar* ("middle"). 750. After the root *dah*, the suffix *go* is applied; there is the elision of the final [radical] and the change of *da* to *na*. The suffix *gapratyaya* [is understood]; there is elision of the end of the root and the substitution of *na* for *da*. Thus, *nagaḥ* ("mountain").

751. *Siñcaḥ saṃjñāyāṃ hanumau kaś ca*: After the root *siñc* (to sprinkle), when used in the sense of a proper name (*saṃjñā*), there is the suffix *kap*, the substitution of *han* for the root, and the augment *num*. Example: *siṃhaḥ* (lion). 752. *Vyāṅi ghrāteś ca jātau*: After the root *ghrā* (to smell), when preceded by the prefixes *vi* or *ā*, there is the suffix *kap* when denoting a genus (*jāti*). Example: *vyāghraḥ* (tiger). 753. *Hanter ac dhur ca*: After the root *han* (to kill), there is the suffix *ac* and the substitution of *dhuṛ* for the root. Example: *dhauram* (a type of fragrant grass). 754. *Kṣamer upadhālopaś ca*: After the root *kṣam* (to endure), there is the elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-lopa*) and, by the word "and" (*ca*), the suffix *ac*. Example: *kṣmā* (the earth). 755. *Tarater ḍriḥ*: After the root *tṛ* (to cross), there is the suffix *ḍri*. Examples: *trayaḥ* (three) and *trīn* (three [accusative]). 756. *Graher aniḥ*: After the root *grah* (to seize), there is the suffix *ani*. Example: *grahaṇiḥ*; with the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*, it becomes *grahaṇī*, a specific disease of the bowels. 757. *Prather amac*: After the root *prath* (to spread), there is the suffix *amac*. Example: *prathamaḥ* (first).

758. And from the root *car*, [the suffix *ac* is applied]; *caramaḥ*. 759. From the root *maṅg*, [the suffix] *alac*; *maṅgalam*. Thus ends the fifth section of the Uṇādi-sūtras. Now begins the section on secondary derivatives (*uttarakṛdanta*). 66.
SK 3169: *uṇādayo bahulam* (A 3.3.1).

These [suffixes] occur diversely (*bahulam*) in the sense of the present tense and in the sense of a name (*saṃjñā*). Some [forms] should be inferred even though they have not been explicitly prescribed. In names, one should recognize the forms of verbal roots and the suffixes following them; one should understand the indicatory letters (*anubandha*) from their grammatical effect (*kārya*). This is the teaching regarding the *uṇādi* suffixes. SK 3170: They are also seen in the sense of the past (*bhūta*). (A 3.3.2)

SK 3171: *bhaviṣyati gamyādayaḥ* (A 3.3.3). SK 3172: *dāśagoghnau saṃpradāne* (A 3.4.73). These two are irregularly formed (*nipātita*) when the recipient (*saṃpradāna*) is the grammatical factor (*kāraka*). One who gives to him is a *dāśa*; that which kills a cow for him is a *goghna* sacrificial post (*yūpa*).

SK 3173: *bhīmādayo 'pādāne* (A 3.4.74): [The suffixes] *uṇ* and so forth occur after roots when the sense is that of the ablative (*apādāna*). Examples: *bhīmaḥ*, *bhīṣmaḥ*, *praskandanaḥ*, *prarakṣaḥ*, *mūrkhaḥ*, *khalatiḥ*.
SK 3174: *tābhyām anyatroṇādayaḥ* (A 3.4.75): After those two [roots mentioned in the previous rule], the suffixes *uṇ* and so forth occur in senses other than the ablative.

The word *tābhyām* is used for the purpose of referring to the recipient (*saṃpradāna*). From that [action], it becomes a thread (*tantu*); because it has occurred (*vṛtta*), it is a path (*vartma*); because it has been traversed (*carita*), it is skin (*carma*).
According to Pāṇini 3.3.10, *tumun* and *ṇvul* occur when another action is the object of an action intended for that purpose;

these two suffixes occur after a verbal root when a verb signifying a future action is the governing word (*upapada*). Because they end in the letter *m*, they are indeclinables (*avyaya*). For example: *kṛṣṇaṃ draṣṭuṃ yāti* (he goes to see Kṛṣṇa); *kṛṣṇaṃ darśako yāti* (he goes as one who intends to see Kṛṣṇa). In this case, suffixes such as *tṛc* do not apply by the rule of "non-identity" (*vāsarūpa*), because the suffix *ṇvul* is explicitly mentioned [as an alternative].

SK 3176: *samānakartṛkeṣu tumun* (A 3.3.158). This rule is intended to exclude cases where the subordinate word (*upapada*) has a meaning other than "desire. When words expressing desire (*icchārtha*) that share the same agent (*ekakartṛka*) are used as subordinate words, the suffix *tumun* shall be applied after a verbal root. For example: *icchati bhoktum* ("he wishes to eat"), or *vaṣṭi vāñchati* ("he desires").

SK 3177: *śak*, *dhṛṣ*, *jñā*, *glā*, *ghaṭ*, *rabh*, *labh*, *kram*, *sah*, and *arh*—when used in the sense of "to be able" (*asti-artha*)—the suffix *tumun* is applied after a verbal root when these [words] are present as governing words (*upapada*). Examples: *śaknoti bhoktum* ("he is able to eat"); likewise in *dhṛṣṇoti* and so forth. The mention of "meaning" (*artha-grahaṇa*) is connected only with *asti*, because it is the immediately preceding one. Example: *asti bhoktum* or *vidyate bhoktum* ("it is possible to eat"). SK 3178: When words expressing "sufficiency" (*paryāpti*) in the sense of "enough" (*alam*) are present as governing words... [the suffix *tumun* is applied]. (A 3.4.66)

*Paryāptiḥ* means sufficiency (*pūrṇatā*). When words expressing sufficiency or capability (*sāmarthya*) are used as governing words (*upapada*), the suffix *tumun* shall be employed. For example: *paryāpto bhoktum*, *pravīṇo bhoktum*, *kuśalo bhoktum*, *paṭur bhoktum*, and so forth. What is the purpose of specifying "words expressing sufficiency"? [Consider: *alaṃ bhuktvā*. What is the purpose of specifying "in the sense of 'sufficient' (*alam-artha*)"? [Consider: *paryāptaṃ bhuṅkte*. Here, abundance (*prabhūtatā*) is understood, but not the capability of the eater. SK 3179:
The suffix *tumun* is used after a verb when *kāla*, *samaya*, or *velā* are the governing words. (A 3.4.167)

The mention of synonyms is for the purpose of indicating the meaning. When words expressing time (*kāla*) are used as *upapadas*, the suffix *tumun* shall be employed. For example: *kālo bhoktum*, *samayo bhoktum*, *velā bhoktum*, or *anehā bhoktum* ("it is time to eat"). The term "command" (*praiṣa*) and so forth is understood to carry over here; therefore, it does not apply in this case: *bhūtāni kālaḥ pacati* ("Time cooks the elements")—this is merely a report (*vārtā*). And [the suffixes] expressing the state of being (*bhāva-vacana*):

under the heading of the word *bhāva*, the suffixes *ghañ* and others that will be explained hereafter shall be used when an action is intended for the sake of another action in the future tense. Example: *yāgāya yāti* ("he goes for the sake of sacrifice").

SK 3181 *aṇ* is used when the object (*karman*) is the attendant word (*upapada*), provided that the action [denoted by the first member] is for the sake of the action [denoted by the second member]. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to *ṇvul*. Example: *kāṇḍalāvaḥ vrajati* ("He goes as one who reaps stalks"). Because it is subsequent [in the order of rules], this supersedes [the application of] suffixes beginning with *ka*. Example: *kambaladāyaḥ vrajati* ("He goes as one who gives blankets"). SK 3182 *ghañ* is used after the roots *pad*, *ruj*, *viśas*, and *sprś* [when the object is the attendant word and the action is for the sake of the action]. (Pāṇini 3.3.16)

The word *bhaviṣyati* is excluded [from the scope of this rule]. That which is stepped upon is a *pāda* (foot). That which causes pain is a *roga* (disease). That which enters is a *veśa* (entrance). That which touches is a *sparśa* (touch).

Regarding the rule *sṛ sthire* (A 3.3.17): the form *sṛ* is one whose case-ending has been elided. The suffix *ghañ* shall be applied after the root *sṛ* when it denotes a stable agent (*kartṛ*). That which moves through a period of time is a *sāra* (essence/constancy). It should be stated that [the suffix is also applied] in the sense of disease, fish, and strength. *Atīsāra* is a disease; here the root *sṛ* includes the causative sense (*ṇic*). The meaning is that it excessively causes blood and so forth to flow out. *Visāra* is a fish. *Sāra* means strength and the solid part [of a substance].

SK 3184: When the meaning of a verbal root (*dhātvartha*) is to be expressed as being established in the state of completion (*siddhāvasthāpanna*), the suffix *ghañ* shall be applied after the root. Examples: *pākaḥ*, *pākau*. SK 3185:
[The substitution of *u* for the vowel] occurs before *ghañ* after the roots *sphurati* and *sphulati*. (Pāṇini A 6.1.47)

In these two cases (*sphāy* and *vṛdh*), the substitution of *ā* occurs before the suffix *ghañ*: *sphāraḥ*, *sphālaḥ*. By the rule "lengthening of the vowel of a prefix before *ghañ*" (*upasargasya ghañi*), we have *parīhāraḥ*. Before the word *kāśa* as a final member of a compound, there is lengthening of a prefix ending in an *ik* vowel: *nīkāśaḥ*, *anūkāśaḥ*. Why "ending in an *ik* vowel"? Observe *prakāśaḥ*; here there is no *vṛddhi* substitution because of the rule "not for a root taught with an udātta accent" (*nodāttopadeśa-*). However, in the case of roots beginning with *ā*, such as *cam*, we have *ācāmaḥ*, *kāmaḥ*, and *vāmaḥ*. As for *viśrāmaḥ*, it is un-Pāṇinian. [The sūtra] *syado jave* (A 6.4.28) [is now introduced].

In the case of the root *syand*, when the suffix *ghañ* is applied, the elision of *na* and the absence of *vṛddhi* are prescribed as irregularities. Thus, *syadaḥ* means "speed" or "velocity," whereas elsewhere it is *syandaḥ*.

SK 3187: *avoda-edha-odma-praśratha-himaśrathāḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.29). *Avodaḥ* means moistening; *edhaḥ* means fuel; *odma* means wetting; [the forms] *praśratha* and *himaśratha* result from the root *śranth*, with the elision of the nasal (*na*) and the absence of *vṛddhi*.

SK 3188: *akartari ca kārake saṃjñāyām* (Pāṇini 3.3.19). [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after a verbal root to form a noun denoting an action, when it does not refer to the agent (*kartṛ*), provided it is a technical term (*saṃjñā*).]

The suffix *ghañ* occurs after a verbal root when the agent (*kartṛ*) is distinct [from the subject of the sentence]. By A 6.4.27, *ghañi ca bhāvakaraṇayoḥ*, there is the elision of the nasal (*n*) of the root *rañj*. Thus, *rāgaḥ* ("coloring" or "attachment"). Why [specify] "in these two" (*anayoḥ*)? [Because otherwise it would apply to other meanings too, e.g.,] *raṅgaḥ* ("a stage"), which is that in which one colors (*rajyati*). *Prāsaḥ* ("a throw") is derived from *prasyate* ("it is thrown"). The rule *saṃjñāyām* ("when it is a name") is merely illustrative (*prāyika*). For example: *kva bhavatā lābho labdhaḥ?* ("Where was the profit obtained by you?"). From this point onward, until the rule *kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam* (A 3.3.113), both [the conditions] "in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*)" and "when the agent is not the subject (*akartari kārake*)" continue to apply.

SK 3190: After all [roots], when expressing a measure (*parimāṇa*), the suffix *ghañ* is applied (A 3.3.20). This is for the purpose of superseding *ap* and *ac*. Examples: *ekaḥ taṇḍulanicāyaḥ* ("one heap of rice"), *dvau śūrpaniṣpāvau* ("two winnowings with a winnowing-basket"), *dvau kārau* ("two acts"). In the case of *dāra-* and *jāra-*, the suffix *ṇil* is applied in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*). *Dāra-* is derived from the sense "he cleaves" (*dārayati*), hence "wife. *Jāra-* is derived from the sense "he causes to age" (*jārayanti*), hence "lover. SK 3191: Also after the root *iṅ* (to study). (A 3.3.21)

The suffix *ghañ* is an exception (*apavāda*) to [the rule for] vowels (*acaḥ*). One studies from this person, thus he is an *upādhyāya* (teacher). There is an extension (*upasaṃkhyānam*) of this [suffix] to denote the feminine when expressing the ablative (*apādāne*), and optionally the suffix *ṅīṣ* after a word ending in that [suffix]. Thus: *upādhyāyā* or *upādhyāyī*. Regarding the root *śṝ* in the senses of wind, color, and covering: the mention of *śṝ* is without case endings (*avibhaktikaḥ*). *Śāraḥ* as wind: here the suffix *ghañ* is used in the sense of the instrument (*karaṇe*). *Śāraḥ* as color: the meaning of the verbal root (*dhātvarthaḥ*) here is "making variegated" (*citrikaraṇam*). *Nivṛtam* means "that by which one is covered" (*āvriyate*); it refers to a covering (*āvaraṇam*). By virtue of the principle of multiplicity (*bāhulakāt*), the suffix *kta* is used here in the sense of the instrument. "As one who has not made a *nīśāra* (covering/wind) like a cow, generally emaciated in the cold season"—this means "one who has not made a covering (*akṛtaprāvaraṇaḥ*)."
SK 3192: After the prefix *upa*, the root *ru* takes the suffix *ghañ* [to form a noun]. Example: *saṃrāvaḥ*. Why "after a prefix"? [Counter-example: *ravaḥ*. SK 3193:
After the prefixes *abhi* and *niṣ*, the word *stana* [takes *ṣatva*] when it denotes a sound. (A 8.3.86)

After this [prefix] *sam*, the dental *s* of the roots *stan* and *ru* becomes a cerebral (*mūrdhanya*) retroflex stop (*abhiniṣṭāna*). Why is it said "in the context of grammatical terminology" (*śabda-saṃjñāyām*)? [Because otherwise: the drum *abhiniḥstanati*.

Regarding *saṃ-yat-ru-du-vaḥ* (A 3.3.23): *saṃyāvaḥ* means that which is mixed (*miśrīkriyate*) with molasses and other ingredients; it is a specific kind of cake (*apūpa*) made from flour. *Saṃdrāvaḥ*; *saṃdāvaḥ*.

SK 3195: *śrīṇībhuvo ’nupasarge* (A 3.3.24). [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the roots] *śri*, *ni*, and *bhū* when no prefix (*anupasarga*) is present. Examples: *śrāyaḥ*, *nāyaḥ*, *bhāvaḥ*. Why does it say "when no prefix is present"? Consider: *praśrayaḥ*, *praṇayaḥ*, *prabhavaḥ*. How is it that *prabhāvaḥ* is used in the sense of "the power of a king"? It is a *prādi-samāsa* (prepositional compound) meaning "excellent power" (*prakṛṣṭo bhāvaḥ*). How is it that *rājño nayaḥ* ("the policy of the king") is formed? It is due to the rule of "diversity" (*bāhulakāt*). SK 3196: *vau kṣuśruvaḥ* (A 3.3.25). [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the roots] *kṣu* and *śru* when the prefix *vi-* is present.

*vikṣāvaḥ* / *viśrāvaḥ*. Why [is the suffix] not used in *vau*? [Answer: *kṣavaḥ*, *śravaḥ*. (Pāṇini 3.3.26: *avador niyaḥ*) *avanāyaḥ* means leading downward; *unnāyaḥ* means leading upward. How is it that *unnayaḥ* means "imagination" (*utprekṣā*)? [It is so] by virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulakāt*).
SK 3198: *pra* [is used] before *drū*, *stū*, and *srū* (A 3.3.27). Examples: *pradrāvaḥ*, *prastāvaḥ*, *prasrāvaḥ*. Why say *pra*? [Counter-examples: *dravaḥ*, *stavaḥ*, *sravaḥ*. SK 3199:
*ni* and *abhi* [are used] before *pū* and *lū* (A 3.3.28).

*Niṣpāva* is a specific type of grain so called because it is winnowed by means of a winnowing basket (*śūrpa*) and the like; it is a threshing (*abhilāva*). Why [is the prefix] *ni-* and *abhi-* mentioned? [Consider: *pavaḥ*, *lavaḥ*.
By rule A 3.3.29, *gra-* follows *ut-* and *ni-*:
*udgāraḥ* (eructation), *nigāraḥ* (swallowing). Why [are] *ut-* and *ni-* mentioned? [Consider: *garaḥ* (poison).

SK 3201: *kṛ* in the sense of grain (A 3.3.30). After the root *kṛ*, when it refers to grain, the suffix *ghañ* shall be applied to *ut* and *ni*. Examples: *utkāraḥ* and *nikāraḥ* of grain; the meaning is "scattering. Why "in the sense of grain"? [Counter-examples: *bhikṣotkaraḥ* (a heap of alms); *puṣpanikaraḥ* (a cluster of flowers). SK 3202: *yajñe sami stuvaḥ* (A 3.3.31). [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *stu* with the prefix *sam* in the context of a sacrifice.]
The place where the *chandoga* singers assemble and praise is called *saṃstāva*. What about [the word] *saṃstava* in the context of a sacrifice? It means familiarity or acquaintance.

Regarding the rule *pra-stro ’yajñe* (A 3.3.32), the analysis is *ayajñe* (not in a sacrifice); since "in a sacrifice" (*yajñe*) is the subject under discussion, it follows that [the suffix *ghañ* applies] when it is not a sacrifice. Thus we have *prastāra*. Why "not in a sacrifice"? Because in a sacrifice, *barhiṣaḥ prastaraḥ* refers to a specific handful of sacrificial grass.

Pāṇini 3.3.33: *prathane vāvaśabde* (A 3.3.33). The suffix *ghañ* occurs after the root *stṛ* preceded by the prefix *vi-* when it denotes expansion (*prathana*) that does not involve sound (*aśabda*). Example: *paṭasya vistāraḥ* ("the expansion of a cloth"). Why "when denoting expansion"? Counter-example: *tṛṇavistaraḥ* ("a spreading of grass"). Why "not involving sound"? Counter-example: *granthavistaraḥ* ("an extensive treatise"). Pāṇini 3.3.34: *chandonāmni ca* (A 3.3.34). [The suffix *ghañ* occurs after the root *stṛ* preceded by *vi-*] also when the word is the name of a meter (*chandas*). [Example: *vistaracchandaḥ* ("a wide meter").]

The word *sra* is understood [from the previous rule]. *Viṣṭārapaṅkti* is the name of a metre (*chandas*). [The term is derived as follows: the suffix *ghañ* is applied in the locative sense (*adhikaraṇe*) to the root *stṛ* preceded by the prefix *vi*, based on the sense "in this [metre] syllables are spread out" (*vistīryante*). Then, a *karmadhāraya* compound is formed. Regarding the rule *chandonāmni ca* (Pāṇini A 8.3.94): "In the name of a metre, there shall be the substitution of *ṣ* for the *s* of the root *stṛ* preceded by *vi* when ending in *ghañ*. Thus, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs.
SK 3207: *ud* [is used] before *graha-* (A 3.3.35);
*udgrāhaḥ*. SK 3208: *sam* [is used] before *muṣṭi-* (A 3.3.36).

The grasping of a wrestler; what about the grasping of a fist? The gathering of goods. (A 3.3.37) *Ghañ* shall be applied after *nī* preceded by *pari*, and after *iṇ* preceded by *ni*, respectively, in the senses of gambling and non-deviation. *Pariṇāyena śārān hanti*: "He strikes the dice with a complete leading. The meaning is "by leading them all around. *Eṣo 'tra nyāyaḥ*: "This is the proper course here"; the meaning is "what is appropriate. Why say "in the senses of gambling and non-deviation"? [Otherwise: *pariṇayaḥ* = marriage; *nyayaḥ* = destruction.

SK 3210: *parāv anupātyaya iṇaḥ* (A 3.3.38). *Anupātyayaḥ* means not passing over (*anatipātaḥ*) that which has arrived in its proper sequence (*krama-prāptasya*). [Example: *tava paryāyaḥ* ("It is your turn"). Why say "in the sense of non-passing over"? [Counter-example: *kālasya paryayaḥ* ("the lapse of time"); the meaning here is "passing over" (*atipātaḥ*). SK 3211: *vyupayoḥ śeteḥ paryāye* (A 3.3.39). [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *śī* when preceded by *vi-* or *upa-*, in the sense of "turn" (*paryāya*).]

*viśāyaḥ* [is formed] from *viśayaḥ*; *rājopaśāyaḥ* from *rājopaśayaḥ*. Why [is the rule] not applied in the following cases? *viśayaḥ* means "doubt"; *upaśayaḥ* means "sleeping nearby. (SK 3212) *Hastādāne cer asteye* (A 3.3.40).

By the term *hastādāne* ("taking with the hand"), close proximity to the object to be taken is indicated. Examples: *puṣpapracāyaḥ* ("gathering flowers"). Why [is it] "taking with the hand"? [Answer: He gathers fruits situated at the top of a tree using a stick. Why "not involving theft"? [Answer: Gathering flowers by means of theft.

SK 3213: *nivāsa-citi-śārīra-upasamādhāneṣv ādeś ca kaḥ* (A 3.3.41). In these cases, the suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *ci*, and the letter *k* is substituted for the initial [of the root]. "Piling up" (*upasamādhāna*) means forming a heap, and that is the meaning of the verbal root itself. The others are qualifiers (*upādhi*) of the *kāraka* which is the meaning of the suffix. In the sense of "dwelling" (*nivāsa*): *kāśī-nikāyaḥ* ("the settlement in Kāśī"). In the sense of "piling" (*citi*): *ākāyam agniṃ cinvīta* ("one should pile the fire-altar up to the sky"). In the sense of "body" (*śarīra*): *kāyaḥ* ("body"), because bones and so forth are piled up (*cīyate*) in it. In the sense of "collection" (*samūha*): *gomaya-nikāyaḥ* ("a heap of cow dung"). Why is this rule restricted to these cases? [Answer: Because of the example *cayaḥ* ("a heap"). Since one could have simply stated *caḥ kaḥ* ("*k* is substituted for *c*"), the statement *ādeḥ* ("for the initial") is made so that the substitution occurs only for the initial [consonant] even in the case of the elision of the *yaṅ* suffix (*yaṅ-luk*). For example: *cekiti* (from *ceketi*).

*Nikecāyaḥ* means the repeated piling up of cow-dung; that is, the act of heaping it again and again. [Pāṇini 3.3.42] states: *saṅghe cānauttarādharye cer ghañ ādeś ca kaḥ*. [The suffix] *ghañ* is applied after the root *ci* when referring to a *saṅgha* (an assemblage), provided there is no vertical superposition (*anauttarādharye*), and the initial *c* is replaced by *k*. Examples include *bhikṣunikāyaḥ* (the community of monks). A *saṅgha* is a collection of living beings. Why "provided there is no vertical superposition"? Consider *sūkaranicayaḥ* (a heap of pigs), where they are piled one above another. Why "when referring to a *saṅgha*"? Consider *jñānakarmasamuccayaḥ* (the accumulation of knowledge and action), which refers to a collection rather than a single unified body.
SK 3215: In the sense of reciprocal action, the suffix *ṇac* is applied in the feminine;
that is, when the action is expressed in the feminine gender, the suffix *ṇac* is used.
SK 3216: *ṇacaḥ striyām añ* (A 5.4.14). SK 3217: *na karmavyatihāre* (A 7.3.6). In this case, the vowels *ai* and *au* (*aic*) shall not occur. Examples: *vyāvakrośī*, *vyāvahāsī*.
SK 3218: The suffix *inuṇ* occurs after a verbal root in the sense of "pervasion" (*abhividhi*).

SK 3219: The suffixes *aṇ* and *inuṇ* [are elided] before a secondary derivative suffix (*taddhita*) that does not denote lineage (*anapatya*), provided it begins with the suffix *ina*. It exists as a pervasive sound (*sāṃrāviṇam*).

SK 3220: *ākrośe 'vanyor grahaḥ* (A 3.3.45). After the prefixes *ava* and *ni*, the suffix *ghañ* is applied to the root *grah* when expressing a curse (*ākrośe*). *avagrāhas te bhūyāt*: "May you suffer defeat"; the meaning is "overpowering. *nigrāhas te bhūyāt*: "May you suffer restraint"; the meaning is "affliction. Why "when expressing a curse"? [Consider: *avagrahaḥ padasya* ("the pause between words") and *nigrahaś corasya* ("the arrest of a thief"). SK 3221: *pre lipsāyām* (A 3.3.46). [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the prefix *pra* to the root *grah*] when expressing a desire for gain (*lipsāyām*).
The monk moves about with the alms-bowl as his support.
According to *Pāṇini* 3.3.47, *parigraha* in the sense of "sacrifice for another" refers to the northern enclosure; it is the taking possession of the sacrificial altar by means of a hawk.

SK 3223: *nau vṛ dhānye* (A 3.3.48). The word *vṛ* here has its fifth case ending elided. Examples: *nīvārāḥ* ("wild rice"). Why "in the sense of grain" (*dhānye*)? Counter-example: *nivarā kanyā* ("a girl who does not choose [her own husband]"). Even though this falls under the domain of the suffix *ktin*, the suffix *ap* is applied by virtue of the rule's broad application (*bāhulakāt*). This is like the word *pravarā* [which means "excellent"] despite being formed with *seti*.
SK 3224: *udi śrayatiyautipūdruvaḥ* (A 3.3.49). [The suffix *ap* is applied after the roots *śri*, *yu*, *pū*, and *dru* when preceded by the prefix *ud*.]
*ucchrāyaḥ*, *udyāvaḥ*, *utpāvaḥ*, *udrāvaḥ*. How is it that "elevations end in falling"? By virtue of the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*). [SK 3225] *ave graho varṣapratibandhe* (A 3.3.51).
The word "optionally" (*vibhāṣā*) carries over. *avagrahaḥ*, *avagrāhaḥ*. Why "in the sense of obstructing rain"? [Answer: *avagrahaḥ padasya* ("the separation of a word").
SK 3227: *pra-vaṇijām* (A 3.3.52).

After the root *grah*, the suffix *ghañ* is optionally applied when the meaning of the suffix refers to merchants (*vaṇij*). This refers, in effect, to the balance-string (*tulāsūtra*). [Examples: *tulāpragrāheṇa carati* ("he moves with the balance-string"), *tulāpragraheṇa*. SK 3228: *raśmau ca* (A 3.3.53). [The suffix *ghañ* is also applied after *grah*] when the sense is "reins. [Example: *tulāpragrāhaḥ* ("the reins of the balance").
*pragrahaḥ* / *pragrāhaḥ*. According to A 3.3.54, after the root *vṛṇoti* in the sense of "covering," there is optionally [the substitution of *pra*] for *pra*; thus: *prāvāraḥ* / *pravaraḥ*.

SK 3230: After the root *bhū* (to be), when preceded by *pari*, [the suffix *ghañ* is applied] in the sense of "disregard" (*avajñāna*). Examples: *paribhāvaḥ*, *paribhavaḥ*. Why "in the sense of disregard"? [Counter-example: *paribhavaḥ* as "being on all sides" (*sarvato bhavanam*). SK 3231:
After a verbal root ending in *i*, [the suffix *ac* is applied].

The addition of *cayaḥ* and *jayaḥ* [to the list] is for the purpose of including words such as *bhaya* (fear) and others, in order to exclude the suffix *kta* and others when used in the neuter gender: *bhayam*, *varṣam*. SK 3232: *ṛdor ap* (A 3.3.57).
The suffix *ap* is applied after verbal roots ending in an *ṛ*-vowel or an *u*-vowel: *karaḥ*, *garaḥ*, *śaraḥ*, *yavaḥ*, *lavaḥ*, *stavaḥ*, *pavaḥ*.

SK 3233: *viṣṭaraḥ* is [the form] for *vṛkṣa* and *āsana*. (A 8.3.93) The substitution of *ṣ* for the *s* of the root *sṛ* preceded by *vi-* is prescribed as a *nipātana* (irregular formation) when these two [words] follow: *viṣṭaraḥ* means a tree and a seat. Why "tree"? [Counter-example: the expansion (*vistaraḥ*) of a sentence. SK 3234: *grah*, *vṛ*, *dṛ*, *niści*, *gam*, and [the root *ci*] also [take *iṣṇuc*]. (A 3.3.58)

The suffix *ap* shall be applied [after roots ending in long vowels]. It is an exception to the rules for *ghañ* and *ac*. Examples: *grahaḥ*, *varaḥ*, *daraḥ*, *niścayaḥ*, *gamaḥ*. An addition should be made for the roots *vaś* and *raṇ*: *vaśaḥ*, *raṇaḥ*. The suffix *ka* is prescribed in the sense of *ghañ*. Examples: *prasthaḥ*, *vighnaḥ*. In the section on reduplication (*dvitva*), it should be stated that *ka* is added after *kṛñ* and others: *cakram*, *ciklidam*, *caknasaḥ*. According to A 3.3.59, *ap* shall be applied after the root *ad* when a prefix (*upasarga*) precedes.

SK 3236: *ghañapoś ca* (A 2.4.38). After the root *ad*, there shall be *ghas* before the suffixes *ghañ* and *ap*. Examples: *praghasaḥ* (devouring), *vighasaḥ* (remnants of food). Why [is it said] "when preceded by a prefix"? [Counter-example: *ghāsaḥ* (grass/fodder). SK 3237: *nau ṇa ca* (A 3.3.60). [The suffix *ap* is added after the root *ad* when preceded by the prefix *ni*, and the substitute *ṇa* is applied.]
When nine prefixes (*upapada*) precede the root *ad*, the suffix *ṇa* occurs and *ap* is also applied: *nyādaḥ*, *nighasaḥ*.
(SK 3238) After the roots *vyadh* and *jap*, when no prefix (*anupasarga*) is present, the suffix *ap* occurs:
*vyadhaḥ*, *japaḥ*. However, when a prefix is present, [the suffix *ghañ* applies]: *āvyādhaḥ*, *upajāpaḥ*.
SK 3239: After the roots *svan* and *has*, the suffix *ap* is optionally applied (A 3.3.62).

In the alternative case, the suffix *ghañ* is applied. Thus: *svanaḥ* / *svānaḥ*; *hasaḥ* / *hāsaḥ*. This applies only when there is no preceding prefix (*anupasarge*). For example: *prasvānaḥ* / *prahāsaḥ*. SK 3240: The suffix *ghañ* is also applied after the root *yam* when preceded by the prefixes *sam*, *upa*, *ni*, and *vi* (A 3.3.63).

In these cases, when there is no prefix (*anupasarga*), the suffix *ap* is optionally applied after the root *yam*. Thus: *saṃyamaḥ* or *saṃyāmaḥ*; *upayamaḥ* or *upayāmaḥ*; *niyamaḥ* or *niyāmaḥ*; *viyamaḥ* or *viyāmaḥ*; *yamaḥ* or *yāmaḥ*. According to Pāṇini A 3.3.64, *nau gadanadapaṭhasvanaḥ*, the suffix *ap* is optionally applied after the roots *gad*, *nad*, *paṭh*, and *svan* when preceded by the prefix *ni*. Thus: *nigadaḥ* or *nigādaḥ*; *ninadaḥ* or *ninādaḥ*; *nipaṭhaḥ* or *nipāṭhaḥ*; *nisvanaḥ* or *nisvānaḥ*.

SK 3242 *kvaṇo vīṇāyāṃ ca* (A 3.3.65): After the root *kvaṇ*, when it refers to a lute (*vīṇā*) or when it is not preceded by a prefix (*anupasarga*), the suffix *ap* may optionally occur. The mention of "lute" is for the sake of including cases where prefixes such as *pra-* are present. Thus: *nikvaṇaḥ* or *nikvāṇaḥ*; *kvaṇaḥ* or *kvāṇaḥ*. But when referring specifically to a lute: *prakvaṇaḥ* or *prakvāṇaḥ*. SK 3243 *nityaṃ paṇaḥ parimāṇe* (A 3.3.66): The root *paṇ* always takes the suffix *ap* when it denotes a measure (*parimāṇa*).

It may be *ap* [the suffix -a]. *Mūlakapaṇaḥ* (a handful of radishes); *śākapaṇaḥ* (a handful of vegetables). A measured handful of radishes and the like is tied together for the purpose of trade; that is its scope. Why "in the sense of measure" (*parimāṇe*)? [Counter-example: *pāṇaḥ* (a hand). [From A 3.3.67] *mada* [takes -a] when there is no prefix (*anupasarga*).
*Dhanamadaḥ* (intoxication with wealth). Why "when there is no prefix"? [Counter-example: *unmādaḥ* (insanity).

SK 3245: *pramada* and *saṃmada* [are formed with the suffix *ghañ*] in the sense of joy (*harṣa*). Why "in the sense of joy"? [Answer: *pramādaḥ* (negligence); *saṃmādaḥ* (intoxication). SK 3246: After the prefixes *sam-* and *ud-*, the root *aj* [takes the suffix *ghañ*] in the sense of domestic animals (*paśu*).

The root *aj* preceded by *sam-* denotes a collection (*samudāya*), and preceded by *ut-* denotes impelling (*preraṇa*). From these roots, when they have "animals" (*paśu*) as their object, the suffix *ap* shall be applied. Because it is stated that [the substitution of] *vī* does not occur before *ghan* and *ap*, there is no change to *vī*. Thus, *samajaḥ paśūnām* means "a herd of animals," and *udajaḥ paśūnām* means "the driving away of animals. Why "in reference to animals"? [Consider: *samājaḥ brāhmaṇānām* ("an assembly of Brahmins") and *udājaḥ kṣatriyāṇām* ("the driving out of Kṣatriyas"). SK 3247: *akṣeṣu glahaḥ* (A 3.3.70). [In this case, the suffix *ap* is applied to the root *glah* with the sense of gambling.]

By the word *akṣa*, gambling (*devana*) is indicated. In that context, the form *glaha* is prescribed for that which is to be taken as a stake (*paṇa*). Thus: *akṣasya glahaḥ* ("the stake of the die"). [As in: *vyātyukṣīm abhisaraṇaglahām adīvyan* ("they gambled at mutual splashing and running toward one another as stakes"). Why "of the die" (*akṣeṣu*)? [Counter-example: *pādasya grahaḥ* ("the seizing of the foot"). SK 3248: *prajane sarteḥ* (A 3.3.71). *Prajana* means the first conception of a fetus. [Thus: *gavām upasaraḥ* ("the mating of cows"). How is it that there are forms such as *avasaraḥ* and *prasaraḥ*? [They are formed] with the suffix *gha* by the rule *adhikaraṇe puṃsi saṃjñāyām*.
SK 3249: *ny-abhy-upa-vi-ṣu hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca* (A 3.3.72). [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *hve* preceded by these prefixes, and there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the vowel.

Examples: *nihavaḥ*, *abhihavaḥ*, *upahavaḥ*, *vihavaḥ*. Why [is the rule] not applied here? *prahvāyaḥ*. SK 3250: *āṅi yuddhe* (A 3.3.73). [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *hve* preceded by *āṅ* when it refers to a battle.]

It is called *āhava* because things are summoned (*āhūyante*) therein. What [is the result] in the case of battle? It is *āhvāya*. SK 3251: *nipānamāhāvaḥ* (A 3.3.74). For the root *hvayati* preceded by the prefix *ā*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*), the suffix *ap*, and vṛddhi; furthermore, it should be stated that this refers to a reservoir for water. Thus, *āhāva* is a watering place, a reservoir of water near a well.
SK 3252: *bhāve ’nupasargasya* (A 3.3.75).

For the verb *hvayati* when not preceded by a prefix, there shall be vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) and the substitution of *ap* in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*). [Result: *havaḥ*. SK 3253: *hanaś ca vadhaḥ* (A 3.3.76). And for the verb *han*, [the suffix *ap* is applied] with the substitution of *vadha*.

After the root *han*, when not preceded by a prefix, the suffix *ap* occurs in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*), and there is the substitution of *vadh* which is oxytone (acute on the final syllable), as in *dasyuṃ vadhenā*. And because of the word *ca* [in the rule], the suffix *ghañ* also applies, as in *ghātaḥ*.

SK 3254: *mūrtau ghanaḥ* (A 3.3.77). When "solidity" (*mūrti*) is to be expressed—that is, when it is the object denoted—the suffix *ap* is added to the root *han*, and *ghana* is the substitute [for *han*]. Examples: *abhra-ghanaḥ* ("a dense cloud"). How is it that one says, "bring the *saindhava-ghana*"? [Answer: By means of the word for a property (*dharma*), the possessor of the property (*dharmī*) is indicated. SK 3255: *antarghano deśe* (A 3.3.78). [The suffix *ap* with the substitute *ghana* is added to *han*] when the sense is "a region" (*deśa*).

This is the name for a specific village of the Vāhīkas. *Antarghaṇa* is an alternative reading. According to A 3.3.79, *praghaṇaḥ* and *praghāṇaḥ* refer to a portion of a house. There are two types of vestibules (*alinda*) at the entrance: the inner and the outer. This grammatical derivation applies to the outer vestibule. It is called *praghaṇaḥ* or *praghāṇaḥ* because it is struck (*hanyate*) forcefully (*prakarṣeṇa*) by the feet of people entering. The suffix *ap* is added in the sense of the object (*karman*); in one case, there is vowel strengthening (*vṛddhi*).

SK 3257: *Uddhana* means "placing upon" (*atyādhāna*). Placing upon is the act of setting something on top. That piece of wood upon which other pieces of wood are placed and then carved is called an *uddhana*. [The suffix *ap* is used here] in the sense of the locus (*adhikaraṇa*). SK 3258: *Apaghana* means "limb" (*aṅga*).

*Aṅga* means a limb of the body; and here it is not every limb, but rather they say it refers to the hand and the foot (*pāṇi* and *pāda*). [The suffix] *ap* is used in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇe*). *Apaghāta* is something else. Regarding A 3.3.82, *karaṇe 'yovidruṣu*: after the root *han*, when these—*ayas*, *vi*, and *dru*—are present as the instrument, the suffix *ap* should occur and there is the substitution of *ghan* for the root. *Ayas hanyate 'nena* ("by which iron is struck") = *ayoghanaḥ*. *vighanaḥ*. *drughanaḥ*. Some say *drughaṇaḥ*. The change to *ṇ* occurs by the rule *pūrvapadāt saṃjñāyām*. This is the name of an axe. *Dru* means a tree.

SK 3260 *stambe ka ca* (A 3.3.83): When *stamba* is the upapada, the suffix *ka* shall be applied to the root *han*, with *ap* as the substitute [for the final vowel] optionally; and in the alternative, there is the substitution of *ghan*. Thus: *stambaghnaḥ* and *stambaghanaḥ*. Only when it is the instrument (*karaṇa*) [is this rule applied]; otherwise: *stambaghātaḥ*. SK 3261 *parau ghaḥ* (A 3.3.84).

In the case of the root *han*, the suffix *gha* should occur after the prefix *pari*, and the letter *gh* is the substitute for the final phoneme of the root. That by which one strikes around (*parihanyate*) is called a *parigha*. According to Pāṇini 8.2.22, *pareś ca ghāṅkayoḥ*, the letter *l* optionally replaces the *r* of *pari* before the words *gha* and *aṅka*. Thus we have *palighaḥ* and *parighaḥ*; likewise, *paryaṅkaḥ* and *palyaṅkaḥ*. In this context, in the rule *taraptamapau ghaḥ*, there is no reference to the technical grammatical suffix *gha*, because that is determined by the specific interpretation of the commentary.

SK 3263 *upaghna āśraye* (A 3.3.85): After the root *han* preceded by the prefix *upa*, the suffix *ap* is added, and there is elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-lopa*). By the word *āśraya*, proximity (*sāmīpya*) is indicated. That which is struck [or approached] by a mountain due to its proximity is called *parvatopaghna*.
SK 3264 *saṅghoddhau gaṇapraśaṃsayoḥ* (A 3.3.86): [The suffix *ap* is added after the root *han* preceded by *sam* and *ud* respectively, when the meanings are "multitude" and "praise"].

*Saṃhananam* is the *saṅgha* (the community); the suffix *ap* is used here in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*). It is called *uddha* because it is "thrust up" or known as preeminent; the suffix *ap* is used here in the sense of an object (*karman*). Since roots meaning "to go" also mean "to understand," the root *han* is used here in the sense of "knowing. *Nigho nimittam* (A 3.3.87): that which is measured all around is a *nimitta* (a cause or mark). Trees are called *nighāḥ* because they are struck (*hanyante*) without distinction [in their measurement]; the meaning is that they possess equal height and circumference.

SK 3266: *ḍvitaḥ ktriḥ* (A 3.3.88). This [suffix] *ktri* occurs only in the sense of abstract state (*bhāva*), by its very nature. Because of the explicit mention of "always" (*nityam*) [in the rule], *ktri* is restricted to the domain of the suffix *mam*. For this very reason, the analysis is made with a *kyanta* form. From the root *ḍupacaṣ*: *pākena nirvṛttam* = *paktrimam*. From *ḍuvap*: *uptrimam*. SK 3267: *ḍvito 'thuc* (A 3.3.89). [The suffix *athuc* is added after roots ending in *ḍu* or having an indicatory *i*].
This too is indeed a *bhāva* [abstract action] by its very nature. [From the root] *ṭuvepṛ*: *vepathuḥ* (trembling), *śvayathuḥ* (swelling).
By A 3.3.90, *yaj*, *yāc*, *yat*, *vicch*, *pracch*, and *rakṣ* take the suffix *naṅ*:

*yajñaḥ* (sacrifice), *yācñā* (begging), *yatnaḥ* (effort), *viśnaḥ* (penetration), *praśnaḥ* (question). Regarding *praśnaḥ*, there is no *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization) because of the *jñāpaka* (indicative evidence) in the rule *praśne cāsanne*. However, the *ṅit*-designation is for the purpose of prohibiting *guṇa* in the case of *viśnaḥ*. [From *rakṣ*: *rakṣṇaḥ* (protection).

SK 3269: By [Pāṇini 3.3.91] *svapo nan*, the word *svapnaḥ* is formed. SK 3270: By [Pāṇini 3.3.92] *upasarge ghoḥ kiḥ*, [the suffix *ki* is applied after verbal roots ending in *ghu* when a prefix is present].

*pradhiḥ*, *antardhiḥ*. That by which something is placed near (*upādhīyate*) is called an *upādhi*. According to Pāṇini 3.3.93, when a word denoting an object (*karman*) is used as a subordinate term (*upapada*), the suffix *ki* is applied to the root *dhā* in the sense of a locus (*adhikaraṇa*). Thus, "that in which waters are placed" is *jaladhiḥ* ("ocean").

SK 3272: *striyāṃ ktin* (A 3.3.94). In the feminine gender, *ktin* shall occur after verbal roots in the sense of abstract action (*bhāva*) and so forth; it is an exception to *ghañ*. However, *ap* and *ac* supersede it due to their higher status [in the order of rules]. Examples: *kṛtiḥ*, *citiḥ*, *stutiḥ*. From *sphāyī*: *sphātiḥ*. The form *sphītikāmaḥ*, however, is a mere error. [The formation] from a root ending in *kta* in the sense of the root-meaning itself, with the addition of *ṇic*, can be explained either by the rule *aca ir* [Pāṇini 7.1.100] or otherwise. [The suffix *ktin* occurs] after the roots *śru*, *yaj*, *iṣ*, and *stu* in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇa*). From *śru*: that by which something is heard is *śrutiḥ*. From *yaj* and *iṣ*: *iṣṭiḥ*. From *stu*: *stutiḥ*. It should be stated that after roots beginning with *ṛ* and *l*, *ktin* is treated like *niṣṭhā* (the past passive participle suffixes *kta* and *ktavat*). By this, the substitution of *n* for *ṇ* occurs: *kīrṇaḥ*, *gīrṇaḥ*.

*lūniḥ*, *dhūniḥ*, *pūniḥ*, and *hlādaḥ*—the short vowel [of the root] occurs before the suffix *ktin* due to a division of the rule (*yogavibhāga*). *prahlanniḥ*. And with the suffix *ti*: *cūrtiḥ*, *phultiḥ*. It should be stated that for the root *cāyati*, there is a substitution of *ci* when *ktin* follows: *apacitiḥ*. From roots such as *sampad*, the suffix *kvip* is applied: *sampat*, *vipat*. The suffix *ktin* is also desired: *saṃpattiḥ*, *vipattiḥ*. (SK 3273) After the roots *sthā*, *gā*, *pā*, and *pac*, the suffix *ktin* occurs in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāve*), as an exception to [the application of] *aṅ*. *prasthitiḥ*, *upasthitiḥ*, *saṅgītiḥ*, *saṃpītiḥ*, *paktiḥ*. How is it that *avasthā* and *saṃsthā* are formed? Because of the indicator (*jñāpaka*) that [the rule applies] in the sense of "establishment" (*vyavasthāyām*).

SK 3274: *ūti*, *yūti*, *jūti*, *sāti*, *heti*, and *kīrti* [are derived with the suffix *ktin*]. From the root *av*, by the rule *jvaratvara-* etc., the substitution *ūṭh* occurs, resulting in *ūtiḥ*. This statement is for the sake of the accent; for the term "udātta" is understood [from the previous rule]. *Yūtiḥ* and *jūtiḥ*: here, the lengthening of the vowel is also prescribed as an irregularity (*nipātana*). *Sātiḥ* is from the root *sā* (*syati*); although the substitution of *it* would have applied by the rule *dyatisyati-* etc., the absence of that *it* is prescribed as an irregularity. Alternatively, if the substitution of *āt* had occurred by the rule *janasana-* etc. from the root *san*, this *nipātana* is for the sake of the accent. *Hetiḥ* is from either the root *han* or *hi*. *Kīrtiḥ*. SK 3275:
After the roots *vraj* and *yaj*, the suffix *kyap* is used in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*).
Vrajyā; ijyā.

According to A 3.3.99: "The suffix kyap is applied after the roots *samaj*, *niṣad*, *nipat*, *man*, *vid*, *uṣ*, *vi*, *śīṅ*, *bhṛ*, and *iṇ* when a specific technical name (*saṃjñā*) is to be expressed."

The suffix *kyap* occurs after the roots *samaj* and others to form feminine nouns expressing an abstract state (*bhāva*) or similar meanings; this suffix is udātta when used as a technical name (*saṃjñā*). It should be stated that there is no substitution of *vī* for the root *aj* when *kyap* follows. *Samajyā*: "a gathering" or "an assembly," because people gather (*samajanti*) therein. *Niṣadyā*: "a shop," because people sit down (*niṣīdanti*) therein. *Nipatyā*: "slippery ground," because people fall down (*nipatanti*) upon it. *Manyā*: "the carotid artery," because one perceives (*manyate*) by means of it. *Vidyā*: "knowledge," because one knows (*vidanti*) by means of it. *Sutyā*: "the act of pressing [Soma]. *Śayyā*: "a bed. *Āśibikā*: "a palanquin," because one goes (*īyate*) by means of it. By A 3.2.100, the suffix *śa* also occurs after the root *kṛ*. (SK 3277)

There is a separation of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) after *kṛñaḥ*: the suffix *kyaP* may occur after the root *kṛ*. [Thus] *kṛtyā*. And [the suffix] *śa* [may occur]; because of the word "and" (*ca*), [the suffix] *ktin* [is also included]. [Thus] *kriyā*, *kṛtiḥ*. SK 3278: *icchā* (A 3.3.101).

The suffix *śa* is prescribed for the root *īṣ* (to desire) in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāve*), and the *ya*-affix is also elided by nipātana. Thus, *icchā*. There is an addition to the rule regarding *paricaryā*, *parisaryā*, *mṛgayā*, and *aṭāṭyā*. Here, the suffix *śa* and the *ya*-affix are applied, and the *guṇa* substitution also occurs. *Paricaryā* means worship; *parisaryā* means wandering around; here too, the *guṇa* substitution takes place. The root *mṛg* (to search) belongs to the *curādi* class and ends in a long vowel (*adanta*). Therefore, there is no elision of the final vowel. With the suffix *śa* and the *ya*-affix, the *ṇi*-augment is elided: *mṛgayā*. From the root *aṭ* (to wander), with the suffix *śa* and the *ya*-affix, the syllable *ṭya* is reduplicated, the *ya* in the preceding portion is removed, and a long vowel is substituted: *aṭāṭyā*. For the root *jāgṛ* (to wake), the suffix *a* is optionally used. In the alternative case, the suffix *śa* is used. Thus, *jāgarā* or *jāgaryā*.
SK 3279 *a-pratyayāt* (A 3.3.102):
The suffix *a* shall be applied in the feminine to verbal roots ending in a suffix. Examples: *cikīrṣā* (the desire to act), *putrakāmyā* (the desire for a son).
SK 3280 *guroś ca halaḥ* (A 3.3.103): [The suffix *a* is also applied] after a verbal root ending in a consonant that has a heavy vowel (*guru*).

After a verbal root ending in a consonant that has a heavy vowel (*guru*), the suffix *a* is used in the feminine. Examples: *īhā*, *ūhā*. Why "after a heavy vowel" (*guroḥ*)? Consider *bhaktiḥ*. Why "after a consonant" (*halaḥ*)? Consider *nītiḥ*. It should be stated that this applies when the past passive participle suffix (*niṣṭhā*) is *seṭ* (bearing an *iṭ* augment). Thus, it does not apply here: *āptiḥ* (where *iṭ* is absent by the rule *titutra-*, etc.). *dīptiḥ* (where *iṭ* is absent by the same rule). It should be stated that for roots beginning with *grah*, etc., [the addition of *iṭ*] is optional in the case of *titutratra-*; thus: *nigṛhītiḥ* or *nigrahitiḥ*, *nipaṭhitiḥ* or *nipaṭhatiḥ*. SK 3281: The suffix *aṅ* is applied after roots ending in *ṣit* and after the group beginning with *bhid*. (A 3.3.104)

The suffix *aṅ* is applied after verbal roots ending in *ṣit* and after those beginning with *bhī* when forming feminine nouns. Regarding the root *jṝṣ*: there is *guṇa* substitution for *ṛ* and *ṛt* before the suffix *aṅ*. Thus, *jarā* ("old age"). Regarding the root *trapūṣ*: *trapā* ("shame"). Regarding the root *bhid*: *bhidā* ("splitting"); this [root] is restricted to the sense of "tearing apart. *Bhitti* ("wall") is something else. Regarding the root *chid*: *chidā* ("cutting"). Regarding the root *mṛj*: *mṛjā* ("cleansing"). Regarding the root *kṛp*: there is also *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization). Thus, *kṛpā* ("compassion"). By rule A 3.3.105, *cintipūjikathikumbicarcaś ca*, the suffix *aṅ* is applied after the roots *cinti*, *pūji*, *kathi*, *kumbi*, and *carci*; it is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *yuc*. Thus: *cintā*, *pūjā*, *kathā*, *kumbā*, *carcā*.

SK 3283 (*ātaś copasarge*, A 3.3.106): After a verbal root ending in long *ā*, the suffix *aṅ* shall be applied when a prefix (*upasarga*) precedes. This is an exception to the suffix *ktin*. Examples: *pradā*, *upadā*. The words *śrat* and *antar* function like prefixes (*upasarga*). Examples: *śraddhā*, *antardhā*. By the rule "after a prefix, the root *dhā* takes *ki*," the suffix *ki* is applied. Example: *antardhiḥ*. SK 3284 (*ṇyāsaśrantho 'yuc*, A 3.3.107): After roots ending in the causative marker *ṇi*, as well as the roots *ās* and *śranth*, the suffix *ayuc* is applied.

This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *a*. [The following forms are derived with the suffix *ana*: *kāraṇā*, *hāraṇā*, *āsanā*, *śranthā*. It should be stated that [the suffix *ana* is applied] after the roots *ghaṭṭi*, *vand*, and *vid*: *ghaṭṭanā*, *vandanā*, *vedanā*. After the root *iṣ* when it does not mean "desire," [the suffix *ana* is applied]: *anveṣaṇā*. Optionally after *pari*: *paryeṣaṇā*; [also] *parīṣṭiḥ*. A 3.3.108: "In the case of naming a disease, the suffix *ṇvul* is applied diversely. (*rogākhyāyāṃ ṇvul bahulam*).

*pracchardikā*, *pravāhikā*, *vicarcikā*; in some places not: *śirortiḥ*. The suffix *ṇvul* should be stated [after roots] when indicating the meaning of the verbal root (*dhātvartha*): *āsikā*, *śāyikā*. The suffixes *ik* and *tip* are used when indicating a verbal root: *paciḥ*, *pacatiḥ*. The suffix *kāra* is used after a phoneme (*varṇa*); "when indicating" applies here as well: *akāraḥ*, *kakāraḥ*, *rādiphaḥ*, *rephaḥ*. The suffix *cha* is used after a word expressing possession (*matvartha*); due to the rule of diversity (*bahulavacana*), there is elision of the final vowel *a*: *matvarthīyaḥ*. [The suffix] *iṇ* is used after words beginning with *āj*: *ājiḥ*, *ātiḥ*. [The suffix] *iñ* is used after words beginning with *vāp*: *vāpiḥ*, *vāsiḥ*; there is a difference in accent. The suffix *ik* is used after words beginning with *kṛṣ*: *kṛṣiḥ*, *giriḥ*.
SK 3286 *saṃjñāyām* (A 3.3.109): In this case, the suffix *ṇvul* is applied to the verbal root [to form a name]. Example: *uddālakapuṣpabhañjikā*.
SK 3287 *vibhāṣākhyātaparipraśnayor iñ ca* (A 3.3.110): Optionally, when used for the purpose of asking a question, the suffix *iñ* is also applied [along with *ṇvul*].

When an inquiry or a narration is intended, the suffix *iñ* shall be used, and optionally *ṇvul*; because of the statement "optionally" (*vibhāṣā*), others [suffixes] also occur as prescribed. For example: "What action (*kāriṃ*, *kārikāṃ*, *kriyāṃ*, *kṛtyāṃ*, or *kṛtiṃ*) did you perform? "I performed every action (*sarvāṃ kāriṃ*, *kārikāṃ*, *kriyāṃ*, *kṛtyāṃ*, or *kṛtiṃ*). Similarly: *gaṇiṃ*, *gaṇikāṃ*, *gaṇanām*; *pāciṃ*, *pācikāṃ*, *pacāṃ*, *paktim*. [Pāṇini 3.3.111:
The suffix *ṇvuc* is used in the senses of turn (*paryāya*), worthiness (*arhaṇa*), and production (*utpatti*).

*paryāya* means sequence or order; *arhaṇa*, *arha*, and *yogyatā* mean fitness or worthiness. When these meanings such as *paryāya* are to be expressed, the suffix *ṇvuc* may optionally be used. Examples: *bhavata āsikā* (the turn of your sitting), *śāyikā* (the turn of your lying down), *agragāmikā* (the turn of going first). *Bhavān ikṣubhakṣikām arhati* (Your honor is worthy of eating sugarcane). Regarding debt: *ikṣubhakṣikāṃ me dhārayati* (He owes me the debt of eating sugarcane). Regarding occurrence: *ikṣubhakṣikā upapādi* (The occasion for eating sugarcane arose).
