The term *vibhāṣā* ("optionally") is no longer in force. When the negative particle *nañ* is present as an upapada, the suffix *ani* shall be used in the sense of abuse (*ākrośa*). Example: *ajīvaniḥ te śaṭha bhūyāt* ("May you, O rogue, be one who does not live!"). *Āprayāṇiḥ*. The rule *kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam bhāve 'kartari ca kārake saṃjñāyām* is also no longer in force. Example: *rājabhojanāḥ śālayaḥ* ("rice grains eaten by the king"). The suffix *kta* is used in the neuter gender to denote the abstract action (*bhāva*). [Rule A 3.3.114]. And the suffix *lyuṭ* [is also used in this sense]: *hasitam*, *hasanam*. The separation of the sūtra (*yogavibhāga*) is for the sake of what follows.

SK 3291: *karmaṇi ca yena saṃsparśāt kartuḥ śarīrasukham* (A 3.3.116). When there is an object (*karman*) by contact with which pleasure arises for the body of the agent (*kartṛ*), the suffix *lyuṭ* (forming an action noun) may be applied when that object is used as an upapada. Although this is already established by the preceding rule [A 3.3.115], this statement is made for the sake of ensuring a compulsory compound (*nityasamāsa*). Example: *payaḥpānaṃ sukham* ("the drinking of milk is pleasant"). Why say "for the agent" (*kartari*)? Consider: *guroḥ snāpanaṃ sukham* ("bathing the teacher is pleasant"). Here, the teacher is not the agent but the object (*karman*). SK 3292: *vā yau* (A 2.4.57). [The final vowel of the first member is optionally long before a word ending in the suffix *yu*.]
The root *aj* may optionally take the substitution *vī* when followed by the suffix *ya*. Examples: *pravayaṇa*, *prājanana*.

By A 3.3.117, *lyuṭ* occurs after [roots] denoting an instrument (*karaṇa*) or a locus (*adhikaraṇa*). Examples: *idhmapravraścanaḥ kuṭhāraḥ* ("an axe for cutting firewood"), *godohanī sthālī* ("a milk-pail"). The section beginning with "the suffix *khal* occurs before [suffixes expressing] instrument and locus" is the governing rule (*adhikāra*).

SK 3294 (A 8.4.24): *antaradeśe* / After the word *antaḥ*, the *ṇ* should replace the *n* of the root *han*. Examples: *antarhaṇanam* ("killing within"). However, when referring to a place (*deśa*), it is *antarhananaḥ deśaḥ* ("a place where killing occurs"). [This rule applies] only when preceded by *at* (short *a*). Example: *antarghnanti* ("they kill within"). [The substitute is] followed by *t* as an indicator (*taparaḥ*). Question: Why? Answer: *antaraghāni* ("it was killed within"). SK 3295 (A 8.4.25): *ayanaṃ ca* / [The *ṇ* replaces the *n* of *han*] also in the word *ayanam*.

The substitution of *ṇ* for the final phoneme of *ayana* occurs when the word *antaḥ* precedes it: *antarayaṇam*. This applies only when it does not denote a location (*adeśe*). Thus, *antarayano deśaḥ* ("a region within").
According to A 3.3.118, the suffix *gha* is generally used in the masculine to form names;
and according to A 6.4.96, the long vowel is substituted for the final of *chādi-* before a suffix marked with *gh*, provided it is not preceded by two prefixes.

When followed by the suffix *dha*, the short vowel is substituted for the root *chad* when it is devoid of prefixes beginning with two consonants. For example: *dantacchadaḥ* ("that by which the teeth are covered"); *ākaraḥ* ("a mine," from *ā-kṛ*). Pāṇini A 3.3.119 states: "The words *gocara*, *saṃcara*, *vaha*, *vraja*, *vyaja*, *āpaṇa*, and *nigama* [are derived with the suffix *ghañ*]."

The suffix *ghañ* is applied [after roots ending in vowels]. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the *ghañ* that will be mentioned later by the rule *halaś ca*. In the sense of "cows move in this," one has *gocaraḥ*, meaning "a place. In the sense of "they move along this," one has *saṃcaraḥ*, meaning "a path. In the sense of "they carry by means of this," one has *vahaḥ*, meaning "a shoulder-yoke. *Vrajaḥ* (a cow-pen). *Vyajaḥ* (a palm-leaf fan). Due to irregular derivation (*nipātana*), the substitution of *vī* for *vy* does not occur. *Āpaṇaḥ* (a marketplace, a place for sale). In the sense of "they enter by means of this," one has *nigamaḥ*, meaning "a Vedic hymn" (*chandas*). And [the suffix is added] after the root *kaṣ*: *nikaṣaḥ* (a touchstone).
By the rule *ave tṛstror ghañ* (A 3.3.120), the suffix *ghañ* is applied after the roots *tṛ* and *stṛ* with the prefix *ava*: *avatāraḥ* (the descent into a well, etc.); *avastāraḥ* (a curtain).

SK 3300 *halaś ca* (A 3.3.121): After a stem ending in a consonant (*hal*), the suffix *ghañ* shall apply. This is an exception to [the application of] *ap*. In the sense "yogins delight in this," we have *rāmaḥ*. In the sense "by means of this, disease and so forth are wiped away (*apamṛjyate*)," we have *apāmārgaḥ*. *Vimārgaḥ* means a path that leads astray or a clearing. SK 3301 *adhyāyanyāyodyāvasaṃhārāś ca* (A 3.3.122): The words *adhyāya*, *nyāya*, *udyāva*, and *saṃhāra* are also [formed with *ghañ*].

*Adhyāya*: [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] after the root *i* (*adhi-i*) in the sense of "that in which one studies. The analysis (*vigraha*) is: "by means of this, they go forth, rise up, or withdraw. There is an extension (*upasaṃkhyāna*) of the rule for *ava-hṛ*, *ā-dhā*, and *ā-vā*. *A 3.3.123*: *udaṅko 'nudake* ("*udaṅka*" occurs when not referring to water).

After the root *añc* preceded by *ut*, the suffix *ghañ* is applied, but not when it refers to water. [For example: *ghṛtodaṅkaḥ* is a leather vessel, so called because clarified butter (*ghṛta*) is poured out (*udacyate*) or drawn up (*uddhriyate*) from it. Why say "not when referring to water"? [Counter-example: *udakodañcanaḥ* ("a water-scoop").
SK 3303 *jālamānāyaḥ* (A 3.3.124):
An *ānāya* is that by which fish and other creatures are brought (*ānīyante*) [in]. Why say "a net" (*jālam*)? [To exclude] *ānayanaḥ*. SK 3304 *khano gha ca* (A 3.3.125).

And [the suffix] *ghañ* [is applied] after the root *khan*. Thus: *ākhanaḥ* and *ākhānaḥ*. The inclusion of the marker *gh* is for the purpose of indicating that this [suffix] occurs even after other roots; by means of this, [forms such as] *bhagaḥ* and *padaṃ* [are explained]. The suffixes *ḍa*, *ḍara*, *eka*, and *ika-vak* should be stated [as substitutes] for the root *khan*: *ākhaḥ*, *ākharaḥ*, *ā khanikaḥ*, and *ā khanikavakaḥ*; these denote a spade. SK 3305:
The suffix *khal* is applied after the prefixes *īṣat*, *duḥ*, and *su* when they have the sense of difficulty (*kṛcchra*) or ease (*akṛcchra*). (A 3.3.126)

The rule *karaṇādhikaraṇayoḥ* has ceased to apply. When these words—*duḥkha*, *sukha*, and *artha*—are used as *upapadas*, the suffix *khal* shall be applied. By the rule *tayoḥ eva*, this applies to both the sense of the abstract state (*bhāva*) and the object (*karman*). In the sense of difficulty (*kṛcchra*): *duṣkaraḥ kaṭo bhavatā* ("The mat is difficult for you to make"). In the sense of ease (*akṛcchra*): *īṣatkaraḥ* ("easy to do") or *sukaraḥ*. It should be stated that for the roots *mā* (to measure), *mī* (to destroy), *lī* (to dissolve), and *lī* (to cling), the substitution of *ā* for the penultimate vowel does not occur before the suffixes *khal* and *ac*: *īṣanniyamaḥ* ("slight restraint"), *duṣpramayaḥ* ("difficult to perish"), *suvilayaḥ* ("easy to dissolve"). [The forms are] *niyamaḥ*, *mayaḥ*, and *layaḥ*. [By the rule] *upasargāt khalghañoḥ* (A 7.1.67).

The augment *num* shall be applied to the root *labh-* only after a prefix (*upasarga*). Examples: *īṣatpralambhaḥ*, *duṣpralambhaḥ*, *supralambhaḥ*, *upālambhaḥ*. Why "after a prefix"? [Consider: *lābhaḥ*. SK 3307: *na sudurbhyāṃ kevalābhyām* (A 7.1.68).

The augment *num* shall not be applied to the root *labh-* after the prefixes *su-* and *dur-*, when they are used alone—that is, when devoid of any other prefix—before the suffixes *khal* or *ghañ*. Examples: *sulabham*, *durlabham*. Why "when used alone"? [Consider: *supralambhaḥ*, *atidurlambhaḥ*. How then do we account for forms such as *atisulabham* and *atidurlabham*? They will be accounted for when *ati-* is treated as a *karmapravacanīya* (governing particle).

SK 3308: *kartṛkarmaṇoś ca bhūkṛñoḥ* (A 3.3.127). When the agent (*kartṛ*) or the object (*karman*)—along with *īṣat* and other such words—are used as *upapadas*, the suffix *khal* shall be applied after the roots *bhū* and *kṛ*. A one-to-one correspondence (*yathāsaṃkhya*) between these elements is not intended here. Furthermore, the agent and the object must be employed immediately after the verbal root, whereas *īṣat* and the others must precede it. It should be stated that this applies when the agent or object expresses the sense of the suffix *cv-* (i.e., a change of state). Because the suffix is marked with *khi*, the augment *mum* is added. Examples: *anāḍhyenāḍhyena duḥkhena bhūyate* → *durāḍhyambhavam* ("becoming wealthy with difficulty"). *īṣadāḍhyambhavam* ("becoming slightly wealthy"). *svāḍhyambhavam* ("becoming very wealthy"). *īṣadāḍhyaṅkaraḥ* ("making [him] slightly wealthy"). *durāḍhyaṅkaraḥ* ("making [him] difficult to make wealthy"). *svāḍhyaṅkaraḥ* ("making [him] very wealthy").
What is the purpose of [specifying] *cvī* and *artha*? [Example: *āḍhyena subhūyate*.

This is an exception (*apavāda*) to A 3.3.128, *āto yuc*. [Examples: *īṣatpānaḥ somaḥ bhavatā*, *duṣpānaḥ*, *supānaḥ*. In the common language (*bhāṣā*), the suffix *yuc* should be stated after the roots *śās*, *yudh*, *dṛś*, *dhṛṣ*, and *mṛṣ*. [Examples: *duḥśāsanaḥ*, *duryodhanaḥ*, etc.

SK 3310: After a *ṣ* that is at the end of a word (*padāntāt*), the *n* [of the suffix *naṭ*] is not replaced by *ṇ*. Examples: *niṣpānam*, *sarpiṣpānam*. Why "after a *ṣ*" (*ṣāt*)? [Counter-example: *nirṇayaḥ*. Why "at the end of a word" (*padāntāt*)? [Counter-example: *puṣṇāti*. This is a locative compound (*saptamīsamāsa*) meaning "that which is at the end (*antaḥ*) of a word (*pade*) is *padānta*. Therefore, there is no substitution here: *susarpiṣkeṇa*. SK 3311: The suffix *ṇini* is used in the sense of necessity (*āvaśyaka*) and debt (*adhamarṇya*). (A 3.3.170)
One who acts with necessity; one who bestows a hundredfold.

And [the suffix] *kṛtya* (by A 3.3.171) is used in the sense of necessity (*āvaśyaka*) and debt (*adhamarṇya*). [Examples: *avaśyaṃ hariḥ* ("Hari must be worshipped"); *śataṃ deyam* ("a hundred must be paid").
And [the suffixes] *ktic* and *kta* are used when a name (*saṃjñā*) is to be formed (by A 3.3.174).

The suffixes *ktic* and *kta* may occur after a verbal root in the sense of a benediction (*āśis*) or as a technical name (*saṃjñā*). By the rule *titutra-* etc., the augment *iṭ* is not applied. Thus: *bhavatāt*; *bhūtiḥ*. SK 3314: *na ktici dīrghaś ca* (A 6.4.39).

When *ktic* follows, there is neither lengthening [of the vowel] nor the elision of the nasal for those roots that do not take the augment *iṭ*, such as *vanati*, *tanoti*, and others. Thus: *yantiḥ*, *rantiḥ*, *vantiḥ*, *tantiḥ*.

SK 3315: *sanaḥ ktici lopaś cāsyānyatarasyām* (A 6.4.45). After the root *san*, when the suffix *ktic* follows, there is optionally the substitution of *ā* for the final vowel, and optionally the elision (*lopa*) of that vowel as well. Thus: *sanutāt*, *sātiḥ*, *satiḥ*, *santiḥ*. [In the case of *devadatta*: the gods would give him, hence] *devadattaḥ*. SK 3316: *alaṃkhalvoḥ pratiṣedhayoḥ prācāṃ ktvā* (A 3.4.18). When *alam* and *khalu* are used in the sense of prohibition, according to the Eastern grammarians, the suffix *ktvā* is employed [in place of the infinitive].

The suffix *ktvā* shall be used when the words *alam* and *khalu*, which have the sense of prohibition, are employed as adjuncts (*upapada*). The mention of "of the Easterners" (*prācām*) is for the sake of honor. Because of the restrictive rule (*niyama*) that [the suffix *ktvā*] occurs only with an indeclinable ending in *am*, there is no compound with the adjunct. In the case of the root *dā* (to give), it becomes *dad* before *ghu* and *mā-sthā* [roots]. *Alam dattvā* (having given enough). By the rule *ghumāsthā...* [the root *pā* becomes *pī*]. *Khalu pītvā* (having indeed drunk). Why "when *alam* and *khalu*"? Consider: *mā kārṣīt* (let him not do). Why "when they have the sense of prohibition"? Consider: *alaṃkāraḥ* (ornament). SK 3317: *udīcāṃ māṅo vyatīhāre* (A 3.4.19).
When the sense is reciprocity (*vyatīhāra*), the suffix *ktvā* shall be used after the root *māṅ*. This is intended to provide for cases where there is no prior time sequence.

SK 3318: *mayater id anyatarasyām* (A 6.4.70). The phoneme *i* is optionally the final substitute for the root *meṅ* before the suffix *lyap*. Thus, one obtains *apamitya yācate* or *apamāya*. Because of the mention of "the Northerners" (*udīcām*), the original form is also permitted: *yācitvā apamayate*. SK 3319: *parāvarayoge ca* (A 3.4.20). [The suffix *ktvā* is also used after a verb when there is a connection with what is prior or posterior.]

When a connection is to be understood between a posterior action and a prior one, or between a prior action and a posterior one, the suffix *ktvā* shall be applied to the verbal root. *Aprāpya nadīṃ parvataḥ* ("The mountain has not reached the river"). Here, the connection of the mountain is with the posterior [action of reaching] the river. *Atikramya parvataṃ sthitā nadī* ("The river stands having passed beyond the mountain"). Here, the connection of the river is with the prior [action of passing] the mountain. [This is governed by the rule: *samānakartṛkayoḥ pūrvakāle* (A 3.4.21).

The suffix *ktvā* occurs after a verbal root denoting an action that precedes in time, provided both roots have the same agent. However, *ktvā* is an indeclinable *kṛt* suffix used in the sense of the abstract action (*bhāve*). Examples: *bhuktvā vrajati* ("having eaten, he goes"). The doubling [of the suffix] is not mandatory: *snātvā bhuktvā pītvā vrajati* ("having bathed, eaten, and drunk, he goes"). By the rule *anudātta-* (Pāṇini 6.4.37), there is the elision of the nasal [in *natvā*]: *viṣṇuṃ natvā stauti* ("having bowed to Viṣṇu, he praises him"). In the case of roots such as *svarati*, by the rule *śryukaḥ kiti* (Pāṇini 7.2.11), there is the obligatory absence of the augment *iṭ* through prior contradiction (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*): *svṛtvā*, *sūtvā*, *dhūtvā*. SK 3321: In the case of the suffix *ktvā*, [the substitution of *ī* for the final vowel of] *skandi* and *syandi* does not take place. (A 6.4.31)

In these two cases, there shall be no elision of *n* when followed by the suffix *ktvā*. Thus: *skantvā*; because it is marked with *ū* as an *it*, the augment *iṭ* is optional: *syantvā* or *syanditvā*. SK 3322: *na ktvā seṭ* (A 1.2.28). A *ktvā* suffix that has the augment *iṭ* (*seṭ*) shall not be *kin*. Thus: *śayitvā*. Why "with *iṭ*"? [Counter-example: *kṛtvā*.
Pāṇini 1.2.7 (*mṛḍamṛdagudhakuṣakliśavadavasaḥ ktvā*):

After these roots, the *ktvā* suffix is marked with the *iṭ* augment (*seṭ*) and is treated as having the *kit* designation. Examples: *mṛḍitvā*. Regarding the root *kliś*, the *iṭ* augment is optional by rule 1.2.26 (*kliśaḥ ktvā*): *kliśitvā* or *kliṣṭvā*. Regarding the root *vas*, the *iṭ* augment is optional by rule 1.2.11 (*uḍitaḥ*): *uṣitvā*. By rule 1.2.28 (*rudavidamuṣagrahiṣuṣvañjām ca*), the *ktvā* suffix is treated as *kit*: *rutitvā*, *viditvā*, *muṣitvā*, *gṛhītvā*. Pāṇini 1.2.23 (*nopadhāt thaphāntād vā*): After a root ending in *th* or *ph* that has a nasal (*n*) as its penultimate letter (*upadha*), the *ktvā* suffix is optionally treated as *kit*.

The suffix *ktvā* with the augment *iṭ* may optionally be *kit*. Examples: *śrathitvā*, *granthitvā*, *guphitvā*, *gumphitvā*. Why [is it not *kit*] after a root ending in a nasal? *kothitvā*, *rephitvā*. According to A 1.2.24 (*vaciluñcyṛtaś ca*), *ktvā* with the augment *iṭ* may optionally be *kit* after the roots *vac*, *luñc*, and *ṛ*. Examples: *vacitvā*, *vañcitvā*, *lucitvā*, *luñcitvā*, *ṛtitvā*, *artitvā*.

SK 3326: *tṛṣimṛṣikṛśeḥ kāśyapasya* (Pāṇini 1.2.25). After these roots, the suffix *ktvā* optionally takes the augment *iṭ*. Examples: *tṛṣitvā* or *tarṣitvā*; *mṛṣitvā* or *marṣitvā*; *kṛśitvā* or *karśitvā*. The optionality of the *kit* designation [of the suffix *ktvā*] applies by the rule *ralo vyupadhāt...* (Pāṇini 1.2.26). Examples: *dyutitvā* or *dyotitvā*; *likhitvā* or *lekhitvā*. Why mention *ralaḥ*? [Counter-example: *sevitvā*. Why mention *vyupadhāt*? [Counter-example: *vartitvā*. Why mention *halādeḥ*? [Counter-example: *eṣitvā*. Why mention *seṭ*? [Counter-example: *bhuktvā*. By the rule *vasatikṣudhor iṭ* (Pāṇini 7.2.52), the augment *iṭ* is added: *uṣitvā*, *kṣudhitvā*, or *kṣodhitvā*. By the rule *añceḥ pūjāyām* (Pāṇini 7.2.53), the augment *iṭ* is obligatory when expressing honor: *añcitvā*.

After [the roots] *añc* and *gam*, [the suffix] *ktvā* becomes *aktvā*; thus also *lubhitvā* and *lobhitvā*. According to the rule *lubho 'vimohane* (Pāṇini 1.2.6), the augment *iṭ* is applied; however, in the sense of "delusion," it is *lubdhvā*. SK 3327: *jṝvraścyoḥ ktvi* (A 7.2.55).
The augment *iṭ* shall be applied after these two [roots] before the suffix *ktvā*. Thus: *jarītvā*, *jaritvā*, and *vraścitvā*.

SK 3328 *udito vā* (A 7.2.56): The augment *iṭ* is optionally added after a root marked with *udic* before the suffix *ktvā*. Examples: *śamitvā* (from √*śam*), where the lengthening is by *anunāsikasya kvi...* [Pāṇini 6.4.15]; *śāntvā*; *dyūtvā*; *devitvā*. SK 3329 *kramaś ca ktvi* (A 6.4.18): The substitution of *kram* for *krām* also occurs before the suffix *ktvā*.

The long vowel *ā* may optionally replace the penultimate vowel of the root *kram* when followed by an affix beginning with a *jhal* consonant and ending in *ktvā*. Examples: *krāntvā* or *krantvā*. Why "beginning with a *jhal*" (*jhali*)? Consider *kramitvā*. By rule A 7.2.51 (*pūṅaś ca*), there is optionally the augment *iṭ*: *pavitvā* or *pṛtvā*. A 3.4.32 (*jāntanaśāṃ vibhāṣā*) [is also applicable].

The *n* of roots ending in *j* and of the root *naś* may optionally be elided when followed by the suffix *ktvā*. Thus: *bhaktvā* (from *bhaj*), *bhaṅktvā* (from *bhañj*); *raktvā* (from *rañj*), *raṅktvā* (from *rañj*). By the rule *masjinaśoḥ*, the augment *num* is added; its elision occurs optionally. Thus: *naṣṭvā* (with elision), *naṃṣṭvā* (without elision). By the rule *radhādibhyaś ca*, the augment *iṭ* is added. Optionally: *naśitvā*. It should be stated that this applies when [the following suffix] begins with a *jhal* consonant. Not here: *añjitvā*. Because the root is marked with *ūdit*, the augment *iṭ* is optional. Optionally: *aktvā*, *aṅktvā*. By the rule *janasana-*, there is the substitution of *ā*. Thus: *khātvā*, *khanitvā*. By the rule *dyatisyati-*, the augment *iṭ* is added. Thus: *ditvā*, *sitvā*, *mitvā*, *sthitvā*. For the root *dhā*, *hi* is substituted. Thus: *hitvā*.
And after the root *hā* [meaning "to leave"], when followed by the suffix *ktvā*, [the substitution of *ī* for *a* is applied]:

*hitvā*. But after the root *hāṅ* [meaning "to abandon"], it is *hātvā*. After the root *ad* [meaning "to eat"], [the substitute *jagdhi* is applied] according to Pāṇini 2.4.36: *jagdhvā*. When in a compound that does not have *nañ* as its prior member, the suffix *ktvā* is replaced by *lyap*: Pāṇini 7.1.37.

In a compound where the first member is an indeclinable (*avyaya*), provided it is not a negative compound (*anañ-samāsa*), the suffix *ktvā* shall undergo the substitution of *lyap*. [The augment] *tuk* is added. Example: *prakṛtya*. Why "not a negative compound"? Example: *akṛtvā*. Because the exclusion (*paryudāsa*) is adopted here, this does not apply in cases such as *paramakṛtvā*. Regarding *A 6.1.86*: "The rule for single-substitute (*ekādeśa*) is considered non-existent (*asiddha*) when the application of *ṣatva* or *tuk* is to be performed. Example: *ko 'siñcat*. Here, *ṣatva* does not apply. Examples: *adhītya*, *pretya*. [In these,] *tuk* is added by the rule *hrasvasya...* (Pāṇini 6.1.71).

SK 3334: *vā lyapi* (A 6.4.38). For roots taught with an anudātta accent, such as *van* and *tan*, there may optionally be the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika-lopa*) when the suffix *lyap* follows. This is a rule of restricted optionality (*vyavasthita-vibhāṣā*). Consequently, for roots ending in *m* that lack an indicatory *iṭ*, and for those ending in *n* that possess an indicatory *iṭ*, as well as for roots beginning with *van*, the elision is obligatory. Examples: *āgatya*. [Regarding the substitution of] *jagdhi* for *ad*: the suffix *lyap* is more powerful than even internal rules (*antaraṅga-vidhi*), because the mention of *lyap* is made in the rule prescribing *jagdhi*. Therefore, in the case of *lyap*, the following do not apply: doubling (*hitva*), the substitution of *da* for *dha* (*datva*), the substitution of *v* for *u* (*vetva*), lengthening (*dīrghatva*), and the augment *śūṭ* and *iṭ*. Examples: *vidhāya*, *pradhāya*, *prakhanya*, *prasthāya*.

Having proceeded (*prakramya*), having taken leave (*āpṛcchya*), having played (*pradīvya*), having recited (*prapaṭya*). SK 3335: *na lyapi* (A 6.4.69). When *kyap* follows, the substitution of *ī* for the vowels of roots beginning with *ghu*, *mā*, and *sthā* does not take place. *Gheṭ*: *pradhāya*, *pramāya*, *pragāya*, *prapāya*, *prahāya*, *prasāya*. For the root *mī* (to measure), there is the substitution of *ā* by rule A 6.1.50 (*mīnātiminoti-*) : *pramāya*, *nimāya*, *upadāya*. Optionally so for the root *lī*: *vilāya* or *vilīya*. The elision of *ṇi*: *uttārya*, *vicārya*.

SK 3336: *lyapi laghupūrvāt* (A 6.4.56). When *lyap* follows, the substitution of *ay* for *ṇi* occurs after a suffix that has a light (*laghu*) vowel as its penultimate. Examples: *vigaṇayya*, *praṇamayya*, *prabebhidayya*. Why "after a light penultimate"? Consider: *saṃpradhārya*. SK 3337: *vibhāṣāpaḥ* (A 6.1.57). [The substitution of *ay* for *ṇi*] is optional when *ap* follows.
In place of the *ṇi* of the root *āp*, there may optionally be the substitution of *ay* before the suffix *lyap*. Thus: *prāpayya* or *prāpya*.
(SK 3338) Regarding the rule for *kṣi*: in place of *kṣi*, there shall be a long vowel before *lyap*. Thus: *prakṣīya*.
SK 3339 *lyapi ca* (A 6.1.41):
When the suffix *lyap* follows, there shall be no vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) for the root *veñ*. Example: *pravāya*.
SK 3340 *jyaś ca* (A 6.1.42): [The same applies] when the suffix *lyap* follows the root *jyā*.
Before the suffix *jya*,
[the *y* of] *vyā* is also elided; as in *upavyāya*.

SK 3342: *vibhāṣā pareḥ* (A 6.1.44). After the prefix *pari*, there may optionally be *saṃprasāraṇa* of the root *vyen* when the suffix *lyap* follows. This supersedes the *tuk* augment because it is subsequent [in the order of rules], and by the rule *hal—* (A 6.4.2), a long vowel is substituted. Thus: *parivīya* or *parivyāya*. How is it that [the forms] *mukhaṃ vyādāya svapiti* ("he sleeps with his mouth open") and *netre nimītya hasati* ("he laughs with his eyes closed") are formed? [The answer is: even though the sleeping and laughing continue at a time subsequent to the opening and closing of the mouth and eyes, they will be justified by the intention (*vivakṣā*) to express that specific part [of the action]. SK 3343: *ābhīkṣṇye ṇamul ca* (A 6.4.22). When repetition (*ābhīkṣṇya*) is to be expressed, the suffix *ṇamul* is added [to the verb], and [the suffix *ktvā* is also used].

When repetition is to be expressed, the suffix *ṇamul* shall be used in the same cases as those previously mentioned for *ktvā*, and *ktvā* may also be used. Examples: *smāraṃ smāraṃ namati śivam* (repeatedly remembering, he bows to Śiva); *smṛtvā smṛtvā*. *pāyaṃ pāyam*, *bhojaṃ bhojam*, *śrāvaṃ śrāvam*. Regarding the rule *ciṇṇamuloḥ*, there is optionally a lengthening of the vowel when *ṇi* is followed by *ṇamul*: *gamaṃ gamam* or *gāmaṃ gāmam*. According to the rule *vibhāṣā ciṇṇamuloḥ*, the augment *num* is optionally inserted: *laṃbhaṃ laṃbham* or *lābhaṃ lābham*. By virtue of the restricted option (*vyavasthitavibhāṣā*), the augment *num* is mandatory after a root that has a prefix.

*pralambhaṃ pralambham* / *jāgro 'viciṇṇalṛṅkṣu*—thus there is *guṇa*. *jāgaraṃ jāgaram* / The same applies to the causative (*ṇyanta*) as well. SK 3344: *na yadyanākāṅkṣe* (A 3.4.33). When the word *yat* is used as a subordinate element (*upapada*), that which would otherwise be obtained [by the previous rule] for an action occurring at a prior time does not take place, provided that the sentence consisting of the prior and subsequent actions does not require another [sentence]. For example: *yad ayaṃ bhuṅkte tataḥ paṭhati* ("When he eats, then he studies"). Here, the suffixes *ktvā* and *ṇamul* do not occur. Why say "provided it does not require another"? Consider: *yad ayaṃ bhuktvā vrajati tato 'dhīte* ("When he has eaten and is going, then he studies"). [In this case, the suffixes do occur.]

SK 3345: *vibhāṣāgreprathamapūrveṣu* (A 3.4.24). The term *ābhīkṣṇye* ("in the sense of repetition") does not carry over [from the previous rule]. When these words are used as upapadas, the suffixes *ktvā* and *ṇamul* are optionally employed after a verbal root denoting an action occurring at a prior time (*pūrvakāla*), provided both actions have the same agent (*samānakartṛka*). Examples: *agrebhojaṃ vrajati* ("he goes after eating first"), or *agrebhuktvā* ("having first eaten, he goes"). *prathamaṃ bhojam*, or *prathamaṃ bhuktvā*. *pūrvaṃ bhojam*, or *pūrvaṃ bhuktvā*. In the alternative case, the *laṭ* (present tense) and other suffixes are used: *agre bhuṅkte tato vrajati* ("he eats first, then he goes"). However, when there is repetition (*ābhīkṣṇya*), this rule applies invariably by virtue of the prohibition of the previous rule; thus: *agrebhojaṃ bhojaṃ vrajati* ("he goes after eating repeatedly") or *bhuktvā bhuktvā*.

SK 3346: *karmaṇy ākrośe kṛñaḥ khamuñ* (A 3.4.24). When a word denoting an object (*karman*) is used as an *upapada*, and an expression of abuse (*ākrośa*) is to be understood, the suffix *khamuñ* is applied after the root *kṛ*. Example: *cauraṅkāram ākrośati*. The root *kṛ* here means "to utter"; the meaning is "having uttered the word 'thief'. SK 3347: *svādumi ṇamul* (A 3.4.26). [The suffix *ṇamul* is applied after a verb when the word *svādu* or its synonyms are used as an *upapada* expressing a state of being.]

The suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the root *kṛ* when it refers to delicious things (*svādu*), provided that the two actions have the same agent; the final vowel of the preceding word is prescribed to be *m*. Examples: having made what was not delicious delicious, he eats—*svāduṅkāraṃ bhuṅkte*; *saṃpannaṅkāraḥ*; *lavaṇaṅkāram*. The words *saṃpanna* and *lavaṇa* are synonyms for *svādu*. By the rule of alternative forms (*vāsarūpa*), the suffix *ktvā* may also be used: *svāduṃ kṛtvā bhuṅkte*. SK 3348: After the words *anyathā*, *evam*, *katham*, and *ittham*, [the suffix *ṇamul* is applied] if the action is already established without its verbal expression (*siddhāprayoga*). (A 3.4.27)

The suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the root *kṛ* when these [words] are present, provided that *kṛ* is established as having no actual usage (*siddha-aprayoga*) in such a state. The meaning is that because it is redundant, it is not fit for usage. Examples: *anyathākāram*, *evaṅkāram*, *kathaṅkāram*, *itthaṃkāraṃ bhuṅkte*. The meaning is "he eats in this manner. Why specify "established" (*siddha*)? Consider: *śiro 'nyathā kṛtvā bhuṅkte* ("having turned his head otherwise, he eats"). Regarding *yathātathayor asūyāprativacane* (A 3.4.28): the rule "after *kṛ*, with the suffix *ṇamul*, provided it is established and has no usage" applies here as well, when there is a reply in response to malice (*asūyā*). Example: *yathākāram ahaṃ bhokṣye, tathākāraṃ bhokṣye; kiṃ tavānena?* ("I will eat in one way, I will eat in another; what is that to you?")

SK 3350: *karmaṇi dṛśividoḥ sākalye* (A 3.4.29). When a word in the accusative case is used as an *upapada*, the suffix *ṇamul* shall be applied after the roots *dṛś* and *vid*. Example: *kanyādarśaṃ varayati* ("he chooses [the girl] having seen her"). The meaning is "all the girls. Example: *brāhmaṇavedaṃ bhojayati* ("he feeds [him] having known him as a Brāhmaṇa"). The meaning is that he feeds every single Brāhmaṇa whom he knows, obtains, or considers to be one. SK 3351: *yāvati vidajīvoḥ* (A 3.4.30). [The suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the roots *vid* and *jīv* when the word *yāvat* is used as an *upapada*.]
"Yāvadvedam bhunkte" means "he eats as much as he obtains. "Yāvajjīvam adhīte" means "he studies for as long as he lives.

Regarding the rule *carmodarayoḥ pūreḥ* (A 3.4.31), it is understood that [the word] "karman" [from the previous sūtra] still applies: *carmapūram stṛṇāti* ("he spreads out enough leather") and *udarapūram bhunkte* ("he eats until his belly is full").

Pāṇini Sūtra 3.4.32: *varṣapramāṇa ūlopaś cāsyānyatarasyām*. When a word denoting the measure of rain (*varṣapramāṇa*) is understood from the whole expression, the suffix *ṇamul* is optionally applied after the root *pūri* when it has an object as its attendant word (*upapada*), and there is optionally the elision (*lopa*) of the vowel *ū*. For example: *goṣpadapūraṃ vṛṣṭo devaḥ* ("It rained enough to fill a cow's footprint") or *goṣpadapraṃ vṛṣṭo devaḥ*. Why does the sūtra say *asya* ("of this [root]")? To prevent the elision from applying to the attendant word itself; for instance, in *mūṣikābilapram*, the vowel *ū* of the attendant word *bila* is not elided. Pāṇini Sūtra 3.4.33: *cele knopeḥ*. The suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the root *knūyī* when the attendant word is *cela* ("cloth"). For example: *celaknopaṃ vṛṣṭo devaḥ* ("It rained so much that the clothes became soaked").

When words meaning "clothing" (*cela*) are used as upapadas for the roots *knū* and *pī*, the suffix *ṇamul* is applied provided that the measure of rain is intended. Examples: *celaknopaṃ vṛṣṭo devaḥ* ("It rained so much that it soaked the clothes"), *vastraknopam*, *vasanaknopam*. According to A 3.4.34, the suffix *ṇamul* is also applied after the root *kaṣ* when the words *nimūla* and *samūla* are used as upapadas.

The author will state later that the term *karman* applies specifically to the usage of verbs such as *kaṣ*. In this section, the phrase "preceding time" (*pūrvakāla*) does not apply. Examples: *nimūlakāṣaṃ kaṣati*, *samūlakāṣaṃ kaṣati*. The meaning is: "he scrapes out root and all," or "he scrapes out with the roots. Even though the verbal root has a single meaning, a distinction arises through its connection with qualifiers such as *nimūla* and so on. Thus, there exists a relationship of qualifier and qualified by way of a general and particular relation.
(Pāṇini 3.4.35): *śuṣkacūrṇarūkṣeṣu piṣaḥ* ("after the verb *piṣ*, when [the object] is *śuṣka*, *cūrṇa*, or *rūkṣa*").

In these actions, the suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the root *piṣ*. *Śuṣkapeṣaṃ pinaṣṭi*: he grinds dryly; the meaning is "he grinds [something] that is dry. *Cūrṇapeṣam*, *rūkṣapeṣam*. SK 3357: *samūlākṛtajīveṣu hankṛñgrahaḥ* (A 3.4.36). [The suffix *ṇamul* is applied] when these are the objects. *Samūlaghātaṃ hanti*: he kills [him] along with the roots. *Akṛtakāraṃ karoti*: he makes [it] unmade. *Jīvagrāhaṃ gṛhṇāti*: he seizes [him] alive. *Jīva* means "one who lives"; the suffix *ka* is applied by the rule regarding roots ending in *i* or *u* (*igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kaḥ*). The meaning is "he seizes one who is living."

SK 3358: *karaṇe hanaḥ* (A 3.4.37). [The suffix *lyuṭ* is applied after the root *han* when a *karaṇa* (instrument) is the object of the action. Example: *pādaghātaṃ hanti*. The meaning is "he strikes with his foot. This rule (*yoga*) is intended for the purpose of using the verb in its original form (*yathāvidhy-anuprayoga*) and for the sake of avoiding a compound; otherwise, in the case of a connection with a different verbal root, it will be stated later that the suffix applies after roots meaning "to injure" (*hiṃsārthānām*). SK 3359: *snehane piṣaḥ* (A 3.4.38). [The suffix *lyuṭ* is applied after the root *piṣ* when the sense is "smearing with oil" (*snehana*).]

The suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the root *piṣ* when the instrument (*karaṇa*) by which one causes something to be crushed is expressed as the object of affection (*snihyate*). Example: *udapeṣaṃ pinaṣṭi*. The meaning is "he crushes with water" (*udakena pinaṣṭi*). (Pāṇini A 3.4.38). Regarding the rule *haste vartigrahoḥ* (A 3.4.39): it applies when the hand is the instrument. Examples: *hastavartaṃ vartayati* and *karavartam*. The meaning is "he rolls a pill with his hand" (*hastena gulikāṃ karoti*). Also: *hastagrāhaṃ gṛhṇāti*, *karagrāham*, and *pāṇigrāham*. (The meaning is "he takes [her] by the hand").

SK 3361: *sve puṣaḥ* (A 3.4.40). The rule "in the sense of an instrument" (*karaṇe*) applies here as well. The word *sva* is taken here in its sense (*arthagrahaṇa*). Consequently, the suffix *ṇamul* is applied when the word refers to itself (*svarūpa*), its synonyms (*paryāya*), or its specific instances (*viśeṣa*). Examples: *svapoṣaṃ puṣṇāti* ("he nourishes his own prosperity"), *dhanapoṣam*, *gopoṣam*.
SK 3362: *adhikaraṇe bandhaḥ* (A 3.4.41). [The suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the root *bandh* when it has the sense of a locus.]

One forms a *cakrabandha*; the meaning is that one binds [it] in a circle. According to A 3.4.42 (*saṃjñāyām*), the suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the root *bandh* when a name is being formed. Examples include: *krauñcabandhaṃ baddhaḥ* ("he was bound in the *krauñca* fashion"), *mayūrikābandham*, and *aṭṭālikābandham*. These are names for specific types of binding.

SK 3364: *naśivahoḥ* (A 3.4.43). [The suffix *ṇamul* is used after a verb denoting motion when it follows a word expressing the agent (*kartṛ*) of the verbs *naś* and *vah*, provided that this agent is not Śiva. For example: *jīvanāśaṃ naśyati* ("He perishes while living"). The meaning is "the living being perishes" (*jīvo naśyati*). *puruṣavāhaṃ vahati* ("He carries while being carried by a man"). The meaning is "the man carries" (*puruṣo vahati*). SK 3365: *ūrdhve śuṣipūroḥ* (A 3.4.44). [The suffix *ṇamul* is used after the verbs *śuṣ* and *pūr* when they follow the word *ūrdhva* in the sense of motion.]

In the case of *ūrdhve kartari* (when the agent is "upright"): *ūrdhvaśoṣaṃ śuṣyati* means that a tree or similar object withers while remaining upright; the sense is that it dries up while standing vertically. *Ūrdhvapūraṃ pūryate* means that a jar or similar vessel becomes full of rainwater or the like while its opening faces upward; the sense is that it is filled while facing upwards. By the rule *upamāne karmaṇi ca* (Pāṇini 3.4.45), and because of the word *ca* ("and"), [the suffix *lyuṭ* is also applied] when the agent is the subject: *ghṛtanidhāyaṃ nihitaṃ jalam* means water placed in a container is well-guarded like clarified butter (*ghṛta*); the sense is that it is preserved as carefully as ghee. *Ajakanāśaṃ naṣṭaḥ* means he is lost like a goat; the sense is that he has disappeared like a goat.

SK 3367: *kaṣādiṣu yathāvidhyanuprayogaḥ* (A 3.4.46). The meaning is that the very same suffix which was prescribed after the root [in the *ṇamul* formation] must be employed as the subsequent verb (*anuprayoga*). It has been illustrated in exactly that manner. SK 3368: *upasaṃvādaḥ tṛtīyāyām* (A 3.4.47).

From this point forward, the term "prior time" (*pūrvakāla*) is understood as the governing factor. Alternatively, the compound is formed according to the rule *tṛtīyā-prabhṛtīny anyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 2.1.30). Examples: *mūlakopadaṃśaṃ bhuṅkte* ("he eats with a radish as a side-dish") or *mūlakenopadaṃśam*. The third case ending (*tṛtīyā*) is applied because the radish, which is to be mentioned [later], functions as the instrument (*karaṇa*) with respect to the act of eating. Although there is no direct verbal connection with the word *upadaṃśin* ("that which side-dishes"), there is nonetheless an implied semantic connection, since [the radish] is the object (*karman*). It is by virtue of this much capacity that the suffix and the compound are justified, due to the force of the statement regarding the third case (*tṛtīyāyām*). This applies also to verbs meaning "to injure" (*hiṃsārtha*) when they share the same object (*samānakarmaka*), as prescribed by A 3.4.48.

When a word ending in the third case is used as an *upapada*, the suffix *ṇamul* shall be applied after a root meaning "to strike" (*hiṃsārtha*) that has the same object as the main verb. Examples: *daṇḍopaghātaṃ gāḥ kālayati* ("He drives the cows while striking them with a stick"), *daṇḍenopaghātam*, and *daṇḍatāḍam*. Why is it stated that they must have the same object? Consider: *daṇḍena coram āhatya gāḥ kālayati* ("Having struck the thief with a stick, he drives the cows"). [Pāṇini 3.4.49:
*saptamyāṃ copapīḍarudhakarṣaḥ* ("And when a word ending in the seventh case is the *upapada*, the suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the roots *pīḍ*, *rudh*, and *karṣ*").

The suffix *ṇamul* is applied after verbs such as *pīḍ* preceded by the prefix *upa*, when they occur with a word ending in the seventh (*saptamī*) or third (*tṛtīyā*) case as an attendant word (*upapada*). Examples: *pārśvepapīḍaṃ śete* (he lies down pressing against his side). *pārśvayor upapīḍam* (pressing against both sides). *pārśvābhyām upapīḍam* (pressing with both sides). *vrajoparodhaṃ gāḥ sthāpayati* (he stops the cows by blocking the cow-pen). *vrajenoparodham* (blocking with the pen). *vraje voparodham* (or blocking in the pen). *pāṇyupakarṣaṃ dhānāḥ saṃgṛhṇāti* (he gathers the parched grains drawing them toward his hand). *pāṇāv upakarṣam* (drawing toward the hand). *pāṇinopakarṣam* (drawing with the hand). SK 3371: When proximity (*samāsatti*) is intended, [the suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the verb *kṛ*]. (A 3.4.50)

The suffix *ṇamul* is applied after a verbal root when the third or seventh case endings are present, provided that "proximity" (*sannikarṣa*) is implied. Examples: *keśagrāhaṃ yudhyante* ("they fight by seizing the hair") = *keśeṣu gṛhītvā* ("having seized [them] by the hair"); *hastagrāham* ("by seizing the hand") = *hastena gṛhītvā* ("having seized [him] with the hand").

By the rule *pramāṇe ca* (A 3.4.51), the same applies when the third or seventh case endings are present. Example: *dvyaṅgulotkarṣaṃ khaṇḍikāṃ chinatti* ("he cuts the piece of cloth with an excess of two fingers") = *dvyaṅgulena dvyaṅgule vā utkarṣam* ("an excess of two fingers, either by means of two fingers or in the space of two fingers").

SK 3373: When there is a sense of urgency (*parīpsā*) regarding the point of departure (*apādāna*), [the suffix -am is used]. Urgency means haste. Example: *śayyotthāyaṃ dhāvati* ("He runs, rising from his bed").
SK 3374: And when the accusative case (*dvitīyā*) is present, [the suffix -am is used].
The same applies when there is a desire to obtain (*parīpsā*). For example: *yaṣṭigrāhaṃ yudhyante* ("they fight grasping at staffs") and *loṣṭagrāham* ("grasping at clods").

According to A 6.1.56, *apaguro ṇamuli*, the vowel *e* of the root *gurī* in the sense of "lifting up" optionally becomes *ā* before the suffix *ṇamul*. Thus, from *asya-apagura*, we have *asyapagoram* or *asyapagāram* ("they fight brandishing [the sword]").

SK 3376: *svāṅge ’dhruve* (A 3.4.54). Following the rule "when there is an accusative," [the suffix] *ṇamul* is added after a verbal root when the word ending in the second case denotes a non-permanent part of one's own body (*svāṅga*). Example: *bhrūvikṣepaṃ kathayati* ("he tells by means of a movement of the eyebrows") or *bhruvaṃ vikṣepam*. Why "non-permanent" (*adhruve*)? Example: *śira utkṣipya* ("having raised his head"). That without which life does not exist is "permanent" (*dhruva*). SK 3377: *parikliśyamāne ca* (A 3.4.55). [The suffix *ṇamul* is added after a verbal root] also when the word ending in the second case denotes that which is being tormented.

When a body part (*svāṅga*) that is being afflicted from all sides is expressed in the accusative case, the suffix *ṇamul* is applied. For example: *uraḥpratipeṣaṃ yudhyante* ("They fight while pressing against each other's chests"). The meaning is: "They afflict the entire chest [of the opponent]. Also: *urovidāraṃ praticiskare nakhaiḥ* ("They tore at each other's chests with their nails"). This rule is for the sake of establishing certainty (*dhruva*). Furthermore, according to A 3.4.56: *viśi-pati-pad-i-skandām vyāpyamānāsevyamānayoḥ* ("The roots *viś*, *pat*, *pad*, and *skand* take *ṇamul* when expressing the sense of being pervaded or being repeatedly performed"). For instance: *gṛhaṃ-praveśam āste* ("He stays, pervading the house"), or *gṛhaṃ-praveśam āste* ("He stays, repeatedly entering the house"). Similarly: *ākāśaṃ-patam patati* ("He flies, pervading the sky"), *ākāśaṃ-patam patati* ("He flies, repeatedly flying through the sky"), *pādaṃ-padam gacchati* ("He goes, stepping foot by foot"), and *pādaṃ-padam gacchati* ("He goes, repeatedly placing his foot down"). Likewise: *tṛṇaṃ-skandam skandati* ("He leaps, leaping over every blade of grass") and *tṛṇaṃ-skandam skandati* ("He leaps, repeatedly leaping over blades of grass"). In these cases, the action is understood as being either pervasive or habitual. However, this does not apply in examples such as *gṛhaṃ praviśya āste* ("Having entered the house, he sits"), where the action is not pervasive or repeated. Thus, the rule is established.

"Only after [the word] *dvitīyāyām*. When a word ending in the second case (*dvitīyānta*) is the *upapada*, the suffix *ṇamul* shall be applied after roots such as *viś* and others, provided that the sense of being pervaded (*vyāpyamāna*) or being practiced repeatedly (*āsevyamāna*) is to be understood. Pervasion (*vyāpti*) is the complete connection of substances such as houses with actions such as entering. Repeated practice (*āsevā*) is the recurrence of an action. The doubling [of the word] by the rule *nityavīpsayoḥ* does not occur, because those two meanings are already expressed by the very nature of the compound itself.

Although the suffix *ṇamul* has already been prescribed for the sense of repetition (*ābhīkṣṇya*), it is nevertheless prescribed here again for the purpose of assigning the technical designation *upapada* when there is habitual action (*āsevā*). Examples: *gehānupraveśam āste* ("he sits [repeatedly] entering the house"), *gehaṃgeham anupraveśam*, *geham anupraveśam anupraveśam*. Similarly: *gehānuprapātam*, *gehānuprapādam*, *gehānuskandam*. However, in the case of a non-compound (*asamāsa*), there is optionally reduplication (*dvitva*) either of the word *geha* or of the form ending in *ṇamul*. (SK 3379) *asyatitṛṣoḥ kriyāntare kāleṣu* (A 3.4.57).

The term *kriyāntara* means that which intervenes or separates an action. When the verbal roots *as* ("to throw") and *tṛṣ* ("to thirst") denote an action that has another action intervening, the suffix *ṇamul* is applied provided that words expressing time ending in the second case (*dvitīyā*) are used as co-occurring words (*upapada*). Examples: *dvyahātyāsaṃ gāḥ pāyayati* ("He makes the cows drink [water] with an interval of two days"). This is analyzed as *dvyahamatyāsam* ("having an interval of two days") or *dvyahatarṣam* ("having a thirsting for two days"). By means of the throwing away (*atyāsana*) and the thirsting (*tarṣaṇa*), the act of drinking by the cows is separated. The meaning is: having made them drink today, he makes them drink again after two days have passed. (A 3.4.58) *nāmnyādiśigrahoḥ*: [The suffix *ṇamul* is applied after the roots *ā-diś* and *grah* when followed by a word denoting a name.]

In the second [example], it is exactly thus: he announces by means of a name; he calls out by mentioning the name. (Pāṇini 3.4.59) "After the root *kṛ*, when expressing something contrary to what was intended, the suffixes *ktvā* and *ṇamul* are used.

Expressing something contrary to what was intended (*ayathābhipretākhyāna*) means speaking unpleasantly in a loud voice or pleasantly in a low voice. *uccaiḥkṛtvā* / *uccaiḥkāram*: he announces something unpleasant loudly. *nīcaiḥkṛtya* / *nīcaiḥkṛtvā* / *nīcaiḥkāram*: he speaks something pleasant in a low voice.

SK 3382 (A 3.4.60): When *tiryak* is used as an *upapada*, the suffixes *ktvā* and *ṇamul* are applied after the root *kṛ* when completion (*apavarga*) is to be understood. Examples: *tiryakkṛtya* or *tiryakkṛtvā gataḥ*. The meaning is: "having completed [the action] sideways, he departed. Why specify "completion"? Consider: *tiryakkṛtvā kāṣṭhaṃ gataḥ* ("having placed the wood sideways, he departed"). SK 3383 (A 3.4.61): When a suffix ending in *-tas* denotes a part of one's own body (*svāṅga*), the suffixes *ktvā* and *ṇamul* are applied after the roots *kṛ* and *bhū*.

Having placed [it] at the beginning, he departed; having placed at the beginning (*mukhataḥkṛtya*); having made it the foremost (*mukhataḥkāram*); having become foremost (*mukhatobhūya*); having become foremost (*mukhato bhūtvā*); having become foremost (*mukhato bhāvam*). [This is according to] Pāṇini 3.4.62: *nādhārthapratyaye cvyarthe*.

The suffixes *ktvā* and *ṇamul* do not occur after the roots *kṛ* and *bhū* when a word ending in the suffix *pratyaya* meaning "not" (*na*)—specifically in the sense of the suffix *cvī*—is the governing term (*upapada*). Examples: *nānā kṛtvā* or *nānākṛtya*; *nānā kṛtvā* or *nānākāram*. *vinākṛtya*; *vinā kṛtvā*; *vinākāram*. *nānābhūya*; *nānābhūtvā*; *nānābhāvam*. Having become one from many substances: *ekadhābhūya*; *ekadhā bhūtvā*; *ekadhābhāvam*. *ekadhākṛtya*; *ekadhā kṛtvā*; *ekadhākāram*. Why is the mention of the suffix (*pratyayagrahaṇa*) necessary? [To exclude cases like: *hirukkṛtvā*; *pṛthagbhūtvā*. (A 3.4.63) After the root *bhū*, the suffix *lyap* is applied when the word *tūṣṇīm* is the governing term.

When the word *tūṣṇīm* is used as an upapada, the suffixes *ktvā* and *ṇamul* are applied to the root *bhū*. Examples: *tūṣṇīṃbhūya*, *tūṣṇīṃ bhūtvā*, *tūṣṇīṃbhāvam*. SK 3386: *anvacyānulomye* (A 3.4.64).

When the word *anvak* is used as an upapada, the suffixes *ktvā* and *ṇamul* are applied to the root *bhū* when conformity (*ānulomya*) is implied. Examples: *anvagbhūya āste*, *anvagbhūtvā*, *anvagbhāvam*. The meaning is: "he sits having become conformable—either in front of, at the side of, or behind [someone]. Why "when conformity is implied"? Consider: *anvagbhūtvā tiṣṭhati*. This means "having stood behind."
Thus, only a mere indication of worldly words has been shown here;
however, the detailed exposition according to the scriptures is presented in the *Śabdakaustubha*. (1)
May this Siddhāntakaumudī, the work of Bhaṭṭojidīkṣita, be for the pleasure of the two blessed ones, Bhavānī and Viśvanātha. (2)
Thus ends the section on primary suffixes (*kṛt*).
Thus ends the latter half of the *Siddhāntakaumudī* composed by the venerable Bhaṭṭojidīkṣita.
The Vedic procedure 67.
The First Chapter.
In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), according to A 1.2.61, there is the singular form for *punarvasū*;

that is, the singular may optionally be used for the two [stars] of the *punarvasu* constellation, as in *punarvasu nakṣatram* or *punarvasū*. However, in common usage (*loke*), the dual alone is used.
According to A 1.2.62, the same applies to *viśākhā*.
As before: *viśākhā* as a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*), or *viśākhe*. According to Pāṇini A 1.4.9, in the Vedic language, [the dual ending] is optionally used when joined with the genitive case.

In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the word *pati* when joined with a word ending in the sixth case (*ṣaṣṭhyanta*) may optionally be designated as *ghi*. [Example: *kṣetrasya patinā vayam*. By dividing the rule into two parts—*iha vā* and *chandasi*—the term *chandasi* is carried over [from the previous rule]. All grammatical operations in the Veda are optional; therefore, rules such as *bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pāṇini 3.2.88) are merely elaborations of this very principle. *Yaci bham*: [The suffixes] *ya*, *ac*, etc., are designated as *bha*. *Upasaṃkhyāna* (addition): An addition should be made for *nabhas*, *aṅgiras*, and *manus* when followed by the suffix *vat*. [Examples: *nabhasvat* (meaning "like the sky"), where because it is designated as *bha*, the substitution of *ru* does not occur. *aṅgirasvat* (meaning "like Aṅgiras"). *manusvat*. [Note: The text provided contains fragments of Pāṇinian sūtras and their commentaries.]

In *manuṣvad agne*, [the form] *manuṣvat* is derived from the root *man* with the suffix *usi* (Uṇādi Sūtra 2.117), *usiḥ* being added by way of the rule *janer usiḥ*; furthermore, the suffix *usi* is applied to *man* as well due to the principle of "diversity" (*bāhulakāt*). Regarding *vṛṣaṇvasu-aśvayoḥ*: one whose wealth (*vasu*) is raining down (*vṛṣan*, i.e., abundant) is *vṛṣaṇvasuḥ*. One whose horse (*aśva*) is a stallion (*vṛṣan*) is *vṛṣaṇaśvaḥ*. Here, because the status of being a word (*padatva*) is established by relying on the internal case-ending, the elision of the *n* (*nalopaḥ*) would have been applicable; however, it is prevented because [the stem] is treated as a *bha*-stem. For this very reason, the prohibition of the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* (*ṇatva*)—which applies to what stands at the end of a word—is also not triggered. Furthermore, by the rule *alloponaḥ*, the elision of the *a* does not occur, because [the stem] is not a complete word (*anaṅgatvāt*). SK 3390: *ayasmayādīni cchandasi* (A 1.4.20). In the Vedic language, forms such as *ayasmaya-* and others are valid even when they do not conform to the standard rules.

These [terms] are correct in the Vedic language (*chandas*). Since the section on the technical designation *bha* is in force, both designations (*pada* and *bha*) should be understood as applicable according to the circumstances. Thus, the *Vārttika* states: "It should be stated that there are [words] possessing both designations. In the example *sa suṣṭhubhā sa ṛkvatā gaṇena*: because it is a *pada*, the substitution of *k* for *s* (*kutva*) applies; because it is a *bha*, there is no substitution of *j* for *s* (*jaśtva*). This is because the designation *pada*, which serves to prescribe *jaśtva*, is superseded by the power of the designation *bha*. In the example *nainaṃ hinvanty api vājineṣu*: here, because it is a *pada*, *jaśtva* applies; because it is a *bha*, there is no *kutva*.
Regarding the rule *te prāgdhātoḥ* (Pāṇini 1.4.80): in the Vedic language (*chandasi*), these [suffixes] occur even when they follow [the root], as stated in A 1.4.8.
And [the augment *aṭ* is applied] even when [the root] is separated [by other elements], according to A 1.4.82:
*haribhyāṃ yāhi*, *ok ā*. *ā mandrair indra haribhir yāhi*.
And [the augment *aṭ* is applied] after the roots *indh* and *bhū*, according to A 1.2.6.

After these two [roots], the *liṭ* suffix shall also be *kit*. Examples: *samīdhe dasyuhantamam* ("He kindled the greatest slayer of the Dasyus"); *putra īdhe atharvaṇaḥ* ("The son of Atharvan kindled [the fire]"); *babhūva* ("He became"). This [rule] has been rejected. Because the root *indh* pertains to the Vedic domain (*chandas*) and because the augment *vuk* after the root *bhū* is obligatory, the prescription that the *liṭ* suffix is *kit* after those two is rendered useless. Thus ends the first chapter. The second chapter. SK 3394: *tṛtīyā ca hoś chandasi* (A 2.3.3).

In the case of the root *hu* (to sacrifice), the third case (*tṛtīyā*) as well as the second case (*dvitīyā*) may be used for the object (*karman*). For example: *yāvagvāgnihotraṃ juhoti*. Here, the word *agnihotra* refers to the sacrificial oblation (*havis*), as seen in such usages as *yasyāgnihotram adhiśritam amedhyam āpadyeta* ("if his consecrated *agnihotra* should become impure"), and because of its etymological derivation as "that which is offered to Agni" (*agnaye hūyate*). The meaning is that one offers and casts into [the fire] the oblation called *yāvagvā*, having relinquished it with reference to the deity. [This is governed by] A 2.3.60: *dvitīyā brāhmaṇe*.

In the case of a usage involving *brāhmaṇa* as the object (*viṣaya*), when that which has its purpose is the object (*karman*), the second case (*dvitīyā*) shall be used; this is an exception to the sixth case (*ṣaṣṭhī*). Example: *gām asya tad ahaḥ sabhāyāṃ dīvyeyuḥ* ("They should gamble with his cow on that day in the assembly"). In Vedic usage (*chandasi*), the sixth case is frequently used in the sense of the fourth case (*caturthy-arthe*). Examples: *puruṣamṛgaś candramasaḥ* ("The man-deer [belongs] to the moon"); *godhākālakādārvāghāṭas te vanaspatīnām* ("The lizard, the kālaka, and the woodpecker [belong] to the trees"—meaning "from the trees"). It should be stated that the fourth case is used in the sense of the sixth case. Example: *yā kharveṇa pibati tasyai kharvaḥ* ("To her who drinks from a small vessel, [there belongs] a small [vessel]").

SK 3397: *yajeś ca karaṇe* (A 2.6.63). Here, in the Vedic language (*chandas*), the genitive case is used frequently with the root *yaj* when expressing the instrument. For example: *ghṛtasya* or *ghṛtena yajate*.
SK 3398: *bahulaṃ chandasi* (A 2.4.39). [The substitution of *samprasāraṇa* occurs] diversely in the Vedic language.

The substitute *ghas* shall occur for the root *ad*. [Example: *ghastān nūnam* ("he has surely eaten"). In the *luṅ* tense, within a mantra, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *cli* by the rule *ghasa...* [Pāṇini 2.4.80]. There is an absence of the augment *aṭ*. [Example: *sagdhiś ca me* ("and my eating together").

In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the dual compound *hemanta-śiśirau* and *ahorātre* follow the gender of the first member. Thus, *hemantaś ca śiśiraṃ ca* becomes *hemantaśiśirau*; and *ahorātre*. [In the formation of these,] the *śap* suffix is elided after roots beginning with *ad-* [by Pāṇini 2.4.72].
SK 3400 *bahulaṃ chandasi* (A 2.4.73): "In the Vedic language, [the elision of *aṭ*] is frequent. Examples:

*vṛtraṃ hanati vṛtrahā* ("He slays Vṛtra, [he is] Vṛtra-slayer"); *ahiḥ śayata upa pṛkpṛthivyāḥ* ("The serpent lies close upon the earth"). Here, there is no *luṅ* (the augment). Even when not preceded by the *ad*-class [of roots], there is sometimes elision (*luk*): *trādhvaṃ no devāḥ* ("O gods, protect us!"). From the *juhotyādi* class [of roots], there is *ślu* (elision of the suffix): SK 3401 *bahulaṃ chandasi* (A 2.4.76).
He gives even dear riches; elsewhere also: "he desires [it] full. According to A 2.4.80:
*mantre ghasahvaraṇaśavṛdahād vṛckṛgamijanibhyo leḥ* ("In a mantra, the suffix *liṭ* is replaced by *l* after the roots *ghas*, *hvar*, *ṇaś*, *vṛ*, *dah*, *vṛc*, *kṛ*, *gam*, and *jan*").

The suffix *luk* shall be elided for these [roots] in a mantra. *akṣann amīmadanta hi*: In the case of the substitute *ghasl*, by the rule *gamahana...* there is the elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-lopa*), and by the rule *śāsivasi...* there is the substitution of *ṣ*. *māhvar mitrasya*. *dhartiḥ praṇan nartyasya*: By the rule *naśer vā*, there is the substitution of *k* (resulting in *praṇak*). *suruco vena āvaḥ*. *mā na ādhak*: Here, the feminine form ending in long *ā* is included [as a condition]. *āprā dyāvāpṛthivī*. *parāvarg bhārabhṛd yathā*. *akran uṣasaḥ*. *tve rayim jāgṛvāṃso anugman*.

The mention of "mantra" is also an elliptical indication (upalakṣaṇa) for the Brāhmaṇa texts. Or, [the rule] "his teeth have not yet appeared" applies here because of the continued application of the alternative (vibhāṣā). It is not applied here in the case of: *na tā agṛbhrann ajaniṣṭa hi ṣaḥ*. Thus ends the second chapter. Now begins the third chapter.

In Vedic usage, according to Pāṇini A 3.1.42, after the first four roots—*abhi-ud-sad*, *pra-jan*, *ci*, and *ram*—followed by the suffix *liṭ*, there is the addition of *ām* and the subsequent employment of the root *kṛ* with the suffix *aṅ*. *abhyutsādayāmakaḥ*: in common usage (*loke*), this means *abhyudasīṣadat*. *prajanayāmakaḥ*: the meaning is *prājījanat*. *cikayāmakaḥ*: in the sense of "he piled up" (*acaiṣīt*), from the root *ci*, there is the addition of *ām*, reduplication (*dvirvacana*), and the change to the guttural (*kutva*). *ramayāmakaḥ*: [this means] *arīramat*. *pāvayāṃ kṛyāt*: in common usage, this is *pāvyāt*. *vidāmakran*: [this means] *avediṣuḥ*.

SK 3404: *gupeś chandasi* (A 3.1.50). After the root *gup*, the suffix *caṅ* is optionally used in place of *cli* in the Vedic language. Example: *gṛhān ajūgupataṃ yuvam*. The meaning is *agauptam* ("you two protected"). SK 3405: *nonayatidhvanayatyelayatyardayatibhyaḥ* (A 3.1.51). [The suffix *caṅ* is not used after the roots *nonayati*, *dhvanayati*, *elayati*, and *ardayati* in the Vedic language.]
And [the substitution of] *caṅ* does not occur for *cli*. "O singer, do not diminish my desire as it approaches; may the fire not consume you.

(SK 3406) After the roots *kṛ*, *mṛ*, *dṛ*, and *ruh*, *aṅ* is optionally substituted for *cli* in the Veda: "I have paid this homage to them"; "he died" (*amarat*); "he perished" (*adarat*); "when he climbed from ridge to ridge" (*yatsānoḥ sānumāruhat*).

In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), the following words ending in *ya* are formed with the suffix *kyap*: *niṣṭarkya*, *devahūya*, *praṇīya*, *unnīya*, *ucchiṣya*, *marya*, *starya*, *adhvaryu*, *khanya*, *khānya*, *devayajya*, *āpṛcchya*, *pratiṣīvya*, *brahmavādya*, *bhāvya*, *astāvya*, *upacāyya*, and *pṛḍa*. (A 3.1.123)

When the suffix *kyap* would otherwise apply after the root *kṛt* (to cut) preceded by *nis*, the suffix *ṇyat* is used instead; there is a transposition of the first and last letters [of the prefix], and the *s* of *nis* becomes *ṣ*. One desiring cattle should pile the *niṣṭarkya* fire-altar. When the word *deva* is an upapada, the suffix *kyap* is applied to the roots *hve* (to call) or *hu* (to sacrifice), and there is lengthening of the vowel: *devahūye* (in the invocation of the gods). The suffix *kyap* is applied to the root *nī* (to lead) after the prefixes *pra* and *ud*: *praṇīya* (having led forward) and *unnīyaḥ* (to be led upward). The suffix *kyap* is applied to the root *śiṣ* (to leave) preceded by *ut*: *ucchiṣyaḥ* (to be left over). From the roots *mṛ* (to die), *stṛ* (to spread), and *dhvṛ* (to perish), the suffix *yat* is applied: *maryaḥ* (a mortal); *staryā* (a female who has been covered)—this [suffix] occurs only in the feminine; *dhvaryaḥ* (one who perishes).

The suffixes *yañ* and *yat* are applied after the root *khan*. Thus: *khanyaḥ* and *khānyaḥ*. After the root *yaj*, the suffix *ya* is applied: *śundhadhvaṃ daivyāy karmaṇe devayajyāyai*. After the root *pracch* preceded by the prefix *āṅ*, the suffix *kyap* is applied: *āpṛcchyaṃ dharuṇaṃ vājyarṣati*. After the root *sīv*, the suffix *kyap* is applied along with the change of *s* to *ṣ*: *pratiṣīvyaḥ*. After the root *vad* when *brahman* is the object, the suffix *ṇyat* is applied: *brahmavādyam*. However, in common usage (*loke*), both *kyap* and *ṇyat* are applied to *vad* after a word ending in a case-suffix (per *vadaḥ supi kyap ca*): thus, *bhavateḥ* and *stauteḥ* take *ṇyat*, resulting in *bhāvyaḥ* and *stāvyaḥ*.

The suffix *ṇyat* is applied after the root *ci* preceded by *upa*, and there is the substitution of *ā* for the final vowel when *pṛḍa* follows as the second member of the compound; thus, *upacāyyapṛḍam*. It should be stated that this applies when *hiraṇya* is the object; otherwise, it is *upaceyapṛḍam*. From the roots *mṛḍ* (to be gracious) and *pṛḍ* (to satisfy), the suffix *ka* is applied according to the rule for roots ending in *i* or *u* (*igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kaḥ*). In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), the suffix *in* is applied after the roots *van*, *san*, *rakṣ*, and *math* when they have an object as the preceding word (*karmaṇy upapade*). Examples: *brahmavaniṃ tvā kṣatravanim* ("I invoke you, the winner of Brahman-power and Kṣatriya-power"); *uta no goṣaṇiṃ dhiyam* ("and may our prayer win cattle for us"); *ye pathāḥ pathirakṣayaḥ* ("those who are the protectors of the paths"); *caturakṣau pathirakṣī* ("the four-eyed guardians of the path"); *havir mathīnām abhi* ("toward the churners of the oblation").

SK 3409: *chandasi sahaḥ* (A 3.2.63). When a nominal suffix (*sup*) is the governing word (*upapada*), the suffix *ṇvi* shall be applied after the root *sah*. Example: *pṛtanāṣāṭ*. SK 3410: *vahaś ca* (A 3.2.64). [The suffix *ṇvi* is also applied after the root *vah* when a nominal suffix is the governing word.]
As before. *dityavāṭ*. The separation of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) is for the sake of what follows. A 3.2.65: *kavyapurīṣapurīṣyeṣu ñyuṭ*.
In these cases, the suffix *ñyuṭ* shall be applied to the root *vah* in the Vedic language (*chandasi*). Examples: *kavyavāhanaḥ*, *purīṣavāhanaḥ*, *purīṣyavāhanaḥ*.
SK 3412: *havye ’nantapādam* (A 3.2.66).

*agniś ca havyavāhanaḥ*; but when it occurs in the middle of a word (*pādamadhye*), as in *vahaḥ*, only the suffix *ṇvi* is applied: *havyavāḍ agnir ajaraḥ pitā naḥ*. SK 3413: *janasanakhanakramagamaḥ viṭ* (A 3.2.67).

By the rule *viḍvanoḥ*—there is the substitution of *ā* [for the final vowel]. *abjāḥ*, *gojāḥ*. "O *indu*, you are the winner of cattle (*goṣā*) and the winner of men (*nṛṣā*). By the rule *sanoter anaḥ*—there is the substitution of *ṣ*. "This one, like a boar with its bristles, has shattered [the enemy]; Dadhikrā has reached the five peoples (*pañca kṛṣṭīḥ*) with his might. *agregāḥ*. According to the rule *mantre śvetavahokthaśaspuroḍāśo ṇvin* (Pāṇini 3.2.71), the suffix *ṇvin* is applied in a mantra.

It should be stated that for *śvetavāh* and others, the suffix *ḍas* occurs in place of the word-base ending. The meaning is that wherever the status of being a "word" (*padatva*) is about to occur, *ḍas* should be stated as an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ṇvin*. Thus: *śvetavāḥ*, *śvetavāhau*, *śvetavāhaḥ*. One who praises with hymns (*uktha*) or by means of hymns is an *ukthaśā* sacrificer; *ukthaśāsau*, *ukthaśāsaḥ*. That which is offered or given before is a *puroḍāḥ*. [From the rule] *ave yajaḥ* (A 3.2.72): *avayāḥ*, *avayājau*, *avayājaḥ*.
SK 3416: *avayāḥ*, *śvetavāḥ*, and *puroḍāḥ*—these are prescribed with a long vowel in the vocative case; and by the word *ca* ("and"), *ukthaśāḥ* is also included. SK 3417:
In the Veda, [the suffix] *viṭ* is applied after the root *yaj* when followed by *upa*.

When *upa* is the upapada, [the suffix] *vic* is applied after the root *yaj*. Thus: *upayaṭ*. *A 3.2.74*: "In the Vedic domain (*chandas*), when a *sup*-ending word or a prefix (*upasarga*) is the upapada, the three suffixes *manin*, *kvanip*, and *vanip* may be applied after verbal roots ending in long *ā*. Because of the word 'and' (*ca*) in the rule, *vic* is also included. Examples: *sudāmā*, *sudhīvā*, *supīvā*, *bhūridāvā*, *ghṛtapāvā*. With *vic*: *kīlālapāḥ*. [The rule] *brahmabhrūṇavṛtreṣu...* [is also applicable].

SK 3419: *bahulaṃ chandasi* (A 3.2.88). Even when there is another subordinate word (*upapada*), the suffix *kvip* may optionally be applied to the root *han* in the Vedic language (*chandasi*). Examples: *mātṛhā*, *pitṛhā*. In the Vedic language, the *liṭ* [perfect] tense is used for the general past (*bhūtasāmānye*). Example: *ahaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī ā tatāna*. Regarding the *liṭ*: *liṭaḥ kānajvā* and *kvasuś ca*. In the Vedic language, the suffixes *kānac* and *kvasu* are optionally used instead of *liṭ*. Examples: *cakrāṇa ghṛṣṇi*; *yo no agne ararivāṃl aghāyuḥ*. Regarding the causative suffix *ṇi*: *ṇeś chandasi*. In the Vedic language, the suffix *iṣṇuc* is added after a root ending in *ṇi* to denote habitual action (*tacchīla*) and so forth. Example: *vīrudhaḥ pārayiṣṇavaḥ*. And regarding the root *bhū*: *bhuvaś ca*. [The suffix *iṣṇuc* is also added after *bhū* in the Vedic language.]

From this [root] alone, as before: *bhaviṣṇuḥ*. In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), there is an addition [to the rule] regarding *pari* and *chāyā* with the suffix *kyac*: "In the Vedic language, after a word ending in *kyac*... The suffix *u* should be applied. Thus: *aghāyuḥ*. Under the heading of *erac*, it should be stated that *java* and *sava* occur optionally in the Vedic language. Examples: *yābhir yūnaḥ* ("with which [the young men run]"); *ūrvor me javaḥ* ("the speed of my thighs"); *devasya savituḥ save* ("in the impulse of the god Savitṛ"). [Vt. 10: In a mantra, the roots *vṛṣ*, *iṣ*, *pac*, *man*, *vid*, *bhū*, *vī*, and *rā* take the suffix *ac* when they are accented on the first syllable. (A 3.3.96).

The suffix *ktin* shall occur after roots such as *vṛṣ* and others, and it shall be udātta-accented. Examples: *vṛṣṭim divaḥ* ("the rain from heaven"), *sumnam iṣṭaye* ("happiness for the sacrifice"), *pacāt paktīr uta* ("and from cooking, cooked foods"), *iyam te navyasī matiḥ* ("this is your newest thought"), *vittiḥ* ("acquisition"), *bhūtiḥ* ("prosperity"), and *agna ā yāhi vītaye* ("O Agni, come for the feast") and *rātau syāmobhayāsaḥ* ("may we both be in the gift"). SK 3421: In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *yuc* occurs after verbal roots meaning "to go" when preceded by particles such as *īṣat* and others. This is an exception to [the rule for] *khal*. Example: *sūpasadano 'gniḥ* ("the fire that is easy to approach").

SK 3422: *anyebhyo ’pi dṛśyate* (A 3.3.130). The suffix *yuc* may also be seen after other verbal roots besides those meaning "motion," even in the Vedic language (*chandasi*). Example: *suvedanāmakṛṇor brahmaṇe gām*. SK 3423: *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (A 3.4.6). In the Vedic language, the *luṅ*, *laṅ*, and *liṭ* [tenses] are used [optionally].

When there is a connection between verbal roots (*dhātvartha*) across all tenses, these [suffixes] may optionally occur; otherwise, the respective suffixes apply according to their own rules. *devo devebhir āgamat* ("The god came with the gods")—here, the *luṅ* (aorist) occurs in the sense of the *loṭ* (imperative). *idaṃ tebhyo 'karaṃ namaḥ* ("I have made this salutation to them")—here, the *laṅ* (imperfect) occurs. *agnim adya hotāram avṛṇītāyaṃ yajamānaḥ* ("Today this sacrificer has chosen Agni as the Hotṛ priest")—here, the *liṭ* (perfect) occurs. *adyā mamāra* ("He died today")—this means "he dies today. (A 3.4.7) *liṅarthe leṭ*:

In the Vedic language, the *leṭ* suffix occurs after a root in the sense of the *liṅ* (optative), such as in injunctions (*vidhi*), and in cases involving the relationship between cause and effect (*hetuhetumadbhāva*), and so forth.
SK 3425: *leṭ* is frequently used for the *liṅ* (optative) suffixes. SK 3426: *itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (A 3.4.97).
The *it* of the *tiṅ* suffixes of the *leṭ* may optionally be elided when followed by *parasmaipada* endings.

SK 3427: *leṭo ’ḍādau* (A 3.4.94). After the suffix *leṭ*, the augments *aṭ* and *āṭ* occur; both of these are marked with *p*. It should be stated that *sib* is frequently *ṇit*. [Consequently,] there is *vṛddhi*: *pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣat*; *supeśasaḥ karati joṣiṣad dhi*; *ā sāviṣadarśasānāya*. Also, when there is no elision of *sip*: *patāti didyut*; *priyaḥ sūrye priyo agnā bhavāti*. SK 3428: *sa uttamasya* (A 3.4.98). [The augment *āṭ* occurs] after that [root] which is final in the *uttama* (first person) [of the *leṭ*].
There may be the elision of the final *s* of the *leṭ* [optative] ending. Thus: *karavāva*, *karavāvaḥ*. The substitution of *e* for the *ṭi* [the final vowel of the suffix] occurs.

According to Pāṇini 3.4.95 (*āta ai*), *ai* is substituted for the *ā* of the *leṭ* ending. As in: *mādayaiti* ("may he exhilarate with these well-prepared offerings"). Here, the *aikāra* (*ai*) replaces the *ākāra* (*ā*) of *ātām*. Due to the force of the rule (*vidhisāmarthyāt*), the augment *āṭ* does not undergo this *aitva* substitution; otherwise, the rule would have simply prescribed *aiṭ* instead. As in: *yo yajāti*, *yajāta iti*.

SK 3430: *vaito ’nyatra* (A 3.4.96). The substitution of *ai* for the *e* of the *leṭ* [optative] suffix occurs optionally, except in the domain of the rule *āta ai* (A 3.4.95). Examples: *paśūnām īśai* ("may he be the lord of cattle") and *grahā gṛhyāntai* ("the cups are to be taken"). Why "except" (*anyatra*)? Consider: *suprayasā mādayaite* ("you two rejoice with good food"). SK 3431: *upasaṃvādāśaṅkayoś ca* (A 3.4.8). [The same substitution applies] also in cases of mutual agreement (*upasaṃvāda*) and apprehension (*āśaṅkā*).

The *leṭ* suffix occurs in the sense of a wager (*paṇabandha*) and in the sense of uncertainty (*āśaṅkā*). "I alone am the lord of cattle" (*aham eva paśūnām īśai*). "Lest we fall into hell while going with deceitful tongues" (*nej jihvā yantau narakaṃ patāma*). Regarding the rule *halaḥ śnaḥ śānajjhau* (Pāṇini 3.1.83), in the Vedic language (*chandasi*), there is also the suffix *śāyac* (A 3.1.84). Because of the word "also" (*api*), there is also the suffix *śānac*. By the rule *hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi*, the *h* of *hṛ* and *grah* becomes *bh*. Thus: "Seize the honey with your tongue" (*gṛbhāya jihvayā madhu*). "Bind [it], O God Savitṛ" (*badhāna deva savitaḥ*). By the rule *aniditām...* (Pāṇini 6.4.24), there is the elision of the *n* of the root *bandh*. Thus: "I seize you" (*gṛbhṇāmi te*). "He brought [it] with honey" (*madhvāṃ jabhāra*).

SK 3433: *vyatyayo bahulam* (A 3.4.85). In the Vedic language (*chandas*), there is frequently a transposition (*vyatyaya*) of verbal suffixes (*vikaraṇa*). Examples: 1. *āṇḍā śuṣṇasya bhedati*. Where one would expect *bhinatti*, [the suffix -ati is used]. 2. *jarasā marate patiḥ*. Where one would expect *mriyate*, [the suffix -ate is used]. 3. *indro vastena neṣatu*. Here, from the root *nī-* in the imperative (*loṭ*), there are two suffixes: *śa* and *sip*. 4. *indreṇa yujā taruṣema vṛtram*. The meaning is "we may cross over. From the root *tṛ-* in the optative (*liṅ*) expressing an injunction, there are three suffixes: *u*, *śap*, and *sip*.

The author of the treatise desires the transposition (vyatyaya) of the following: case endings (sup), verbal suffixes (tiṅ), voice (upagraha), gender (liṅga), number (nara), tense (kāla), the suffix hal, accent (svara), the agent (kartṛ), and the suffix yaṅ. This [transposition] is also established by the principle of diversity (bāhulaka). 1. Regarding "in the place of the sacrificial fee" (*dhuri dakṣiṇāyāḥ*): although one would expect *dakṣiṇasyām*, this is used instead. 2. Regarding "those who carve the top-ring for the horse-sacrifice post" (*caṣālaṃ ye aśvayūpāya takṣati*): although one would expect *takṣanti*, this is used instead. 3. Regarding "voice" (*upagraha*), i.e., the middle and active voices (*parasmaipada-ātmanepada*): in the phrase "he desires a student of sacred knowledge" (*brahmacāriṇam icchate*), although one would expect *icchati*, this is used instead. 4. Regarding "against the current, another wave fights" (*pratīpam anya ūrmir yudhyati*).

In the case of *yudhyata*, where *yudhyante* was expected; in *madhos tṛptā ivāsate*, where *madhunā* was expected; *naraḥ* means "man"; in *adhā sa vīrair daśabhir viyūyāḥ*, where *viyūyāt* was expected; *kālaḥ* refers to a suffix expressing time; in *śvo 'gnīn ādhāsyamānena*, *lṛṭ* occurs where *luṭ* was expected; in *tamaso gā adukṣat*, where *adhukṣat* was expected; in *mitra vayaṃ ca sūrayaḥ*, where *mitrā vayam* was expected; however, the transposition of vowels will be discussed later.

The word *kartṛ* refers to the agent in general. Consequently, there is an interchange of suffixes (*kṛt* and *taddhita*) expressing that agent. [Examples: *annādāya* (for *annāda*), where *ac* occurs in place of *aṇ*. There is a specific rule regarding the *avagraha* (pause). Starting from the *ya* of *yaṅ*, the *pratyāhāra* is formed by means of the *ṅ* in *liṅyāśiṣyaṅ* (Pāṇini 3.1.86); the interchange of these is already stated in rules such as *bhedati*. (SK 3434: *liṅyāśiṣyaṅ*).

In the Vedic language, the suffix *aṅ* is substituted for the root when followed by the optative (*liṅ*) in the sense of a benediction (*āśis*). [Example: *vaca um-* — *mantraṃ vocemāgnaye* ("May we speak the mantra to Agni"). The substitution of *ag* for the root *dṛś* should be stated. [Example: *pitaraṃ ca dṛśeyaṃ mātaraṃ ca* ("May I see my father and mother"). However, if *aṅ* were applied, there would be *guṇa* substitution according to the rule *ṛdṛśo 'ṅi*.
[This is prevented by: *chandasy ubhayathā* (Pāṇini 3.4.117).

It has been stated in the section on verbal roots (*dhātu*) that a suffix may bear both the designation *sārvadhātuka* and *ārdhadhātuka*. In the example *vardhantu tvā suṣṭutayaḥ*, the meaning is "may they cause you to increase. Because it is an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix, there is the elision of the causative marker *ṇi*. In *viśṛṇvire*, because it is a *sārvadhātuka* suffix, the suffix *śnu* is applied and the root undergoes the change to *śṛ*. By the rule *huśnuvoḥ—*, the *yaṇ* substitution occurs. Regarding the rule *ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca*: the suffixes *kikin* occur after roots ending in long *ā*, roots ending in *ṛ*, and the root *gam*; these two suffixes function like the perfect (*liṭ*). Thus, from *bhr̥* we have *babhrir vajram* ("he bore the thunderbolt"), and from *pā* we have *papiḥ somam* ("he drank the soma").

*dadir gāḥ* ("he gave cows"), *jagmir yuvā* ("the youth has gone"), *jaghniḥ vṛtram amitriyam* ("he has slain the unfriendly Vṛtra"), *jajñiḥ*. Since [the suffix] is already established by the rule for the behavior of the *liṭ* [perfect tense], the *kittva* (the property of being *kit*) is for the purpose of blocking the *guṇa* substitution prescribed by the rule *ṛcchatyṝtām*. By the rule *bahulaṃ chandasi*, there is the substitution of *u* [for the root vowel]. Thus: *taturiḥ* ("one who has crossed over"), *jaguriḥ* ("one who has gone").
[The suffixes] *se, sen, se, asen, sek, sena, adhyai, adhyain, kadhyai, kadhyain, śa, dhyai, inta, itavai, itave, iṅ, itena* are used in the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*). (Pāṇini 3.4.9)

*se*: *vakṣe rāyaḥ*. *sen*: *tā vāmeṣe*. *ase*: *śarado jīvase dhāḥ*. [The word *asen* is udātta on the first syllable because it begins with the suffix *-asun*. *kse*: *preṣe*. *kasen*: *gavām iva śriyase*. *adhyai*: *adhyain jaṭharaṃ pṛṇadhyai*. [In this case, the accent is on the first syllable. *kadhyai*: *kadhyain āhuvadhyai*. [In this case, the accent is that of the *nit* suffix. *śadhyai*: *rādhasaḥ saha mādayadhyai*. *śadhyain*: *vāyave pibadhyai*. *tavai*: *dātavāu*. *taveṅ*: *sūtave*. *taven*: *kartave*.

SK 3437: *prayai*, *rohiṣyai*, and *avyathiṣyai* (A 3.4.10)—these are irregularly formed (*nipātita*) in the sense of the infinitive suffix *-tum*. Their meaning is "to go forth," "to ascend," and "to be unshaken" respectively.
SK 3438: *dṛśe* and *vikhye* (A 3.4.11).

"To see" means "to make known. According to *Pāṇini* 3.4.12, *ṇamul* and *kamul* are used after the root *śak* when it is an auxiliary verb meaning "to be able," provided that the sense of the infinitive (*tumun*) is intended. For example: *vibhājaṃ nāśakat* and *upalupaṃ nāśakat*, which mean "he was not able to divide" and "he was not able to erase," respectively. That is to say, the meaning is "to divide" (*vibhaktum*) and "to erase" (*apaloptum*).

SK 3440: *īśvare tosunkasunau* (A 3.4.13). [The suffixes] *tosun* and *kasun* are used when *īśvara* [is employed in the sense of] "capable of. Examples: *īśvaro vicaritoh* ("he is capable of wandering"), *īśvaro vilikhaḥ* ("he is capable of scratching"). The meaning is "to wander" (*vicarituṃ*) and "to scratch" (*vilekhitum*).
SK 3441: *kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ* (A 3.4.14). [The suffixes] *tavya*, *anīya*, *kṛtya*, *enya*, *tvana*, and *na* are used in the sense of the *kṛtya* suffixes.

One should not speak barbarously (*na mlecchitavai*). One should plunge into [the water] (*avagāhe*). One should be desirable to see (*didṛkṣeṇyaḥ*). There is the obligation to act extensively and clearly (*bhūryaspaṣṭa-kartvam*).
And regarding *avacakṣe* (A 3.4.15):
"one should not be pointed out by an enemy" (*ripuṇā nāvacakṣe*), meaning that one should not be made visible.

Pāṇini 3.4.16: *bhāvalakṣaṇe stheṇkṛñvadicarihutamijanibhyas tosun* (The suffix *tosun* is added after the roots *sthā*, *kṛ*, *vad*, *car*, *hu*, *tam*, and *jan* when indicating a characteristic action).

Examples: *āsaṃsthātoḥ sīdanti* ("They sit until the completion"; the meaning is "they sit until the end"). *udetoḥ*. *apakartoḥ*. *pravaditoḥ*. *pracaritoḥ*. *hotoḥ*. *ātamitoḥ*. As for the Śruti: *kāmam āvijanitoḥ saṃbhavāmaḥ* ("We shall come together at our pleasure until [the time of] birth"). Pāṇini 3.1.47: *sṛpitṛdoḥ kasun* (The suffix *kasun* is added after the roots *sṛp* and *tṛd*).

The rule "bhāvalakṣaṇe" (when indicating a characteristic of an action) applies here as well: "O mighty one, before the gliding of the cruel one; before the piercing of the collarbones. Thus ends the third chapter.
The Fourth Chapter.

[SK 3445] *rātreś cājasau* (A 4.1.31): The suffix *ṅīp* shall be applied after the word *rātri* in the Vedic language (*chandas*) when it does not refer to a female being (*ajasviṣaye*). Example: *rātrī vyakhyad āyatī*. In common usage (*loka*), however, the suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied by the rule *kṛdikārād aktinaḥ*, and it is oxytone.

SK 3446 *nityaṃ chandasi* (A 4.1.46): In the domain of the Veda (*chandas*), the suffix *ṅīṣ* is invariably applied after words beginning with *bahu*. As in: *bahvīṣu hi tvā*. The inclusion of the word "invariably" (*nitya*) is for the sake of the subsequent rule. SK 3447 *bhuvaś ca* (A 4.1.47): [The suffix *ṅīṣ* is also applied] after the word *bhū*.

The suffix *ṅīṣ* occurs in the Vedic language (*chandasi*). Examples are *vibhvī* and *prabhvī*. In the rule, the form ending in the suffix *ḍu*—namely *vi-urasam-bhyaḥ*—is cited; this is because the word *utaḥ* is understood as being carried over from the previous rule. However, the substitution of *uvaṅ* is a Vedic anomaly (*sautra*). *Mudgalāc chandasi lic ca*: In the Vedic language, after the word *mudgala*, there is the suffix *liṅ* (which functions like *ṅīṣ*), and there is also the augment *ānuk*. The accent is that of the *lit* suffix. Example: *rathīrabhūnmudgalānī*. *Dīrghajhvī ca chandasi* (Pāṇini 4.1.59):
The suffix *ṅīṣ* is prescribed here even though it would not have applied because the stem ends in a conjunct consonant (*saṃyogopadha*). Example: *āsurī vai dīrghajihvī devānāṃ yajñavāṭ*.

SK 3449: In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *ūṅ* is applied after the words *kadru* and *kamaṇḍalu*. Thus, *kadruḥ* and *kamaṇḍalūḥ*. It should be stated that [the suffix *ūṅ* is also applied] after *guggulu*, *madhu*, *jatu*, and *patayālu*: *guggulūḥ*, *madhūḥ*, *jatūḥ*, *patayālūḥ*. After an indeclinable (*avyaya*), the suffix *tyap* is applied. An addition (*upasaṃkhyāna*) should be made for *āviṣṭya* in the Vedic language: *āviṣṭyo vardhate*. SK 3450: In the Vedic language, the suffix *ṭhañ* [is applied].

After *varṣā*, there is the suffix *aṣṭak* as an exception; there is a difference in accent: *vārṣikam*. According to A 4.3.20, *chaṇ* (*ṭhañ*) shall be applied after *vasanta* in the Vedic language (*chandasi*): *vāsantikam*.

SK 3452: In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after *hemanta*. [Example: *haimantikam*. The separation of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) is for the sake of what follows.
