"Of a monosyllabic root, the first [syllable] is doubled"—it should be stated that "in the Veda, optionally. *yo jāgāra*, *dāti priyāṇi*. Regarding the rule *tu-j-ādīnām dīrgho ’bhyāsasya* (Pāṇini 6.1.7): *tu-j-ādi* is an *ākṛti-gaṇa*. *prabharā tūtujānaḥ*, *sūrye māmahānam*, *dādhāra yaḥ pṛthivīm*, *sa tūtāva*.

SK 3510: *bahulaṃ chandasi* (A 6.1.34). In the Vedic language (*chandas*), there is optionally (*bahulam*) vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the root *hve*. Example: *indram āhuva ūtaye* ("They call upon Indra for protection"). In the Vedic language, when the word *ṛc* follows, there is vocalization of *tri* and elision of the initial sound of the following member; this should be stated as a rule. Example: *tṛcaṃ sūktam* ("a hymn consisting of three verses"). Why "in the Vedic language"? Example: *tryṛcāni* ("groups of three verses"). In the Vedic language, the suffix *matup* is applied diversely after the root *rui*. Examples: *revān* ("wealthy") and *rayimān puṣṭivardhanaḥ* ("possessing wealth, increasing prosperity").
SK 3511: *cāyaḥ kī* (A 6.1.35). [The vowel of the root *cāy* is replaced by *kī* before the suffix *matup*. Example: *kīrtimān* ("famous").

They have perceived one [form], but they have not perceived another. The form *nicikyur* is derived from the root *ci* with the suffix *liṭ* and the ending *us*. Because the rule of *bahulagrahaṇa* (the principle of diversity) continues to apply here, it does not occur in this instance: *agniṃ jyotir nicāyya*. [Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.1.36:
*apaspṛdhethām-ānṛcur-ānṛhuś-cicyuṣe-tityāja-śrātā-śritam-āśīr-āśīr-tāḥ*.

These forms are irregularly prescribed (*nipātyante*) in the Veda (*chandasi*). *indraś ca viṣṇo yad apaspṛdhethām*: In *spardh*, the form *āthām* occurs in the imperfect (*laṅ*). *arkam ānṛcuḥ*, *vasūny ānṛhuḥ*: In the perfect (*liṭ*), the suffix *usi* is applied after the roots *arc* and *arh*. *cicyuṣe*: In the perfect (*liṭ*), the suffix *thās* is applied after the root *cyu*. *yas tityāja*: In the perfect (*ṇal*), the suffix *usi* is applied after the root *tyaj*. *śrātās ta indra somāḥ*, *śritā no grahāḥ*: In the past participle (*niṣṭhā*), the suffix *t* is applied with the substitution of *śrā* for the root *śrī* meaning "to cook. *āśīraṃ duhre*, *madhyata āśīrtaḥ*: [The same applies] to the root *śrī* itself when the suffix *kvip* is used and in the past participle (*niṣṭhā*). *khideś chandasi* (A 5.1.12): [The suffix *usi* is applied] after the root *khid* in the Veda.

In the case of *khid* meaning "to distress" (*dainye*), there may optionally be *ā* substituted for its initial vowel: *cikhāda*, meaning "he distressed. [Vt. 14] *śīrṣan* is substituted for the word *śiras* in the Vedic language (*chandasi*): *śīrṣṇaḥ śīrṣṇo jagataḥ*.

SK 3515 *vā chandasi* (A 6.1.106): After a long vowel, before the suffix *jas* or a vowel beginning with *i*, the single substitute for both [the preceding and following vowels] may optionally be the long vowel homogeneous with the preceding one (*pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*). Examples: *vārāhī*, *vārāhyau*; *mānuṣīr īlate viśaḥ*. This rule also applies by way of a separate syntactical connection (*vākyabheda*) to the two subsequent sūtras. Therefore, before the suffix *ām*, the preceding form may optionally occur: *śamīm ca śamyām ca*, *sūrmyam suṣirām iva*. Furthermore, by the rule *saṃprasāraṇāc ca* (A 6.1.108), the substitution of the prior form (*pūrvarūpa*) may also optionally occur: *ijyamānaḥ*, *yujyamānaḥ*. SK 3516 *śeś chandasi bahulam* (A 6.1.70): In the Vedic language, the suffix *śe* is frequently elided.

There shall be elision (*lopa*). [In the formulas] *yā te gātrāṇām* and *tā tā piṇḍānām*, the subsequent form (*pararūpa*) should be stated for *emana* and similar words in the Veda (*chandas*): *apāṃ tveman*, *apāṃ tvodman*. A 6.1.83: *bhayya-pravayye ca chandasi* ("And *bhayya* and *pravayya* in the Veda"). That from which one fears is *bhayya*. From the root *vī* (to weave), *pravayyā* is a specific formation (*nipātana*) restricted to the feminine gender; elsewhere it is *praveyam*. Why "in the Veda"? [Otherwise: *bheyam*, *praveyam*. There is an addition (*upasaṃkhyāna*) regarding *hradayyā*: waters existing in a lake are *hradayyā āpaḥ*. [This is derived by] the suffix *yat* in the sense of "existing there" (*bhave*) in the Veda.
Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.115: *prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare*.

An *eṅ* vowel situated in the middle of a *ṛc*-verse-foot remains in its original form (*prakṛti*) when followed by *ati*, provided it is not followed by *va* or *ya*. Examples: *upaprayanto adhvaram*; *sujāte aśvasūnṛte*. Why "within the verse-foot" (*antaḥpādam*)? Consider: *etāsa ete arcanti*. Why "not followed by *va* or *ya*" (*avyapare*)? Consider: *te avadan*. Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.116: *avyād-avadyād-avakramur-avrata-ayam-avantv-avasyuṣu ca*. [An *eṅ* vowel remains in its original form] also before the words *avyāt*, *avadyāt*, *avakramuḥ*, *avrata*, *ayam*, *avantv*, and *avasyu*.

In these cases, even when there is *vyapara* (an intervening consonant), *ati*, *eṅ*, and *prakṛti* [apply]. Examples include: *vasubhir no avyāt*; *mitramaho avadyāt*; *mā śivāso avakramuḥ*; *te no avrata*; *śatadhāro ayaṃ maṇiḥ*; *te no avantu*; *kuśikāso avasyavaḥ*. Even though the *Bahvṛca* reciters do not apply the *prakṛtibhāva* (non-application of sandhi) in such instances as *teno 'vantu*, *rathatūḥ*, *so 'yam agāt*, and *te 'ruṇebhiḥ*, this is nevertheless to be justified by the principle of *bāhulaka* (diversity/irregularity). However, in the *Prātiśākhya*, this matter is indeed expressly stated as a rule. [This refers to] A 6.1.117: *yahuṣyuraḥ*.

In the Yajurvedic mantra, the word *uraḥ*, ending in *eṅ* (e or o), remains in its original form (*prakṛtyā*). For example: *uro antarikṣam*. This rule is stated because there are no *pādas* (metrical quarters) in the Yajus; thus, it is necessary to specify that the word does not occur within a *pāda*. In the Yajurvedic mantra, the following words remain in their original form: *āpaḥ*, *juṣāṇaḥ*, *vṛṣṇaḥ*, *varṣiṣṭhe*, *ambe*, *ambāle*, and *ambike*, provided they occur before [the aforementioned endings]. Examples include: *āpo asmān mātaraḥ*; *juṣāṇo agnir ājyasya*; *vṛṣṇo aṃśubhyām*; *varṣiṣṭhe adhi nāke*; and *ambe ambāle ambike*. Precisely because of this specific rule, the short vowel substitution prescribed by A 6.1.118 (*ambārthanadyor hrasvaḥ*) does not apply to these forms.
And in the case of *aṅga* and so forth (A 6.1.119):

when the word *aṅga* begins with *eṅ*, and when an *akāra* follows that which begins with *eṅ*, the preceding *eṅ* remains in its original form (*prakṛtyā*) in the *Yajus* texts. Example: *prāṇo aṅge aṅge adīdhyat*. And [the preceding *eṅ* remains in its original form] before an unaccented vowel followed by a guttural consonant (A 6.1.120).

In the Yajurveda, when followed by a guttural consonant (*kavarga*), the letter *dh*, or the vowel *a* which is unaccented (*anudātta*) and followed by *ati*, the *eṅ* vowels remain in their original form (*prakṛtyā*). Examples: *ayaṃ so agniḥ*; *ayaṃ so adhvaraḥ*. Why "unaccented"? Consider: *atho 'gre rudre*. Here, the word *agra* is acutely accented on its first syllable (*ādyudātta*). Why "followed by a guttural or *dh*"? Consider: *so 'yam agnimataḥ*. [Also, the *eṅ* remains unchanged] before *ava* and *pathāsi*: *avapathāsi ca* (A 6.1.121).

In the Yajurveda, when followed by the word *avapathāḥ* beginning with the vowel *a* and having an anudātta accent, the *eṅ* diphthongs [of the preceding word] remain in their original form (*prakṛti*). Example: *trīrudrebhyo avapathāḥ*. [Here,] because it is the *laṅ* [suffix], the *tiṅ* ending is anudātta according to the rule *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*. Why "anudātta"? Consider: *yad rudrebhyo 'vapathāḥ*; here, due to the rule *nipātair yadyadi...* [the preceding word does not retain its original form, as it receives the *nighāta* accent]. Pāṇini 6.1.126: *āṅo 'nunāsikaś chandasi* ("In Vedic usage, the nasalized [variant] of *āṅ* occurs").

When *aci* follows, the nasalized vowel *āṅ* shall occur, and that [nasal] shall remain in its original form (*prakṛtyā*). Examples: *abhra āṃl apaḥ*; *gabhīra āṃl ugraputre*. It should be stated that in the Veda (*chandasi*), there is the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*) for *īṣāakṣa* and others. Examples: *īṣāakṣo hiraṇyayaḥ*; *jyā iyam*; *pūṣā aviṣṭu*. SK 3526: *syaś chandasi bahulam* (A 6.1.133). In the Veda, the elision of the *su* of *sya* may optionally occur before a consonant (*hal*). Example: *eṣa sya bhānuḥ*.

SK 3527: *hrasvāc candrottarapade mantre* (A 6.1.151). After a short vowel, the augment *suṭ* shall be added to the word *candra* when it occurs as a subsequent member (*uttarapada*) in a mantra. Example: *hariścandro marudgaṇaḥ*; *suścandra dasma*. SK 3528: *pitarāmātarā ca chandasi* (A 6.3.33). In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the forms *pitarā* and *mātarā* are used [for *pitṛbhyām* and *mātṛbhyām*].

In a *dvandva* compound, there is a fixed form (*nipāta*). [For example: *pitārā mātarā ca* ("the father and the mother"). Also, with *ca*, the order may be reversed: *na mātarā pitara nū cid iṣṭau*. In Vedic (*chandas*), for the word *samāna*, when it is not preceded by *mūrdhan* and does not end in *udarka*, its substitute is *sa-* in the case of a subsequent member (*uttarapada*) other than those beginning with *mūrdhan*. [Examples: *sagarbhyaḥ*. In Vedic, this substitution occurs diversely (*bahulam*) in the feminine. For the words *viśva* and *deva*, the substitute *adri-* is applied. [Examples: *viśvācī ca ghṛtācī ca*; *devadrīcī nayata devayantaḥ*. [Also: *kadrīcī*. Pāṇini Sūtra 6.3.96: In Vedic, the forms *sadhamāda-* and *-sthā-* [are used].
The substitute *sadh* shall occur in place of *sa-* when it is followed by *hasa*. Furthermore, in this case, there is the term *sadhamāda*. [Examples: *somaḥ sadhastham*. SK 3530:
*pathi ca chandasi* (A 6.3.108).

When the word *pathin* is the subsequent member (*uttarapada*), the substitute *kava* occurs for *ku-*, and there is also the substitution of *kā* for *ku-*. [Examples: *kavapathaḥ*, *kāpathaḥ*, *kupathaḥ*.

SK 3531: *sāḍhyai*, *sāḍhvā*, and *sāḍha* are [forms] in the Veda (nigama). When the suffix *ktvā* follows the root *sah*, the first two forms are derived with the suffix *tṛn*, while the third is a *nipātana* (irregular formation). In the phrase *marudbhir ugraḥ pṛtanāsu sāhvāḥ*, the substitution of *l* for the medial *ḍ* of *ac*, and the substitution of *hl* for *ḍh*, are prescribed in the *Prātiśākhya*. Regarding *āhahi*: when it occurs between two vowels, that *ḍakāra* becomes *lakāra*; that same *ḍhakāra* becomes *hlakāra* when it is joined with an *ūṣman* (sibilant). SK 3532: And in the Vedic language (*chandasi*). (Pāṇini 6.3.126)
The substitution of *āt* for *aṣṭan-* occurs when a subsequent word follows. *aṣṭāpadī*.

In a mantra, there is lengthening of the vowel in the words *sāman*, *aśvin*, *indriya*, and *viśvadevya* before the suffix *matup*. *aśvāvatīṃ somāvatīm*; *indriyāvānmadintamaḥ*; *viśvakarmaṇā viśvadevyāvatā*.
SK 3534: In a mantra, the long vowel [ā] is substituted for the word *oṣadhi* when followed by a case-ending other than the first. For example: *yad oṣadhībhyaḥ* and *adadhāty oṣadhīṣu*. SK 3535:
In a Ṛgvedic verse (*ṛci*), the long vowel [ā] is substituted for the final vowel of the items *tu*, *nu*, *kha*, *makṣu*, *taṅku*, *tra*, *uru*, and *uṣyāṇ*.

The [final vowel] would be long: *ā tū na indra*, *nū martaḥ*, *uta vā ghā syālāt*, *makṣū gomantam īmahe*, *bharatā jātavedasam*. The mention of *taṅ* here includes the case where the substitute *thā* is treated as having the marker *ṅ*; therefore, it does not apply here: *śṛṇota grāvaṇaḥ*, *kūmanāḥ*, *atrā te bhadrā*, *yatrā naś cakrā*, *uruṣyāṇaḥ*. By the rule *ikaḥ suñi* (A 6.3.134), [the long vowel occurs] only when there is a long vowel in a *ṛc* verse: *abhīṣuṇaḥ sakhīnām*. Here, *ṣ* is substituted by *suñaḥ* [from A 8.3.107], and *ṇ* is substituted by *naś ca dhātusthor uṣubhyaḥ* [from A 8.4.27].

SK 3537: *dvyaco 'tas taṅaḥ* (A 6.3.135). In a mantra, there is lengthening [of the vowel] after a two-syllable word ending in *at*, when followed by a *taṅ* suffix: *vidmā hi cakrā jarasaṃ*. SK 3538:
*nipātasya ca* (A 6.3.136). [Lengthening also occurs] after a particle (*nipāta*).
For indeed, by the rule *evādīnām api dṛśyate* (Pāṇini A 6.3.137), the long vowel may also occur for other words standing as the first member [of a compound]. For example: *puruṣaḥ*, *daṇḍādaṇḍi*.
In the Veda, both [forms] are permitted (A 6.4.5):
for a long vowel in place of *nām*, either [the short or the long form may be used]. For example, the Bahvṛcas read "dhātā dhātṝṇām," while the Taittirīyas read the short vowel only.
(A 6.4.9) In the Vedic corpus (*nigama*), the short vowel is optionally substituted for the long vowel of a word preceded by *ṣ*.

In a word preceded by *ṣ*, a long vowel may optionally replace the penultimate (*upadhā*) vowel before a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix, provided it is not the vocative singular. Examples: *ṛbhukṣāṇam* or *ṛbhukṣaṇam*. Why is the restriction "in the Veda" (*nigame*) stated? [Answer: Because in secular usage we have *takṣā* and *takṣāṇau*. SK 3542:

In the *mantra* literature, the elision of the causative suffix *ṇi* is prescribed for the root *jan* when followed by the agentive suffix *tṛc* beginning with *iṭ*. Example: *yo naḥ pitā janitā* ("He who is our father, the progenitor").
In the rule *śamitā yajñe* (A 6.4.54), the meaning is "one who has caused [the sacrifice] to be pacified.
In the rule *yupluvor dīrghaś chandasi* (A 6.4.58), there is lengthening [of the vowel] in Vedic usage.

The word *lyapi* is understood [from the previous rule]. [The suffixes] *viyūya* and *viplūya*. Regarding *āḍajādīnām*, Pāṇini Sūtra 3545 states: "In the Veda (*chandasi*), [the augment] is applied diversely (*bahulam*); even when used with *māṅ*, the augments *aṭ* and *āṭ* do not occur; yet they do occur even when used with *māṅ*. Examples: *janiṣṭā ugraḥ sahane turāya* (let the fierce one be born for the sake of the powerful one), and *mā vaḥ kṣetre parabījāny avāpsuḥ* (let them not sow other seeds in your field)."
SK 3547 *irayo re* (A 6.4.76):

First, *dadhra āpaḥ*. Because the substitution of *rebh-* is considered *asiddha* by virtue of being *ābhīya*, there is the elision of *ā*. Here, once the augment *iṭ* has been applied to the word *re*, the substitution of *rebh-* occurs again; for that purpose, the dual ending is specified in the rule as *irayoḥ*.
SK 3548 *chandasy ubhayathā* (A 6.4.86).

In place of the *bhū* and *sudhī* [stems], there shall be *yaṇ*, as well as *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ*. *vaneṣu citraṃ vibhvam* / or *vibhuvaṃ* / *sudhyo navya magne* / or *sudhiyo* / In the Vedic language (*chandas*), for *tanu* and others, [the substitution] occurs diversely. *tanvaṃ puṣema* / or *tanuvam* / *tryambakam* / *triyambakam* / By the rule *tanipatyoś chandasi* (A 6.4.99), there is elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhālopa*) of these two before an affix beginning with *k* or *ṅ*. *vitatrire kavayaḥ* / *śakunā iva paptima* /

SK 3550: *ghasibhasor hali ca* (A 6.4.100). "And may there be for me a feast (*sagdhiḥ*); may your two bay horses (*harī*) eat the parched grains (*babdhām*). [In this context, the substitution of *dh* for the imperative suffix *hi* applies after roots ending in *h*, as well as after those ending in *jhal* consonants.
SK 3551: *śruśṛṇupṝkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi* (A 6.4.102). [The substitution of *dh* for *hi* occurs after the roots *śru*, *śṛṇu*, *pṝ*, *kṝ*, and *vṛ* in the Vedic language.]
Hear my call! Listen to my songs! Bestow wealth upon me! Make wide room for me!
(SK 3552) *vā chandasi* (A 3.4.88):
[the substitution of] *hirapy* or *api* [for *hi*] is optional in the Vedic language.

SK 3553: After a verbal root ending in *i* or *u*, the substitute *dhi* shall replace *hi*. Examples: *rārandhi* (from the root *ram*); the *parasmaipada* ending occurs by metathesis (*vyatyaya*), the *śap* suffix is elided (*ślau*), and there is lengthening of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) and the substitution of *gh* for the final consonant. *asme prayandhi* (from *yam*); *yuyodhi jātavedaḥ* (from *yu*). In these cases, there is elision of the *śap* suffix after *yam*, and elision of the *śap* suffix after *yu*. SK 3554: In Vedic mantras, the augment *āṭ* is added to the beginning of the [verbal base] of roots beginning with *ā* that belong to the *ātmanepada* class.
There is elision of the initial [phoneme] of the word *ātman* when followed by *āṅ*. [Example: *tmanā deveṣu*.

According to A 6.4.141, *vibhāṣarjoś chandasi*, in the Vedic language, the substitution of *ra-* for the *ṛ-* of the word *ṛju* is optional before the superlative suffixes *iṣṭhan*, *imanic*, and *īyasun*. [Examples: *tvaṃ rajiṣṭham anuneṣi* or *ṛjiṣṭham*.
Pāṇini 6.3.175: *ṛtvyavāstvyavāstvamādhvīhiraṇyayāni chandasi* (In the Vedic language, the forms *ṛtvyá*, *vāstvyá*, *vāstvá*, *mādhvī*, and *hiraṇyaya* are [irregularly] derived).

*Ṛtvyam*: that which exists in the season (*ṛtu*). *vāstvyam* and *vāstvam*: that which exists on the site (*vāstu*). In the case of the word *madhu*, when the suffix *aṇ* is applied, the substitution of *yaṇ* is prescribed for the feminine form: *mādhvīr naḥ santv oṣadhīḥ* ("May the plants be sweet for us"). From the word *hiraṇya*, when the suffix *mayaṭ* is prescribed, the elision of the syllable *ma* is prescribed: *hiraṇyayena savitā rathena* ("Savitṛ with his golden chariot"). Thus ends the sixth chapter. Now begins the seventh chapter.

*Śīṅo ruṭ*: According to *bahulaṃ chandasi* (A 7.1.8), the augment *ruṭ* may optionally be applied. In the alternative view that "there is elision [of the *n*] in the *ātmanepada* endings," there is elision of the *t*. Thus, we have *dhenavo duhre*; when there is no elision, *ghṛtaṃ duhrate*. In *adṛśram asya*, *ais* replaces *bhisa* after a short vowel.
SK 3558: In the Vedic language, [the substitution of *o* for *au*] occurs frequently (Pāṇini A 7.1.10), as in *agnir devebhiḥ*.
SK 3559: In the Vedic language, [the substitution of *o* for *au*] does not occur after any other [vowel] than *a* (Pāṇini A 7.1.26).

The substitution of *adaḍ* for the dual endings *sva* and *am* does not occur [in the Vedic language]. In other cases, [the substitution of *adaḍ* occurs], as in *vārtraghnam*. Why "in the Vedic language (*chandasi*)"? [Consider: *itarakāṣṭham* (in the secular language). In a compound that is not preceded by the negative particle *nañ*, the suffix *ktvā* is replaced by *lyap*.
According to A 7.1.38, *ktvā* also [occurs] in the Vedic language, as in:
*yajamānaṃ paridhāpayitvā*.

Pāṇini 7.1.39: *supāṃ sulukpūrvasavarṇāc cheyāḍāḍyāyājālaḥ*. In the case of *ṛjavaḥ santu panthāḥ* ("May the paths be straight"), where one would expect *panthānaḥ*, the substitution of *su* occurs. In *parame vyoman*, where one would expect *vyomani*, the elision (*luk*) of the genitive ending (*ṅeḥ*) occurs. In *dhītī matī suṣṭutī*, where one would expect *dhītyā matyā suṣṭutyā*, the long vowel of the same class as the preceding vowel (*pūrvasavarṇadīrghaḥ*) occurs. In *yā surathā rathītamobhā devā divispṛśā aśvinā*, where one would expect *yau surathau divispṛśau* and so forth, the substitution of *ā* occurs. In *natād brāhmaṇam*, where one would expect *natam*, the substitution of *āt* occurs. In *yā deva vidma tā tvā*, where one would expect *yam*, [the substitution of *tā* occurs].

In *yuṣme vājabandhavaḥ*, [the suffix] *śe* is applied where *asmabhyam* would otherwise have been used; in *asme indrābṛhaspatī*, [the suffix] *śe* is applied where *yuṣmāsu* would otherwise have been used. In *uruyā* and *dhṛṣṇuyā*, [the suffix] *yā* is applied where *uruṇā* and *dhṛṣṇunā* would otherwise have been used. In *nābhā pṛthivyāḥ*, [the suffix] *ḍā* is applied where *nābhau* would otherwise have been used. In *anuṣṭhyocyāvayatāt*, [the suffix] *aṅ* is applied to *anuṣṭhāna* (meaning "in accordance with" or "established order"), just as in *anuṣṭhā*. In *sādhuyā*, [the suffix] *yāc* is applied where *sādhu* would otherwise have been used. In *vasantā yajeta*, [the suffix] *āl* is applied where *vasante* would otherwise have been used. There is also an extension [of these suffixes] for the forms *iyāṭ*, *iyāṅ*, and *īkāra*.

In the case of *urviyā* and *dārviyā*, where *uruṇā* and *dāruṇā* would otherwise be expected, the suffix *iyā* is applied. In the case of *sukṣetriyā*, where *sukṣetriṇā* would otherwise be expected, the suffix *ḍiyāc* is applied. Regarding the phrase *dṛtaṃ na śuṣkaṃ sarasī śayānam* ("like a withered frog lying in a pond"), some say that the long vowel *ī* is substituted for the genitive ending (*ṅe*). In that case, although the word would be expected to have an udātta accent on the first syllable, there is an irregularity (*vyatyaya*) resulting in the udātta accent being on the final syllable. However, in reality, the genitive ending is elided (*luk*) after a stem ending in the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*; as for the substitution of the vowel *ī*, another example must be sought. The rule should be extended (*upasaṃkhyāna*) to include the forms *āṅ*, *yā*, and *jā*. In the phrase *pra bāhavā sisṛtam* ("stretch forth your two arms"), where *bāhunā* would otherwise be expected, the substitution of *āṅ* occurs.

By the rule *gher ṅiti*, there is *guṇa* [substitution]. In the case of *svapnayā* and *svamenā*, where *ayāc* was expected, [the substitution occurs]. In *sa naḥ sindhum iva nāvayā*, where *nāvā* was expected, *ayār* [is substituted]. This is the accent of *rit*. *A 7.1.40: amo maś*: For *am*, which is the substitute for *mip*, there shall be *maś*. The letter *a* is for the sake of pronunciation (*uccāraṇārtha*). Because it is marked with *ś* (indicating it is a *śit*), it replaces the whole (*sarvādeśa*). By the rule *astisicaḥ*, *iṭ* is added. In *vadhīṃ vṛtram*, where *avadhiṣam* was expected, [the substitution occurs].

SK 3563: *lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu* (A 7.1.41) [occurs] in the Vedic language (*chandasi*). Examples: *devā aduhra* (the gods milked), where *aduhat* was expected; *dakṣiṇataḥ śaye* (he lies on the right side), where *śete* was expected. Why "in the middle voice" (*ātmane*)? [Consider: *utsaṃ duhanti* (they milk the spring). SK 3564: *dhvamo dhvāt* (A 7.1.42). [The substitution of *dhvāt* for *dhvam* occurs in the Vedic language.]

In the phrase *antarevoṣmāṇaṃ vārayadhvam*, the form *vārayadhvam* is obtained when [the rule] applies. Regarding *yajadhvainam* (Pāṇini 7.1.43), the elision of the final phoneme of *dhvam* is prescribed when *enam* follows; thus we have *yajadhvainaṃ priyamedhāḥ*. The statement by the author of the Vṛtti—that the substitution of *ya* for the phoneme *va* is prescribed—is based on a mere error.

SK 3566: *tāt* shall be substituted in place of the second-person plural ending (*madhyama-puruṣa-bahuvacana*) [of the imperative]. As in: *gātram asyānūnaṃ kṛṇutāt* ("Make his limb whole"), where *kṛṇuta* would otherwise have been expected; and *sūryaṃ cakṣur gamayatāt* ("Let the eye go to the sun"), where *gamayata* would otherwise have been expected. SK 3567: *taptan*, *naptan*, and *than* [are also substituted for the second-person plural endings].

The form *tasya* remains as it is. Regarding *śṛṇota grāvāṇaḥ*, since *śṛṇuta* would have been expected, *tap* is applied. Regarding *sunotana pacata brahmavāhase dadhātana draviṇaṃ citram asme*, *tanap* is applied. Regarding *marutas tajjujuṣṭana*, since *juṣadhvam* would have been expected, there is a substitution for the *parasmaipada* ending and the elision (*ślu*) by way of irregularity (*vyatyaya*). Regarding *viśvedevāso maruto yatiṣṭhana*, the meaning is "how many you are. The suffix *ḍati* is Vedic after the word *yat*. For the root *as*, there is the substitution of *than* for that [suffix]. By *idanto masi* (Pāṇini 7.1.46), the final vowel of *mas* is replaced by *i*.

The term *mas* is cited without a case-ending; the vowel *i* is for the sake of pronunciation. Thus, this [suffix] *mas* would be characterized by having the vowel *i* as its final constituent element; that is to say, the augment *ig* would be added to *mama*. This occurs where one would otherwise have *namo bharany emasi*, *tvam asmākaṃ tava smasi*, or *imaḥ smaḥ*. According to Pāṇini 7.1.47 (*ktvo yak*), as in *divaṃ suparṇo gatvāya*.

SK 3570: *iṣṭvīnam* (A 7.1.48): The suffix *ktvā* is irregularly prescribed as having the substitutes *īnam* and *ant*. Example: *iṣṭvīnaṃ devān* ("having sacrificed to the gods"), where *iṣṭvā* would otherwise have been expected. SK 3571: *snātvī-ādayaś ca* (A 7.1.49): And [the forms] beginning with *snātvī* are also [irregularly prescribed].

The word *ādi* has the sense of "type" or "kind. The vowel *ī* is substituted for the phoneme *ā* [in the suffix *ktvā*]. For example: *svinnah snātvī malād iva* ("as one who has sweated bathes from dirt") and *pītvī somasya vāvṛdhe* ("having drunk Soma, he grew strong"). This occurs where *snātvā* and *pītvā* would otherwise be expected. Regarding the rule *āj jaser asuk* (A 7.1.50): after a stem (*aṅga*) ending in a vowel of the *a*-class, the suffix *jas* takes the augment *asuk*. Thus: *devāsaḥ* ("O gods! and *brāhmaṇāsaḥ* ("O Brahmins!").

SK 3573: In the Vedic language, the augment *nuṭ* is added after the genitive plural ending *ām* when it follows *śrī* or *grāmaṇī*. Example: *śrīṇām udāro dharuṇo rayīṇām mūtagrāmaṇīnām* ("the noble sustainer of glories, of riches, and of the leaders of hosts").
SK 3574: In the Vedic language, the augment *nuṭ* is added after the genitive singular ending *goḥ* at the end of a metrical foot.

For we know you, O hero, as the lord of cattle (*gopatiṃ śūra gonām*). What about at the end of a *pāda*? [Example: "Hundreds of cows (*gavāṃ śatā*) in the *pṛkṣayāma*s. Even at the end of a *pāda*, it does not necessarily occur; for in Vedic (*chandas*), all such rules are optional. [Example: "The Virāj, the lord of cattle (*virājaṃ gopatiṃ gavām*). Even in Vedic, the substitution of *anaṅ* for words beginning with *asthi* is observed: "Indra [fought] with the bones of Dadhyañc (*dadhīco asthabhiḥ*)."
And *ī* [is substituted] in the dual, according to A 7.1.77, for words such as *asthi* and others; e.g., *akṣībhyāṃ te nāsikābhyām*.
In the Vedic language, according to A 7.1.83, [the substitution of *ī* occurs] for *dṛś*, *svavas*, and *svatavas*.

The augment *num* shall be added to these [words] before the nominative singular suffix *su*. For example: *kīdṛṅṅindraḥ* ("What kind of Indra?"), *svavān*, *svatavān*. [By the rule] *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya* (Pāṇini 7.1.102), [the *u* is replaced by *ū*].
In the Vedic language (*chandasi*), there is the substitution of *bahulaṃ* (variously).
For example: *tatūriḥ*, *jaguriḥ*, *parācaiḥ*.

SK 3579 *hru hvareś chandasi* (A 7.2.31): In the Vedic language, the substitute *hru* shall occur for the root *hvar* when followed by a *niṣṭhā* suffix. Example: *ahrutam asi havirdhānam*. SK 3580 *aparihvṛtāś ca* (A 7.2.32): [The substitute *hru* also occurs] in the word *aparihvṛta*.

The absence of the substitute prescribed by the preceding rule is here established as an irregularity (*nipātana*). In the phrase *aparihvṛtāḥ sanuyām vājam*, both *iṭ* and *guṇa* are irregularly applied according to A 7.2.33, *some hvaritaḥ*. [Thus: *mā naḥ somo hvaritaḥ*.

The suffix *ka* is applied after the verbal roots *gras*, *skabh*, *stabh*, *ut-stabh*, *catt*, *vikast*, *viśas*, *śaṃs*, *sṛś*, *āstṛ*, *tarutṛ*, *tarūtṛ*, *tarūtṛ*, *varutṛ*, *varūtṛ*, *varūtrī*, *ujjvaliti*, *ṣariti*, *vamiti*, and *amiti*. (A 7.2.34)

Eighteen [forms] are irregularly formed (nipātyante). Among them, for the roots *grasu*, *skambh*, and *stambh*, since they are marked with the *udic* indicatory letter (*udit*), the augment *iṭ* would have been prohibited in the formation of the past participle (*niṣṭhā*); however, the augment *iṇ* is here irregularly prescribed. [Examples: *yuvaṃ śacībhir grasitām anuñcatam* ("By your powers, you two raised up those who were swallowed"); *viṣkabhite ajare* ("the two supports, undecaying"); *yena svaḥ stabhitam* ("by which heaven was supported"); *satyenottabhitā bhūmiḥ* ("the earth is propped up by truth"). Although the form *stabhita* is already established, the specific prescription of the prefix *ut-* again is so that it should not apply when preceded by other prefixes. In *cetayāvace*, from the roots *ceti* and *yāvaci*, and from *kasa* in the sense of "motion," there is the absence of the augment *iṭ* after the suffix *kta*.

"He has been cut from here and cut from there; the dark horse, O Aśvins, was indeed cut in three ways. Regarding the phrase "the heart of the supine one which was cut," the plural form *vikastāḥ* in the Sūtra is used with reference to the multiplicity of instances of cutting; therefore, the singular usage is also perfectly correct. From the roots *śasu*, *śaṃsu*, and *śāsu*, the suffix *tṛc* is applied without the augment *iṭ*. [Examples include: "one who dissects the horse of Tvaṣṭṛ," "the presser of stones and the reciter," "the Praśāstṛ and the Potṛ. After the root *tṛ*, and after *vṛṅ* and *vṛñ*, when the suffix *tṛc* is applied, the augments *uṭ* and *ūṭ* are prescribed as substitutes.

"Tarūtāraṃ rathānām," "tarūtāram," "varūtāram," [and] "varūtrībhiḥ suśaraṇo no astu. Here, the formation with the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is for the sake of elaboration (*prapañca*), for the word *varūtṛ* has been specifically prescribed (*nipātita*). Consequently, since the meaning is already conveyed by *ṅīp*, the substitution of the vowel *i* for the *śap* suffix is prescribed after the four roots beginning with *ujjval*. [The roots are: *jval* (to blaze), *kṣara* (to flow/move), *ṭuvam* (to vomit/emit), and *ama* (to go, etc.). In this context, some also read *kṣamiti* immediately after *kṣariti*.

In this context, the verbal root *kṣam* (to endure) is to be understood. However, in the colloquial language (*bhāṣā*), there are the forms *grasta*, *skabdha*, *ustabdha*, *uttavdha*, *catita*, and *vikasita*; as well as *viśasitā*, *śaṃsitā*, *śāsitā*, *tarītā*, *taritā*, *varītā*, and *varitā*. There are also [the verbs] *ujjvalati*, *kṣārati*, and in an alternative reading, *kṣamati*, *vamati*, and *amati*. Regarding the Vedic forms *babhūtha*, *ātatantha*, *jagṛbhma*, and *vavartha*, it is said in the *nigama*: "We know that fountain from which you have arisen; by which you have stretched out the wide mid-air."

"We have grasped your right hand, O Indra; you have dispelled the darkness with light; you have become manifest. In the *bhāṣā* (vernacular), however, [the forms] are *babhūvitha*, *ātanitha*, *jagṛhima*, and *vavaritha*. Regarding the rule *saniṃsasanivāṃsam* (A 7.2.69):

after the root *sanati* or *sanoti* preceded by the word *sanim*, the suffix *kvasu* takes the augment *iṭ*, and the substitution of *e* for *o* and the elision of the reduplication are irregularly prescribed (*nipātana*). [Example: *añjitvāgne saniṃ sasanivāṃsam*. It should be stated that for words such as *pāvaka*, the change to *tva* does not occur due to the suffix-final *ka* in Vedic usage. [Example: *hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ*.
SK 3584: *ghor lopo leṭi vā* (A 7.2.70).
*dadhadratnāni dāśuṣe*, *somo dadad gandharvāya*, *yad agnir agnaye dadāt*. SK 3585: *mīnāter nigame* (A 7.3.81).
*Śiti* is short. They measure out the vows; they measure out in the world. [The rule] *astisico 'pṛkte* (Pāṇini 7.3.96) applies;
furthermore, there is frequent irregularity (*bahulam*) in the Vedic language (A 7.3.97).

Regarding the form *sarvamā idam āsīt*: when the root *as* is used in the *laṅ* tense, the suffix *tiṅ* is applied; due to its being a single consonant (*apṛkta*), the rule *halḍyādilopaḥ* causes the elision of the initial *t*. Then, the rules for *rutva* and *visarga* apply. However, in *saṃhitā*, the rule *bho-bhago-...* changes the *s* to *y*. By the rule *lopaḥ śākalyasya*, this *y* is dropped. [In the phrase *gobhir akṣāḥ*,] there is no augment *iṭ* after the suffix *sic*; this is a Vedic usage. The augment *aṭ* is added. The remainder is as before. [In the case of the nominative plural ending *jas*,] the rule *hrasvasya guṇaḥ* applies. [The rule] *jasi ca* [is also relevant]. Regarding the endings beginning with *jas*, there is an option in the Veda (*chandasi vāvacanam*) prior to the rule concerning the substitution of the penultimate vowel in the *caṅ* reduplication. Thus: *adhā śatakratvo yūyam*.

*śatakravaḥ* [is formed from *śatakratuḥ*]. Just as [the substitution of *u* for *o* occurs] in *paśunṛbhyaḥ* and *gave*, it should also occur in *paśave*. Regarding the prohibition [of the substitution of *u* for *o*] before a vowel by the rule *nābhyastasyāci*, it must be stated that "it occurs diversely (*bahulam*) in the Veda. Thus we have *anuṣag jujoṣat*.
By the rule *nityaṃ chandasi* (A 7.4.8), in the domain of the Veda, when the suffix *caṅ* follows, the substitution of *ṛ* for the penultimate vowel *ṛ* is obligatory. Thus we have *avīvṛdhat*.

SK 3588: In the Vedic language (*chandas*), for a word ending in *ā* that is not *putra* and not distinct from *putra*, the substitution of long *ī* and lengthening do not occur before the suffix *kyac*. Example: *mitrayuḥ*. [The suffix] *u* is applied by the rule *śyāc chandasi*. Why say "not *putra*" (*aputrasya*)? Example: *putrīyantaḥ sudānavaḥ*. It should be stated that this applies to words beginning with *putra* and others. Example: *janīyantam anvaggravaḥ*. The meaning is "they desire people" (*janam icchanti*). SK 3589: In the Vedic language, the forms *durasyuḥ*, *draviṇasyuḥ*, *vṛṣaṇyati*, and *iṣaṇyati* are established. (A 7.4.36)

These are irregularly formed (*nipātyante*) with the suffix *kyac*. However, in the spoken language (*bhāṣā*), because the suffix *u* is absent, [the forms] *duṣṭīyati*, *draviṇīyati*, *vṛṣīyati*, and *riṣṭīyati* do not occur.

Regarding the rule *aśvāghasyāt* (A 7.4.37): in the Vedic language (*chandas*), the substitution of *āT* for the final vowel of *aśva* and *agha* occurs before *kyac*. Examples: *aśvāyanto maghavan* ("O Maghavan, those seeking horses..."); *mā tvā vṛkā aghāyavaḥ* ("May the wolves, seeking to harm, not [seize] you"). The prohibition "not in the Vedic language" (*na chandasi*) does not apply only to the substitution of *iK* (the *it* augment), but also to the long vowel (*dīrgha*). In this regard, this very sūtra is the indicator (*jñāpaka*).

SK 3591: *devasumnayor yajuṣi kāṭhake* (A 7.4.38). The suffix *āt* is substituted for these two [roots] when followed by the suffix *kyac*, provided they occur in the *yajus* of the Kaṭha recension. Examples: *devāyanto yajamānāḥ* ("The sacrificers, seeking the gods..."); *sumnāyanto havāmahe* ("...we invoke, seeking favor"). Here, the word *yajus* does not refer merely to a mantra, but rather indicates the Veda as a whole. Consequently, this substitution occurs even in a mantra consisting of *ṛc* verses, provided it is situated within the Yajurveda. Furthermore, it also occurs in the Ṛgveda, provided that the mantra is seen in the Kaṭha recension of the Yajurveda. Why say "in the *yajus*"? [Counter-example: *devāñjigāti sumnayuḥ*.
Haradatta states that since the Kaṭha recension also exists among the Bahvṛcas, this serves as a counter-example.
Regarding Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.4.39, *kavyadhvarapṛtanasyarcilopaḥ*:

the final phoneme of these [words] is elided when followed by the suffix *kyac*, provided the context concerns the *ṛc* (Vedic verse). Examples include: *sapūrvayā nividā kavyatāyoḥ*, *adhvaryuṃ vā madhupāṇim*, and *damayantaṃ pṛtanyum*. Furthermore, the substitution of *hi* occurs for the root *dhā* (*dadhāti*) and for the root *hā* (*jahāti*) when followed by the suffix *ktvā*.
In the Vedic language (*chandas*), there is an option (*vibhāṣā*) [to apply the substitution of *i* for *a*] according to A 7.4.44:
*hitvā śarīram* or *hitvā vā*.
According to A 7.4.45, the forms *sudhita*, *vasudhita*, *nemadhita*, *dhiṣva*, and *dhiṣīya* [are also established].

In *su-vasu-nem*, the vowel *e* is substituted for the root *dhā* when the suffix *kta* follows; thus, "the mother [bears] the well-placed embryo in her womb" (*garbhaṃ mātā sudhitaṃ vakṣaṇāsu*). In "well-placed in the fire" (*vasudhitam agnau*), the form is likewise established. In "like manly deeds performed at the place of distribution" (*nemadhitā na pauṃsyā*), it is seen even with the suffix *ktin*. Also, in "and the white one, the bestower of wealth, in its distinctness" (*uta śvetaṃ vasudhitiṃ nireke*) and "place the thunderbolt, O Indra, in your right hand" (*dhiṣva vajraṃ dakṣiṇe indra haste*), where *dhatsva* would otherwise be expected. In "may I, possessing good seed, place the seed" (*suretā reto dhiṣīya*), the augment *iṭ* occurs in the optative (*liṅ*) due to the blessing; by the rule *iṭo 't*, *as* is substituted for *iṭ*, resulting in *dhāsīya*, which is then modified. In "he was not greedy" (*alobhi*), it should be stated that the substitution of *māsa* occurs in Vedic usage.

*mādbhiḥ* / *śaradbhiḥ* / Regarding *svavaḥ* and *svatavasaḥ*, [the suffix] *uṣan* is applied after the word *uṣas*. [The term] *svavadbhiḥ*: the suffix *asun* is added to the root *ava*; those who possess excellent protection (*ava*) are *svavasas*, and by them [is it meant]. *tu* is a verbal root found in the *sūtra* (Dhātupāṭha); from that, *asun* is added. Those who possess their own power (*tavas*) are *svatavantas*, and by them [is it meant]. Haradatta says [the prefix] *sam* [is added]. However, according to the system of the *Pañcapādī*, it was previously explained as *uṣaḥ kit*. [Regarding the form] *na kavateḥ yaṅi*: by rule A 7.4.64, *kṛṣeś chandasi*, there is no substitution of *cu*-sounds for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) when the suffix *yaṅ* follows. Thus: *karīkṛṣyate*.

The forms *dadhāti*, *dardharti*, *dardharṣi*, *bobhūtu*, *tetikte*, *alarṣi*, *apanīphaṇat*, *saṃsaniṣyat*, *karikrat*, *kanikradat*, *bharibhrat*, *ṛvidhvat*, *udavidyutat*, *paritrataḥ*, *sarīsṛpatam*, *varīvṛjat*, *marmṛjya*, and *aganīgan* also [have the reduplicated syllable strengthened]. (A 7.4.62)

These eighteen forms are irregularly formed (*nipātita*). The first three are from the root *dhṛ* or from *dhṛ* in the sense of "to hold. In the case of *bhū* with the elision of the *yaṅ* suffix (*yaṅluk*), there is an absence of *guṇa*; thus, in the common language (*bhāṣā*), *guṇa* is obtained. From *tij* with the elision of the *yaṅ* suffix, the *taṅ* (middle voice) endings are used. In the present tense (*laṭ*) of *iyṛ*, the substitution of *l* for *r* and the absence of *it*-strengthening are irregularly prescribed as an exception to the rule of retaining the initial consonant (*halādiḥśeṣa*). [As in: "O warrior, destroyer of cities, you who cause trembling, you are exhilarated" (*alarṣi yudhma khajakṛt purandara*). The specific mention of the *sip* ending is not restrictive. [And: "The skillful one is exhilarated" (*alarti dakṣa uta*).

In the case of the root *phaṇati* preceded by the prefix *āṅ*, when it is in the *yaṅ*-lopa (elided *yaṅ*) form with the present participle suffix (*śatṛ*), the augment *nīg* is prescribed for the reduplication: *anvāpanīphaṇat*. In the case of the root *syandi* preceded by *sam* in the *yaṅ*-lopa form with the *śatṛ* suffix, *nik* is substituted for the reduplication, and there is the change of the dental *s* of the root to *ṣ*. In the case of the root *kṛ* in its *yaṅ*-lopa form, there is an absence of the *cut* substitution for the reduplication. In the case of *krand* in the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, *cli* is replaced by *aṅ*, there is reduplication, an absence of the *cut* substitution for the reduplication, and the augment *nīg*: *kanikradaj januṣam*. This means "he cried out" (*akrandīt*).

In *vibharti*, there is an absence of the *jaś*-substitution for the reduplicated syllable. In *vi yo bharibhrad oṣadhīṣu*, from the root *dhvṛ* with the suffix *yaṅ-luk* followed by the present participle suffix *śatṛ*, there is the augment *vi* for the reduplicated syllable and the elision of the root vowel *ṛ*. [The example is] *davidhvato raśmayaḥ sūryasya*. In *dyuti*, there is an absence of *saṃprasāraṇa* for the reduplicated syllable, the substitution of *at*, and the augment *vi*. [The examples are] *davidyutat*, *dīdyat*, and *śośucānaḥ*. In *tarati* with the suffix *śatṛ* and *ślau*, there is the augment *ri* for the reduplicated syllable. [The example is] *saho jā tastritaḥ*.

In the case of *sṛp* with the suffix *śatṛ*, when *ślau* is applied in the second person singular, there is the augment *rīk* for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*). In the case of *vṛj* with *śatṛ* and *ślau*, there is *rīk* for the reduplicated syllable. In the case of *mṛj* with *liṭ* and the suffix *ṇal*, there is *ruk* for the reduplicated syllable and *yuk* for the root. In the case of *gam* preceded by *āṅ* with *laṭ* and *ślau*, there is an absence of the *cut* substitution for the reduplicated syllable and the augment *nīk*. "vakṣyantī vedāganīganti karṇam" (RV 10.27.12). According to the rule "sasūva iti nigame" (A 7.4.74), in the Vedic language (*nigama*), when *liṭ* follows *sū*, the Parasmaipada endings are used, and the augment *vuk* as well as the substitution of *ā* for the reduplicated syllable are prescribed as irregularities (*nipātana*). "gṛṣṭiḥ sasūva sthaviram" (RV 1.164.10). In the common language (*bhāṣā*), it is "suṣuve."

SK 3598: *bahulaṃ chandasi* (A 7.4.78). In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the substitution [of *iṭ*] may optionally occur for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*). Example: *pūrṇāṃ vivaṣṭi*. This is a form derived from the root *vaś*. Thus ends the seventh chapter.
Now begins the eighth chapter.

SK 3599 *prasamupodaḥ pādapūraṇe* (A 8.1.6): These [prefixes] take a double form when used for the purpose of filling out a verse-quarter (*pāda*). Examples: *praprāyam agniḥ*; *saṃsamidyuvase*; *upopa me parāmṛśa*; *kiṃ nodudu harṣase*. SK 3600 *chandasi iraḥ* (A 8.2.15): In Vedic literature (*chandas*), the substitute *ira* is applied [to the root *i*].
The *m* of the suffix *matup* following a stem ending in *ivarṇa* or *repha* shall be replaced by *v*. Examples: *harivate*, *haryaśvāya*, *gīrvān*. SK 3601: *ano nuṭ* (A 8.2.15).

The augment *nuṭ* is added to the suffix *matup* after a stem ending in *an*. Examples: *akṣaṇvantaḥ*, *karṇavantaḥ*; [the phrase] "that which has bones" (*asthanvat*) and "that which is boneless" (*anasthā*).

SK 3602 *nād dhasya* (A 8.2.17): The augment *nuṭ* is added after a word ending in *n* before the suffix *gha*. [Examples: *supathiṃtaraḥ*. The augment *tuṭ* should be stated [after *bhūridāvan*]: *bhūridāvattaro janaḥ*. [The suffix] *īn* is added after *rathin*: *rathītaraḥ*. [Superlative: *rathītamaṃ rathīnām*. SK 3603 *nasattaniṣattānuttapratūrtasūrtagūrtāni chandasi* (A 8.2.61): In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the forms *nasatta*, *niṣatta*, *anutta*, *pratūrta*, *sūrta*, and *gūrta* are established as such.

In the case of the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) following the roots *sad* preceded by *nañ* or *ni*, the substitution of *n* for *s* is not applied by way of a grammatical irregularity (*nipātana*). Thus, one obtains *nasattam añcasā* ("not sitting on a seat") and *niṣattam asya carataḥ* ("of him who is moving while seated"). This occurs because, according to the rules, one would otherwise obtain *asannam* ("not sitting") and *niṣaṇṇam* ("seated"). Following the root *und*, when preceded by *nañ*, the form *anuttam* is obtained. *Pratūrtam* is derived either from the root *tvar* or from *turvī*. *Sūrtam* is derived from the root *sṛ*. *Gūrtam* is derived from the root *gurī*. According to Pāṇini 8.2.70, in the Vedic language (*chandasi*), after *amnas*, *ūdhas*, and *avara*, both [the substitution of] *ru* and *repha* (the letter *r*) are optionally applied. Thus, one obtains *amna eva* or *amnareva*; *ūdha eva* or *ūdhareva*; *eva eva* or *avara eva*.
SK 3605: And [the substitution of *bhū* occurs] for the great utterance (*mahāvyāhṛti*) *bhuvas*, i.e., for *bhuvas* and *bhuvar*. SK 3606:
*om* is substituted [for *oṃ*] at the beginning of a recitation (*abhyādāna*).

The word *oṃ* shall be protracted (*pluta*) at the beginning [of a Vedic recitation]. Example: *o3m agnimīle purohitam*. Why say "at the beginning"? Consider: *om* (the single syllable). SK 3607: *ye* [is protracted] in the sacrificial ritual (*yajñakarman*). Example: *ye3 yajāmahe*. Why say "in the sacrificial ritual"? Consider: *ye yajñmahe*.

SK 3608 *praṇavaṣṭeḥ* (A 8.2.89): In the ritual of sacrifice (*yajñakarman*), the substitute *om* shall take the place of the final syllable (*ṭi*). Example: *apāṃ retāṃsi jinvato3m*. Why "of the final syllable" (*ṭeḥ*)? To prevent [the substitution] from applying to the last letter of a word ending in a consonant (*halanta*). SK 3609 *yājyāntaḥ* (A 8.2.90): [The substitute *om* applies] at the end of a *yājyā* verse.

In sacrificial rites, the final *ṭi* (the last vowel with its following consonant) of those *yājyā* mantras is pronounced with a protracted (*pluta*) vowel. For example: *jihvām agne jihvām agne cakṛṣe havyavāhā3m*. Why [is it not so] at the end? [Because the rule applies] to the *ṭi* of each individual sentence within the *yājyā* verses, which consist of a collection of sentences; however, it is intended that the protraction applies to the very last [syllable] of the entire [verse]. Regarding the rule *brūhipreṣyaśrauṣaḍvauṣaḍāvahānām ādeḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.91): in sacrificial rites, the initial syllable of these words is pronounced with a protracted vowel. For example: *agnayenubrū3hi*, *agnaye gomayāni pre3ṣya*, *astu śrau3ṣat*, *somasyāgne vīhī vau3ṣaṭ*, and *agnimā3vaha*.

SK 3611: *agnītpreṣaṇe parasya ca* (A 8.2.92). When there is an injunction addressed to the *agnīdh* priest, the initial syllable is protracted (*pluta*), as is the syllable following it. Example: *o3śrā3vaya*. SK 3612:
*vibhāṣā pṛṣṭaprativacane heḥ* (A 8.2.93). In a response to a question, the particle *hi* may optionally be protracted.

*Pluta* [occurs]. "Did you make the mat? "Indeed, I made it. "I made it, indeed. Why [is it said] "when questioned"? [As in: "He will surely make the mat. Why [is it said] "of *hi*"? [As in: "He is indeed making the mat. SK 3613: *nigṛhyānuyoge ca* (A 8.2.94).

In this case, the final syllable (*ṭi*) of that sentence is optionally *pluta*. "Today is the new moon," [you] said. [The word] "new moon" is used when one who speaks thus is displaced from his own position by means of reasoning and is thus questioned.
SK 3614: *Āmreḍitam* [is pluta] when used in scolding (A 8.2.95).

For example: *dasyo3 dasyo3 ghāṭayiṣyāmi tvām* ("O thief! O thief! I shall have you executed!"). The mention of *āmreḍita* is an indication for any doubled word (*dvirukta*). For example: *caura3 caura3*. SK 3615: A word joined with *aṅga* [is pluta] when it requires a finite verb (*tiṅ*) (A 8.2.96).

A finite verb (*tiṅanta*) joined with *aṅga* is elided [in the sense of reproach]. Example: *aṅga kūja3 idānīṃ jñāsyasi jālma* ("Hey, you fool! Shout now, and you shall see"). Why "finite verb"? Example: *aṅga devadatta mithyā vadasi* ("Hey, Devadatta, you speak falsely"). Why "expecting something more" (*ākāṅkṣam*)? Example: *aṅga paca* ("Hey, cook!"). This does not expect anything further. Only in the sense of "reproach" (*bharṣana*)? Example: *aṅgādhīṣva bhaktaṃ tava dāsyāmi* ("Hey, study! I will give you food").
[This applies also] to those being deliberated upon (*vicāryamāṇānām*). (A 8.2.97)

The final vowel (*ṭi*) of sentences becomes protracted (*pluta*). For example: *hotavyaṃ dīkṣitasya gṛhā3 i* / *na hotavya3m* / Thus, it is deliberated whether [the oblation] should be offered or not. Deliberation (*vicāra*) is the examination of the true nature of a thing by means of the instruments of knowledge (*pramāṇa*). However, regarding the rule *pūrvaṃ tu bhāṣāyām* (A 8.2.98), when things are being deliberated, the first [of the two alternatives] is protracted: *ahir nu3 rajjur nu* ("Is it a snake or a rope?"). Here, "priority" (*pūrvatva*) is relative to the usage. Because of the mention of *bhāṣā* (spoken language), it is understood that the preceding rule applies to the Vedic language (*chandas*).

SK 3618: And in the case of *pratiśravaṇa* (answering), the final vowel (*ṭi*) of a sentence is protracted (*pluta*) when expressing assent, a promise, or being attentive to what is heard. "Give me a cow, sir! "Yes, I shall give it to you. "Sound must be eternal. "What did you say? SK 3619: In the cases of a question-ending or respectful address, [the final vowel] is unaccented (*anudātta*).

The *pluta* vowel shall be *anudātta* (unaccented). This rule prescribes merely the *anudātta* quality for the already established *pluta* vowel used in cases such as calling from a distance (*dūrād dhūta*). Examples: *agnibhūta 3 i*, *paṭa 3 u*. In these two instances—*agnibhūte* and *paṭo*—occurring at the end of a question, the final syllable (*ṭi*) becomes an unaccented *pluta*. Example: *śobhanaḥ khalv asi māṇavaka 3*. Furthermore, according to A 8.2.101, when the particle *cit* is employed in the sense of a comparison (*upamā*), [the preceding word becomes *pluta*].

The final syllable (*ṭi*) of a sentence becomes a protracted (*pluta*) vowel and is unaccented (*anudātta*). Example: *agnicid bhāyā3t* ("One who has built a fire-altar might fear," or "He might fear like a fire-altar-builder"). Why "in the sense of comparison" (*upamārthe*)? Counter-example: *kathaṃcid āhuḥ* ("They say somehow"). Why "when [the particle] is employed" (*prayujyamāne*)? Counter-example: *agnir māṇavako bhāyāt* ("The young Brahmin might fear like a fire"). And by the rule *uparisvidāsīd iti ca* (A 8.2.102), the final syllable (*ṭi*) becomes a protracted vowel and is unaccented. Example: *uparisvidāsī3t* ("Was it above?"). However, in the case of *adhaḥ svidāsī3t*, the protracted vowel is acute (*udātta*) because of the rule *vicāryamāṇānām* (A 8.2.97).

SK 3622: *kharitam āmreḍite 'sūyāsaṃmatikopakutsaneṣu* (A 8.2.103). When a reduplicated word (*āmreḍita*) follows, a protracted (*pluta*) circumflex (*svarita*) vowel occurs if envy (*asūyā*), approval (*saṃmati*), anger (*kopa*), or censure (*kutsana*) is implied. In the case of envy: *abhirūpaka 3*, [meaning] "O handsome one! Your handsomeness is wasted. In the case of approval: *abhirūpaka 3*, [meaning] "O handsome one! You are truly beautiful. In the case of anger: *avinītaka 3*, [meaning] "O ill-mannered one! Now you shall know, you scoundrel! In the case of censure: *śāktīka 3*, [meaning] "O spearman! Your spear is empty [of use]. SK 3623: *kṣiyāśīḥpraiṣeṣu tiṅākāṅkṣam* (A 8.2.104). [The protracted circumflex occurs] after a finite verb (*tiṅanta*) when it requires another finite verb to complete its sense, provided the context involves a request for permission (*kṣiyā*), a benediction (*āśis*), or an injunction (*praiṣa*).

In the case of a finite verb (*tiṅanta*) expressing a desire, the final syllable (*ṭi*) becomes a circumflex (*svarita*) protracted vowel (*pluta*) when there is a difference in action. Example: *svayaṃ ha rathena yāti 3 upādhyāyaṃ padātiṃ gamayati* ("He himself goes by chariot, while he makes the teacher go on foot"). In the sense of a request (*prārthanā*): *putrāṃś ca lapsīṣṭa 3 dhanaṃ ca tāta* ("May you obtain sons and wealth, my dear"). In the sense of commissioning (*vyāpāraṇa*): *kaṭaṃ kuru 3 grāmaṃ gaccha* ("Make the mat; go to the village"). Why "expressing a desire"? [Counter-example: *dīrghāyur asi agnīd agnīn vihara* ("Long-lived are you, O Agnīdh; distribute the fires"). SK 3624:
Even for a non-final syllable, [the protracted circumflex occurs] in questions and narrations. (A 8.2.105)

In these two cases, the *svarita* vowel of the final syllable—even if it is not the last word—is protracted (*pluta*). Examples: *agamaḥ 3 pūrvā 3 n grāmā 3 n*. This [protraction] applies to all words when used in narration (*ākhyāna*). Example: *agama 3 m pūrvā 3 n grāmā 3 n*. Regarding the rule *plutāv aica idutau* (A 8.2.106):

when a protracted vowel is prescribed for *ai* and *au* in contexts such as calling from a distance, then in that very instance where *ai* and *au* would have been protracted, their constituent parts *i* and *u* are what actually undergo protraction. Examples: *ai 3 tikāyana*, *au 3 pagava*. In these cases, the *aic* diphthongs become four-mora (*caturmātra*) sounds.
When a vocative address occurs that is not a *pragṛhya* vowel and is not distant, the *u* or *ū* of the first half [of the word] is replaced by the *i* or *u* of the subsequent [half]. (A 8.2.107)

In the case of a protracted vowel (*pluta*) used for addressing someone from a distance, when the *ec* vowel is not *pragṛhya*, the first half becomes the long *ā* (*ākāra-pluta*), while the second half becomes *i* or *u*. This occurs only at the end of a question, in expressions of respect, when deliberating, in a return greeting, and at the end of a sacrificial verse (*yājyā*). Examples: - At the end of a question: *i* 3 (as in *kim i 3*) - In expression of respect: *paṭa 3 u* ("O you who are clever! - When deliberating: *hotavyaṃ dīkṣitasya gṛha 3 i* ("Should one sacrifice in the house of the initiated one? or *na hotavya 3 m* ("One should not sacrifice"). - In a return greeting: *āyuṣmānedhi agnibhūta 3 i* ("May you be long-lived, O Agnibhūta!"). - At the end of a sacrificial verse.

"Let us worship Agni with hymns. What is the purpose of this enumeration? [To show: "I shall have you killed when Viṣṇu has become present. It need not be stated that [the word] *dhūta* occurs when not far away; however, the mention of "end of a word" (*padānta*) must be made so that it does not apply here: *bhadraṃ karoṣi gaur iti*. Why [is the condition] "not a *pragṛhya*" used? [So that it does not apply to: *śobhane māle*. This modification involving protracted vowels (*pluta*) in the Vedic language (*chandas*) when there is an address (*āmantrita*) should be stated: *agna 3 i patnī vaḥ*. Regarding those two [rules], [it is said]: *tayor yvāvaci saṃhitāyām* (A 8.2.108).

The sounds *y* and *v* are substituted for *idut* [the vowels *i* and *u*] before a vowel (*aci*) in *saṃhitā*. Examples: *agna 3 yāśā*; *paṭa 3 vāśā*; *agna 3 yindram*; *paṭa 3 vudakam*. Why "before a vowel" (*aci*)? [Counter-example: *agnā 3 i varuṇau*. Why "in *saṃhitā*"? [Counter-example: *agna 3 i indraḥ*. The mention of "*saṃhitāyām*" is a governing rule (*adhikāra*) extending to the end of the chapter; it is intended to exclude *idut* from the scope of the preceding rule, or alternatively, because the substitution of *y* and *v* is not yet established (*asiddha*), it serves to block the application of the rule *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya* (P. 8.2.4). SK 3628: *matuvaso ru saṃbuddhau chandasi* (A 8.3.1).

The term *ru* is an indeclinable designation. It shall replace the final phoneme of a stem ending in *mat* or *vat*. By the paribhāṣā "alo 'ntyasya" (Pāṇini 1.1.52), this replacement occurs for the letter *n*. Thus: *indra marutva iha pāhi somam* and *harivo medinaṃ tvā*. The substitution of *v* for *r* is by the rule *chandasīraḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.15). [Furthermore, the forms] *dāśvān*, *sāhvān*, and *mīḍhvān* are formed by A 6.1.12.

These are prescribed as *nipātana* (irregularly formed) words ending in the suffix *kvasu*. [The example is: *mīḍhvastokāya tanayāya* ("O bounteous one, for our offspring and progeny"). There is an addition (*upasaṃkhyāna*) for the word *vana*. There is a general inclusion of both *kvanip* and *vanip* [suffixes]. However, the technical rule regarding *anubandha* (indicatory letters) does not apply here, because no *anubandha* is specified in this context. [The example is: *yastvāyantaṃ vasunā prātaritvaḥ* ("He who comes to you with wealth, O early-rising one"). [This is derived from] the root *iṇ* with the suffix *kvanip*. According to A 8.3.8, *ubhayatharkṣu*, when followed by a *chavarga* consonant that has *am* (a vowel) preceding it, the *n* of the suffix may optionally become *ru*. [The example is: *paśūn tāś cakre* ("He made them cattle").

SK 3631: *dīrghād iṭi samānapāde* (A 8.3.9). After a long vowel, the substitution of *ru* for the *n* may optionally occur before an *iṭ* augment, provided that both [the *n* and the *iṭ*] reside within the same *pāda*. Examples: *evāṃl acchā sumatī*, *mahāṃl indro ya ojasā*. Because the word *ubhayathā* ("in both ways") is understood as a governing rule (*anuvṛtti*), it does not apply here: *ādityān yāciṣāmahe*. SK 3632: *āto ’ṭi nityam* (A 8.3.3). [The substitution of *ru* for the *n*] occurs invariably after a word ending in *ā* before an *aṭ* suffix.

When *ru* follows, the nasalized (*anunāsika*) substitute invariably takes the place of the preceding *a*. Thus, *mahāṃl indraḥ*. However, the Taittirīyas read it with an *anusvāra*. Regarding this, the ancients maintain that it is a Vedic anomaly (*chāndaso vyatyayaḥ*). Consequently, the utility of the rule [Pāṇini 8.3.2] must be reconsidered. In the case of *svatavān pāyau* (A 8.3.11), the *ru* is optional. Thus: *bhuvas tasya svatavāṃlaḥ pāyur agne*.
SK 3634: *chandasi vāprāmreḍitayoḥ* (A 8.3.49).

In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the visarga may optionally become *s* before *k* or *p*, with the exception of the word *pra* and a reduplicated form (*āmreḍita*). Examples: *agne trātar ṛtasya kaviḥ*; *girir na viśvataḥ pṛthuḥ*. Here it does not apply: *vasunaḥ pūrvyaḥ patiḥ*. Why say "excepting *pra*" and so forth? Observe: *agniḥ pra vidvān*; *paruṣaḥ paruṣaḥ*. SK 3635: *kaḥ karat karat karat kṛdhi kṛteṣv anaditeḥ* (A 8.3.50). [In the Vedic language, the visarga of a word ending in *as* becomes *s*] before the forms *kaḥ*, *karat*, *karat*, *karat*, *kṛdhi*, and *kṛte*, provided they do not belong to the root *ad*.

The *s* shall be substituted for the visarga [of the word *div*]. As in: *pradivo apaskaḥ*, *yathā no vasyasaskarat*, *supeśasaskarati*, *uruṇaskṛdhi*, and *somaṃ na cāruṃ maghavatsu naskṛtam*. Why say "except for *aditiḥ"*? [Because in that case it would be: *yathā no aditiḥ karat*. By Pāṇini 8.3.51 (*pañcamyāḥ parāvadhyarthe*), the *s* shall be substituted for the visarga of a word ending in the fifth case when the word *pari* follows in the sense of "above" (*uparibhava*). As in: *divas pari prathamaṃ jajñe*. Why say "in the sense of 'above'"? [Because in another sense it would be: *divas pṛthivyāḥ paryojaḥ*.

SK 3637: *pātau ca bahulam* (A 8.3.52). [The substitution of *ṣat* for *sāt*] occurs diversely before the root *pā-* "to protect," provided that [the preceding word] ends in the fifth case (*pañcamī*). Example: *sūryo naḥ divaḥ pātu*.

SK 3638: *ṣaṣṭhyāḥ pati-putra-pṛṣṭha-pāra-padapayas-poṣeṣu* (A 8.3.53). [The substitution of *ṣat* for *sāt* occurs] after a word ending in the sixth case (*ṣaṣṭhī*) when followed by *pati*, *putra*, *pṛṣṭha*, *pāra*, *pada*, *payas*, or *poṣa*.

To Vācaspati Viśvakarman; to Sūrya, the son of heaven; praising the ridge of heaven; [reaching] the further shore of this darkness; enveloped in the station of Ilā; bestowing the milk of heaven; bestowing royal prosperity upon the sacrificers; or from *iḍā* (A 8.3.54).

In the case of *patiputra* and other such words, as in *ilāyāḥ putraḥ* ("the son of Ilā") or *ilāyāspade* ("in the place of Ilā"), the sibilant of *nisaḥ* becomes a retroflex (*mūrdhanya*) before the root *tap*, provided it does not denote repetition. Thus, we have *niṣṭaptam rakṣaḥ* ("the demon is burnt away") and *niṣṭaptā arātayaḥ* ("the enemies are burnt away"). Why "provided it does not denote repetition"? Consider *nistapati*; this means "he heats again and again.
(Pāṇini 8.3.103: *yuṣmattattatakṣuṣvantaḥpādam*.)

The dental *s* of a word situated in the middle of a *pāda* becomes cerebral (*ṣ*) when followed by these words beginning with *t*: *yuṣmad*-substitutes (*tvam*, *tvā*, *te*, *tava*), *tribhiḥ*, *tebhiḥ*, *ābhiḥ*, *apsu*, *sadhiḥ*, and *agniḥ*. Examples: *tribhis ṭvaṃ deva savitaḥ* (with those three, O God Savitṛ); *tebhis ṭvā*; *ābhis ṭe*; *apsv agne sadhiṣ ṭava*; *agniṣ ṭad viśvam*; *dyāvā pṛthivī niṣṭatakṣuḥ*. Why "within a *pāda*" (*antaḥpādam*)? Example: *tad agnis tad aryamā*. In *yan ma ātmano mindābhūd agnis tat punar āharj jāta-vedā vicarpaṇiḥ*, the word *agniḥ* marks the end of the preceding *pāda*, not its middle.
According to some, this applies within a *yajus* [mantra]. (Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.3.104)

In the presence of *yuṣmat*, *tat*, and *takṣuṣu*, the *s* of *sasya* optionally becomes a retroflex (*mūrdhanya*). Examples: *arcibhiṣ ṭvam* ("by means of flames, you"), *agniṣ ṭe agram* ("the tip of yours, O Agni"), *arcibhiṣ ṭatakṣuḥ* ("they fashioned by means of flames"). In the alternative case, one has *arcibhis tvam* and so forth.
Regarding the rule *stutastomayoś chandasi* (Pāṇini A 8.3.105):

*nṛbhiṣ ṭutasya* ("praised by men") and *nṛbhiḥ stutasya*; *goṣṭomam* and *gostomam*. Since this was already established by the rule *pūrvapadāt* (A 8.3.106), this [present rule] is for the sake of elaboration (*prapañcārtham*).

SK 3643 (A 8.3.106): After a cause situated in the first member of a compound, the *s* of the following [suffix] optionally becomes *ṣ*. Example: *yad indrāgnī diviṣṭhaḥ*; *yuvaṃ hi sthaḥ svarpatī*. SK 3644 (A 8.3.107): [The *s* of a suffix] following the root *suñ* [becomes *ṣ*].
The *s* of the particle *suñ* following a cause (*nimitta*) situated in the preceding member is changed to *ṣ*. Examples: *ūrdhva-uṣuṇaḥ*, *abhī-ṣuṇaḥ*. Regarding *sanoteḥ anaḥ* (Pāṇini A 8.3.108):
[Examples include] *go-ṣāḥ indo nṛ-ṣā asi*. Why "of *ana*" (*anaḥ*)? [Counter-example: *go-saniḥ*.

SK 3646: After the roots *sah* (to endure/overcome), *pṛtanā* (army), and *ṛta* (truth/order), [the suffix *kvin* is applied]. Examples: *pṛtanāṣāham*, *ṛtāṣāham*. By virtue of the word "ca" (and), also *ṛtīṣāham*.
SK 3647: In the Vedic language (*chandas*), when there is an intervention by *ni*, *vi*, or *abhi*, [the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*] is optional.

The best of crops; he sat down (*nyaṣīdat*); he sat down (*nyasīdat*); he despaired (*vyaṣīdat*); he despaired (*vyasīdat*); he praised (*abhyaṣṭaut*); he praised (*abhyastaut*). According to Pāṇini 8.4.26, *chandasy ṛdavagrahāt*, there is *ṇatva* for a *n* following an *ṛ*-ending word that is an *avagraha*: *nṛmaṇāḥ*; *pitṛyāṇam*.

SK 3649: *naś ca dhātusthor uṣubhyaḥ* (Pāṇini A 8.4.27). [The substitution of *ṇ* for *n* occurs] after a letter situated in a verbal root (*dhātustha*), following *u*, *ṛ*, or *ṣ*. Examples: *agne rakṣā ṇaḥ*; *śikṣā ṇo asmin*; *uru ṇaskṛdhi*; *abhīṣu ṇaḥ*; *mo ṣu ṇaḥ*. Thus ends the eighth chapter. This concludes the Vedic grammatical procedure (*vaidikī prakriyā*).
The section on vocal tones (svaraprakriyā) 68.

SK 3650: *anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam* (A 6.1.158). This is a governing rule (*paribhāṣā*) concerning the application of accentual rules. In whatever word a specific acute (*udātta*) or circumflex (*svarita*) accent is prescribed, that single vowel (*ac*) being excluded, the remainder of that word shall consist of unaccented (*anudātta*) vowels. For example: *gopāyataṃ naḥ*. Here, by the rule *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ*, the suffixes beginning with *san* are treated as verbal roots; thus, by the root-accent (*dhātusvara*), the vowel *ā* of the suffix *yak* becomes acute, while the rest of the word remains unaccented. It should be stated that "the accent taught later is stronger [than one taught earlier], except in the case of verbal suffixes (*vikaraṇa*)."

In the example cited by him (*gūṇāti*), the accent of the root (*dhātusvara*) of *guṇ* and the accent of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*) of *āya* are not retained. What is meant by "elsewhere"? [Consider] *yajñaṃ yajñam abhivṛdhe gṛṇītaḥ*. Here, even though the accent of *śnā* is "later taught" (*sati-śiṣṭa*), it is not retained; rather, the accent of *tas* alone is retained. **SK 3651: *anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.161)** Where an acute (*udātta*) syllable is elided following an unaccented (*anudātta*) one, that [unaccented] syllable shall become acute. In *devīṃ vācyam*, the *ṅīp* suffix is acute.

SK 3652 (Pāṇini 6.1.222): When *añcu* follows, with its initial vowel elided (*luptākāra*), the preceding [word] shall have an acute accent on its final syllable. This is an exception to the rule regarding the accent of the "cessation of the acute" (*udāttanivṛttisvara*). Example: *devadrīcīṃ nayata devayantaḥ*. It should be stated that this does not apply when a taddhita suffix follows. Examples: *dādhīcaḥ*, *mādhūcaḥ*; here, the accent is simply that of the suffix (*pratyayasvara*). SK 3653 (Pāṇini 6.1.198): And [the word] in the vocative case (*āmantrita*) [has an acute accent on its final syllable].
The first syllable of a vocative should be acute. For example: *agna*, *indra*, *varuṇa*, *mitra*, *devāḥ*. This is according to Pāṇini’s rule *āmantritasya ca* (A 8.1.19).

Every vocative (*āmantrita*) that follows a word [within a compound] and stands at the beginning of a *pāda* shall be *anudātta*. This rule from the eighth chapter is an exception (*apavāda*) to the previously mentioned rule of the sixth chapter. Example: *imaṃ me gaṅge yamune sarasvati*. Why "not at the beginning of a *pāda*" (*apādādau*)? Example: *śutudri stomam*. A preceding vocative is treated as non-existent (*avidyamānavat*).
